rooms.name: Elsendor - On the Western Edge of Town

userData.LongDescription: Elaborate war banners hang over the road and large monster skulls decorate the walls of buildings nearby. The clash of steel and loud cheers can be heard from beyond the wicked portcullis of the arena to the east. Onlookers have gathered around impressive warriors outside of Centurio Clan Hall the west and a crowded marketplace filled with exotic goods is to the north.

In the center of the quiet plaza a large tree is surrounded by flowering bushes. On the eastern edge of the road a sheer cliff face juts out of the ground and a dark cavern has been exposed. Sweet smelling incense wafts out of a small toolshop to the north. To the west a building with gigantic marble pillars stands proudly and the signs for a few shops can be seen to the south.

Rows of shelves line the walls and every conceivable space has been filled with different sized bottles. Pungent haze fills the air which originates from a complicated-looking array of beakers, decanters, and tubes on the counter. A stocky man with herb-stained fingers operates a burner beneath one of the glass tubes. A small sign is posted near his desk against the wall.

Most of the western wall of this room is taken up by an enormous viewing screen which displays Lucavi activity in the various realms.  Several computer terminals are stationed around the room for Militia personnel to use to track down and relay important information.

rooms.name: Elsendor - The Inn of Eternal Life

userData.LongDescription: The raucous laughter from the bar belies the sense of comfort found within the inn's walls. Long tables are filled by adventurers, some sharing stories and others preparing for battle. A thick trail of cigar smoke emanates from the staircase leading to the gaming hall below. Against the western wall, a roaring fire beneath a polished stone mantle breathes warmth into the inn. A young woman stands behind the counter situated between the social areas and the rooms beyond. There is a small sign on the counter.

The hedges and trees to the north offer a sense of serenity the area. Plush sections of grass invite passersby for a moment's rest. To the west, a sturdy iron arch maintains a connection to another realm. Off to the east, the base of a cliff marks the end of the road. Directly south, the Elsendor Bank stands proudly with elaborate alabaster pillars of marble and gold-tooled lettering on the metope.

Forgotten after the installation of the Skydock, the expansive plateau was once the site of a great arena.  There has been something of a resurgence in popularity lately, largely due to the crowding of the city. A variety of tents are set up, and there is construction happening on the ruined foundations of older buildings. To the east a painted wagon with large streamers has been setup at the base of the cliff.

The Elsendor Militia Raid Hub is a small, circular room with a large skylight in the center of a domed ceiling. There are three tunnels that branch off to the north, south, and east. Each path leads to a single room housing a large computer designed to process a raid assignment. The path back to the main headquarters is to the west.

The road has been worn by decades of foot travel. A meticulously trimmed hedge weaves between thick rows of trees along the northern edge of town. A busy marketplace is visible to the west, and to the east an iron arch is at the junction of cobblestone roads. An odd stable is situated between two beautiful flower beds, which mask a strange smell from that vicinity.

Citizens sit within the rows of wooden pews of this holy place. White flowers have been hung on the marble columns that are along the wall. Running down the center aisle is an ornate carpet that leads up to an elaborate altar. The vaulted ceiling extends high above and channels the grandeur of God. From the southern wall, light shines through a massive stained glass window, which depicts a pair of knights locked in battle.

The cobblestone road bears marks of heavy use. A pair of equipment shops are on either side of the road and each has a sign hanging over their door. The sounds of a hammer striking metal emanate from the shop to the west while the smell of polish pours out of the one to the east. Barrels of water, racks of recently forged weapons, and stacks of logs are piled outside of the shops. At the end of the road further to the north, a large iron arch holds a black portal.

Parked near the base of the cliff is a sturdy wooden vardo. Banners in a variety of bright colors stretch from the vardo to poles topped with lanterns. The end result looks like an explosion of color with the vardo in the center. An old man is sitting on a simple chair next to the wagon.

The Elsendor Militia Headquarters are spartan in decor, reflecting the no-nonsense nature of defending Elsendor against the Lucavi armies. Rows of armaments line the walls, all recently tended to. Enlistees can be seen coming and going, be it to check in with the company clerk, to activate an assignment, or to shop in the armory.

A large iron arch holds a portal open and the ruins of an ancient base can be seen through it. The cobblestone road wraps around the militia headquarters to the west and joins with the main road to the north. The eastern border of Elsendor consists of a forest with extremely dense undergrowth, except for a small natural alley that's been worn in by foot traffic.

Bright embers burn within the furnace against the northern wall.  A sturdy anvil sits next to a blackened log which is covered with red hot forging tools. There are two stout troughs for quenching against the western wall, one contains a viscous oil and the other has clear water within. Boxes of exotic ores and materials are stacked near the forge entrance to the east. The air is thick with the stench of sulfur and flux.

This is the newbie equipment room.  A small old man sits behind a desk here and points to a sign as you enter.  For those just starting on their adventures, this is the place to pick up some free equipment.  The main shop is back up.

A sprawling two-story room, this rowdy clan hall is full of adventurers and vagabonds.  Items of great value are for sale, available only to those who have made a name for themselves by performing important missions.  A small sign is hanging from the counter, describing the shop.

A large gilded gate controls entrance to the town of Memoria. The gate, tightly locked, has vines and moss covering the hinges, indicating that it is seldom opened. The town beyond the gate is somehow obscured even when peering through the bars of the gate.

The ceiling of the bank is a beautiful stained glass skylight, providing a dazzling light source inside of the stone structure. Tellers stand behind a long marble table with a decorative cloth draped over it. Behind the tellers, a closed portcullis guards the vault. A couple of queues with red satin ropes have been set out for the citizens of Elsendor, but busy adventurers are able to immediately get service through an express lane. A double-height oak door leads out to the streets of Elsendor. A notice has been posted near the express lane.

Whatever building used to be present on this road has been demolished, and the beginnings of a small quarry has been dug into the earth between the surrounding shops.  A wooden staircase leads down into the quarry, but an outdoor booth blocks the way to it, selling the magical stones that have been dug up.

This room is filled with rows of gray cots. Each space is kept very clean by the attendants in the room, and a person behind a desk at the entrance checks each person entering to see if they need to be here. If you need a place to rest during a raid, you may do so here.

Warm and cozy, this small shop is tucked away in a side alley, little-frequented and obscure. There's not much to the place: a large bookshelf, a stone fireplace, and a waist-high display counter are the only prominent things. The shopkeeper sits behind the counter in an old rocking chair, knitting. She smiles at anyone who enters.

This is an odd little room filled with gigantic canary cages hanging at variable heights.  Upon the center back is a large and posh throne of the finest upholstery.  There are giant caches of zodiac emblems and stellazio coins placed all around the throne, locked and kept away for safekeeping.

This room is filled with all manner of volatile chemicals, bomb casings, loose wires, timers, ready-made explosive devices, and magical items that cause bangs.  Painted on the wall behind the counter is a huge caricature of Bob's insanely grinning face and the name of the shop.  A photograph on the counter shows a happy family of several hundred people.

The commotion of the city gives way to the serene hum of the portal. A massive crystal suspended by a wrought iron arch serves as a focusing point for the portal's magic.  The road leading north and south is a little narrower than the avenue going west. Two odd signs hang over the street to the north and another portal hums quietly to the south.

This room, relatively barren in nature, has a single focal point in the center. Some markings along the wall glow and lead towards the center of the room, as though they are funneling energy towards the dais in the center. A small chest sits on the dais, radiating an aura of powerful magic.

Tendrils of frost spread from the base of the portal and icicles hang from the iron arch supporting the threshold to another realm. Adventurers walk briskly through the vicinity near the portal as blasts of arctic wind frequently escape. In the distance to the east, Elsendor Square lies beyond a few shops. A few obscure buildings inhabit the road to the north and the horizon is visible to the south.

rooms.name: Entrance to the Deep Dungeon - Elevator Room

userData.LongDescription: A stone stairwell spirals downwards into deep darkness below.  A voice activated elevator rests in the north wall, ready to descend to any level of the dungeon a person has visited.  A sign rests over the elevator, while an opening in the west wall leads to the rest of the town of Elsendor.  A small board with fiery red letters sits next to the staircase, displaying an important message.

The cobblestone roads throughout the city all come to one point, Elsendor Square. Barter, laughter, and bustling adventurers all contribute to the energetic atmosphere. Shops can be seen in every direction, except to the south where a massive cathedral towers over the city park. The steeples of the church cast a long shadow which perfectly frames a massive statue, the centerpiece of the square. Adjacent to the statue, a small circle of crystal bricks are embedded into the square.

This room houses a large computer devoted to powering the systems used during a raid. The decor is purely functional, designed to maximize cooling to the power unit so as to avoid overtaxing any systems and causing a system crash in the militia's defense systems.

The ancient stairs empty onto a large landing carved into the face of the cliff. The resulting space is sheltered from the sun, and large enough for several people to rest before continuing. A stone ledge forms a solid barrier from which to enjoy the splendid view of the rocky canyons below. The climb continues either upwards into the city, or down to the mesa.

The organization known as the Tantalus Theater Troupe, which is actually a band of thieves posing as performers, has made this building into their headquarters.  The building itself serves as a clock tower; a massive clock makes up most of the building's front wall.  The back of the clock face can be seen from inside the building, and dozens of massive gears all around the building are keeping it turning.  Scattered across the haphazardly nailed floorboards are several coat racks and chests, carrying costumes.

As far as curio shops go, this one is unusual.  Various tools of uncanny origin and power line the walls and showcases, and the interior decor seems to be going for a Gothic look.  Long arches and high ceilings dominate the atmosphere with a feeling of grimness, countered only by the bargain bins and helpful wares markers, and of course the till near the shop's grand entrance.

A constant flow of traffic surges and ebbs from Elsendor Square to the east. Crates containing piles of furs and monster parts have spilled into the road from the unpainted wooden shop to the south, while muffled explosions occasionally come from the stone quarry to the north. An occasional cold snap whisks in from the portal to the west.

rooms.name: Elsendor - A Road Along the Cliffs of Elsendor

userData.LongDescription: The southern horizon can be seen through a thin row of trees along the road. A brisk wind pushes through them carrying the dust from the canyon below. The cobblestone road leading east and west winds slightly as it follows the cliff's edge. Occasionally the breeze changes direction and pulls the aroma from the city park from the east. Further to the west is the plaza serving as a cargo yard and staging area for the skydocks.

Rustling leaves, singing birds, and the smell of freshly cut grass turn this simple park into a sanctuary from the commotion of busy city life. On the southern edge of the park, majestic marble steps lead to the cathedral doors. The road from the north breaks into smaller paths and winds throughout the scenery but eventually reconverges into the cobblestone road that runs east to west on the southern border of Elsendor. On the northern end of the park, a quietly humming portal is framed by a wrought iron arch.

Shelves line the stone brick walls of the modestly sized shop; a wide variety of armor sit upon them. A large chest near the entrance is filled with the materials that are used to make the padded lining for the inside of the larger pieces. Under a window on the northern wall, a small desk is cluttered with various tools for minor repairs and suit assembly. Against the back wall, a wooden ladder leads up to a tiny loft where the shopkeeper lives. A small sign sits on a table alongside a few shields.

Succulent aromas waft into the road from the Elsendor Inn and the sounds of clanking tankards and laughter escape from the tavern within each time an adventurer passes through the entrance to the north. The southern building is the Item Shop and has a wide variety of wares displayed in crystal cases in the window. The city square lies to the west and appears to be a hub of commerce; while a glimmering portal leading to another realm is nearby to the east.

This room houses a large computer devoted to powering the systems used during a raid. The decor is purely functional, designed to maximize cooling to the power unit so as to avoid overtaxing any systems and causing a system crash in the militia's defense systems.

Completely barren except for the Faculty member standing in the corner of the room, this training room has nothing to interfere with the combat soon to come.  Training can occur by saying 'list' to get a list of valid monsters and then saying 'train <monstername>' to begin combat.  Should you at any time wish to end combat simply say 'end training'.

This room appears to once have been a shrine of technological advancement, though it doesn't seem to have had much use recently. All sorts of screens are mounted along the wall, with wires connecting them to a variety of machines that performed unknown tasks long ago. What exactly this place was used for may never be known. The only thing that appears to be functioning is a glowing shape off to the side of the room.

The lobby of the Arena is dimly lit by torchlight. Bloodied weapons and tattered scrolls litter the dirty floor. A mural depicting four ancient beings in the eternal struggle is displayed for all to see. There are four small alcoves and each holds a warp crystal which leads up to a raised platform for one on one contests. Along the eastern wall, a large pit leads to the battleground for group matches. On either side of the portcullis leading out of the arena, a set of stairs leads up to the viewing area.

A chocobo of enormous proportions sits in the center of a humble stable. The ceiling of the hovel bears a gigantic hole. Curtains cover the windows, but sunlight streaks in from above. Lesser birds chirp from the roof and the occasional golden feather wafts by. A large sign has been posted near the majestic bird.

Racks, displays, and counters are filled with a wide assortment of armaments. A display near the entrance holds blades of various designs in a fan-like manner, while smaller weapons adorn racks attached to the stone walls. In the center of the shop, a large bearskin rug is laid out and has a small receptacle filled with staves placed on it squarely. Near the back of the shop, a set of stairs marked 'Free' leads downstairs and next to it a polished counter has a small sign displayed.

A metal pier extends out into the air off the edge of a cliff to the southwest. The pier is ideal for boarding and unboarding airships and other vehicles. The skies beyond the cliff are clear and blue. A long steel walkway north leads back to the main roads of Elsendor.

This small shop is adorned with many different items for ninjas, from shuriken to swords. The shopkeeper behind the counter keenly watches the store. A small display near the eastern wall has items that offer aspiring and veteran samurai alike a medium upon which to evoke the spiritual power of their iaido: powerful and portable seals that characterize the elements of the world's most iconic and successful line of katana. There is a small sign on the counter.

The roads from the east and north converge into a circular plaza. Shipments of goods and large cargo containers are stacked throughout, awaiting pickup from local vendors. A small office is located at the front of the long pier stretching to the south. Clerks and merchants scurry around the plaza, verifying what has arrived and what needs to go. To the north, a frosty iron arch sits in the middle of a junction. To the west ancient stairs, worn smooth by time and use, winds down the cliff.

rooms.name: Elsendor - Outside of the Militia Headquarters

userData.LongDescription: Pristine and well-maintained, the Elsendor Militia Headquarters stands out from other parts of Elsendor. There are no stray boxes, litter, or loiterers around the entrance to the massive building. To the west, the city park sits in the shade of the cathedral and citizens lounge on the grass. An odd, deserted laboratory is at the end of a long walkway to the south.

Three sets of stairs lead up to the flight deck of the Big Whale. Chrome walls with odd glowing symbols mesh nicely with the polished portion of the floor. At the center of the flight deck a massive amber-colored crystal floats over a hole in the floor.

Heavy limestone walls surround the modest arena in a definitive ring. Coarse sand, baked by the severe sun, covers the entire arena. The constant fights in the arena churn the sand, hiding the evidence of blood.

This is the very bottom of the dungeon, where hell's own magician makes his presence felt.  Coarse slabs of stone are held in the air as platforms irrespective of gravity.  Raw magic courses through the very air and sets the stage for a dire confrontation waiting just ahead.

The cobblestone roads meet in a small circular plaza, forming a busy marketplace lined with several shops.  An enormous canvas provides a little too much shade to the plaza. The light of a single lamppost in the plaza's center illuminates the shop fronts, some of which are open and inviting, while others are covered by dark curtains and have closed doors. War banners can be seen to the south and a stable to the east.

An ominous black portal hangs within a wrought iron arch. An eerie quiet surrounds the portal as if sounds are disappearing into its abyss. Far to the south, Elsendor Square hosts a myriad of adventurers. Fluted marble pillars decorate the building to the east and the mixed smell of chocobos and flowers spills in from the west.

This dank, musty room located a few feet below the inn is inhabited mostly by a table surrounded with a series of chairs. The concrete slab flooring, cinder block walls, and dim lighting make the room give off a warm cozy vibe to essentially anyone who has ever played D&D. The sole source of luminescence in the room hangs from the ceiling above the table, and is barely bright enough to make visible the occasional poster taped to the wall.

Nestled at the end of a back alley between buildings, this open-air 'shop' looks more like a small smithery than anything else. The very back of the space is lined with wooden shelves, as well as a small furnace. A workbench and a cistern line the wall between the back area and the customer counter in the front.

rooms.name: Elsendor - A Path Along the Forest

userData.LongDescription: The trees and undergrowth of the nearby forest have been allowed to flourish near the buildings along the eastern border of Elsendor. A sign stands at the end of a dirt path leading to a small clearing. To the north, an out-of-place cliff juts from the ground. The familiar sound of hammer and anvil come from the forge to the west, with each stroke punctuated by a strange sizzle.

The staff clerk keeps a well ordered room, but there is so much paperwork that it is sitting in piles everywhere. The clerk continually processes reports from militia members, moving paper along in a never-ending stream of data processing. A small monitor sits in the corner of the room. The exit back to the main hall of Militia HQ is to the east.
The elevator descends into a solid and dark path.  Only the sight of powerful magic waves to the northern beyond offers some sense of direction.

The walls of this shop are lined with countless furs, pelts, and other objects of the trade, obtained from creatures of all shapes and sizes. A small, flickering light casts shadows about the room and across the small counter towards the rear of the shop. To the north, the exit leads back to the streets of Elsendor.

This room houses a large computer devoted to powering the systems used during a raid. The decor is purely functional, designed to maximize cooling to the power unit so as to avoid overtaxing any systems and causing a system crash in the militia's defense systems.

All that seems to be visible is a small series of connected platforms and a dormant machine floating to the southeast. The fenced-off platforms seem to be suspended in dense fog. A bit of light is afforded by a tall, lit lamppost and a glow from the northwest casting vague shadows along the cobblestone floor. To the northeast, a doorway leads to another platform.

An empty, metal room awaits those who travel through this gate. Two doors are the only truly notable features of the room itself. The air coming through the gate is stale and dusty, but also seems to carry an almost sinister stench. This pillar leads to the post-apocalyptic era: the year is 2300AD, and the location is Bangor Dome, one of the last standing structures left in the world.

A lively fair can be seen through this time gate. The smell of fresh cooked meats and cacophony of voices and music travel through the pillar. Visible through the light of the gate, a large device of unclear purpose can be seen. Stepping through this gate transports travellers to the Millennial Fair hosted at Leene Square in the year 1000AD.

This pillar of light, one of the nine total time gates that exist in this place, stretches upward endlessly. Through the gate, a small cave can be faintly seen. Also, a chilly breeze can be felt coming from the other side. One may deduce that it leads to the end of the Ice Age, 12000BC. To the southeast, a cloaked man can be seen leaning up against the lamppost, dozing lightly. In every other direction lie the pillars that lead to other important eras.

A gate stands ajar at the edge of the platform. Passing through this small gate leads to a staircase taking travellers to the pillars northwest of this platform. The glow emanating from there is much brighter that the faint light cast by the lamppost to the southeast. The cobblestone floor gives way to a staircase cleanly cut from solid stone. Looking over the edge of the walkway reveals nothing but more of the all-encompassing dense fog.

A stone pier of sorts juts out into the darkness away from the main platform which lies to the northeast. The walkway seems to be made from cinder blocks as opposed to the cobblestones of the main area. Just beyond the edge of the walkway, the legendary time machine known as the Epoch floats in the void.

The image seen through this gate seems to be from high atop a mountain. A vast prehistoric jungle full of reptiles and primitive mammals stretches out below the mountain. No ground can be seen directly below the gate, so one can safely assume the gate is embedded in the side of a cliff. This gate leads to the top of what is known as Mystic Mountain in the ancient era of 65,000,000BC.

The image through this pillar depicts the inside of a small house belonging to a couple of imps. From this perspective of inside their cabinet, one can see the table where they would drink and converse. This is Medina Village, in the year 1000AD, the home of the demi-human decendants of the mystics.

Not much can be seen looking through this time gate. The other side of the gate seems to be located in the middle of a cave among huge piles of rubble from which there is no exit. These are the ruins of the Tyrano Fortress after Lavos fell from the sky and crashed there in the year 65,000,000BC, leaving a massive crater.

This is the center pillar among the other eight in the End of Time. Through the gate is a futuristic, metal room full of dormant machinery. No sound comes from the other side of the gate, but dirty, stale air flows through it. The ruination of the dome beyond is evident. This gate leads to Proto Dome, in the ruined age of 2300AD.
In every direction is a black void. A spotlight shines on a wooden chair. A pendant swings in the background.

A small clearing surrounded by a dense collection of trees can be seen through this corner time gate. Birds and small creatures resembling mushrooms can be seen faintly seen moving through the underbrush within the pillar. The fragrant smell of evergreens wafts into this realm through the pillar. This gate seems to lead to Guardia Forest in the year 1000AD. This era seems a bit more inviting than the harsh prehistoric and future eras.

The location of this pillar is the northernmost place in the End of Time. To the south, the pillars are spread out in a three-by-three array. The image through through the time gate is that of a densely forested canyon. From this vantage point, a stream can be seen bubbling through the center of the canyon. This pillar leads to 600AD, the height of the Middle Ages.

For some unexplained reason, Spekkio, the legendary Master of War, has taken up residence in this pedestrian room of the End of Time. Cobblestones make up the floor in this room. They are arranged in a circular pattern originating where Spekkio stands. The light in this place seems to emanate from the Master of War himself; another mystery in an impossible realm.

Only a hardy, weed-like grass has been able to grow on top of this raised clearing. Thin outcroppings can be seen all the way down to the river below, serving as historical indicators of the water level. The clearing extends to the west and slopes down to the south. An old wooden bridge connects to another raised clearing to the east.

The ground gives way to a wide ravine with a raging river coursing through it. The trees and bushes within the canyon are getting their autumn colors and hide a small, shaded clearing to the east. A sheer cliff face to the north has a simple rope ladder secured to the top, allowing for easy travel.

Short cliff faces surround a patch of grass, creating a small clearing. Tall bushes grow at the top of the surrounding rock turning the clearing into a secluded grove. Other than crabgrass, only a small bush of yellow flowers grows in defiance of the oppressive shade. A deep blue portal fluctuates wildly in the center of the clearing.

The sloped path from the north hugs the exposed sandstone as it connects the platforms of differing heights. A few bushes with yellow flowers thrive in the absence of the plants that cover the rest of the canyon in a golden palette. To the southwest, a rope ladder hangs down to a large glade, and, to the southeast, an outcropping overlooks the river.

The outcropping does not extend very far from the clearing to the north. With the thorny bushes covering the crevice to the west and a steep dropoff to the east, there isn't much space to move around. To the south, after a long drop, a grassy platform with a ladder leads out of the canyon.

An old wooden bridge leading west connects to another raised glade. Far below a river flows through the sandstone canyon, easily carving its path, creating pedestals of vegetation. Bright golden leaves cover the canyon in a spectrum of amber hues. A rope ladder leads down to a lower clearing to the south.

Large golden bushes cover the landscape and paint the canyon hues of amber. Covered with crabgrass and a few simple plants, a wide clearing is nestled against two short cliffs. A deep crevice runs between the cliffs which eventually converge and form a terrace. Swaying slightly in the wind, a rope ladder to the northeast leads up to the top of the two cliffs. Far to the south, smoke rises from the chimneys of a small village.

To the northwest, a grassy slope leads up to an old wooden bridge which offers a means to cross the river. A small flowering bush grows beside a craggy boulder and near it rests an empty chest, long forgotten. Far below, a raging river wages war on the sandstone walls of the canyon.

Rugged bushes tower above and their golden canopies blanket the raised clearing in a cool shade. A thin wall of branches acts as a natural barrier to the dropoff on the west and north sides of the platform. An old, empty chest lies abandoned near the edge of the platform. A rocky outcropping extends to the south and an old wooden bridge can be seen off to the east.

To the north stands the Cathedral. As churches go, this one's pretty big. Stained glass windows decorate the front and small flowers line the path to the door. A small forest surrounds the area, but a break in the trees allows passage. To the far east, the Guardia Castle is visible.

This is the weapon and armor shop. Behind the counter are many weapons ready to be sold, of several different types. There are helmets and other defensive gear hung up on racks also ready to be sold. A small forge burns behind an anvil.

You are standing on a dusty path leading to the town. The mist is a bit thicker here and the trees make it harder to see. Northeast of there is a forest. To the south you see the outskirts of the town.

At this place, the paths from the Guardia Cathedral, Zenan Bridge, and Guardia Castle all meet. Zenan Bridge, from the south, leads to the southern continent. The cathedral is to the west of here and provides various holy ceremonies, such as a wedding or a funeral. To the far east, Guardia Castle sits as the ruling place of the continent.
You are standing in the southern part of town. Here you see a sign on the side of the street. There are two buildings standing here, each of them has a sign over the door.

You are standing in the Truce inn. There is a small table in the middle of the room with a couple of chairs around it. At the counter you see a bar tender which is also the inn keeper. Around the table people are sitting enjoying their drinks.

This part of the dusty path leading westward from the medieval town of Truce is surrounded by a small forest to the south and a somewhat larger forest to the north. A large castle seems to be in the northern forest, but there is no clear way to get there. The path continues to the east and west.

To avoid going through the lake, the dusty path has curved around the southeast side of it. This was done to keep the general populace going from the bridge (to the southwest) to the town or castle (to the northeast) drier than if they had to walk through the pond, thus keeping them happy and causing them not to riot.

You are standing in the center of Truce. This seems to be the most well kept part of town. As you look around you see an intersection of roads. To the north there is a general store. To the south there is a weapon/armour shop and an inn.

The path here bends, leading east and south. There is a lake to the west, full of sparkling water. There is also a way into the forest to the north, but the way it appears, it does not seem to be a way to Guardia Castle. Speaking of the castle, it is beyond a large collection of trees, to the northeast.

You are standing in the northern part of town. Here you see a sign hanging on the doorway. There is another house in bad shape across the street. You wonder if the sign means this is a shop of some sort.

You are standing on a dusty path. Truce canyon is to the north, while a village stands to the south. There is a mist in the air and its somewhat dark outside. You see an old sign on the side of the road.

You are standing in the western part of town. To the east you see the town square and to the west there is a road extending out of town and onto the forests of the northern continent. Here you see a sign on the side of the road, it seems to be important.

You are standing in the east end of town. There are people walking about in the streets doing their daily chores. To the west is the town square and in all directions there are alleys with small houses.

While there isn't much to see here, it appears that there is now a path available through the large forest to the north, which is the only thing seperating the castle inside from the rest of the world. To the west, there seems to be a lake in the distance, while the town of Truce is visible to the east.

You are standing in the general store of Truce. Here you see a counter and a salesman is standing there waiting to help you. Behind the counter there are various items for sale with many prices that don't seem to be too expensive.

You are standing on the outskirts of town. The mist has cleared up a bit and you can see clearly again since there are no trees. You can see a couple of shops here in this old town and a few weather beaten houses by the shore.

High, vaulted ceilings meet overhead here in the middle of the cathedral over an isle between rows of pews. The whole area still seems strangely small compared to the massive appearance of the building when it is viewed from outside. Three nuns are sitting in the pews, and the last one is now grinning by the organ.

The floor of the hallway is covered with a smattering of the bones and carcasses of many animals and people. Some are old, but other bones look fresher. Stairs lead back down towards the entrance, leaving the hallway as the only way to go without heading towards the main cathedral.

The sounds of feeding and the muttering of gutteral voices in a strange language fill the room, their agitation rising as whatever poor fool served as their last meal ran out of flesh. Bones are piled on top of each other, some of them with bits of muscle and skin still clinging to them. Anyone who lingers here runs the chance of becoming yet another corpse!

rooms.name: The Northern End of the Hallway

userData.LongDescription: The end of the hallway finally appears, terminating in a door that dominates the northern wall. There are candles on the walls, providing limited light as they flicker in the damp air, threatening to go out. The door handle is stained with blood from many other travellers who had evidently not fared well thus far.

This room is sparse, lacking the large numbers of creatures and bones found elsewhere. Many bats hang above, clinging to the dim ceiling, most of them sleeping soundly. A door just to the east leads on, while the room continues to the south.

The huge gothic-style door opens onto a strange chamber. The final room of the Cathedral is lit by sunlight that is blinding after so long in the overwhelming darkness. Queen Leene of Guardia is being held captive near the rear wall. The corpses of those who have tried to rescue her before litter the room.

This room seems to be a dead end. Pale light flows in from a stained-glass window high in the wall, revealing that the room is bare of decorations and anything else. Strange chants are coming from the eastern wall, though it appears to be solid. Then again, when is anything in this place ever what it seems?

The floor of the stairway landing is covered in puddles of blood, though the dark liquid is probably of no more use to its original owner. The cool stone of the eastern stairway looks far more inviting than the bloody stairs that lead further away from freedom and deeper into this maze.

The hallway turns here, with one leg heading east and the other, north. This corner is steeped in shadows, with only a few flickering candles to provide any light at all. The bloody trail comes from the east and proceeds north, deeper into the cathedral's hidden chambers.

A large organ stands at the end of the cathedral, its pipes reaching towards the ceiling. Looking back over the room, it is evident that this place looks much larger from the outside. Something is glinting softly in the dust on the ground, and from it to the organ, a trail of blood disappears into the wall.

The stone stairs and high ceiling cause sound to carry in an uncomfortably loud manner, as if this place wasn't already spooky enough. The deep darkness hardly serves to muffle the sounds of footsteps, but it does provide the monsters that dwell here with the perfect place from which to launch an ambush.

Rising above is the Truce Cathedral. The building is nothing short of massive, towering up against the sky in a beautiful layout of stone and stained glass. The cathedral has a strange aura emanating from it, as if something about this place is not quite right.

Several high-pitched squeals sound overhead - perhaps more hostile bats. Yet more corpses decorate the corners of the room with their gruesome grace. Doors to the west and south lead out of the profane final resting place of these poor people.

In the middle of the bloody hallway, a cluster of skulls have come to rest against the walls. A rivulet of blood flows between them. The blood is definitely coming from the under the door to the north. By contrast, the southern path looks much more inviting.

Two doors are now visible, but just barely. It is very dark, as the room is lit only by a torch on its last few minutes of burning. The torch gutters and flares, causing shadows to jump and weave on the floor and walls. From beyond the door comes what sound like human voices, but it could be a trap.

This darkened hallway terminates suddenly at a door clean of any blood. Though there are no monsters here, the sound of snarling and chanting slips out from behind the door. Perhaps this is some kind of place of worship for the monsters. To the west, the hallway continues.

The path splits here in three directions. Just to the north is a door, around which the stairway parts to both the west and east. A staircase also leads down to the south. The sound of snarling from inside the door reverberates through the wood of the door, an unintentional warning to the wary traveller.

The lack of light in this room makes distinguishing between shadow and reality increasingly difficult. A few near-burnt-out candles flicker dangerously, casting jerky shadows on the wall. Some of the shadows' movements go against the natural movement of the shadows of the candle, and noises that sound oddly like eating emanate from the darkness.

From the vantage point of this staircase, much is visible.  Down to the west is a hallway, leading deeper into the cathedral. Even further to the west is another platform about the height of a human adult, as well as a staircase by which the platform can be reached.  Just to the east is a doorway, and to the north, the edge of another door can be seen.

The only light in this northern end of the hallway comes from behind a closed door to the north. The door is very near, just a few feet farther north. To the south, the hallway plunges into complete darkness.

The door leads into a small prison cell. A straw mat and some water are all the comforts that are offered to those imprisoned here. The inside is damp and dirty, conditions that would leave a prisoner downright miserable. Perhaps some clue as to the evil in this dank place can be gained here.

Light flickers through a doorway in the north, adding a bit of illumination to this otherwise almost pitch-black place. The sound of bats flapping their wings and squeaking comes from up above, filling the room with sound. A door to the south provides an exit, and the room continues north.

There is very little in this small, dusty room. Pale light filters in through a window, though it is dimmed by the mold-clouded, aged glass it must penetrate. A small table stands in the middle of the room, the only furnishing in sight.

The long hallway runs north and south. The light from the door to the north leaks out into the hallway, but it can not penetrate the darkness of the southern end. The fresh corpse of a citizen is lying on the ground near the door. Even in the dim light, the corpse looks fairly well-mangled.

There are no enemies by this staircase, but the fact that they have passed through here recently is evidenced by the blood trail that continues from the south to the east.  At the top of the staircase are some rooms, shrouded in more darkness. To east is a hallway, and beyond that is yet another staircase. South leads to a turn in the hallway.

This room is almost pitch black, save the light from an exit to the north. Sounds that just might be from monsters fill the darkness, but the shadows are too dim and confused to give any indication of exactly how many might be present at any time. A door to the south is rimmed with light.

The massive statue rises up in the back of the room, behind a table. Brilliant light shines in from many stained glass windows, as if this was a shrine to their God. Something odd and lumpy is laying on the table, for which a purpose has yet to be determined.

The only thing here is a staircase leading up. The path opens up at the top, allowing a small door to open off of a platform.  Though there is very little light at the base of the staircase, it is fairly bright farther up. A door to the south provides access to a long hallway.

At the northern end of the very long hallway is a heavy gothic door. Beyond it is whatever is killing so many creatures and causing the flow of blood. The smell of bodies is very strong, and the corpse of a Guardia knight has been carelessly discarded in the corner of the room.

Here begins the long, final hallway through the Cathedral. The hallway has become the final resting place of many unwary explorers. A rivulet of blood runs along the floor, dripping down from the northern end of the hallway. Far in the distance is a door that seems to be the source of the stream.

The passages seem to multiply as more ways open up in this dark and gloomy place. To the west is a long hall, leading off into darkness like every other passageway found in here. To the north is a stairway, clawing its way up off of the dusty, dark floor. South leads towards the organ room of the cathedral. Bones lie scattered over the ground.

In this room, there is a Hench, Nagaette, and Diablo.  They don't attack for some reason.  One says to you, 'You don't have to wear that human disguise in here.'  You realize they won't attack, and to not blow your cover, you won't either.

This area inside the cathedral is a worship chamber with rows upon rows of wooden pews. This room appears to be the entire structure, as no doors are visible, but it is much smaller that it appeared from the outside. Despite the room's small size, it could fit a fairly large congregation. However, most of the pews are empty, with only four nuns in attendance.

The hallway runs north and south and at this point, aside from the bloody floor, it is not quite so gruesome. Of course, there is the pile of bones to the west, but at least they are fairl unidentifiable. Some of the blood seems to be coming from the pile, but most of it flows south from the door to the north.

The door in the wall here seems to continue the trend of leading deeper in the Cathedral and closer to some unknown danger. There are no monsters here, but several primitive sounds can be heard from beyond the door. Aside from the ominous door, there is a passage running east and west from this point.

On the floor of the stairway landing are drops of blood, still wet from when their owner shed them. The cool stone of the western stairway looks far more inviting than the bloody stairs that lead further away from freedom and deeper into this maze.

This is the start of a long hall leading to more secret rooms deeper in the hidden section of the cathedral. Stairs to the east and west lead to other parts of the area. Many bones, shoved out of the way against the walls, lie in the hall. The trail of blood ends to the north in a giant pool.

There is a giant puddle of blood in the center of the room, and monsters have tracked the blood from the puddle to the door to the north.  The dim light from this room does not do much to penetrate the darkness of the northern one. The smell of blood hangs in the air sickeningly.

This hidden room is fairly small, but it is not empty. Though there are no bones on the floor, there is a table to the north. Behind the table is a statue... the same one the Imps chanted to in 1000 AD, in Medina Village!

The dimly lit, damp, dark hallway runs east to west. The deeply shadowed corners are the perfect hiding places for monsters. The shadows cling to the walls, leaving the middle of the hallway faintly visible. More fresh blood glistens on the floor in a trail that leads off to the west.

Darkness covers this hidden chamber behind the organ. The sound of snickering echoes from deeper within the cathedral's bowels, bringing to mind frightening speculation about what lurks there. The blood trail continues to the east, gleaming wetly in the dim light. A small button protrudes from a panel in the southern wall.

The long hallway runs from a well-lit area to its other end, where a doorway hides in shadows. The door gets closer as the light begins to fade, and just before the door is the end of the blood trail. A pool of blood spreads out over the width of the entire hallway, a gruesome sight.

The houses and shops of Potos surround you here, at the center of town.  Nearby is a humble equipment shop, selling weapons and armor to travelers.  A huge apple tree towers above you to the south, and you can see a hole in the ground southeast of where you stand.  A large house sits on a low hill to the northeast, and a path leads southwest to what appears to be a shop.

The Potos Village Elder's home, easily the largest building in Potos, sits on a raised foundation just to the north, about two feet off the ground.  A large hole in the ground is visible to the south, with small piles of dirt surrounding it.  The center of town is also visible to the southwest.

rooms.name: A small store in Potos Village

userData.LongDescription: This shop is fairly well lit.  An old man sits behind the counter, reading a book of some sort.  Various pieces of equipment are mounted on the walls of this shop.  A sign sits on the counter.

The Potos Village Inn stands nearby.  Right next to it, there is a large sign with the letters 'INN' on it.  To the north, a large sign with a picture of a flask on it is visible, as is a large apple tree to the northeast.

The path continues south, leading out of the village to the southern forests.  The Elder's house stands majestically above all the other buildings of Potos to the north, and the village's center is visible to the northwest.  Right next to you is a hole in the ground, surrounded by small piles of dirt.

This house is well lit and much more decorated than the others in Potos.  A fire burns in the corner fireplace, and there is a candle burning on a table to the left of the entrance.  In another corner, a staircase leads down.

A dim light fills this room.  This house is quite simply furnished, with only one room.  A bed is against one wall, and there is a rocking chair not far from the bed.  The place is well kept and fairly clean.

The inn is very warm and well-lit inside.  A man behind the counter is waiting to rent you a room for the night.  Not far from him, there is a fire softly crackling in the fireplace, providing the warmth to this room.  A sign hangs behind the innkeeper.

This shop is fairly well lit.  An old man sits behind the counter, reading a book of some sort.  A glass case on top the counter shows the medicines the shop carries.  A sign sits next to the glass case.

Away from the forest surrounding Potos village, a huge apple tree, heavily laden with apples, provides shade around you.  To the west, a large sign with the letters 'INN' on it is visible.  The center of town is north of the tree.

This deep hole in the ground appears to be the lair of some sort of monster.  The bones of some unidentifiable animals are strewn about the ground here.  The light is very dim, and it is very stuffy here.  The hollowed-out area at the bottom of the hole isn't big, but there's enough room to fight.  It's probably possible to scale the side of the hole to get back up to the town.
Except for the plain wooden crates and barrels that line the walls of this room, it is quite bare.  The room is stuffy and smelly.  A stairway leads back up to the Elder's house.

Nearby, an item shop sells potions and other, similar needs to travelers.  You can see a large sign labeled 'INN' south of here. Northeast, the village continues to its center, and the way to the Rabite Fields is visible to the north.

A light breeze blows in from the rabite fields to the west.  A row of trees helps define that this is the western entrance of Potos Village.  Not far from here is a humble looking house.  Paths of dirt lead south and southeast from here.  A small sign has been thrust down into the dirt of the path.
The lands race below as Flammie darts across the sky, taking adventurers to their destinations. Flammie is a friendly dragon, and one can say hi to get acquainted with him.

This is a small path between some trees south of Potos village.  To the east you can spot another trail heading off in that direction, but to the south the main trail out of town continues.  There are wild pink flowers growing here, blowing in the breeze.

A makeshift wooden bridge consisting of two long planks of wood has been placed over a ditch.  At the bottom of the ditch is a stream trickling gently from the north.  The trees around this part of the trail are thinning, none standing as tall as the high trees visible off to the east.

The path continues eastward, and the plants here are more numerous than they are to the west or south.  The limbs from trees reach across the narrow path, and it's difficult to walk through without either being scratched by them or ducking very low.

This is a fork in the road with a trio of small signs directing travelers.  The southern road apparently goes south to Pandora, the northwestern road heads to the Water Palace and the eastern road is the way to Potos.  The path is surrounded by trees here, providing a perfect place for small monsters to hide.

A small little man stands at the base of a staircase. He waves at you. Atop the staircase is a giant cannon. This cannon is used for transporting daring adventurers about the lands of Secret of Mana. To the west lays a large path through the forests south of Potos. The cannon man points at a sign.

You are at the city gates of Potos village.  To the north and west of you is the village, but to the south lies great plains and forests that lie in between the towns.  To the south you can see a path between the trees with small animals running around.

Young, short trees have started growing out into the middle of the path, though they're small enough to walk around or even step over.  At the trunks of the taller trees surrounding the path to the north and south, small creatures can be heard hiding in the woods.
The path continues along a hillside.  The hill climbs up to the north, a bit too steep to walk up safely.  The trees tower above you atop the hill, casting shadows everywhere.

You stand in front of a quaint little house that stands alone in the middle of the forest.  You notice an Inn sign of the front as well as a shop sign.  The place is neatly kept with all the bushes neatly trimmed and kept.  You see a sign above the door.

A shallow stream of water, flowing from the north, crosses the path once to the north and then again here.  Though there's a plank helping travelers to step across the crossing to the north, this part of the stream must simply be walked across.  Fortunately, it's less than an inch deep, and there's a shallow slope leading down to it that can be easily traversed from either side.

The grassy path curves to the west slightly as it nears the Water Palace.  Trees line either side of the path, except for where a waterway lines the northern edge.  The palace itself can be seen from here, and its beauty outshines anything else in the area.  A sign sits close to the waterway.

You stand before a small creek on a path south of Potos village.  There is a bridge over the creek leading to a field in the south, and it's easy to tell that the path makes a turn to the west ahead past the bridge.  The sun is shining down on the grass on this beautiful day, making it perfect for a journey.

This is the home of the worldly cat, Neko.  He is here to aid adventurers in their journeys through this world, and though he moves around at times, he can always be found here.  Neko has a variety of items to sell, and also has beds made on which you could spend the night.

The water is shallow here, and can easily be walked through.  The surface slightly shimmers because of the wind, and some lily pads float patiently around.  Along the outer edge of the waterway, grass and flowers grow up the bank of the water.  The Water Palace is directly to the northwest.

From this distance, some of the details of the palace to the north can be made out.  Four waterfalls cascade endlessly from the palace's stone roof, down the front walls of the building.  There is a small trail leading through the trees off to the west toward a cottage.

This is a small field south of Potos, near a bridge that extends over a bubbling creek.  There are many small animals in the area, though most of them disappear into the foliage when they hear footsteps.  The path turns west here, and there appears to be a fork in the road in that direction.  There is a sign here as well.

The tall grass, nearly shoulder height, makes it a bit difficult to pass through this narrower part of the path.  A small pond - more of a puddle, really - has a few lilypads growing in it.  Coming from the bushes are the sounds of small animals, scurrying through the high grass.

rooms.name: A Portal at the Water Palace

userData.LongDescription: An ancient portal surrounded on three sides by crumbling pillars stands in the middle of the peninsula.  The peninsula is mostly covered in grass, and is surrounded by shallow water.  There is evidence of an old rock path that once lead up to the portal.  The Water Palace looms close by to the north, offering protection even from a distance.
The trail continues between the dense trees.  To the south, a brick building can be made out through the foliage, but the only way to get there is to follow the trail around to the east.

The road south is cleared out and lined with marker stones, leading into the town of Pandora.  Two rows of flat stones surround the trail, preventing plants from growing out onto this section of the path.
The grass is waist-high in this bend in the trail.  A tiny amount of water trickling down from the hillside has collected in a small pond.

The path twists and turns, and between the dense trees, a small opening can just barely be made out.  A narrow trail between the trees seems to lead into a secluded area, but without venturing in, it's impossible to tell what lies beyond.

Thick patches of grass grow along the path, even though it must be well trodden.  A small stream lines the southeast side of the path, which runs into the forest to the east.  A rock cliff lines the northwest side of the path, almost making the place seem like a small valley.  The Water Palace can be seen somewhat close by to the north.

This is a large field where the path widens, with a big tree in the middle of it.  To the west there is a small bridge with a small strip of land going up the other side.  To the southeast there is the road back to Potos and Pandora.

You are on a narrow strip of land on the west side of the creek.  There are some more monsters here as well, to contend with your travels.  To the north you can spot a small path lined with stones leading to the west, and further to the north you can make out a huge palace.

rooms.name: In Front of the Water Palace

userData.LongDescription: The path up to the Water Palace leads down into the shallow water that goes around the large building.  The water is clear and looks refreshing, and the smell is just as nice.  The waterway to the west is blocked by some rocks, but the way east around the palace is open.  The great doors of the palace make an impressive image.

There is a small, single bed in the far wall of this room, and furnishings are limited. This room looks like it might be a spare room of sorts, possibly a guest room. The staircase leads back down to the main room of this house.

There is a table in the middle of this room, set perfectly with very fine china. It appears almost too perfect, undisturbed. There are many colors in this room, yet there is an aura of depression throughout it. On the wall is a child's painting of their family, but they have only blank expressions, like many people in the town.

This house is made up of two rooms, separated by a doorway. This room appears to be a dining room, as there is a table in the middle of the room, and from the west, an aroma drifts that smells like chicken. These windows are framed with purple drapes, and there are plants hanging from either side.

The southern gate swings slowly on its hinges while to the south, more fields are visible, though the trees look slightly denser than before.  It would probably be best just to move along, and not bother the ghost-like people of this city.

You can buy an assortment of items here, from potions to hi-ethers. There is a helpful-looking sign right here with some words written on it. The merchant who works here is trying his hardest to get you to buy his products, waving his hands around and pointing to everything.

Setting next to the house here, two pots of buttercups stand.  To the east, a little island covered in trees, with many people wandering around pointlessly.  To the west of this house an inn comes into view.

This room, also as bland as the one downstairs, has very few things in it. There is a bed off to the corner which has a layer of dust over it, and there is a half-melted candle in the middle of the room. The wooden floor creaks with each step, but the only way to go is down the stairs.

A road to the side leads off to the item shop.  Two large rose bushes are growing up to the side of the building, and someone has very nicely planted yellow tulips.  Passing through the streets, some very odd stares are given, and the people here seem almost ghost-like.  To the south lies the inn of the town.

This area south of Pandora is fairly small. There is an impassible forest to the west and south, and rocks scattered about to the north. It's possible to see the gates for the village of Pandora to the north, and even farther into the distance, Pandora Castle. The path leads east towards a large ruins.

There is very little light being cast into this room, and there is a feeling of mystery as well. There are a few beds lined up against the wall, perfectly made, but with layers of dust upon them, as if no one has used them in months. The only way to go is to go east, back into the main room of this Pandora house.
This looks like a warm place to stay for the night.  There are

A large white house, made in perfect symmetry has been built here.  It is a friendly looking two storied building, with white washed walls.  There are two clay pots on the side of the house, and a nice little brick chimney.  To the south a path leads to another house, and over a canal.  To the east, the northeastern gate can be seen, but is blocked off by a guard.

Large and luminous, a large house stands here.  This house has pretty flowers in its garden, alternating colors, pink and yellow.  On the side of the house, there is a large wooden waterwheel, which turns quite slowly.  There is no noise, aside from the trickle of water.

These are the gates to the city of Pandora.  Canals span across the city, the light reflecting off of them.  There is a slight breeze which creates little ripples across the clear, blue waters of the canals.  The ground is covered with a lush soft grass, but something isn't quite right.

This house appears to be extremely plain, stripped of any furnishings. The only things of interest are the pictures on the wall. Each one is different, ranging from a little child's drawing, to a large oil painting on canvas, but there's something not quite right about them. Something stands out, and seems like it shouldn't be there.

The ruins to the north look even gloomier than they did from near Pandora. Black walls and black statues complete the dark picture. There's even one of the statues that can be seen inside the ruins here as well. The forest still stops any movement to anywhere but Pandora and the ruins, and to the west is the way to Pandora.

There is a fire burning merrily in the wood stove, and three clay pots on the window sill, each labeled with a different spice. Wood logs line the edge of the room, ready to be cast into the fiery stove. Someone has prepared some soup in the pot here, and the aroma is drifting through the door to the east.

A large home stands here, casting a large shadow around it.  The white house has ivy beginning to grow up the sides, and some rather large bushes.  Through a window, a man and a woman are visible and many orange flowers.  To the north, a small armory is in view, and to the west is the southern gate.

This is a rather small shop, but it has some things on display to buy. The merchant across the counter points you to a sign to your right, where something is written. There is also a small armor rack in the southwest corner of this building.

This is a larger island, surrounded by wooden bridges. There is an armory here, it is a rather small building, cube in shape with slanted roofs and a small sign, nailed to the wall. To the north, there is the northeastern gate of Pandora, but it looks as if it were blocked. To the south, there is the largest house in the city, surrounded by bushes and ivy.

This gate has been opened for the public to enter the castle. There is an armory to the south, over a clear blue canal.  To the south, and to the north are more fields, similar to the ones off of the northern gate. The sun shines at an angle here, casting shadows that only add to the mysterious feel of this town.

This house in Pandora is filled with the scent of cinnamon and potpourri. Agains the northern wall there are two beds, and a table is set by the beds. There is also the scent of food coming from somewhere in the house, as the people here are probably making their dinner. There is a staircase leading up to the second level of this house, and a doorway leading out to Pandora.

Standing tall, the front of a white-washed building can be seen, which can easily be identified as an inn, due to the large wooden sign.  There are two chimneys on either side of the roof, with smoke billowing out of each.  There seems to be a lack of song birds, leaving the eerie sound of water in the canals.  To the west is an exit out of Pandora, where it's possible to travel on to Kippo Village and Gaia's Navel.

This house appears to be very...unique. There is a pink checkered carpet running along the floor, and orange flowers everywhere, causing a clash of colors. The bright green shutters on the window adds to the complete crappiness of this room, and there is a table in the middle of this room.

The hallway is lit up by ensconsed torches on the dusty brick walls. There is an oak door that leads to the north, and a remodelled staircase will lead back to the middle level of the castle. The flooring looks dull and well trodden, making it almost as colorless as the walls.

This piece of land is devoid of the plants and grasses commonly found in the soil around here. The area is well lit by the sun, making it the only area not lost in the shadow of the great wall. A large stairwell is to the north, complete with a brass banister, leading up atop the outer wall. Heading west will lead to the center of the courtyard.

The long hallway of the castle comes to an end, leading to a wooden door on the north wall. A pink carpet stretches out, covering the middle of the hallway, and a few of the flags of Pandora are hanging up. A lone shining torch tries in vain to illuminate the mostly dark scene. A portrait of the Queen of Pandora hangs on the west wall, overlooking the entire hallway.

The grass meets up with a corner of the silver-bricked castle, where there are lots of unruly weeds. Along the castle wall to the north, there is a wide-open window that leads into a bathroom. The dirt path leading to the entrance of the castle is to the west.

A small turret grants a little standing room on the heavily-traversed path atop the castle's defensive outer wall.  Beneath the turret, a narrow opening in the sleek stone wall allows archers to shoot from a perfect angle.  The ground outside the castle, the courtyard within the walls, even the bridge and wooden gate separating castle from town are all visible from here.  The wall continues to the north and east.

The throne room stretches out in every direction a great length. The floor is draped in a dark purple carpet, covering extremely wide steps that lead ever so slightly upward. The walls are adorned with portraits of previous kings and queens adorned in royal vestments. There are several grand looking windows between the portraits, as well as several fancy candle-lit chandeliers hanging from the ceiling by long golden chains. The seats of sovereignty are visible further to the north.

There is a large rectangular oak table in the center of the room, accompanied by several stiff oak chairs. A potted plant sits idly in a corner of the room, next to a large, purple cushioned sofa. A picture of the King of Pandora hangs on the ancient gray wall. Between a venerable set of swords and a suit of armor hanging on the wall, a small window lets light in, leaving a small outline of brightness on the table.

Deep down in the basement of the castle, the air becomes rather cold. The walls are barren, old, and dusty, as well as the unkept floor. Treasure chests take up a lot of the space, stacked on top of each other, with cascades of cobwebs gliding down from the tops of the piles. Wimpy torches by the entrance of the room are not helping light the room up one bit.

This segment of the hallway is marked by the giant oak double doors that are accompanied by two of the gray, bow-tie patterned flags of Pandora. Carvings on the doors match the pattern on the flags, and large, shining brass handles are placed in the center of them. Torches on the southern wall burn brightly. The hallway continues to the west, where it ends, and to the east, back toward the middle level of the castle.

This turret is an excellent vantage point for the surrounding area; the inner courtyard is entirely visible, and the hardy grasses in front of the castle are mere feet away. To the east, the land below is lush with wild vegetation.  The wall extends northward, to a stairwell, and far to the west, around the castle's perimeter.

The actual seats of sovereignty for the king and queen of Pandora are situated against the north wall. The floor goes slightly upward in the form of wide steps and has been covered by a dark purple carpet rug. Large, candle-lit crystal chandeliers hang from the ceiling and large windows on the side walls light up the entire chamber. All along the walls are portraits of the previous Kings and Queens of Pandora. There is an exit to the west, marked by a large oak door.

There is a large lantern in this room on the north wall. The torch is brilliant against the gray stone floor, and silver walls, so that only one corner of the room is left in shadow. On the east wall, there is a painting of a rather large fish in human's clothing, depicted in a meditative pose with an erupting volcano in the background. The only exit is back down the hall to the west.

Beds are set through the room, with narrow paths between the beds that are just wide enough for an endtable. At the foot of each bed is a suit of armor.  Numerous small touches, attempts to make the room a little homier, stand out: a brilliant green plant stands tall next to one unmade bed, a bookcase stands in a corner.  A clock on the northern wall tick-tocks patiently.  The only exit is the wooden door that leads back out into the courtyard.

Deep down in the basement of the castle, the air becomes rather cold. The walls are barren, old, and dusty, as well as the unkept floor. Treasure chests take up a lot of the space, stacked on top of each other, with cascades of cobwebs gliding down from the tops of the piles. Wimpy torches by the entrance of the room are not helping light the room up one bit.

The grass grows fully inside the courtyard, completely covering the ground, where a few flowers have grown.  A small rock rests in the shadow of a wide stairwell, leading up atop the castle wall. Next to the rock is a small wooden door, and the open courtard stretches eastward, back toward the grand columns of the castle's main entrance.

A pair of brass railings herald the eastern end of the long walkway, stretching across the top of the castle's outer wall. At the path's corner stands a tall tower, a part of the castle's interior building, with a pair of barred windows facing the walkway. Birds' nests have been constructed atop the edge of the tower's roof. A stairway leads back into the comfortable safety of the inner courtyard, while the tiled path leads south.

The relatively small room is cluttered with hanging utensils and cookware on the walls. A fireplace burns brightly, right next to a stove and a pile of firewood in the corner of the room. There is a large counter with cutting boards, ingredients, and dishes stowed away in the open cupboards underneath. The floor has been cleaned and shined to the point where it is rather slippery.

This long hallway runs east and west, leading deeper into the castle. A pair of open lanterns are built high into the wall.  The flames keep the hall well-lit, and illuminate an ornate flag. To the east, the hallway appears to end, while the western path bends around a corner. The castle's entrance lies southward, under the giant arch.

Massive walls seem to dwarf the small courtyard here; to the south lies the great outer wall that protects the castle from invaders. Immediately in front of them, two massive pillars stand on each side of a large, oak door, leading into the castle.  The courtyard is a narrow strip of land that stretches between the walls. The worn soil indicates that most people do not bother to explore it.

The stone bridge to the south leads to and from the magnificent Pandora Castle. Large, silver-colored stone composes the grand, intricate walls of the castle to the north. There is a small, dirt path that leads into the castle. A bright blue moat peacefully splashes underneath the stone bridge.

A golden rail leads up to a small opening at the top of the stairwell. The courtyard in all its shadiness is visible over the railing.  To the south, a path has been carefully constructed along the top of the castle's outer wall.  Outside the castle, the moat is the only thing visible.  The stairwell leads back down into the castle's courtyard.

The window on the west wall lets sunlight in and brightens up the entire hallway. Outside the window, the moat that surrounds the castle and the city of Pandora itself are visible. Further off in the distance, a large castle enshrouded in a light mist can also be seen. The walls are made of old gray bricks, and the floors are tiled with a dull mahogany colored tesselation.

This part of the castle looks much newer than the rest, indicated by shiny silver bricks and clean mahogany tiling on the floor. The south wall seems to be made up of both old bricks and new bricks mixed together. There is a stone staircase covered in a pink carpet with thick brass railings that leads down and further east.

The hallway comes to a corner, with a torch illuminating the small passageways to the east and south. The walkway to the east leads to the entrance of the castle, and to the south, the hall opens into a sitting area.  There are some vases on the west wall that contain some of the wildflowers from outside, as well.

The room opens up into a comfortable looking lounge, complete with a fireplace, a few chocolate brown leather sofas, and a self-serve bar. The floor is covered with a warm, rose colored rug and the ceiling is adorned with a glistening crystal chandelier. There is a wooden staircase that leads to the middle level of the castle, and the north exit heads toward the entrance to the castle.

This entrance hall is fairly long, with numerous small, symmetrical nooks that have been built into the hall's design.  To the north lies another intimidating arch, beyond which lies a hall stretching in other directions. The hallway is particularly dark as there are not any lanterns nearby. The entrance to the castle and its massive doors is southward.

The grass meets up with a corner of the silver-bricked castle, where bright yellow flowers bloom. The moat of water is in plain sight here, its still waters reflecting the color of the sky. The dirt path leading to the entrance of the castle is to the east.

This turret is an excellent vantage point for the surrounding area; the inner courtyard is entirely visible, and the hardy grasses in front of the castle are mere feet away. To the east, the land below is lush with wild vegetation.  The wall extends northward, to a stairwell, and far to the west, around the castle's perimeter.

The Trann Dome looks much like everything else on this barren planet, old, metallic, and rusty.  The rusty, metallic walls are extended slightly away from the platform below.  A small gap full of junk metal stands between the platform and the walls.  A rather misshapen arch leads the way deeper into the Trann Dome.  The floor has many dents and screatches in it, as well as being torn in many places.  The path leads north slightly, where it turns east, going deeper into the dome.  A large door leads the way out of the dome.

The land ends abruptly as it turns from solid ground to sandy beach, and then into the waves of the far-spanning ocean.  The water all around is a sickly red and purple color, and not even a single fish or bird is visible in or on the water.  Across a great channel is another small island, and a few small craters dot the land.  The road is visible from here, leading over towards Trann Dome and also heading back towards the north.  The wind continues unabated here, and lightning flashes as strongly as ever.  With the coast as shallow and short as it is, the only path available is back to the northwest.

This single room is all that is left of the structure known as Bangor Dome.  The room is small and cramped, and is filled with a thick layer of dust and broken bits of metal.  Everything about this place seems to be fashioned from a dull, dark metal, and the building itself seems to have held up decently against the test of time.  A small glowing globe of blue light rests in the middle of the floor, and a large intricately carved door is set into the northern wall.  It is almost completely silent here and there seems to be nothing one can do here.  Two small steps lead down to a runway, and that leads towards an opening to the outside.

The road comes to a junction in this area, leading north and west.  The road is pock-marked with small craters and is heavily lined with cracks.  Trann Dome stands a short distance to the west, while Bangor Dome looms off to the north.  Off the road is dull, sick looking earth, and the ocean is visible off to the south.  There's a small trail leading off to the southeast, off the asphalt road.  The weather continues to beat the land mercilessly, and the wind continues to howl.

rooms.name: Outside Trann Dome on a Broken Highway

userData.LongDescription: The road ends here, just before the entrance to Trann Dome.  The dome is large enough to house dozens of people, though there might not be that many humans left alive in this desolate world.  All around the bleak landscape continues, and the broken road heads off to the east.  The door to the dome itself is open.  Off to the west and south, the large ocean that surrounds this continent can be seen, and the wind continues to blow fiercely.

rooms.name: Outside Lab16 on a Broken Highway

userData.LongDescription: The road ends here before the shattered ruins of a city.  Several wrecked buildings lay here, crumbling and broken beyond all hopes of repair.  Lying in the dirt is a sign with the words 'LAB 16' written on it, and the entrance to the city is still open.  All around the heavy wind continues to blast across the land, but it seems to be blocked by the criss-crossing patterns created by the ruined buildings.  Large craters dot the surface of the land, and some of them have penetrated into Lab 16 itself.  Off the coast to the east, dark water laps against the shore, and visibility beyond the coastline is extremely poor.  Dark clouds still hang in the sky, blocking sunlight while providing brief flashes of lightning.  The road leads back towards Bangor Dome, which looms silently in the distance.

rooms.name: Outside Bangor Dome on a Broken Highway

userData.LongDescription: Bangor Dome is accessible from here, as it stands just north of this devastated highway.  Running from the northeast to the southwest in an L shaped pattern is an asphalt road, still faintly lined.  However, there are two huge craters, one larger than the other, that cause a massive break in the road.  In the distance to both the east and west there are large bodies of water, though the water doesn't appear to be conducive to a swim.  There is an extremely strong wind blowing here, which is throwing dirt and debris everywhere.  The entire planet seems to be in pain, and flashes of lightning occassionally fly across the sky.
