There is hardly any sunlight that penetrates the thick smog above and there doesn't appear to be a single living thing making its home here.  Off to the northeast, the road continues towards the remains of what might be a city.  To the southwest, the road winds around Trann Dome.

This area of the dome is quite different from any other section of the dome.  Here, there lies a carpet, though it is old and ragged, it is a carpet nonetheless.  A few old-looking pots lie against the wall, adding a few decorations to the place.  A large machine used for some purpose lies in the northwest corner, against a wall.  A strange door lies to the north.  It has no door handles and has a golden statue of a dragon's head in the center of it.  The path through the Dome stops here, with the only direction available being towards the east.

This is a rather large platform compared to the platforms near the entrance.  It fills up an area that makes the dome feel much more spacious than at some places.  Small pillars of metal rise up from the junk slightly to the south of the platform.  Cracks line the metal in many places, making it hazardous to walk in some places.  A few steps lead down and the platform goes west towards another open space in the dome.  The path travels east back towards the entrance of the dome. A dusty machine stands in the corner.

The highway takes a 90 degree turn here, heading west and south.  Deep cracks line the asphalt, but it has somehow managed to stay in recognizable condition.  Just off to the north are two craters, one of which is far larger than the other.  The road is winding around the back of Trann dome, and the southern path is leading towards its entrance.  The weather conditions here are abysmal, with dark, lightning filled clouds blotting out the sun.  High speed, dust filled winds blow about, constantly picking up and depositing dirt and debris everywhere.  The coastline is visible off to the east, but the water doesn't look overly hospitable to maintaining life.  The western road heads off towards Bangor Dome.

The road winds around Bangor Dome here, leading off towards the ruins of what appears to have been a futuristic city.  There are large craters all around the area, some of which are breaking up the road.  The coastline runs just along the eastern side of road, and dirty, sickly water is lapping up against the shore.  From here, a small island is visible, but it doesn't appear to have anything on it.  Overhead, a dark cloud barrier blocks sunlight, and only occasional flashes of lightning provides any decent light in this blasted world.  A heavy wind, filled with dirt, seems to blow endlessly, covering the planet with random particles.  The road also leads to the west, towards Bangor Dome.

The highway stretches onwards here, approximately half-way between Bangor and Trann Domes.  There is a massive crater just to the west of the road, but it did not impact close enough to disrupt the highway.  The road heads both to the northeast towards Bangor Dome, and to the east towards more open road.  This particular span of land appears to be a peninsula, as water is just faintly visible in all directions, save to the north.  The skyline is just as dull and dour as ever here, and lightning continues to flash in the heavens.  The wind is still as powerful as ever here, and continues to blow dust everywhere.

The inside of the Trann Dome is much smaller than it looks to be from the outside.  The metallic walls are backed away from the platform that people stand on.  Junk, as always, fills the gap between the wall and the platform.  Pipes fill the area of the roof, traveling to various places throughout the dome.  To the south, the exit of Trann Dome can be seen.  A small staircase leads west.

The road leading north exits the ruins of Lab 16 under the guardianship of a trashed traffic signal. Ominously, directly below the traffic signal, is a manhole cover surrounded with drag marks. Piles of debris prevent any means of moving around the manhole cover. The road south leads further into the ruins of Lab 16.

A massive block of concrete, embedded in the dirt, almost completely blocks off the path leading to the south. To the north, the ruins of Lab 16 continue to stretch on. The dirt trail to the west runs between two piles of debris before opening into a small clearing.

Broken asphalt, a ruined fire hydrant, large blocks of buildings, and manhole cover are all that remain of Lab 16. Long gone are the days when the city was a bastion of scientific research, now crumbling piles of debris are all that remain. The large clearing extends to the east, while a path to the north runs through a narrow gap between the mounds of detritus.

The area, framed in by fallen debris, is nearly perfectly square. The smaller pieces of rubble common throughout Lab 16 appear to have been pushed into the larger piles. As a result the  cracked asphalt is much easier to traverse. A rubble pile has collapsed on a small path leading north rendering it unusable, though the road to the east appears safe enough.

The abandoned jumble of metal in the middle of the road was once a car. While some of the damage to the poor machine could be attributed to whatever befell Lab 16, however, the huge bite marks on the bumper are too recent. The pile of debris that forms the northern barrier is made from massive chunks of building.

Ruins of the once-great city wrap around a small portion of road leaving only two paths through the detritus. The cracked asphalt of the road vanishes under the wall of rubble to the east, and to the south. The road is partially cleared to the west for a little ways at least. A narrow dirt trail running next to a huge piece of rubble leads north.

Lab 16 was a vast facility, comprised of a large collection of research labs so expansive it was more akin to a city than a simple facility. Now all that remains are the decimated ruins. Massive broken blocks of concrete litter the area creating a maze of debris. In spite of whatever calamity caused this destruction, or maybe because of it, strange lifeforms appear to call these ruins home.

rooms.name: In the Shadow of a Tower

userData.LongDescription: A tall, derelict water tower overshadows the fractured road, threatening to collapse at any moment. Dark streaks of a suspicious substance lead towards a manhole cover next to a mound of rubble on the southern edge of the road.

Heaping piles of detritus looms over the small bend in the broken road. The precariously balanced blocks of concrete and random pieces of garbage threaten to collapse onto the road at any moment. A narrow path south leads to a more open area, while the road to the east vanishes around a sharp turn.

A heap of debris collapsed over a manhole cover to the south, an indication the ruins of Lab 16 are less than stable. The occasional flicker of movement and the tumbling of stones serve as a constant reminder that a number of monsters call these ruins home. The ruined road continues to the east and west.

The remnants of several buildings have landed around a manhole cover, creating an intersection of sorts. In the middle of the intersection is a manhole cover, seemingly unmarred by the destruction reaped on the city around it, though the claw marks around it are a bit ominous. The twisted shell of a car has been smashed into a rubble pile with a tremendous amount of force.

Fragments of a broken building spiral upwards into in a single daunting tower whose structural integrity is less than impressive. The ruined uneven path, defined by the piles of old Lab 16, swerves sharply west, away from the looming death trap.

The cracked and ruined ground provides awful footing, however the monsters that inhabit the ruined city have adapted to overcome this obstacle. Large blocks of what used to be Lab 16 block off any avenues of exploration except heading back to the west. Another untouched manhole cover is tucked into the southeastern corner.

The asphalt gives way to raw earth in what was once a park of some kind. Twisted playground equipment can be glimpsed sticking out of the mountainous rubble piles surrounding the dirt patch. Footprints from the various creatures that live here track through the dirt to the west and to the south.

The scattered remains of Lab 16 lay abandoned in the bare dirt lot. To the south the lot connects to a road, and to the east is a small pathway between two piles of rubble. A gigantic mutant is resting atop one of the rubble piles taking a nap.

A burned-out, derelict car has been deserted in the middle of the road. The ravaged road stretches out to the west, while an extremely narrow dirt path leads south into a clearing. The ubiquitous piles of rubble frame in this portion of the road, preventing any other direction of travel.

Mountains of rubble, and other detritus, block nearly every direction of exploration. A narrow dirt path to the south, and the shattered remains of a road leading east are the only ways to go. The dirt path trails through a narrow valley of rubble. The roadway is comparatively wide and continues for a considerable distance before disappearing around a corner.

Resting in the middle of the intersection, a rusted out hulk of a truck, basking in the weakly flickering red light of the traffic light. The light is, somehow, still hanging from the pole over the road, and only serves to highlight the irony of the scene. The road goes to the east a short distance before being cut off by another pile of rubble.

The abandoned road underfoot has cracks through it, where the old asphalt has buckled under the weight of time, or perhaps the mutant creatures that make this place home. Through a corridor of trash, a clearing to the north can be seen, while to the east a sizable dirt patch is filled with footprints.

Various drag marks fill the area around the unblemished manhole cover in the center of the path. Clearly, there is something hunting these ruins from the sewers. Another smashed car has been compacted into a rubble pile to the south only confirms this. Over the path north a faltering traffic light flickers periodically.

The narrow corridor, sandwiched between to piles of debris, is the perfect place to stage an ambush. Debris along the broken road through the corridor would hinder any escape attempt. In the middle the road, like a hunters trap, is another manhole cover. At the end of the corridor the road turns to the west.

Short, heart-shaped leaves sprouting from the gaping holes in the asphalt are a surprising dash of color in the grey-washed landscape. Piles of the old Lab 16 surround the open clearing, which continues to the west. A narrow path goes north and disappears around a sharp corner.

The path breaks into three here, leading north, west and south. To the south is a bit of an eerie wide open platform, surrounded by scrap heaps. The path west leads to a mesh platform bridge. The northern path reveals a much more welcome sight, as it leads to the center of the dome, where the inhabitants of the Arris Dome are.

The highway takes another sharp turn here, leading east again. The large dome complex is very near, looming above like a metallic monstrosity. The vast diseased sea lies to the south, bringing about a sickly feeling. The wind is just as strong here, and it might be a good idea to take shelter in the dome.

This room feels and looks much safer than any other place in the dome. There are more steel containers here, and the ground is covered in dusty cloth rugs. Among the clay pots, there is one fairly large in size, filled with soil. This part of the dome seems to be fairly well taken care of, hence the covered platform, as well as the lack of scrap metal. To the west lies a lowered platform with a large row of storage containers, and on a corner stands a large, black pod-shaped machine. The circular pod with the ladder is here, in plain sight.

The highway delves into this wreck of a building complex. Bits of destroyed buildings dot the road, presenting massive problems to the unprepared adventurer. Crushed skyscrapers line the ground here, like spires of death. There are two options here, either to head into the ruined complex known as 'Lab 32' or head back south.

The loopy highway takes yet another turn here, heading north to a destroyed building complex similar to Lab 16. Near the tall mountains here is a small circular dome with a wooden sign just in front of it. Other than the dome and the sea to the south, there isn't much else to see here.

This small part of the dome is rather uninviting and eerie, with the deep mist adding to the intimidation. Deactivated, torn debugger robots are strewn along the path, creating the sense of a recent massacre. The path continues west among the piles of machinery, stopping at a set of stairs that are partially obscured by a heap of scrap.

The path of platforms leads down from here into a narrow area surrounded by scrap. The intimidating pile of scrap and machine wrecks looms near in the lowered area. The mist does well to further add to the sense of uneasiness. Who knows what could be lurking around?

rooms.name: Near the center of the dome

userData.LongDescription: This part of the Arris Dome seems more furnished and conditioned for living. Big, steel containers lie here and there, possibly storing food and other conveniences of life. Little clay pots and jars lie strewn on coarse, dusty, cloth mats, as a way of rationing food supplies. Just to the west is the center of what little activity remains in the Arris Dome.

Past the set of stairs is a fairly small-sized platform, higher than the rest of the metallic heap. Glancing about, it seems some of these machines were old guardian robots of the dome, now destroyed and forgotten. The walkway leans against the western wall, leading to another set of stairs that connect to a sole path of mesh platforms.

The mesh platforms create a crude bridge over the yard of junk piles and odd bits and pieces. There are no railings or safeties on the platforms to prevent unwary adventurers from falling into the abyss below, so caution is a must. Nearby, the denizens of the Arris Dome huddle to keep themselves protected from the harsh weather.

The rusty arch marks the entrance to the fallen Arris Dome, a massive wreck of what once could have been the pinnacle of technology. Old metal platforms and creaky wooden boards line a crude path to a large platform in the middle of the dome. Due to the mist looming around the dome, it is impossible to get a clear view. Perhaps it would be worth it to investigate.

The highway takes a sharp turn south here, oddly. Craters and debris dot the land, making travel unneccesarily harder. Far to the southeast, a large dome complex can be seen, like a neglected, forgotten relic of the past. Massive bodies of water can be seen to the north and to the far south. The highway leads both west and south, leading further to the dome complex, or back to the destroyed building complex.

A quiet corner in the Arris Dome, the silence in this wide open platform is almost tangible. Dried streaks of red line the platform, among torn bits of metal. It seems that there may have been conflict and battle here in the past, but how long ago, no one knows.

rooms.name: A bend in the metal path

userData.LongDescription: The path made out of platforms forms a sharp turn left, eventually leading down to a descent. Near the center of the dome lies a circular pod with a ladder leading down somewhere. Taking a closer look, it seems that this group of people barely pass being human and look more like soulless vegetables. The mist still looms around like an omen, and it beckons for travelers to explore.

This is the southwestern corner of the dome and not a very welcome place either. The mound of machinery still looms high above, cloaked by the ever-present mist. Apart from the junk heap and path, there are thick metal pipes that course through the dome, seeming to lead somewhere. Nearby, metallic stairs lead to higher grounds.

rooms.name: Before the entrance to Arris Dome

userData.LongDescription: The road takes a smaller branch off the main path, leading up to a rusty arch. This must be the entrance to the now fallen Arris Dome. Other than the entrance, there seems to be nothing more here, other than the usual plague of craters and building wrecks. A smaller dome is nested off to the east between mountains.

Cold winds blow through the massive wrecks of buildings. The gloomy ambience of the place shows, with disheveled roads pockmarked with small craters everywhere. Bits and pieces of destroyed buildings lie here and there, creating obstacles to the otherwise linear road. To the north, tall unforested mountains block further passage. The smashed highway leads to the east.

This is a platform hugging the northwestern wall of the dome, holding many storage containers that hold various pieces of weaponry, armor and medicinal supplies, as well as whatever the citizens of Arris could salvage. A metal plaque is fastened to the wall.

This narrow, lowered platform is almost overshadowed by the platform up top. A set of stairs is by the western end, leading back up to the raised platform. To the northern end, a ladder is barely seen through the shadows and mist. The walls are of a terrible pattern, closing in at the middle section, making the platform that much narrower.

A sudden chill shoots down as an actual working fan blows gentle winds down the platform. Square metal plates line the path north, creating one long road. At the end is an isolated platform connected to the mesh through a set of steps, ending at a metal door at the northern wall.

Just down the metal ladder is a small mesh platform with steps leading down to a narrow room. The mist is thicker than usual, limiting vision even further. A small passage leads somewhere in the northern wall, that being the only interesting thing around. A few bits of scrap lie here and there, though not much in comparison to the upper layers of Arris.

Past the metal door is a long, wide platform leading nearly to the back of the room. Metal steps lead to higher ground to the west and east, though the eastern raised mesh platform looks to be a dead end. Fans are embedded on the wall, though probably jammed and nonfunctional. The metal door is to the south, providing a nearby exit.

This small room is where the food and supplies of Arris Dome is stored, though everything seems to have decomposed some time ago. The refrigerator containers are damaged and broken, food spilled out of them. Nothing much of edible value remains here; the people of Arris Dome had been placing hope on something that's failed years ago.

Similar in position to the horizontal beam to the south, this catwalk seems to serve no purpose. A door is here, also damaged and won't budge at all. The platformed floor here is dusty and worn, connected to flimsy railings. The mist is even thicker here, dangerously nearing the point where a blind man would not be at a disadvantage.

This platform of mesh leads a short way to the north, but it ends with the metallic wall. Three fans are attached to the eastern wall here, all broken and useless. Below the mesh platform is a pile of junk, all seeming to be garbage and other forms of broken machinery. The metal steps here lead back to the main platform.

rooms.name: At the end of the mesh path

userData.LongDescription: The mesh platform comes to a halt here at the northern wall, with only the steps providing the further road. The lower platform leads back to the south, eventually stopping at another set of steps and a parallel mesh platform on the other side. A busted fan lies on the northern side of the room, looking lonely and neglected.

The short passage into the northern wall is nearby, giving a small glimpse as to what's on the other side. The mist is still thick and heavy here. A small mound of scrap lies at the end of the path in this narrow room, though it doesn't look too important. There is a metal ladder to the east.

The beam leads to a narrow catwalk going along the northern wall, curving a bit up to the ladder. Railings have been constructed to prevent accidents, though they look rather flimsy. Bodies are still strewn among the catwalk here, with the occasional unfortunate machine inbetween. Two ways to go here, back south to the beam complex or to the east, approaching the northern ladder.

The path leading to the northern ladder takes a turn to the north here. Even more bodies are strewn about here, almost completely clogging up the beam. Among the row of corpses, some destroyed bits of robotic guards can be seen, hinting at some conflict between the humans and the robots had on this beam, some time ago in the past.

A large intersection is here, leading off in four different directions. Each direction looks quite similar, all of them being beams leading in either of the four ways. The northern path is completely adjacent to the ladder on the northern wall from where the intersection is, though there might be some loops in the path after. No different than any other part in the rafters, this place has its share of the grand view of bloody humans and machines in a junkpile.

The square platform serves as a small doormat to the large metal door. A set of metal steps lead to the east, onto a mesh platform that provide a way back to the southern part of the long room. Scraps of metal dot the ground below the platform.

Yet another deformed atrocity known as a molded platform is here, providing footing over the uneven terrain below. The wall to the north comes to an end here, a small path leading north. A set of stairs is to the south, leading to the looping mesh platform. Junk piles are scattered all around below the platform, hiding the true depth and ground of this room. Another platform leads to the west, leading up to a mesh platform that borders the room.

rooms.name: Further up on the mesh platform

userData.LongDescription: Death accurately describes what's going on around this part of the platform. Five dead bodies in different positions are strewn about the room, each messily mauled and torn. The mesh platform suffers, its beauty tainted by the spilt blood of the people. The path leads further north to a turn to the east from here.

The mesh platforms are rather tattered here, connected by small metal platforms and steps. Two dead bodies are here, seeming to try to block the passage. What lies beyond the metal door to the east is anyone's guess, though there's no knowing except for trying it out. The path leads to the east and to the west from here.

The path of beams split in three directions here, leading north, east and south. Below is a clear view of the wreck that happened in the past, a gruesome display of machinery wrecks and human bodies. Looking down would probably not be such a good idea, as it's a long fall down from the beams.

This long path north completely sticks to the western wall of the room, composed of several mesh platforms that are hoisted just over a massive array of scrap heaps. The walls here are metallic and dusty, the occasional broken fan embedded to the wall as a relic of the dome's ventilation systems.

rooms.name: A platform on the northern end

userData.LongDescription: The raised platform here is as gaudy and bad as some other places. Small and large platforms are hacked on together, bolted by pieces of leather and whatever could be found, even scrap bits of metal that are out of shape. It leads to the south and to the west, with a ladder on the side to lead to the lowered ground. Three fans drone by the northern wall.

The mesh platform provides a small route around the wall, though why the wall is here in the first place is anyone's guess. Below the platform is a lot of junk and corpses, both metallic and humanoid. Looks like they were mercilessly swept as garbage underneath the platforms when they died. The fan provides a chill, and the path leads to the east.

rooms.name: At the end of the eastern mesh path

userData.LongDescription: The path of mesh platforms ends at the northern wall, four metal steps lined one after another leading down to a sad, small square platform that almost seems to be a doormat. The large metal door is rather complex in style and shape, though it has one distinctive feature; the metal valve in the center.

A wide platform is past the door, actually made from different metal plates of varying sizes and shapes. A large piece of leather is placed on top, bolted on to crudely keep the platform from falling. Stairs lead to a mesh platform that loops around the wall to the north. To the direct east is a small path going off to another part of this gigantic room.

The rafters are a lot more crude than anyone would imagine. Narrow red metallic beams line the topmost layer of the dome, nearly creating a checkered hatch to its spherical cover. The mist adds another challenge to travelers of the rafters. Caution and courage are definitely good ideas here.

The small path goes up to a short trip through stairs, leading to a platform with a good sight over the rest of this large room. To the far north is a plank leading all the way to another platform, ending at a wall with many functional fans on it. The east leads to a lowered path that seems to lead to the same place up north, and to the west is a rather crudely placed platform.

This is another partially ruined beam, its other end missing, probably down with the wave of the dead below. Far to the north, there is a glimpse of another ladder leading down somewhere, though it is inaccessible from this place. The mist seems to be even thicker here, so be wary.

The mesh platform continues to the far north here. A slow breeze blows through the room, caused by the large metal fan lies embedded onto the western wall. The room seems to be rather grim and somber all by its own, filled with the mist and littered with dead bodies here and there. The path leads further north, and to the south as well.

The path takes on another turn here, this time with two directions, south and east. To the east is a large four-way intersection between two metal beams, and to the south is the path leading back to the ladder. The mist still lingers around here, always an obstacle, and of course, the gruesome sight below providing visual entertainment to the corpse-inclined.

The ladder looks ominous, what with all the piles of bodies strewn around it. The catwalk leads to a halt here at the ladder, leaving only two options. Enter the ladder and face what is to come, or turn back and run. The mist looms about, seeming to wait for a decision to come.

rooms.name: At the end of the path

userData.LongDescription: Metal walls surround the room. Far to the east is the ladder to the upper floor. The ground stops short before the western wall. A mound of scrap fills the gap between the wall and the floor. Looking through the mist, a glimpse of a doorway is barely visible to the east, perhaps leading somewhere more interesting.

rooms.name: Northern end of the narrow platform

userData.LongDescription: This narrow platform was probably originally built for maintenance work, because of it's positioning inbetween the large machines. The path leads down to the south, a set of stairs partially hidden by one of the tall, large production machines. Another set of steps are just to the west, leading all the way to the southern part of the room.

This odd-shaped platform is shaped like a hexagon, made from six smaller triangular platforms. The walls are metallic and cold. The room is still intact and in perfect symmetry, with no damage to it. Two doorways leading north and south are visible.

Just down the ladder is a small passage leading north. The walls are rather tight together, almost seeming to be able to close together. To the north, there seems to be a rather large room, but no details seen from here. The mist still accompanies the area, never fading. The ladder is also here, leading back up to the upper layer.

rooms.name: Another turn on the path of mesh

userData.LongDescription: From here, busted engines and machines as well as metal pipes are seen underneath the platforms. Though what their purpose is unknown, it is clear that they are all useless and broken now. The mesh path leads to the west from here, ending at a staircase by a metal pillar. The path to the south is also viable, leading to the southern ends of the room.

rooms.name: A curve in the mesh platform

userData.LongDescription: The path takes a turn to the north here. Scrap metal and other pieces of junk are still scattered throughout the void below, sometimes almost seeming to float, for no bottom can be clearly seen. The mist blankets the area, wrapping everything in its tranquility. The path leads to the north and to the west from here.

The horizontal beam ends on a charred tip here. Further on, the bloody massacre of mauled machines is visible. To the west is an intersection, perhaps that would be a wiser choice in path selection. Either way, there is nothing much to accomplish here, except to turn back.

The mesh path stops at the northwestern corner, and takes a turn to the east here. Mist envelops everything around here, even the dead bodies around as their veiled coffin. Two broken fans are here, as dead as the unfortunate humans who have pitifully expired. There are two paths here; south and east.

The mesh platform comes to a halt here, only the void surrounding it remains. The metal door is to the northern wall, the valve handle in place. Machines and other bits of metal lie all around down in the void, suggesting some existance of a bottom, but certainly not visible.

The horizontal beam takes a halt, adjoined to a small catwalk hugging the eastern wall. From the catwalk, a small platform nearly buried in the machine wrecks is visible, leading to a demolished door below. The mist adds to this sad scene, almost seeming to want to mask its true, hideous feature. There's nothing too much up here, except for the good view of the room below.

This lone platform is rather depressing, all out on its own. A chasm which none would want to fall into lies to the west, and nearby, a large metal door. The walls seem to create permanent, unblockable barriers. Perhaps it would be wise to leave before more feelings of paranoia occur.

This is a small L-shaped hook on the path that leads to a larger platform. A metal pillar glimmers around the inner curve of the L, an aesthetic sense finally showing in this place. There are also many pieces of scraps and junk in the void, as well as machines. The mist looms around, stagnant and never changing.

This particular part of the beam hugs the southern wall of the dome, eventually leading to a narrow catwalk area. A metal door is embedded to the wall, though damaged and even dynamite won't budge it. The mist still gleams in the air, almost like an unholy mantle. The only path left is back to the intersection at the north, so consider that.

The platform of mesh dead-ends against the metallic wall, providing access to broken fans attached to the walls. Below the mesh platform is a pile of junk, all seeming to be garbage and other forms of broken machinery. Back to the south, shallow metal steps lead down to the main platform.

rooms.name: A mesh platform on the west end

userData.LongDescription: To the west is a long mesh platform leading north, made of long rectangular-shaped mesh plates. The path hugs up to the western wall, with the ventilation fans nearly seeming to blow wind to push people off the ledge. A set of stairs is to the east, leading down to the platforms below.

The mesh platform still leads further to the north from here, also leading an equal distance to the south. At the end of the path is a pair of steps leading down to a narrow platform among the machinery wrecks. The piles of scrap are cleanly visible under the mesh, creating a bit of an ominous feel.

rooms.name: The end of the long platform

userData.LongDescription: This marks the end of the row of platforms that are adjoined to make a long path, stopping right before a wide gap of broken machinery. A metallic chest is on the corner, opened and looted. Metal pipes run through the ground below the platform, some partially buried in the mounds of scrap that plague the area.

This room is tight and narrow, the metallic walls seeming to seal in like a steel coffin. A large fan swirls slowly on the wall, as a ventilation system. The room branches both west and east, the western path ending at a ladder leading somewhere. However, the path to the east has no floor. A metal door with a valve handle lies at the end of the eastern path, but is inaccessible without figuring out the mechanism to reach it.

rooms.name: A turn in the path of beams

userData.LongDescription: The eastern path from the original intersection takes a turn north here, leading to more complex beam routes. The pile of corpses below fill the air with a bloody stench. This certainly isn't the nicest place to be, especially with the thick mist blocking plenty of the view.

This room is simply impressive, with all sorts of mechanical gadgets lining the walls. Two computer screens complete with speakers are on the back wall, deactivated. A horde of cables and other sorts of mechanical wonder fill the room, and there seems to be much to do here. The door is to the south, providing passage back to the rest of the dome.

The metallic path branches into three here, going west, south and east. The intersection is still to the south, forever indifferent. To the east is a short path leading to another catwalk, while the path west seems to lead to the northern ladder. Bodies of humans are scattered around the place, some barely hanging on to the beam.

This is the northern end of the lowered path, a metallic ladder leading up to higher ground. A large fan rotates nearby, sending a sudden chill down the narrow platform. The platform high above is a rather patched work, with plating of different sizes and shapes. The mist looms around, unimportant yet a hindrance.

This ladder expands a height much taller than the previous ladder, extending to even the rafters up above. Nothing else seems to be of interest in this particular spot, though the terminals to the east might be of some. Caution would be advised, for the thick mist still lingers here.

rooms.name: A turn in the looping path

userData.LongDescription: The narrow platform comes to an end here, metal steps connecting it to a raised mesh path. The dead body of a man lies in the corner, his flesh rotting away. Scraps of metal still fill the spaces below the platforms, aiding the eternal mist in obscuring the true depth of the room.

The clanging sound of metal against metal can be heard as you enter the hot, steamy weapon shop. Hanging against the walls just behind a colossus wielding a mithril hammer are some weapons of very good-looking quality. The huge man points at a wooden list on a wall and returns to his noisy work.

As soon as you come in you realize this is this town's mayor's house. Expensive looking tapestries and paintings loom high upon the walls. In the center of the room is a long table, where valuable-looking silver platters lie. A fireplace with a bear skin just in front of it cover the western part of the lounge. The room is well lit, but you can't seem to grasp where the light is coming from, since the windows are shut by curtains and the fireplace can't give off that much luminosity. A set of stairs leads to the second floor.

Smoke rises up from a small building below, warming the air on this ledge but creating a smell that is not particularly pleasant. Overlooking most of the town, this ledge is blasted by the icy mountain winds that are absent in the rest of the town below. A small shack, crumbling with age, stands on this cliff. Cobwebs cover the windows, and the lock on the door is broken.
You are in a small house in the town of Narshe.  There doesn't seem to be anyone home right now, but there is a small fire burning in the fireplace.  It feels warm and cozy here.

This ledge is quite wider than the bridge stretching east toward the back of a house. On the mountainside is a mine shaft. An eerie light is coming from inside, most probably emitted by series of torches and electric lanterns, yet...

The luxury of this room makes the rest of the town look like an slum. Crystal candle-holders hold the source of the light in this room, reflected countless times in the mirrors covering the walls. A bed with very comfortable-looking bed sheets is right in the center of the room.

This old shed is seriously falling apart. Cobwebs cover the windows so thickly that it's impossible to tell which windows are broken and which aren't. This building apparently was once used by someone for storage, judging from the multiple empty chests and crates, but its owner has obviously abandoned the place. A busted grandfather clock is the only thing left that isn't an empty container.

You stand at the top of a long flight of stairs with a large cabin in front of you.  It is one of the largest homes in the village, giving you the sense that it holds some importance.  You can see all the gleaming lights of the city from here, and the view is spectacular.

This small area here is a solid dead end. The rock wall of the mountain cliff has curved into this niche, and continues on far beyond here. Many tracks of footsteps lead up to the wall, but stop there. The wall itself has very few features, other than icicles hanging from the cliff above. The only visible path here is to the east.

The gates to the town of Narshe tower protectively over the small town. Just to the north is the huge arch that allows people access to the city, but two guards stand watch over it at all times. There is a huge portal here which leads back to the central area, and to the south are the airship and a vast plain with many different creatures.

This path west of the town gate of Narshe is right next to a cliff wall that towers high. Snow falls off of the above cliff edge every so often, and icicles hang down from the edge. The wind off of the plains comes in and collides with the air off of the mountain here, making this path very windy. To the east is the town entrance, and to the west is a dead end niche.

This is the eastern side of the town of Narshe.  Two roads, one leading southwest and the other leading west, start from a set of stairs carved in the rock of the northern stone wall.  The way east is blocked by a huge rock wall towering about thirty feet high, and right up against it, a small guard fortification has been erected.

This road leads north toward the mountains. There are no more houses past this point. A slight steepening of the ground here makes the road rise in elevation as it nears the cliffs to the north. The way slowly curves toward the town, southeast of here.

You are in the far western part of Narshe.  You can see a shop in front of you with a diamond symbol on it, as well as a long staircase.  Against the west wall of the shop, a guard station has been built to help defend the town from attack.  You can spot a large house at the top of the staircase, that looks like it could use some investigating.  The rest of the town is back to the east.

The road now gets really steep as it goes further north.  Sets of wooden stairs with small guard stations next to them are placed against the bigger hills so that it is easier to go up or down the road.  The guard stations look new, as if they were recently built to help strengthen the town against attack.  A bridge looms about twenty feet above the road, linking the two rocky edges that nearly come together overhead.  The low moan is much louder as the mine gets closer.
You are standing on some kind of balcony just behind the house. A bridge to the west links it to a mountain ledge where you can see a hole in the rock, probably a mine shaft.

This is the warmest place you've been in since you set foot in this town. Here, people talk and have fun sitting near the long flames burning in the fireplace. The smell of good food makes your stomach ache from envy. Just in front of you is a counter, with the innkeeper standing just behind it. He looks at you, smiles, then points at a sign hanging on the wall behind him.

This is a well lit room. A fireplace burns in the southern wall, heating the surroundings with delicate warmth. A table rests in the center, two chairs standing near it. Bookshelves lay against the northern wall, right next to a solid-looking oak door. To the south is the exit door.

This place looks like the western path of the town of Narshe. Several roads here lead to different buildings.  To the west there is a shop with a weird looking diamond symbol on it.  Straight to the north is a common house like any other in the village.  Farther to the west there is a very large house on top of a cliff.  Right here there is a shop with the sound of clanking metal coming from within.  Back to the east is the center of the village.

This road winds around the mountainside of the eastern Narshe cliffs. From here, about fifty feet up in the air, the view of the small town is wonderful. The sounds of its machinery are easily carried up the cliff like a deep, low voice, inviting yet spooky. The smoke coming from the town and spilling upward through the sky gives to it the look of an awful dragon pit. Far toward the west side of the town, higher in the mountains, are more holes, which must without a doubt be more mines. The road goes south from here, or goes back northwest.

Just to the north of a small arch in a wall that allows one to enter or exit the town of Narshe is a fork in the path.  The road splits up into many directions here, with the center of town lying just to the north.  The inn is close by, and the smell of freshly baked bread drifts out in the company of laughter and voices. A little ways to the south are some vast, grassy plains, and far to the north you can make out some mountains and caves.  A short distance to the south are the city gates and a portal to the central area.  A sign stands here on the ground.
Walking on the narrow bridge, you look down, only to notice you are about fifty feet above ground. Better not fall off, or else...

A long set of stairs leads down toward the center of Narshe, to the south. Immediately to the north is a house of one of the residents of Narshe. There is also a narrow road darting southeast on the side of the eastern rock cliffs. It does not look like it is used very often.

This is Narshe's item shop. Here, you can buy all kinds of goods. Just in front of the door is a counter, behind which stands a fat lady, either the shopkeeper or the shopkeeper's wife. Just behind her are shelves filled with potions and other odd-looking stuff. There is a sign on the wall beside the shelves.

This place reminds you of a general clothing store. Clothes of all kinds are hanging on the walls, ranging from normal everyday clothes to combat armors, including rare, fancy metal protective garments. Behind a counter stands a bald, fat man, the shopkeeper, staring at you with pig eyes. Just behind him is a sign pinned on a wall.

This must be the center of this very remote town. Modern-looking houses surround you, flanked with weird devices that produce energy for the ovens and lamps at night. A low moan can be constantly heard the mountain range to the north. The road goes northwest from here, toward the mountains, south, toward the town gate, and east toward another section of road. Straight north is a set of stairs, leading to what is an armor shop, according to the sign hanging above the door. On the west side of the center of the town are a few more shops. There is yet another building northeast, which looks very warm and inviting. The sounds of music and the smell of fresh bread flow out of it.

At the top of a flight of snow-covered stairs is a small house with a sign nailed to the front of it.  There is a lot of smoke comming from the chimney of the house, giving the idea that it is some sort of armor shop with a hot fire burning inside to forge the metal.  The entire town can be seen from this perch, and it is oddly beautiful from this height.

This small shop is full of all sorts of things, from rings and medallions, to gloves and shoes.  An old man stands behind the counter polishing some unidentifiable object.  There's a locked door leading to the shop's back room, and another door that leads out into the street.

You have climbed up a set of stairs and find yourself in the northwest corner of town.  You can see a great distance to the south of here, and can even make out the ocean far in the distance.  There is a small house in front of you, and the door seems open.

It's difficult not to stumble upon the single bed while walking in this dimly lit bedroom. In the feeble light, it's hard to notice, but there is a small door in the northern wall - a back exit from the house. A window in the door grants a view of a snowy ledge outside.

A quick look around reveals more of the desolation and destruction in the area.  The scarred earth, dying vegetation and brackish ocean which surrounds the island of Narshe are but a few of the vivid reminders from a dark time in the past.

The plains start here and continue south towards the ocean. To the east is the road that leads into the mountain town of Narshe. Its glimmering lights shimmer in the mountain range farther to the north. The plains end where they seem to meet the southern horizon, giving way to the crashing waters of a vast ocean.

The plains here look less lively now, with a distinct lack of vegetation. The twisted, deathly remains of what used to be a wonderfully lush area are evident in this husk of formerly burgeoning life. A small cabin stands in the middle of the clearing. To the southwest, a ferry port is busy conveying passengers to and from the Figaro island.

This rather simple cabin is the home of Duncan, former teacher of the martial arts.  A large window is on the opposite side of the cabin, offering a great view of the outside.  A fireplace is on the left wall, and a black belt hangs above it.  A table with a pot of flowers on it is in the center of the room, and beneath it is a red carpet.

The plains end abruptly and the ocean begins, taking over the task of being monotonous. The surroundings seem to get a little less lively from here, and are even worse farther to the south.  A dock, which supports travel between the Narshe island and the Figaro island, also lies to the south.

This peaceful little valley is nestled into a small area that is surrounded by mountains on all sides. A shining blue mountain lake adds to the picturesque quality of the setting, its cool waters reflecting the sky. The lake is fed by tiny springs that flow forth from the mountains, and it supplies water to many of the creatures that roam the plains. In the distance to the south is a great blue ocean.

The mountains and shore have given way to a huge field of grass and wildflowers just south of Narshe. Little creatures run through the grass, detectable only by the scratching sounds they make as they go. Far to the south, a vast ocean rolls its grey waves into shore, while mountain ranges dominate the skyline to the north and west.

In the middle of these vast plains, they truly do seem endless. In every direction, green-blushed plains with small creatures darting through the grasses are all that can be seen nearby. Far to the north rests a snow-capped mountain range, and to the south a sea shimmers in the sun.

These are the very flat plains south of Narshe. To the north you can see the mountain village of Narshe, the smoke from its chimneys curling toward the heavy grey sky. It is nestled in some very rugged, mountainous terrain. To the east, west, and south all that is visible are the seemingly endless plains, colored soft green by the grass that covers them.

Gentle waves wash the shores of a vast ocean through eternity. The sand is wet and cool, holding the molded shapes of footprints that do not look human. Far to the south across the ocean, a desert continent is just barely visible on the fading horizon. The northern mountains reach towards the sky, cradling the town of Narshe in their shadows.

The floor is polished wood, and in the center of the area a hole has been cut into the floor. More railing has been placed around it.  On one side there is not railing, so that people can climb down the ladder that has been placed in the hole. From down below come the sound of the gears of the airship turning and pushing the airship through the air.  To the northeast you can see an old man standing by a large stairwell, looking over at you.

You climb down the steep stairs on the deck of the airship, down into the inner portion of it.  A man stands here by the entryway and nods as you enter.  Directly in front of you there is a large railing and looking down over it you can see a few pieces of furniture and a table. To the west there is a large hole in the floor where a ladder has been placed, so that you may go down and look at the inner workings of the airship. To the east you can see a small door and a large staircase leading down to the platform below.

Racing through the sky, the airship suddenly slows.  The clouds overhead darken, and the wind starts to blow rather strongly.  The deck has a set of stairs to escape the weather - maybe taking refuge wouldn't be a bad idea.

rooms.name: On the Deck of the Falcon

userData.LongDescription: You have climbed aboard Daryl's Airship, The Falcon, and you ready yourself for flight.  The risk taking gambler, Setzer, stands at the controls of the airship. Why don't you 'say hi'? From here you can go to almost any of the areas in the Final Fantasy 6 realm.  Above you, a huge white balloon can be seen.  It keeps the airship afloat while flying.  There are also several huge propellers on all sides of the Falcon that lift the airship into the sky.  At the other end of the airship there is a flight of stairs leading down into the inside of the Falcon.

All around you gears turn about on their spokes.  These gears and motors turn the propellers on the outside of the airship, so that the ship can actually stay/fly into the air. Some personal effects of a swordsman of Doma are in a corner, left over from the time when this airship was the headquarters of those fighting against Kefka's rule. There is a ladder leading back up to the main area of the airship.

Before you a finely crafted wooden staircase descends down into the meeting area below.  Behind you there is a little door leading back into a small room. A small railing lines the side of the balcony so that no one falls down to the floor below.  To the west you can see an old man standing by a staircase that leads back up to the deck.

This is a small meeting area beneath the balcony above. The wall forms an indentation to the north, where a small couch has been placed. The couch has been sewn with blue, gold, and a fine red threads. In front of it the main floor of the room has been cut out and in its place shiny dark and light green tiles have been laid. There is also a large staircase here leading back up to the balcony above.

The door opens with ease and as you step inside you can see a very quaint and small room.  In the center of the room near the back wall is a small wooden chair with blue fabric on the seat and back. Also on the back wall is a little window lined with fancy red curtains.  On both sides of the wall, white curtains have been hung upon the walls. This is where Setzer used to peer out into the clouds in the old days.. The floor is made of small wooden planks and behind you there is a small door leading back out, into the main area of the airship.

A patch of thick grass can be seen swaying with the breeze.  There are two tall obelisks that look like mini pyramids on the path, and trees to the south and west.  A stream runs parallel to the path, a little to the northeast.

This is a small ravine, enclosed by a cliff face to the west, and trees to the east.  There is no wind or sun in the ravine, because the cliff and the trees block both from entering.  To the north are some stairs, and the path continues southeast.

The path gets wider here, and some flowers dot the path.  There is a cliff face to the west, and to the east the center of Gaia's Navel is clearly visible.  There are many vicious monsters guarding the center, so proceeding with caution is probably the best idea.

The rock wall now curves around the edge of Gaia's Navel, almost making it a circle.  A few flowers and trees occupy the path, along with two medium-sized rocks.  A slight breeze wafts through the area, cooling the area off a bit.

A slight breeze blows through the area.  There is a small clump of trees here, with a few carefully placed rocks laid to one side.  To the northeast, the path leads into shallow water, while the stairs to the south take you in towards the center of Gaia's Navel.

This is an odd-looking area.  There are trees to the south and east that run into a large mountainside to the north.  Right in front of the mountainside is a mound of dirt covered in grass that is big enough to walk on.  The area is filled with flowers and grass, and there is a stream that flows under a bridge to the west.

After the entrance to the waterfall, the cave continues down into a deep tunnel, with little visible light. The ground is submerged in dirty water from Gaia's Navel. To the west, the center of Gaia's Navel is visible past the waterfall. Rocks stick up above the shallow water.

A field of beautiful pink tulips stretches to the north ending near two steep and rocky hills. Blowing in from the east is a a soft breeze, setting the flowers in motion, releasing their sweet scent into the air. Between the hills a thin path begins, leading towards a gloomy forest.  To the east a cannon pokes out over the trees.

Waterfalls sprinkle water from above, while the water keeps flowing in towards the center of Gaia's navel directly to the south.  Some lily pads flounder in the crisp, clear water.  A school of goldfish swim by, oblivious to your presence.

This Cannon Travel Center can only send people to the Potos cannon.  The cannon itself sits atop a small hill.  A short man stands at the base of the hill, waiting for customers.  The smell of spent powder permeates the air.  A few stones line the path, along the edge of a small grove of trees.

There is a forest to the west, but the trees are so close together that nothing can get in.  There is also a cliff to the east.  Between the forest and the cliff, there is only a small space to walk.  Anyone walking here has to watch their step to keep from falling over the edge.

Almost all of Gaia's Navel can be seen from here.  The natural circular path going in towards the center is beautiful, yet you see many monsters waiting to hinder your journey.  There are trees and flowers to your west, and a rock wall to your south.  The main path continues to the east and southwest.

The bluffs on either side of the path meet a short distance ahead, behind a portal.  A line of statues sits to either side of the path, watching those who pass.  Over the hills to the north, a dark and gloomy forest can be seen.  The smell of decay is carried on a breeze from the north.

There is a forest to the west that can't be entered, and a cliff to the east.  There is only a small space to walk between the forest and the cliff, so anyone passing by must pick their steps carefully.  The cliff juts out a little here, but so does the forest, giving no extra walking room.

There are trees along the western side of the path, and low rock wall along the eastern side.  A row of flowers line the rock wall, given much water by the nearby pool.  There are some large spots on the ground where the earth never soaked up all the water.

There are a few trees surrounding you, and a patch of thick grass lies in the area.  An obelisk sits off to the southeast, and a small body of water sits off to the southwest.  Kippo can be entered from here, and to the north is Gaia's Navel.
The path ends here, giving way to a thin bridge to the north made of two long planks of wood.  There are trees to your east, blocking your view.  Some birds can be heard chirping in the trees.

There are trees to your south, and a sharp drop to your north.  A squirrel can be seen sitting on a treetop over the edge of the cliff, happily munching on a nut.  There is a large dirt patch on the ground, but from what in unknown.

Water flows down over the rock wall to the north in a beautiful waterfall.  The water flows by and over another cliff to the south onto a lower level.  There are a few lily pads in the water, and some rocks just waiting to stub someone's toe.

The path here gets narrow as it leads into a shallow stream of water.  There are a few large trees around.  The center of Gaia's Navel is to the west over a cliff edge, and a rock wall looms to the east.

This is an intersection.  The path continues north and southwest, but there is a small path that goes off to the east.  There are trees and flowers randomly placed on the trail, as if they were just thrown there.

Two waterfalls fall down from above, keeping the stream flowing.  Another waterfall flows over a cliff to the south.  Some lily pads float slowly along the stream, pushed by a light breeze.  There is also something shiny in the water.

It is a small wooden bridge only two planks wide, yet it looks quite sturdy.  One can only hope they don't lose their balance, and fall to the area below.  Below the bridge, there is a small area that would be ideal for resting.

A clearing opens up to the west and north.  A slight breeze makes the grass sway, and the trees rustle.  An obelisk sits in the clearing, and some pretty flowers attract the attention of some insects.  Pandora isn't too far off to the east.

There are many trees to your east, and a sharp drop to your west.  There is one lone tree in the middle of the path, surrounded by a few flowers.  Some birds can be heard faintly chirping in the trees, as if they were trying to keep quiet.
There are trees to the north and south.  An area of thick grass is swaying in the breeze, and an obelisk sits in the path.  Kippo isn't far off to the west.

The narrow path is lined with an impenetrable forest of trees to the west, and a cliff to the east.  There isn't much room to walk, so one must walk carefully. Making the path even more treacherous are the pretty wild flowers that grow here.

A slight breeze whips through your hair, but two trees on the trail don't even rustle.  The trees sit against the rock wall going around Gaia's Navel in a small niche.  A few flowers dot the trail, and some trees from the next level down to your northwest poke over the ground level.

rooms.name: A Wide Path in the Woods

userData.LongDescription: A small stream and a bridge can be seen to the west, leading to Pandora.  There are trees to the north and south, with some small mounds of dirt covered in grass spotting the path.

A small, mysterious mound of dirt fills the middle of the trail, its purpose unknown.  Tall, restless trees are to the east and west, providing the trail with lots of shade.  The trail continues north, and there is a wooden bridge to the south.

There are rock walls on the east and west, and trees to the northwest.  As the rock walls continue south, they get closer together, until you have just enough room for one person to fit through.  The main path continues south and northeast.

There is a mountainside to the north, and a stream runs to the east and south.  There are only a few trees on the path, and some obelisks can also be seen.  The ground is spotted with patches of thick grass.  There is a bridge to cross the stream to the east.

A light breeze sweeps through the area.  There is a large rock nearby, surrounded by a patch of thick grass.  Trees are everywhere, except for an opening to the northwest and a bridge to the east.  A small stream runs under the bridge, and Pandora can be seen directly across it.

This is a small plateau on which many flowers are crowded.  A stream lies to the northeast, and some stairs lead south.  Some large trees loom a few feet to the west, giving shade in the evening.  Some mist from the nearby waterfall inhabits the area, giving a slight chill.

The trail is narrow here, and leads into a pool of water to the north.  Trees line the southern edge of the path, and curve up towards the entrance to the pool.  A low rock wall lines the northern edge.

This is a path in the woods, with tall trees to the north and south.  The path has two obelisks on it, which are surrounded by thick grass and a few flowers.  A clearing opens up to the southwest, and a bridge that spans a small stream to the east.

Trees circle the small clearing, except for paths to the north and west.  The area is filled with thick, green grass and quite a few flowers.  A few small mounds of dirt covered in grass can also be seen.

The cliff face sits on the southern side of the path, where it meets a line of trees that continue east. The cliff drops off directly to your north.  Some flowers stand alongside the cliff, perilously swaying over the edge in the breeze.

There is no water flow here, although there are waterfalls to the east and west.  They both pour water into the area, making a slowly swirling pool.  Most of the grime the water carries is stuck here in the endless cycle.  Many lily pads also float here.

Behind the western waterfall, the path continues into a wide cave. Water flows from the east down into the cave. To the east, the center of Gaia's Navel is visible. A group of lily pads lies collected near the entrance, wilted from the lack of sunlight.

There are rock walls to your north, east, and south, and a bridge above.  The area is mostly shaded, and quite cool.  This is the perfect place for a resting spot.  It is tempting to sit here for a few hours and take a nap.

The area is a shallow stream. A few small fish dart about, trying to avoid being stepped on.  Two waterfalls sprinkle down from above making everything wet.  A lily pad flows over the edge of a waterfall to the next level down of Gaia's Navel.

This is the center of Gaia's Navel.  Waterfalls pour water into the pond, and the water has almost nowhere to go, except for the two caves that can be seen behind them.  This causes the water to be disgusting, and wading through it as fast as possible is probably a good idea.  There are some rocks sticking out of the water, and some deserted lily pads.

The path narrows here, leaving a small entrance to the shallow water to the northwest.  There are a few trees on the eastern part of the path, and the ground drops off sharply to the west.  Anything falling over the edge would not come out unscathed.

This is a large open area with lots of thick, lush grass and a few flowers.  Two obelisks sit in the middle of the clearing, and you have a sudden urge to stand between them.  There are trees to the south and west, and a stream can be seen to the northwest.

This is the southernmost point of Gaia's Navel.  A rock wall looms to your south, and another drops off before you to your north.  Some flowers dot the trail, and a light breeze blows in from the west, whistling as it hits the rocks.

The cellar of the Water Palace much resembles the entrance, as it is far darker than the rest of the place.  The only light comes in from a few small sconces set into the walls.  A small bridge crosses a thin bed of water, leading to another section of the basement, while a staircase leads back to the Water Palace proper.

This small cell is very Spartan in decor, with the exception of two large pillars on the east and west ends of the northern wall.  The only light in here comes from two small lanterns set into the same wall.  Besides that, there's very little of interest here.  The open gate stands to the south.

The path here widens into a large platform, with four more of the large torches at each corner of it.  The floor appears to be made of a dark blue cobblestone.  To the north a staircase leads to a large pool of water, flanked on each side by long waterfalls.  Also, this platform seems to be.. floating?

Pure elemental energy suffuses this realm, to the extent that nearly nothing else exists.  There are no perceivable floor, walls, ceiling, just mana.  It is a realm beyond mortal comprehension, and is where the most powerful of elemental beings reside.

The west side of the platform is fairly drab, consisting of two more torches, and a miniature river of water, flowing down from a waterfall on the wall.  The waterfall's source cannot be seen, but that's just part of the magic of the place.  The channel of water flows down, turns the corner of the platform, and drains off a waterfall at the south end of the platform.

A long walkway runs in a north-south direction, with rectangular pools of water running parallel to it.  The water looks rather shallow, and is very soothing.  Two rows of fat torches run along the sides of the platform, glowing with an eerie green light.  The ornate torches each have a small emerald set in their base.

A large staircase here leads into what would most likely be the cellar of the Water Palace.  Other than that, nothing of interest is on the east side of the platform, except a channel of water, which is identical to the one on the west side of the platform, waterfall and all.  The stage for the Mana Seed is to the west.

This platform is wider than the one to the south, and consists mainly of a large rectangular body of shallow water.  The water is around knee-level, and is unnaturally cold.  The water flows in from several waterfalls coming down from the platform to the north.  At the sides of the platform are several more torches.  Further to the north, two staircases lead to the next platform.

The chief point of interest on this platform is the large stage that houses the Mana Seed of Water.  The stage is shaped like a pyramid, with several small rectangular platforms stacked on one another, with a staircase leading to the top.  On each side of the stage is a large torch, glowing with a fierce green flame.  Behind the stage, the wall is light blue, with what appears to be something like stained glass windows.  The platform continues on to the east and west, and leads to another platform to the south.

On this side of the water, there is much of the same decoration as on the other side:  sconces, cobbled floors, brick walls.  However, there's a large gate to the north, which appears to hold a cell behind it.  In front of it are two strange panels set into the floor, covered in some kind of green markings.  A small bridge stands to the west.

An old building sits here, home to the shopkeeper of Kippo.  The stream in the middle of town cuts west just south of the shop, and runs off into the forest.  Some wild flowers are growing next to the building, as well as in the forest to the west.  A few pots sit next to the stream, waiting to be filled.

Two old people walk around a well kept house, doing odd jobs and chatting to each other.  Two beds lie in a corner of the room, and a large table sits in the middle of the room.  The table is set with three full cups.  Obviously, these people are expecting some company.

This is the first floor of the shop.  The shopkeeper stands behind the counter, waiting for you to buy something.  Some plants sit on the counter, and a chair sits in one corner of the room.  Behind the counter are all sorts of cabinets and drawers holding the various items for sale.  The shopkeeper points to a sign.

A massive apple tree sits in the middle of the area, surrounded by wildflowers.  There is a forest to the east, blocking the path.  To the north, the land is elevated enough so that it can't be reached, and there are many kinds of plants and bushes growing there.  Some people are here, having a picnic under the tree.

This is a cozy little inn.  There are a few beds in the larger portion of the inn, most of which are free.  There is a table near the beds where travelers can sit down and have a few drinks.  A candle sits on the counter, lighting up a sign that is hanging on the wall.  The innkeeper smiles at you warmly.

To the north and west of town, a steep hill slopes upward.  To the west, the hill meets trees, which run south along the edge of Kippo.  Bushes and plants are in abundance on the hill, and some flowers sit along the edge of the stream that runs through the village.  There is nothing here of interest, so nobody usually comes in this direction.

A stone path leads up to an old house over which a dark cloud hangs, as if it is an omen.  Trees line the western edge of the area, and a few flowers have sprung up along the stream.  A small bridge goes across the stream, allowing passage.  There are some pots in front of the house, in various states of emptiness.

There are two large windows in the room, and through one a large shaft of light comes through.  The shopkeeper sits behind the counter, dozing off.  In his hands sit a cup, full of something.  The light from one of the windows falls on a sign that is next to the shopkeeper.

The room is quite small, yet there is lots of furniture in it.  Two beds lay in one part of the room, nicely made up and ready to be used.  A table is against one wall, and a large cabinet against another.  A shaft of light shines through a window, making a square pattern on the floor.  There is also a mirror on one wall.

The south and east are blocked by trees, except for a wooden fence that lines the path out of Kippo.  A cozy inn sits here, being powered by a waterwheel.  The stream next to the inn cuts through the middle of the village, making up the town's water supply.  A small garden is in front of the building, consisting of a few flowers.

Trees line the eastern edge of town, keeping out the wind.  A stone path leads up to the stairs of an old house whose windows are open and inviting.  There are some potted plants in front of the house, and some flowers scattered around the area.  A bridge runs across the stream in the middle of town, in obvious disrepair.

A table sits in one corner of the room, set with cups and plates, and surrounded by four chairs.  There is a small kitchen section for cooking, and a desk sits against a wall.  Otherwise, the room is quite empty.  A large red rug covers most of the wooden floor, and some pictures hang on the walls.

The path splits in a four-way intersection at this part of the camp. To the north, the path continues past several barricades, while to the west, several suits of magitek armor can be seen. The path also leads to a dead-end up the eastern ramp, while to the southeast, the scorched remains of a structure stand along the bank of the river.

Debris and scattered rubble are all that remain of makeshift housing for the soldiers used back in the Doma siege. A wooden barricade blocks the southern and western edges of the now empty riverbed, where Kefka poisoned the waters to destroy Doma long ago. The only way to go is back to the main part of the camp to the north.

Purple tinged sand fills the riverbed, remnants of the poisoned water that the Imperial forces used to annihilate the citizens of Doma -- the entire ground is stained and dead. The bridge that used to cross overhead lies in ruins to the north and south, but there is enough debris on each bank to climb back up. Makeshift barricades to the east and west block further passage along the riverbed.

The southern path ends at a broken bridge over a dry riverbed, while the northern path heads towards the exit to the Doma continent. To the west, a burnt canvas tent, originally used to house imperial soldiers and supplies, now lies toppled. To the east, a ramp heads upwards towards another similar tent.

Scorched sand lines the entrance to the former Imperial camp, wrecked by destruction and nature. Blackened remains of trees and other foliage can be seen all around, some a victim of the elements, some a victim of poisoned water. To the north, a barricade constructed from sandbags lines both sides of the path to the continent, while charred tents and a dry riverbed are visible to the south.

A narrow passage sandwiched between a stone wall to the west and rows of boxes to the north and east, several magitek suits take up most of the available space. Above the wall to the west lie the falling structure of a scout tower, while beyond the eastern boxes lies a large canvas tent draped along the ground. The only way out is back to the south, to the main camp.

Amidst the ruins of a small storage shed on this raised area lay pieces of scrap metal and shrapnel, as well as large wooden splinters from crates. There appears to be debris buried in the sand, some of it extending several feet into the ground. Over the edge to the east, several barricades can be seen in a narrow passage, while to the west, many magitek suits rest against the wall. A ramp to the south leads down.

Stacks of boxes and crates, resting along the northern and southern stone walls, line this narrow passage between two larger areas within the camp. The boxes appear to contain various supplies, although nothing very useful can be seen at a quick glance. To the east, several generators and magitek suits can be seen, while a large, open area is directly west.

The path leads in four different directions in this part of the camp. To the south, a large, open area is visible, along with an exit to the continent.  To the north, a narrow alley holds several magitek suits. A ramp leads up to the northwest, where a large scout tower can be seen, while to the northeast, the ruins of a large canvas tent rests on the ground.

The collapsed remnants of a large command tent lie along the majority of the area, while bits of stone and rubble can be seen on the ground everywhere else. Boxes and other supplies rest on the southern edge of the ramp, which heads back down to the main camp. Over the western edge, the remains of a couple of trees can be seen amid the sandy wastes.

Standing among the ruins of a former Imperial storehouse, boxes are stacked upon each other along the corners of the crumpled stone walls. The scorched and charred sand underneath is rife with rubble and debris from the building. The only way to go is the path back to the main camp to the northwest, as the dry riverbed to the east and south is impassable.

The partially scorched, collapsed canvas tent, used in the past for strategy and military meetings, lies along the ground to the north among crates of supplies. To the west, a narrow alley with several magitek suits rests below a platform with a large scout tower. The only way to go is back to the southwest, to the path connecting the main parts of the camp.

Boxes and remnants of stone walls line the northern edge of this raised area, while the platform drops off completely to the east and south. Over the eastern edge, the ruins of another storehouse can be seen amid scorched sand and dirt, while a dry riverbed lies past the southern end. The only way to go is down the ramp to the west, headed back to the main camp.

The path branches, leading to the north, east, and west. To the north, several magitek suits and power generators are visible in the main camp, while to the east, a ramp leads up to the ruins of a facility. A scout tower is on a raised area to the west, while passage south is blocked by both a makeshift barricade made of sandbags, as well as the depths of a dried up riverbed.

This large open space of the former Imperial camp is somewhat different from other visible sections, namely in that, while most of it is dead, there is a relatively large amount of plant life. Although life was once supported here, the ground is as broken as elsewhere, and won't be supporting life any longer. To the south, the ruins of a building can be seen, while boxes and magitek suits are visible to the east. A scout tower is visible to the far north, while another path leaves the camp to the west.

Rising several feet into the air, a wooden scout tower overlooks the entire camp and beyond its southern perimeter. It appears that time and nature have weathered it unstable, as it looks like it would be unable to support any weight. To the west, the ruins of a facility can be seen, while to the south is a dry riverbed. The eastern ramp leads back down towards the camp.

A large wooden tower stands high in the air, although much of the structure, including the platforms at the top, have collapsed due to weathering and age. Over the edge of the wall to the east, an alley with several magitek suits can be seen, while beyond that, the ruins of a canvas tent cover the ground. The only way to go is down the ramp to the southeast.

The pathway ends before a large, barricaded tent, while to the west, it heads down the ramp into the main part of the camp. Through the blocked entrance of the tent, several out of date maps and military papers can be seen on top of a table, likely relics from before the world was torn apart. The only way to go is back down the western ramp.

This narrow passage is home to several stacked crates along the western wall and many magitek suits resting to the east. The crates appear to be filled with military rations, while the magitek suits appear to be either broken or out of power, rendering them inoperable either way. The only way to go is south, back to the main camp.

A large canvas tent, now in dilapidated ruins, rests on the ground to the north, while to the east, a large pile of chewed up bones lie on the ground. The ramp leads back down to the main camp path to the west. The wind kicks up dirt and stained sand from the riverbed to the south, all moisture from the earth evaporated years ago.

Towering several feet into the air, massive generators pump a continuous stream of power through numerous cables into nearby Imperial magitek suits. Crates are stacked along the walls, although they appear to have been ransacked long ago. A ramp leads to a higher platform to the north, while the main path continues to the east and west.

Stone walls, several feet high, rise up on both the eastern and western sides of the pathway. On the ground, barricades of wood and sandbags provide cover and hiding points, while stacks of boxes filled with supplies rest against the western wall. Several paths open up within the camp to the south, while the northern path ends at a broken bridge leading into the northern riverbed.

Paths split and branch in all directions as generators and magitek suits line much of the area. The paths east and west lead through narrow corridors, eventually into larger spaces, while the southern path splits at a dry riverbed. The wreckage of a large tent can be seen to the northwest, while several boxes and more magitek suits line the northern passage.

Clanking and clattering never ends in this place, as the machinery strives to complete functions laid out for it by ancient people, long ago.  Giant chocobo statues seemingly guard the door south that leads farther into the Catapult.  The way back to the airship lies to the east.

A narrow stairway, this leads deep into the recesses of the Catapult, and the noise level seems to be rising, perhaps from the closeness of the machinery all around.  Some of this machinery looks lethal if messed with, like giant gears that could crush a person.
