Machinery and gears spin and whirr all around, creating an unceasing din of technological noise.  Pipes and gears and metal gadgets of all sorts weave in and out of the walls, all seemingly used for some greater function.  The Airship Hangar lies down the steep stairway to the south.

The noise seems slightly muted here, perhaps some soundproofing was set into this room.  A glowing ring of light invites people to set up camp away from the noise of the rest of the area.  Doors to the north and south lead to other areas of the Catapult.

A lot of beds fill the room, this is obviously the sleeping quarters for people working in the Catapult.  A row of plants are set at the far side of the room from the door that goes back out to the foyer.  A couple empty pots sit by some of the beds.

A large table dominates the center of the room, books and gizmos piled all over the top of it.  A few bookshelves are along the north wall, holding a few books for easy access during experiments.  Some of the underground base's raw machinery is laid bare in the southern section, large gears spinning along and steady paces.

The foyer of the Catapult has many doors leading to the habitation areas of the base.  Plants grow in planters placed in between the doorways to give a lighter feel to the room.  South leads to the sleeping area, southwest to the library, and southeast to the lab room.  North leads back out of the personal quarters.

Large bookcases line the walls, filled with books on all sorts of subject matter.  Tables in the center of the room are set up for people to read without taking a book out of the room.  A button is on the southern wall, but looks damaged.

Appearing to be a large indoor garden within this high-tech underground station, the people who built this structure most likely used this place as a lounge when not doing work.  The greenery is nice and well-kept.  Stone chocobo statues flank the door to the south, silent guardians of whatever lies beyond.

This is an open area of the Catapult, with large chocobo statues and plants growing in planters around the room.  A stairway leads down deep within the Catapult.  A button is near the door to the north, wedged in the pressed position.

This room looks dusty from disuse, as if no one ever comes down here.  Some of the machinery is actually broken in this section, with vines creeping around the gears.  A locked door bars passage to the north, and the only way out of this room is up the stairs back out of these depths.

The airship of the ancient kingdom of Lonka sails high above the continents below.  The Lonka Airship is shaped very much like a normal ship, but a pair of propellers rise out of the deck, spinning fiercely to keep the vessel aloft.  The vehicle is plated with an adamantium alloy and seems to have a number of unusual devices set up.  Adventurers can use this airship to travel across the lands, and a simple 'hi' is all it takes to get started.

Approaching the sharp corner up ahead, the currents grow wild and unstable, producing rapids which make the boat bob some. The boat is growing unstable, and the rocks along the waterline of the cliffs have begun to crumble and drift upstream.  While the canal zigzags, you can see that the it takes another sharp turn far up ahead.

This is the source of the canal's chaos.  As the boat reaches the whirlpool, it begins to head in a circle with the flow of the water around the whirlpool. Something must be keeping this whirlpool going, and until it's gone, adventuring further is impossible.

rooms.name: In front of the Canal Gate

userData.LongDescription: This is the entrance to the Torna Canal.  The gate has been newly repaired and tightly locked shut.  It is difficult to tell whether the gate is in place to keep people out, or to keep something in.  Up above, a family of birds watches the area from their nest. A small skiff sits here, in case anyone needs to get through.

Surrounded by walls of rushing water, the inside of the whirlpool is Pandemonium. The remains of many boats are rapidly stirred around here due to the force of the current, however, there's no way to tell how far it goes.  The boat is following the path of the whirlpool and will soon smash into the bottom of the canal.  The only option is to jump overboard and hope for the best.

Now, the current has become so fast that even the larger denizens can't escape the canal.  The boat is suprisingly stable, but even the rocks along the waterline of the cliffs have begun to crumble and drift eastward.  While the canal zigzags, further to the east, it takes another sharp turn.

The mysterious current grows as the outcroppings of rock cause turbulent rapids.  The boat can pass through here easily as long as it avoids the dangerous cliffs on both sides. The creatures that call this place home swim past the boat trying to escape the growing flow. They're coming from the sharp bend to the south which leads to the source of this unnatural current.  Past this point, there is no turning back.

From aboard the boat, one can see that the current is moving so quickly that fish can no longer escape. The water tumbles over the rocks breaking at their peaks and carrying away the bird nests built too close to the water.  You can almost make out a turn far ahead that leads to the source of this chaos.

This is the northern-most section of the canal's bend.  The water splashes up against the northern cliff as it makes its way around the rocky curve. More violent beasts swim here examining the boat for food. They're rushing toward the unknown force ahead that's drawing the water to it. The gate back to the southwest remains the best escape from this treacherous area, but there is no going back.

From here, the canal heads northward around a penninsula to the east, and the gate leading back to the ocean is to the south. More angry creatures swim here ready to attack the unwary. They seem to heading toward the ship from the north, but you can not see beyond the end of the peninsula due to the high cliffs. A group of birds perched on a low section of cliff squawk at the ship.

The canal rapids grow more and more raging as the boat comes to the sharp, southern turn.  Up ahead, you can see the source of the chaos: a whirlpool lies to the south sucking everything towards it.  Even the canal's fish are being sucked into the aquatic phenomenon.

The floor of this room is submerged in several feet of cold, salty water. Darkness smothers the sounds of breathing and moving water as if to suffocate all of the life that this haunted place unwillingly hosts. Rotted barrels and crates litter the floor, combining with the darkness to make for dangerous footing. The narrow stairway to the north leads up towards light, while a second set of stairs to the south leads down into deeper darkness.

A long hallway turns a corner and opens onto a shorter hall running east-west. To the immediate south is a door through which weak, watery daylight reaches its desperate fingers, seeking purchase in the darkness of the ship's hold. The northern doorway is lost in shadow, as is whatever lies beyond its threshold. The long, flooded hallway leads to the southwest.

Darkness seeps in, covering the shattered floorboards in partial shadows. Mist swirls down through the stairwell, further obscuring the floor and other surroundings. A door in the center of the south wall leads into what appears to be a small room. The open southern exit leads deeper into the broken ship.

Damp, musty air fills this small cabin in the middle of the ship graveyard. Mist swirls around the legs of a map stand near the center of the northern wall. The same mist pours through jagged holes in the floor to fill the chamber below. A door leads out into the heavy light of an overcast day and stairs lead down.

Murky fog presses in from all sides. The ghostly shapes of broken ships rise out of the grey water in the semi-darkness. It is easier to hear the water lapping at the edges of the planks leading into the graveyard than it is to see it. The stench of brine and dead, decaying fish is everywhere. The horrible smell sinks into everything it touches, permanently permeating the area. The pirate ship is back to the west, but the graveyard opens up uninvitingly to the northeast.

Stairs lead up and down out of this small chamber in the heart of the broken ship. Most of the floor boards were shattered by the force of the whirlpool that took the ship down,  and the few that remain creak under the slightest weight. Heavy mist writhes through the room, hiding dangerous broken sections of floor.

Though much of the rest of the ship is flooded and decayed, this section has gone largely untouched by the damage. Crates line the walls, still securely locked and fastened in place. A few beds occupy one corner of the room, indicating that this must have been the crew's quarters. It does not look like anyone was in here when the ship went down.

The bow of the ship hangs precariously out over the dark water of the graveyard. White boulders thrust up out of the bleak depths, providing stepping stones that lead directly north. The shore is just barely visible at the end of the treacherous pathway. It appears to be a small, sandy cove enclosed by high cliffs.

Daylight has abandoned the bowels of this gutted ship as the room plunges into darkness. Thin light, barely enough to make the basic features of the room distinguishable, filters in from above. Maneuvering through the flooded room is made difficult by scattered barrels hidden by the dark water. Stairs lead up towards the light and down to the southeast.

The bow of a ship thrusts above the misty water, its broken mast at an awkward angle. The destroyed windows of the cabin stare out in a silent mockery of death. To the north, the cabin door stands open. There is a path of wooden planks to the west and to the east, a stepping stone provides a path to the next ship over.

The deck of this ship is slick with a greenish slime that is just starting to dry in the muted light of the sun. More of the slime clings to most of the ship's hull, along with hundreds of barnacles. Oddly, a chest sits in the middle of the deck, its lid thrown back. The ship continues north of the chest towards a string of stepping stones.

Once a storage room, this chamber is now empty of all but the shells of boxes that were once full of supplies that have long since rotted away. The smells of mold and salty brine permeate the still air. Mist pours down from the room outside to flow out over the floor in the semi-darkness. It trickles down through broken floor grates to an even deeper level. The only way out is back up the stairs.

The murky water laps at broken crates and barrels that lay scattered throughout the room. The floor is in such a state of disarray that the already dangerous footing has become even more treacherous. The smell of death is stronger here, where the sunlight has not penetrated the darkness for years. A few steps up to the east end at a raised platform that was once part of a larger deck. There is another exit to the northwest.

Wooden walls and floor planks have been made slimy and rotten through constant contact with the sea water. The broken stumps of what might once have been the bases for the masts of the ship guard either side of the southern door. Stairs lead up into darkness, though daylight creeps in from the south.

Though deep in the hold of the lifeless ship, this room is surprisingly unsubmerged. A long walkway with a wooden railing clings to the wall as it looks down over a deeper level that is completely flooded with murky water. The lower level can be accessed by taking the stairs. The only other exit is a doorway to the south, through which a glimmer of light enters the room.

This small room looks like it used to be a storage area of some sort. Old, empty crates that are slowly decaying into piles of rubble line one wall. Heavy mist smelling of decayed wood covers everything in a hazy glow. The wooden planks of the floor are rotten and treacherous near the back of the room. A small door stands open to the north.

The plank comes to an end where it meets the first ghost ship. The bow rises out of the dark water, the only memorial to the crew who lost their lives when it sunk. The mast has snapped off at the base and the wood of the deck is slick with sea spray, though still stable enough to be carefully navigated. The pirate ship is somewhere to the southwest. A small wooden door leads below decks.

This small beach is enclosed on all sides by high, formidable cliffs. The sand has an orange cast to it, which contrasts sharply with the lead grey sea and the darker grey of the cliffs. The surf rushes up over the sand, erasing the marks of anyone's passing with frustrating efficiency. A gap in the cliffs is visible to the north. The ship graveyard stretches off to the the south, accessible by a trail of large white boulders.

Sea water laps at the walls of this room, covering over the stairway that leads down to the next submerged level. The rotted floor is dotted with broken drainage grates that can not compete with the sheer amount of water flooding the room. The door to the north leads away into darkness, while the daylight seems to be coming from down below. The ship must be tilted for the light to come through in this odd way.

Either the water level is rising, or the ship is laying at an angle in the sea. All that really matters is that the water is covering the lower, southern portion of this room. A few storage containers are lined up along the walls where the floor is still fairly dry, but their contents have long since spoiled beyond recognition. The door to the north is the only exit besides going down the stairs and into the water.

White boulders marbled with green algae thrust up out of the ocean. They are placed in an eerily straight line between the closest ship and the shoreline to the north. The grey waters crash over them, leaving the boulders dully reflective and slippery. The beach to the north is a gash of ruddy color amongst the grey stone of the surrounding cliffs.

Lined with shattered floor grates, the walls show the devastating effect of being constantly under water. The wooden planks of the floor are not in any better condition than the dilapidated walls and threaten to give out under any undue pressure without a moment's notice. The only exits are up the stairs or through the door to the north.

The rank odor in the air permeates the ship nauseatingly. Jagged holes gape in the floor where the rotted planks have given way under too much weight. The overwhelming darkness closes in over everything, making the soft glow of daylight just barely visible down the hallway to the north stand out starkly in the oppressive gloom. There is another darker exit to the southeast.

Heavy, dust-filled cobwebs hang from the ceiling, trailing down through the musty air. The misty floor is littered with the dirty strands of spider silk. Smashed grates in the floor are almost completely obscured by the pale blanket that covers everything. Stairs lead up towards murky daylight and down into deeper darkness.

This pathway of planks provides a treacherous walkway out over the fitful sea. Salty water creeps with curious, foamy fingers over the wood to leave it wet and slick. The pathway seems oddly contrived in this otherwise haphazardly arranged maze. It leads north towards one of the broken ships and east into the mist.

Daylight pours in from a door to the south, revealing a partially flooded floor. Sea water laps at the middle of the slanted wooden plank floor, covering over the stairway leading down. Holes gape along the walls of the half-submerged room, forcing anyone walking through to stick to the middle of the room.

Blessedly dry and even warm, this is the perfect place to rest for a little while. Heavy wooden doors prevent any monsters from disturbing the occupants of the room while they recuperate. Locked chests and boxes line the walls, but there is still just enough open floor in the center of the chamber to pitch a small tent. A door leads out into a larger room and stairs head towards the top deck of the ship.

The portholes along the exposed side of this shattered ship stare out at its final resting place with an eerie blind gaze. The water laps at a few planks, all that remains unsubmerged. Thick mist closes in, leaving this unsteady remnant alone in the ocean for the moment. The only way off of the planks is the stepping stone to the west, barely visible in the pale mist.

Decayed planks end in ragged edges, creating a small island of a platform. Shaky, damp stairs lead up off of the platform and toward the weak sunlight. To the west, a few steps allow access to a section of the ship that is otherwise invisible beneath the cold, dark water. The air is damp and chilly, leaving the surface of the wood dangerously slick.

The ship has come to rest in a place meant for the dead. The lost husks of sunken ships jut out of the water at awkward angles like badly broken bones. This still-intact ship is a tenuous refuge from the terrors of the surrounding place, which can only be called... a ship graveyard.

A small section of the deck is all that remains of this once sturdy and dependable vessel. A partially shattered beam, probably once part of the mast, now lies horizontally across the water, creating a path to the west. A strange white stepping stone leads east and a path of planks leads south.

This dead-end room is partially submerged in dark, dirty sea water. The smell of decaying matter suffuses the air sickeningly, adding to the gloomy atmosphere. The darkness is so complete that the walls are only visible once they are close enough to be touched. The weight of the massive ship overhead presses down on this small chamber, aggravating any latent claustrophic tendencies a traveler might be trying to suppress.

The dim, overcast skies cover the graveyard of ships in light the color of yellowed bones. The ships bob like the broken toys of a careless child as the water crests in waves all around them. The deck of this ship, damp with sea spray, is full of holes. A stairway leads down into the ship and to the east, a beam thrusts out over the ocean and into the mist.

Below decks, the ship is partially flooded with murky seawater that seeps in through the jagged holes in the floor. Shattered windows of look out onto the seemingly endless graveyard. An old, yellowed map still rests against the northern windowed wall of the cabin. A door leads back out onto the deck and a staircase in the southeast corner of the room leads down.

The southern end of this part of the field is lined with flowers.  The forest around the field is bright and cheerful.  A stream runs southward, out of a pond, into the forest.  To the north, the path turns back into the forest, while west leads over a bridge.

The field continues along the edge of the woods.  The stream disappears north, into the woods where it can't be followed. The ground is crossed with rabite trails. A bridge leads across the stream to another part of the field, while to the south a narrow path leads alongside the stream through the field.

The path runs alongside the canal. A patch of tall, thick grass grows just south of the canal, where the path leads into the forest. The path leads away to the east, following the canal.  A few flowers line it as it enters the forest to the south.

The path divides, north and south.  To the west, a fairly large pond is visible. To the south, the field continues around the edge of the woods. To the north, the path leads to the edge of the water a short distance away.

A small clearing opens to the northeast.  The western edge of the clearing is lined with a number of flowers. The woods to the west are bright and cheery. Off in the distance, the sound of running water can be heard.  To the southeast, a path leads away, while northeast leads to another clearing.

The path has narrowed considerably.  The forest is quieter than elsewhere.  Only a very few rabite trails pass through this part of the path. A few stones line the path to the west, while to the north the path leads to a canal.

The path runs alongside a canal.  The path has narrowed considerably due to the trees to the south and the canal to the north, but is still easily passable. It continues along the canal to the east and the west, until it turns south into the forest again.

A clearing opens northward. A few flowers line the edges of the clearing, but for the most part the ground is clear.  A small patch of tall grass sits in the south of the clearing.  To the north, the field stretches to a small channel of water.  To the southwest, another clearing is visible.

A canal runs just north of the path.  The canal is bounded on this side by a low levee made of mud and stone.  A few stones have fallen from the levee and now lay on the path.  To the west, the path continues along the levee, while to the south it leaves the water behind.
A small cave opens up around this area.  The stones in this area look a little strange.  You get the feeling this is the home of an... unholy... beast.

A few flowers line the field to the north.  The ground is covered in rabite trails, as far as the eye can see.  The field continues northward from this place, while to the west it stretches to a stream off in the distance.

The village is barely visible from this side of the stream.   More rabite trails can be seen on the ground, all of them well travelled. To the north, the field continues into the woods.  A bridge leads east over a small stream, back towards the village.

The path narrows a bit along this part of the field.  The trees to either side are quite close, but there is room to pass between them.  A few rabite trails pass through, but not many.  To the north and south, the path turns west and opens up into an open field again.

The field stretches out to the east, as far as the eye can see.  Rabite trails lead through the field, making it easier to travel. The woods to the north and south of the field are bright and cheery.  Further to the east, the field turns away, out of sight, while to the west a bridge leads across a small stream.

Rabite trails run along the ground through the field.  Just to the west, a small bridge spans a babbling brook. The field seems to continue on through a wooded glen further to the west, while to the east Potos Village can be seen.

The path ends at a slope into this pond. The pond extends west, then south, then leads into a stream.  The sun warms the water to a comfortable temperature.  To the north, the waterfalls that feed this pond can be seen.  To the south, the path leads away from the pond.

The pond ends just to the south.  A few water flowers are growing in the pond.  A stone pedestal sits in the center of the pond, looking important.  A few waterfalls can be seen to the north, past where the pond ends. To the east, the path leads out of the pond.

The field goes no further.  To the north, the lake prevents further travel, while south and west are blocked by trees.  The field is filled with flowers, and a large patch of tall grass grows near the western edge.  To the east, a bridge leads across a stream.

The southern wall marks the end of this tunnel, with the railway coming from the north and stopping shortly before the rock face. A coal cart rests against a buffer stop at the end of the line, filled with rocks from the rock face. In an alcove to the west, a set of ascending stairs have been carved from the surrounding rocks. Icy winds stream into the tunnel from the opening at the head of the stairs, drawing with it flurries of snow from outside.

A layer of snow covers this rocky ledge overlooking the town of Narshe. A wooden cantilever bridge runs to the west, crossing over the approach to the mine entrance below. Above and to the east lies a building jutting from the rock face, supported partially by a set of stilts. In an opening in the rock to the northeast lies a set of descending stairs, leading down and into the mine.

A set of stairs in the center of the room ascend to a raised dais to the north, on which sits a fractured block of luminescent ice. The only light is a soft blue glow coming from the fractured block and the chunks of ice scattered around it. The sole exit lies to the south.

Wide streaks of slime crisscross the floor of this dimly-lit chamber. Several hollows are visible in the chamber walls, many of which are filled with refuse. A decaying corpse lays against the wall, next to a chipped and overturned feeding bowl. A passage continues to the north, and a soft blue glow from that direction lends a small measure of light to this chamber. To the south lies a broken gate.

In the cliff face to the northeast is a small cave entrance. To the south is a set of wooden stairs leading to a lower ledge, and beyond that the town of Narshe. A large metal vessel sits to the side of the stairs. East of the ledge, a bridge that once crossed the eastern crevasse now lies broken and cannot be crossed.

The mine continues south, while a low cave opening, to the west, leads to the main tunnel. A section of railway makes a sharp turn, exiting the room via the opening to the west, and the mine to the south. Towering in a corner of the room is a huge engine made of steam pipes, cables, and spinning wheels. The engine leaves just enough clearance for the railway's coal carts to navigate the tight turn. The air is warmer, due to the heat radiated by the engine, and the occasional puff of steam emitted.

This snow-covered, rocky ledge overlooks the town of Narshe, to the south. The ledge continues to the east, and to the northwest lies a small cave entrance. West of the ledge, a bridge that once crossed the western crevasse now lies broken and cannot be crossed. Directly underneath the ledge lies the entrance to the Narshe Mine.

The remains of a broken gate, which once blocked transit through the opening to the north, now hangs from a single hinge on its frame. From the cave walls on each side of the gate hang large oil lamps, now doused. To the south lies a small loading platform and buffer stop for the railway, which heads further south into the tunnel.

A pair of extinguished torches hang from the walls of this small, dimly-lit chamber. Without the torches, the only light comes from outside, via the two entrances to the southeast and southwest. Crates of goods are stacked against the natural stone walls, and a draft continually passes through the cave.

This large, rocky ledge gives a beautiful view of the surroundings: the rooftops and glowing windows of Narshe to the south; the rugged, snowy, and cloud-wreathed mountains to the north; the wooden cantilever bridge east, spanning the gap between the ledges. A set of wooden stairs climbs north, higher into the foothills. An abandoned shack lies to the west.

The stone walls narrow here, and the wooden shoring reinforcing the tunnel creates a narrow space through which an iron railway passes, traveling from the south and ending at a buffer stop to the north. There is enough room for the passage of a coal cart, and little else. A single electric lamp hangs from the shoring overhead, its flickering light casting shadows on the walls.

A long, wooden cantilever bridge extends over the road in Narshe, from a narrow ledge to the east to a larger ledge to the west. Snowcapped mountains stretch out to the north, and the town of Narshe can be seen to the south, and below the bridge. Strong gusts of wind cause the bridge to creak and groan, and the icy wooden flooring leaves little traction to be had.

A long, dark mining tunnel stretches to the north and south, while a secondary cave opening is carved through a section of the eastern wall. The air is damp and cold, and chilly gusts of wind draw in the frigid air from outside of the mine. Strung across the walls are lengths of cable, which connect a series of electric lamps that lend a hazy purplish light to everything nearby: the railway, the roughly hewn stone walls, and the wooden beams reinforcing the low ceiling overhead.

The low, groaning sound is getting really loud, this close to the entrance to the mineshaft just ahead. An eerie purple light comes out of it, giving the mine quite an ominous appearance. Another bridge lies between the two mountainsides, just about fifteen feet overhead.

The winds from the mountains blow around the snow atop the mountain, making it seem colder than it really is. Farther away, you can spot a passage leading into the snow to the north.  It is possible to jump down the ledge to reach it.

The wind atop the mountain is rather chilly and makes it unbearably cold to stay here long. There seems to be a path in the snow leading to the other side of the mountain, but you cannot be sure, as there is a lot of snow obscuring your vision.
The winds from the mountains blow around the snow atop the mountain, making it seem colder than it really is. Farther away, you can spot a passage leading into the northern part of the mountain.
The winds from the mountains blow around the snow atop the mountain, making it seem colder than it really is. Farther away, you can spot a passage leading into the snow to the north.
The winds seem to have calmed down here, and you can see that this is clearly a dead end. Maybe if you backtrack you can find out where the northern side is.

The winds from the mountains blow around the snow atop the mountain, making it seem colder than it really is. Farther away, you can see the other side of the mountain... But not in this path that you have taken, for this one is a dead end.

This is the mountaintop at Narshe. You can see the village below and the mine complex also. Lots of snow has gathered here and there seems to be a small path leading to the north. Perhaps to something good, or a trap.

You have come upon a deadend. The ceiling here is very low, and the only light that allows you to see comes from behind you, to the east. Here, again, rodent droppings cover the floor in a nasty mess. It seems a colony of wererats made this place their lair.

This is the foot of a long wooden stairway darting upward in this huge cavern. The freezing wind here blows quite fast. East of here is a deep, deep chasm, crossed by a rope bridge leading to another part of this gigantic cave.

You have now arrived upon a weird part of this cave. The tunnel goes east and west, but in the wall to the south is a small opening. Taking a closer look, you can see that there is a small set of stairs leading down into the darkness. Strangely, you can hear some kind of singing coming from deep in that darkness...

A set of wide sturdy wooden walkways have been built extending over a deep and deadly-looking gap in the stone ground. The walkway extends in three directions from a T-junction, but the area to the west looks like a small dead end.

The cold Narshe winds are in full force on this, the front side of the mountain. There is snow all around, covering the somewhat narrow ledges and the cliff face itself. The town is actually completely out of view here, due to a large jutting piece of the mountain that is in the way. There is a way to the south, and a westward path seems to lead to a staircase in the distance. There is also an entrance into a cave here.
The ground here seems to become slightly lower than the one to the east. The cavern plunges down into the darkness south of there. Here too, the air smells awfully bad.

This passage is along a staircase, or rather, a series of staircases. Pipes run along the ceiling and a generator wheel turns here. Torches and a lamp provide the lighting for the area. The passage goes both north and south, with a wind whistling through the cave, making the torches flicker briefly.

Raised above the rest of the cave is an old campsite for miners, with benches surrounding a burnt-out campfire and an old storage chest full of rusted cutlery. The site has good visibility but is nested deep inside the rock, making the place seem safe and secure.
This is another part of the mine where a curve appears in front of you. The way now leads west and south from here.

rooms.name: The Western Cavern of the Moogle Den

userData.LongDescription: This portion of the cavern stretches to the south, where a cave-in seems to have collapsed what used to have been a staircase that led to another section of the cave.  The warm, homey atmosphere of the adjoining cave to the east doesn't seem to stretch into this section of the caves.  A small wooden chest lies beneath a light layer of rocks, its loot having been plundered what could have been ages ago.  The only way out seems to be beneath the archway to the east, heading back into the den of some kind of creature or creatures.

From here, on high ground, you can see very clearly where you are. To the south stretch the long plains of the Narshe valley. North are the high mountains tower over the small Narshe village just east of here. An opening in the mountain to the north goes back inside the mountains themselves. To the east, a bridge used to lead to a ledge leading down toward the town, but it seems to have been ripped off by the strong winds blowing here.

The walls of the cave run north and east, making it impossible to travel west or south.  Straw lies scattered on the ground in some areas while, at the same time, appears to be collected into piles in other areas of the cavern floor.  To the east, the cave wall leads to a small alcove where a wooden door has been set into the wall.  To the north, a stone archway leads to a darker part of the cave.
This narrow tunnel is clearly carved out by human tools, and is barely high enough to stand up in. A curve in the tunnel, following the vein of coal, goes from the south to the east.

This room in Narshe's secret exit mine passage is very small. A torch burns on the north wall, illuminating the rocky walls and pipes in the ceiling. A switch lies to the northwest, no doubt used to manipulate the secret passage in the past. The exit to this passage is to the south and a staircase to the northeast leads deeper into the mines.

You were thinking earlier that this cave was natural, but, surprisingly, to the north is a set of stairs leading up inside the mountain. The ceiling is still too high for you to see, as it is lost in the deep darkness above you. An eerie, purple light comes from the walls, lighting your way through this very weird cave. Once more, an acrid smell lingers in the air here, yet it's a bit weaker than the one you noticed earlier.

The wind is extremely harsh here, with no cover whatsoever, and the ground is covered in snow. It's possible to see the Narshe plains in the distance, but the cliffs make it impossible to see anything to the north. There is a tall staircase here leading up the cliffs, built purely out of wood, and there is a path along the cliffs to the east.

From this snowy ledge it would be possible to see out onto the Narshe plains on a clear day, but sadly, today is not a clear day with the wind and snow around. Still, it's possible to see the walkway near the mountain down below, but Narshe proper is blocked out by more cliff face. You can almost see the entrance to Narshe, but the roof of the house that the cliff leads onto is also in the way. The only path is back to the north.

The atmosphere of the den feels warm and inviting; a near perfect environment to lay down roots.  The cave stretches to the east, where it curves south into a small alcove with an odd, wooden door somehow attached to the cave walls.  Just to the west, a large archway made of rock leads to a different portion of the cave.  To the south, the walls curve east towards that strange, wooden door.

Spanning a deep gap in the cavern below are a series of narrow wooden walkways. For the most part, they seem sturdy, but there are no handrails, and one plank is missing. The walkways form a bridge between various dug-out stone areas filled with mining tools.

This small circular area is mainly illuminated by a strong, single burning torch on the northern wall, and the shape of the cavern makes this area shielded from the wind that is audible through the cavern opening to the east. The western wall of this cavern has scratches and scrawls on it, some of a whimsical nature, and some just seemingly random. To the south is a staircase leading into what looks to be an internal room for this passage.

This section of the mine, though dangerous, has tools. To the north, a set of roughly cut set of stairs leads to some kind of wooden bridge. Coming from somewhere in the cave, a foul smell assaults your nostrils.
The ceiling here is very low, and the floor is covered with rodent droppings.  An old rusted mine cart is filled with ratty scraps of cloth, turned into some kind of nest.

This interior cave ledge is just wide enough to allow passage. Just west is a rope bridge, crossing a deep chasm. From the south comes a very strong blowing wind, erupting from a hole in the wall, which probably leads outside.

The cozy atmosphere permeates the air of the moogle den.  Many straw beds, obviously made for moogles, are scattered throughout parts of the cave.  The ceiling of the cave extends high into the air.  Far to the south, a wooden door can be seen.  Far to the west, a stone archway leads to a different section of the den.

This spacious cavern seems to hide many mysteries in its depths.  Large, natural pillars of rock climb several yards into the air, meeting a cavern ceiling that would be high above even the tallest human.  The cavern dwindles down to a smaller alcove to the south.  To the north, the cave also dwindles to what seems to be a wooden door of all things.

The sight from here is astounding. You are standing just outside an opening in the stone wall on the north, while, all around you, is the hugest cavern you have ever visited. The ceiling is lost in the darkness, water dripping from its heights as small dropplets. A strong wind blows here, darting inside the small tunnel to the north. A set of wooden stairs, probably added by the inhabitants of Narshe, plunges down into the darkness.

The walls of this alcove in the cave narrow slightly to the south as the cave opens up into a much wider, more spacious portion of the cave.  Pillars of rock jut into the air, giving the illusion that the cavern is almost like a giant maze.  Oddly enough, a rather ordinary, if old, wooden door provides the only passage to the north.

As you walk in the mine, you can hear some kind of low moan coming from deep inside. It's probably nothing more than machinery... The roof here is about 8 feet high, and a long wire, stretching from deeper in the mine, seems to give energy to the lamps tilting over your head. The floor is covered with what must be rodent litter. The tunnel goes west from here.

The ceiling in this section of the mine is much higher than the one in the other corridors. Judging by the aspect of the walls, this is probably a natural cave that the miners uncovered. The tunnel goes west, from where you can hear scurrying sounds, and east in another part of the natural cave.

This is a rather small alcove inside the cave portion of the Narshe mines.  Most of this portion of the mine seems relatively untouched by whatever was used to carve the stone of the main section of the mine.  To the north, the mine opens up into a large cavern with pillars giving the area a maze-like feeling.  Slightly to the west, a staircase carved from rock leads to another portion of the mine.

This spacious cave has the appearance of being lived in.  Several straw-woven rugs litter the ground.  Many piles of straw are scattered here and there, almost looking as though they are beds, but they're much too small to be made for humans.  A narrow passage leads south to a wooden door.  An archway of stone leads west, to a different section of the den.

rooms.name: A small section of the mine

userData.LongDescription: This is a small section of the cave, where the walls wrap around in all directions, making the only exit the one to the east.  Rocks crumble off of the walls, filling the floor with many pebbles.  A small chest sits on the ground, resting against the western wall, but it seems to be locked.

This room is expansive, and it's amazing that it even fits underground. The floor underfoot is a mix of the standard floor here, gold-covered tiling, and metal grating. The walls are filled with torches and statues, and the pyramid in the center has even more torches and statues on it. Two massive pillars near the back of the room support the ceiling high above, and the fog falls down through the grating, being heavier than air. A staircase up the side of the altar leads to the top, while to the south is the passage out of this creepy place.

This pit is dark, with only the light from above illuminating it. On the southern part of the room is a row of spikes that look very deadly. The rest of the room is surrounded by normal stone walls, and the ground is gilded with golden patterns and tile. A rope leads up out of the pit.

This corner is a bit higher than the rest of the floor, as a short set of stairs from the south lead up to it. The light from the south also illuminates this corner, though the fog is regaining its density, reducing the usefulness. There are torches and statues here, as expected. The west passage leads to another south-leading corner.

This corner of the hall has the heaviest fog in the area, with the wall torches just barely spreading the light needed to see. There are more cat statues on the walls here in between the torches, as well as a decaying body. The hall goes north and west from here, leading deeper into the darkness of the ruins.

The foyer to this place is dark, but the torches in the walls provide enough light to see by. There are four more statues here, as well as a large center tile area. There is one large tile in the center of the room, and a path of them leading towards a main door. There are also two smaller doors to the left and right of the room.

This first intersection on this floor corresponds with a change in the walls, from the alternating cat faces and torches, to simply torches. Through the fog it is possible to see three directions to go in the distance: north to a distant door, south to a stairway, or east towards the entrance.

The most noticeable thing about this room is that there is no fog in here. The constantly closed door must keep any serious amount of fog out. A large table sits in the center of the room with three chairs on one side and four lit candles on it. Sitting up against the northern wall there are a pair of cabinets and a pair of decorative armors. The back wall, on the other hand, has two swords, two candelabras, and some plants hung in one of the upper corners. There's only one way out of this room: the entry door.

This small fog-filled room widens a little from the intersection area, with torches on the walls of the room. Another body lies in the corner here, decayed beyond belief. There is a staircase to the south, leading to the next floor of this dangerous ruin, as well as the corridor towards the northern intersection.

The light from the hole in the ceiling can barely be seen, leaving this corner as dark as the majority of the ruins. It's illuminated by the simple torches, with the magical fog doing its best to make up for the visibility of the last few rooms. From this corner it's possible to see the next major stairway, leading down from the room to the south.

Another piece of this twisty passage leading through the ruins has the same type of statues and torches as the rest of this place. To the west is the first intersection in this place, while down a slight staircase to the south is the path towards the exit.

rooms.name: Entrance to the Basement of the Ruins

userData.LongDescription: This part of the underground basement area of the ruins is filled with a magical fog, making it difficult to see clearly. There are more cat statues on the walls, as well as some torches that still manage to provide enough light to see. A door here opens to the stairs, while a dark corridor leads south.

This small room widens a little from the hallway, just enough to fit two door-flanking torches on the northern wall. Three stone cat faces sit on the northern wall as well, looking over this tiny side-room. The door to the north is the only other exit from the room besides the southern corridor.

This corner of the hallway has had a number of the torches go out, leaving it dark and difficult to see in. The fog all over makes it almost impossible to see the lit torches to west and north, which must be the only ways out of this darkness. A few torches here remain lit, but cannot do much more than announce their presence by their light.

This room is absurdly well lit, and well kept too. The statues on the wall look flawless, the torches bright and full of fuel, and the stone walls smooth and shiny. Fog fills the area here, but it isn't so much of a concern. Two pillars hold up an overhang covered in even more torches, as well as the ceiling. To the north is a wide open room with a pyramidal altar, and the door here leads to the second floor.

The walls in this hallway are evenly covered with torches, spreading enough light through the fog to see by. This part of the hall twists so that it is impossible to see anything but that the corridor goes south and north from this small stretch. The pervasive fog flows around like water, almost.

This courtyard is a large area just inside the ruin walls, with a brick path leading up to the main stairs. Even more of those gargoyle statues stand watch here silently. There are a number of spikes blocking the left and right paths, but the main staircase leads up to a large door in the middle.

This whole room seems to be centered around the gargoyle statue sitting on a dais in the northern part of the room. There are three of the odd cat faces on either side, as well as two candelabras with lit candles in them. This is a dead end room, with the only exit being the door.

It seems strange that a room like this exists in the ruins. A large table sits in the center of the room with three chairs on the northern side and four lit candles on it. Sitting up against the northern wall there are a pair of cabinets and a pair of decorative armors. The back wall has two swords, two candelabras, and some plants hung in one of the upper corners. There's only one way out of this room: the entry door.

The walls in the corridor are evenly covered with torches, providing light to see by in this thick fog, as has been the case for the rest of the ruins. This part of the hall bends, which makes it impossible to see anything but that the corridor goes south and north from this small stretch.

The fog is very thick down here, making it difficult to see more than a few feet. A stone wall sits to the north, underneath the balcony, while two pillars with a torch on each and the row of torches on southern wall provide all the available light. A staircase leads up to the balcony, and a hallway goes south into the dark fog.

Up the long staircase, this altar stands at the center of the ruins. A floor with intricate golden patterns makes up the top of the pyramid. It is possible to see all the torches around the top of the room from here, as well as many other details of the statues around here, due to the fog being so light. A large hole is here, leading down to a pit below the altar, while the stairs lead to the floor of the room.

This hallway is strewn with broken and battered skeletons, few of which have anything approaching equipment on them. The torches on the wall make this place look even more scary, their fog-piercing light highlighting what is left of these people. To the east is a area where most of the torches are out, while to the north there is more of this ruin.

This corner of the hall is relatively clean, compared to the mess of bones to the south. Torches are lighting this part of the hall well, making it possible to see the standard cat statues on the wall. The fog is present, as always in this place, and to the west it is possible to see a well lit turn in the hall, filled with rubble. South, of course, is the corner filled with bones.

There is a strange balcony here, overlooking the first room of the second ruins basement area. There isn't much more than a stone bump separating the balcony from the room below, and it's not a very wide balcony either. The floor here is made of tile patterns, as opposed to the rest of the ruins' stone. A staircase on the western side leads down to the floor of this entry room, and a door leads up to the first floor.

This corner has less fog than the one to the east, but otherwise is very similar. There are more cat statues along the walls, as well as the torches that keep this place from being pitch black. To the east is the way to the exit, while going north takes one deeper into these ruins.

On this small balcony there are three arches, marking the entrance to this place. Right under them is the large entry door, as well as four stone faces above each archway pillar. Oddly enough, there are also a lot of small torches set above the arches that are invisible from the courtyard. It's still impossible to see over the walls, though, even from this raised perspective.

This small hallway only seems to serve as a turn-around leading from the door to the stairs downward. There's not much to it, only some of the simple wall torches, a pair of statues, the entrance door, and the stairs down. Some strange magical fog can be seen creeping up the stairs, looking dark and purple.

This corner of the ruins has collapsed in, leaving rubble all over the floor. All of this light makes it easy to see, though, with the bright sunlight piercing the fog well. There are plenty of torches in the walls, but they're irrelevant, with all the open light. The fresh air coming in through this hole also makes the stench of death in the rest of these ruins painfully clear. To the north and east are normal, dark, fog-filled corners in the ruins.
In every direction, nothing but all consuming blackness can be seen. Somehow the ground feels solid despite not actually being visible. The only exit may in fact be to summon the Phantom Train.

Occasionally, a flash of white, or a few points of light can be seen, though they vanish just as soon as they appear.  A cold wind blows through the forest, causing the bushes and trees to rustle ever so slightly.  Oddly enough, one of the larger trees has something carved into it, though it's kind of hard to believe that anything else living has been through here.

The path keeps on to the west, ultimately leading towards a train far off in the distance.  It's still rather difficult to make out any specific details about it, but it's easy to tell that its engine is sending out a rather thick plume of smoke.  The exit to the forest lies a good distance to the south, while the way to the east leads to the train.

rooms.name: Before a Fallen Log in the Phantom Forest

userData.LongDescription: Oddly enough, a huge log lies across the path, half of it buried into the ground.  There are no small plants, or mushrooms growing on it, nor are there any animals living in it.  Additionally, there's no sign at all of disease, or decay anywhere at all on it.  Indeed, it's almost as if a tree decided that it no longer wanted to stand up straight, and one of the rare few humans to enter this place later cut away the top portion of it to make further passage a bit easier.

A soft wind rustles through the thick, thick trees of this obviously haunted forest.  The only sound that can be heard is a soft, far away moaning from a decidedly human source.  Despite this, though, there's a very well defined path leading through this place, lined on either side by grass and bushes.  To the east, the path leads deeper into the woods, while to the west, the path leads out of the forest.

rooms.name: A sharp turn in the path

userData.LongDescription: The path makes a sharp turn south, and there's a rickety, wooden signpost near by to make that perfectly clear by pointing in that direction.  The rather eerie mood of the forest is enhanced by a now not-so-distant moaning coming from further down the path.  Of course, if one were feeling a bit faint of heart, he could always turn back west to leave.

Nearly invisible spirits dance and fly over the surface of the pond, while the water sparkles with an otherworldly essence.  A small rock sticking up out of the water with a strange flower growing out of it.  Oddly enough, no other such flowers grow in the forest, so one must wonder how this one got here.  A natural spring bubbles along the shore, its water flowing into the enchanted pond.

rooms.name: A trail through the Phantom Forest

userData.LongDescription: As the path continues deeper into this decidedly spooky place, the moaning gets just a little bit louder.  Additionally, a small rock sticks out of the ground, and though it's actually rather inconsequential, it's one of the few things that breaks the almost painful sense of same-ness in this forest.  The path pushes on further to the east, while the less brave can go back to the west.

This segment of the twisting path through the Phantom Forest leads even deeper in, and even closer to the source of the moaning of the departed.  A thin wisp of smoke can be seen off in the distance, though it'd be hard to imagine what might be creating it.  Back to the north, the road leads back out of the forest, for the sake of the less than brave.

rooms.name: Before an enchanted body of water

userData.LongDescription: Although there's a bush or two growing on the extreme east and west sides of this body of water, its banks are mostly clear of plant life and other debris.  In place of living organisms, spirits fly in circles above the water's surface.  The lake itself gives off an unnaturally perfect reflection, with the trees on the other side creating a landscape that most any painter would love to see.  There's still a fairly easy to follow path going to the east and south, with east leading further into the forest, and south leading towards the exit.

The path makes another sharp turn north, leading towards a wooden platform that stands before the train waiting off in the distance.  It's obvious, now, what the purpose of the train is, as a line of ghostly figures trail towards it, waiting to take their final ride to the after life.  The path also leads back to the west, and to the outside, for the faint of heart.

Just ahead, the Phantom Train awaits, giving off an aura of unwelcome-ness to the not deceased.  A long, seemingly endless line of spirits trails from the forest to the south towards this vehicle, hoping to finally find their peace on the other side.  A set of stairs lead up to the train to allow access, but it may not be the best of ideas to sneak on without being dead, as the locals may not be too receptive towards warm bodies.

rooms.name: A trail in the Phantom Forest

userData.LongDescription: An exceptionally large tree... perhaps the cousin to the one that fell to the west... shoots up from the northern half of the path.  However, unlike the trees in most forests, there are no nests adorning the branches of this behemoth, nor are there animals crawling in, or through it.  To the west, over the fallen log, lies the way out, while to the east, past this gargantuan tree, lies the path deeper into the forest.

The path here branches out to the north, and also to the south.  To the north, there's a wisp of smoke floating upwards from an unseen source, and to the south, the mists of the forest are thick, obscuring whatever may lie in that direction.  Occasionally, flashes of light can be seen, though it's hard to say whether they're real, or just the tricks of a bored forest dweller.

rooms.name: Before a northern turn in the path

userData.LongDescription: The path makes an abrupt turn to the north, and there is a sign posted next to it to indicate this.  In that direction, there is a large pond... or maybe a small lake surrounded by trees, and dotted with small pieces of land.  Back the west lies the exit to the forest, and the fallen log, while the moaning of the dead lies to the north.

There is just enough room for one in this spot.  There's not much to see here.  Just another ledge across the moat that's a part of castle.  A small door is there too.  The moat below is running through some grates underneath the castle.  It's more purplish here.  A leather-armored skeleton is stuck in the drain, and the head is slightly crushed.  Another gruesome death from the war.

This room is full of katanas, formerly used by the swordsmen of Doma.  The curved swords are stacked neatly against the walls of the room.  A ghostly old man hovers behind a counter, pointing to a sign on the wall.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs along the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside of outside.  Down below, in the inside, is the dock platform, where most of the goods that were brought in were stored.  Outside, down below, is the path around the castle and the moat.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs along the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside of outside.  There's a building above you, a storage depot for the soldiers.  Down below, you can see the whole inside of the castle.  On the outside is part of the graveyard and most of the outside pathway.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs along the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside of outside.  Down below is the inside of the castle, open in all its glory.  Outside is the main door and the moat.  The horizon stretches for miles, a beautiful sight indeed.

This is the Elite Crossbowmen's Room.  This room is furnished just like the Elite Guards, and it may be a bit nicer.  A large target rests on one wall and their are still some arrows lodged in it.  There are several bunks here, about 10.  Many of the men slept with their crossbows, so there's a small little holster by each bunk.  A large desk rests near the door, covered in papers.  A closet held all of their things, before the raid on the castle.

Waves crash hard upon the stone docks of Doma Castle.  Small concrete posts are used to tie the boats down, and some still have ropes tied around them.  The moat here is a bit muddy, but turns bluer as you look out over the ocean.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs along the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside of outside.  Down below, you can see inside and outside. Inside is the outside market, and on the outside is the eastern side of the castle.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs along the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside of outside.  Down below, in the inside, is the dock platform, where most of the goods are stored.  On the outside stretches out the docks, where the goods are recieved. You can also see the beach from here.
The wall of the castle is now half-way submerged in the moat.  There seems to be some bubbles in the moat.  Looking in the water only reveals bubbles and something very dark and evil...

This is the 3rd area to the Marine Knights Quarters.  This is where most of the bunks are located, but there is still a large opening to run out to the stairwell.  Most of the men in this area were training to become Crossbowmen, the Elite Guards' offensive air support.  You can still see notches and other groves in a large target on the wall where the men practiced shooting with their crossbows.  These men were the support for their fellow Marine Knights, but they were still main fighters.

rooms.name: Outside the corner of Doma Castle

userData.LongDescription: This is the corner of the outside of the castle.  A huge chunk of the top lies on the ground with a skeleton trapped underneath, probably one of the last soldiers who lived here or someone who was apart of the last war.  More rubble is scattered on the ground, a few skeletons and armor pieces lay about.  The moat appears to be a bit muddy here, almost getting a purplish color.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs along the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside of outside.  Down below, in the inside, is the dock platform, where most of the goods are stored.  Ouside is the corner of the castle and part of the docks.  You can see the grate that the poison is pouring through, and where the skeleton has it's head crushed.

This is the entrance to Doma Castle.  Looming like a dark monolith, this haunted castle stands as a reminder of the past wars between the great Doma nation and the evil Empire.  Rubble from the war still remains on the ground.  Huge chunks of the wall are missing.  Those pieces are all around on the ground, and there are some skeletons lying underneath them.  Paths around the castle are on each side of you.  A door swings open from a gust of wind.

A gray empty room stands before you.  It's full of empty boxes, all marked with the Doma Eagle.  They've all been opened, and some have been kicked in.  Most of the room has also been beatup, as the walls have lots of scratches on them...

This is where most of the residents of the Doma castle live.  The hall here is carpetted, unlike the soldier quarters.  The walls are also made of green marble.  A lot of the high officials and other outstanding members of the court have apartments here.  There are many statues lining the hallway, and most of them are of mythological origins.

A blue carpet with yellow embroiding greets you.  The rest of the floor is a red marble stone, which is beautifully crafted, and you can see a small bird in each one, almost like the symbol of Doma.  Stairs lead up to the main area of the castle, and they are very well crafted, as the rails are made of an old oak that it still today polished to perfection.  Two doors lead to the city like area under the main area.  Statues of the king and queen that last ruled the nation are sitting atop podiums next to the door to the courtyard.

This is the courtroom where those seeking an audience with the King and Queen gather.  This room stretches to the top of the castle, and some balconies look down on the courtroom from overhead.  Looking up, you can see the sky, as holes have been punched through by boulders thrown at the castle.  Back south, there are two swords crossed above the doorway leading back to the rest of the castle.  These swords are inhumanly huge, about 9 feet in length.  They rest on a shield, which is about 15 feet long.  The door to the throne room is north, with stairs leading to it.

rooms.name: Around the corner in the West Main Hall

userData.LongDescription: Here are more doors that lead to more soldier quarters.  This area leads to the stairs to the top level of the castle.  There are many paintings, going towards the heroes of late years.  The last is Cyan.

Sitting high above their subjects, King Alexander and Queen Ariel sat in these thrones.  They were surely once very beautiful, furnished with jewels, gold, silver, and silk.  They were built for royalty.  They sat upon a pyramid platform, with stairs that lead up to them.  Two suits of armor stand behind them, and watched the royal couple.  But that was then and this is now.  These seats have been robbed of their jewels and some parts have been hacked off.  And now the curse over this place has infected even the suits of armor.

This used to be the Doma Castle Inn.  There's lots of dust here, covering two lonely beds.  A dresser rests between the two beds.  A sign hangs upon the wall, telling visitors instructions about this room.

Slightly larger than the rest of the courtyard platform, this is the main one, which is actually on the main foundation of the castle.  Gray slopes in the water give more insight to this fact. A door with the symbol of Doma is ajar, and two skeletons that used to be guards lay next to it.  More bridges connect to here, connecting the market and dock platforms.  High above you can see the sun gleaming.

This is the end of the eastern hall, a bit of a large room where there are several doors and a stairwell.  One door leads to the apartment of the famous Cyan, one to a noble's room, and then there's the stairwell leading up to the castle ramparts.  A shelf hands in the corner, with several plants hanging from it.  A painting hangs on the wall.
A sign welcomes all visitors to the Courtroom.  The room is huge, and is connected to a larger area where the King and Queen held court.  High above, citizens could sit and watch trials from above.

Here is the long hallway that connects underneath the main stairs.  The inn door is here, and further down is the old market.  Back to the west is the trading shop, and everything seems quiet.  A large portrait of the King and Queen hangs here, watching and greeting all visitors.  Several large pots with dead roses and tulips hang from the ceiling.

This is home to the 2nd Legion Guards, brother-in-arms to the Elite Guards.  These men are still elite, but they are the lower branch, and are usually used to guard the castle and the citizens.  Most of these men will become Elite Guards or will be sent out to other Doma outposts.  This room is much like the neighboring room.  It's very well furnished, offering the best the castle has to offer.  There is one desk here, for the leader of the Legion.  There are 10 bunkbeds here, as this Legion has 20 men in it.  A closet stands open on one wall, barren.  A door to the west leads to more quarters.

Dark sinister forces have siezed this land, and you can feel the dark powers coming from it.  As most of the castle is basked in a evil glow, the graveyard is masked in a blanket of dark clouds, chilling winds, and creepy vibes.  There are several tombstones about, many of them desecrated, but some are still readable.  A note is attached to the gate.  The darkness is setting in...

This is an apartment for one of the nobles.  This room is quite nice.   It's covered in exotic furs from Narshe.  A large bed rest in the middle, some what of Narshe origin.  A large desk rests near it, covered in papers concerning the nation.  Across from it lies a shelf full of ancient books.  Next to the shelf is a large painting of the noble.

This is another platform in the courtyard.  It looks to be the practice area of the soldiers, but it also can act as an outside market area.  The catwalks above send shadows down, blanketing the area in small bits of darkness.  It looks a bit gloomy.  Some skeletons lay near the moat on a tattered blanket, and they are not wearing armor.

This is a small path around the castle.  It's a bit thin in some places and you can almost fall into the moat.  A large piece of the wall is missing, and one can see through to the inside of the courtyard.  The piece of the wall that fell is now halfway submerged in the moat, with the other half sticking on the side of the bank.  Moss is now covering it.  A skeleton is attached to the wall, its head missing.  More grim reminders of the war that went on here.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs along the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside of outside.  There's a building here, a storage depot for the soldiers.  Down below, you can see inside and outside.  Inside is the outside market and most of the platforms and bridges.  Outside is the eastern side of the castle, along with the front side.  Straight down below is the graveyard, surrounded in a dark mist.

This was the great Cyan's apartment.  The room is very well furnished.  A large king sized bed rests near the door, covered in green silk seats and a large green wool comforter.  The pillows are nicely fluffed.  A dresser hugs the corner, and there's nothing really in it.  Most of the room is stone, with green and gray marble blocks.  A painting of a blonde girl and a small boy hangs tilted over the bed.  A large window looks out over the moat.

Here is the western hall of the main level.  This is where most of the soldiers live.  Most of the rooms in this hall and further around the corner were built just for them.  Along the walls are paintings of the greatest warriors.  There are also several pedestals with statues of great beauties and heroes.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs along the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside of outside.  Down below, inside, is the area where the goods from the docks are taken.  Outside is just the western side of the castle, nothing special save the moat.

Here is the first guard area, home of the Doma Legion Guards.   These men were once the toughest band of fighters.  No one could stop them, and they never lost a battle.  That was until the Empire came along.  These troops were the first to die, caught underfire from the Magitek Armors.  This room is where they stayed, having 5 bunkbeds, a few desks, and a closet full of armor.

This is home to the Marine Knights, the castle's main guards.  Most of the Knights were killed during the war, and were a huge loss to the castle.  This is the biggest room in the Guards Quarter area, stretching most of the castle. Here you can see row after row of bunks, totaling over 200 bunks!  A shelf runs the entire length of the room, and this is where all the men stored their weapons, armor, and medals or trophies they may have gotten in battle.

rooms.name: Hall to shopping area of Doma

userData.LongDescription: This is a long hallway with a few doors.  The rooms have been turned into shops where a lot of imported goods are sold.  There's a cafe at the end of the hall, an inn right next door, and a weapon shop straight ahead.  Here the floor is a blue marble color, helping to distinguish it from the other floor.

rooms.name: Sentry Box atop the Castle Doma

userData.LongDescription: You are standing in a sentry's box atop Doma Castle.  It's not that big, just enough for a small group of soldiers to watch the distance.  And you can see in most directions.  It's very beautiful.  There's a small chair here, a bit weather-worn, but it still looks comfy.

You are standing in the inner courtyard of the castle.  It is made up of bridges that are connected at the doors, one to the outside at the south, and one to the north, leading inside.  There are other platforms to the northwest and northeast, but they are further north of here. The moat runs underneath, still a dingy muddy color. Above are the catwalks for the upper level.  A few pieces of rubble are scattered on the bridges here.  Some pieces of armor float along with the moat's current.  A skeleton lies near, in a sitting position.

You are standing on the top level of Doma Castle.  It's mainly gangplanks and small platforms that are held above the platforms below.  There's a sentry's box over to the east, peering out over the land surrounding Doma.  To the south you can see a path going around the edge of the castle, on top of some gangplanks and platforms.

A cold wind blows down from the stairs here.  The stairwell is kept in a bleak gray stone room, different from the halls that were plastered in red marble.  There's a painting here, portraiting some duel between two men.  A small podium holds a plant that seems to be dying.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside or outside.  In this spot, you could only fire at people down below.

This area is slightly smaller in comparision to the main and eastern areas of the Courtyard.  Here looks to be the main area where they receive goods.  A few boxes sit in the corner, unmarked and full of rotted crossbow ammuntition.  A door leading to the docks is closed.  A skeleton of a guard lies near the door.

You are standing on the top level of Doma Castle.  It's mainly gangplanks and small platforms that are held above the platfroms below.  You are standing near the top of the castle's Courtyard.  Rubble now covers the doors that once lead to the courtroom.  You can see that the main tower has been destroyed.  But it's a good thing that the stairs to the north weren't covered.
This is a small path around the castle.  It's above the moat and hugs the castle walls.  Pieces of armor and swords stick out all over the ground, and piles of wall rubble are scattered everywhere.

Just above the stairs leading out, this is the main area of the castle.  This room is the main area of the castle.   This room is huge, with two halls leading to various areas.  A door with the royal crest of the house of Doma and the Doma eagle stands erect across the stairs, inviting visitors to the royal court.  Several chandeliers hang from the ceiling, many sparkling with jewels.

rooms.name: Outside the corner of Doma Castle

userData.LongDescription: This corner of the castle is still pretty intact.  Moss has started covering the bottom of it and some skeletons are at the bottom.  A graveyard is further east, and a sign is posted next to an iron gate.  The small iron gate greets the weary who wish to pay homage to the dead.  The moat seems to go around the graveyard, and it's a bit clearer on this side.  Small fish swin about in it.

This is a land bridge leading to the once great castle of Doma.  A dark, muddy blue moat runs around the castle and under the bridge.  Several pieces of armor and swords can be seen sticking up out of the banks of the moat, a dim reminder of the wars that plagued this castle.  The castle stands in the distance, a mixture of technology and stonemasonry, but most of it is crumbling down.

This is an apartment for one of the nobles.  This room is quite nice.  It's covered in exotic furs from around the world.  A large bed rest in the middle, of Figaro origin.  A large desk rests near it, covered in papers concerning the nation.  A large painting hangs on the wall.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone outside or inside.  This area is a lot large than most, allowing a full detail of soldiers to line up and fire arrows at oncoming enemies down below.  Most of the inside can't be it, as this area stretches over most of it, connected by five metal beams.  Down below is the main door and the moat.

This is the Doma market area. This is where all the citizens went to sell their goods and to socialize. It is still filled with tiny little booths, still stocked with goods. All of them are worn from time and neglect, and none look too useful. The area is a bit indented into the ground, as you have to step down to get into it.

This is the room of a Doma noble.  Most of the room is heavily furnished, from silk bedding to woolen carpet and a tiger-fur chair. A desk in a corner seems to be made of an old oak, and it appears to be held together with brass nails.  There are a few paintings here and there, many of them of the noble.  A bed rests in the middle, with red sheets and a curtain around it.

This is 2nd area of the Marine Knights Quarters, and this is the main practice area.  Here, after hours, the soldier would practice with wooden swords, trying the hone their combat prowess.  A circle drawn with white paint is in the middle of the floor. The shelf still runs the wall, still empty.

You are now on a path around the castle.  It's mostly a gangplank that runs along the edge of the castle, allowing the soldiers to fire at anyone inside of outside.  Down below, you can see inside and outside. Inside is the outside market, and outside is the behind side of the castle.

This house is well-built, but a lot of the furniture and appliances are badly in need of repair.  The clock isn't ticking, the door is falling off its hinges, and a hole has burned through the side of the stove.  A single squeaky bed is against the wall.  A wooden counter holds a vase of dead flowers and a bowl of burnt steaks.

This tiny cave has two exits from which light pours in, one leading out to the badlands and one leading onto a cliff overlooking a waterfall.  The ceiling is less than five feet high, and it is necessary to duck to walk through.  A pillar of light shines down from a hole in the ceiling.  The damp mist is cool and refreshing.

A grand, majestic waterfall flows right under this cliff, which reaches out above the top of the Barren Falls.  Water pours down the cliffside and eventually flows out into the ocean, which is visible far below.  Grass grows on this cliffside, a rare sight in the Barren Lands.  A thick mist rises from the pouring water.  The source of the river must be high in the mountains above.

A horribly constructed wooden platform is the only way to travel on this part of the Lete River.  The shaky path was clearly built by someone who was trained in a field other than carpentry.  A large section of the platform is composed of one large sheet of wood, balanced atop three rocky spikes that are sticking up out of the water.  The rock structures in the river ought not even be visible from atop the walkway, but a large hole that has rotted into the plank affords a view of them.

There is a massive, four foot long turtle shell stuck in the southern wall of the river, about a meter above the ground.  The shell isn't just lodged into a crevice in the rock, but rather the stone seems to have somehow actually formed around the shell.  The tame flow of water going around this bend does not reach anywhere near the height of the giant shell, which has nevertheless become somehow bleached white.

Onboard a small skiff atop the flowing water, it is only possible to follow the river's natural flow forward.  The rushing river echoes through the deformed cave.  A low ceiling with jagged edges reaches down far enough to create a risk of head injury.  Fossils embedded in the ceiling are visible.

This tunnel connects the Lete Underground River, to the south, to some sort of flooded cavern up north.  A small amount of water covers the entire floor of the cave, moving slowly down to meet the river.  A metal sign has been nailed into the cave wall above the southern opening, reading "Emergency Escape," but the sign is badly rusted.

The tunnel between the Lete Underground River and the abandoned cave that lies buried alongside it slopes down to the waterway at an uncomfortable angle, making trudging up through the moving water a difficult task for those entering the wrecked cavern.  The water is not deep at all, barely covering one's ankles, but is moving at a pace just fast enough to require precaution.  Smooth limestone makes up every surface of the tunnel.

Two great stalagmites in the middle of the river reach nearly up to the ceiling.  They do not seem to have formed in any natural way, but rather to have been somehow shoved up through the ground from below by some enormous geological force.  The stalagmites are sharp rather than smooth, and are made of an odd black rock that is found nowhere else in the cavern.  A shallow stream bubbles in gently from the south, a few inches deep.
