This tunnel, barely large enough for a human to walk through, leads underground at a steep angle toward the sound of rushing water.  The tunnel seems freshly carved, and steps have been cut into the cave floor to aid passage.  The steps are quite steep, but a cool breeze coming from the cavern below makes the climb less harsh.  The plains of the Serpent Trench are visible outside.

The river rushes around a sharp bend, splashing violently against the wall of the cave as it turns north.  A ledge on the southern wall provides a safe place to walk alongside the river.  Large stones in the river allow one to hop north through the shallows to a raft, but the river begins to get deeper upstream to the east.

To the north, a landslide has occured, causing many large rocks to fall into the river.  The rocks provide a relatively dry route to climb across.  Just to the west, though, they begin to fall off, leaving a trail which is useless to those not wishing to walk underwater.  It seems that someone who felt that travel further upriver should be possible has built a wooden platform to walk across to the west.

The access tunnel suddenly drops straight down at the bottom of a steep decline.  A thick rope, tied securely to a metal stake at the top of the dropoff, is the only way to proceed down any further.  Small ledges have been carved into the sides of the vertical shaft, which appears to be recently drilled.  Light from the cave entrance barely reaches, reflecting off of the stone walls.

rooms.name: Entrance to the Lete Underground River

userData.LongDescription: In this expansive cavern, a rock platform underfoot spans across the width of a rapid underground river, forming a natural bridge overlooking the river.  The cave walls around this waterway are irregular, jagged, and full of strange fossils.  A narrow tunnel, drilled into one of the cave walls, crawls up toward the surface.  The water is rushing quickly beneath the bridge.  A dry ledge, jutting out from the wall, leads west alongside the river.

rooms.name: At the bottom of an underground waterfall

userData.LongDescription: The ledge alongside the river leads to a waterfall.  The river flows from a higher tunnel and then falls down to this lower section.  The abrupt difference in the passage's height is accompanied by large, irregular jags in the rock surfaces, giving the cave a most unnatural appearance.  A ladder beside the waterfall leads up to a dry ledge.

A large, safe ledge is several meters above the water, offering a safe haven from the dangers of the river below.  A small natural stone ramp climbs up to the ledge from the rapids below.  On the southwest edge of the ledge, a long plank is set up that leads over the water to a tied-up raft.

The river splits in a complicated fashion.  The water pours in from the south, and splits to make two streams heading north and west.  The northern stream merely curves sharply right and loops back around to this same intersection, while the western stream continues steadily downriver.  A couple of small skiffs have been tied up near the ledge, and could be used to go down the northern bend.

Two tiny flows of water merge from the east and south, forming a somewhat deeper trench that is nonetheless still shallow enough to walk through.  The lack of ferocity in this part of the Lete River can be attributed to the fact that the river has been divided.  To the south, one can see where it first splits; beyond that, there is only one path further upstream.  This cave is quite spacious despite the small size of the river.  A single shattered raft looks to have long ago crashed against the northern wall, and is almost entirely rotted.

The current flowing in from the west is barely more than ankle-deep.  The cool water flows gently over the stones and fossils in the riverbed.  The eastern wall of the cave has a most peculiar split across is about halfway up; the stone composing the wall below the split is of a noticably different composition than what is above the split.  It looks almost like the natural walls of the river have been crushed by the upper layer of stone.  There is a narrow gap between the two layers of rock.

A number of large, wooden rafts are floating atop the Lete River side by side.  Though there is no easy path to get any further upriver, a rope does load up the wall of the cave to a ledge high above.  The jagged spikes that make up the walls of this underground cavern allow for easy climbing to whatever awaits above.  It is possible to walk east downriver across the tops of the tied-up rafts.

The river flows rapidly, threatening to unforgivingly sweep away anyone foolish enough to fall in.  A fossilized skeleton of some sort of octopus is visible in the middle of the river, embedded into the rock beneath the water.  Other fossils decorate every wall of this underground cavern, which directs the Lete River downstream to the northeast.  A narrow ledge leads alongside the river.

A huge outburst of sharp rock juts at an angle from the ceiling, reaching down into the water.  The cave enclosing the Lete River is full of such odd protrusions, which indicates the severe violence of the tectonic activity that initially formed the cave.  Large stones in the middle of the river form a wary path.

A few rafts made of logs tied together have been secured along the northern bank of the underground river, and are stable enough to walk on.  More such rafts are to the west, and it is possible to hop from raft to raft.  In the middle of the river, a huge, flat chunk of land has erupted diagonally out from below the water, and several of the rafts have run aground on it.  It is possible to trek north across the burst of rock toward shallower water.

A truly mammoth turtle shell provide the only dry place to stand in the underground waterway, as no ledges are present in this section of the cave and the water is far to deep to simply walk across.  The giant fossil extends east, taking up a large section of the river.  To the west, it seems that someone who felt that travel further upriver should be possible has built a wooden platform to walk across.

This tunnel drudges north through murky water toward what looks like a once-inhabited cave.  A pair of lanterns are set in the wall, though they are far too damp to light.  Furniture is visible in a chamber to the north.  The water moves slowly but with resolve, and is just deep enough to be annoying and uncomfortable.

The Lete River's flow is relatively calm in this loop, but it is strong enough to prevent one from rowing upstream on such a small and poorly built skiff.  The rocks that define the inner edge of the loop are steep and dangerous.  Deep under the water, huge shells are visible on the river floor.

The water rippling in from the south and east is shallow enough to walk across without getting more than one's feet wet, but as the two streams merge, the river deepens.  To the north, it quickly becomes too deep and too fast to stand in safely, but a ramp has been built over the river, creating a boardwalk.  The irregular walls of the cave are loaded with small shells that have become somehow lodged in the rock.

Fossilized exoskeletons from some sort of crustaceous creature, each as big as a man's head, cover a large rock island in the middle of the river.  A few rafts have crashed into the rock, and it is possible to hop south from raft to raft over the deeper water.  The water flowing in from the south splits three ways as it hits the large rock, heading north, east, or west.  The division of the current allows the water in all three directions to be shallow and calm enough to walk across easily.

rooms.name: At the top of an underground waterfall

userData.LongDescription: Water runs past a dry platform and gushes over the side of a cliff to the south, creating a spectacular waterfall.  A ladder leads down to a ledge at the bottom.  A series of stepping stones in the middle of the river acts as a sort of path to progress upstream through the rapids.  The water rips violently past the stepping stones.

Though there is no ledge to stand upon on the side of the river, a large shell from a gigantic turtle lies in the river, taking up nearly the width of the cave and providing more than adequate footing.  The shell has lost its color and is completely white.  Any bones that were once inside it have been eroded or washed away, as a hole in the top of the turtle shell provides a view of its hollow innards.  The giant shell is at least forty feet long and continues to provide footing to the west.

A makeshift raft, made of small logs tied together with wet rope, is tied to a strange burst of rock.  Stalagmite is not really the best term to use for this rock formation, as it is diagonal, irregular, and clearly the result of violent tectonic activity rather than centuries of slowly dripping water.  The large raft provides a relatively dry place to stand, and is sturdily fixed in place.  A long wooden plank, with one end on the raft, provides a path over the river to a northeastern ledge.  A series of stepping stones leads south.

rooms.name: Before a tunnel overlooking the Lete River

userData.LongDescription: A large opening in the northern wall of the cave leads into a tunnel, which appears to connect to some sort of chamber beyond.  A slow trickle of water runs gently out of the tunnel and over the edge of the ledge, washing down the rocks into the river below.  A rope, leading down to some rafts below, is tied around an iron stake which has been pounded into the ledge.

rooms.name: Atop a caved-in mass of rubble

userData.LongDescription: A huge pile of boulders has fallen into the north bank of the Lete Underground River, a result of some cave-in that must have occurred in the past.  The rocks have piled high enough to reach above the water's surface in many places, but they have not completely blocked off the waterway, nor travellers' passage down it.  The rubble can be climbed across to traverse up the river.  A huge, fossilized turtle shell, bleached white by the water's flow, stands in the water to the east.

For whatever reason, someone has gone to the trouble of constructing a rather unstable platform on which adventurers can walk to progress up or down the underground river.  The wooden boards that make up the walkway are held together by bent nails, soggy ropes, dead roots, and what looks like it might actually be chewing gum.  Nevertheless, it seems capable of supporting a person's weight.  Exceptionally strange imprints from fossils can be seen on the cave walls, which glitter like crystal.

A mold covered, broken frame of a bed has become stuck in a crevice in the stone wall of the flooded cave.  A metal lamp stand, covered by a wet tablecloth, stretches above the waist-deep water.  The water is not clear enough to see through, but a soaked rug can be felt on the ground in most of the room.

Almost neck-high, the water is difficult to move through in this sunken tunnel.  Stairs lead up out of the water to the north, creating tiny waterfalls as the water slowly pours over their edges from above.  The difference in height is enough to make a noticable flow heading east toward the cavern's exit.  An empty crate floats atop the pool.

This tiny tunnel extends from the side of the storage room.  Not even high enough to stand up in, this narrow passageway can only be entered by crawling on one's hands and knees.  This fact, combined with the standing water that fills the cave, makes it difficult to keep one's head above the water.  A solid metal chest is tucked away in a crevice underwater at the end of the passage, solidly locked.

The wet stone floor is slick from the algae that has grown on its surface.  The water in this tunnel does not appear to be moving at all, save from the motion of footsteps trodding through it.  Small stalactites overhead drip water slowly, moist from some unknown source of water above the cavern ceiling.

A soft flow of water washes in from the southwest, where an old door leads to another section of the cave.  Though the wooden door has been worn by the flowing water, it is usable.  A torch on the wall hangs tilted, unlit.  Soggy, ruined books float shin-high in the water that covers the floor of this abandoned lair.

Though it resembles a bedroom, the true purpose of this tiny cave room is lost.  A single bed sits atop the dry stone floor, as this room is above the water level.  An old chair is placed at the bed's side.  A tiny ledge juts out from the wall like a counter, and a bowl of medical supplies is placed there.  A simple wooden door is in the southwest corner.

For whatever reason, a door has been built into the narrow passage that leads northeast.  Of course, the door has been damaged by the flooding, but the water on this raised area is only a few inches deep and the door is usable.  A damp torch dreams of the days when it lit the wall.  A couple of steps lead down into deeper water.

At an opening that once led outside of this cave before it sank underground, solid stone has tightly sealed off any exit.  A pair of darkened torches guide the way to the blocked opening.  Only a single small crack breaches the solid rock.  From this crack flows a quiet stream of cold, fresh water, which pours into the hideout.  This gentle underground spring is responsible for the flooding that has overwhelmed and conquered this abandoned, washed-up fortress.

To the south and west lies a deep trench filled with cool water.  Several crates, most broken and all empty, float atop the water's surface.  Though the trench is too deep to see into very clearly, it looks like supplies from the crates have sunk to the bottom.  The bridge which leads south overtop the pit is actually a few inches underwater, as is the ground at either end of it.

Several heavy crates and chests are submerged beneath the flooding that fills this passage.  Scattered rotten planks float around, torn off of whatever they used to be a part of.  On the stone floor lies a broken lantern which has fallen from the wall.  To the north is a storage area, but the flood damage has likely ruined everything that is stored there.

Several inches of cool water carpet the hard stone floor, which is slick and a bit slimy.  A dozen swords of varying sizes hang from hooks on the wall, ready to grab and use in battle at a moment's notice.  The swords are rusted, though, left in deterioration with the rest of this crumbling lair.  A bridge leads north above a water-filled gap.

A pair of high bookshelves close off this section of the room from the rest.  On the lower shelves of the bookcases, many books are missing, and the ones that remain have been thoroughly ruined by the water.  On the higher shelves, though, many of the books remain relatively intact.  A number of soaked books have escaped the shelves and float atop the chest-high water.

A large wooden crate full of rusty shields and weathered helmets perserveres in the shallow water, right at the edge of a drop-off to the south.  Water runs across the floor, and seems to be coming from the southwest.  A door in the stone wall leads to some seperate room where privacy must have been a concern.

From inside this high-ceiling room of the underground cave, it is clear that the entire cavern has been flooded.  No signs of life are visible, and it is likely that whoever once inhabited this cavern has abandoned it.  A couple of chairs bob up and down in the knee-high water that covers the entire ground.  A more narrow tunnel to the south leads to the Lete Underground River.

Crates, pots, chests, and boxes have been stacked atop one-another in this storage area, where the water is nearly waist-high.  An old lantern hangs on the wall, but it is not lit and is covered in mildew.  Bugs crawl over spilled rotten food that was being stored.  A large assortment of weapons and armor have been left to rust.

A small dining table sits under the water, with its tablecloth being held down by a heavy ceramic bowl.  If there were ever any chairs or stools around it, they are long gone.  Metal steps head up to a higher section of the cave, and to the east is a grand meeting table.

This high ledge is positioned well above the water that fills the rest of the cavern, and it is dry and safe enough for one to be able to sit down and rest a while.  There are torches set up, though they do not work.  The cavern's ceiling closes in overhead.  A pile of fish bones stinks from the corner.

A torch hangs from the wall, unlit.  A deep recess in the floor looks like it probably was a safety hazard before it became filled with water.  Now, though, it's a six foot deep pool that spills over onto the floor.  A small makeshift bridge leads south toward a caved-in exit and an underground spring.

Spoiled tonics and potions, reeking badly, line those shelves which are above the water level.  Many of the containers are open or cracked, allowing fungus and bacteria to grow inside the old medicine bottles.  Accompanying the ripe odor of the stagnant brews is that of a thoroughly rotten desk, which looks as though it would collapse with a touch.

Bookshelves spanning halfway across the large cavern block off the area just to the north.  One bookcase lies on the floor, face down.  Three more stand upright, walling off the northern part of the room.  Whatever manuscripts fill the fallen bookcase are inaccessible and probably soaked.

A thin layer of water barely covers the top of a gray metal table that rests on the floor of this sunken cave, and the two highback chairs that surround it pierce out of the water's skin by at least a foot.  A slimy rug covers the stone floor, green from algae.  A steep set of stairs leads up to a high ledge, well out of the water, which looks safe and dry.

The water plunges waist-deep across the length of this abandoned room.  Several beds, frames rotted and linens covered in mold, float around the room freely.  A counter in one corner reaches above the water's surface, and looks like it might once have been manned by an innkeeper.  A wooden sign hanging above the counter, though too rotten to make out clearly, looks like it probably used to say "INN."  No one will be sleeping in these beds now, though.

Several wooden chairs are floating calmly around a large meeting table.  The grand table actually sticks up well above the water, and a number of documents are scattered across it along with a globe and an oil lamp.  A suit of silver armor is set up on a display stand next to a clay pot that has been drowned by the flooding.

The desert comes to an end here, trailing off to a small pile of rubble to the south.  To the east lies Figaro Cave, but there seems to be no way to get to it from that direction, although a path can be seen through the southern rubble pile.  There's a sign hammered into the sandy ground by the rubble.

To the north lies a path to the western tower of Figaro Castle, while to the east lies what appears to be a safe haven of sorts.  The winds here dissipate almost entirely, lending an eerie silence to the desert.  Even the continued random bouncing of tumbleweeds lends no sound to the area.

The desert starts to taper off to the west, giving an excellent view of the ocean.  To the south and east lies more of the desert.  To the southwest and northeast is more of what could be called the 'ocean shore'.  It's hard to tell what stretches further, the ocean or the barren desert.

One of the few remaining non-desert areas right by the Figaro Desert, these plains maintain a devastated look from unfortunate events in the past.  The only path not leading back into the desert is to the north, where more plains lie.  A mountain range lies to the south, while a small city can be seen across the ocean to the northeast.  Lizards scamper about, enjoying being by water...  despite it being undrinkable.

Sand lizards, a consistent if annoying sight, lie about lazily here.  The winds pick up slightly blowing the sand around into a miniature sandstorm.  To the west, another of Figaro Castle's towers looms largely.  The sweltering temperature generated by the sand and blazing sun continues to make travel uncomfortable.

rooms.name: Southwest of the city of South Figaro

userData.LongDescription: More of the scorched earth that passes for plains lies here, crumbling away by the shore.  A mountainous outcropping to the north towers into the sky.  The ocean is cradled into a small pocket east from here, with more plains visible further east.  It offers further evidence of the barren and wasted environment on this island.

The ocean spreads out endlessly to the south with no end in sight.  A shelter of sorts is visible to the northeast and oddly, the winds seem calmer here, decreasing the power of the sandstorm.  The sun emits waves of heat, sending the temperature up to severely uncomfortable levels.

The ocean spreads out endlessly to the south with no end in sight.  A shelter of sorts is visible to the north and oddly, the winds seem calmer here, decreasing the power of the sandstorm.  There are a few skeletons here, but no sign of corpses of any form.

The ocean shore continues along the eastern edge here, while to the north, west and south lies yet more of Figaro's desert.  The sun provides more blistering heat to the desert, creating among other things, various mirages in the distance upon its sandy surface.

All around you lie mountains.  The only ways out are back to the southwestern plains or towards the southeastern forest.  There's an opening in one of the mountain walls that looks like a cave entrance.  The grass here seems to die out, being replaced by dirt and sand blown in from the Figaro desert.

The winds pick up slightly in this area, offering a minor reprieve from the heat.  The western tower of Figaro Castle stands out in the northeast.  Scurrying through the sand, sand lizards continue to act unaware of the misery and death that surrounds them.  Continuing a random meandering path through the desert are more tumbleweeds.

Sand spreads out endlessly, looking maddeningly plain and identical as far as can be seen.  No matter the direction, sand lies ahead.  For variety, there is the presence of sand dunes, sand lizards, sand bleached skeletons... even the tumbleweeds are covered with sand.

Part of one of the Figaro Island's extensions, this section of plains seem slightly healthier.  With a few traces of plantlife, however weak and frail it is, there is a sense of hope, as if the scorched earth is trying to restore some of its past glory and beauty.  The absence of any ocean waves to eat away at the already fragile ground aids this healing to a degree.  The ocean can be seen not far to the northeast and southwest, monotonous in its volume and vastness.

The sand here takes on slightly a rougher appearance, making barefoot travel even more ridiculous than before.  The atmosphere remains arid and stiflingly hot, easily capable of wearing out an unwary adventurer.  Judging by the appearance of sundry types of corpses and skeletal remains, this part of the desert has claimed its fair share of victims.

This is Lonewolf, the master thief's, hideout.  It is plain yet secluded from the rest of the desert.  Lone Wolf's tent is the same color as the desert sand, and a hole the size of a small room has been dug underneath it.  Within the hideout are some useless baubles and trinkets, probably worth enough coin to buy some food with.

One of the few remaining non-desert areas right by the Figaro Desert, these plains maintain a devastated look from unfortunate events in the past.  Paths back into the desert lie to the northwest and west.  A small city can be seen across the ocean to the east, on the peninsula formed during the Times of Ruin.  Lizards scamper about here, seeming to enjoy not being harassed by both hot sand and hot weather.

If a part of the desert could be seen as bland and average, this would be it.  An absence of debris, skeletons, corpses, sand dunes, tumbleweeds...  there's just a solid, even layer of sand.  Not even a trace of footprints or a path can be seen anywhere.  How this came to be is beyond understanding.

Figaro Castle rises into sight to the south.  There is no trace of lizards, corpses, skeletons or anything else.  The wind has died down completely, giving this part of the desert an unnerving, eerie silence.  The blazing sun offers no solace, relentlessly covering the desert with a stifling, invisible layer of heat.  Paths towards both towers of Figaro Castle stretch out to the southwest and southeast.

To the east, the devastated ocean flows northwest into a small pocket surrounded by plains.  More of the scorched earth that passes for plains lies here, looking very frail.  Not even lizards, one of the more common sights for this area, can be seen anywhere.

A small section of the ocean trails off to the southeast, surrounded by plains and forestland.  The forest itself continues an unsettling trend of health, more lively than anything else in the area.  Some lizards scurry through the forest here, mindless to the good fortune they have to be around such a place.  The south end of a cropping of rock juts out of the ground to the west.  Occupying space against the ocean's shore, the town of South Figaro stands as a bastion of civilization amidst the wilderness.

rooms.name: Mountain Path to the Figaro Cave

userData.LongDescription: To the north, the Figaro mountains continue to tower high into the sky, with no visible end in sight.  A path leading into the mountains lies to the northwest.  A smaller mountainous outcropping of rock lies to the west, preventing travel in that direction.

The desert seems to stretch out endlessly to the south and west, with no visible end in sight.  To the north lies what passes as the ocean in this horrid realm.  To the east, a path leads to a dock.  Another path can be seen to the southeast leading to more of the desert's edge.

Crumbling apart as the wind blows across it, this section of the plains seem doubly affected by the results of the Times of Ruin.  Part of one of the Figaro Island's extensions, a complete lack of any plantlife gives the impression of a wasteland more than of plains.  The absence of any ocean waves to eat away at the already fragile ground helps perserve the short lifespan this area may have.  The ocean itself can be seen to the northeast, southeast and southwest.

The ocean spreads out from the north to the southeast, offering a stark contrast to the barren desert.  The desert's edge continues to the south and the northwest, while the path to the desert lies to the west.  The water isn't safe to drink, judging by the twitching sand lizard by the shore.

The sand stretches out endlessly in all directions, making it easy to get lost.  The sun continues to relentlessly shine down, seeming to enjoy enhancing the desert's lethal potential.  The absence of any shade aids the sun in its quest of suffering.  However, the lizards dashing about don't seem to care, having developed a resistance to the heat.

The sheer amount of death and decay here, due to numerous skeletons and corpses, lends an aura of hopelessness to this part of the southern edge.  Even the ocean offers a better sense of positive emotion than the immediate surroundings.  The wind has died down almost completely, leaving no trace of a sandstorm.  A shelter lies to the northwest, probably the lone beacon of hope in this desert.

The ocean continues to relentlessly force the desert to retreat, slanting the desert/shore edge in a southeastern direction.  However, the desert area to the east seems as endless as the ocean view to the west.  The presence of tumbleweeds and corpses displays the lethal nature of the desert, even if it seems to be shrinking at the whim of the ocean.

To the east, south and southwest lies more of the desert, while to the north and west lies the ocean.  Always a hostile and barren area, a quick glance around shows many different forms of decaying material, as well as skeletons and tumbleweeds.

The sand seems to stretch out endlessly in all directions, making it easy to get lost.  Certainly a lethal area, judging by the presence of skeletons and corpses lying around.  The sun relentlessly shines down from the sky, making the air stale and uncomfortably warm.

The ocean recedes into a small land pocket to the north and northwest, collecting and forming a small pond.  With the gradual eroding of the plains though, it may soon grow into a lake.  Lizards dash about in a frenzy, apparently distressed by an unknown force.  The ocean-aided winds pick up here, blowing the plains debris into a sandstorm more commonly seen in deserts.

rooms.name: West of the city of South Figaro

userData.LongDescription: One of the few remaining non-desert areas on the Figaro island, these plains look scorched and give off an aura of defeat and hopelessness.  Figaro Desert is barely visible to the northwest, with only a small part of the edge discernable from this point.  The mountains in the area loom largely in the northeast, while a smaller, yet no less dangerous outcropping is easily visible to the east.

The barren surroundings of the desert spread out in every direction, offering no visible contrast to the sand, debris and dead material within.  The wind blows sand into the air, making visibility limited.  The sand lizards for once are not pleased with the conditions of the area, scrambling around for a place to shield themselves from the flying sand.

The ocean spreads out to the east, as far as the horizon.  To the southeast, the scenery changes from sandy desert to devastated plains.  More of the desert lies to the south, west and north.  There are no indications of the hostility the desert beholds in this area, like skeletons or corpses.

To the northeast, the ocean can barely be seen, although those experienced with this area know it is not close to being an oasis for any thirsty adventurer.  The surroundings here in the desert remain relatively lifeless, with an assortment of tumbleweeds, skeletons and corpses within sight.  One corpse in particular stands out, that of a mostly undecayed humanoid.

The desert tapers off completely to the west, providing an excellent view of the ocean.  To the south and east lies more of the desert.  Heading northeast leads to more of the desert edge/ocean shore. It's hard to tell what stretches further, the ocean or the barren desert.

First constructed to be used for ferrying people and supplies from Narshe to Figaro Castle, the upsurge of monsters has made using the docks and ferry for casual travel unadvisable.  An old man stands by the edge of the docks, looking out upon the ocean with a sad look on his face.

What passes as an ocean in this realm can be seen by the eastern horizon, while to the northeast Figaro's port is barely visible.  All other paths lead to more of the desert.  The presence of brambles and tumbleweeds give a faint clue to the desolation that the rest of the desert holds.

If not for the ocean front to the north, all there would be to see is sand, with the occasional rotting corpse, collection of bones or sand lizard breaking up the monotony.  As it is, the desert spreads out to the west, south and east, looking as barren and hostile as ever.

The sand stretches out endlessly in all directions, making it easy to get lost.  The sun continues to relentlessly shine down, seeming to enjoy enhancing the desert's lethal potential.  The absence of any shade aids the sun in its quest of suffering.  However, the lizards dashing about don't seem to care, having developed a resistance to the heat.

More of the scorched earth that passes for plains lies here, crumbling away by the shore.  The ocean maintains a dreadful and murky appearance.  Whether anything can live within it is not likely.  More paths along the shore lie to northwest and northeast, while one to the north leads away from the shore.

The sand seems to stretch out endlessly in all directions, making it easy to get lost.  The sun relentlessly shines down from the sky, making the air stale and uncomfortably warm.  Not one of the friendlier areas of Figaro's desert, corpses and skeletons are littered throughout the area.

One of the few remaining non-desert areas right by the Figaro Desert, these plains maintain a devastated look from unfortunate events in the past.  Figaro Castle is barely visible by the northwestern edge of the horizon, clouded almost entirely by a seemingly endless sandstorm.  The mountains in the center of the Figaro continent stretch into the sky.  A path to the northeast leads into the mountains, while one to the northwest leads back into the desert.

The area doesn't look very hospitable, as can be expected from a desert.  Sand as far as the eye can see, and a lack of vegetation or sufficient moisture.  To the north lies a foul reminder of past travesties, a small stretch of damaged ground leading to the ocean.

Figaro Castle's eastern tower looms here, detached from the main section of the castle by a single enclosed hallway. Several smaller towers jut up from the desert, the sound of whirring fans audible from their tops. Footprints both man and bird can be seen in the sand, indications of soldiers on patrol.

The winds start to die down here, greatly increasing visibility.  Figaro Castle itself can be seen to the southeast, although the only entrance inside lies at the western tower.  There are a few corpses and skeletons strewn about here as well, acting as a reminder to how dangerous the desert can be.

To the northwest, the eastern tower of Figaro Castle looms largely.  The temperature generated by the sand and blazing sun maintains its stifling level, making continued travel uncomfortable.  Sand lizards continue to skitter about with nary a care in the world, while corpses and skeletons continue to be a common sight.

A welcome shelter from the hostile desert weather and conditions, yet it is eerily quiet.  No sound can be heard from this point.  No wind, no blowing of sand...  even the skittering of energetic sand lizards lends no sound.  It's almost as if this area is frozen in time.  A complete absence of hostile life completes the peaceful, if slightly unnerving, atmosphere.  A lone skeleton lies here, testament to the burning heat.

The winds start to pick up here, reducing visibility.  Figaro Castle can barely be made out through the sandstorm, while its eastern tower is slightly easier to make out to the south.  The only entrance inside lies at the same eastern tower.  There are a few corpses and skeletons strewn about here as well.

Another corner of the desert looms ahead, within a short distance to the east.  The ocean seems a little less murky here, although the fact the sand lizards still don't try to drink it indicates it's not safe.  There is a complete lack of wind, giving no breeze to counter the hostile rays of the sun.  A path to the southeast leads to more plains.

The winds pick up slightly in this area, blowing around sand like a miniature sandstorm.  Sand lizards, which appear to be one of the few consistent sights in the desert, lie about lazily.  If they are troubled by the blazing temperatures the desert generates, they certainly don't show it.  To the southwest, the eastern tower of Figaro Castle can be clearly seen, no worse for wear despite the castle's age.

The ocean shore continues here, offering a contrast with cracked earth and murky water.  Unfortunate events in the past led to these terrible conditions, and there looks to be no hope of recovery anytime soon.  The end of this section of the island can be seen to southeast, leading off to yet more of a dreary ocean view.  For once, even the lizards seem depressed.

Figaro Castle's western tower looms here, detached from the main section of the castle by a single enclosed hallway. Several smaller towers jut up from the desert, the sound of whirring fans audible from their tops. Footprints both man and bird can be seen in the sand, indications of soldiers on patrol.

To the west, the devastated ocean seemingly spreads out with no end in sight.  More of the scorched earth that passes for plains lies from the north to the southeast.  Not even lizards, one of the more common sights for this area, can be seen anywhere.

To the north lies a path to the eastern tower of Figaro Castle, while to the west lies what appears to be a safe haven of sorts.  The winds here start to pick up, stirring up a sandstorm.  Tumbleweeds almost hover above the sand with the wind's aid, while lizards continue to act like absolutely nothing is happening.

To the east, the desert trails off into a small patch of plainsland.  Beyond that, the brackish ocean can be seen.  This plains/desert compromise continues to the north as far as the eye can see, while a block of mountains can be seen to the southeast.  There are no signs of death or decay here, not even a half-decomposed corpse.

The ocean spreads out endlessly from the west to the southeast.  The sight of Figaro Castle is a vague one from here, due to the continued presence of a sandstorm.  Per usual, the lizards here don't seem to care much, instead chasing each other around for no explained reason.

The great castle of Figaro towers above, standing as the only point of interest in an otherwise empty desert. Several surprisingly small dunes of sand gather at the base of the castle's exterior walls. High above, the whirring sound of fans can be heard. The desert extends seeming endlessly in all directions.

To the east, the desert trails off into a small patch of plainsland.  Beyond that, the brackish ocean can be seen.  This plains/desert compromise continues to the south as far as the eye can see.  There are few indications of the hostility the desert beholds in this area, which is a rare sight.

The village ends at the forest to the north and east.  Bushes line a small area, in which Neko is keeping a shop.  The forest closes in from the north and east, shading the shop.  Far to the south, a path leads out of the village into the Great Forest, while to the south and west the village continues.

The Great Forest is in the grip of winter.  A thin layer of snow covers the ground.  A lake sits to the south, frozen solid.  To the west and south, the forest continues, unchanging.  To the east, a path lined with stones leaves the winter wonderland.

The Upper Land continues in every direction.  The path runs along the base of a huge mountain to the north.  A few stones and flowers line the path.  A small lake sits in the center of the path, its clear water filled with fish.  Two paths lead away, on to the south and the other east.

The Cannon Travel Center serves the Great Forest of the Upper Land.  A hill rises just above the trees, topped with a large cannon.  A short staircase leads up the hill.  A short man stands at the base of the hill.  To the west, a row of stones lines a path into the Great Forest.

The Upper Land forest continues away in all directions.  The path is well worn, and little grass grows in the center.  The exposed dirt is well packed from long years of use.  A few flowers bloom along the edge of the path.  Three paths lead away, one north, one west, and one northwest.

The path ends at a line of stones.  Across the stones, another path can be seen.  A few flowers grow among the stones.  A line of trees seperates the path from another path to the north.  Far to the north, a mountain rises high above the forest.  The path leads away only to the west.

The path runs along the north side of a line of stones.  Across the line  of stones lies another path, but it can not be reached.  To the east, a line of trees seperates the Upper Land forest from the Great Forest.  A few flowers bloom amongst the stones.  The path leads away to the north and the west.

The Air Palace rises high above the forest.  It sits at the top of a short staircase up a small hill.  A second staircase leads up the front of the palace to the door.  Pillars support the front of the palace.  To the south, a path leads towards the Sprite Village.

The Great Forest is in a state of perpetual summer.  A lake to the north is home to a few fish.  The trees are alive with birds, while a few insects fly between flowers.  To the east, a hill pokes over the trees, home to a large cannon.  A path leads to the base of the hill.  To the north and west, the perpetual summer continues.

A wall of trees lines the path on the east side, separating the Upper Land forest from the Great Forest.  Yellow flowers bloom along the edge of the path.  A single gray stone sits in the path.  Far to the north, a mountain rises above the forest.  The path leads away to the west and south.

The eastern end of the Sprite village is filled with only a few houses.  The grass has grown quite high, and flowers bloom unchecked.  The trees of the forest around the village are green with life.  The village continues to the west.

It is always winter in this part of the Great Forest.  A thin layer of snow covers the ground.  The trees throughout the forest are adorned with icicles.  To the north and east, the winter wonderland continues, while to the south, a path lined with stones leads to another part of the forest.

The Great Forest is always in autumn.  The red and yellow leaves still cling to the trees.  A few birds still nest high above in the trees.  Any flowers have withered and died.  To the east and south, the forest continues away.  To the west, a path lined with stones leads to another part of the forest.

A wall of leaves shields the path from the rest of the forest.  A few flowers bloom at the edge of the path, and a few stones are scattered about the forest.  Far to the north, a huge mountain towers above the forest.  Paths lead away to both the north and the northeast.

The Great Forest is perpetually spring.  The trees are all in blossom, and a few birds roost.  Flowers are blooming all around the forest.  To the west, a path lined with stones leads out of the perpetual spring, while to the north and east the perpetual spring continues.

The stage which houses the Mana Seed stands proudly, showing none of the chaos and destruction which occurred outside.  Even while lying dormant, the seed sheds a shining aura which spreads throughout the room, lending a bluish hue to the entire area.  The way back down lies to the south, as does the exit to the Air Palace.

The Great Forest all around is in the throes of autumn.  The leaves on the trees are brilliant reds and yellows.  Flowers all around the forest are closed and wilted.  A few birds roost in the trees.  To the north and east, the forest continues away.

The Great Forest is in a state of perpetual spring.  The trees are in full blossom, and flowers all around are in bloom.  A few birds nest in the trees above.  To the north, a path lined with stones leads out of the perpetual spring, while to the south and east it continues.

The path follows the eastern shore of a lake.  The clear water of the lake is filled with fish, and water flowers dot the surface.  It stretches away a short distance to the south, followed by a path.  Two other paths lead away, north and west, into the green forest.

The inside of the Air Palace is quite open.  Eight pillars rise from the floor in a circle around the massive stage.  The stage sits in the center of the room, home to the Mana Seed.  The entire palace is colored a light blue.  To the south, a door leads out.

The path runs through the Upper Land forest.  A small hill sits just to the east, covered with fragments of crystal.  Far to the north, a mountain rises high above the forest.  Flowers bloom alongside the path and all around the hill.  The path continues away to the north and east.

Winter has taken hold on this part of the Great Forest.  A thin layer of snow covers the ground.  The trees are heavy with snow and ice.  A lake sits just to the north, frozen solid.  To the north and west, the winter wonderland continues away.

The Great Forest is perpetually summer.  The trees are always green, while flowers are perpetually open.  Birds roost in the trees, while small animals romp in the forst.  To the north and east, the perpetual summer continues through the forest, while to the west a path, lined with stones, leads to perpetual spring.

The Great Forest, or at least this part, is always summer.  Trees all around are covered in green leaves.  A few flowers are open to the sun.  To the south, a small lake stretches away.  To the west and south, the summer continues.  To the north, a path lined with stones leads to another part of the forest.

Many flowers bloom along the path.  Leaves growing thickly on the trees shade the path from the harsh sunlight.  A few stones are scattered around the forest floor.  A short way to the east, a lake is visible, along with a path leading to it.  Two other paths lead away to the north and south.

The Upper Land is huge, stretching to the far reaches of the continent.  Trees all around the path are green with life.  A few flowers grow along the path.  To the north, a small lake is visible, and beyond it a mountain rises.  The path continues to the north, south, and southeast.

The forest continues in all directions.  All around, flowers bloom at the edge of the path.  The trees above are green with life.  A few stones lie alongside the path.  To the north, the path leads to a cave, while to the west and south the paths lead through the forest.

rooms.name: In the Great Forest - Sprite Village Entrance

userData.LongDescription: The Great Forest is in a state of perpetual spring.  The trees are in full blossom, and are home to a few birds.  Many flowers grow in the forest, all in bloom.  To the north, a path leads into the Sprite Village, while to the south and west the Great Forest continues.

The cave links Matango with the rest of the Upper Land.  This is the eastern end, the end that leads out into the forest.  A few stalagmites rise from the floor around the cave.  To the west, the cave continues a short distance.  to the south, an opening leads out of the cave.

The forest continues away in every direction.  Trees on every side of the path are green with life.  Insects busily fly between a few flowers, which bloom alongside the path.  A path to the south is lined with stones.  Two other paths lead away, one to the north and the other east.

The path runs just south of a line of rocks.  The line ends just to the west, at a small hill.  The hill is covered with tiny fragments of shattered crystal.  The path follows the line of stones to the northeast, out of sight, while to the west it follows the line of stones past the hill.

The Great Forest is always in the season of autumn.  The leaves on the trees have turned red and yellow.  Flowers around the forest are withered and dead.  A few birds still roost in the trees, but for the most part the forest is void of life.  To the south and west the forest continues.

A narrow path leads through the forest.  It is bordered on both sides by trees, green with life.  A few stones sit alongside the path.  Far to the north, a mountain rises high above the forest.  To the north and south, the path continues away.  To the east, the path leads to a Cannon Travel Center.

The Moogle village sits in the center of the Great Forest.  The seasonal regions have no affect on the village.  Around the edges of the village, green leaves grow on the trees.  The village itself is broken into smaller areas by low rows of bushes.

The cave is a passage from the peaceful city of Matango to the rest of the Upper Land.  Off to the northwest, the cave continues, but is inaccessible from this part.  Many stalagmites grow upwards from the floor, making walking difficult.  Just to the south is an exit to Matango, while to the east the cave continues a short distance to another exit.

The forest continues in every direction, to the ends of the continent.  The path through the forest is lined with green trees and blooming flowers.  A few stones are strewn about the path haphazardly.  To the north, south, and east paths lead away.  The one to the north is lined with stones.

The forest stretches away in all directions.  A few moss covered stones are scattered among the trees.  A large number of red and yellow flowers grow along the edge of the grassy path.  Far to the north, a huge mountain rises far above the forest, covered in giant mushrooms.  A few small holes have been burrowed into the ground by large caterpillars.  Three paths lead away, one north, one south, and one east.

The Great Forest is in a state of perpetual spring.  The trees are all in full blossom.  Flowers bloom all around the forest.  To the east, a stone lined path leads out of this perpetual spring, while to the north and west the springtime continues.

The Great Forest, at least this part of it, is held in the grip of winter.  A thin layer of snow covers the ground, and the trees are laden with ice and snow.  To the southeast, a frozen lake is visible.  To the south and east, the forest continues, unchanging.

The moogle village ends at the forest to the north and west.  Far to the southeast, a path leads into the Great Forest.  The trees along the edge of the village are green with life.  A few bushes divide the village into smaller areas.  Flowers along the edge of the forest bloom.  To the east and south, the village continues.

The forest continues in all directions.  A few flowers bloom along the path.  Far to the north, a huge mountain towers over the forest.  Green leaves adron the trees all around, limiting visibility.  A short distance to the south, sunlight plays on the surface of a small lake.  To the west and south, paths lead away.

The western end of the Sprite village is full of houses.  The grass has grown quite high, and is full of blooming wildflowers.  The houses in this end of the village have gone into disrepair.  An important looking house sits atop a hill, but it too is in disrepair.  To the east, the village continues.

rooms.name: In the Great Forest - Moogle Village Entrance

userData.LongDescription: The Great Forest is perpetually summer.  The leaves are green, and many flowers are open to the sun.  Countless birds nest in the trees.  To the north, a path leads into the Moogle Village, while to the south and east the Great Forest continues.

The forest is vibrant with life.  The trees alongside the path are heavily adorned with bright green leaves.  Only a few red and yellow flowers bloom along the path.  To the west, stones line a path to another part of the forest.  Three other paths lead away, to the north, south, and east.

The Great Forest is held in the grip of autumn.  The leaves on the trees have turned yellow, orange, and red.  A few flowers lie withered and dying in the forest.  The trees are home to only a few birds.  To the north and west, the forest continues.  To the south, a path lined with stones leads away.

The forest continues away in all directions.  A wall of green lines the path to the north.  Countless flowers bloom amongst the trees all around.  Far to the north, a mountain rises high above the forest.  Two paths lead away, one to the south and the other to the east.

The Upper Land forest stretches away to the west.  The trees are covered with green leaves.  Stones and bushes limit movement to a single path. The path leads away to the north and to the southwest.  To the east, stones line another path to the Great Forest.

The Upper Land forest continues in all directions, to the far reaches of the continent.  A path runs through this part, lined with flowers and statues.  Trees grow all around the path.  To the north, a mountain rises high above the forest.  A cave leads into the mountain, while to the south the forest continues.

Pure elemental energy suffuses this realm, to the extent that nearly nothing else exists.  There are no perceivable floor, walls, ceiling, just mana.  It is a realm beyond mortal comprehension, and is where the most powerful of elemental beings reside.

The Sprite village has been abandoned.  All around, empty houses sit in disrepair.  The grass on the ground has grown long from years of neglect.  Wildflowers bloom all around the village.  A few statues sit in the village, making a line from north to south.  To the east and west, the village continues.  To the north, a path leads away.  To the south, a path leads to the Great Forest.

The path ends at a barrier of stones and trees.  Across the barrier, another part of the forest can be seen.  A few yellow flowers bloom among the gray stones.  To the east, a line of thick trees seperates the path from the Great Forest.  To the south lies the only path away.

The path runs along the western shore of a small lake.  The crystal clear water of the lake is alive with fish, and a few water flowers float on the surface.  To the east, a path follows the southern shore of the lake, while to the north and south, two paths lead into the forest proper.

The path follows the eastern shore of the lake.  The lake is swimming with fish, and numerous flowers dot the surface.  Paths to the north and west follow the shores, while to the southwest a path leads into the forest. To the east, a path lined with stones leads to another part of the forest.

The Cannon Travel Center is based at a hill in the Upper Land.  The cannon sits atop a small hill, while at the base a little man stands.  A short flight of stairs leads up the hill.  A few stones are scattered around the clearing at the base of the hill.  To the west, a path leads into the forest.

The forest borders the village to the south and west.  The forest shades part of the ground.  A few bushes run across the village, dividing it into smaller areas.  A short distance to the east, a path leads south into the Great Forest.  To the north and east the village continues.

A small clearing opens in the forest.  Two hills rise from the ground, each about 10 feet above the ground.  A short staircase leads up to each of them.  The forest all around is green with life.  To the north, a path leads to the Air Palace.  To the south, a path leads to the Sprite village.

This technically qualifies as a house, in the general sense of the term.  The flooring and the front wall are made of stapled-together plywood.  The back wall is the inner metal framework of what might have once been a wall, with pipes and ducts going in and out of it.  A large television is set up on top of a safe, and there are some tables and other furniture.

Along the path is the back of a large robot, stone ionic pillar, a rusted cannon, and a large red beam.  Sharp sheets of scrap metal and tangled up metal pipes protrude from nearly every hole within the scrapheap making a dangerous obstacle course.  Down one end of the path are many rooftops that look like they can be climbed down from.  The other end of the path is hard to see down due to a large stack of vehicles.

Tire tracks lead down the dusty road, which based on the patterns must have been made by a group of motorcycles.  A wrecked jalopy hangs upside-down in mid-air, impaled on a thick metal beam in an impossible position.  The road leads northwest toward a giant concrete wall, or southeast toward most of Sector 5.

This hovel has been set up as a shop to sell medical supplies to people in the slums.  A large iron segment of 3ft. diameter pipe stretches across the middle of the room, creating a makeshift counter.  Crates and boxes are stacked along the wall behind the counter, the tops of them being used as shelves.

There are three windows along the platform, and a stairway leading down.  In the middle of the room is a brass chandelier hanging from the support beams above.  A rocket has broken through the wall below the platform on one wall and has created a large gap that disconnects the platform's pathway.

The front half of a bus that was somehow cut in half has been connected to a trailer home.  The windows are smashed and a large piece of concrete has fallen on the roof, severely denting it.  Outside of the trailer home, a large tarp has been draped over an area with some cookware, creating an outdoor kitchen.

rooms.name: On top of a church roof

userData.LongDescription: The damaged church roof is a dull turquoise color, and the once white stones of the nearby bell towers have been tainted by the pollutants in the air and harsh weather.  Many types and sizes of wreckage are stacked in large piles against and around the church.  One pile reaches as high as the roof, and the nearby debris can create an impromptu path away from the church.  Otherwise, the only exit is down into the church from the hole nearby.

This is an empty dirt path leading through Sector 5.  There are small bits of concrete, rebar and glass that have fallen from the plate above and embedded themselves in the ground.  To the south is the back side of a shanty house.

The floor is made up of a series of hanging beams that cross each other in the middle of the room.  The central hanging beam creates a path past the office wall towards the sanctuary of the church.  The ceiling is directly above, and it is made of wide panels of wood and rafters the same size as the hanging beams.

A group of rusted tin shanties have been erected, huddled next to each other, created out of whatever materials were left lying around.  The dirt path outside ends as it is replaced with fractured pavement.  The dusty air is difficult to breathe.

Light shines through the stained glass windows into this humble structure, with shattered wooden planks and broken pews strewn across the floor.  Crumbling stone pillars rise up all throughout the room, extending to support the simple wooden ceiling high above.  A large hole in the ceiling allows a single column of bright sunlight to shine through, directly onto a circular flower garden that has been planted at the church's altar.  Beautiful yellow flowers grow in the garden in utter defiance of the devastation surrounding them.

Even in the desolate, post-apocalyptic remains of the slums, life apparently continues.  A sort of brick road leading through town is in the process of being built in the dirt from pieces of stone that fell from the plate above.  The road is half-finished.  An industrial spotlight hooked to a solar generator has been installed to light the area at night.

A landfill landslide seems to have covered a portion of the road in junk, but it's been packed down so hard that it's not much worse to walk across than the original dirt road.  Large sheets from a tin roof have been laid across some of the worse parts of the junk road to create better footing.

Considering the state of the rest of the slums, this is an astonishingly nice house.  The kitchen and dining room have a stone tile floor, and there are cute curtains covering the windows.  A glass-doored cabinet contains some nice dishes which the owner has on display.  The circular dining table in the center of the dining room has a fresh white tablecloth and sits on a nice braided rug.  There are stairs leading up the second floor.

This trailer home is actually more like one and a half trailer homes - the front half of a wrecked bus has been attached onto it to add extra space.  It's still absolutely packed with all kinds of junk, much of which is in cardboard boxes.  Roaches scurry around the place and the smell of urine fills the air.  The windows are all blown out and the ceiling is caving in.

rooms.name: On the edge of a broken floor beside a stairway

userData.LongDescription: Shattered wood panels poke from the edges of this ledge that was created when the huge rocket crashed through the office floor creating a large gap that disconnects the ledge with the rest of the office. Connecting to the ledge is a stairway that stretches up towards a platform higher above.

rooms.name: On a beam above the altar

userData.LongDescription: A series of thick wooden joists cross the ceiling, connecting to a central supporting beam large enough to walk on.  Visually, it looks like ribs that support the structure of the church.  The central beam continues through the middle of the church.  One end of the beam leads to the office area, while the other beam eventually stops at the church entrance.  A refreshing patch of yellow flowers can be seen growing at the altar below.

rooms.name: On a platform in the corner of the room

userData.LongDescription: The platform is beside an engraved wall with a circular design and a steep stairway leading on the top of a series of hanging beams that support the walls.  A path down is seen possible by traversing a gap to the platform that hugs the other side of this upper level of the church.

A highway bridge passes overhead.  The area underneath it is in pretty good shape, relatively speaking - the ground is clear of debris, at least.  A number of cardboard boxes and blankets are under the bridge, where the people of Sector 5 seem to be living.

A quick look at the houses reveals that they no longer have any inhabitants.  Heaps of trash have plummeted through many of their ceilings, conveniently making an easy pathway from one roof to the next.  On the far end of the grouping of houses is a slide that looks like it can be used to get to the ground level of this area.  Another path created by an advertising sign leads deeper into the wreckage.

Despite the utter devastation, life continues in the worst parts of the Midgar slums.  What appears to be the massive exhaust pipe from a Mako Reactor is lying on its side, with curtains draped in front of the end to create a makeshift door.  Lights flicker from within.  Some other sort of building has fallen on top of it, possibly from the upper plate, and been smashed into pieces, but the sturdy cylindrical pipe remains undented.  It appears to be a home.  A portion of the ground is comprised of crumbling bits of concrete, while the rest is merely hard dirt.

rooms.name: On a beam above the sanctuary

userData.LongDescription: A enormous hole in the ceiling showers light into the church.  Below are several dusty pews lined up on both sides of the main aisle below. A broken beam is seen stuck between the edge of the hole and the central hanging beam, which makes for a nice jumping off point to the roof of the church.  The central beam continues past the broken beam for several feet, while the other end leads to the area above the altar.

A large circular flower garden has been planted in several rows.  Many of the flowers are in bloom.  This room seems like one of the safest places in all of Midgar, free from the endless destruction and dystopian poverty that plagues the city.  Back to the southwest is the two-story house that this garden belongs to.

A long sheet of ridged tin plating creates a wall along the side of the path, holding a potential landslide of garbage in place precariously above the road.  The tin sheet has a coat of green paint that has mostly faded off, and graffiti has been sprayed on top of the paint.  The road itself is mostly clear of debris.

The opened ceiling provides a soft light throughout the room.  Large wooden barrels can be seen hugging a wall and randomly scattered on the floor.  An old rocket protrudes from the opening in the ceiling, and its nose rests against the floor surrounded by large rubble.

The shaft of a large utility crane extends up from the first floor through a hole in the flooring, then takes a ninety degree turn and makes up half of the second floor's ceiling.  The arm of the crane sticks out through the northwest wall.  A large family bed is in the corner of this room, and faded papers are taped to the walls.

A dirt road has been cleared between the remains of collapsed buildings.  Nearly every structure in sight has been demolished in some way or another, though considering that most of them look like they were either old trailers or makeshift hovels to begin with, it would be more surprising if any of them were still intact after the various disasters that have affected Midgar.  The only building seemingly untouched is an old church to the southeast.

Bricks, pipes, broken concrete, drywall, wood planks, stone, glass, old tires, scrap metal, knotted cabling, pieces of vehicles, dead bodies, toxic sludge and mounds upon mounds of general filth are covered in a five foot layer of dust along the side of this road.  Most of the debris seems to have fallen from above.

An unusually nice house, segregated from the slums by a staircase and large flower garden, has somehow survived intact.  The misery of the rest of the ruins of Midgar seems to melt away among what must be some of the only plant life for a great distance, arranged into neat rows around the front yard of the two-story house.

Alongside the dirt path is a shanty built entirely out of sheets of tin.  Pieces of it have fallen off, leaving the single room inside exposed to the cloud of dust that covers the slums.  Metal piping stretches out from the house to some sort of generator, which has been smashed beyond repair.  Some train tracks have fallen from above, blocking the path south.

A small rugged church stands stalwartly, the sole standing structure visible in any direction.  The roof is falling apart, many of the windows are broken, and one of the bell towers has collapsed, but compared to the utterly annihilated landscape around it, the building is a beautiful testament to the perseverance of hope amidst the destruction caused by Meteor.  The rest of the once great city of Midgar appears to be little more than ruins.  Large portions of the plate overhead have been severely damaged, raining refuse and debris down upon the slums.

The ground under the slums was apparently paved at one point in the past, but has crumbled in this part of town and is now mostly dirt.  What pavement remains is partially covered in dirt that's sifted down from the plate of upper Midgar that blots out most of the view of the sky.  A small house made of stapled-together plywood seems to have electricity.

Sunlight illuminates this section of the road, shining through a massive crack in the metal plate high above that makes up the ceiling of Midgar.  Dust continuously sprinkles down from the rupture in the plate as the ruins of Midgar gradually settle.  The five foot layer of dust covering the surrounding trash suggests that it's been falling for a long time - maybe years.

This metal tube has been turned into a home by some survivors of the fall of Meteor.  Some blankets in the middle of the floor apparently serve as beds, and a pair of tables lean against the curved walls precariously, holding the inhabitants' few possessions: some old books, a box of medical supplies, and three bowling trophies.  A television sits in the corner, but there is no electricity.

Along the walls of this room are decorative banners and a stained-glass window that provides a small amount of light for a small office space located behind a flight of stairways.  The path towards the flight of stairways has been destroyed by an enormous rocket that has crashed through the building.  However, it is still possible to leap to the beginning of the stairway.  Stones and wood planks lie scattered around what remains of the floor and wraps behind the rocket towards another path leading downstairs.

rooms.name: Hole in the wall leading to Sector 6

userData.LongDescription: A giant concrete wall, several meters thick and covered in obscene graffiti, stretches up into the sky.  The wall blocks the road northwest leading to Sector 5 - or at least it would, if there weren't a gigantic hole in it.  The road, a flat stretch of dust, is relatively clear of debris.  Following this road southeast will lead into Sector 5.

The proprietor of this shop has apparently decided to collect some of the more useful junk that has fallen into the slums and sell it.  How some of this stuff qualifies as useful is anyone's guess, though.  Most of it is broken pieces of vehicles, electronics, or machinery, but there are also just huge chunks of scrap metal all over the shop.  A rusty radio sits on the shelf behind the counter, blaring awful static-filled music.

rooms.name: In Front of the Salvage Site

userData.LongDescription: It looks like there might have once been an asphalt road here, but it's covered in so much rubble that it's hard to tell.  A giant robot hand sticks up out of a pile of broken wood and concrete.  The enormous wall blocking off access to Sector 5 is to the southeast, but there's a hole in it.  To the northeast is a military camp.

This is a long, dusted path leading along the edge of the Shinra salvage site. A huge part of the unfinished plate looms overhead, able to provide massive amounts of unneccessary shade. With the very uneven terrain and debris around, it seems like a natural obstacle course. To the southeast is a path leading to a salvage site.

A row of shanties is surrounded by a partially knocked-over wooden fence.  Every third slat of the fence has a red Shinra logo on it.  The shanties are barely holding together, but they do appear to be lived in.

This is a pretty large tent owned by the supplier. Lit by only a kerosene lamp hanging by the ceiling, this circular tent has many oddities that the group has salvaged from the ruins of Midgar, as well as supplies that come from the outside, sent in to aid the explorers and salvagers. There is a sign hanging by the tent entrance.

This is the outer edge of the ruins of the once flourishing city, Midgar. Currently in a state of wreck, not much is going on within this metropolis now that Shinra has taken a major hit to their financing. The glassy outer wall of the city has shattered into pieces, leaving crumbs of glass lying everywhere. The metal gates to the city have been damaged, allowing access to the curious.

rooms.name: Dusted Path out of the Salvage Site

userData.LongDescription: This is a long, dusted path leading away from the salvage site. Rubble and dirt mix to form the rather forcefully carved dirt road. A half-broken, half-charred sign made out of metal is on the ground. The path to the southwest leads to Shinra's salvage site, whereas a further path leading northeast leads deeper into Sector 6.

This large tent, serving as the Shinra Salvage Site Barracks, looks rather cheaply made, without decent cover for the floors. There are mats placed in neat rows to the left and right, with little pillows on top of them. Scattered about are people dressed in military garbs, each doing something different.

This tent is heavily furbished, and looks very grand. The flooring is made out of a thick carpet, and the curtains composing the walls of the tent made from a heavy cloth that allows for privacy and protection from weather. A low, wide table takes up most of the space in the tent, with miscellaneous objects placed on it, as well as a large map of Midgar.

The state of Midgar leaves a lot to be desired, with rubble and fragments of buildings scattered all around. A crude path of dirt is present along the concrete pieces that seem to lead further into the wreck of the city. To the northeast, there is what seems to be a group of tents. Southwest leads to the perimeter of the fallen city.

This is a fairly depressing path riddled with rocks and dirt, as well as huge chunks of concrete and metal, once part of buildings. To the path rising up ahead are a few more tents, and to the path to the west is a bonfire as well as what seems to be the central hub of the salvage site.

This spacious tent is kept very clean, with white tent walls and a floor covered in thick white sheets. Several mattresses are scattered about, unrolled and ready to contain the wounded. Located on one end of the tent is a rather large medicine cabinet, bottles of medicine stacked on top of it. There is a sign hanging by it, as well as a box below.

rooms.name: A Branching Path through the Salvage Site

userData.LongDescription: At this point, the path branches into three. To the northeast is a large tent that looks to be quite important. To the southeast are the soldier barracks, built with a flimsy perimeter wooden fence covering it. To the west is a road leading down to the center of the salvage site.

This is the center point of Shinra's salvage site. There are a few tents scattered about the wreckage, and people moving about left and right, carrying work tools. In the middle of the salvage site is a campfire, burning gently. To the east and west, there are tents, and within the northern scope of direction seem to be other points of interest. There is a sign planted right by the campfire.

This site was once a center of entertainment for the children of the slums.  Now, it lies in ruin, the various contraptions pierced, broken and in various states of disrepair.  A nearby portable bathroom lies on its side, crumpled and unusable.  It stands in contrast to a fairly intact pair of child-height swings.

This dark building once was used as an inn, though it has long since been abandoned, and its contents mainly looted.  An empty, barren counter sits to the side of the entrance, an empty and broken glass cabinet behind it.  A few bedrooms are further in, though even the mattresses are missing, only the sad wooden frames remaining.  The only objects remaining here are those that were destroyed, and ironically they help contribute to picturing an image of what the town used to be like.

At the furthest point in the back sector of the Wall Market stands a large, two-story mansion, in a state of extreme disrepair.  Windows shattered, roof collapsed, door broken and shattered, and buried under debris coming from both itself and the plate up ahead.  East leads to a large clearing by the sector wall, while south leads to a trash heap.

Although half-buried with debris, this corner of the Wall Market is still very visibly a row of stores, perched within their little alcove.  A stand with a large cauldron lies abandoned nearby, once a food vendor.  A jewelry and materia store retains the only accessible door; its neighboring CD store is half-crushed by a large fragment of a supporting pillar.

The post-disaster appearance of this store leave little doubt as to how many of its contents still remain; counters and shelves appear empty and broken, leaving only merchandise posters and store signs to hint as to what might have once been sold here.  A rickety wooden door leads outside.

This building looks to have relied on lights and neon more than any other place in town, due to how many parts of it have been smashed down, emptied sockets remaining.  Tell-tale signs of this place having been a brothel or some house of humble prostitution in the past are kept as, perhaps, a twisted sort of posterity to future generations.

This very dark, circular building looks to have been an automated shop of some kind, mainly due to the lack of any counter or other devices that a human shopkeeper would have found convenient, such as a cash register.  Instead, a sole electronic panel of some sort sits on the back of the building, now obviously out of power.  A list beside it looks to possess a sort of menu as to what it provided.

This clearing is remarkably free of obstruction and debris, although conversely, there isn't much to see here either.  The wall stands upforth and solid, several dozen feet in thickness, painted a dark gray with various manners of graffiti.  A single, solid cable hangs by the wall, leading up the plate somewhere.

This impressively-stocked weapons and armor store looks to still be extremely functional - a miracle given the state of everything else around it.  Although there is no one at the counter, a vending machine cabled up to a motor battery seems to still be open for business.  The store's layout is divided between the customer section, and a chain fenced staff area where weapons and machinery are tinkered upon.

A pharmacy stands nearby this part of town, evident by the 'Medicine' sign hanging above it.  Whether any items remain in there, however, is another kettle of fish altogether.  Judging from the mountainous pieces of scrap that sit in front of the store, it is fairly easy to presume that back in its glory days, this path would have been accessible.  But now, explorers are forced to make do with going around elseroute.

This humble, strictly stone-still shop stands against the ebb and flow of time, and while its wooden peers have since withered down, its canvassed exterior has allowed it to remain fairly intact.  At this point, however, it is not good for much other than shelter from harsh weather, due to how its contents have been conveniently looted.

The road to the north is almost completely blocked off by a mountain of scrap and junk parts; to the northeast, a still-accessible weaponries store remains open, although it likely has no one manning it.  To the west was something approaching a dive bar, although the entrance is shut and barred.  Further north leads to a dilapidated mansion, while south leads towards the front portion of town.

This uncannily vanilla corner is impressively free of debris, perhaps kept that way by local scavengers.  Paths lead west and north, made painfully clear by humongous heaps of scrap metal of all shapes and sizes.  Other than the omnipresent pile of junk that seems to span an entire horizon, there is not much to do but to head elseplace here.

This non-descript split in the road possesses one shimmering object of magical nature, a save point.  Other than that, this branching multitude of paths exists just to serve the needs of those passing by, allowing them to conveniently travel from place to place in town.  Due to the presence of earlier said magical artifact, this place looks safe enough for one to stay in.

A building commands the space of this intersection.  In its operating season, it would have had dozens of LED lights lustrously displaying its purpose - a clothing bazaar.  A colorful sign points out that the chain stocks both haute couture and bargain basement products.  Unfortunately, the door has jammed completely shut due to damage.

A diner stands nearby, once perhaps the local place for the civilians of Wall Market to get something in their stomachs.  All around there are the pitiful remains of buildings, some shops that sell mundane items, and some selling material of a more seedy and dangerous nature.  To the north, another shop is visible, and a split in the road is visible to the east.

This part of town surprisingly maintains its former use, even in the wrecked days.  It's a pity all it ever did was, obviously, link parts of town to one another, as evidenced by the three-pronged junction point present.  To the west, the path leads to what looks to be an inn and a round, damaged building of some sort.  To the north, the road leads further along, deeper into town.  Southeast takes one to a separate part of town.

Once a concentrated mass of debauchery and indulgence, the pitiful leftovers of this seedy slum town do not contribute much to its former glory.  All around, it's fairly easy to see that this town relied a lot on various neon lights to boost its reputed image.  To the immediate west is a hollow building, once a fairly clean inn.  Up ahead is a blasted building with an 'Item' sign grafted onto it.  The paths lead north and east, and the road to the south leads out of this mess.
