Past the row of stores is a large clearing of dry ground, surrounded by a horde of cardboard and wooden boxes, as well as a nearby scrap shack.  Very close down the lane is a huge building with a glistening, muscular man and a dirty cloth sign that says 'MALES MALES MALES'.

There was a time when this gym would have been full of sweat and calories burning.  Now, it lies abandoned and wrecked, although it is still somewhat simple to see the layout of the exercise house.  The various mirrors that cover the walls are still present, although most of them are shattered; a boxing ring, tattered, still dominates the gym.  Various cardio and ab-toning machines lay unused with dust and grime covering them.

A few inconsequential buildings with no signs line the east side of town.  It looks like they might have been either civilian houses, or storage warehouses of some sort.  To the north, a clear path leads deeper into Wall Market, while to the south a road leads around a corner to somewhere else.  An atmosphere of wreckage accompanies this blasted town.

This is the northern end of this former playground, conveniently bordering with the gate to Sector 7.  Unfortunately, the gate is sealed off with an enormous mountain of metal, all crushed in a most unpleasant manner together.  To the east, a path can be seen that leads elsewhere in Sector 6.

This long bar-style restaurant looks to have been a fairly social place when it was operative.  Straight from the entrance, one is treated to a long row of at least twenty red stools spanning a long wooden counter, from directly behind which one would be served food.  Now, however, the only bare scraps of food remaining are those rotten beyond the core.

The security checkpoint disguised as a simple mezzanine leads down into the plaza outside of Shinra Tower. Red and blue posters, endorsing Shinra propaganda, are on the walls here. The train car passenger doors are misaligned with the platform and aren't usable in their current position.

The massive wall is anything but barren, with still-wet spray paint covering seemingly unreachable areas. The piles of rubble that obstructed movement below blends into the scene of devastation. The over-sized cable continues towards the missing upper plate.

A few larger pieces of debris litter the top of the train cars and have blocked the escape hatches, but the lack of any cover has let the wind and rain keep the tops of the cars relatively clean. To the east, an unobstructed view of Sector 7 offers a grim vista. The Sector 0 Train Station, which serviced Shinra Tower, is to the east.

The damaged conduit from below conjoins with another that's mostly intact. It appears there is a service hatch that is powered by a nearby junction box. The lights from the junction box are still brightly glowing. Shinra Tower is clearly visible from this vantage point.

A conduit being held firmly in place by heavy gauge cables is the best footing option at this height. There's a dimly glowing junction box and a jerry-rigged battery that's providing power to the over-sized fan above. More train tracks are hanging from above and seem like they're stable enough to climb up onto from the fan overhead.

The rail system and conduits from the nearby infrastructure have melded into a somewhat usable platform. Large portions of track have become entangled with the electrical panels, creating a weaving metal walkway. A conduit hangs further down and connects back with the cooling unit it was once a part of.

The leading engine of the train that serviced Shinra Tower hangs off the tracks. Oil occasionally drips from the underside of the machinery down to the sector below. The roof of the cars make for decent footing and following the train will lead to Shinra Tower. The swinging bar to the west leads to the sector below.

From the top of the wall it's possible to see to the other side of Sector 7. Even in ruins, the Sister Ray towers over the far northern wall dominating the horizon. The beams that once supported the plate hang from above and a large power cable extends to the sector below.

The metal panels from a conduit have been badly damaged or are missing entirely, which make for excellent footing. A large section of rebar sways in the wind nearby and looks like it might the only way over to the other side. The conduit levels off up above and provides ample standing space.

Wreckage from the rail system that used to run above the plate hangs above the wall. Exposed wires crackle with electricity that arcs at anything that swings nearby. The twisted metal and refuse has made it possible to reach a large conduit which might provide a clear passage under the cable used to get up here.

Soot covers the cooling unit's casing. It's been permanently stained and unaffected by the years of being exposed to the elements. The over-sized fan blades have formed a walkway and make it possible to reach a crossing signal that's stuck in the up position. The footing is a little unstable, but doesn't look like it's going to fail anytime soon.

The roof of the passenger cars makes for solid ground compared to the mangled mess of tracks and conduits below. It's still very slanted, but the rivets give good traction. The escape hatches on the top of the cars have been crushed by falling debris. The suspension railway used by the train is far above any walkable surface and continues on towards Shinra Tower.

This car was still at the train station when the engine derailed. The mezzanine below leads down into the train station that serviced Shinra Tower. Although the train cars continue on, progressing above them is no longer possible because they go into the subway tunnels that lead beneath Sector 0. The escape hatch here looks like the only means of escape for those that were trapped inside.

The large metal conduit that runs throughout this area hangs perilously over Sector 7. Many panels have fallen off, leaving dangerous looking wires exposed. The conduit looks like it was originally part of a nearby cooling unit. Safe passage is possible under the cable and over to another part of the destroyed support beam.

Travelling this lonely road seems to take ages as the wind rushes about.  Since there are no forests, the wind is able to blow freely about, thus making it quick and chilly.  A dew resides on top of the soil that surrounds the road.  The road extends to the east and to the west.

In an age when most human technology has long since been destroyed or deteriorated due to neglect, several computers amazingly whir with activity in this place. The monitors shed a light that seems quite foreign in this place as statistics and images change frequently upon them. To the north, however, is something much more out of place. A vortex of energy can be seen through the open doorway. It too hums in a deep, unearthly voice. A set of stairs leads up to a catwalk along the eastern wall.

A large, but run-down dome is here surrounded by smaller, ransacked metal domes and bins. The bins and lesser domes look as if they might have held food stores and a greenery, but have long since been raided by the desperate remnants of humanity. The greater dome sits slightly elevated on the wasteland. Its entrance is a heavy steel door which thankfully opens as a person approaches it. A sign above the door proclaims this place to be Proto Dome.

The road stretches to the north and south with hardly a thing to see except for vast expanses of destruction in every direction. A large metal dome can be seen in the distance to the southwest, an ancient vestige of a long-dead civilization. Craters line this ruined highway and the faint odor of seasalt is being carried in the wind.

Computers and machinery in horrible condition line the walls of this room. The only light in here is afforded by the swirling vortex that is the time gate and a faint glow from the room to the south. A panel sits near the wall in front of a monitor, both of which appear to be broken. The walls, floor, and ceiling all seem to be made from a tempered steel.

rooms.name: On a catwalk inside Proto Dome

userData.LongDescription: This section of the catwalk is beside and at a lower level than the area containing the enertron. Machines and metal paneling make up the walls around the catwalk. To the north, the machines on the left taper off and a faint glow seeps in from another room at the other end. There is a set of stairs leading up to the platform to the west. On the east wall there seems to be some etchings made in the metal.

A stiff, cold air rushes through here, coming off of the ruined building to the north.  The road here extends to the east and north.  Life is non-existent on and off of the road.  The earth surrounding the road is damp and muddy; it is also devoid of life.

The road bends to the west and north here. The eastern edge of the road is bordered by the coast. There are two distinct features of this world that can be seen from this place. First, to the west is one of this era's domes that once provided shelter to humanity, but it now stands empty. The second feature, to the east, is a vast soot-colored ocean. Salt permeates the air, but there is also an almost unidentifiable baser stench: the reek of death and rot. Nothing could live in the dark murkiness of that ruined sea.

rooms.name: On a catwalk inside Proto Dome

userData.LongDescription: A glow emanates from the room below. The machines that make up the wall at the other end of the catwalk tapered away and opened up to a room with several functioning computers running. The whir of those machines can be faintly heard over the winds blowing outside. Due to the glow coming from below, some carvings can be seen on the eastern wall panel.

The road here has been devastated by the unearthly force that that arose many generations ago. Debris lines the sides of these battered streets. To the south, past and plain of rubble and craters, a dome peeks over the horizon. Also, in the distance northeast from this place, a ruined skyscraper towers over the rubble.

Musty, stagnant air fills the once glorious Proto Dome. The metal paneling that constitutes the walls and floor has deteriorated and rusted in many places. Nonfunctional machinery line the walls and machine parts are scattered around the floor. There is no sign that life has inhibited this place in many generations. This place seems to be home to wasted potential and lost causes. The dome expands to the north, while the door to the south leads out into the wasteland.

The road forms a three-way intersection here.  One of the paths extends to the south, the next pushes to the north, and the last one stretches west.  To the north, a large factory can be seen.  Past the intersection to the east is more of the muddy soil, but also in sight is the dark, ominous ocean.

The air becomes more dank the further one ventures into the dome as the ventilation systems have long since terminated their function. There is just enough light to make out several rundown machines and a lone functional enertron in the northwest corner of the room. Also, near the east wall there are some stairs leading to a catwalk. There seem to be no signs of people living in the dome, nor is there any food here to draw them to this place.

A large concrete wall that stands ten feet high is the main fortification for the factory that stands just to the north.  There is no concrete barrier where the road extends into the factory.  A chain-linked fence is ravaged and open where the road enters, leaving plenty of room to go into the factory.  The earth surrounding here isn't muddy, but rigid and dusty.  The road heads south towards an intersection.

None of this era's inhabitants venture to this place. The landscape is as barren of life as one could expect on the surface of the moon. Craters dot the landscape. To the north a massive gash in the earth stretches for miles. Farther north, the remnants of a building lie empty amid the rubble. The dead landscape stretches out to the east, while the road leads west and south.

Completely inside of the former Lab 32 structure is a long stretch of unadultered highway that extends eastward. To the southeast is a small concrete path that follows along the side of the highway. The scent of fumes and a haze of smoke waft about the room.

More structural fragments line this segment of the road, few from the highway above, and the majority from nearby former structures. A very faint mist can be seen to the east, enveloping the lower areas of the path. The path descends eastward and ascends westward.

The road leading to the north and into Lab 32 isn't as bad as the rest of the lab. It remained mostly intact, save for the outermost parts which are torn up. On the western half of the road, there is a large pile of metallic debris. A small tapping of feet can be heard from some animal residing in here. The road also leads to the Proto Dome.

rooms.name: In the middle of the path

userData.LongDescription: The nadir of the path converges here. Two paths mirror each other:  one going upward to the northeast and one going upward to the northwest. On the ground is a half-inch deep puddle of the same liquid that graces the low points of the mirrored paths. A steady billow of fog enraptures the room. An extremely large portion of the highway has fallen off here and has pierced the ground, nearly forming a wall to the north.

At its lowest point, the path is enveloped in a miasma of fog and other fumes. Over the course of several years, breathing this air constantly would cause permanent physical harm, but a brief trip through won't cause any damaging effects. The path is also damp, giving hint that a source of some liquid is near. The path bends downward to the southeast and climbs upward to the west.

The eastern portion of the former Lab 32 structure is still full of the destruction that was wrought in 1999. No signs of native biological life are to be found here. Particles of concrete and shards of metal are strewn about everywhere. There is a small path that leads down to the southwest, and a winding path leading back south.

The road, complete with holes and debris scattered about randomly, leads from the Arris Dome to the decimated Lab 32. The carnage wrought by Lavos in 1999 will forever torment these lands. Occasionally, a deformed animal scurries about in the debris, making small metal tapping sounds with it's feet as it rushes about within the piles.

The side path off of the main highway slowly descends from the height on which the highway itself is located. Continuing down this path, more destroyed buildings can be seen not too far off in the distance. The path itself extends to the east and northwest.

The side route off of the main drag slowly descends from the elevation on which the highway itself is located. Continuing down this path, more totalled buildings can be seen not too far off in the distance.  The path itself extends to the west and northeast.

At the southwestern most point, the path is enveloped in a haze of fog and other fumes. Continually breathing this air over a period of time would cause permanent physical harm, but a brief stint through won't cause any lasting effects. The path is also damp, giving hint that a source of some liquid is near. The path bends downward to the southwest and climbs upward to the east.

Several large pieces from buildings line this portion of the road, a couple from the highway above and the bulk of them from nearby former structures. A very faint brume can be seen to the west, enveloping the lower areas of the road. The path descends westward and ascends eastward.

This narrow ravine runs to the north, up the mountain, and to the south, towards the foot of the mountain.  A river runs down the mountain, gradually widening here, and quickly widening shortly to the south.  High cliffs run to the east and west, preventing any travel other than to the north and south.  Small clumps of orange and yellow flowers grow scattered about the green grass that covers much of the ground here.  Plants grow upon the cliffs, but are too high up to be reached.

The path splits abruptly here, forming a T.  The path north leads to a village, which is little more than a few scattered huts and campfires.  A break in the trees to the south serves as an entrance to the expansive forest.  Travel to the east is blocked by a lone mountain rising high into the air.

A shallow river covers much of the ground of this portion of the ravine.  Small patches of dry, grassy land break up the flow of the water.  Orange and yellow flowers grow on the small islands.  Large cliffs to the east and west cast shadows over the surface of the river.  To the south, the ravine widens, and so does the river.  To the north, the river quickly narrows, as the path goes up the mountain towards the peak.  The base of the mountain can be seen to the south of here, where a path leads away from the mountain.

A small river runs southwards, while a grassy path runs to the west and south here.  A muddy bank extends from the western edge of the river, while the eastern edge runs up along a large cliff.  A small rock rests near the northern end of the river, with small yellow and orange flowers growing upon it.  A sheer cliff face rises up to the north, preventing any travel in that direction.  A black sphere hovers high overhead, in front of the cliff face.

The sound of drums beating and the smell of meat being cooked slowly drifts from the east, while the sound of wild creatures can be heard to the west, in the expansive range of mountains.  This path seems to lead to a village, as well as the forest that can be seen spreading to the southeast.

rooms.name: Near the top of Mystic Mountain

userData.LongDescription: A path runs to the north, up the face of the mountain towards the peak, and to the east, where it eventually turns southwards, running down the mountain.  Several small rocks rest on the ground, surrounded by small patches of yellow and orange flowers.  To the northeast, the cliff face runs straight up, eventually ending at the peak.  This area is enclosed by numerous small cliffs, preventing travel in any direction other than to the north or east.

A gradually widening river runs down the eastern side of this narrow ravine.  High cliffs to the west and east make travel in those directions impossible.  A solitary rock sits in the middle of the pathway, midway between the western cliff and the river.  A muddy bank extends from the western end of the river outwards.  The path to the south continues down the mountain, while the path to the north soon turns west, fading out of view.

rooms.name: At the base of Mystic Mountain

userData.LongDescription: A large rock sits at the southern end of this area, the foot of the Mystic Mountain.  This is the mouth of a ravine, extending northwards and leading up the face of the mountain.  A shallow river covers much of the eastern portion of this area, while the west is a narrow strip of dry land, which broadens towards the base of the mountain.  High cliffs enclose this area, preventing movement in any direction other than north or south.  A path to the south leads away from the mountain, while the path to the north continues into a narrower portion of the ravine.

Numerous small plants grow out of the grass on the peak of this mountain. A sheer cliff drops away from the southern edge of the peak, while the path starting on the western edge of the peak runs to the south, up and down the slope.  Numerous rocks rest scattered along the path and the peak of the mountain.  A black sphere hovers directly in front of the cliff face a short distance down from the peak.  Thick foliage grows on much of the peak, preventing travel along the mountain in any direction but down.

rooms.name: At the base of a mountain

userData.LongDescription: A large mountain rises directly to the north, and it looks like a path has been carved leading up its slope.  Despite its height, the mountain seems like it would be easy enough to climb.  An occasional shrieking sound can be heard from the top of the mountain, presumably from whatever creature makes its home here.  A crossroads can be seen to the east, as well as a thick jungle.

The ruins of Laruba Village stand to the north.  All that can be seen of them from here are the tattered remnants of a lone hut in a destroyed section of the forest.  To the south lies a large clearing with a view of the surrounding area.  On either side of the makeshift path stand many trees, marking the border of the forest.

This hut is actually quite large, despite its outward appearance.  It appears that some form of commerce goes on here, as many hides, feathers, tusks, and horns from various primitive beasts are piled up everywhere.  Also laid out on the ground is an assortment of weapons and armors.  The proprietor of this business seems to be a grizzled old man who stands in the center of the hut.

This hut actually seems to be quite a bit larger than most of the huts in the village, and is much more extravagantly decorated.  A pair of rugs made out of the skins of prehistoric tigers lay on the floor, while the heads of slain beasts adorn the walls.  A large fire burns in the northern half of the hut, and a few plants add a little greenery to the room.

Surrounding the large path between the nearby ruins and Ioka Village is a mixture of scenery.  The ground is comprised of nothing but dust and rocks with no clear boundaries.  To the south lies a mountain range, and to the west stands a great forest.  The remains of the Laruba Ruins stand to the north; the Hunting Grounds and the Dactyl Nest to the northeast.

The path reaches a halt here as the forest grows too thick to continue to the west, north, or east.  Fog covers the area endlessly.  Almost all of the grass is destroyed, but a few small patches live on; even the bushes have begun to wither and die.  A few small flowers and rocks separate the ruins from the forest.  To the south is the largest portion of the wreckage.

rooms.name: In front of the Hunting Grounds

userData.LongDescription: This area is nothing more than a small crossroads.  A path leading from the campground to the dense jungle to the north passes over a path heading east-west.  To the east, the path leads to a small hut, while the western path seems to stop at the base of a large mountain.  The guttural sounds of animals fill the air near the fetid jungle to the north.

A dark fog permeates throughout the region, which was once a grand place; where it originates is unclear.  Two totem poles stand guard, protecting the village as though nothing ever happened.  Parts of the grass have been burned.  On both the east and west sides of the path stand trees.  To the north is more destruction; to the south, an escape.

The path opens up in the middle of the village.  The burned patterns in the ground seem to indicate that it is in this space that the villagers would gather and meet.  To the north is nothing but more ruins; to the south the entrance to this sparse place.  The forest still boxes the area in from either side.  The area itself is rather barren, with the exception of a few rocks and some flowers.

Flanking the entrance to this large meeting ground are two totem poles.  The path from the village runs between them, and then continues north all the way past the campground.  In the center of the campground, a circle of drums has been set up around the remnants of a fire.  It looks like this would make an excellent place to take a nap, assuming the natives allowed it.

There are two prominent structures in this area that catch the eye, the first of which is a primitive hut.  The hut seems to be made out of the dried skin of some kind of reptile, and does not seem like it would protect from much more than the sun and rain.  To the east, a strange wooden structure has been erected for reasons unknown.  It looks like some form of watchtower, but who created it is a mystery.

This hut is not very large inside, with barely enough floorspace for a few people to sleep comfortably.  The rest of the room is taken up by several clay pots, filled with grains and other plants.  Also, a small fire burns softly near one of the walls.  The path outside can be seen through the hut's door.

This little path ends abruptly in front of a prehistoric abode.  This hut does not appear to be as large as the one that can be seen in the center of the village, but the villagers don't exactly live in the lap of luxury.  A thin curl of smoke rises from a hole at the top of the hut, and it smells like cooking meat.  The path leads back east.

This hut stands far apart from the rest of the village proper, far past even the campground itself.  Those who live inside are probably not the social type.  A short distance south of the path, the large bleached skeleton of some primitive animal is half-buried in the dirt.  Further exploration in that and any direction but west is stopped by several rock outcroppings.

The main path continues north through this area, bridging a small creek on its journey.  Smaller paths lead off in a couple directions, to other areas of the village.  Huts can be seen all around, and a very large bonfire stands in the middle of this area.  Across the creek, it looks like there is a large meeting area of some sort.

The smell of roasting meat fills the entirety of this hut, and the large carcass of an unknown animal seems to be the cause.  The meat is being slowly cooked over a small fire in the center of the hut.  A huge stone table on the western edge of the hut has been laden with fruits and vegetables to complete the meal.

To the west, the forest gets considerably denser and darker.  However, the rest of the area seems to be fairly bright, and a dirt trail meanders to the southeast.  A large puddle of mud has formed in the middle of the path, slightly impeding travel.  A fresh set of muddy footprints leads north, into the thick, impassable woods.

In this section of the jungle, the main path goes north and south, in a remarkably straight line.  A smaller path branches off to the east, but it clearly appears to be the road less traveled.  Lush yellow flowers bloom along the trail, adding some much-needed color to the otherwise excessively verdant landscape.

The path to the north cuts off here, and abruptly spills into a churning pit of boiling tar.  Several small creatures have apparently gotten trapped in the pit, and are struggling feebly to free themselves.  A large tree next to the quagmire seems to be slowly sinking into the muck, as several of its roots are already deeply embedded in the tar.

Despite being almost completely surrounded by a thick pool of black tar, this strange peninsula somehow manages to avoid sinking into the muck.  Very little foliage grows in this area, probably because the arable soil has been eroded away by the swamp surrounding it.  A small path to the southwest leads back to the jungle, as all other directions are blocked off.

This is the entrance to a thick jungle, and a break in the trees leads south, towards a village.  A vast canopy of leaves spreads out above, blocking out a good portion of the sunlight, though it is not too dark to clearly see that a large sign has been planted into the dirt here.

The bubbling of a brook running alongside the path to the west is the dominant sound in this area, its only competition being the squawking of noisy birds that have made their homes in the trees of this jungle. A few forms of aquatic plant life have eked out an existence along the banks of the stream, despite the current. A trail through the woods continues east and south.

This section of the jungle is considerably darker than the area to the southwest, due mostly to the excessive amount of trees here.  Very little light is able to filter down through the thick canopy of leaves overhead, filling the largely sunny forest with a dense and oppressive darkness.  A small trail leads east through the trees.

A variety of exotic and colorful flora flourishes in the humid environment of this lush jungle.  Bright yellow flowers bloom in the underbrush of the trees, nursed by rainfall that filters down through the leaves above.  A clear trail has been cut through the plant life, leading to the southeast and to the north.

This section of the hunting range continues on in much the same fashion as the rest of the forest does, though the trees here have noticeably more vines hanging from their branches and winding around their trunks.  While there are vines throughout the jungle, they just seem to be in abundance here.  A path continues through the trees to the north and southwest.

This appears to be the closest thing to a southeastern corner this forest has.  Trees form a wall to the south and east, leaving only the west and northeast open as viable travel directions.  Except for the occasional sound of something dying in the distance, the only thing of note here is the decaying skeleton of what appears to be an unfortunate adventurer.

The ground in this forest path is littered with a large assortment of rocks of various sizes.  None of them are large enough to block the path leading south or northwest, but some of them are fairly big.  Scattered amongst the rocks are various specimens of some bright red fruit, apparently fallen from a nearby tree.

rooms.name: Before an opening in the wall

userData.LongDescription: The conveyor belt continues moving to the west, and the wall is getting closer.  There is an opening that the conveyor belt goes into, but it is pitch black and appears to have no light source at all.  There being no safe alternative to escape the belt, the only choice is to enter the wall.

Neon green lights are placed around a level platform.  Near the center part of this metal platform is a ellipse.  This ellipse functions as an elevator between levels within the Factory.  The elliptical elevator leads upwards, while the hallway leads south.

This 10 foot by 7 foot area functions almost like a loading and unloading zone for the facility.  There is a large opening leading to the conveyor belt.  Metal gates surround this platform, excluding the side that faces the belt itself.  There is a door leading into the Quality Control  structure; also, there is the possibility of getting on the conveyor belt.

In this tightly sealed, dim room are several completed robots, held in storage. Strangely all of them appear to be active.  This is due to the Factory itself still being active and running autonomously. The robots circle about the room in an odd manner. The only exit from here is the door.

rooms.name: At an intersection in the facility

userData.LongDescription: The ground level turns into an intersection due to a ladder extending down from the above catwalk.  Directly above is the disjointed catwalk while the ground level extends to the east and west.  The catwalk wraps around the wall quite intricately while the ground is spartan and plain.

At the northwestern corner of the mainframe hub lies the enormous switchboard for the entire factility.  Massive bandwidth lines are behind a locked door with a half inch thick plexiglass window to see through.  By each switch on the board is a set of lights, flashing either green or orange.  From here there are paths to the south and to the east.

rooms.name: At a corner on the second floor

userData.LongDescription: The long hallway diverges from it usual east-west flow here at the corner. A humming sound can be heard from here, most likely eminating from the elevator to the north. To the west is a very long stretch of hallway, broken only by a doorway that is in the northern face of the wall.

It would seem the majority of the work is done within this machine, as all of the wires are added and the shell is completed.  There are more arms hanging from the ceiling of the machine than there were previously.  As before, these arms detect life and do not attempt to wire it and add a metal plate onto its back.  The conveyor belt keeps going out of the machine.

This section of the catwalk provides the only true, complete view of the facility. From here, everything that isn't behind a closed door is visible. The entrie production line scheme can be seen from here as well. The catwalk breaks to the north and to the south.

In this portion of metallic hallway, there resides a computer terminal.  Other than that, the room itself is quite bleak.  A dreary, plain metal wall is opposite that of the computer terminal.  Beside the terminal is a set of instructions on how to use it.

Stuck in the southwestern corner is an opened service hatch used to get down to the third floor when the elevators aren't in use.  Other than the hatch itself, the corner is pretty bare. No instrumentation is located here. There are exits to the north and to the northeast.

After some exposure to the heightened decibel levels, the intensity of the sound seems to decrease. Up above and to the north, a catwalk is isolated from the rest of the upper level. The production line doesn't falter in its automation as it continues to produce robots. The ground moves both east and west.

rooms.name: At the base of a ladder

userData.LongDescription: At the end of the hallway is the ladder that leads up to the first floor of the Laboratory.  On the wall by the ladder is a small plaque that states this is the second floor of the Laboratory.  To the west, there is a long hallway.  A small ventilation duct on the ceiling by the ladder circulates air throughout the hallway.

In the middle of this section of hallway is a doorway marked 'Computer Room'.  The door would slide from the right half of the doorway, but power to the doorway itself has been severed.  The paths from here lead east, west, and through the doorway to the north.

At this intersection, a sign visible to the east would indicate that an elevator lies in that direction. To the north, the monotony of the hall design is interrupted by the archway for a series of rather thick blast doors. A small panel lies before the door, likely an operating mechanism.

The eastern part of the break room is much cooler than the other half. This is due to the refrigeration unit giving off cool air.  Other than the refrigerator, there isn't anything else located on this half of the room. A small closet is open on the south wall, but has nothing inside. The exit from here is to the west.

Sloping downward slightly, this hallway leads into a much larger room than what is visible at the moment.  A plethora of audible sounds can be heard from here, such as soldering, grinding, and cutting of metals.  The hallway ends and the facility begins to the south while travelling north will lead to an elevator.

rooms.name: At the northwest corner on the second floor

userData.LongDescription: At the northwest corner of the second floor in the Laboratory, there is an opening in the north portion of the wall.  Above that opening is a sign that says 'R-storage'.  Entering into the storage unit is impossible due to the small gap that encloses the entrance.  The corner adjoins two directions, one to the east and one to the south.  To the south is a metal door.

Through the metal door lies the engineer's station.  This room is used to monitor the production of the assembly lines and to make sure there are no foul-ups.  After its automation, the engineer who had this menial task was no longer needed.  The only exit is out of the door.

This conveyor belt moves at a decent speed towards an open machine.  The machine's opening looks like a doorway minus the door.  On top of the machine there is a vent that is releasing a minor amount of fumes.  These fumes change the scent of the facility slightly.  The only way to go is into the machine.

rooms.name: In the southeast corner of the Lab

userData.LongDescription: Two paths adjoin here in the southeast corner of the Laboratory's first floor. A white glow emanates from the north, while to the west stretches a hallway that is a bit dimmer.  On the wall is an air vent that causes air to flow about the room. To the west is a corridor while to the north lies an elevator.

rooms.name: Before a room on the upper level

userData.LongDescription: This corner is darker compared to the rest of the facility because there is no direct light source near it.  Only certain parts of the facility can be seen from here.  On the north wall near the corner is a strange unmarked door.  The walkway leads to the west and to the south.

This medium size structure housed what was a very important operation, Quality Control.  With no more employees, this operation has died off.  Workstations are scattered randomly about with various parts, tools, and nearly finished robots.  The door leads out into the facility again while a maze of workstations lead east.

rooms.name: An exit from the conveyor belt

userData.LongDescription: Although riding a conveyor belt around a production facility might give some a thrill, there must be an exit.  A loading zone that is used to take robots from the conveyor belt is up ahead.  Proper timing is the key to getting off of the conveyor belt; otherwise anything on it should be prepared for another lap around because the belt isn't making stops any time soon.

Long automated arms, each with a different tool, are doing work on a robot up ahead on the conveyor belt. Fortunately for anyone riding the conveyor belt, these arms detect biological life and do not attempt to work on it. Sparks fly and metal is formed by these machines. The conveyor belt continues out of the machine.

The southeastern corner of the first floor in the factory is well lit.  A powerful white light shines from above.  Along the ground to the north is a conveyor belt that is spinning north.  Along the sides of the belt are green running lights.  To the west is the entrance to the factory.

This is a small control room overlooking what looks to be the facility's main reactor. Direct access is impossible from here, as blastproof glass shields this station from the area ahead. A door looks to lead out there, but it's been long since sealed off. A series of controls line a countertop of sorts, no wires visible for what they're connected to.

rooms.name: Before an open robot storage unit.

userData.LongDescription: On the northern side of the hallway, there's an open portion on the wall with a small sign above it reading 'R-storage'.  Fitting into the storage would be difficult because of the very small size.  To the west is a corner on the second floor and to the east is another stretch of hallway.

The hall itself ends and forms a corner on the upper level in this enormous facility.  Right beside the wall is a ladder that is leading down to the ground floor.  All of the sounds of production are much louder.  The upper level path continues to the west while the hallway pushes north.

rooms.name: Within a hallway on the second floor

userData.LongDescription: The air here carries with it a deep scent of ionization.  Being purified of harmful air pathogens, it wafts freely about the hallway.  Within the center of this section of hallway is an air duct that is exhuming the air.  The hallway itself extends to the east and to the west.

rooms.name: Between two sections of the conveyor belt

userData.LongDescription: This part of the path sits in the middle of the conveyor belt.  To the north, south, and east, the conveyor belt can be seen moving in its cyclical manner.  The grime on the floor seems to get thicker as the path extends to the west more.  The two exits from here are to the west and to the east.

rooms.name: Western half of the Control room

userData.LongDescription: This side of the room yields nothing new.  Further examination of the door shows that it leads to the crane itself, but the door is locked tight and unable to be opened due to the controlling terminal being disabled.  The only choice is to turn back east.

The ground level comes to a dead end here.  Strangely enough, there is a door on the north face of the wall at the end of the path.  The door is unlabeled.  There are no sounds coming from within the door.  The path moves back to the east or through the door.

The room itself comes to a dead end here at this point, but near the dead end wall is an oval which is illuminated by a red light.  A small sign on the back wall says that this is an elevator and it leads down to the Factory.  The room continues towards an intersection.

In front of this metal door sits the southwestern corner of the second floor of the Laboratory.  The corner is brightly lit and well ventilated.  To the east stretches a long hallway, the end of it not visible.  An emergency beacon is broken in the ceiling above, unable to alert the inhabitants of the Laboratory of danger if it were to arise.

rooms.name: Upper level of the QC structure

userData.LongDescription: From the upper floor within the Quality Control center, a complete view of the operation is possible. There are several stations that are empty or have minor clutter from tools. Any other station has a partially disassembled robot that was being worked on. There is a door that leads out of the Quality Control structure and a ladder that goes down to the main floor.

The catwalk ends beside a door on the north wall.  A walkway can been seen looking across to the east.  Why these two paths were never connected remains a mystery, possibly a design flaw.  There is a door to the north and a catwalk path back to the west.

rooms.name: At the base of a ladder

userData.LongDescription: Now standing at the base of the ladder, one of the more defining features of this area is the stainless steel railings that hug the walls of this floor. Posts jut symmetrically, every five feet or so, lending to the architectural precision present throughout this facility. The flooring is comprised of a dense grating, not an ounce of give displayed even to the heaviest of adventurers. Lighting isn't bright, a simple, dull, yellow glow from the lamps suspended from the ceiling, but certainly enough to easily navigate through the hallway east.

The western half of this corridor is dimmer as compared to the eastern half. There are four small floor vents that are taking in air within the corridor. Near the west end of the corridor is a door. The corridor also leads east towards a corner.

This section on the ground level runs parallel with one of the conveyor belts. The production seems to be moving quickly and without hinderance. The sound that the assembly line makes is much louder near it. The ground continues to the west while a ladder returns to the walkway above.

rooms.name: In a corner on the ground floor

userData.LongDescription: This corner is located rather close to the conveyor belt, which can be seen quite visibly to the west.  This part of the ground floor is a bit grimy as compared to other sections.  Speculation says it comes from the conveyor belt and the large machines which are nearby this path.  The path to the west passes under a section of the conveyor belt while there is a ladder to the north.

At the north end of this small straightaway, there lies a circular disc that functions as an elevator.  Around the elevator are running lights that fill the room with a white glow.  On the wall is a sign that reads 'Laboratory - 1F'.  To the south continues the first floor of the Laboratory.

rooms.name: A dead end in the path

userData.LongDescription: The path finally turns into a dead end here as it hits the western wall of the facility. The conveyor belt continues into the wall to the north and comes out of the wall to the south. The grime seems to be a bit less thick here than it is to the east. The only path from here is to the east.

In the northwest corner of the first floor lies an oval shaped disc.  This room, other than that disc, is a dead end.  On the dead end wall is a sign that says that the oval is an elevator that will take you down to the Laboratory.  The room is lit up by a pale green light.  To the south is an intersection.

This section of the catwalk branches off into several different paths.  There is a door to the north and a ladder along the west side of the catwalk.  The catwalk itself extends to the east and to the south.  The view from the catwalk is quite nice as well, providing almost a full view of the facility.

Engraved in the metal wall is a computer terminal. The terminal itself seems to be frozen. Fortunately, before the system locked up, it released a hatch somewhere. The corridor continues to the east.  At the west end of the corridor, there is a door, which is opposite of the computer terminal.

A maze of workstations is seemingly scattered about the room in a random fashion.  Perhaps the emergency that forced everyone to evacuate is the cause of this disarray.  Tools, parts, and mostly-finished robots lie strewn about on these stations.  A ladder shoots up to the upper floor of the Quality Control center while the maze of stations leads west.

Upon exiting the first machine, the most notable stop is another machine.  The exterior of the machine up ahead is nearly identical to the previous one, the only difference being a gauge or two.  A paltry amount of fumes escape a vent from on top of the machine.  The conveyor belt keeps moving into the machine.

rooms.name: Moving back west on the conveyor belt

userData.LongDescription: After completing the curve, the conveyor belt moves to the west.  There are no machines ahead for the robots to go into.  This ride must have been to cool them down so they didn't burn whoever had to handle them.  The belt continues moving to the west.

rooms.name: The southwestern corner of the first floor

userData.LongDescription: This corner of the first floor is well lit and tidy.  To the north is a conveyor belt which is rotating at high speeds towards the south, preventing travel to the north.  To the east is the entrance of the Factory.

rooms.name: Eastern half of the Control room

userData.LongDescription: There is a large terminal in the center of the room. This terminal once was used to store data about the crane and its functions, but now has errored like some of the other terminals. On the western half of the room is a door leading somewhere. The only other exit is the door that leads out.

This corridor is quite secluded and lonely. Wedged between two airtight metal doors, a musty air looms about this room. The air is thick and damp and has an odd scent, but nothing harmful. There are doors to the north and south, and other than those exceptions this corridor is barren.

rooms.name: Within a corner in the mainframe room

userData.LongDescription: The eastern path of the mainframe storage room is just a deadend.  A mainframe sits here behind a large plexiglass window.  In the corner is some kind of storage box, but that box has been open for quite some time and left for bare.  The only exit from here is back to the west.

rooms.name: In the southeastern corner of the facility

userData.LongDescription: This enormous facility had to stop somewhere, and it was stopped at one point here in the southeast corner.  Barring such structural significance, there really isn't anything of importance here.  Two paths adjoin to form this corner, one to the north and one to the west.  The northern path is short and has a ladder at the end.

rooms.name: Before the elevator on the second floor

userData.LongDescription: Breaking north from the corner is a few more feet of hallway, and then the main attraction of this deadend, the elevator.  The elevator follows in the same fashion as the others; running lights around the sides and a circular disc that moves from floor to floor.  Going back south leads to the southeastern corner of the second floor.

rooms.name: A possible escape from the belt

userData.LongDescription: Upon exiting the machine, the belt begins to turn northward.  At the end of this curve it begins to head back the way it came.  To the southeast is a small corner that is easily within leaping distance.  Exiting the belt from here is possible by leaping into the corner.  The only other option is to continue riding it around.

rooms.name: Below the catwalk on the belt

userData.LongDescription: Two ground level paths can be seen from here, one to the north and one to the south.  Up above the steadily moving conveyor belt is the catwalk path that extends from the north to the south.  The catwalk is reachable by hand from the conveyor belt.  The belt continues moving to the west.

More grating and paneling constitute this otherwise mundane section of hallway. Making a ninety degree turn, the sign that noted an elevator looks to have been telling the truth as the lift is visible at the end of the adjoining hallway. One of the ceiling lights flickers every three seconds, perhaps mimicking the desire of a wayward adventurer that just wants out of here.

The corner at the end of the western corridor reveals a hatch.  There is a white light directly above the hatch to provide light for those coming or going.  To the west is a corridor while the hatch leads down.  On the wall to the east is a reminder to all of the former employees.

This room marks the beginning of the inside of the Factory.  Two large metal doors protect the Factory entrance.  On the wall immediately across from the doors is an inactive computer terminal.  The hallway leads east and west from here.

rooms.name: In a corner near the conveyor belt

userData.LongDescription: This dead end corner is located just southeast of the conveyor belt that transports the robots about the facility.  From here, the sides of the conveyor belt rotating non-stop are the only thing in sight.  The lighting in this corner is a tad dim.  The only exit from here is to the east.

On this end of the hallway is an intersection between three paths.  The path to the north leads to a circular disc that glows green.  To the south is a conveyor belt that rotates to the south, allowing passage to the south.  To the east is a stretch of hallway that leads to another intersection.

From this corner along the heightened walkway, there is an excellent view of the entire Production Facility.  In view, there is a large conveyor belt system assembling more robots.  There seems to be some kind of control operation to the north.  A ladder leads downward to the ground level, which is right by the production line.  The walkway continues to the north and to the east.

The walkway has a very abrupt end to it.  Visible to the west is a smaller catwalk, but the walkway does not connect to it.  At the edge of the walkway is a ladder that leads down to a different portion of the ground level.  The walkway also heads to the east.

At the end of the one way conveyor belt is an intersection on the first floor.  Travel to the south is cut off due to the conveyor belt spinning the opposite way, but there are two more paths available.  To the west lies more hallway while to the north lies a glowing oval.

Caution tape marks a few feet before the elevator, a small security bar attached to the wall to aid in preventing things from passing through when the lift is on another floor. A few sparks shower from the wiring in the ceiling on occasion, closer examination yielding a bit of fraying, likely from rats. In fact, the decayed carcass of an electrocuted rat rests against the wall, its body contorted in an expression of unadulterated pain.

Through the unmarked metal door lies a plain room. Most likely used for a break room at some point, this room now serves no purpose. On the eastern half of the break room is a refrigeration unit. The metal door exits the break room while there is an eastern half of the room.

rooms.name: An intersection within the final hallway

userData.LongDescription: A T-shaped intersection is reached which is near large blast doors. A sign along the wall denotes what lies on each end of the hall. Here, the typically blemish-free floor sports what looks like the scars of a conflict or accident long ago in the form of scorch marks and dented, broken strands of mesh plating.

The layer of grime gets thicker as the path continues moving west.  This grime can most definitely be attributed to the machines.  Anything that comes in contact with the grime becomes a little bit slicker.  The path turns into a dead end to the west and becomes less grimy to the east.

rooms.name: Inside of a large mainframe hub

userData.LongDescription: Around this room are many large mainframes, all still active and operating.  There is a definitive hum coming from the machines denoting their existant functionality.  This area is very well ventilated, and is spotless from dust.  An active computer terminal is cycling through long lists of data.  The rooms splits off into three directions, west, east, and southwest.

At the end of the long catwalk which spans the entire facility, there is a door marked 'Quality Control Room'. The catwalk ends several feet before this and connects into a solid concrete structure within the production facility. The only thing on this platform is the door for the Quality Control Room. The only other path is to the north.

A number of terminals litter this room, monitors displaying the diagnostics of various systems throughout the facility. The lighting is a bit brighter at this dead end, but not by much. A segment of the flooring in a corner looks to have been removed for maintenance, some old tools are strewn about the floor.

Nearly mirroring the hallway that runs along the northern half of the second floor, this room is only missing one thing from being a clone, and that is the robot storage. Other than that one difference, the hallways are identical. To the west is the corner while to the east is a door and more hallway.

The roar of the waterfall is muted now, but is still quite audible in this section of the cave. The stone floor seems to be like a bridge, with very deep water blocking the way east and west. Openings are visible to the north and south.

The roar of the waterfall seems to grow louder in this small, square-shaped cave. The light coming through the waterfall wavers and casts odd shadows around the place. Algae gives the dark stone walls a slightly greenish sheen, barely noticable in the dim, wavering light. Small fish swim around in the shallow waters contained within this part of the cave. An opening can be seen in the northwest.

The shallow waterway curves from the south to the east, and doesn't go around behind the Water Palace.  Grassy banks line both sides of the water.  Some lily pads with flowers float around as if bored, and some small gravel lines the bottom of the waterway.  Even from the side, the palace looks imposing.

rooms.name: Near the End of the Large Cavern

userData.LongDescription: The peninsula seems to hook to the west as it gradually gets narrower. It is no less slippery than before, being that much closer to the source of the water. The bluish light is a lot brighter in this area of the cave... In fact, the ethereal light seems to look like a beautiful mermaid holding a staff.

The cavernous room arches upwards, several stalactites dripping water everywhere. Puddles of water collect in various parts of the rocky platform, sustaining small pockets of life wherever possible. On either side of the peninsula, the water flows quietly and noiselessly. A bluish light can be seen to the north.

The peninsula ends in a sharp point, as if there's something very important to the west. The water continues to flow past, its smooth surface interrupted only by the occasional droplet of water from the stalactites above. A blue, ethereal light lies to the east.

The shallow pool is surrounded on all sides by rock cliffs, but the highest point is to the north.  A waterfall runs off the cliff to the north, and a cave opening can barely be seen through it.  Many lily pads flounder here, and a medium sized rock sticks up out of the water, making one wonder if there are any that are hidden.

The walls have been cut away to form a circular rock stairwell. A rough, crumbling staircase leading up is set into the wall. Another blinking light hangs askew near the stairs. Its ambience makes the stairway appear eager to receive a guest...or swallow one whole.

The low lighting of the cave makes this spring appear a pool of ink. Its surface throws back an almost completely black reflection, like a photograph and its negative. It is impossible to tell how deep it is. Indeed, it is not much of a stretch for one to remember fairy tales and picture the spring as some sort of enchanted, bottomless pool.

Another long, narrow rock corridor leads deeper into the caves. Weak, flickering light, hardly enough to make anything visible, trickles into the corridor. Shadows play on the walls and ground, waxing and waning. They almost seem ready to reach out and grab with an ethereal hand...

Four passages connect, resulting in a large, rectangular intersection. There are some sort of lights hanging from the walls, flickering on and off like insane fireflies. Three narrow passages branch to the north, west, and east, and a grand, sweeping passage to the south, underneath an overpass, provides stunning contrast.

The cave's suspended ledge ends with in a fishhook to the north. Decomposed scraps of what may have once been wood are strewn across the floor in front of the wall. A thin layer of sand covers the ground; strangely, it is perfectly smooth, with no prints or marks.

rooms.name: Cave to South Figaro, north entrance

userData.LongDescription: A slender anteroom cut in stone, the room is some degree cooler than the other rooms, although nothing in the immediate area would explain why this is so.  A well-travelled path leads north to a dark spring or south to another section of the cave.

A twisting pathway curls like a snake, finally resolving into a passage that leads southeast. One lone light hangs from the wall, but it is trying (and failing) to keep the path lit. Visibility is poor; however, a vampire might feel welcome. And is that blood that stains the wall...?

The path curves into an L-shape. A doorway is set into the wall, from which dim light streams. Through the door a passage leads deeper into the caves, where light from the outside cannot reach and additional means of illumination are necessary.

A flat, narrow wooden bridge connects the twisting path to the northwest and the tiny landing to the east. Below the bridge is a deep crevice, which appears bottomless in the poor lighting. The bridge itself shows visible signs of warping. How much longer will it hold up?

The view east is obstructed by a group of stalagmites rising from the ground like stone sunflowers. A set of stairs appears to lead up, and air, faintly fresh-smelling, comes from above. To the left of the stairs is a ramp that leads to a higher level of the current floor.

The passage here is sufficiently wide to accommodate several people at once. This is in part due to the large nooks and crannies set into the wall, most likely from natural means. There are no lights in the immediate vicinity; the end result is a subdued darkness that makes the crannies hollow cheeks in a rock face.

A huge cave-in marks where the entrance closest to Figaro Castle once was.  There is a thin layer of dying grass along the ground, and a light breeze weakly causes it to sway to and fro.  A pair of torches on the east and west walls provide a faint source of light.  The only way out is back through the northern path.

The path forks at a ninety degree angle, branching out to the south and southwest. Long, dark cracks on the ceiling make the overhead area appear a giant spiderweb. A fine powder of pulverized rock covers the floor; it contains faint footprints of both men and beasts who have passed through before.

The cave's upper catwalk ends in a mini-cliff to the north. A rock wall lies beneath the cliff, cutting off access to the lower path. The walkway continues to the southwest, or ends in a ramp to the south. Fine sand covers the ground, yet there are no tracks in it, as though no creature has dared to explore the upper ledge of the cave.

The widest passage ends abruptly at a tall rock pile. Some eight feet above is another pathway, which ends in a jutting precipice. The upper path at one time collapsed near its end, resulting in this heap of rocks. The arch towers above all, a silent and unseeing witness.

The long, straight north-south corridor is considerably better lit than the surrounding areas, thanks to the lights hanging at regular intervals. Small rocks litter the ground. Some sort of crystals are embedded in the walls. Are they of any value?

The narrow path ends at a rock wall that stretches to the ceiling. The walls are very irregular, with large rocks sticking out at irregular places at head, chest, and knee level. It is extremely difficult to navigate around the rock protrusions. Propped against the wall is a chest.

A small amount of natural light illuminates the area between two identical staircases leading down. The eastern stairway appears to lead back into the main level of the caves, while even more light floods the stairway to the west. The pathway is a semi-circle shaped in a giant frown. No artificial lights hang on the walls, for with the sunlight that filters from the western stairs, additional lighting is unnecessary.

To the east of the bridge is a tiny platform made of stone. It has room for half a dozen people to stand on it at once, if they all crunch themselves together. An empty chest lies against one of the walls, its open lid yawning. There is also something different about that wall, but it's not quite obvious what it is.

Three paths converge into a T. The easterly path tapers off to a narrow walkway through blocky, parallel rock walls. North is an elongated, reasonably well-lit passage, and to the west the path snakes around an outcropping and disappears. Perhaps the cave has secrets to hide down one of the paths.

rooms.name: Caves to South Figaro, south entrance

userData.LongDescription: A huge rock womb marks South Figaro's entrance to the cave.  A light breeze blows dust and pollen through the outside opening, and sunlight floods in.  Oddly, the influence of the outside makes the cavernous area appear to be a stone ballroom.  A flight of stairs leads into the cave, which is cut inside the mountain.

rooms.name: Jidoor Continent - Outside The Opera House

userData.LongDescription: In the midst of the bleakness of Kefka's effects, one structure has managed to withstand the Light of Judgment.  The world famous Opera House is here, a warm and inviting structure.  The surrounding environs have been swept clean of corpses and skeletons, as they are not very befitting of a place of artistry.

The city of Zozo is a dark, damp, rotten place, with a matching populace.  Founded by thieves outcast from Jidoor to the south, the place is festering with criminals of all types.  The city is built into the side of a cliff, and it casts a dark shadow over the whole area.

Extravagant buildings can be seen in every direction, with the closest being the Katana shop. The city entrance seems to be well maintained, with a sign set nearby to welcome visitors. The main square of Lower Jidoor and the rest of the city lie to the east. A large mansion can be glimpsed to the far north on its own elevation, its gigantic size in comparison to the other buildings an indication of the wealth of its owner.

Between the buildings of this shopping center in the lower area of Jidoor, a large public garden blooms, its flowers and greenery providing a bright and cheerful contrast to the desolate world beyond the town limits. A stone sidewalk surrounds the garden. The plants here are all neatly trimmed, and the whole area seems expertly maintained.

This is the far end of the second row of the Auction House, since it is in the middle, there are alot of people using it. The lighting is really bad here, a person couldn't see to the tip of his/her nose here it's so dark. As for what a person might see, it would be a big headed fool sitting in front of him/her in row 1. Far to the east is the beginning of Aisle 2.

Brightly colored flowers adorn the sides of the walkway, sharing the space with some carefully cultivated  shrubs and grass. A small wooden fense separates the cobblestone road from the plants to prevent them from being disturbed by the feet of travelers. The road continues north towards the Auction House, and to the south lies the weapon shop and a stairwell to the lower tier.

The second aisle seems to have been filled up quite well. There are many people sitting here and bidding on stuff. The podium is a little farther north. The lighting in this aisle seems to be different from the first aisle, since the overhead lights here are tinted blue. Whoever remade the building sure put a lot of money into it to make it look fancy.

With all the people in the first row, there seems to be no sitting spots anymore. The lighting in this row is nicely done, since there is a soft blacklight thrumming above the row. Most of the people in this part of the row are salesmen, looking for a good price on some rare items that pop up every once in awhile. The podium is back to the east, and there is someone making a bid on the current item up now. To the east is the first aisle, and to the west is more of row one.

This is the middle of the first row. It seems rather empty and is at the back of Auction House. There is a person auctioning off something at the podium, but there doesn't seem to be any bids as of yet. To the distant east is the entrance to the Auction House and to the west is the last row.

Rows of thickly reinforced glass cases line the walls of the shop, enclosing armaments of various kinds within their transparent surfaces. High above them, a few of the cheaper weapons are hung on pegs, with a set of ladders nearby allowing easy access to them. The shopkeeper stands behind the cases, and a sign is set on the wall next to him.

The first row seems to be rather empty, since it is near the back of the Auction House. Most of the seats seem brand new and haven't been used yet. the place must've been rebuilt since the ruin that Kefka made last year. To the east are the doors of the Auction House and to the west is more of row 1.

rooms.name: Upper Jidoor - Outside the relic shop

userData.LongDescription: A small shop resides at the western edge of the upper city. The upper side of its thick, hardwood door sports a panel of transparent glass, through which one would be able to see the merchandise. A sign is set against the door, on which  the words 'relic shop' are written in bold letters.

The balcony affords an excellent view over most of the lower city. Gold plated balustrades support the structure, inlaid with large decorative gemstones at regular intervals. A set of stone stairs can be used to get to the lower city, and the rest of the upper tier lies to the east.

The slightly muffled sounds of chatter and clinking glasses echo from the inn, and the smell of food, alcohol and a weird floral scent occasionally drift through the area as the doors are opened by people going in or out. To the east lies the bustling main road of the lower city, which still looks pristine despite it being frequently traversed.

Rows of glass cases are set near the walls of the relic shop, thickly reinforced to protect the merchandize within while remaining transparent. A wooden counter lies behind them, manned by an older gentleman, and a sign is set against it. A painting is framed near the door out of the shop.

Sprawling from wall to wall, a long wooden counter and marigold carpet, with a vivid floral pattern, span the entire length of the inn's reception. Large potted plants are placed throughout and fill the room with a floral aroma, which mixes strangely with the smells of food and drink being served and taken by patrons.  Set in front of the door leading towards the rooms, a small table with a visitor's log and a bottle-glass lantern sit against the wall, complete with a padded chair. A small sign sits at the very end of the counter.

This is the far end of the first row of the Auction House, since it is near the back, you can't hear what the announcer is saying up at the podium. The place was rebuilt after Kefka destroyed it almost a year ago. Far to the east is the entrance to the Auction House.
A citizen of Jidoor strolls haughtily.

Beautiful katanas are displayed in glass cases in this richly furnished shop, their tops forming a counter behind which stands the young shopkeeper. A sign is set on the wall near the counter, and a painting is framed next to it, depicting a line of swordsmen in combat.

Various sets of armor are displayed throughout the shop, some hung on walls and others placed on racks. A counter is set against the northern wall, and a wooden sign is set next to it. The hardwood door leading out of the shop bears no decorations on this side.

rooms.name: Upper Jidoor - Outside the Auction House

userData.LongDescription: Large and imposing, the Auction House takes up most of the eastern part of the upper city. A few evergreen trees to the west of the structure lends it an even more beautiful cast, and a huge set of double doors lead into the building proper. The main intersection of the upper plaza is past the trees to the west.

This is the middle section of the second row. There seem to be alot of people who are sitting here, so there are no seats available. The lighting in this particular section is excellent. The auctioneer is standing at the podium, announcing another rare item. To the east is part of this row, while to the west is the western end of row two.

This is the chocobo rental shop, WARK!  There are some chocobos in the stables in the back, dancing back and forth in anticipation of the next ride.  Straw is littered liberally across the floor, even extending into the street.  Paintings of chocobos hang behind the counter where the owner is.

rooms.name: Upper Jidoor - outside the weapon shop

userData.LongDescription: A rather spacious shop lies nearby, with small windows that allow one to view the merchandize within. A simple wooden door is the only means of entry to the shop, its surface painted with the picture of two crossed swords. Lower Jidoor can be accessed from the stairwell nearby, the balcony is to the west, and a nice little walkway lies to the north.

Evergreen trees and other shrubs are planted to the north and east of the upper city square, providing a nice contrast to the humongous buildings that also lie in those directions. The enormous shadow of Owzer's mansion, located on the hill to the north, looks almost as if it was trying to hide behind the trees nearby but to no avail. The entrance of the Auction House is to the east, and a smaller fork leads west, ending outside of a small shop of some kind. The stone stairwell nearby leads to the lower city.

Armors and combat gear of all varieties can be seen through the window of the shop, catering to a myriad of fighting styles. An ornately decorated hardwood door provides entry to the shop proper, its surface painted with depictions of armored figures in various poses. A stairwell is nearby, leading towards the upper level.

This is the first aisle of the Auction House. It is fairly busy here, and many people are filling up the row, getting ready to auction on rare and great items.  The place is very fancy, and the light is a pale blue shimmer, giving the row a mystical look. One can go south to more rows, or west, to go further down this row.  North will take you to the bidding room.

The mansion is gigantic up close, and it seems that someone is inside, because there are shadows to be seen moving around in the windows on the first floor of the mansion. The mansion is painted in a dark grey color, and seems to be nearly four stories high and six stories wide. There are two guards standing at the doorway to the mansion, they seem to be making sure that the mansion isn't entered from this entrance. The doors to the mansion lie to the north, and back south is the upper plaza.

This is the middle section of the first row. There seems to be no seats available here, since more of the citizens of Jidoor have taken them, getting ready for the auction. The light here is shimmering, and provides an all-around good mood to the area. To the east is part of this row, while to the west is the end of row one.

This is the Bidding Room of the Auction House.  The Auctioneer stands on his podium in the front of the room, looming over the amassed people here.  He holds auctions every hour, one minute past the hour.  To find out how to bid, read the sign next to the podium.  South is the first aisle of the Auction House.

The many roads of the lower city all intersect at the main square, forming a bustling hub. There is a barn of some kind to the east, sporting a large sign with a bird painted on it. An ostentatious stone  stairwell lies in that direction as well, leading to the upper level of Jidoor. The city entrance is to the west, and to the north lies an archway which leads directly below a balcony on the upper level.

The second row seems to be rather cluttered, since a lot of people seem to be sitting here making bids on objects for sale. There are some seats available, but they probably won't be for long. Above, the lights seem to be colored differently than the ones in aisle one. To the east is the aisle, and to the west is more of this row.

The distinctive warks and scents of a chocobo rental waft from the barnlike shop nearby. A stairwell leads to the second level of Jidoor, and a very large building can be glimpsed on the eastern side. The main square of Lower Jidoor lies to the west.

This is the far end of the first row of the Auction House. There is alot of noise coming from this section and it seems to be from people who are making outrageous bids on some of the items displayed in the Auctioneers Hall. The lighting here is extremely poor here. There seem to be alot of seats, but most of them are filled. Far to the east is the beginning of Aisle one.

The Auction House seems to be packed with citizens of Jidoor. There seems to be some commotion ahead, but it's hard to tell if there is an auction going on right now without getting closer to the front of the room. To the north, there is a stand to display items for sale. There are four rows of seats lined from the stand back to the entrance. The doors out of the Auction house are here and will take you back to the Upper Plaza.

The red carpet covering the stairs is more of an ugly brown due to mud and rainwater being tracked across it and never being cleaned up.  A bucket sits in the middle of the room, positioned to catch water that drips from a leak in the ceiling.  A faded bronze sign with a chocobo head painted onto it is the only decoration.

rooms.name: Inside the west half of Zozo Tower

userData.LongDescription: The walls on this story are slimy to the touch, as if the rain has gotten inside and caused mildew.  In fact, the rain is getting inside.  The dark clouds can be seen through large cracks in the ceiling.  The floor here is noticeably slanted, something underneath having partially collapsed.  The building groans as if it is struggling to stay upright.

The road is haphazardly laid throughout Zozo, but this section takes the cake.  A huge slab of stone meant to be flat on the ground has somehow become jutted two meters into the air.  A barbed wire fence to the south blocks off several buildings, with a sign that clearly indicates that the owners do not want trespassers.

This entire floor of the tower is devoted to one huge stairway, as are the next three.  For perhaps a hundred feet up, stairs climb back and forth across the tower, from wall to wall, lit only by a few poorly spaced oil lamps and what little sunlight pushes through the rainclouds to the windows.

Catwalks and metal stairs continue to lead towards the top of the tower, forcing any who would climb to once again get soaked by the rain.  The stairs, though full of dents from the ongoing storm, are holding on well enough to be mostly usable.  The ground, far below, would be quite a drop for anything that fell.

Overhead to the north, a bridge hangs, connecting two sections of Mt. Zozo.  The creaking from the bridge melds with that of the tall building to the south, making the whole city seem unstable.  An overturned dumpster reeks in a most wretched fashion, full of trash that has long since rotted.

This must have been the location of some shop or another at some point, because a counter is set up to keep people from coming to this back area from the rest of the room and a few empty jars are left sitting under it.  A sign on the wall behind the counter is too broken for anyone to be able to tell what it used to say.  Stairs lead back down.

An enormous building to the west must be at least ten stories tall, nearly reaching to the top of the mountain.  The rains pours down all around, the large structure offering no shield from the storm.  The building towers over the city, threatening to fall on it.  Its entrance is to the south.

The rain attacks from all directions, piercing even the most sheltered and secluded spaces.  This narrow road sinks between two barriers: to the east, a mountain rises up; to the west, a skyscraper.  Sunlight does not reach this place, and no lamps are set up to light this path.

A tattered, wet, filthy rug covers the floor near the doorway, inviting guests to come in so that they can be mugged by the residents.  Some broken pots line the edges of the room, and a counter separates one corner of the room as if this were once meant to be a store.  The broken frame of a cuckoo clock hangs on the back wall.

Though the rest of the tower, and in fact the rest of the city, is in a total state of ruin, this top floor has somehow been kept in order.  Though in poor shape compared to any other city, the fact that the walls were recently painted and are not crumbling at all is incredible for Zozo.  A sturdy door leads in.  With no elevator, the only way down is the long chain of stairways to the ground below.

This room, less than eight feet by eight feet in size, is literally built into a cave.  The ceiling is completely natural, but walls and a floor have been built over the rest of the rock surface.  This room must have been used for something unique once, but it is now abandoned.  Astonishingly, the rain is in full force inside this room.

A run-down building seems to lead up into the side of the mountain.  The building's entrance has a sign labelling it a cafe, but it does not look like the kind of place that would serve travellers drinks.  An overturned trash can near the building contains what appears to be someone's unfortunate victim... or part of him.

Rain pours down relentlessly on this city, failing to wash away its evils.  The constant storms have caused much of this city to decay, leaving broken debris strewn across many of the roads, and not a soul seems interested in the city's well-being enough to so much as sweep it aside.

This road continues westward to a huge tower, the largest building in Zozo.  The building must be at least ten stories tall, if not taller, and does not look like the sort of place that would have a working elevator.  Boxes and crates are piled along the ground, a shipment that never made it to its destination.

rooms.name: Scaling the west half of Zozo Tower
