userData.LongDescription: The drab, gray exterior of the ruined tower lends it a depressing look, as if simply being in the city of Zozo weren't bad enough on its own.  A set of rickety metal stairs leads up to the highest floor of this side of the skyscraper, though with the tower slightly leaning as it is, the steps are slanted, wet, and dangerously steep.  A man can be seen jumping back and forth between buildings in the rain.

The main road of Zozo comes to an abrupt end as it leads directly into the side of the mountain.  What looks like it might have once been a passage leads southwest, but someone has set up quite a roadblock, making this a dead end.  A building half-inside the cliff seems to be in fair shape, structurally.

rooms.name: A catwalk connecting to Mt. Zozo

userData.LongDescription: A sort of makeshift wall hides the side of the mountain, but any but the least observant could see through the concealment, considering the wall stops about two feet past the end of the catwalk.  Past that, the mountainside can be seen to be right behind the wall.  Two doors lead into what must be caves, one door clearly labelled "Mt. Zozo."

The roof of almost every other building in Zozo can be seen from this height, and unsurprisingly, the vast majority of them are filled with holes.  The dismal rain continues to beat down upon the tower, slowly eroding the structure.  A door leads inside, away from the harsh weather.  On the outside of the tower further up, no catwalks are visible for several floors.

A cliff, the base of Mt. Zozo, creates a steep incline to the north.  Part of a building, hanging two stories above the ground, is built into the the side of the cliff, and would almost create a shield from the downpour were there no wind and no leaks in the building's structure.  The entrance to the building is to the southwest.

There may have once been a way to get from this floor to the one above it, but what looks like it should have been the path is now a crumbled gap in the terrace, and a large pillar is leaning out of the wall in the same place.  There's no way to continue upward, though a small door leads into a small haven from the unending downpour.

Though it's the correct amount of height for one floor, there's nothing at this level except a small landing.  Stairs go up one more floor, or down two more floors.  Though the tower is structurally in better shape closer to the top, there is a different kind of neglect, as if this section is rarely used.

Amidst rain falling down, Mt. Zozo is visible from here, and it's possible to locate several of the bridges that connect cave exits and entrances.  The dark, dreary sky does little to lighten the mood, but the top of the tower is close.  Metal stairs continue up or down, and a wooden door leads away from the perpetual storm.

Just through an open door, stairs lead down into the first floor.  There doesn't seem to actually be anything inside the building on this floor, and metal stairs attached to the outside of the building continue upward.  Rain beats against the side of the building, creating a rather miserable atmosphere.

It is astonishing that this building is still upright.  Even from the road, it is clear that broken supports, flimsy stairs, rusted ladders, and shattered windows far outnumber their non-neglected cousins.  Much of the required climbing to reach the top looks to have to be done on the outside of the tower, adding to the unsafety.  If the place were going to collapse, it probably would have done so already, but it is certainly not the sort of place someone afraid of heights would want to go.

rooms.name: Inside the west half of Zozo Tower

userData.LongDescription: Even though numerous beams and planks connected to the walls and ceiling seem to have been put in place to hold things together, this hallway feels like it is sinking.  In a place like this, it's less likely to be an illusion caused by the height, and more likely to actually be sinking.  A set of stairs near the end of the hallway is partially obscured by walls that were probably not that close together when they were first built.  Through a small door to the west, a second set of stairs leads up as well.

A small closet used to be all this room was, but either a curious person or a lack of attention has made one of the walls collapse, revealing a slightly larger room full of dozens of makeshift supports and planks that are probably the only thing keeping the top floor from falling down into this one.  Dust that had built up has turned to mud since, due to rain leaking through the door.

rooms.name: Inside the west half of Zozo Tower

userData.LongDescription: The structure creaks and moans audibly at this height, as if it is ready to topple over any second now.  A damaged doorway leads out into the rain.  An abandoned shop of some sort has been left here, long pillaged.  It appears to have been abandoned for quite some time, but then again, weather like this can make anything look deteriorated in just days.

An ornate blue and yellow throw rug occupies the center of the room at the top of the stairs.  A long staircase zigzags down for quite a ways before landing on the eighth floor.  The bottom must be a hundred feet down, and the stairs are wet and slippery.  A door leads outside to the catwalks.

A counter in one corner, judging from the sign above it, was being used for a while by some crook to charge entrance fees to the tower.  The station is currently being manned by a large blood stain.  Stairs lead up to a exit to a catwalk, the only way to go up any further.  A door back out to the street shakes in the wind.

A row of lamps lines the wall, but unsurprisingly, every last one of them is cracked and inoperable.  Some thoughtful person apparently must have laid a carpet on the floor some time in the past.  At present, there is a series of lumps under it in one corner resembling a person's limbs, torso, and head.  The lumps are not connected to one-another.

A mildew-covered building with a sign stolen from an inn is in serious disrepair, looking ready to collapse any minute.  The front window is shattered into pieces, but there is no glass on the ground, suggesting that it has been broken for quite some time.  An opening on the second floor is boarded up.

The never-ending rain from outside penetrates the gap in the broken door, soaking most of the floor near the entrance.  This cafe has no bartender, nor any sort of drink collection, making it less of a cafe and more of a brawl room.  Broken bottles and overturned stools are strewn about, making quite a mess of the place.

A thin strip of flooring connects the window used for tower-leaping to some rickety steps leading upward.  The pouring rain runs down the stairs and off the edges to the ground far below.  No stairs lead downward, and the only way to get to the bottom of the tower is to jump across to the other side first.

The stairwell changes direction back towards the other wall in order to fit within the confines of the walls.  In fact, it changes direction again another floor up, being just too tall to fit nicely inside.  There is a worn carpet on the stairs to aid with traction, but the rain coming in through the windows is making it almost as slippery as the stone floor.

This corridor, maybe thirty meters long and barely wide enough for one person, is extremely cramped for space.  The worst part, though, is that the walls on both sides are cracked and falling apart, sliding in further and further as the months go by.  There are no doors to whatever space might be on the other sides of those walls, but then, there are entire floors of this tower that don't seem to have any way of being accessed.

rooms.name: A tiny room inside Zozo Tower

userData.LongDescription: The space in this room is barely enough to lie down in.  An open, empty chest is in the middle of the room, and even the lock has been stolen from it.  The walls of the room are set up in a strange triangular shape, as if this were meant to be a small shrine.  It's not currently being used as anything of the sort.

Looking at the evil city of Zozo from this balcony, it is obvious how the city got that title.  Every building in sight is either run-down and abandoned or outright collapsed, with the exception of a large tower.  Directly below, the road, if it can be called such, can be seen in all its potholed, muddy, unfinished glory.

Two extraneous walls jut out from the side of the room, coming almost halfway across the room and then stopping, dividing the room into three sections.  The resulting sections have very little light, even with the opening to the balcony nearby.  A leak in the ceiling drips down directly into a crack in the floor by some strange chance, letting water leak down to the next floor.

A desk and office are taking up half of the area of this room.  An old man sits behind the desk, sorting through paperwork and waiting for patrons, and apparently is not in fear of being attacked.  Signs on the front of the desk give a clue as to why: this is the office of welfare, and he is the city's only source of actual money.  Mounted on the back wall are his government-granted defenses, which look like they should be mounted on a tank.

This building is no bigger than a large bedroom, but that may be partly a result of a portion of it having collapsed.  A good number of signs line the walls, stolen from everything from chocobo stables to garden sheds, many shattered from pieces of the walls or ceiling falling on them.  The walls of this place are slanted, though clearly not on purpose, and might fall over if someone leaned on them too hard.

rooms.name: The room at the top of Zozo Tower

userData.LongDescription: A single wooden chair sits facing an empty bed.  The carpet right in front of the chair is faded, as if that spot were suddenly exposed to a very bright light.  The triangular shape of the room is peculiar, but whatever purpose it might have served is forgotten.  This could almost be called a throne room, but for the lack of a throne.  There is a sense of significance in this room, but distant, as though it were something lost to faded memories.

rooms.name: A room with a huge clock

userData.LongDescription: A giant clock dominates the room, standing six feet high.  The ticking is loud and incessant.  The face of the clock, notably, has both analog and digital time displays, though they do not match.  Little else is in this room, though the lack of rain dripping through the ceiling is notable.

rooms.name: Scaling the west half of Zozo Tower

userData.LongDescription: Back to the east is the main section of the skyscraper, past a small sub-tower barely the size of a small room.  The smaller tower stands between the two halves of the skyscraper, and almost looks like it is there solely for the purpose of helping people jump across.  An open doorway leads inside, not to be inviting, but because the door has been ripped off by the wind and rain.

The building to the north is literally sagging under its own weight.  The entire structure is lopsided, and there is a pile of bricks where part of the outer wall used to be.  Several large girders are being used to prop the place up, but even so, were it not built into the side of the mountain, it would probably have collapsed into a pile of rubble by now.  Several crates sit outside the building.

Rain somehow blows in through the door leading out to the catwalk, even despite the fact that the door is closed.  A pair of signs hanging on the wall seem to be labelling a large stain on the wall as an item and armor shop.  Apparently stealing shop signs and hanging them in odd places is all the rage these days.

A small overhang attempts to shield this balcony from the storm.  Alas, it is in vain, for even the bottom side of the overhang is somehow being drenched by the rain.  Three different kinds of rain can be felt all attacking at once: a sharp diagonal sting, a gravity-defying torrent, and a heavy blatter.  All in all, a rather terrible mix.  A single weathered door leads into the skyscraper's relative shelter.

The large skyscraper to the south creaks and moans from the attack of the storm on its weathered supports. A part of the tower near the top extends past the base, precariously hanging over the dirt road, shaking and rattling in the fierce wind.

rooms.name: Scaling the west half of Zozo Tower

userData.LongDescription: There appears to be nothing of interest on this floor, which is the top floor of the west section of the building.  The roof and most of the walls of this floor have caved in, leaving it totally unusable.  A portion of the structure is still erect, and it is possible to jump from a window to the other tower, which continues upward.

The skyscraper seems to have split, and two other, smaller towers can be seen to the west, although there is no visible way to properly access them.  A popular way to improperly access them seems to be to leap between them, from one window to another.  A small closet that opens to the outside, big enough for one person to stand in, has had both its door and window permanently opened for just such a purpose.  Some thoughtful person has even left detailed instructions pinned to the windowsill.

rooms.name: The room at the top of Zozo Tower

userData.LongDescription: A long, beautiful, decidedly out-of-place carpet rests on the path down through the center of the room.  Somehow it is kept clean, though it's admittedly a bit wet and torn around the edges.  Symmetrical walls and columns line the sides of the room, though one of the columns has broken and fallen over onto the floor.  The end of the hall opens into a final room, and the arrangement of this room suggests that it is leading up to something meaningful, but the state of neglect implies otherwise.

The downpour continues.  In the middle of the street lies a dead woman; likely a visitor to the town, judging from her clothing.  The weather in Zozo is constantly dark and miserable, and both the architecture and the moods of the citizens seem to be affected by it.  The mountain and the tower block the light from reaching this road, but somehow not the rain.

rooms.name: A catwalk connecting to Mt. Zozo

userData.LongDescription: This ledge, kind of a balcony next to the cafe, is actually built onto the mountain.  The mountainside has been concealed by construction that makes it look like the outside of a building, but any room inside such a building would have to be less than a foot thick, and gaps between the boards allow the rock surface to be seen in places.  Why the wall was constructed is anybody's guess.

Rolling fields of emerald grass spread out over a flat landscape, interrupted only by a single farm house and a large barn. It is pretty quiet, with a fenced-off area in front of the barn, though every so often the chirps and warks of a chocobo may be heard.

Barren soil spreads throughout the area, giving a dull grey appearance to anyone passing through. Years of depleting the nutrients and spirit of the planet take their toll, leaving a bleak landscape. The only signs of life outside the massive metal walls barricading the city of Midgar are small rodents scurrying around, and disappearing into their burrows.

Barren soil spreads throughout the area, giving a dull grey appearance to anyone passing through. Years of depleting the nutrients and spirit of the planet take their toll, leaving a bleak landscape. The only signs of life outside the massive metal walls barricading the city of Midgar are small rodents scurrying around, and disappearing into their burrows.

Barren soil spreads throughout the area, giving a dull grey appearance to anyone passing through. Years of depleting the nutrients and spirit of the planet take their toll, leaving a bleak landscape. The only signs of life outside the massive metal walls barricading the city of Midgar are small rodents scurrying around, and disappearing into their burrows.

Emerald grass grows out over the hills and plains. A gentle wind breezes through, making the appearence of waves flowing through the endless blades.  Perked ears, and a wriggling nose of a rabbit can be seen before it hops off into the fields.  Kalm can be entered here.

Barren soil spreads throughout the area, giving a dull grey appearance to anyone passing through. Years of depleting the nutrients and spirit of the planet take their toll, leaving a bleak landscape. The only signs of life outside the massive metal walls barricading the city of Midgar are small rodents scurrying around, and disappearing into their burrows.

rooms.name: In front of the Mythril Mines

userData.LongDescription: This marks the entrance to the Mythril mines. The cave entrance stands high to the south, like one single impressive mound ready to swallow careless travelers in its darkness. Mountains surrounding the entrance, with their great height, obscure the area in an eerie dark light.

A large room filled with various instruments and controls fill the area, with engineers at their respective consoles. At the front, a large panoramic window spreads, giving a nearly 180 degree viewing radius. The hum of engines can be heard as the Highwind floats in place. The full-fledged pilot stands at the helm, awaiting to take any adventurers to the various realms on the planet of Final Fantasy 7. A white arrow leads out of the room, to the other areas of the airship.

Metal decking and supports surround the area, making for a fairly large room. The hums of engines and turbines are quite noticeable, seeming to come from all around the airship. A small bridge leads to the cockpit, where a pilot will take anyone where they want. A set of stairs leads up to the outside deck, for anyone needing a bit of fresh air.

A long stretch of metal and wood make the outside deck of the Highwind. Anyone can see for miles around if it's a clear enough day. A constant breeze sweeps through, with higher gusts coming from the engines, and turbines humming loudly all around. A small door leads back down into the main area of the airship.

A long stretch of metal and wood make the outside deck of the Highwind. Anyone can see for miles around if it's a clear enough day. A constant breeze sweeps through, with higher gusts coming from the engines and turbines humming loudly all around. A small door leads back down into the main area of the airship.

A fence extends a long way around a large field in the Chocobo Ranch. The area is very flat, giving a clear view of the entire field. Grass covers the majority of the area, though there is the occasional small dirt mound. The gate here leads back to the rest of the ranch.

A small ranch for chocobos stands surrounded by beautiful fields of grass and a few trees.  There is a chocobo barn and a small house.  Between the house and the barn stands a tall silo made of sturdy gray stone and a ladder reaching to its domed roof. Beside the silo is a traditional well.  The sunlight is strong, and shines off the roofs of the buildings.  Above the barn's opening is a trademark painting of a yellow chocobo.

A red brick fireplace sets the mood for the room, which seems to be a combination kitchen and dining room.  Along a wall is a gas stove with various cooking items scattered around its counter.  Opposite to the wall with a stove is an opened window that lets in a gentle breeze and light that shines down on the dining table.  There is also a door on the same wall as the house's entrance.

This side of the barn contains six chocobo stables.  Each stable has been allocated troughs and buckets.  Ranching tools that have been worn down stand against the wall beneath two large windows that adorn the wall that stands where the walkway ends.

The fence is long and surrounds quite a bit of space.  Inside the chocobo pen there are many chocobo tracks seen in the moist patches of ground. A breeze permeates the area, and a tall tree in the corner of the pen has made a shadow that overlaps the green grass and ground.

The entrance allows a large view of the whole barn.  The barn has a main path that ends far on the other end of the barn, with several chocobo stables on both sides of the walkway.  Four stables have been built next to the barn's double doors, and after these first four stables is a small section on each side for storage.

This room is rather tidy and is equipped with three sturdy beds that are placed in a row.  To help illuminate the room, two windows are posted in the middle of the room, opposite of each other.  Another window opposite of the entrance stands above the farthest bed, but is closed and dull of light.  Close to the entrance is a polished corner table that is tightly tucked in its shaded corner and littered with small knickknacks.

This is the upstairs bedroom in the large house. There is a huge neatly made bed, and it's obvious that whoever sleeps in it must be very large. A large amount of laundry has been laid out on the bed to be put away later, and the balcony windows are open, allowing a cool breeze into the bedroom.

At the base of the mountains is a small, quaint cabin. It looks inviting enough, though it stands alone in the wilderness. There is a sign out in front of it as well. There is a small cluster of mountains to the north, and you can make out a cave in the side of one of the mountains.

The mystics of Medina have built a shop and sell weapons and armor. Despite a large sign banning all humans from entry, it seems that the minimum-wage clerk is quite laid back and will sell his wares to anyone with money.

This is the Medina town square. Surrounding the raised square platform are four huge cement walls, and the only exit is a gate to the south. The center of attention here is apparently a huge statue in the center of the square. A device connected to some speakers is playing bizarre music consisting of monsters singing some strange chant.

This is a large home in Medina village, with traditional mystic furniture, and enough room for servants. The house has a full kitchen. and something seems to be cooking on the stove. A staircase leads up to a second floor.

This is the cabin home of someone who apparently is a master of blacksmithing, and possibly more arcane arts.  Masterwork weapons hang on the wall, and several unfinished blacksmithing projects are on the table or in barrels along the wall.  A paper blueprint on the table shows strange magic glyphs in an ancient language.  The owner's personal living necessities seem to have been taken over by the needs of his projects.

This is the northeastern part of Medina Village, the village of mystics. There is a large square to the south, but it's impossible to see into it from this angle due to the huge cement walls that surround it. The buildings in this town look very much like human buildings, despite being lived in by imps and demons. To the northeast, a path leads into the forest towards a glowing blue pyramid.

Along the outskirts of Medina Village, the grassy road passes between a row of buildings and the central plaza that dominates the village. It's impossible to tell what might be going on in there, as the view from this angle is blocked by the high cement walls, which are unpainted and undecorated. Just flat, brutal cement forming a barrier between civilization and whatever lies within.

This is the center of Medina village, and stone steps lead up to the gates that head in to the huge town square, a glaring and almost brutal sight compared to the rest of the village. The square is strange and creepy, as some strange chanting noises are coming from inside its cement walls.

This is a small house which seems relatively mundane, except for the swirling blue time portal in the cupboard, ripping a hole through the fabric of reality. Fortunately, closing the cupboard seems to stop the noise. The house consists of a single room, and the front door is wide open. There are two beds here and all the kitchen things that one might expect.

This wilderness path stretches between Medina Village, to the east, and a small cluster of mountains to the west. Medina is just a dot on the horizon from this distance - only the fact that it stands on top of a hill makes the cement structure in its center still visible.
This area is nothing but a field of stars, slowly moving across the sky.

This is a small trail that leads to the southwest of Medina. There's a road leading out of town up to a certain point, and then the path continues along the grasslands. From atop a hill, the ocean can be seen to the south, beyond some grasslands.

This is a wilderness path a fair distance southwest of Medina Village, at a point where the coastline to the north is changing directions, curving westward as the road leads away from Medina. To the north and south, all that's visible is ocean, but to the west is a small cabin at the base of a group of mountains.

This is Medina Village, the village of mystics, although one could be forgiven for mistaking it for a human town at a glance from afar. The buildings here seem to have been either built by humans, or modeled very closely off of human structures. A row of houses lines the outer edges of the village, but the far more unusual sight is the large cement square structure to the east, in the village center.

This is the eastern part of the largest house in Medina Village, home to the village elder. Covering a huge dining table is a mountain of food, consisting mostly of meat, but with a small amount of fresh fruit and a few other delicacies. The furniture is a mixture of modern conveniences and ornamental relics, which appear to be from primitive and medieval mystic cultures.

This trail leading through the woods, away from Medina Village, is relatively short and well-lit by tiki torches along the sides of the path. To the north, the trail leads to a glowing blue energy pyramid. Some of the trees along the trail seem to have been cut down to make pilgrimages from Medina to the mysterious pyramid easier.

This site is clearly some incredibly ancient ruin. A crumbled base is all that remains of what was once apparently a stone building, moldy gray stone bricks pieced together on the ground. At the four corners of the perfectly square base of whatever this structure once was, four glowing magical orbs are set into the floor, and glowing barriers of blue energy are being emitted from them, encasing the stone floor in an energy pyramid. The area around the energy pyramid is all natural forest, having grown up around the ruins.

At the four corners of the perfectly square base of whatever this structure once was, four glowing magical orbs are set into the floor, and glowing barriers of blue energy are being emitted from them, encasing the stone floor in an energy pyramid. The area around the energy pyramid is all natural forest, having grown up around the ruins.

A door is built into the face of a small cliff on the edge of the village. It appears as though some creature may have made a dwelling in a cave. There are no windows and it's impossible to tell what lies beyond the door.

A faintly defined trail through the hills leads from the south towards the base of one of the mountains, and stops at the mouth of a large cave. Strange noises come from within, and a cold draft comes from the cave. The path heads south as well, in the general direction of a small cabin.

Directly to the north you can see the large machine that is known as Gato. He was built to test the strengths and weaknesses of people, and also as a way for people to practice their combating skills. The path also heads southeast towards Leene's Bell.

Between two merchant booths stocked with wares for sale, the race track is visible, with racers lounging about and boasting instead of actually racing.  Still, the air is filled with happy chatter, the festival atmosphere obvious to all.
This is a dusty race track that runs through the fair.

You stand before a large, and strange device. There are two pods on either side of it.  In the center, between both of the pods, a strange blue orb can be seen. It is a time gate, that was formed due to a malfunction in this machine. To the south you can see a large bell hanging from an archway.
This is a dusty race track that runs through the fair.

rooms.name: The stairs, east of Leene's Bell

userData.LongDescription: White stone stairs lead down to a path to a side area. The path curves north, and leads to what looks like a concert by a prehistoric band. Even from where you stand, you can hear them beating their drums and hollering up a storm. To the west is Leene's bell, which hangs from a large arch in the center of the area.

This is a stone pathway near Leene's Bell, leading from the center of the fairgrounds to a side show area. Stairs lead down and to the west past some tables, where another one of Lucca's inventions appears to be on display.
You step from the tranquility of the path, into the hectic, chaotic mess that is the fair. Balloons float everywhere, dancers spin, and various objects are thrown into the air by jugglers.

rooms.name: Road to the Rock Age Band

userData.LongDescription: People crowd around you trying to get into where the band is playing.  You can see some tables and people dancing to the east, while to the south there is a little girl crying..and a man guzzling soda pop.

The fragrance of chocolate and sweets fills the air as people walk by a rather extravagant candy shoppe. Available for purchase are great sugary delights. The man at the counter waves at potential customers and invites them over to look at his wares.

You stare at the device. It is a very odd thing, standing at six feet,and it is 5 feet in width. On the top and the bottom, are two hollow metallic cylinders with bright lightbulbs that switch through six different colours. It doesn't look very efficient, and since Lucca built it, you'd better keep your distance, lest it blow up on you.
You have reached the room of Gato.  You wonder how tough the sack of scrap metal will be, and because Lucca's inventions always blow up, if it will even work.
This is a dusty race track that runs through the fair.
This is a dusty race track that runs through the fair.

You stand beneath a large and beautiful bell in the middle of the plaza, hanging on a free-standing stone arch. An inscription says this bell was a gift from the king to his wife, centuries ago. Lovely smells flood your nose from the north. There is a small flight of stairs leading down to a race track of sorts, and cobblestone paths head west or east to two more staircases.
You hear moans and several screams of terror. Now what could be making all this ruckus?

rooms.name: Melchior's Arms Store at the Millennial Fair

userData.LongDescription: A large tent covers a weapons shop.  A picture of the face of an old man with spectacles is sewn onto the tent above the entrance, along with the text, "Melchior's Arms Store" and two swords.  Melchior himself is not here, but an attendant is manning the shop.  There is a sign on his tent.

A large tent looms at the end of this path.  Something smells musty and stale from inside.  Is this the cause of all the noise?  The entrance is closed, with a sign saying that the attraction is out of order, but there are still screams coming from inside.
In the center of the fair is a giant fountain that sprouts water out of beautiful carved figure heads.
This is a dusty race track that runs through the fair.
There is a game set up that patrons of the fair can play, involving a weight that can slide up a pole and strike a bell if one hits the base of the device hard enough with an oversized mallet.

rooms.name: Road to the Rock Age Band

userData.LongDescription: You stand near a small staircase leading up to a raised platform towards Leene's Bell. A man stands near a table here, guzzling soda pop while another man times him. It must be some type of game. There is also a little girl here who is crying. It appears she has lost her cat. To the north you can hear some funky, prehistoric type music.

You stand before a small, glimmering, multi-colored timegate. Strange red and blue colors whirl within the gate's interior. On both sides of you, two interesting pods have been placed. It appears to be a teleportation device, probably built by Lucca. To the south, the walkway leads back into the main areas of the fair.
This is a dusty race track that runs through the fair.
This is a dusty race track that runs through the fair.
This is a dusty race track that runs through the fair.
The long marble steps lead away from the festivities and lead the way north to Leene's Bell.  To the south is a racetrack encircling the fairgrounds.

You stare at the device. It is a very odd thing, standing at six feet,and it is 5 feet in width. On the top and the bottom, are two hollow metallic cylinders with bright lightbulbs that switch through six different colours. It doesn't look very efficient, and since Lucca built it, you'd better keep your distance, lest it blow up on you.

The road ends in a little corner, surrounded by trees. In the center of the room, various tables are covered with food. Fans of the Rock Age Group are screaming and moshing to the tunes of the group. Up on the stage, the lead singer screams vulgarities into the mike.

You can hear a strange, rap type music coming from the northwest. In that direction you will find Gato. He was built by the brilliant Lucca, and has yet to break down, which is quite surprising, due to the fact that most things she builds do, indeed, break down.

The ground of the desert is a mixture of sand and rock, giving it the typical appearance of badlands.  There are almost no signs of vegetation, as the landscape does its best to strangle all life.  The harsh rays of the sun reflect off the sand, emitting heat from both above and below.

The once verdant, green grass appears to wither and die as it approaches the town of North Corel.  The town itself is more slum than actual town, with the land around it withered and dead and most of the buildings made out of scraps and junk.  Many of the buildings are little more than tents.  The town of North Corel is to the north and the mountain-surrounded grasslands are to the south.

Located in the shadow of the Gold Saucer, the town previously known as Corel has become a prison town.   Quicksand makes the edges of the desert impassable on foot.  The desolate land makes it a harsh place to house the convicts from around the world.  Most of the buildings appear to barely be standing, as the wood they are made from has rotted through in many locations.  The entrance to the prison is a gate for a ramshackle wooden fence.

rooms.name: On the second tier of North Corel

userData.LongDescription: A burnt-out house sits to the left here, having been fixed up with scraps of junk.  It's apparently still lived in, though its door is closed and locked tight. A well is in the ground to the northeast, though it appears that it hasn't been used in a while.  A large stone... thing blocks the way to the northeast, and a ramp to the north leads up to a building in reasonably decent shape, given the condition of the rest of the town.

The backside of this rather large building is by far the best-looking thing in this town, though it would likely be in a ghetto, were it anywhere else.  A broken sign is leaning against the wall of this building, and there is a boarded-up window a few feet away from it.  The entrance to the building lies around the corner to the southeast, but getting there is nigh impossible from here.

A town composed of nothing but junk, North Corel is a place that has had its share of tragedy.  It was a booming coal town, before it was burned to the ground by the diabolical Shinra corporation.  A dirt path leads northwest into the town proper, and towards a few ramshackle shops looking more like children's lemonade stands than anything else.

North Corel's general store is here, with a rather impressive stock, given the state of the village.  A burlap sign reading, 'General Store' sits on a large stick that has been stuck into the ground near the store, which sits right on the old minecart track.  Old boxes sit behind the counter, which is made of cast-off pieces of wood.  A gruff old man stands behind the counter, leaning on it with a far-off look in his eyes.

rooms.name: Outside of North Corel's weapon shop

userData.LongDescription: The counter of this store consists of an iron strongbox, and the inventory consists of stuff stored in a pile of wooden boxes behind the storekeeper.  There is no sign telling that this is the weapon shop.  Instead, a rack made of old wood is behind the shopkeeper, bearing a few swords and a bracelet, as well.  The shopkeeper himself is a strong-looking young man who appears to be bored with standing around here, waiting on the store.  To the left, there is a sign reading, 'Gold Saucer', and beneath it, there is a path leading towards the Ropeway.

These tracks, leading out of town to the northwest, are covered in abandoned garbage.  There are several wooden crates and a number of bags full of rail ties sitting directly on the tracks, and some oil drums and rope are also strewn about.  It's possible to continue on foot, but the tracks are unusable.

A few dusty beds and a bored clerk make up the inn of North Corel.  The clerk is a woman in her early twenties, dressed in a dark blue dress covered by a black apron.  A picture depicting Barret hangs above one of the beds, and one of Dyne is above another bed.  It doesn't appear that too many people have been here, though the beds don't look to be too uncomfortable...

This rather large building is about the least junky thing in the entire village, besides the Ropeway.  Its doors are open wide, and an absolutely filthy mat is lying on the ground before them.  The windows are either barred, or boarded, and the building itself appears to have escaped being damaged too badly in the fire that ruined most of Corel.  A ramp to the south leads onto a stone platform, though it appears to be rather shaky.

The Ropeway train is about the only way for tourists to get to the Gold Saucer, and could easily be called Corel's claim to fame.  It is a train with two propellers on it, that rides along a track while hanging on a pair of ropes.  It's painted a dark, dark blue, and can be entered via a pair of sliding doors on one side of it.

A rather large pile of junk is directly to the right here, bearing waste, and pieces of scrap metal or wood.  A few feet above that pile, and directly opposite of it, is a smaller pile of junk.  This one has a few pieces of coiled wire, some pieces of ripped fabric, and other less important, or less identifiable things.  These piles of junk, along with a few randomly strewn about pieces of scrap form some what of a path leading to the north, and to Mt. Corel.

An old tent with its flaps closed, and staked to the ground tightly sits here, a symbol of what the once beautiful village of North Corel has become... a shantytown.  Entrance into it doesn't seem possible, short of cutting through it, though it's unlikely that anything of use is inside.  Down to the southwest, the tool shop is still visible, for travelers in need of supplies, and to the northeast, a path weaves on through rather unsightly piles of junk.

A tent with its flaps tied shut lies to the right side of this dirt pathway.  To the left, great heaps of junk are piled up, and the occasional rat scurries through it.  Past the heaps of junk, there is a shop with a sign made of burlap that reads, 'General Store'.  An old, rusted, and obviously worthless mining cart track with several of its wooden ties missing runs to the northeast.

Apparently, walking onto the platform above isn't a good idea.  The remains of a rope bridge, once suspended over this pit, now hang down into the pit.  It's possible to use the broken bridge like a ladder to climb back up to town.

rooms.name: By a few old oil drums

userData.LongDescription: An old, burnt wooden shack is to the left here.  Its doorway and windows are boarded shut, and apparently, nobody's lived there in quite a long while.  Old, metal drums that were probably once used to hold oil are here, though one is standing, and has a fire lit in it.  The old minecart track is visible again, and it would lead out of the city to the northeast, and into North Corel... but a pile of junk is covering it, currently.

rooms.name: Outside of North Corel's tool shop

userData.LongDescription: What appears to be a pile of junk with a guy standing near it is actually North Corel's tool shop.  A large sign made of wood proclaims this, and is probably the only piece of non-scrap wood there.  The counter is made out of old, slightly rotten wood planks, and the shop's inventory is held in a few old boxes cluttered behind the shop's keeper.  The weapon shop is to the west, and the tool shop is to the east.  Additionally, a path to the northwest leads to a second tier of this town.

This circular room is filled with claw machines, cheap arcade games, and fortune telling devices.  In the center of the room is a raised area that says "WONDER SQUARE" in bright teal letters on the floor, with a picture of a planet behind the text.

The lobby for the chocobo races is very thematically designed. Columns patterned with chocobo feathers can be seen throughout the architecture. A large counter with clerks ready to facilitate racers stretches across the east wall. Large monitors hang from the ceiling, showing off the current race statistics.

Stairs lead from a lobby area up to a glass-walled walkway, through which visitors to Gold Saucer can visit the Wonder Square, Gold Saucer's most popular section.  Obnoxious, cheerful music plays at a loud volume throughout the area.  A large number of yellow spotlights shine down on the lobby.  A three-story-tall digital viewscreen is showing an advertisement for a stage play.

Formerly used as a small museum for the Battle Square's owner, Dio, the spacious room has been converted into a shop for VIPs of the Battle Square.  There are far fewer items adorning the wall than the normal shop, but they appear to be of a much higher quality.  A staircase leads back down to the Battle Square's main shop.

This long stairway leads up towards the doors of the famed Battle Square.  Large spotlights throw colorful lines across the sky, and strange, distant music can be heard.  Several green corridors with neon lights above them lead to different parts of the Gold Saucer, and one labelled 'Station' leads back to the foyer.  A large sign stands nearby.

All around are various weapons of battle:  whips, swords, hammers, spears, daggers, etc., all displayed for sale.  However, the only way to purchase any of them is through Battle Points.  A staircase leads up to the viewing room, while north leads towards the Battle Square itself.  An inn is nearby, and the entrance is to the south.

A dozen moogles wearing visors and carrying clipboards flutter around this tiny room, managing the finances of both the Battle Square and of any contestants who need to withdraw or deposit money.  A huge, oversized vault door takes up most of the room.  There are no tables, counters or other furniture; just bags of money and piles of coins.

Around the perimeter of this circular room is a row of rainbow-colored circles, each with a small picture on the floor in front of it.  These continue around most of the room, except for a hallway leading out of the Gold Saucer, and a large map with 'info' written on the floor in front of it.  The circles all lead to a separate section of the Gold Saucer.

This dusty, well-trodden inn consists of a few cots strewn about on the floor of a dull gray room.  A man stands behind a counter, waiting to collect the gold fee for resting here.  He looks fairly bored.  About the only decoration in the room is a large portrait on one wall.

A plastic brick road leads from the central area of Gold Saucer to the Speed Square rollercoaster to the northwest.  The bricks in the path are purposely molded to look like old, crumbling stone, but are clearly completely fake.  Some of the walls around the exits are made up of the same material.  Huge rollercoaster tracks can be seen stretching into the sky high above.

This gray steel room is the entrance to the amusement park's rollercoaster.  There are yellow handrails arranged around the platform to help form people into a line while they wait to get on the ride.  Arrows are painted on the ground.  There's a gift store that sells photographs of riders after they get off.

This room has banners hanging from the columns, each with a different grand insignia. There are a number of pedestals here, on top of which rests a glass display case. The records for the best of the best racers can be found here, with each course on a different pedestal.

The entrance to the world-renowned Gold Saucer is possibly the gaudiest place in the world.  A huge pink moogle statue towers overhead, its mouth being the passage through which the ropeway enters and leaves.  The passage into the Gold Saucer itself is denoted by a large plastic creature with the word 'Welcome' written on it in huge letters.

This shop is clearly for the chocobo enthusiast. There are all sorts of chocobo-themed items on display, from cute chocobo toys to powerful equipment designed to give an edge during races. A sign indicates that all items here are purchased with Choco Coins. You can use the 'list' command to see what is on sale.

The arena of the lobby is crowded with eager fighters, all of them punching, kicking, and doing other things to warm themselves up for the coming trial.  Near the front of the room, there is a wooden desk.  Behind the desk, a tired-looking receptionist sits, and before it, a small line of people wait for their chance.  To the left of the desk, a pair of large, double doors with the word 'Challenger' written across them lead into the actual arena.  To the south, the Battle Square's shop awaits.

You are standing on a wide long path. You can see the southern continent from here. You see in the distance a town to the southeast and some mountains to the far east. On the bridge you notice some soldiers standing guard. They seem to be just out of combat and counting their losses with a troubled look on their faces.

This is the border between Zenan Bridge and the Guardia continent. Zenan bridge, an ancient work of sturdy wood, has stood and acted as a way to the southern continent for countless years. Unfortunately, it has since become under attack. To the north, the mighty castle of Guardia rises above a surrounding forest.

You are standing closer to the other side of the bridge. Here you can get a closer look at the giant skeleton. Off in the distance you hear the sounds of battle, and the giant skeleton starts advancing towards you. In front of him there seem to be some more of those deceased.

You are standing on a wide long path. You can see the southern continent from here. You see in the distance a town to the southeast and some mountains to the far east. On the bridge you notice some soldiers standing guard. They seem to be just out of combat and counting their losses with a troubled look on their faces.

The lack of grass or any other plant life along the road is quite pronounced, making the whole town feel dead.  Rows of houses lines the sides of the dusty road, most of the doors shut tight.  One building in particular, though, is open to the public, and a sign hanging outside the front door labels it as the Senor Frog's Bar & Inn.

A bell hanging from the door is set up to ring when customers enter.  This store has a nice down-to-earth feel, and features many homemade goods such as dolls and bags of candy.  Pharmaceutical goods are on display behind the check-out counter.  The whole store smells strongly of scented candles.
A citizen of Dorino is idling about.

rooms.name: Outside a house in the desert

userData.LongDescription: In the middle of the desert, this single house stands alone and serves as a landmark.  Astonishly, three relatively healthy trees are growing in the desert sand right around the house.  Small fences around the trees prevent the soil mixtures underneath the trees from being overtaken by the desert surrounding them.

The harsh weather has taken its toll on this land, drying out much of the ground.  A wall blocks entrance from this direction into the town of Dorino to the southeast.  A path to the south leads toward the town gates.  To the north, Zenan Bridge spans the gap between the northern and southern continents.

A path leading up Denadoro Mountain begins at the base of the mountain, just to the north through some trees.  The tall mountain looms above, cries of various beasts echoing down to the base.  A short distance to the south is the edge of a huge desert, spanning out as far as the eye can see.

The fireplace crackles softly with a low fire, a stew roasting in a pot above it.  A pair of shoddy beds are standing next to each-other on a bearskin rug, which covers most of the floor in this bedroom.  A bag of chicken feed is next to the beds.  On top of a dresser by the fireplace is a small picture of some sort of creature.

In the back of the restaurant building, behind the bar, is a small inn for travellers to spend the night at and rest their achy bones.  Several beds are available in a back room, which is not particularly well shielded from the noise of the tavern.  There is a small sign posted on the counter.

rooms.name: The house of the elder of Dorino

userData.LongDescription: The dry wind blows softly in through the front door of the elder's house, which is permanently ajar.  A kitchen counter along the back wall has a bookcase attached to it, filled with tomes of rain-making rituals.  Despite the dry heat, a small fire burns in the fireplace, cooking a lean pork roast.

Behind the bar stands a burly man with a long mustache and greasy black hair, polishing glasses and serving drinks.  The bar has half a dozen wooden stools in front of it for customers to sit on, and a ragged placemat has been placed in front of each seat.  A few other tables are arranged near the bar for those who prefer them.

This house seems rather humble.  It has a table with a few chairs surrounding it and several potted plants, but not much else.  Light shines in through a nearby window, making patterns on the hardwood floor.  It's obvious that somebody lives in this house, but whoever does must not be home right now.

This land is nothing but desert, though a forest is visible in the distance far to the west.  Though there is some dirt mixed in with the sand, it is still far from being suitable for life.  Past the edge of the desert to the south, a trail is visible leading into the town of Porre.  A harsh wind blows across the desert unforgivingly.

The gates of Dorino lead northeast into town.  The town is well shielded from attack with its high walls and single entrance.  To the southeast, a large desert spans much of the continent.  Wind blows from a nearby mountain range across the dusty plains.  The massive Zenan Bridge is visible a little ways to the north.

The wood floor in this home is made of whole logs instead of planks, making it a pain to even walk across the room.  To make up for the uneven flooring, a thick animal skin has been laid out across most of the floor.  A smaller skin sits under the dining table, which is quite poorly made and would be slanted even if the floor were flat.

Here lies a gaping hole in the quicksand. The wind is blowing sand everywhere. A quick look around shows more...sand. A small scorpion also skitters on an eroded rock about here. To the horizon on the east, a comfortable house stands. To the south lies a dark forest with a pitch black sky overhanging.

The town of Dorino is particularly dusty and dry, a side-effect of the large desert south of the town.  A sign in a store window advertises the store's everyday low prices on everyday items, and the door is open.  The town gate, to the southwest, leads out onto the open plains.

Standing to the north is a forty foot tall mountain, the top of which is flat and covered with grass and the occasional bush. Further down the sides the rock begins to take on a more rugged form, contrasting to the sheer walls above. At the southern base of the mountain a cavern has formed, which is surrounded by green rock. To the left and right of the cavern's mouth are smooth, chalkish-white walls of stone, looking as if split in two some time ago. The grass on the ground seems to stop growing about two yards away from the entrance. A dirt path leads to the west.

A checkered carpet adorns the floor under the large oak table which spans the width of the room.  Several smaller tables are scattered around the room, hot meals laid upon them.  An ice chest sits against one wall.  Large windows cover the polished wooden walls, allowing customers to look outside and see the dusty town around them.

Along this northern border of the town, grass lines parts of the road, and even a couple trees are growing in some of the yards.  Nevertheless, it is still quite dry.  Gray and brown wood houses line the road, and combined with the dusty road give the town a genuine "old west" feel.  The town wall opens up toward the shoreline to the northeast, though there is no port.

rooms.name: The house of the elder of Dorino

userData.LongDescription: A fluffy pair of beds occupy the center of this bedroom, which is attached to the main room by a short foyer.  A rug adorns the wood floor, though it is actually far uglier than the floor underneath.  Three glass windows would be letting light in were the curtains not pulled shut.

A well-worn dirt trail leads southeast towards the town of Porre, while a second trail leads west into the cursed woods.  Some particularly dense trees to the south create a natural town wall.  Though there is some grass growing around the path, the beginning of a desert is visible a short distance to the north.

This strange place is actually a small cave, only about fifteen feet long and ten feet wide.  The cave is hidden by a large, beautiful waterfall covering the southern exit.  Most of the lair is covered in a strange green slime, and has a horrible smell to it.

This is a mountain ledge overlooking a huge waterfall.  West of you is another mountain ledge, covered in dense trees.  A bit north of you there is another waterfall, and a small, glistening lake below it. A rope ladder leads up.

This ledge is blocked off on the western side by several of the huge trees growing on this mountain.  Another rope bridge leads to an eastern ledge. You can see several different waterfalls from here.  Apparently, they're scattered all over the mountain.  A rope ladder leads to a lower part of the mountain.

This area is shadowed by huge trees above, making the area dim and hard to see in.  A rope ladder leads down the mountain. There is an open and looted treasure chest on a ledge below, about fifty feet below.  Several smaller trees poke up between the ledges.

This is a small mountain ledge with a wonderful view of a glistening waterfall below.  There is a good view of nearby areas from here.  There is a ledge to the north of you, and one to the east.  A sturdy looking rope bridge leads south, and a crude rope ladder leads up to the northern ledge.

This mountain ledge has a wonderful view, as it is several hundred feet high, and drops straight down off the mountain.    More of the mountain's red trees are scattered about here, and a rope ladder leads back down.  A waterfall can be seen far in the west.

A gentle stream flows through this room, and down a waterfall to the south.  A bright, glistening rainbow can be seen around the waterfall.  Ledges can be seen on both sides of the stream, and another rope ladder leads down off a western ledge into another area.

The shadows of huge trees cover this area, dimming the light and making it harder to see.  There are some odd markings on the mountain ledge walls here which appear to be made by ninja stars.  A rope ladder leads up further into the mountain.

Rope ladders connect two near ledges together.  A huge cave opening lies on the northeastern mountain ledge, leading into darkness.  Another waterfall, and a lake can be seen off the side of the ledge.  Both are glistening brightly in the sun.

This room is surrounded by dangerous cliffs.  The tops of the ground level trees are visible from here.  Below the cliffs is the source of the stream at the bottom of the mountain, a glistening lake.  A bridge leads north, onto another section of the mountain.  Also, a ladder leads down towards the base of the mountain.

A horrible presence seems to come from every part of this cave, suggesting some huge monster lives here.  There is a hole in the ceiling, lighting up the room and allowing some wind to blow through.  An odd aura of power seems to engulf this entire room.

Several huge trees with beautiful red and yellow leaves are growing next to a bright, glistening stream here.  A treasure chest sits up a ledge, out of reach.  A crude rope ladder leads up into the mountain.

The thick forest trees engulf this area in shadows.  Hardly a spot of sunlight can be seen.  A group of bright starry objects float round in the center of this room, forming a save point.  The sound of rushing water can be heard to the east, where another ledge is in the distance.

This is the base of Denadoro Mountain.  A glistening stream lies to the west, and some cliffs to the west.  The area seems rather untraveled by adventurers, as almost all the footprints around seem to be made by something not quite human.

This is the entrance to the cursed woods.  A dirt path is cleared northward, and a sign is posted to the west.  There is a treasure chest about twenty feet northeast of the entrance, looted long ago.  The forest is too dense to go anywhere except north.

The path continues onward to the north.  Another orange treasure chest lies on the ground, also opened and empty.  Around it are a few bushes.  It seems rather hard to tell whether they are dead, or are that color naturally.  There is a patch of yellow flowers growing here which you can smell from several feet away.

This room seems to be the living quarters for something.  It is well kept, considering it's a hole in the ground.  A few shelves are hanging off the walls, along with a bed lying to the side of the room.  Both seem to have been crudely hand made of the trees in this forest.  A table with a single chair sits on the southern side of the room.  A ladder leads up and out of this room.

The path comes to a dead end.  There is what remains of a bush in the northern part of the clearing.  There is a ladder coming out of it, leading down into another area.  The yellow flowers are scattered everywhere around this clearing.  There are some odd noises coming from the area of the bush.

This friendly wooden building holds a few beds for travellers to rest in, covers tucked in tightly.  The rustic atmosphere is enchanting, but the mattresses on the beds look like they're straight out of the middle ages.  A large number of uncurtained windows let light in, since there is no artificial lighting in the inn at all.  There is a sign posted.

rooms.name: The house of the elder of Porre

userData.LongDescription: The front door of the elder's house opens straight into the living room.  There is an old-fashioned spinning wheel used for sewing clothes sitting next to a small chair in the corner.  A washbowl and some pieces of china are resting on top of a bookshelf that doubles as a kitchen counter.  The majority of the room is taken up by a large dinner table.

Behind the wooden counter, a large cauldron boils, releasing the sweet smell of delicious food.  Chairs are lined up in front of the counter, and a couple of prepared meals are set out and waiting to be eaten.  A red and tan checkered rug is spread out across most of the room.

The house of Tata, a large two-story building, is open and filled with noise and commotion.  The surrounding houses are all fairly small in comparison.  To the south of the row of houses is a stone wall guarding the beach from invasion.  The waves can be heard beyond rolling gently.  A salty sea mist fills the air.

Tata must be a bit self-absorbed, because there are posters of him all over the walls.  There is a fireplace in the back wall, burning softly.  The breakfast table is covered with drinks and hors d'oeuvres as if for a large party.  The windows have fancy red curtains, which are currently open.

A couple small buildings, rather close together, block the wind coming from the east.  One has a sign above the front door labelling it as an inn, and the other simply has a welcome mat.  A clump of trees lies to the west and southwest, with a single path leading northwest out of town.

A large house belonging to the elder of Porre stands erect.  The building is surrounded by thick forests which are too dark to see into.  The house is only one floor tall and is made of plain gray stone.  Though nothing fancy, its seclusion from the rest of the town is noteworthy.  The rest of Porre is visible down a dirt trail to the east.

Paths stretch in every direction toward the different sections of town.  A thick wall of trees blocks travel to the northwest and helps to shield the town from attack.  The grass is wet with dew from the constant fog, but the soil underneath looks unusually dry and dead.

Shelves cover almost all of the walls inside this shop.  Atop said shelves are numerious different kinds of food, soap, empty jars, and medicine, among other things.  Hanging behind the counter is battle gear that can be purchased.  The shopkeeper leans on the long wooden counter, waiting for purchases.

This small bedroom is only big enough for the one bed in it, and even that barely fits.  A small dresser is beside it, atop which are a number of small mirrors.  An entryway leads into the living room, though there is no door.  This bedroom has far too many windows, allowing the walls to be nearly consumed by them.  A couple of the windows are covered up with posters.

An enormous wooden keg is on tap in the corner.  Several chairs are pulled up to the counter, and a couple more are stacked against the wall.  A few barrels of food are lined up beside the counter.  A pair of large windows let sunlight in, illuminating the stains on the rug.

rooms.name: The house of the elder of Porre

userData.LongDescription: An ugly brown rug covers most of the floor.  Two beds, made of uncomfortable-looking straw, are side by side.  A small night table in-between the beds has a vase of yellow flowers on top of it.  For whatever reason, there are a pair of barrels in the room, one of which is filled with bamboo sticks.

The entrance to Tata's house has a polished wood floor and nice stone walls.  A small tapestry on the wall has a picture of a medal of some sort and the words "Tata, the legendary hero" woven into it.  A set of stairs leads up to the second floor, and the front door is propped wide open.

The slanted ceiling peaks to a point in the center of this room, and falls toward either side.  Where it hits the east and west walls, it's only three feet high, but that didn't stop the owner from placing a four-foot-tall dresser against the western wall.  The dresser is a foot away from the wall and looks quite ridiculous.  Several beds are lined up next to each-other.

A hazy mist fogs up the town of Porre, rolling in from the ocean to the east and south.  A number of houses and such are clumped together in this part of town, but the only one enterable is a large cafe.  The others are locked tight.  Most of these buildings are rather primitive, and some even have thatched roofs.

The sound of running water can be heard from an opening in the northeastern corner of this passage.  The light from a torch in the northern wall, as well as the reflections of one around a bend to the south, reflect off the algae growing on the walls and floor, casting the passage in a cyan light.  The stone floor is cracked and buckled, and the algae grows in the cracks.  To the south, the passage continues, ending an opening leading to another cavern.

Light emanating from the algae growing on the walls and floor here provides the only illumination for this part of the tunnel.  The tunnel winds eastward, where a small set of stairs leads down, over a ledge, and around a bend in the tunnel.  Small alcoves barely large enough for a human to fit in dot the western and southern ends of this cavern, while to the north, an opening leads into another cave.

A river runs beneath the stone floor here, flowing to the south and southeast.  A small gap in the floor towards the center of this bridge provides a view  of the water rushing below.  A small ledge lies at the western end of the bridge, running to the northwest where the floor slopes to meet it.  The floor and ledge both have small bits of green and blue algae growing on them.  A small open chest sits at the southern part of the ridge, filling the space between the ledge and the drop into the water.  The floor rises to the northwest, leading to a platform, while to the east the bridge leads to another portion of the cavern.  To the north, a small island, unreachable from here, rests in the water, with an opening leading deeper into the cave.

A small chest lies on a raised alcove at the western end of this cavern.  A small set of stone stairs covered in algae lead up to the alcove.  The chest itself is open with small patches of algae beginning to form on it.  The walls are covered by algae, reflecting the light of the single torch set in the northern wall.  The only way out of this cavern is to the east, where a small opening leads into another cave.

A small set of stairs leads up to a raised pool at the northern end of this cavern.  The pool, walls and floor of this cavern are all overgrown with a pale blue algae, eminating a cyan light.  The water in the pool swirls in what appears to be a vortex.  The pool itself is large enough for a human-sized creature to easily fit in, and no bottom is visible from the surface.  The cavern continues around a bend to the south, where a small opening leads into another cave.

A small waterfall feeds into an underground river beneath the floor of this wide-open cavern.  Masses of pale blue and green algae cover the walls and parts of the floor, giving off slight illumination.  An algae covered rock sits near the eastern wall, overlooking a drop into the river.  A dampness hangs over the entire room, while water sprays from the waterfall onto the floor.  The entire room takes the form of a stone island, suspended over the river below it.  In the northeast wall, a set of stone stairs leads upwards into blackness.  A small bridge of stone lies to the south, leading into another cave, while a large bridge leads west, across the body of the river.

A single torch set in the center of the north wall provides illumination for this cavern.  The light is reflected by pale blue and green algae covering the walls, casting cyan light around the room.  The floor contains small patches of the same algae as the walls, while an algae-coated stone set of stairs leads north, out of the cavern.  The cavern continues to the west, where another set of stairs lead up into a raised alcove.

A single, large stalagmite springs out of the ground near the center of this otherwise open cavern.  Masses of pale green and blue algae cover the walls and cling to the stalagmite, pulsing with a soft light.  The cavern is wide towards the western end, but quickly narrows towards its eastern tip.  A torch has been embedded in the stalagmite, with another in the northwestern wall, providing illumination for the cavern.  Near the western end of the cavern, stairs lead down into the darkness, while at the eastern end, a ladder leads up to a small ledge.

Small stone bridges lead north and south from this stone platform.  Beneath the floor of the platform, a river runs southwards, fed by a pair of waterfalls in the northwest corner of the cavern.  Small clumps of glowing algae cling to the stone floor as well as to a ledge running across the eastern edge of the platform.  The northern bridge ends in a peninsula, containing an old chest, while the southern bridge leads into another cavern.  Southeast, around the ledge, extends another bridge, leading eastward.

A small set of stairs leads up and around a bend in the tunnel to the west, running out of sight.  Algae grows in the cracked stone floor of this cavern, reflecting the light of the single torch set in the northern wall.  To the east of the torch an opening leads north, into a different region of the cave.  The walls of this tunnel are covered in the same algae as the floor, giving the entire room a cyan tint.

Green and pale blue algae clings to the stone walls of this cave, casting the entire room in a cyan light.  The floor is covered in the same algae, though not as heavily as the walls.  Small drops of water fall from the ceiling and run down the wall, making the entire room damp.  Two torches rest in the walls, one in the northwestern corner, the other in the northeastern, providing full illumination for the room.  Daylight spills in from an opening to the south, while the cave curves on to the northwest.

This small ledge lies several meters off the ground below.  The walls are covered in pale blue and green algae, while water drips from the ceiling, forming pools on the floor.  An open chest sits at the base of the eastern wall, while a torch is set in the northern wall, slightly to the right of a ladder leading up.  Another ladder leads downwards, towards the floor below.

Water runs rapidly underfoot here, flowing in from the west and the north, and then continuing south, flowing through a crack out of the cavern.  Stone pillars jut out of the riverbed, supporting numerous stone platforms overhead.  Blue and green algae grows on the riverbed, making this area very slippery.  Fighting against the current, it is possible to travel north or south, where stone landings lead out of the river and onto dry land.

A putrid smell hangs over this chamber, emanating from several decaying corpses.  A single torch set in a bend in the eastern wall provides light which reflects off of the algae covering the floor and walls.  A large rock sits at the base of the bend, it too covered with algae.  Around the bend to the north, a small set of stairs leads up to a pool of water.  To the south, an opening in the cavern wall leads to another portion of the cave.

A small set of stone stairs descends into a rapidly rushing river at the southern end of this landing.  An algae-covered rock rests in the northeastern part of this landing, occupying a large portion of the space.  The floor is covered by algae as well, made wet and slippery by water splashed up from the river below.  Across a small gap to the east and higher up rests a much larger stone platform, under which the river runs.  In the wall to the north, two waterfalls spill into the river.  To the west, an opening in the cavern wall leads into a small passage.

Blue and green algae covers the walls and ceiling of this slightly curving tunnel, giving everything within a slightly cyan tint.  A torch sits in the northern wall near the eastern end of the tunnel, with another near the west edge.  Also near the western end, the southern wall gives way to a ledge.  A ladder leads from the ledge further down into the cave.  The tunnel also curves southeast into another portion of the cave.

This passage runs in a north-south direction, with two torches providing lighting.  One torch lies at the far northern end of the passage, out of reach from here, while the other is in a small bend in the eastern wall.  Blue and green algae grows along the walls and floor, reflecting the torch light, and giving the entire passage a cyan tint.  An opening is to the south, leading into another portion of the cave, while the passage continues northward.

A sparkling cluster of stars swirls near the northern wall of this small landing, allowing undisturbed sleep.  Just to the west of the save point rests a large, algae-covered rock, reflecting the light from the stars.  Just off the western edge of this landing, a waterfall flows down into the river, which then runs off to the south.  A small set of stairs at the southern end of this landing lead down into the river, while an opening in the northern wall leads into another cavern.  The walls and floor of this cavern are covered by slick, blue and green algae, giving off faint cyan light.

A warm, humid breeze blows over the grassy ridgeline that runs east to south. The trail widens slightly as it approaches a solitary tree that has managed to grow on top of the cliff. A section of dusty earth near the trunk has been worn into the ground by a large animal that's chosen this spot as a resting area.

A small inlet leads into a narrow clearing. A clear stream originates from a pool of bubbling water, largely covered with branches and leaves. The branches covering the small pool look intentionally placed, but for what purpose is unclear. A dense undergrowth makes it possible, but difficult to travel west into the forest maze.

The trail connects to a small, grassy mesa with a trickling creek running along the northeastern edge. Most of the platform is covered in coarse crabgrass that seems to thrive on the rocky terrain. The gully to the west and beyond the cliff's ledge is filled with bushes with creeping vines that seem to be expanding in every direction.

The narrow, grass-covered ridge line curves as it travels above the small clearings below. Hidden in the branches of the trees that tower over the trail, multitudes of chirping birds and trilling insects fill the air with their songs. The trail follows a gentle slope to the south, while to the west, it slightly widens as it levels out.

The dirt trail doubles back on itself as it connects the gully to the top of a series of connected cliffs. The ground is littered with ruts and too many animal tracks to identify individual species, as this seems to be the easiest way to climb out of the cleft terrain. A few bushes with incredibly large flowers are growing near the trailhead and seem to be the dominant plant life in the immediate vicinity.

Lush trees tower overhead and keep the muddy clay path covered in shade. Beams of sunlight pierce through the dense canopy, nourishing clusters of brightly colored flowers that speckle the undergrowth. In contrast, hiding within the shade, fanged flowers fill the spaces between the bushes that line the path leading east.

A small reed basket sits near the southern edge of the path where the sun has dried a portion of the muddy trail. Large footprints lead away from the trail and into some bushes to the north. The eastern side of the path borders the top of a short rocky cliff which has thick, leafy vines growing up from a thin grassy outcropping.

Bizarre animal cries come from somewhere in the canopy far above the jungle floor, which covers most of the ground in shadows. Only a couple of trees and some short grass have managed to thrive on this rocky clearing. Creeping vines, extending from the bushes in the gully below, have begun to peek over the edge, foreshadowing their imminent domination of this space.

The path follows a gentle incline north as it connects a raised trail to a glade lower to the west. Trunks of nearby trees brush against the eastern edge of the trail as the wind pushes through the area. Long vines extend from them and drape across the trail, hanging off the opposite ledge as they search for sunlight.

Giant trees and bushes have managed to maintain the integrity of the path despite the flooding that left much of the vicinity a muddy hole. The stream flows towards the north with a flattened river bank following along. Tucked away near a crevice between two cliffs to the south, a small reed basket sits near the water.

The trail passes under a large arch draped with exposed tree roots and nascent vines. A particularly prolific strain of flowering plants have overtaken the cliff faces exposed to the sun. The same sunlight has parched the trail and hardened the tracks left by some clawed creature.

rooms.name: A Massive Glade within the Forest Maze

userData.LongDescription: Long grass, flowers with elongated stems, and random boulders are the only features the broad expanse around a mighty mountain. Although the crag is filled with caverns throughout its surface, there's one near the bottom that appears like a gaping maw in comparison.

Thick vines and bushes cover the rock faces that make that border the path. Bright green bushes with fuzzy leaves have grown rampantly, almost hiding the trail completely. The growth throughout the jungle is untamed, but this is almost undisturbed.  To the east, the trail becomes more defined, while to the south, it practically dwindles to a suggestion.

A network of root holding up an eroded cliff to the north leads up to an enormous tree covered in flowers. The stream angles away from the cliff and towards Ioka village as it disappears around the bend. Claw marks, animal tracks, and deep ruts populate the muddy trail that runs from south to east.

A mossy pedestal of clay towers over the riverbed left behind by some recent flood. It appears to be held in place by a twisted pair of gnarled tree roots that disappear into the muddy earth towards a small cliff to the west, with thick vines growing up it. Only a small stream remains from whatever deluge caused the wash-out, which has deposited a fallen tree that offers a path over the water to the east.

This clearing is devoid of much forestry. Nothing flourishes here, and the ground has signs of uneven footprints trampling the soil. Broken branches are scattered around, interspersed with dead leaves here and there.

This clearing is devoid of much forestry. Nothing flourishes here, and the ground has signs of uneven footprints trampling the soil. Broken branches are scattered around, interspersed with dead leaves here and there.

A major portion of this elevated plateau has fallen away. It's been reduced to a small, winding trail, but some of it has remained in position due to supporting roots. The weeds and plants that once grew on the detached landmass have browned and withered, while the grass along the trail is still lush and green.

Bright daylight pours in through an opening in the canopy far above. Giant flowers have taken full advantage and are flourishing in this well-lit glade. A flowering vine has extended from the edge of the trail and wrapped around a small, moss-covered rock in the center of the trail. Off to the side a kidney-shaped depression, covered in bits of fur, marks the resting place of a very large beast.

The fractured terrain causes the path to split into a few different directions. A small inlet to the east leads up to the edge of a small creek, but the dense undergrowth makes it difficult to navigate to. To the west, the walls of the gully begin to migrate towards each other, while to the northwest they expand to create a large opening.

Wild plant growth spills away from a thick canopied oasis to the south, stopping abruptly once it reaches the parched soil of the prehistoric wasteland.
