Carried in on a humid breeze, the sweet smells of exotic flowers are accompanied by primeval sounds; the bellowing roars of massive beasts and piercing caws of screeching birds ring out in warning.

The rocky pass extending from the cliff to the north reaches out to a small mesa to the southeast, creating a small land bridge. Dense vegetation has filled the space below, which is fed by a nearby creek. The trail itself follows a gentle slope to the west as it descends into the gully.

Prehistoric bushes crowd the path, reducing the trail to little more than a winding suggestion. The leafy fronds and shaggy vines block the already dim sunlight from reaching the moist bog-like earth and a sickly-sweet smell rises from the undergrowth. The path connects two openings, one to the west and another to the south.

The muddy trail winds through dense undergrowth, which becomes stunted as it approaches some cliffs that jut from the earth. The formation breaks through the canopy, allowing a generous amount of sunlight to the surface. A secluded copse flourishes against the rocky precipice, encouraged by the unabated sunlight.

Broad blades of grass cover the outcropping sticking out from the cliff face to the west. Nestled against the rocky wall, there are large bushes with extravagant flowers and grasping tendrils that have rooted into the cracks in the craggy wall. Along the northern portion of the ledge, a large mass of vines has overgrown the edges, allowing easy access up and down the cliff.

The terrain is covered in lush vegetation that almost obscures the edge of the cliff to the south. The thick bushes are almost seamlessly replaced by the tops of towering trees that soar over the forest floor. A grassy trail leads east and up to an elevated path that encircles the clearing to the north.

Gigantic bushes and leafy fronds fill this verdant gully. Only the very center of the trail is devoid of any plant growth, likely due to the amount of foot traffic that passes through. Short cliffs border the trail, which only serves to amplify the massive distance to the jungle's canopy.

The trail twists above the vegetation-covered earth, following the winding cliff as it travels through the jungle. A large break in the canopy has allowed more sunlight onto this part of the trail, which has resulted in it becoming a bare stone path. As the trail progresses to the east and into the shade, the grass is able to recover and grow freely.

This clearing is devoid of much forestry. Nothing flourishes here, and the ground has signs of uneven footprints trampling the soil. Broken branches are scattered around, interspersed with dead leaves here and there.

rooms.name: A vast chamber in the Reptite Lair

userData.LongDescription: The ground in this section of the cavern appears to have suffered incredible amounts of stress from many claws or other natural weaponry. Openings have been dug through the soft earth, leading down into darkness. The stone walls also appear to be fractured, with claw marks suggesting a huge creature attempted to dig through them. The dim torchlight barely illuminates the region.

The small hole is extremely tight, as it descends deeper within the lair. A tunnel this narrow and uneven was clearly not designed to be used by humans. From below the dim light of a torch illuminates some aspects of the tunnel, and the rest of the shaft is in complete darkness. A puddle of water collects in one corner of the hole, dripping down into the remainder of the opening to the lair's depths below.

A pile of rocks sits in the northeastern corner of this room, near an earthen shaft. Tied to a small hook-like protrusion at the top of the shaft is a rope ladder leading downward. Points of light can be seen softly glowing from within an excavated hole opposite the rock pile. The walls appear to have been badly gouged and clawed, especially directly above the assortment of stones and boulders.

rooms.name: A vast chamber in the Reptite Lair

userData.LongDescription: Dim light shines through the area from a torch hanging on a sconce, illuminating a room of clawed rock and broken earth. The ground of the large chamber appears to have been carved, a circular hole having been dug through it. The walls seem to have withstood an immense amount of fractures and cracks.

A small, narrow tunnel descends deeper into the lair. The vertical shaft is poorly made, roughly shaped and uneven. Though the entrance of the hole appears large, inside the actual tunnel is rather cramped. The eroded stone walls shed dirt at the lightest touch, and the odd claw marks present elsewhere in the region can also be seen here.

rooms.name: A vast chamber in the Reptite Lair

userData.LongDescription: A puddle of water sits in one corner of this vast, cavernous chamber. The ground appears to have sustained significant damage. Large chunks of the floor have been torn from the ground, making uneven surfaces. The walls are made of cracked stone, dens carved into them by something immense. A hole has been excavated through the earth, leading down into the dark.

A long twine rope ladder makes its way up the earthen shaft. A pile of rocks can be seen through the opening where the ladder snakes its way upward. Most of the room is in shadow, as the lighting is dim. Droplets of water plop steadily onto the ground, pooling to create shallow puddles.

The earthen tunnel is cramped and nearly vertical. Roughly shaped and uneven, the rock walls appear to have been clawed through. The torchlight from above is dim, illuminating only a few feet into the shaft before being swallowed by the creeping darkness. The narrow hole continues downward, deeper into the lair.

A crude set of stairs has been clawed into a slope leading up to a natural circular dais.  Stalagmites stand erect atop the platform, grisly corpses impaled on them as warnings.  Torches are stuck into crevices in the walls, providing ample light.

rooms.name: A vast chamber in the Reptite Lair

userData.LongDescription: The colors of the cavern appear to meld and mix together, due to the poor lighting conditions through the chamber. The stone walls have been scarred by deep grooves, most likely made by a creature's claws. An opening has been excavated in the midst of this chamber. The bright torchlight only reveals a few feet of the hole, the rest of which fades into darkness.

Not everything is distinguishable in the small, vertical tunnel as it reaches its end. The edges of the room are in complete darkness. The light from the torches below barely glows bright enough for one to navigate down the shaft. The odd claw marks present elsewhere in the lair speckle the walls, and puddles of water drip into the tunnel from above.

The walls of this vertical tunnel are scored by claw marks and have clumps of green moss speckling their surfaces, as well as a fair amount of slime. The claws carved small openings in the stone, inside of which a plenitude of slime collects. Roughly shaped, the entire construction is eroded by the puddles of water that drip down the shaft into a vast, cavernous chamber.

A narrow hole descends deeper into the lair. Faint pinpoints of light trickle in from above, but otherwise the room is mostly dark. The walls within this small room are clawed in several places. Water drips steadily on the soft earth.

The walls of this tunnel are bare and smooth, but for the deep holes scattered across them. It's as though a creature crawled across the side of the tunnel rather than going along the floor, and as a consequence its claws left deep furrows in the rock. Water slowly runs out from each hole, trickling down the walls and disappearing into the darkness below. As the tunnel widens, a narrow ledge can be seen crudely dug around the circular opening.

rooms.name: A hallway within the Reptite Lair

userData.LongDescription: A long hallway leads northward, torches along the walls alight with a bright yellow flame. A plenitude of thick moss grows around a doorway in the western wall. The earth is scarred due to the passing of many creatures.

rooms.name: The bottom level of the Reptite Lair

userData.LongDescription: This is a large chamber, well-lit by several ensconced torches located in each corner. Although the walls show marks of being dug into by something, the smoothness of the floor can still be seen between piles of dirt. A large doorway to the east opens up to the rest of the lair.

This three-way intersection is well-lit by the torches hanging in crevices along the walls. The torchlight continues northwards, where a staircase leads to a podium. More of the hallway can be seen southward, with dense clumps of moss growing on the walls. A crude rope ladder can be glimpsed in the distance to the west.

The constant updraft of warm air is thick with the odor of mildew and broken earth. Somewhere, deeper in the lair, small scrabbling noises echo up the cramped quarters. Without the aid of fresh air intake the miasma only grows thicker as the roughly shaped tunnel continues deeper into the earth.

The massive cave mouth serves as the entrance to the Reptite Lair. The opening of the cave is not man-made, but rather natural earth that has been carved by what appear to be claw marks. The stone walls of the cavern appear to be mostly whole, though what look like dens have been dug through them. The colors in the region appear to blend and mix in an odd way, which may be the result of the dim lighting, coming from torches set in sconces on the walls at random intervals.

You stand before another rope ladder that heads even higher on the cliff.  Looking up, you can spot a rock ladder that goes across the canyon directly above you, from there it appears only a short walk to the top.  Your mind begins to race with anticipation as to what may be there.

rooms.name: At the top of a ladder

userData.LongDescription: You stand at the top of another ladder, on a small piece of land that protrudes out from the side of the cliff.  The path continues on to the east through a small group of trees.  Through the trees you can make out another open area, and yet another ladder that heads up higher.

rooms.name: At the top of a ladder

userData.LongDescription: You are at the top of a ladder that goes downwards to the path back to the village.  To the south of you is a path that runs alongside and above the path that you were just on, and it appears that you cross the path that you were on at a stone bridge that you can see to the south.

You are a short ways north of the rock bridge that you had noticed to the south, and before you there is a small rope ladder that you can climb to take you to higher reaches of the canyon.  There are more powerful enemies here, looking to contest with your progress on the mountain.

You are on another open part, with cliff walls on all sides of you.  To the north of you, you can make out the top of the cliff far above, but just to the north, there is yet another ladder leading even higher on the way to the top.  More monsters lurk here as well.

You stand just before the peak of the mountain, as just to the north you can see the top.  A warm breeze blows through your hair as you try to make out what is there, a last set of enemies stands here before you reach your goal.

rooms.name: At the base of a Mountain

userData.LongDescription: From the base of this very steep mountain, a footpath to the top has been trodden into the jurassic stone, through the giant ferns, oversized mushrooms, and other plants that overrun the cliffs.  Far to the north it's possible to make out a ladder up to a higher level of the gorge in the mountain, and a little ways up a rock bridge is visible heading across the canyon.

You are on another narrow ledge, overlooking the canyon below.  To the east is another rocky bridge that crosses the canyon.  Across the bridge there is one final ladder that allows access to the highest reaches of the mountain.  There are a few more enemies here as well.

You are on a narrow rock ledge, and there is a rock bridge across the gap that you saw earlier to the east here.  You can spot another rope ladder up to an even higher level of the canyon across the bridge.  To the north there is a small path leading north to a ladder that will take you back down.

You stand before another ladder that will take you even higher on the mountain.  To the west is a rock bridge that will take you to the path back to the village.  You can spot even more dangers ahead, as you continue on your trek to find whatever is at the top.  There are some more monsters here as well.

You are but a few levels away from the top of the mountain, as you can make out the passage north far above you.  The path continues on to the south, as you can see that is where the rock bridge crosses the canyon.  To the east across the bridge you can see the final ladder before you reach the top.

This is the final rope ladder on the mountain, as far as you can tell.  At the top you can hopefully find whatever is at the top of the peak.  You think that you can make out some squawking, but you are not for certain.  Back to your west there is the rock bridge that you came on, and the path back to the village.

You stand in a small open area, surrounded by cliffs on all sides.  From here, it appears to be all up, as a series of ladders lies in front of you.  Far above your head you can see another rock bridge that goes across the path that you are on.  Back to the west you can see the path back to the village through some trees.

You are at the peak of the Dactyl Nest Mountain, and the view here is spectacular.  There is a huge Dactyl here in a nest that will allow you to ride on them to reach other areas of the prehistoric.  To the south is the path back down to the base of the mountain.

You stand before a small rope ladder that heads upwards so that you can reach the top of the mountain, and find whatever is there.  Back to the south is the narrow path to the village.  There are also more enemies here to prevent you from reaching the top.

Torches light the small room, showing the cavern's stone walls off in a way not normally expected. Being very similar in looks to other caves around the world, the only true difference to be seen is the incredibly brittle stone that makes up the walls. Rats scurry quickly about, looking for some sort of food to scavenge. As to be expected in most caves, bats cover the ceiling, some every so often dropping off and fluttering away into the darkness to the west. The ground is made of a hard black stone, though it quickly turns to mud to the west. To the north a bright light shines in.

The water is deeper than its counterparts to the west and south, though the reason behind its purple tint most likely keeps fish from living in it. A large nest of about a ten feet radius rests upon the water, floating gently against the stream. Inside the scraped together nest are arcane runes, similar to the ones seen to the west and south of here. The ever present fog blocks your view of both the ceiling and further upstream. From the sound of it, the stream carries on to the west and south.

The sound of trickling water can be heard from the east, the water a foot above the ground. At the end of the water is a pile of debris to the west, containing pieces of wood, mushroom, and bone. From what can be heard, the water weaves through to the west into a huge reservoir of water. Finding no dry ground, most travelers tread in the water, choosing to avoid the muddy walkways on the sides of the cavern. A heavy mist hampers any further sight to the east and south, though rat squeaks can be distinguished through the splattering of water to the east.

A glaring light flows in from the north, causing the room to be an oven as the black stone making up the ground absorbs the heat. The darkness is pierced by the sunlight, and a majority of the vermin found throughout the cave have vanished, leaving travel unimpeded. Beside the mouth of the cave, a pale hand lies across the stone. The hand belongs to a dead soldier, his armor ripped apart by a set of claws, along with him himself. Blood has seeped to the floor, and forms into a puddle around him. To the south a ramp leading downwards heads into a slightly well-lit room. Stones block the entrance to the north, light trickling in through the cracks.

The light is dim, and small bats constantly cause the lights to flicker. Dark, arcane symbols are written both on the torches and the stalagmites, contrasting against their light. Every couple of minutes a handful of dirt drops from the ceiling, emitting a putrid odor into the thickening air. Attached to the roof are several planks of rotting wood, creaking with the effort of holding the thousands of pounds of rock atop it. Further down the rock wall a dark liquid slides down, looking faintly of blood. Ancient, blueish-green bones litter the path leading to the east and west.

Orange, uneven walls twist towards the east, disappearing into the darkness. Clinging to the walls are small, flickering torches, giving off just enough light to see the bone cluttered ground. Rat nests are nestled beside the glowing stalagmites at the entrance, looking long abandoned. A thick, humid air flows in from the east, smelling slightly of bats. Through the mist, the distorted light of the entrance can be seen. A rarely treaded path leads toward the east.

The mud usually seen deeper in the cave forms a bank for the river, allowing travellers to escape the murky waters. Though this section of cavern barely differs geographically from the western side, the dark, arcane symbols are no longer seen about the walls or stalagmites. The orange, clayish stone that makes up the southern wall seems fragile, cracking easily at the slightest weight. Most likely the damp air and constant tunneling has weakened it. A torch attached to the southern wall is surrounded by large cracks and crevices, showing signs of age. The stream to the north heads into a heavy fog, while the path leading east is well-lit and dry.

This is a silent dirt path down with decayed, leafless trees on the sides. To the north is a large castle, looking ominous and demonic in the moonlight. The wind blows fiercely, rustling the blades of grass about. South leads to a large mountain with a small cave entrance on it.

The thick mist seen elsewhere in the cavern seems to have thickened greatly. Most likely due to a large source of heat below the caves, hot steam rises from the water, leaving enough visibility to see about three feet away. Through the heavy fog a dim torchlight is seen to the south, showing a point of dry land. To the north an oddly shaped nest can be made out.

The overpowering stench of guano is emitted from the ceiling and multiple holes along the southern walls. Growing onto the stone to the east is fungi of many sorts, each mushroom differing in color and potency of poison. The runes normally seen throughout the cave are missing, though the darkness is just as thick as always. Planks of wood are lined up against the corner to the northwest, looking as if freshly cut, and giving off the faint smell of pine. A haphazardly built bridge is built over a thin ravine crossing to the north. The ground is muddy, an indication that water isn't too far away. A path marked by stones leads to the west.

This is the Matango Inn.  Travellers can rest for the night in a warm bed made of straw.  The floor is clear except for three beds.  Behind the counter, a merchant keeps the inn.  Through a door to the south lies a hallway and the rest of the castle.

This hallway connects the throne room to Truffle's room.  The floor is bare.  The walls are adorned with a pair of candles, and a few vines grow down from the ceiling.  A staircase leads up to Truffle's room, while to the left the throne room is visible.

The city of Matango sits to the northwest.  The ground is dotted with large mushrooms.  Several townsfolk wander around aimlessly in the area just to the south.  The entire city is surrounded by parts of the Upper Land forest.  A cave opens to the north, leading out of the city, while to the south the path leads to the city.

The castle walls extend southward to the edge of the hill.  The castle of Truffle sits just to the north, towering over the forest.  Below the hill, a clearing swarms with townsfolk.  A staircase leads down the hill, while to the north a few steps lead up to the main entrance of the castle.

rooms.name: In front of the mushroom castle

userData.LongDescription: The castle rises high above the ground just to the north.  In every direction, the forest stretches away as far as the eye can see.  Just to the south, the hill ends, dropping a good distance to the ground below.  A shop sits just off to the west, while immediately to the north the main entrance to the castle opens.

A small path leads from a door to the south, that opens into the castle, to a cave opening in the north, dark and ominous.  Dappled shadows move gently on the ground as the sun streams through the thick canopy of trees, swaying in the wind.  The grass underfoot is soft and springy, bouncing back from a traveler's steps unharmed.

This clearing serves as a meeting place for the people of Matango.  The forest acts as a wall between the city and the rest of the Upper Land.  To the north, the castle of King Truffle is visible.  This clearing continues a short distance west, while to the north a cave leads out of the city.

Truffle's room is fairly sparse for a king's room.  It is furnished only by a double bed.  A couple of candles mounted on the wall light the room.  Four pillars, one in each corner, help support the ceiling.  Two windows in the south wall look out on the Great Forest.  To the west, a hallway leads to the throne room.

This clearing is primarily a meeting place for the citizens of Matango.  The forest all around the city seperates it from the rest of the Upper Land.  The castle of King Truffle sits atop a small hill to the north.  To the north, a staircase leads up the hill to the castle, while to the east the clearing stretches away.

This hallway connects the throne room and Truffle's room.  The hallway is quite full.  A table sits against the north wall.  A few vines grow down from the ceiling, and a candle is mounted on the wall.  The west wall is barren except for a few paintings.  To the east, Truffle's room can be seen, while to the south a staircase leads down.

This is the main hall of the castle of King Truffle.  A straw carpet covers much of the floor here.  To the east, a hallway leads to the inn and also to a back door out of the castle.  To the north, a door leads to the throne room.  To the south, a door leads out of the castle.

This is a hall to the east of the main hall of the castle of King Truffle.  The floor and walls are bare.  To the west, the main hall is visible, as well as the passages to the throne room and out of the castle.  To the north, a door leads to the Matango Inn, while to the south a back door leads out of the castle.

This is the throne room of this castle, if one could call it that.  Two thrones sit in the north part of the room, squat and wide, clearly not meant for humans.  A few vines grow on the wall behind the thrones.  A small riser seperates the thrones from the main floor.  To the east, a small hallway leads away, while to the south a doorway leads to the main hall.

This is the item shop of Matango.  A low stone counter, topped with a thin wooden plank, crosses the center of the room.  A merchant stands behind the counter to sell his wares.  A few pots sit on the floor, and a few candles adorn the walls.  To the south, a door leads out.

Stairs lead down from the upper level onto this small, dead-end overlook. Rubble covers everything on this ledge, which has sight over a small passage leading west and south. The rocks make it dangerous to jump down to the lower passage, as they litter the ground everywhere.

Jagged rock walls and a small stream block all passage, except for the path back to the west. The stream itself is a pale green color, and light seems to pour into the area from places both upstream and downstream, making the water shimmer and sparkle.

The cavern's shape has formed into a cross. To the north, many stalagmites dot the cavern, with a narrow path snaking further north. West and east both lead nowhere, with chasm and wall barring the way. To the south, an opening leads further downwards, to a lower level.

Bright light pours down from the ceiling into this cave. The only visible exit is the one back out of this cave. The warming light has encouraged heavy plant growth, unnatural for inside a cave. The ceiling from which the light comes in appears to have several large holes in it, as if to allow passage for something huge.

The passage widens into a larger area with stalagmites dotting the southern edge of the passage, but a path between some of them looks just wide enough to use. A set of stairs leads north and up, and another set can be seen southeast, but it cannot be reached from here.

Three sets of stairs lead from here, as well as a path leading to the northeast. The third set is unreachable, as a large pit sits in front of them, leaving only the northwestern and northeastern stairs available to foot traffic. A large chasm covers the northern region of this area.

A small, unremarkable passage links the southwestern ledge with a small staircase. To the west, a set of unreachable steps lie behind a small hole. The ground is full of many tiny pockmarks, caused by past inhabitants of this cave, none of whom can be seen now.

rooms.name: Path to the Cave of the White Dragon

userData.LongDescription: This is the northern part of a small field of giant mushrooms. The mushrooms dominate the scene, towering eight feet high, and making progress through the field a tricky situation at best.  Wind swirls around and through the stalks, rustling the leaves and swaying the trees gently.

The path nears a large, pitch-dark chasm, while getting all narrower with each step. Light streams out from between the stalagmites to the south, casting eerie shadows all about. The ground here is rough and uneven, and freshly overturned, as if something has been tunneling through it. Combined with the poor lighting, it makes passage next to the chasm extremely difficult.

The long passageway forms a horseshoe, with grassy patches covering the northern and southern floors. From this point in the passage, nothing can be seen further in either direction. The light dims to the northeast, in the opposite direction of the entrance.

The rock floors have given way to a more natural dirt floor, with little spots of grass and plantlife growing in a few places. The northern wall is broken down in some spots, where stalagmites have grown up to a great height. A rock wall also prevents passage to the south and east, leaving only a western continuance, and a set of stairs leading down.

A large chasm snakes throughout this cavern, forming the path into the shape of the letter 'C'. The path hugs close to the walls, extremely narrow. The dim light has brightened considerably, as it looks like the south portion of this cavern is linked to the surface world.

The staircase opens up into a small dead-end. At the far west end of the cavern, a small orb is on a ledge. The orb glows with a dull brown color, and has many facets. Strangely, the orb seems powerless, despite its mystical nature.

A large pit makes movement through this section of the cave difficult, but is it narrow enough to jump. Next to the pit is a small post, jutting out of the ground. A small patch of sand is the defining feature of the floor, as it catches the eye right away.

The roof of this cavern is dangerously close to this mass of land. A large, dark chasm lines the northern and western sides of the mass. On the eastern side, a post sticks out from the ground, with solid ground within jumping distance over the eastern rift. A small set of stairs lead south onto a lower level of the cave.

rooms.name: Path to the Cave of the White Dragon

userData.LongDescription: The ground rises on the eastern and western sides, creating a valley leading to the north and south.  At the northern end, an opening leads into a dark cave, and the south leads to the larger area of the field.  A small patch of the big mushrooms sits in the center of the path.

A long, narrow passage links two sets of stairs, both of which lead down to a lower level. To the south of the passage lies a dark pit. Skulls, ribs, and other bones litter the passageway, especially concentrated in the western region. Nothing else in the passage hints at a sign of danger.

rooms.name: Entrance to the Cave of the White Dragon

userData.LongDescription: Light seeps in from the entrance of the cavern, lighting the area. The walls form an extremely narrow passage, with not much to see within. A set of steps have been carved into the rock, linking the outside world with the depths of the cavern.

Sandwiched between heavy overgrowth and two caves, is a small clearing. Rich, dark grasses cover the floor of this clearing. Large, yellow mushrooms sprout up everywhere, nearly human height in some cases. The overgrowth bounding this clearing is thick and dark, too treacherous to enter.

After passing through narrowly seperated walls, the path opens up into a wide area. A small hole blocks all passage to the west, and the cavern walls close in from all other directions, except the exit back north.

This small chunk of land is raised from most of the rest of the cave and has a small staircase that leads down to a lower level. On the southern part of the landmass, a post is jammed into the ground. To the west of the post, is another landmass, and it looks just within jumping reach of this one.

Light floods into the passage from an opening on the west side. To the north of the passage, an exit leads up, to a higher level. The two exits are connected by a narrow passage, which curves like a snake. Fresh air blows into the passage, from the outside.

Rocks litter the floor of this area, and the light has strangely strengthened, with the east seeming to be the source of the light. The sound of running water can also be heard from that direction, but it is faint. A post is here, sticking out of the ground.

rooms.name: Path to the Cave of the White Dragon

userData.LongDescription: A small field full of giant mushrooms make navigation tricky; threading through the giant stalks could prove to be difficult.  The trees overhead cast shadows from the dazzling but dimmed sun overhead, and the  shadows move gently over the mushroom caps, giving a surreal feeling to the entire scene.  An opening to the south leads back to Fung Castle.

To the south, large stalagmites block most of the light, causing the area to be cast in darkness. The area only has two outlets, a staircase to the northeast which leads to an upper level, and another set of steps which lead further into the depths. A large chasm prevents all passage northwards.

Three paths branch out from this centralized location. Southwards, two walls close in, the narrow passage leading out of sight. To the west, the path narrows considerably, and passes by a large black hole. North of here, a set of stairs climb upwards to a new level of the caverns.

A passage takes a long, winding journey down from the clearing, leading in a clockwise fashion, with the entrance from the clearing being in the north. The passage takes a circular path to a small opening in the walls. A small ledge can be seen high above in the northeast, looking over the passage.

Just past the edge of the trail, the cliffs drop off sharply, tumbling down perhaps thirty feet at a quite vertical angle.  Sparse patches of wild grass have grown tall here and there around the trail, but for the most part, the mountain pass is made of tough rock.

Grass and rocks cover the trail, making it difficult to ascend or descend the mountain.  The path is not as well-worn as one would like, the tall grass apparently being very resilient.  The space between the rock wall to the east and the steep drop-off to the west is narrow.  To the northeast, the trail heads up toward a cave.

A narrow opening in the mountainside leads into a tunnel, which descends toward the base.  It could almost be called a pitfall, with its steepness and the tall grass partially concealing it. The remains of an old landslide create rocky terrain which would be difficult to cross were the path any steeper.  Stones and rubble cover the ground.

Strange purple flowers dot the path here and there, bright and vibrant in color.  The ground falls away on both sides of the path, which leads out onto a sort of peninsula.  Further ahead, a bridge connects the path to another section of mountain.  Where the peninsula begins at the side of the mountain, a cave leads down toward the base.

rooms.name: Before a cave that leads up to the summit

userData.LongDescription: The trail runs straight into a cliffside and stops, as if the wall wasn't recently there and the trail once continued around the side of the mountain to the summit.  It doesn't continue anywhere now, but instead, a small cave in the northern cliffside contains a tight, almost vertical shaft that climbs upwards to what must be the peak.  A rope is hanging inside the cave to aid ascension.

This tunnel is too narrow to be comfortable, and the low ceiling and lack of light aren't helping any.  The cave slopes downward toward a dead-end, almost like a trap, though there is nothing at the bottom.  Stalactites reach down low enough to create a danger of hitting one's head.

A strange, shining rune drawn on the stone floor creates a protective field to ward off the monsters that inhabit most of North Mountain, making this a suitable place to rest up before a journey to the summit.  This cavern is mostly round with a dome-like ceiling, and large openings to the east and southwest let light flood in from the outside.

A large gap in the middle of the trail would strongly discourage travel to the east, if not for a tightrope straddling the chasm.  The rope seems sturdy and is well-attached to the ground with wooden posts on either end.  Solid ground would admittedly be preferable, but there isn't any, so travelling down the mountain will require travellers to perform a short circus act.

A rope bridge with its planks made of oak logs is connected to this ledge, posts driven into the hard ground.  The bridge leads north, across a gap to another section of the cliff.  Large purple flowers are scattered in clumps through the dirt and grass that make up the path, some grown nearly knee high.

Huge purple flowers grow all around, making it difficult to even walk while navigating around them.  Some of the flower plants are several feet high and as big as a large bush, and the colorful petals seem to almost glow as they dance in the breeze.  Aside from the flowers, the ground is rather barren, though, the path being made more of dirt and rock than grass.

A narrow opening in the cave wall peeks through to another tunnel, but the crack is too small to pass through, only a few inches wide.  To the south, though, the cave extends, and sinks down as though leading to a cellar.  A pool of standing water, probably full of bat dung, reflects sunlight spilling in from the exit.

This section of cave is almost like a slide, with the slick rock surface and the slanted floor.  One side of the cave just sort of drops off into a pit, landing who knows how far down.  The ceiling is very low, descending at a more extreme rate than the ground.

An opening barely large enough for a person to squeeze through leads outside and lets light in.  The entrance looks to have been chiseled to a degree to make it wider, and it is about a meter up in the wall.  Some flat stones and a box have been moved in place to allow easier climbing.

A narrow passageway to the south leads deeper into the cave, going down so steeply as to almost be a slide.  Light gleams in from an exit nearby, bright enough to make the cracks in the stone floor visible.  Several small boulders are pushed up against the wall, as if to clear a path through the cave.

A steep, narrow trail up the side of a cliff leads into North Mountain, ancient home of dragons.  To either side of the trail, it drops straight down, nearly fifty feet by the time the trail reaches the cave entrance.  The cave leads into the mountainside, beginning the path to the peak.

This bridge spans two ledges on North Mountain, and hangs over a deep gap.  The bridge itself is made of hard oak logs, and strung together with a sturdy length of rope.  Tall posts, as high above the ground as two men, are driven into the cliffs on either side for the bridge to hang from.  The north cliff is significantly higher.

A cavern entrance is chiseled into the mountainside, leading further up the mountain.  A trail winds southward along the cliff's edge, overlooking the surrounding desert.  On a nearby ledge, just a few strides out of reach, beautiful purple flowers grow in plenty around a large plant.

A humongous pile of boulders in the middle of the path nearly blocks the entrance to a cave leading down North Mountain.  Perhaps the result of a landslide, the boulders are lodged firmly into the ground after having apparently fallen quite hard onto the trail from some ways up.  Some of them look to be planted three or four feet into the ground at least.

The significant drop that's been on the south edge of the trail now has placed itself right in the middle of the trail, making a gap too wide to leap over.  A stake has been pounded into the ground on either side of the gap, though, and a rope is tied in place to theoretically allow the trail to continue up the mountain.  Of course, continuing on the trail means balancing on a rope for fifteen or twenty strides.

The rock walls on both sides of the trail create a sort of valley.  Tall grass is plentiful along the edges of the path, but the many footsteps of travellers have worn down the middle of the trail to the dirt bedding.  The peak can be seen above to the northwest.

Hundreds of gorgeous purple flowers are on all sides of the path, large and bushy, barely leaving an opening in the middle for the path.  The flowers give off a strong aroma, somewhat sickening at such a large quantity.  A narrow cave shaft leads down, a rope tied firmly at the top, and flowers have been cut away around the cave entrance.  The path continues north to the peak.

The path along the ledge comes to an abrupt stop, narrowing to a point and then dropping vertically like nobody's business.  A plump bunch of purple flowers such as can be seen elsewhere along the cliffs is deposited right at the point of the dead end.  The desert, maybe as far as a quarter of a mile below, can be seen stretching out to the south.

A large natural hole in the ground would be quite a fall into the section of cave below, if not for the stairs that have been carved into the steep rock wall.  The cave continues to the east, sloping upwards toward the summit.  Although enough sunlight permeates into the cave to see the path by, small groups of stalagmites are obscured by the darkness and would be easy for one to trip over.

The end of the path is not marked by a wall, but rather by the ceiling meeting the floor as they both slope downward.  An opened box has tumbled into the dead end and gotten stuck.  The stone is smooth and shiny, and sunlight coming from back at the entrance reflects off the walls enough to see clearly by.

From the summit of North Mountain, the surrounding land can be seen for miles and miles. The gorgeous scenery is breathtaking, and looking down the slopes of the mountain, the purple flowers that dot the cliffs make the landscape seem colorful and alive.

This ledge sort of crops out from the main mountain, jutting out like a long tooth from the path to the west.  There is a bit of a breeze at this height, but it's surprisingly warm considering the altitude.  Purple flowers grow around a pair of posts, which hold up a wooden bridge leading south.

The tunnel path veers sharply to the left while going uphill, and if the stone surface did not reflect light so well, it would be easy for spelunkers to walk face-first into the wall.  Situated inside a crevice in the wall is a nest of some sort, abandoned.

Light enters from the opening to the path outside, illuminating the cave interior enough to allow passage.  The cavern opens into two directions, and following the passage to the north there is a noticable incline as the tunnel leads up to higher parts of the mountain.

A narrow tunnel between the main cavern and an opening out to the cliffside zigzags erratically, preventing much light from making it all the way inside.  As if to take advantage of the dimness, thick stalagmites shoot up from the ground everywhere, just begging to be bumped into and tripped over.

An exit back out onto the trail lets sunlight into the cave.  The exit looks to have been chiseled at to allow enough room for passage.  The tunnel twists around towards a set of carved stairs leading down a steep slope.  Though the cave is otherwise natural, someone apparently needed to get up to the peak, and must have had these stairs carved into the stone.

This tunnel connects to the path through the cliffs outside, and steers toward a save point to the northeast.  There is more than enough sunlight to be able to see well, and a strange scratch is carved into the tunnel wall.  A puddle of standing water looks particularly unfit for drinking.

The ground outside is masoned with gray and the occasional beige cobblestone.  There are two barrels against the wall of the house beside the aged wooden door.  Sand-colored bricks wall off the landing from the rising and falling water beyond it.  A water wheel is busy turning and churning the bustling water.  A narrow walkway along the side of the mansion comes to an oddly abrupt end at its rear.

The dark masonry of the pier leads down to a ship, the ferry to Nikeah.  The boat appears to be engine driven, rather than sail powered, and quite seaworthy.  A few dockhands mill about the boat, and a small pile of goods rests near the entrance to the ship, waiting to be carried away to the warehouse.  The exit is to the north, back to the town's center.

A narrow path here runs between the mansion's top floor and the guardrail on the walkway.  The windows looking out are barred in wrought iron, both to encourage the honesty of citizens strolling along the wall, and to deflect any missiles that may be heading towards the soldiers defending the town.  The wall heads south further on, while the stairs leading down from wall are to the east.

Resembling that of an octagonal alcove, the mansion's foyer is quite small and only sparsely decorated.  A vase full of large red roses has been attached high upon the wall adjacent the mansion's entrance, warmly greeting all who enter.  Beside the roses an oil lamp burns, brightly illuminating the foyer.  A mat has been placed at the entrance encouraging visitors to shake loose any debris that might have followed them in.

A few soldiers are normally stationed here, watching the forest below for signs of activity to alert the town. The mansion appears to be built into the wall itself, and one of the top floor windows is open to air out the house.  Along the wall further south there appears to be the main lookout station for soldiers, and the northwestern corner of the wall is just to the north.

The cold, hard exterior the dungeon presents seems to have been specifically constructed with the goal of instilling extreme hopelessness and despair in would-be occupants.  Everything within the dungeon is built from coarse unfriendly gray stone, which are especially prone to absorbing the icy air.  Vicious snake-like heads protrude from pillars between a pair of iron-barred cells, both of which have been left open.  How this dungeon ended up in the depths below the mansion is a mystery.

The room is quite small, barely large enough for children to run free.  The walls are made with beige-colored bricks, and the floor is masoned with cold gray stones.  On the wall is a bulbous glass lamp incarcerating a spry flame.  Below it stands a shiny stove made of a brassy alloy.  Towering beside the stove is a decorous bookcase whose shelves are brimming with books.  Spread across the floor is a rug with a simple repeating pattern of mustard yellow and russet skewed rectangles.  Surrounding this pattern are alternating borders of the same colors in spiral braids.  The wall recesses, and in its depth stands an armoire storing curious objects.  A large clay pot is placed so it just barely blocks the armoire.  A small circular table is set with a skimpy white cloth that inadequately drapes over its edges, revealing its single leg and four feet.  A corked green long-necked glass bottle has been placed atop the table, off-center, and beside it a small plate has been laid.  Two

This room appears to be the storage area for the Cafe; a few wooden crates and a large pot lie on the ground, where the bartender can access them easily.  A small stove is here for him to make his own meals, and to dispell the chill damness of living underground.  There is also an empty, dusty desk here, though for what reason is anyone's guess.  To the north, another door leads to the bartender's bedroom, and the stairs lead out to the cafe.

The dull clay red carpeting terminates as the stairs end.  An ornate wooden balcony borders along the stairwell.  The second floor walls are lined with beige-colored bricks and the floor is set with gray stones.  Placed in the corner of the landing is a small rounded wooden end table to display a pot of flowers, three enormous roses in bloom cradled by supple green leaves.  The gray stone brick of the floor introduces a hallway covered with a mustard yellow and green design on a predominantly red carpeting.

This small, cozy house just outside of town is the home of the great martial artist Duncan.  A small patch of flowers still grows in the ground here, perhaps kept alive as a form of discipline in the harsh world. A small path leads around the house, and out of the town to the north.

This is the home of the great martial artist who trained Sabin and Vargas, Duncan.  Surprisingly, there is no training equipment on the ground, only a very clean rug, two chairs and a neat bookcase.  A tea kettle is resting on the stove, and a set of stairs on the east side of the room lead down.

The cell is a claustrophobic ten by ten foot box engulfed almost completely in darkness.  What little glow that does enter reveals a square metallic object in the rear corner.  Fortunately the iron bars at the front of the cell have a door-sized opening allowing free passage in and out.

A dozen sealed crates littered all about the floor, create a maze navigatable by only the most nimble of feet.  Passage to the western side of the room is made impossible by a cluster of various objects.  However, a crooked path running narrowly between an antique phonograph and a bucket, allow an escape into the eastern side.  A tall grandfather clock slowly ticking away, stands near an extremely decrepit door that must lead further into the basement.

The Relic Shop is one of the many novelty shops that caters to the rich urban elite of South Figaro.  They offer elaborate pairs of eye protection, pendants, and talismans to protect its customers from the monsters of the World of Ruin.  It's probably just stuff and nonsense, though; a wise adventurer would save money for something more utilitarian, and less gaudy. A set of stairs against the north wall leads to the inn and the cafe, while a doorway out lets one explore the town.

The cobblestone paths from the northwest and west meet up with the masonry of the pier here.   This spot provides an excellent view of the ocean and of the river that provides South Figaro with its fresh water.   Moorings rust slowly from the salt spray, and a few travelers gather here, newly arrived from the Nikeah ferry to the south.  They are most likely headed to the Cafe for a meal and, for those with more money to burn, for an evening with a woman of ill repute.

A blue light at the center of the room sparkles so brightly, that it perpetually illuminates all aspects of the cloister containing it, putting the dim lighting seen throughout the rest of the basement to shame.  Before the exceptionally mesmerizing quality of the light, the large wooden support beams crisscrossing overhead are barely noticeable.

A small room, but with the bit of finery that makes all the difference when you are trying to impress a customer, the South Figaro item shop features a grandmother clock, a long counter topped with large red flowers, and a rug to wipe a person's feet on.  A list is posted of what they sell, and the shopkeeper looks more than willing to sell them to anyone.

This bridge connects east and west South Figaro to each other, shadowed by the large apartments and the Inn, located on the second story of the towns' buildings.  Looking into the water, a few fish hide here, escaping the bright sunlight.  The entrance to town is to the west, while the shopping district can be seen in the distance to the northeast.

A small but respectable quarters for the bartender, the first impression upon entering the room is the owner of this room does not recieve many guests.  Lit from some lamps on the sides of the room, the light cast by the lamps only falls upon one small table, a bookcase, the bartender's bed, and a few crates in the corner of the room.  The cold stone floor is covered by two large tapestries, one under the table, and the other under the bed, for protection of ones toes during the winter nights.

Choosing a destination within this short hallway is like an adventure; with three identical doors evenly spread throughout its course and nothing identifying where each might lead.  A dimly lit lamp is mounted next to each of the first two doors, while a recessed bookcase standing beside the last makes it the odd door out.

A thick musty odor encases the hall. It originates, no doubt, from three heavy-set bookcases standing side-by-side within a recession in the wall.  The recession seems to have been designed with these particular bookcases in mind, as they all stand perfectly flush against one another.  If any spot within the basement the dim lighting should be otherwise, this should be it.  However, the lamp attached to the middle of the wall fails to even partly illuminate the furthest of the three bookcases.

The mansion's owner must be purchasing poorly made grandfather clocks because yet another one is stationed within this side of the room.  A white clothed table and two chairs are set up neatly, making them appear very out of place compared with the rest of the storage room's clutter.  The tripping hazard on this side manifests as a number of large pots scattered aimlessly about.

The Arsenal shops have their own source of hydro-electric power, a small waterwheel that feeds off a stream running into the ocean, enabling them to produce the equipment that Celes, Edgar, and Sabin used to retake Figaro Castle.  To the east, stairs lead up to the wall which surrounds South Figaro and contains the lookout stations.

A small shop sits here, with the picture of a lamp posted next to the door.  The shop even has a small grass lawn surrounding it, perhaps kept alive by potions from the shopkeeper.  A look west shows the park, and the network of canals through the city.  The wall continues north and south.

The ship is cleaned, stocked with goods, and almost ready to leave for Nikeah.  The engines rumble gently, again indicating it's modern status.  Anyone seeking passage to Nikeah merely needs to speak with the captain.  For any who are not ready to leave for Nikeah yet, the pier leads out, and back to the city.

At the counter of this establishment, in the golden days of the world, one could buy Bard Hats, Green Berets, and Gaia Gear here.  That time is long since passed, however, ever since the Jidoor Auction House bought them all up.  They are still in business, though, and the goods they sell are listed here.  The armor shop shares a fireplace with the Weapon Shop to the west, in an attempt to encourage their business.  The shopkeeper stands here, next to a beautiful vase of flowers.

Despite the dim lighting, the cold emptiness of the basement is clearly seen and felt.  A long wooden support beam runs overhead connecting two monotonous brick layered walls.  Presently, dirty gray stones come together in a patternless cohesion, forming a fitting floor for the purposes of a typical basement.

rooms.name: In front of the Relic Shop

userData.LongDescription: This small piece of land is home to a shop boasting two signs. One is an Inn sign and the other is the Relic Shop sign, as the lower level is the place for the rich connoiseur to pick up items claimed to prevent poisoning, blindness, or magic altogether.  Of more import to the average traveler is the Inn, which is located above the Relic shop on the second story.  Cobblestone paths lead northwest, to the exit, southeast, to the ferry, and under an arch to the north, which leads into the center of town.

South Figaro is shipped the finest in weapons that Figaro's high technology can produce, and supplemented with the skilled efforts of their own smithy.  The Weapon shop is heated by a fireplace that is shared with the Armor shop to the east, and which is constantly kept blazing, no matter the season or the weather.  A small list is posted on the wall, of the products sold here.  A doorway leads out to the street.

From the flowers to the fireplace, this room is tastefully done.  At once spacious but snug, the room is well lit with a touch of privacy instilled by the southern section of the room, where a bookshelf partially conceals the study.  This house belongs to the servant of the richest man in South Figaro, who apparently pays quite well, if the servant can provide himself with such a place.  A table with three chairs provides room for the man, his grandson, and a guest to eat dinner.  The old man still sits in another chair in his study, reading over a book of some sort. A stairwell leads to their cellar, which emerges at the ground level.

The eastern half of the Cafe is reserved for drinking, and the long bar seats a good many men, some doing shots, most chugging bottles of the local home brew.  The bartender hurries back and forth behind the bar, keeping everyone's drinks filled and marking the additions onto everyone's tabs.  From the looks of it, the cafe makes a fortune on liquor.  But then again, with this much alcohol being consumed it would be unwise to start a fight; the smallest disagreement could turn into a fierce barroom brawl.

Caught between the warehouse to the west, and the ferry entrance to the east, constantly barraged with the loud noise, working, and swearing of dozens of men, the house here has been left in disrepair and slowly rots from the dampness of the sea.  Barrels of goods rest against the house here, along with several layabout workmen who give passerby appraising looks, considering their skill in battle, and how much money they have.

Connected to the rest of the town by cobblestone bridges, the southeastern part of South Figaro is where most of the populace lives, in stylish apartments overlooking the ocean.  The secluded doorway to a rather large house is also here, suggesting some amount of wealth with the small lawn outside of it.  One bridge leads west and to the entrance of town, while another crosses the town's park, with the weapon shop's sign in view.  To the south, a narrow but well-kept street leads toward the ocean.

This bare section of the wall is swept clean of sand and debris by the soldiers who occupy it, on their continual mission of keeping watch for bands of monsters.  Smoke rises from the chimney of the Arsenal, which can be seen directly below the wall.  Walkways lead west and southeast, to other parts of the wall.

Not much can be found in this room, except for a bucket, a pot, a desk, and a cabinet, probably for dishes.  All look empty, and the desk is built into the wall itself, nearly immovable.  This looks like a good place to hide, but not much else.  The rest of the basement is to the west.

High above South Figaro, the inn has an unusually large variety of services.  Both single beds, and a bridal suite are available, though the bridal comes at a hefty pricetag.  The bridal is located through a separate door, kept private from the common room.  Music filters in from the cafe to the south, along with the carousing of the patrons there.  A stairway on the western wall goes down to the Relic Shop, and to the exit.  By the innkeep's desk is a small sign.

The hallway is moderately spacious, allowing for at least two people to walk side-by-side.  A high-framed door is placed within a recession of the northern wall.  Just a few feet further down, near the hallway's end, a second door stands identically within another recession.  More than adequate illumination of the door and its small metal handle arrive from an oil lamp placed high on the left side of the recession.

This open space is large and hardly in use.  The fireplace in the distance emanates a fervent aura of warmth into the otherwise stale emptiness.  A large wooden credenza placed against the wall hosts a pot of blooming roses.  An oil lamp posted above lends the roses a golden glow.  A dust-ridden rug precedes an alternate doorway leading to the outside.

This is where most of the soldiers are stationed, as it guards the entrance to the town and lacks any easy way to get there, becoming very easily defendable.   A few shingles are missing from the roof of the Chocobo Rental Shop, where the soldiers have lept over the guardrail to slide off the roof and to the ground below in times of crisis.  It would probably hurt, though, as the ground below is cobblestone and the drop looks to be about ten feet.  A few barrels supply ethers and potions for the troops, in case of a prolonged attack.  The exit from the wall is back by the Arsenal stairway, to the north.

This is one of the lookout points of South Figaro, with a few guards stationed to alert the city should monsters attack suddenly.  A swift stream runs into the city, supplying fresh water to the seaport town.  The wall continues to the northwest and to the south, while a long flight of stairs leads to the town below.

This corner of South Figaro is a small square plot of land, running against the wall if entering from the west, and into a large house when coming from the north.  The area is small, but out of the way of main traffic, people are regularly found here.  An alleyway around the bridges further west begins here, and ends at the armor shop to the north.  The main southern square is to the west.

The stairwell leads from the ground level to the upper story, in a small room that appears to serve little function but to support the floor above.  A doorway leads outside, to the southern square, while a small hallway leads east, to another small storage room.

This is the Chocobo Rental Shop, South Figaro branch. A chocobo mills around the northern half of the room, pecking grain and looking bored.  The shop's interior is rough with wooden floors and straw lining the pen-like enclosure just to the north, the building is obviously designed chiefly to hold livestock, not display some fashionable trendy design.  A few pictures line the walls with artistic drawings of chocobos, and a few prize winners of the shop owner's racing days.

rooms.name: At the Base of the Stairs

userData.LongDescription: This area of town lies at the base of the wall, with just a small, easily defendable corridor between the wall and the ocean, should attacks come from South Figaro's flank.  Since the coast is clear, however, the citizens mull about, walking up the stairs to the item shop, and between the town's heart and its outskirts.  A path around the eastern edge of the wall leads north, to another house.

The cold emptiness of the dungeon is magnified greatly within the confines of this tiny cell.  The gray stoned surfaces lining the cavity afford comfort to no one, their cold apathy drowning the cell like the smothering darkness throughout it.  Occasionally a faint glow of light splashes over the bars at the front of the cell, revealing an old metal chest.

This alley lies between a building that houses the town's waterwheel, and a giant stone wall surrounding the town's center.  The western edge of the alley ends abruptly in the form of the streams running through town.  The alley is a little shady and dark compared to most of town, but is as safe as any of the town's other thoroughfares.  Bridges are visible over the stream to the west.

The Cafe is the premier eating establishment, meetingplace, traveler's rest area, and house of ill repute in South Figaro.  The room bustles with the waitresses carrying drinks, businessmen conversing in hushed tones, and drunkards crashing their beers against each other at the bar.  Definitely a good place to have a good time, there are plenty of tables to go around, so have a seat.

One of the shabbier areas of town, the buildings here are warehouses mostly used to store the goods shipped between South Figaro and Nikeah.  A long alleyway leads north and out of the town, while to the east there is more waterfront.  The way further southward is blocked by the ocean.  A few unscrupulous workmen lounge about here, resting against the crates.

rooms.name: Entrance to the South Figaro Cafe

userData.LongDescription: With the lack of space on the first floor, the entrance to the cafe is up a small flight of stairs located here.  This small room is only large enough to serve as the foyer to the large establishment, and as the convenient place to store people who are too drunk to drink, judging from the small pile of them here.  Making use of the large void upstairs, the waitresses just throw them over the balcony to the ground below, where they lie until they wake up, and either go home or drink some more.  A doorway leads out to the streets of South Figaro.

A lone lamp dimly lights the way down into the basement.  Shadows pervasively dodge the meek lighting, emphasizing the expectedly dark ambience a hidden passageway should have.  The air is moist with a chilly draft blowing through like clockwork, making it especially cold.  Another stairway running against the draft's current leads further down.

A thick stand of trees extends to the north, just east of a platform raised more than a dozen feet above the ground. A narrow, almost hidden trail through the trees is visible far to the north. A tiny, cobblestone path leads south, squeezed between the ocean to the east and the house to the west.

It seems that of all the towns of the world, the town of South Figaro has suffered the least, as the Light of Judgement never fell here.  Though much of the population was lost in the war against Kefka, children still run through the streets and the town is prospering.  Past the roads through the town, a far-off suit of magitek armor is visible, a remnant of the town's occupation by the Empire's army and left as a monument to Kefka and the Empire's defeat.  All along the south edge of town the ocean laps against the town's sea wall, and any traveler would remember that South Figaro is a port city. The chocobo rental shop is just north, smelling strongly of the large birds.

The room is quite small, sizably comparable to that of a walk-in storage closet.  Against a wall, one of the green-cushioned chairs normally seen throughout the mansion above sits alone.  Across from the chair is an empty wooden bucket.  Considering the pleasant and bright atmosphere of the mansion above, it would be hard to believe this might be a room setup for interrogation purposes.

This is the home of the wealthiest person in town, and it looks the part.  The mansion itself is huge, rising two stories and positively dripping with opulence, no doubt in imitation of Owzer's house, in Jidoor.  The cafe and the ferry are to the south, while the commercial center is further east, visible past a few more bridges.

In the center of town is a small park, with a few flower bushes that are carefully kept alive after the world's destruction. A waterwheel turns infinitely here, providing the citizens a small amount of electricity for lamps in town after hours.  The arsenal is to the north, along with an immense suit of magitek armor from the time of South Figaro's occupation by the Empire.  The road west leads to a large mansion, even taller than the city's walls.  In a southerly direction the street leads to more waterfront property, and perhaps some interesting individuals that live there.

The eastern edge of South Figaro's mansion begins here, along with two workmen repairing a window on the house.  Across a small creek one can see the mansion's private dock, where the owner could escape in a time of attack, or where they could have their supplies delivered directly to them.  A small bridge, covered in cobblestones like the rest of the city, leads east to the town arsenal.  The mansion's entrance is to the west.

The Arsenal's eastern door, leading to the armor shop, is located inside the large building immediately north of here, outfitting the guards with the protection they need to fend off the bands of monsters around.  A small alleyway leads south, separated from the town center's water wheel by a small amount of building space.  A long flight of stairs leads upwards here, to the top of the wall where the soldiers are stationed.  The weapon shop is to the west.

From here one can see most of South Figaro, and the network of bridges that connect the town's many parts.  The view of the forest is blocked on all sides by the huge wall around the town, and buildings mostly block the ocean, but glimpses of waves cresting far offshore can still be seen. The town appears to be built on the water itself, and two creeks flow through the center of town.  A bridge leads east to the rest of town, with the exception of a large mansion to the north.  The stench of Chocobo and the exit prevails towards the southwest, and to the south the Inn is visible.

A great brick fireplace acts as a centerpiece for the hall, flames burning fiercely from its mouth.  Beautifully crafted suits of golden armor stand on either side of the fireplace, each resting their gauntlets on the pommel of a heavy broadsword.  Oil lamps set high upon the walls encircle the entire room, diminishing any shadows the fireplace's flames might play with to near nil.  A gorgeous rug covers the majority of the stone floor.  At the hearth of the fireplace a smaller rug of much rougher appearance has been placed to protect the larger from the fire's regurgitated ashes.  A stairway in the western wall leads to the second floor of the mansion.

This small platform has a door leading into into a house, and is at a medium height between the top of the wall and the ground level of the city, but otherwise is unremarkable.  A guardrail lines the edges of the wall, to prevent citizens from falling to their deaths unnecessarily.

A bucket is placed against the wall and near it an armoire stands on a mustard yellow and russet rectangular-patterned rug.  The wall recesses for a warmly lit fireplace. A bed large enough for two persons sits at the middle-eastern side of the room.  An emblem of a white letter 'B' in a white winged-circle on top of a blue and green striped background is repeated twice on the footboard of the bed.  Beside the bed stands a tall bookcase whose shelves are filled with numerous volumes.  In front of the bookcase, placed against the wall is a small metal-framed wooden crate.  An unusually cool draft haunts the room, its origin unclear.

The view of the water is excellent here, and many citizens gather to listen to the sounds of water and the few seagulls that have found a safe harbor here.  Glancing across the stream immediately west, one can see the people milling about the cafe.  The center of town is to the north, the base of South Figaro's wall is to the east.

For the size of the house on the outside, it is certainly unexpected to find such a tiny, sparse room as the main entrance.  But that appears to be what it is, the floor swept and walls bare, with a door leading further in, and another leading out to South Figaro's wall.

In the dimly lit downstairs, few things are of any interest to the eye except for the cobwebs in the corner of the room. Besides the stairway leading up, this room is filled only by a glowing blue save point in the center of the floor.

The ornately designed red, green, and mustard yellow carpeting comes to a dead end along with the hallway.  Prior to the dead end, the wall recesses into a second door.  The door is identical to the first: wooden with metal bracings and a small metal handle for opening it.  An oil lamp lights the recession and the door within it.

This small landing overlooks Duncan's house, and more ocean water.  If one was feeling adventurous, it might be possible to follow the rooftops west, over the large house which stands there, all the way back to the entrance of town.  However, the roofs look steep, and it would be unwise to tempt fate.  A shop is located not far to the north, while stairs lead closer to the ground.

A thick forest surrounds South Figaro, sheltering it from some of the world's harsher winds but also hiding a few monsters that lurk around the town.  The town itself is very well protected, both by guards and by an imposing wall.   The large wall which protects the city is most prominently in view, with lookout points to guard from the monsters of the World of Ruin.  To the east lies the first beginnings of the town itself.

This walkway along the top of the wall runs between a shop to the south and a landing towards the north.  Acres and acres of thick forest are visible to the east, a sign that perhaps the world can recover from its hideous disfigurement by Kefka.

The northernmost part of the wall is sparsely guarded, as the wall is nearly impenetrable, and a portcullis protects the small stream leading into town.  The site provides a lovely view of the forest around South Figaro, though.  The walkway continues east and west.

This is the eastern end of the wooden walkway which collapsed into the lifestream. Looking to the west it almost seems like a bizarre ship, with the remaining pillar serving as its mast. To the northeast, some agitated looking vendor seems to sell his wares on something which looks like the remainder of a set of stairs which lead upstairs. To the southwest a salesman is selling accessories.

This part of Mideel is especially littered with wooden wreckage from the collapsed walkway. It is not easy to find an even footing without tripping over a board or other rubble. Even in all this devastation, some of the villagers haven't given up hope. A vendor is selling a few items which he salvaged from the collapsed item shop here.

This is one of the saddest sights so far here in Mideel. The equipment shopkeeper had to grab most of his wares and leave his small shop. Now he has to display them on a wooden crate which seems to have been hastily nailed together. Looking around at the ragged people it is doubtful he will manage a lot of sales, especially since the rubble doesn't exactly attract visitors.

The only part of the walkway which used to span Mideel is the lone wooden pillar which used to hold up the little bridge. Behind it, a little rocky path leads up to the mostly destroyed clinic, but the earthquakes made a part of it collapse into the lifestream, thus a person who wants to get there would have to jump.

A dirt path is leading northeast towards the destroyed town of Mideel. It is littered with wooden planks and boards and all sorts of other debris. A deep green glow can be seen further along the path originating from a sea of lifestream which erupted below Mideel spelling doom for the little town.

A hidden beach spreads out from the edge of town, leading out into a lagoon. Light sparkles off of the waves that gently lap against the shore. A faint change in the color of the water can be seen below the surface, though whether caused by a sandbar or the wellspring of the Lifestream eruption nearby cannot be determined.

rooms.name: Wooden Wreckage on the Lifestream Lake

userData.LongDescription: Most of the wooden walkway which used to cross Mideel village fell into the lifestream when the erupting pressure made the ground burst open. The foundations of the walkway remain, littered with wooden wreckage from above. A pillar of the walkway remains as a as the only elevated structure in Mideel apart from a rocky path to the northwest which used to connect Mideel with the small clinic it was famous for.

rooms.name: At the shore of the Lifestream Lake

userData.LongDescription: The path out of the crater meets the little lake created by the lifestream here. Directly ahead looms one of the support pillars of what used to be a wooden walkway when most of Mideel was still located above sea level. The bridge has collapsed into the lifestream and is the only part of the southern Mideel which is still reachable from here. Even so, one has to jump over a small rock platform to get to it.

On top of the crater there are the remains of the little clinic Mideel used to be well-known for. Now the few remaining medical practitioners, a nurse among them, have to treat people under the open sky because the roof and walls collapsed. It is possible to rest in one of the beds of the clinic.

All that remains of Mideel's materia shop is a set of stairs which leads up nowhere. It is possible to jump into the lifestream off them of course, even though a plunge into the green liquid would almost  certainly harm most lifeforms. A tradesman selling materia is standing on the stairs, with his limited selection it is doubtful he will be able to sell anything though.

Since the path to the clinic collapsed into the lake below, the only way to get there is jumping across a gap to the top of the crater wall. One slip could lead to a fall into the lifestream resulting in a severe case of Mako poisoning so it's best to be careful. Looking into the crater, the northern part of Mideel can be seen which has totally sunk into the lake.

There is a small forested area immediately surrounding Nikeah, making the town a bit more pleasant than it might be from the dismal climate.  The town's tallest buildings can be seen over and through the foliage, marking a general direction to the town's center.  The area outside the trees is most desolate in comparison, hardly a tree ight/ight, just tall grasses and strange beasts.

In the midst of harsh weather, ever-increasing numbers of monsters, and the long-lasting effects of Kefka's Light of Judgement, the city of Tzen still stands.  In every direction, however, the bleak landscape dominates the mood.  Although citizens can be heard going about their business in the town, no birds fly in these skies, nor probably ever will again.  The destruction Kefka unleashed may never be fully undone.

The chocobo shop smells strongly, acrid odors rising from piles of hay in the corners of the warmly-lit stable.  A small area at the entrance to the stable is roped off from the area where livestock is kept, and several large feathered birds strut around the stable making noises to each other.  An energetic caretaker is required to keep up with the birds, and the owner busies himself brushing down the yellow birds, checking their birds' food and water supplies, as well as cleaning their stalls.

A mighty work of masonry, this bridge spans between the Albrook Continent and the Serpent Trench.  Travellers came from far-off Albrook, Tzen and Nikeah to connect the two continents and allow travel between them.  Below the bridge, the ocean rushes by, and the supports that thrust up from the water are covered with a green mossy film.  This bridge acts as a save point, and one could rest here and set up camp if desired.

This place stinks of chocobos.  Which is no surprise to the observant, since there are a fair number of them being stabled in this small shop.  The birds are in pens, wearing leather saddles and ready to take customers anywhere their hearts desire.  Buckets of greens are scattered all over the place.  A wooden counter is along the wall by the door.

You are on the far western side of a long narrow room in the tyrano fort.  In front of you is a long stairway leading up.  You can see light streaming down from the top of the stairway, and you let out a sigh of relief knowing that you can get outdoors again and out of this wretched place.

You are in a dimly lit room, with grey tiles that cover the floor.  Some of these tiles are missing, and all you can see below them is pitch black, these bar travel in certain directions.  There is a line of windows along the wall far to the north, and there is a huge grey wall to the east.  Travel to the west is impossible due to missing tiles, and south to the door is the way back to the entrance.

You stand on a long stone bridge, heading across a chasm to a massive stone spire.  The spire is painted with depictions of some sort of event, but has no entry; this bridge is the highest accessible area.  The winds here are very strong, creating a very real danger of falling off.  At the south end of the bridge leads back into the lair.

You stand before a huge skeletal head of a reptile.  Its mouth is open, allowing you through to the next part of the fortress.  To the east of you is another one just like it with its mouth open too, leading to another part of the castle.  To the south is the way out of here, as you can see a doorway supplying light to the room.

rooms.name: Outside the lair, on a ledge

userData.LongDescription: You stand on a ledge towering about 300 feet above the ground on the Tyrano Fort, as you can see the top in plain view from here.  This ledge is wider than most, and you feel that the end of this voyage draws close.  To the east, you can see a part of the ledge going north leading to a huge door back into the lair, and far to the west you can spot another smaller door, leading into the fort as well.

You are just inside the fort, with a door just behind you leading back outside.  This room looks similar to many others here, with moss covering the floors and two bone cauldrons on either side of room, providing dim light.  There is another skeletal head here, serving as a door to the passage to the north.

You are in a small room, just behind the skeleton head door.  There isn't a whole lot here, aside from the regular fare of monsters.  Back to the south is a door that leads back to the ledge outside the lair.

This is the western end of a narrow ledge outside the Tyrano Fort.  A stiff wind blows here, threatening to blow you off the ledge.  Luckily, there is a large black door here leading back into the fort, and to safety.  This place provides nicely for the airborne monsters that live up here.

This room is barly lit by two bone cauldrons on either side of the room, allowing enough light to see by, but not much else.  There is a long grey staircase in front of you leading up to an even higher level of the Fort, and back to the south is a door leading outside.

rooms.name: In front of the Tyrano Lair
