userData.LongDescription: You stand in front of a huge black fortress that towers hundreds of feet above your head.  It has a huge black spire sticking out of the top of it, and you can only imagine what is at the top.  There is a large door in front of you, and you can hear all sorts of sounds coming from within.  This place gives you the creeps.

rooms.name: Outside the lair, on a ledge

userData.LongDescription: This is a fork in the roads, with exits all leading to doors back into the lair.  To the north is the biggest door, and it appears to be heavily guarded by foes, to the east and west are smaller doors, each leading to different parts of the lair.  From this vantage point, you can see almost all of the world, including the tiny village far to the west, it is spectacular.

This is a narrow balcony that is on the side of the fort, as you can see a sheer drop off to the south.  The ledge continues on to the east, where you can see another door leading back into the lair.  Terrasaurs are here in great numbers, as it seems to be and ideal environment for the airborne beasts.

This is the northeast corner of a large dark room, with tiles lining the floors.  To the southwest, the holes in the floor are too numerous for travel, but to the west and south you can spot ways through.  The north wall here is covered with huge windows that allow a small amount of light into the room, other than that this place is very dark and creepy.

This corner is the northwest part of a large, dimly lit room.  A thin crack of light is visible around the edge of a huge door.  To the south, many of the tiles on the floor to be missing, making travel impossible.  To the east is the way back down to the entrance of the fort.

You are standing just before another set of stairs that lead into the depths of the Tyrano Fort.  The stairs wind downwards into the blackness, leaving you no clue as to where they lead.  There is a large cell just to your west, and you can see that it is open from here.  A few more monsters linger here as well.

You stand in front of one of the cells in the fort.  There are some bones that serve as bars for the gate of the cell, but for now they are open, revealing a shadowy figure inside.  The the east you can see a stairway leading even deeper into the lair, and back to the west is the way back up.

You are in a long narrow dark chamber inside the Tyrano Fort.  A little ways to the north you can see a stairway heading up even farther into the lair, and to the south you can see a door leading back outside and eventually down to the bottom of the lair.  Moss covers the floor here, and you can see movements in the shadows giving you an eerie feeling.

You are on the top of a long set of stairs, and find yourself on a narrow ledge outside the lair.  Looking down you can see the base of the lair about one hundred feet below you.  The ledge continues on to the west, as you notice a door leading back into the lair there.  This place is perfect for flying adversaries.

You are just behind the skeletal head that you passed through earlier.  You can see a dark stairway heading down into the dungeons of the fort in front of you.  It is very cold and damp in here, the perfect environment for the kinds of creatures that live here.  There are some more monsters here as well.

This is a small dark room, behind a skeleton head door.  In this room stands the throne of the King Reptite.  Sitting on the throne is the king himself, and he appears to be guarding something.  The only exit is south, leading back out to the ledge you came from.

You are just inside the fort, with a huge black door that leads back outside just behind you.  The floor here is covered with moss, and just in front of you is one of those huge skeletal heads that you saw earlier.  There are two huge cauldrons of fire in the room, giving you the sense that this place holds some importance.

You are in a small room, with those familiar bone cauldrons on either side, provinding light to the room.  There is a huge black door in front of you, with a stream of light shining through the crack.  You get the feeling that you are almost at the top of the Fort, and that your goal is nearly within reach.

rooms.name: On a ledge, outside the Lair

userData.LongDescription: This is a small windy ledge that is very high up in the Tyrano Fort.  You would guess that this ledge is some 200 feet above the entrance of the lair.  The ledge continues on to the east of you, where you can spot two more doors that lead back into the lair.  Behind you is a door leading back to the stairs from which you came.

rooms.name: A small room in the tyrano lair

userData.LongDescription: Two huge torches, constructed from tyranosaur leg bones, light the corners of this small room.  Aside from a pair of egg-shaped containers, little else adorns this room.  The ceiling is maybe thirty feet high, and the iron gate of a door leading out to the balcony is sized to match.

rooms.name: Outside the Lair, on a ledge

userData.LongDescription: The eastern end of the ledge rises high above on the side of the fort, butting up against the mountain the fortress is built into. An imposing door leads into a room detached from the rest of the lair. Far below the cusp of the ledge, a dactyl can be seen waiting at the gate. The path along the fortress to the west leads to two doors, each leading back into different parts of the fortress proper.

This is the east end of the ledge outside the fort.  Peering down, the ground is visible hundreds of feet below.  There is a huge black door here that leads back into the Fort and, undoubtedly, to more monsters.  There are more Terrasaurs here as well, attempting to knock you off the ledge.

The temperature just inside the entrance of the Tyrano Lair descends at a frightening rate, levelling out to a stark contrast from the hot and humid weather outside.  The floor is made out of small black bricks, extremely smooth to the touch.  There is very little lighting, no doubt to the benefit of the denizens of this place.

You are inside a small dark cell, with nothing much here except the way out.  Some monsters lurk in the shadows here, as this cell doesn't seem to be in use right now to hold prisoners captive.  Leaving the cell leads back to the main part of the lair.
A portly Terrasaur waddles about, its belly jiggling with each step.

You stand before a dark cell that seems designed to hold someone captive.  The bars are made of the ribcage of some massive beast.  Other than entering the tiny jail cell, the only other option seems to be going back to the east, and returning to the higher levels of the Fort.

rooms.name: On a ledge, outside of the Lair

userData.LongDescription: You are in the center of a balcony off the side of the Tyrano Fort.  To either side of you there are doors that lead back into the fort, but directly in front of you is the biggest door, you get the feeling that it has the most importance.  This place provides an ideal location for the flying beasts that lurk here.

You stand just behind a huge skeleton head that stands in the passage to the south, giving you an eerie feeling.  It is cold and damp here, but you notice a small amount of light coming from the stairway to the north.  There are more enemies here as well, standing in the way of the stairs.

You are in a dark corner of the dungeon, as the only exits are north and west.  You can see a huge guard blocking the cell entrance to the west, as you figure that someone very powerful must be held in there.  Moss grows up and down the walls here, and there is hardly any light making it a perfect environment for monsters.

You stand in a huge well lit room, that appears to be the main room of the Tyrano Fortress.  There is a huge bone throne in the center of the room.  Behind the throne is a passage to a bridge outside, which appears to be the lair's summit.

This is a small, dark corner of the fort, just east of the entrance.  It's impossible to make out what is to the north, due to the extreme darkness, but a cold stone wall curves to the east and south.  There are more monsters here lurking in the shadows, ready to defend whatever is at the top of this horrid place.

Before you is a huge skeleton of the head of a reptile.  You can make out a similar one to the west.  Both of them have their mouths open, giving you access to further reaches of the fort.  Their eerie presence gives you the sence of uneasiness as you continue in the fort.  There are more creatures here as well, looking very vicious.

You are in a small rectangular room with little light, save the small sliver of light streaming through the stairway just in front of you. Behind you is a door that leads to the way back to the entrance of the fort, but just in front of you is an upwards leading stairway that will take you back outdoors.

This is the lowest level of the Tyrano Lair, as far as you can tell.  It is very dark and cold down here, and there is barely enough light to see.  You can make out some moss growing on the floor, as this area is not visited often. There appears to be another smaller cell to the west, as well as some monsters lurking in the dark.

This is the east side of a long passage in the Tyrano Lair.  There is a stairway in front of you, with light streaming down from it, as you can make out the sky as you peer up the stairwell.  To the west there are two more stairs, leading to different parts of the fort.

This is a narrow passage leading along side of one of the cells.  The way to the east leads in front of the cell, and it looks as though you could enter it in that direction.  Back up the stairs will take you to the first floor of the fort.  There are more hulking apes here to bar your way.

rooms.name: Outside the lair, on a ledge

userData.LongDescription: You are in a corridor of sorts, with two stone walls towering on either side of you.  Monsters are poised all around here to prevent you from entering the huge black door that stands just feet in front of you.  To the south is a split in the road, with doors on either side, allowing for access to other areas of the Fort.

rooms.name: Outside the lair, on a ledge

userData.LongDescription: You are on the eastern edge of this ledge that protrudes from the side of the Tyrano Fort.  In front of you is a door leading into the lair, but more importantly there is a huge door to the northwest that seems to lead to the foremost room in the lair, farther west is another smaller lair that leads into the fort as well.

Packed dirt and sturdy stone walls form the lower level of the Chocobo Sage's house.  A wooden frame with a small gate encloses a chocobo hutch in the west corner with a convenient drinking trough adjacent.  Stairs on the east side of the room lead up to a wooden loft.

A cozy loft overlooks an indoor stable, connecting via stairs.  Well insulated and articulated wooden construction is broken only by a wide, stone hearth projecting warmth and light from the northeastern corner.  A tapestry of a chocobo hangs near the mantle while extensive shelving on the north and east walls holds a variety of pots, pans, books and trinkets.  A long table astride the loft's railing is impeccably clean, matching the detailed organization of the baubles in the house.

In contrast to much of the surrounding ice and snow, a lone house occupies a small grassy area at the foot of the mountains.  The house frame is rectangular, with a steeply pitched roof made of green slate tiles.  A chimney occasionally pipes thin wisps of smoke into the crisp mountain air.  Whomever lives this remotely must live a rather reclusive existence, judging by the elevation and grade of the mountainous terrain quickly reached in every direction.

This is a dirt path going north-south that stretches deep into the end of the Truce peninsula, which at the end contains the Zenan Bridge. Trees are planted around, decorating the place. The grass blows gently in the soft breeze. The sun shines brightly above, slightly covered by the great white clouds.

rooms.name: An L-shaped section in the path

userData.LongDescription: The dirt path takes into two directions here, south and east. To the east is a long road leading eventually into the town of Truce. To the south is the Zenan Bridge, the bridge that links two land masses together. Nearby is a dark opening leading deep into the Guardia Forest.

A row of brick houses line the western edge of the village. None of them hold particular interest, except for a lone one in the corner, resting at the foot of a tree-speckled mountain. The dirt path from here leads to the center of the village.

This is a well-kept kitchen. The tiled floors are squeaky clean, everything is in place. A stove rests against a wall next to a refrigerator. It looks quite different from the kitchens around town, being more refined and mechanical, for example the toaster, microwave and the oven.

rooms.name: A bend in the path of dirt

userData.LongDescription: The dirt road takes a turn here, leading further south into the village center. Trees surround the area like a wall of wood, preventing any easy access other than what the path gives. The sun shines brightly, giving warmth and a fresh feeling. To the east is the Millenial fair's entrance.

This is a well-kept bedroom. Everything's clean; the bed is made, the curtains folded open, and the sun shining through. The floor is swept and wiped clean, the glass of the window shiny and sparkly. Whoever owns this room must have a strong sense of cleanliness.

rooms.name: In front of a large house

userData.LongDescription: This house is large, composed of two floors. It's easily the size of a small mansion, even set on a small island off of the mainland. The walls are made of a fine stone, with large framed windows to show its elegance. Stone steps are placed before a grand set of double doors. To the north is a long wooden bridge that leads back to the mainland.

This is a pretty decent-sized house, well-kept and in good condition. Nearby is a couch for guests, with little family pictures hanging on the wall. Beyond that is the kitchen and dining area with a wide oak table  and accompanying chairs in the center. The kitchen is right next to the table, with the usual range of cooking and washing utensils.

This is a long pier leading to a small hut. The ferry lies anchored just nearby, ready to take people all the way south to Porre. The waves in the sea lap and overlap against the pier, and seagulls squawk against the crashing of the waves. An almost silent wind blows softly.

The house nearby is rather large in comparison to the others in the village, with a second story to it. Just to the east is the coast, with the infinite sea lapping and overlapping the beach nearby. A few trees dot the area here, providing some shade from the sun.

rooms.name: A bend in the dirt path

userData.LongDescription: A sharp turn in the road just out of the village, leading to the west and north. Trees are lined around, creating psychological barriers and discouraging people from straying off the path. To the north is the village of Truce, a nice, quiet village. To the west is the main road, leading to different places.

The interior of the house... certainly does not reflect what it looks like outside. Junk pieces of machinery are scattered around on the wooden floor, while books and other bits of mechanical wonder are stacked high above. A large table filled with blueprints and other sorts of schemes is in the center of the room. Capsules and other machines are lined against the wall... what kind of person owns this house, no one knows for sure.

This is a small, one-room house. The floor and walls seem to be rather poor and crude, chipped away and wearing out with time. The windows are slightly cracked, sloppily placed together, and thin curtains are hung to shut out the sunlight. A small lightbulb hangs from the ceiling, providing a little bit of light. The room is messy with clothes, food and other sorts of junk scattered around the place. This is truly the home of a poor person.

This is a rather small corridor connecting different rooms in the home. In particular, stairs to the west and east can be seen, connecting to two different rooms. Doors are placed on the north and south walls, leading to different rooms as well.

This is where travelers and people book their ferry tickets, though right now it's out of use as the ferry is free. A counter is set on one part of the room, couches and tables on the other as a courtesy for waiting customers. There isn't a lot to do here, much like any other booking office.

This inn is the finest establishment there is in Truce, not to mention being the only one around, too. Doubling as a tavern, it is also a place where people meet and have a good time in. A large counter is set on the eastern side of the inn, with barstools set in a row next to it. A piano rests on the corner, and to the direct north is the inn receptionist desk. A small sign hangs next to the desk.

rooms.name: A general store in Truce, 1000 AD

userData.LongDescription: This store looks rather small compared to the building outside. A small porch for customers is placed, with stools, tables, and magazines as common courtesy. Swords, guns and other weapons are lined up on a rack, and a large cupboard filled with medicine is on the wall. This store looks to be a general-purpose store.

The peninsula comes at an end here, connected to the large Zenan Bridge that spans the gap between Truce and Porre. The grass wavers gently in the breeze while the sun shines brightly down upon the land. Far to the south past the bridge is a road leading into a great forest. Shrubs line the dirt path like a thicket.

Nearby stands a large, wide building. A wooden sign hangs just above the doorway, with a sword and gourd symbol on it. To the east is a fork in the path, leading to the center of the village. Down to the south is a long path leading out of the village, to perhaps adventure and other wonders.

This is the center of the small village. A fountain of stone is nearby, and grass coats the land all around. All around the square are dirt paths that lead mostly to different houses. The coast is visible to the east, along with a fairly large two-story house that might provide some interest.

This is a cozy little bedroom in the two-story house. The flooring and walls are made out of quality wood. Nearby, stairs lead down to the first floor of the house. A bed stands on the eastern corner of the room, and heavy, thick curtains block the light from filling this room. There seems to be quite a lot of miscellaneous junk in here. A large dresser stands on the corner of the room.

The path takes a few turns here. To the south is a long wooden bridge leading to a huge house in the center of an island. The path leads to the west as well, leading along the great forest known as the Guardia Forest. The sun envelops the area in its warmth, creating a peaceful atmosphere.

A dirt path stretches out through the wide area surrounded by bundles of trees. Just to the south is Truce, a bustling, busy-looking village. To the north is the village square, named after a past Queen of Guardia, Leene. Currently it hosts the Millenial Fair, a spectacle of entertainment for all the villagers and travelers nearby.

This small bedroom is rather ordinary in size and furniture, with a bed on the corner, a large window on the northern wall with thick curtains and a few other things of necessity. However, nearly everything is cluttered with paper! Research notes, ripped diary entries, everything is scattered about.

This is the southernmost part of town, another row of houses lining the coast to the south. Two buildings are of particular interest here. One is an inn, with a large 'INN' label hanging by its doorway, as well as a blue-roofed house with a sign standing outside. A long pier lies to the east, with a large ferry sitting near. The path also branches to the west, leading out of the village to maybe more means of adventure and interest.

Most of the ground in this area is littered with rocks and gravel.  A worn path leads to the southeast, to a small clearing.  A path also leads to the north, but appears a little less used.  The grass has grown a little thicker here than some of the other parts of the forest, and slightly impedes movement.  A small butterfly flutters around one of the flowers on the ground.
Birds chirp peacefully in the trees surrounding this clearing, filling the air with a slight sense of serenity.  Bright flowers form a fragrant carpet on the ground.  A path leads northeast.

Paths stretch out in three directions from this point.  All that are visible besides the occasional rock or bush are trees.  Lots of trees. A large group of them stands to the north, while they also block movement to the west.  It is somewhat strange that the Royal Family of Guardia would put up such a large buffer between their castle and Truce.

The trees here form an impassable barrier to the east, south, and north.  The only way to travel in or out of this area is by two paths cut to the west and the southwest.  The paths themselves are faded and occasionally aren't even visible.  This area of the forest seems a little less traveled.  A lone bush stands just outside of the northern wall of trees. Every now and then, a brown flash of fur is visible, but soon disappears.

The thick forest is cut away here enough to form a large arc. The dirt path follows almost straight through the middle of the cleared space. A patch of flowers are in plain view, surrounded by tufts of greenery.  The only exits are those of the arc, northeast and southeast.

The majestic Guardia Forest spreads out as far as the eye can see.  Birds chirp quietly in the trees, while small woodland creatures race around the treetops.  A large rock lies imbedded into the ground here.  The trees are rather thick to the east and west, but directly ahead a path has been cut.  The entrance to the forest lies to the south, leading back to the main Truce road.

The castle of Guardia can clearly be seen from this edge of the forest.  The woods thin out towards the north, where the path leads to the castle.  The trail also can be followed to the southwest, deeper into the forest.  A winding track leads east to what seems to be an empty clearing, blocked by a group of brambles and rocks.  By your feet stands an old oak sign.

This small clearing is densely surrounded by trees.  The entrance, in fact, is barely visible among the thick tree trunks.  However, it doesn't appear possible to exit through it, due to the large wall of brambles and other objects.  All that is in this clearing, in fact, is a solitary gate.  The whole clearing is lit up by its eerie blue glow.

The trees in this area of the forest form a dense wall, making further movement north impossible.  Small tufts of grass shoot up here and there among the roots of the trees, and there is the occasional flower scattered among them.  A rough dirt path that looks like it has been used often leads to the east.  The path has faded off to the southwest, but still looks passable.

The fragrant smell of flowers is highly recognizable in this small clearing.  Large purple blooms grow all over the ground here, causing a sense of peace and serenity to hang in the air.  A few large rocks are scattered in the grass.  A large bush on the north side of the clearing shakes slightly as the wind picks up.  The only way out of the clearing appears to be through the path to the northwest.

The wall around the raised area turns south here, running into the line of trees and creating a dead end.  The grass has been recently cut, creating a nice, safe haven for children to play.  The grassy area continues back to the east toward the town's entrance, where a flight of stairs leads up into the main area.

A corner is formed here by walls to the west and north holding up the raised platform.  The western wall forms a large shadow over most of this section of road.  Small gray mice scamper across the pavement in search of food.  A group of mice is huddling in the corner, trying not to be noticed by the citizens of Tzen.

A flight of stairs leads down from the mansion entrance to this road.  The lower story of the mansion is being repaired to the north.  The mansion continues to the west, and this road follows in front of it, but the road doesn't actually lead to anywhere except a patch of grass and the edge of town.

An old man stands behind a wooden counter, ready to serve his customers.  The floor is carpeted with a gaudy red and gold throw rug.  Looking at the floor for too long could easily make a person dizzy.  An oak chair sits near the counter, theoretically for customers to sit in, but one of the armrests has been broken off, and the chair's cushions have been removed to help make the shopkeeper's seat more comfortable. A small sign hangs in front of the counter.

The lower floor of the huge mansion blocks the way north, continuing to the east and west.  This road follows it, leading in front of the mansion from the mansion's front door to the east to a dead end to the west.  This road doesn't really go anywhere, making it look as though the city planners didn't really know what they were doing when they designed this part of town.

This rather ordinary gravel path runs throughout the town of Tzen, connecting all of the stores and other buildings.  The road here is rather boring, consisting of the ground between the item shop and a ledge to the north.  This part of the road doesn't really seem to lead to anything.  There is a large, open plaza to the east.

Tzen was one of the last towns Kefka smashed during his reign of terror, and the repairs are not quite finished.  This part of the road used to be part of the item shop, until it was levelled.  The wall has been fixed, but the shop is somewhat smaller now than it was before the world collapsed, due to Kefka's Light of Judgement transforming the bathroom into a sidewalk.  The repairs are only superficial, and the side of the building looks as though it might collapse in a heavy rainstorm.

The sounds of a busy town can be heard all around.  Some birds perched on the town's outer wall chirp happily.  This part of the road serves as a kind of main plaza for the town of Tzen, being the largest unobstructed paved area in town.  A narrow alley to the south leads past the item shop to the town entrance.

This short, narrow alley does not appear to lead anywhere except to a dead end.  A brick wall to the north holds up a flight of stairs leading to the inn.  To the south is a guardrail guarding a ledge overlooking some thick trees, but it is too far down to jump.  This alley looks like it would be dangerous to be trapped in.

The town of Tzen is a small refuge from the harsh conditions outside.  The Light of Judgement has obviously hit this town more than once, judging from all the holes in the roofs of buildings and other heavy damage to the town.  To the north, a mansion is being rebuilt from the ruins of what it once was.  A flight of stairs leads up into the main part of town.

This road is small and narrow enough to be considered an alley.  It creates a path between the town entrance and an open road to the north.  The burnt-out item shop, which can be entered to the south of here, blocks the path west.  The Tzen inn hangs overhead, accessible via a flight of stairs to the southeast.

This road, high above the ground, is the home of Tzen's weapon and armor shops.  A small building at this end of the road is clearly marked as a weapon shop, while the armor shop seems to be further to the northeast.  The weapon shop, quite oddly, has no windows.  The owner apparently favors to simply not repair the large hole in the building's roof.

A table with one chair sits in a corner for guests to use. Standing behind the counter is the innkeeper, an old woman with a friendly smile.  Through a small door, some warm-looking beds invite travellers to stay here the night.  A fireplace burns near the beds with a kettle hanging over it, and whatever is being cooked in the kettle smells delicious.  A sign is on the counter.

The pleasant grassy path continues to the east and west.  A brick wall to the north marks the beginning of the main raised section of town.  A thick line of trees to the south prevents wild animals and monsters from approaching the park, and also helps keep any children who decide to play here from venturing out too far.

rooms.name: In Front of the Tzen Mansion

userData.LongDescription: The huge building that could be seen from the town entrance sits just to the north.  Repairmen hustle about, restoring this mansion to its original glory.  The door to the mansion has not yet been attached to the building, allowing free access in and out of the front door.  To the west, a set of stairs leads parallel to the mansion down to another road.

The item shop to the south is the most interesting aspect of this part of the road.  A sort of plaza in this part of town serves as a place for citizens to congregate during the day.  The plaza continues to the east and north.  The sidewalk narrows to the west to curve around the item shop.

This is the site of the armor shop of Tzen.  The front door of the shop is open, and the shopkeeper can be seen inside straightening his merchandise.  A yellow sign with a picture of a shield hangs beside the door of the armor shop.  Some cute little white flowers in the window seem somewhat out of place for a building that sells tools of war.

With a weapon shop just to the southwest and an armor shop just to the north, this is easily the busiest place in Tzen.  The ever-increasing monsters outside the town force every citizen to make sure he or she is armed at all times, and as a result the weapon and armor shops do a lot of business.  The brick road here is different and newer looking than the stone flooring on the roads below, having been repaved recently.

Looking down the stairs here, one can see most of Tzen.  Directly below is a plaza where citizens congregate during and after business hours to socialize and discuss business.  The relic shop can be entered from here.  It is also possible to walk to the north around the relic shop though a small grassy area.

Boxes lined up against the left wall hold the various merchandise sold by this armor shop.  Not one, but two metal signs with pictures of shields are nailed to the wall, just in case anybody comes in not knowing that what kind of a store this is.  An old woman waits for customers from behind a short wooden counter.

An ugly rug depicting a red, yellow and green pattern covers the floor in fron of the counter.  Two chairs rest along the east wall for weary travellers to sit in.  A pile of crates and chests lines the back wall behind the relic shopkeeper.  A clock adorns the back wall as well.  The shopkeeper herself sits patently at the counter, waiting for customers.

This grassy path is a few meters below the main area where most of the business in Tzen takes place.  It seems very peaceful in this small grove, secluded from both the dangerous outside world and the busy business section of town above.  This path has been turned into a kind of children's park for the youngsters of Tzen.

This section of road overlooks the small field to the east below the main road.  Some young children are playing happily in the grass there, hooting and hollering and running around.  Two sets of stairs can be seen from here, one to the northeast and one to the south.  Both lead up to a raised section of the road which Tzen's weapon and armor shops rest on.

The road continues to the north toward the old mansion.  A set of stairs here leads up to the weapon and armor shops.  South of the road is a sort of grassy park surrounded by trees where children can be heard laughing and playing in the small field.  To the east is the dilapidated item shop and the town entrance.

This part of Tzen seems to be particularly busy, with many citizens hustling to and fro.  Not surprising, since both the weapon and armor shops are rather close.  A stairwell leads up to the shops, both of which seem to be doing quite a lot of business.  The stairs are chipped and worn from years of use.

This main area of Tzen is several meters above the town entrance.  A set of stairs leads down to the edge of town and a small park.  The rather small  building at the top of the stairs seems to be some sort of store, judging from the sign next to the door.  To the east, an inn is set up on a second platform even higher than this one.  A large mansion is being rebuilt to the north.

This is part of a plaza in Tzen where citizens spend some of their time.  There is a large pothole in the road, and a family of mice has made its home in the hole.  A flight of stairs leads up to the relic shop which hangs overhead.  The stairs are cracked and chipped from previous trauma that Kefka unleashed on this town.

To the north, a huge mansion is under repair.  It appears to have been completely destroyed at some point, and is being rebuilt from scratch.  Repairmen walk around the building carrying tools and paint.  The road south from the mansion leads to this plaza where townspeople congragate during the day.  A ledge to the west overlooks another, lower road that passes in front of the mansion.

The road does not continue this far, and there is grass covering the ground at this dead end.  This part of the mansion has already been finished, and the construction is centered more to the east.  The mansion comes to an end here, but the way further west is blocked off by a thick line of trees marking the edge of town.

The grass here has grown exceptionally tall, almost knee-high, having not been cut by the relic shop owner in some time.  Apparently whoever runs the shop doesn't think people need to walk through his backyard.  Trees surround the path and prevent any further passage.

Tzen's inn seems to be in fairly good condition.  White flowers rest in the window, and a cozy-looking sign lets travellers know that this is a place where they can stay and rest.  Something is being cooked inside, and a sweet aroma fills the air.  A group of pine trees helps to create a barrier between this area of town and the overworld to the east.

A steep set of stairs leads up to an inn.  Although it is hard to see clearly from this angle, the inn seems to be in fairly good shape.  A sweet aroma flows down the stairs, inviting travellers to stop and visit.  A narrow alley east of here passes to the south of the stairs and then quickly comes to a dead end.  To the west is the entrance to the town.

The relic shop sits to the southwest, blocking the way west here.  The ground here is carpeted in lush grass which somehow survived despite the world's fall.  Trees line the eastern edge of this path, creating a barrier between the town and the outside.  The grassy path extends to the north, where it ends.

Tzen's weapon shop carries an array of claws and swords from around the world.  Tzen is proud of its assortment of elemental weapons, and they are shown off proudly on the wall behind the counter.  A small list of the weapons sold here is posted on the wall.  The exit leads back out to the street.

This rather ordinary road runs from the stairs leading up to the armor shop toward the large mansion to the north.  A path shoots between the shattered form of the item shop to the east and the wall holding up the armor shop to the west.  To the north, the form of a large mansion is visible.  It seems that the mansion is still under repair, as workers can be seen painting the outer walls.

The mansion that originally stood here a few years ago was flattened, and the new one is apparently still under construction.  Although this part of the hallway is completed, further west the wall is not quite finished, and there are bricks scattered across the ground.  To the south, stairs can be seen leading down.

'Under construction' doesn't begin to describe this end of the hallway.  Quite simply, there is no wall here.  A single corner support holds the roof up where the corner of the wall will eventually be.  It is possible to walk outside, but there's a large cliff a few feet past the edge of the building, and it would be unwise to fall down it.

This hallway leads out of the bedroom to the north and into the series of hallways to the west.  This particular hallway is redundant, and even connects with the hall to the north of the bedroom, but its meaninglessness has a certain luxurious charm.  At least it's supposed to, anyway.

This northern part of the dining room has a plain tile floor with no rug or cover.  A vase of giant roses sits cheerfully in the corner.  A cozy fireplace heats the room, and a kettle hangs over the fire.  A window in the north wall is shuttered closed; the view wouldn't be that great anyway, with the ruined world as it is now.

The main room of the basement consists of a large open lower area with pretty much nothing in it and an upper area with a dining room.  A short set of stairs goes up into the upper area.  The ceiling is about fifteen feet above the floor of the lower area, but a more normal nine feet high from the floor of the upper area.  The floor here is beautifully carpeted, but no other decorations can be seen.  The lower area expands to the east and west.

The entrance to this mansion is rather well-decorated.  A number of lamps hang on the walls, rather redundantly since there is no front door to keep light from coming in.  A fine table sits in one corner of the room, with a large potted plant resting on top of it.  Two expensive-looking urns sit by the side wall, and an uncomfortable but very nice chair stands next to the door into the next room.  A carpet covers the floor.

This corridor is very plain for being in such a nice house.  There is no furniture, and the only thing on any of the walls is a single lamp to illuminate the area.  The walkway is straight with no doors, but rather wide for a hallway, big enough to fit three people side by side.

During the construction of the mansion, this room is being used to store things that will eventually go elsewhere in the house.  Boxes and crates cover the floor, and a number of large pieces of furniture need to be assembled before they can be put in their proper places.  There is more storage to the west, and a flight of stairs leads to the lower floor, if one can maneuver through the maze of boxes to get to it.

This room contains the stairs leading back up to the main level of the mansion.  There is nothing in this room except the stairs leading up, a door into the main basement room, and a lamp.  The room is as big as a small bedroom, which seems like a ridiculous waste of space.

This mansion has a network of hallways on this floor connecting the dining room, the bedroom, and the stairs to the lower level.  Many of the hallways are not needed, but perhaps the owner thinks they add to the sense of luxury of the house.  To the east, the kitchen warms the whole house and the dining room seems to invite guests to enter.  The bedroom is accessible to the south.

This raised area is like a cross between a stage and a dining room.  A rail guards the edge of the floor to the south, looking out over the rest of the basement like an auditorium.  An antique wardrobe and chest line the north wall, the wardrobe blocking a window in the wall from opening properly.

This long section of the basement seems like a kind of mini-auditorium, except that the raised area that should be the stage is set up as a dining room.  The would-be auditorium continues in both directions.  A wall tapestry depicts an artist's interpretation of the War of the Magi.

Stairs leading up to the dining room and an open door into a room to the south are pretty much the only features of note in this part of the basement.  The same extravagant carpeting covers the floor, and desperately needs to be cleaned, as the ongoing construction has created a lot of thick dust and small debris.

There are two beds in this western part of the bedroom.  A large phonograph rests merrily in the corner, but for all its elegance, there is no disc to play, making it rather useless.  The beds themselves have white linen sheets and fluffy comforters stuffed with chocobo feathers.  An old chest is unlocked, but alas, contains clothes rather than treasure.  Which is to be expected in someone's bedroom.

From the far end of the room, it is almost impossible to see up to the dining area.  The brick wall holding the stage up is not finished yet at this end, and it's obvious that the bricks are fake, only an inch thick, glued to the wall.  A high window looks out to the grasslands beyond Tzen.

This part of the storage room is actually more cramped than the area to the east, if that were possible.  Everything from potted plants to art supplies is piled up high with no attempt at organization.  There is no light in this room; if there is a lamp on the wall anywhere, it is obscured by all the junk.

This long hallway stretches north and south to either end of the house, connecting the two main corridors.  The walls in this part of the house are totally unadorned, giving a less-than-extravagant feel unbefitting of such a nice mansion.  A pair of lamps hang from the ceiling, but are unlit.  All in all, this is a rather gloomy section of the mansion.

This part of the basement is set up like a small dining room, and is remarkably plain despite being the focal point of the area.  A small table that could seat two people stands here.  A fireplace built into the back wall has no place to put logs or start a fire, though it is unclear whether it is not finished being made or is intended to just be a decoration.  The lower basement spreads out below, looking for all the world like some sort of theater.

This small kitchen is connected to the dining room to the east.  The kitchen is not very complex, consisting of a stove and a small table.  The stove is wood powered, and a pipe coming out of it goes through the outer wall to let smoke out.  The wooden table is covered in chopped onions.

This part of the mansion is decidedly unfinished.  A gaping hole in the outer wall creates a breeze through the house.  Outside, through the hole, a set of construction worker's tools can be seen with a small hand-written sign resting on them.  The sign appears to have been sitting there for at least several weeks, judging from the amount of dust.

The pattern of the beautiful stone wall is broken here by a door leading to a stairwell.  The door is wide open for anyone to go in and out, and it's odd that there would even be a door for a room that just contains stairs.  This hallway continues to the west, where it looks like it ends.

The hallway ends here, but strangely, does not actually lead to anything.  There is no room at the end of the hallway, no door leading into the next area.  The hallway just stops.  The owner of the house has placed a desk against the end wall to make the area seem at least a little more useful.

This lower area of the main room is completely open, and looks like it could be used for dancing.  A large group of lamps on the wall here seems to be trying to make up for the dimness in the rest of the mansion.  A picture frame hangs from the wall, but there is no picture in it.

This portion of the bedroom contains one bed and a bookshelf stuffed with books.  The bed appears to be very comfortable, with soft covers and several pillows.  The bookshelf looks quite expensive, with intricate patterns carved all over it.  Rows of books line the shelves, mostly novels and poetry.

Two hallways intersect here.  The resulting space could almost feel like a real room if the unbroken wall to the south didn't jettison out, taking up much of the space that would otherwise exist.  There are no windows or lamps in this part of the house, but light from the intersecting hallways is enough to see by.

This room, unlike most of the rest of the mansion, is completely finished and decorated.  It is being used as an art gallery to display the finer pieces collected by the owner.  A silver vase, a portrait of a female knight, a beautiful antique grandfather clock, and a dozen other works of art are arranged about the room.

A large brown and tan braided throw rug covers most of this room's floor.  Right in the middle of the rug sits the dining table.  Chairs with comfortable-looking green cushions on the seats form a semi-circle around the table, which prominently displays a plain white tablecloth.

This is a very nice bedroom.  A beautiful flowerpot sits by the wall, filled with dried flowers. Two doorways lead out, one into the north hallway and one into the south hallway.  A lamp above the door dimly lights the large room.  The actual beds are against the sides of the bedroom in either direction.

This dining room doesn't seem like the kind of setup that would actually be used by the mansion's owners; almost every piece of furniture is an antique.  A wooden chest adorns the corner, while a wood stove inconveniently sits in the middle of the path to the east.  A large window takes up most of the north wall, and would be showing the barren fields behind Tzen were the shutter not closed.

The effect of being in a mansion is lost in this part of the house, as there is no furniture, no window, and not nearly enough light.  There is still some beauty in the place, though: the walls and floors are made of gorgeous limestone and marble, respectively.  It's amazing that the owner had the finances to rebuild the house with such expensive materials after the original building collapsed.  Perhaps they reused the stone from the wreckage.

Excitement can be felt in the air upon entering the Coliseum's Inn. Future hopefuls crowd the rooms and form tight lines around the check-in desk. A lot of chatting, and bragging, about the fights can be heard as future combatants prepare for battle.

Basically a simple stone room with a single, long wooden counter for wagering, this unadorned and unassuming room perfectly fits the cold, uncaring neutrality of battle that the Coliseum represents. Various warriors and other contestants wander in and out of this room at random, wagering, fighting, and on occasion being carried out on stretchers. There are only two ways out of here: the archway leading back to the entrance, and the giant bronze doors leading into the maw of death itself. A large sign hangs next to said doors with the rules.

The semi-circular stands provide an excellent view of the arena.  Trash from past bouts lay strewn about the various rows of seats along with other, less savory, reminders of previous fights.  While large in area, the stands are still cramped due to the enormous mass of fans packed into the seats.

Welcome to the Coliseum, where seekers of fame and fortune come to brave fierce monsters and test their luck and courage for the chance to win incredible prizes. The entranceway is rather stark; nothing but stone walls, an archway to the west leading into the wager room, and a red curtain to the east over which a placard reading "Infirmary" is hung. Warriors and potential contestants of all types wander through the area regularly. On the north wall, a large sign with the rules of the Coliseum is hanging.

This is a small cave on the rim of a massive crater.  There is some debris on the ground composed mostly of stone.  Amidst the rubble, a time gate crackles with unstable energy.  The ground is warm, and appears freshly disturbed.  It is possible to leave the cave, but there is nothing beyond except for a great crater.

An entrance to a massive dome is westwards. The treacherous wasteland surrounds the frozen area. Snow falls heavily and unendingly, covering the ground completely. In the distant north, the distinct figure of the enormous mountain can be seen. To the east, the ocean has not been liquid water for many years.

Precise, steel machine parts line the walls, waiting to be used. To the west, a massive computer screen towers over the rest of the room. The floor is covered with a combination of dust and oil, making travel difficult. Along the confusing eastern path, a wavering ramp is deteoriating into unusability.

To the far north, a huge computer screen can be seen. The ramp to the east is quite rusty. The lighting here is quite dim and seems to be fading away. Dark clouds of dust seem to float around. The winding path to the outside is westward. The bleak, steel wall blocks the way to the south.

The path finally comes to an end at the entrance to the monstrous mountain. The fog is everpresent, but the fierce winds have died down.  The walls narrow down into a single path, which leads into the heart of Death Peak. Some roars echo throughout the mountain.

The ancient, reflective dome to the north has seen many years of constant precipitation. To the east, a slippery path leads to the mountain. A glacier to the south is about ready to break off from the rest of the frozen continent. The winding, snow covered trail does not continue to the west.

A orange computer panel lies in the middle of the compact room. Dusty oil marks lead to the north away from the computer. The ramp to the west seems to be overly rusty. To the east, advanced, humming machinery can be seen and heard. The southern path leads back to the metallic entrance of the dome.

The steel wall blocks off all possible passage to the east. Ancient, deactivated robots line the walls to the north and south. The complex machinery in the center of the room hums quite loudly, and is glowing. Oil drips from the pipes above, forming a noticeable puddle on the path to the west.

A once-working robot lies unused on the western wall. Scattered computer parts and ramps form a confusing path to the east. The bleak, gray walls belie the years passing by. To the south, the blizzard is coming down impossibly hard. A small, antiquated computer is in the middle of the room.

Oil marks mar the western wall. A strange crest glitters on the door to the north. A large computer screen fills up most of the small room. To the east, scattered machine parts lie on the floor, waiting to be swept away. The southern path leads back to the inner parts of the dome.

The gargantuan, snow-covered mountain looms to the north. To the south, the winding, frozen road continues on. Scattered, broken robot parts line the chilly, eastern side of the road. A giant, icy crater looms dangerously to the west. The path is covered with a mixture of snow and oil.

The path stops at the dusty, metallic wall. Glowing buttons lie the eastern side of the room, beckoning to be touched. To the west, a ramp that leads to the rest of the dome can be seen. The floor is covered with sharp, rusty parts. The southern exit has been blocked off by broken down machines.

The snowy paths up the mountain are treacherous. Massive gusts of wind howl through the air, creating a thick fog cloud over the mountain. On the way up the path, only a few trees are visible. The edgy cliffs and razor sharp icicles stretch out into the fog, disappearing into nothing.

A widening, deepening crack in the ground lies to the east. Meanwhile to the west, the frozen, desolate ocean stretches to the horizon of the world. To the distant north, a gigantic snow-covered mountain can be seen. The unmaintained road to the south is full of various potholes and bumps.

The tangled path to the east seems to be covered by dull, grey snow that has been darkened by oil leaks. To the north, a massive, metallic dome can be seen. A snow capped mountain stands tall to the northeast. A giant, deep crater, formed by an meteorite, lies to the right side of the road.

A frozen barren surface is all that can be seen in every direction. To the east, an enormous, treacherous mountain looms over the landscape. To the south, the twisting road continues. A rusted steel ladder leads back down to the sewers below. The blinding, freezing snow blows in every direction.

The Epoch is a small vehicle made of an unknown metal, equipped with rocket boosters and a pair of wings, and endowed with the ability to travel through time. There are only three seats on board. On the main control panel is the time gauge of the Epoch, as well as a number of levers and buttons. To the left of the gauge, there are two small speakers and a microphone where a voice recognition system has been installed. On both sides, the Epoch's metallic wings are spread out. Compartments decorate the front of the Epoch. In order to start the voice program, please say 'hi'. This will load the automated system.

A rusty, eroding ladder leads up to the frozen, barren surface. There is barely any source of light here. At the bottom of the ladder is a cold, dark walkway, covered in mud and filth. The walkway is surrounded by aging walls and sewage while leading to the east and west.

There are faint footprints in the floor here. The ladder leads to the freezing surface. Brittle cracks in the decaying ceiling have cobwebs all over them. The mucky, gray walls surround to the west, east and south. A cold wind blows through. The northern path leads to the rest of the sewers.

A cat purrs quietly. The water flows alongside to the south. The floor has many cracks caused by the constant moisture in the air. The northern wall has been stained throughout the years by grime and the soaking of sewage. The sewers continue on to the east.

A grey trash can is in the middle of the path. The damp moisture in the air makes visibility quite low. To the west, the rest of the sewers beckon. The northern path leads back to the entrance. The darkened waters flow quietly to the south and east.

Large chunks of caterpillar feces lie around. Carapaces that have been shedded mark the room. The ceiling grates are bronze-colored with rust. Deteoriated robot parts litter the area, as well. The floor is greasy from the constant moisture eroding it. To the south, the entrance is approaching. To the west, the rest of the sewers await.

A bright red button lies just out of reach for normal human beings, but it looks like a jumping robot could hit it. To the south, a dim light brightens the dirty path. A bronze grate blocks passage to the north. To the southwest, a damp tunnel is there.

The dim lighting prevents vision more than eight feet around. The slippery floor prevents cautious motion. The slowly flowing waters quietly continue down. To the north, the sewage overwhelms the area. To the east, the path continues on.

Tiny spider webs hang from the ceiling. Refuse is scattered around on the ground, making the path treacherous and smelly. Leaking, tritium pipes hang from above.  A frog leaps along the path to the east. To the south, darkness and the caverns await.

The west is blocked by the walls and a grate of the sewer. The murky waters surround this room to the south. Back to the east, the rusty ladder can been seen. A somewhat clean diary lies open here, waiting to be read. A scurrying rat passes by, avoiding human contact.

The dark, unwelcoming walkway leads northwards. A small, eroded pebble marks the path. A slimy snake slithers around the floor, searching for food. To the west, a dim tunnel hides secrets. The bricks in the walls are slowly falling into the water.

An ancient ladder to the depths of the sewers leads downwards. The floor is covered in grime, however some footprints have been caught in the muck. The grate to the west seems to be falling apart while the dim lighting makes visibility quite low. A rusty bridge leads to the east.

A cluster of stars twinkles brightly. The exit of this level of the dirty, damp sewers is to the south. A metallic grate stands in the way of the path to the west. The northern waters flow westward, carrying the sewage on to the dilapidated filters.

To the west, the other side of this level of the sewers can be seen. Frog prints have been left on the floor. A steel ladder lies in the darkened room to the south. A sluggish turtle meanders around the room. To the east, the rest of the sewers await.

To the east, the decrepit bridge has fallen apart. To the south, filthy water has not been processed in quite a while, perhaps years. To the west, the rotting stench covers the entrance to the sewers. A foggy mist also surrounds this area.

A dark tunnel leads the way while visibility is low. To the northeast, a source of light is very faint. The western path returns to the more visible sewers of this level. The oily water is to the northwestern direction. The floor is covered with dirt and mud.

A switch that lies just out of reach for midsized creatures appears to be broken. The south passage leads to the rest of the damp sewers. To the east, the entrance and cleaner air await. The water here isn't any cleaner, but it almost seems as if creatures are living in the water.

This winding level of the sewers has ended. The eroding ladder leads upwards to the first level of the sewers. The oily waters seem to be still here, not moving or hiding secrets. A small, moss-covered rock marks the way back to the north.

The sewers go on and on, to the west and east. The southern waters flow slowly, and are still as rank as ever. The room is shadowed by access intakes on the ceiling and in the floor. Above is a ladder leading back upwards. Thumping sounds can be heard in the distance.

A toad slithers around the sludge. A broken switch is just in reach of human beings. The green, slime-covered wall blocks passage to the north. The eastern waters flow quietly beneath the surface. An open treasure chest occupies the side of the road.

A soda can stands straight. The bend in the room turns south, so the water now flows on the east and west. A turtle paces about the room. Grates, covering the tunnels, block passage to the north. The cold, embittered walkway to the sewers continues on to the east.

The moss-covered walls indicate that no one has been here for quite a while to maintain the walls. An antiquated ladder leads to the depths of the sewers. The northern path has a set of distinct footprints. A broken bridge leads to the east, but has no hope of being repaired.

A dying grey rat scurries about, trying to survive off what little food it can find. A foggy mist hovers over the room. To the north, a glimmering treasure chest sits on the grimy ground. The trail to the south reveals the dusky, shrouded caverns of the sewers.

A slow turtle slowly meanders around the room. A piece of moldy, aging cheese sits in the middle, waiting to be eaten. The path to the east leads back to the beginning of the sewers. To the west, the exit to this level of the sewers is barely visible.

You are at the western edge of this frozen continent, and on a path leading around a mountain range. Far to the north is a mountain, with what looks like a cave in the side. This path continues to the southeast around the mountain range.

rooms.name: Shop at the bottom of the cave

userData.LongDescription: You are at the bottom of the Terra cave.  Just to the east of you is a place that looks like there used to be a passage, but rocks now cover it. However, in front of you is a man who seems very skilled in making weapons.  He points to a sign above his head, and nods at you.

You are at another crossroads in the cave, with one path leading down into the cave even farther, and the other path heading into another home of the people of the village.  Back to the east you can climb up the way you came back to the entrance of the cave.  You can sense that the cave bottom is nearing.

rooms.name: Fork in the Terra Cave Tunnel

userData.LongDescription: Three paths lead out of this cavern, running to the south, northwest, and northeast.  Walls of damp earth run around the cavern, giving off a strong smell.  Thick green moss grows all over the walls and ceiling, while small pools of mud dot the ground.  The path to the south leads to another large cavern similar to this one, while those to the northeast and northwest lead down narrow tunnels.

You have exited the cave with the time gate, and find yourself in a frozen world.  The wind rips at your clothes, and snow flies at you in massive waves.  It is very possible that no one lives here at all, and that it may not even be worth exploring this frozen wasteland.  North and south of you are oceans, and to the east and west are small land masses.  Far to the east is a faint glow.

You are now at the entrance of a small cave, and away from the freezing wind of the outside.  For some reason, a staircase rises in front of you, leading further into the cave. Faint voices seem to be coming from it...could it be civilization?

You are at the western part of this continent, and you find yourself at a fork in the road.  To the north you can see a small cave in the side of a mountain, and to the south there is a small path which allows travel in that direction, around the mountain range.  You wonder if anyone could be living in this frozen world.

You are at the base of a set of stairs, and there is cave opening on front of you.  To the east of you, there is another ladder leading further down into the cave.  People here go about their daily lives, running by you, not taking any notice of you, entering and leaving caves.

You stand in front of another long ladder that goes even deeper into the village.  You notice the presence of the moss that covers the floors here, and wonder how it grows in such a cold place.  Back to the east is the way out of the cave, and as always there are more  villagers walking around here.

This is a small cave, with the wind howling inside of it.  You can see on the outside it is snowing and very cold indeed. There is a magical gate here that will take you back to the end of time.  It doen't look there is much here yet.

You are some ways west of the gate cave, and as you look around there is nothing but snow, mountains and ocean.  To the south there is a large mountain range hindering travel in that direction, and to the north there is ocean.  You think you can make out a small cave in a mountain to the northwest.

A moss-covered chain runs from a similarly covered rock up through a hole in the ceiling, towards a mountain floating in the sky above.  The cave is otherwise quite barren, with walls made of wet, compact earth.  The floor is composed of damp earth, with a handful of small mud puddles located in small dips in its surface.  A tunnel to the south leads down a short dirt staircase and into another cavern.

You are at the top of a long string of ladders downwards to the depths of Terra Cave.  There are villagers all about you, and they seem to be moping around.  There is a ladder right at your feet going down, and there is a huge cave opening in front of you, that you suspect someone lives in.

The smell of damp earth pervades this cavern.  Walls of dirt rise up to every direction but the north.  A small opening in the west wall leads out of this cavern and into another cave system.  Green, almost vine-like moss grows all over the walls, heavily concentrated towards the ceiling.  A tunnel continues northwards, leading to another large chamber of the cave.

You are standing on a small stretch of land that connects the two major landmasses of this continent.  To the northwest lies the cave with the gate that you came here with, and to the east is more of the continent.  You can see a strange glow clearly now coming from the east.

At the end of the path is a strange device with a beam of light shooting straight up out of it.  There's no way to tell what it is or what it does by looking at it, but it doesn't seem dangerous.  There is a pad on top of it as well.  This is the far eastern part of the continent; the only paths to take are to step onto the pad, or go back on foot.

This is nearly the bottom of the cave, and as far as you can tell, there is only one more level past this one.  To the east there is another cave that looks just like the other ones with families in them, and back up is the way out of the cave.  Also to the east there is another laddder that heads downwards.

You are on a small strip of land which extends into the ocean. There is a mountain in front of you on the land, and a cave is carved into the side.  It looks dead, and might be good shelter from the extreme cold of this place.

This is the top of the stairway in the cave, and there is a door directly north of you, proving that there is, or at least was, a group of people living here. Noises come from beyond the door. It seems much warmer here then south of you, as if there were fires burning beyond the door for heat.

Inside the freezing dark cave, against all odds, is a bustling village full of people.  These people look very simple, and are dressed all in rags, but they seem to be content with their lives.  Caves line the walls here, and the people of the village reside and work in them.

You are in a small part of land which is south of the mountain range. The only way out is the way you came in, to the northwest, as every other way is enclosed by the mountains or the ocean. There is nothing here of interest, and the temperature seems to be getting colder by the minute.

You are deep in the Terra cave, and you stand at the base of a ladder that heads upwards, back to the outside world.  The cave continues on to the west where you can spot another ladder heading down even farther into the cave.  There are more villagers here as well.

A set of stairs made from firmly packed dirt run from the floor to an elevated tunnel that runs through the northern wall.  Another tunnel runs southeastwards, leading to another cavern.  Green moss grows along the walls of thick, damp dirt that surround this chamber.  Small mud puddles are scattered about the floor, while drops of water fall from the ceiling.

You stand in front of a counter in the village inn.  A young woman stands behind the counter with an inviting smile on her face.  She points to a sign on her desk.  The beds here are made of some sort of soft mossy substance, and though it may not be the thing you are used to, they still get the job done.

This is a home in Terra cave, and there are more of the village's citizens walking about.  The home looks like every other one, with the basic, primitive appliances, and the simple chairs and tables. Back out is this earthbound village.

You stand at the top of the final stairway in Terra cave.  At the bottom you can see a man who seems to be guarding an assortment of very powerful weapons and armor.  In front of you is a cave with a sign hanging over it.  Somehow you imagine that it is not a home in this village.

This is a typical home in Terra cave, as some village people carry out their lives in this small, dirty cave. You look around and see all the necessities of life in their simplest forms: a makeshift oven, a few cupboards, and the such. Back outside of the cave is the main part of the village.

You are standing in another home in Terra cave, and there are more people of the village walking around here doing housework.  This cave is just like the ones you have seen earlier, with a simple stove and all the bare neccessities of life available.  Back out is the rest of the village.

rooms.name: Dead-end in the Terra Cave Tunnel

userData.LongDescription: This tunnel quickly narrows to a point, preventing any further travel to the north.  Small patches of mud lie underfoot, while thick clumps of vine-like moss grow out of the walls.  The dirt walls, floor and ceiling are all damp, and the smell of earth is strong.  A much larger cavern stretches out just to the southwest.
Between and underneath the boards on this wooden walkway is blackness. The boards here are dry and cracked, and look as if they should be replaced by some kindhearted person.
Here looks to be a good source of fresh, crisp outdoor air. A bright light is cascading onto the floor here, and the slight whistle of a windy mountainside is audible.

Clouds pass overhead here, and a strong breeze caresses the cliff face. The breeze swirls and whistles around rocks jutting out of the rocky cliff, giving a sense of dizzying heights. Grass grows stubbornly here, and looks as though it doesn't have an easy time staying rooted.

rooms.name: At the top of a stairway.

userData.LongDescription: Here is an oblong landing, and its secure flat ground offer a safe respite from the rickety wooden structures providing the ways in and out. The dirt is soft here, and the mist has all but vanished, leaving only the normal, moist atmosphere of a cavern.

rooms.name: The base of a long stairway.

userData.LongDescription: At the base of the long stairway, the cavern opens up more fully, and any sounds are echoed many times before disappearing. Visible only are the immediate surroundings, the rest disappearing in the lightless space. The walls are noticeably more wet here than near the entrance.

A wide, expansive platform opens up here, creating an intersection with multiple paths to choose. The mist here has dwindled to small wisps, and visibility is limited only by the darkness. Light is shed here by a beam of light coming down from the ceiling to the southeast.

Below and around here is more of the empty blackness, but now it is shrouded in a thick grey mist, dampening everything here. What little dirt on the floor there is has now turned to mud, and the exposed rock is glossy and slick.

A wall to the west blocks any further progress in that direction. Back to the east it gets lighter, and the dank smells rising from the blackness here are disgusting. It's possible that something dead is lying down there.

Above hangs the remains of an old wooden bridge. Some stairs lead down into the blackness, while a shadowed path leads to what looks to be a dead end. There are a few cracks in the dry, rocky earth here. The air feels a little bit damp further from the entrance to the outdoors.

rooms.name: At the top of a long stairway.

userData.LongDescription: Stairs disappear into the creepy blackness below, while the stench of mildew rises up. The air wafting up from below feels cooler, and more moist. Here a rich, earthy smell is prevalent, while the craggy, broken rocks create a nice sort of contradiction in perception.
Stunningly high up, this is the peak of the mountain. A majestic view encompasses all the countryside. Wind whistles about the rocks scattered here, and blows so hard that it mats the grass down.

Water is trickling from crevices in the rock walls, and there is a faint odor of must and decay here, as there is in all cavernous places. The brown rock on the floor is lightly covered with dark, rich soil. There is a beam of light shining in through the passage to the outdoors.

To the west is a long, narrow, creepy looking bridge. Parts of the shoddy thing look as if they are about to plummet downward. Where the stakes are tied down to hold the bridge up the rope is rotting and thin. The bridge to your east is in better condition, but not by much.

Bathing the floor, a shaft of light has erupted from a small gap in the ceiling. The moisture in the air is increasingly intense the further into the cavern, and it has become now a fine mist. Everything here is shimmering a bit with the moisture. Even the dirt on the floor is becoming a little soft with the wetness.

Through the thickening folds of mist is visible a strange twinkling blue light. It seems to grow and fade in intensity, and seems shapeless but gemlike at the same time. The ground around it is bathed in a silvery blue light, causing shadows to stand out from the smallest of pebbles.

rooms.name: At the top of a long stairway.

userData.LongDescription: Here there is a very small ledge to stand on, surrounded by darkness. The mist in the air has grown thicker yet, and it seems to be sinking into the blackness around the ledge.

rooms.name: On the landing between the stairways.

userData.LongDescription: Here is a simple and small landing between two sets of stairs leading up and down. The edge is frighteningly close, and as in the rest of the cavern so far, the wooden stairs here are creaking and weak.

The planks on this bridge heave and bend under any weight put on them, and seem to be just at their breaking point, even when holding nothing. On the sides of the bridge is nothingness; deep, continuous darkness.

rooms.name: At the top of a stairway.

userData.LongDescription: To the west is an old, rickety bridge that seems dangerous yet passable, except for the large break in the middle of it. It looks as though something fell down and broke a section right out. There are stone steps leading down into murky blackness.

This is Cyan's cavernous room. In the northwest part, a beam of light streams down, clashing silently on the floor. Arranged in the middle of the room is what seems to be a desk, with neatly arranged papers laid on top and a feather pen sitting in a bottle of ink. Behind the desk sits an ornate chair, neatly pushed in. There is a locked chest in the northeastern corner as well.

Coming from the northeast and proceeding to the east is a thin, rocky path. Here, the pathway curves to the east with the shape of the wall. The mist in the air seems to be thinning, but is still visible.

Here is a sharp bend in the walkway, leading to firm ground, and back into the midst of the blackness. It is difficult to say exactly how the structure of this walkway is suspended, as it is difficult to see far below it. The walkway seems to be hovering in midair.

Here is another part of a broken bridge, with just the middle missing. The rest of it is more or less intact, but too dangerous nonetheless to cross. The mist seems to be clearing here, and the light of day is visible just to the north.

Streaming down from the ceiling is another shaft of light, bathing the area in radiance. Another rickety bridge stands to your west. The air here smells fresh here, but the humidity is intense once again, despite being near a doorway to the outside.
The cavern walls here form a natural sort of hallway, enclosing into a low ceiling. The moisture evident earlier is not nearly as evident here, and the dirt is dry with exposure to the outdoor air.

rooms.name: At the bottom of a long stairway.

userData.LongDescription: Disappearing above are many stone steps, crumbling and cracking. The floor here has the vague shape of the letter L, proceeding north then east to the stairwell. Vision again is becoming difficult, as there is no light source around here, and the shadows seem to coalesce into life.

The air is dense with moisture, and it seems to be forming thin, wispy clouds. The clouds look to be getting thicker to the west, with a gradual decline in that direction. Leading off into the darkness is a southerly path. The ground here is beginning to get slippery with the moisture.

rooms.name: The bottom of a long stairway.

userData.LongDescription: Here the soil is softer, and seems more rich with life than atop the stairs. The air is thick with moisture, and smells richly. The steps disappear again into the darkness above, while below are a few more steps leading off of this landing. A few clusters of broken rock lie on the edge of the chasm leading indefinitely far down.

You are on the western side of a rocky outcropping, with some tough, small grass covering the ground. It thrives here, tucked in a more shielded part of the mountain. Wind whistles lowly, but doesn't blow directly on this side of the mountain.

rooms.name: Outside, the eastern side of a bridge.

userData.LongDescription: On this windy ledge, a rope bridge sways strangely with the gusts of wind. Its ropes are wearing down, but it looks passable. Grass clings tediously to life in small, knotty clusters. Small weathered rocks hold the bridge's ties down, keeping it anchored and preventing it from being blown away.

Staggeringly far below it is possible to see through the thick darkness a dead end near a broken bridge. The bridge ahead and behind is cracking and looks weak, but looks safer than the other bridges.
Here the earth is cracked and broken, and separates into two directions. Southwest leads off into misty darkness, and a short ramshackle bridge runs to the south.

A large, thick shaft of light is cast down through a small hole in the cavern roof far above. It brightens up the surroundings quite a bit. It becomes easier to pick out individual pebbles from the dark brown mass on the ground, and the water shines as it trickles slowly down the walls. A bridge runs its path off to the west.
This is the eastern side of a rocky outcropping on Mount Zozo. Grass grows thickly here, despite its hardy nature. Wind whistles around, but does not blow directly in this niche of the mountain.

rooms.name: Outside, on the western side of the bridge.

userData.LongDescription: On the ledge here is about the same setup as there is on the other side. The bridge is in usable condition, but could stand repairs. Two more small rocks anchor the bridge down while clusters of the same small, hardy grass grow in little crevices in the rock.

Streaming down from above is a beam of light, illuminating the surroundings quite well. It is quite walled in here, the only exit being the entrance. The rock walls seem to tower up and over the area, creating somewhat of a domed ceiling.
Through the unbearably thick mist, long and deep scratchmarks are etched into the walls here, and clawprints cover the floor. Embedded in the floor is what looks to be a large depressed metal button.

This is the Mana Fountain of the Tree, Dryad's element. The room glows a bright green, marking the colors of mother nature. Large, fat torches glowing with a green flame are placed around. The Mana seed of the Tree elemental has been stolen and is missing from it's place on the top of the fountain.

This part of the Tree Palace has been modified by a certain cat merchant to suit his stores. A piece of the wall on the palace is gone, replaced by a locked stash of merchandise. A counter is set along the alcoves on the wall. Other than the store outlet, there seems to not be anything else of interest around. A sign is planted down onto the ground nearby.

This is a large square platform that could've once been the grounds of a battle. Three paths, west, south and east can be seen from this point, although the eastern path is blocked out due to the lack of a connecting platform. To the west is a looping path leading up to the Seed room.

The narrow path of stone takes a bend to the south at this point, eventually leading to a set of stairs, leading up to where the Mana seed of the Tree elemental rests. Beneath the pearly white stone platforms are black stone floors. To the east is a large stage platform, wide and flat.

Pure elemental energy suffuses this realm, to the extent that nearly nothing else exists.  There are no perceivable floor, walls, ceiling, just mana.  It is a realm beyond mortal comprehension, and is where the most powerful of elemental beings reside.

This is a grassy cliff on the northern edge of the Tree Palace, overlooking the eternal blue sea. Waves crash against the cliff face endlessly. A few seagulls fly overhead, squawking, almost adding to this ocean-like image. The cliff descends a little to the east, creating a walkable path.

This section of the island touches the sea level, continuing even deeper in. The path takes two turns here, west and south.
