To the south is what seems to be a dead end, and a steep path up overtakes the western road. The grass is green all around the island, blowing gently in the wind, amidst flowers of all sorts.

A set of stairs leads up to the seed room, where the Mana Seed of the Tree elemental is kept safely. To the north is a short path of solid stone platforms leading to the center stage. The spiritual aura of the Tree elemental Dryad seems to be innately present within this place, giving it a nice, nurturing feel.

A large field of red and green flowers dot this area, making it look very stunning and beautiful. The sun shines brightly, basking the field with warmth. The ruins of a few pillars of the Tree Palace lie around, actually adding to the beauty of the area rather than detracting from it.

rooms.name: Before the doors of the Tree Palace

userData.LongDescription: The Tree Palace is one of the most mysterious palaces in all the world, once transformed into the vile Grand Palace. Now it has sunken once more, only leaving the uppermost layer above sea level. A set of white steps lead up to white double doors. Red and green flowers dot the earth all around. A dirt path leads to the west, circling the perimeter of the palace.

If this section of the outpost has one primary feature, it is the enormous staircase leading up to the ramparts. It is, however, nearly matched by the stack of crates that stand beneath rusty ductwork that weaves in and out of the brick wall. Like many sections of the base, it is not without graffiti or posters. There is also a large pothole in the middle of the ground.

The Imperial base is at its most drab in this location. Steel girders and crumbling debris block off the view of the majority of the camp. Passage can still be made, but it is a winding journey through the wreckage of what may have once been a fine watchtower. Several boxes occupy the one uncluttered area, stacked neatly against the railing.

The Imperial camp's cobbled streets slowly give way to lush green grass as it stretches toward the mountainside. Two high towers rest on the northern and southern sides of the street, fitted with little more than ladders and cool, cool beach chairs. Crates of supplies are stacked up around the bases of each tower, preventing access.

rooms.name: A corner in the Imperial camp

userData.LongDescription: Cobbled stones and bricks bombard this area with clashing design. The building to the northeast stands out blatantly against the almost-green of the pavement. Small craters have been dug into the ground, crushed stone overflowing from the battered holes. Each one is spaced evenly apart in an alternating pattern, almost as if something very heavy were stomping through. A wanted poster has been fixed to a nearby wall.

Looking beyond the evenly spaced bars of the rails guarding this path, a small shack lies below. Blue shingles line the rooftop, and the slate grey of the smokestack arches high into the air. Compared to the rest of the area, it is a godsend. But the pathway is in shambles, overturned boxes and smashed barrels turning navigating the area into something of a maze.

This is one of two entrances to the Imperial outpost. The fortified gates are open, leading into the base proper. Immediately ahead of the entrance is the western wall of a large building. A few posters spreading propaganda about the Returners and the Empire are strewn over a nearby wall. A large stairway can be seen to the north, several enormous crates stacked beside it.

This is a small stretch of cobbled street. It stretches from east to west. The main feature of this section of the base would the the large building that lies square in the center. It can be entered through a heavy wooden door from this side of the outpost. On the wall opposite the building, there are two large tapestries.

This section of the upper walkway features broken railing and upturned tiles. Due to the broken railing, the view of the warehouse below is entirely unobstructed. Lined up along a small wall to the west, there are several dirty boxes, crates and barrels. Passage remains unobstructed to the north, whereas there is light damage to the road to the south.

Not quite the end of the line, the path takes a ninety degree bend to the north and east. The pathway is otherwise rather bland, dusty stones marred with scuffs from heavy machinery and boots alike. It's a well worn path, leaves lining the edges near the guard rail.

The same speckled bricking that makes up the rest of the building makes its presence known here as well. Deep underground the building, this room likely once served as storage. Treasure chests and large boxes lie scattered around the room, some of them covered with blankets and pushed together to serve as makeshift cots. A large woodfire stove rests in one corner, a few buckets nearby. There are even a few chairs.

This is a super-cramped room beneath the bar. There are two kerosene lamps in this tiny room, one mid-way along the stairs and another beside a door. There seems to be very little in the way of decor: a chair sitting by its lonesome in one corner, with a bucket pushed underneath it.

This section of the encampment is elevated high above the rest. It overlooks the canyon below in several directions, the deep-spanning chasm almost threatening to swallow the base whole. Old posters and other debris litter the walkway, especially around the stairs. The area downstairs is a platform that leads to the vast and open wilderness. The railing in this section has been torn out entirely.

rooms.name: At the foot of the stairway

userData.LongDescription: This is a fairly desolate section of the base. Aside from the enormous stairway climbing toward the heavens, the platform has very little going for it. Someone has drawn a chalk hop-scotch path leading over the edge of the platform and into the abyss. Someone has dropped a pouch of marbles as well, little shiny orbs dangerously littering the street. A cobblestone road leads further to the east.

This section of the outpost overlooks several portions of the base. There is a high flying view of the canyon below, as well as the wastelands out to the west. Nearby are a set of stairs, and pathways with safety railing lead around the outer perimeter. Nearby to the stairs is a large flagpole. Set against the railing there is an open barrel.

This is another fairly desolate part of the encampment. Very little exists here, outside of the platform that overlooks the unbelievably deep ravine. The deep, dark gap of the chasm is longest here, the other side almost impossible to see from this vantage point. The only truly interesting sight outside of the pit would be the ventilation system, ducts and girders weaving in and out of the walls both above and below the extended platform.

rooms.name: Between a wall and a deep place

userData.LongDescription: This is a very desolate section of the base, a narrow pathway between a large building and the canyon below. An immense poster has been pasted onto the wall of the building. While this is the closest section to the platform on the opposite side of the gap, the depth of the ravine is still very daunting. The lack of railing is very unsafe, and has likely caused several accidental deaths.

rooms.name: The rear of a large building

userData.LongDescription: Two enormous red tapestries hang from the northern wall, tied to the railing of the ramparts above. With gold trim and the symbol of the Empire emblazoned across the front. Staircases can be seen to the east and west, and the back end of a large brick building to the south. A few broken bottles and crumbled papers litter the ground here and there.

This part of the outpost is well-maintained, if cluttered. Rows upon rows of crates sprawl on an extended platform overlooking a deep ravine that separates the two sides of the outpost. On the opposite side of the canyon, a large staircase can be seen. The deep hole in the ground travels further to south, with no protective railing to speak of. On the other side of the gap, there lies a set of stairs and another platform. As with other places on the base, there is a large crack in the stone where something heavy appears to have fallen.

This section overlooks the main base. A broad stone path leads both to the north and south. Crudely constructed, a small watchtower rises from the outer wall. It casts an ominous shadow, blanketing the iron girders that litter the area below. Broken crates are crumbled beneath it, broken bottles and jars shattered amidst the debris.

Thick, dark shadows loom over the pathway, spiderwebbing mercilessly across the ground. The source is blatantly obvious: enormous rusty girders and air ducts looming in the sky overhead. Bursting from walls and disappearing into others, the heavy metal ligaments of the pre-apocalyptic base cast a worn look over the area. The railing guiding the edge of the outer perimeter has the occasional ribbon tied to it. Closer to the bottom, it becomes apparent that several tapestries dangle either down into the base or into the canyon on the opposite side.

The ramparts come to a distinct end. A crumbling guard rail has seen better days, most of it having already fallen into the depths of the abyss below. The pavement on the walkway has been up-ended almost completely, skidmarks leading up to the edge of the dilapidated street.

This area is a wide open space, save for the larger-than-life box of supplies that has been upheaved and practically demolished. MREs and other rationable goods spill out of a hole in one side of the box, a smaller box placed in front of it to keep even more from spilling out needlessly. From this vantage point, it's easy to see that the large building in the center of the base is L-shaped. In the opposite direction, a platform extends deeper over the ravine. It's still a very long drop.
An Imperial soldier is here, going Commando.

The air in the armory is very hot and oppressive.  A small pool of lava lies in a semicircle around a stone workbench and small work area in the middle of the room.  Some pots lay near, most likely holding water.  A display of some of the armorer's creations line the back wall.

The small plateau to the southwest allows sight of the lower portion of Dwarf Village.  A few patches of grass grow along the east wall, and some small rocks are strewn about the ground.  The noises of a busy village come from the north.

The room opens up into a giant cavern that holds all of Dwarf Village.  It seems that the cavern was formed naturally, and the dwarves just made it their home.  There is a large hole in the floor to the north, and there are some rocks and other debris lying around.

The smaller parts of the ship end here in what must be some kind of massive storage bay. This is easily the largest accessible room in the whole ship, yet it remains primarily unused. The sound of moving gears under the metal-plated floor echoes throughout the otherwise-silent room.

An intersection in the cave leads in three different directions.  The exit is back to the south, while north leads deeper in.  Water drips down from the ceiling onto the ground, making a large wet spot in the middle of the intersection.

A small arch in the stone leads to the north.  The walls have many nooks and crannies, but still conform somewhat to the shape of a hallway.  The grass grows all over the ground, and some rocks are strewn about.

The stage is a natural stone platform on the east side of the room, with a small set of stairs leading up to it.  A small counter sits next to the stage, where the tickets are most likely taken.  A large blue and tan plaid rug covers the floor.  There is a path behind the counter that goes into the room east of here.

The water from the falls outside splashes into the room, creating a small pool a few inches deep.  Some loose rocks in the water make it easy to trip.  A few small steps lead up onto dry ground to the northeast.

A dwarf with a friendly smile stands behind a plain wooden counter, waiting for customers.  Some pots line the north wall, and the room is plainly furnished.  A table with three chairs lies close to the south wall, while three neatly made beds sit in the middle of the room. A sign sits on the counter.

The cavern gives off a dark and gloomy look, but the dwarves don't seem to mind.  A large patch of grass is growing on the ground, next to a pile of rocks that have been left lying around.  A sign stands in front of the door to the inn.

The path gets thinner along the plateau as it comes to a door on the west side.  Some grass grows along the north wall, and some small rocks have been brushed up against a wall.  Other than that, the area looks clean and well kept.

The dwarf runs the length of both rooms to tend to the needs of his customers.  A chair sits against the right wall behind the counter, and a plaid rug covers the floor.  The dwarf obviously hasn't put too much thought into decorating.

The item shop is connected to the room beside it, with one dwarf working both shops.  The dwarf stands behind a sturdy wooden counter, extending across the length of the room.  A wooden hat rack can be seen behind the counter, and a plaid rug furnishes the floor.

The stairs are obviously of dwarven make, given away by their exquisite craftsmanship.  The stairwell is large enough for almost any type of person, although there is an occasional rock sticking out of a wall.  The ceiling is also quite low.

Most of the village can be seen from the small plateau.  The ceiling is quite low here, but high enough for dwarves to walk easily.  The floor and walls look very well kept, and a sign sits in front of the door.

The walls look old and worn, and a pillar-like projection extends from the eastern side.  Some grass grows along the western wall, and a large rock sticks out of the ground in the middle of the hall.  Some rocky debris lies about.

A set of stairs lead up to the north, where the rest of the dwarven town lies.  There is also a giant hole in the ground to the west.  Large rock spikes are randomly placed along the ground, which look to be very old and weathered.

rooms.name: The Deck of the Scorpion Army's Ship

userData.LongDescription: Made of both sturdy wood and metal, this ship, which belongs to the Scorpion Army, has managed to tunnel underground to the Dwarf Village. At several places on the deck, glowing machinery can be seen carrying out whatever processes they were intended to perform. A staircase leads into the interior of the ship itself, while a length of rope dangles from above, giving access to the Dwarf Village above.

This section of the ship is just a small room. There's not much to this place other than the post-modern style metal sheeting covering all four walls as well as the floor and ceiling. There is also a small chair in the center of the room, lying on its side.

The hallway wanders off to the north, deeper into the cave.  Some grass grows along the wall next to a few small rocks and stones.  There are also spots of wet mud in a few places, caused by drops of water dripping down from above.

The air in the cave is moist, caused by the nearby waterfall.  A long set of stairs lead down, and a faint light can be seen at the end of the corridor.  Some grass grows on the dirt, and some medium sized rocks are sticking out of the ground, waiting to trip someone up.

The rocks look old, but well kept.  Some grass lines the west wall where it curves out creating a small alcove.  Some medium sized rocks are sticking out of the ground, and more are piled against the wall.  A sign stands next to the stairs, indicating what is up them.

A simple square table lies in the center of the room with two chairs at it, and two beds lie against the north wall, made nicely.  Some pots lie around the room, just for show.  An impressive display of swords and armor is set up in the northwestern part of the room.

The small hallway connects the Dwarven Armory to the stairs that lead out of the cave.  It is barely wide enough for two people to fit through, but tall enough for mostly anyone to walk.  The heat from the nearby armory makes the air stifling.

The stairs are very well made, but the steps are a bit short.  The ceiling is a bit low, but not low enough to cause trouble.  There is a small niche in the east wall where a small animal could live, but it is too dark to tell.

The inside of the ship is very metallic. The floors are metal, the walls are metal, the doors, ceiling, and paneling are all metal. In places, instead of the same paneling along the walls, small pumps operate to transfer fluid through various pipes running through the ship. A staircase leads to the upper deck, while a set of double doors leads north.

A short hall extends to the north, leading to another section of the cave.  A group of large rock spikes extend out of the ground off to one side, and a small ledge extends out into the hole to the south.  Some debris is lying around on the ground.

The walls form an irregular shape along the side of the cavern.  There is a hole in the ground to the east, and a set of stairs leading north.  Many large rock spikes stick out of the ground, and it looks as if there were once even more spikes that have been since torn down.

Abandoned weapons fill the largest part of this tiny room. Dozens of rusted battleaxes lean against the north wall, and a great assortment of long-unused swords of various types have been stacked up haphazardly on both the east and west sides of the room. A handful of dusty, wooden crates are stacked neatly along the southern wall.

The smooth tiled floor on this platform is a stark contrast to the rough stone that makes up the walls. In the center of the floor lies a large, purple carpet that does not quite stretch from the southern stairs to the immense, northern, double doors. Grandiose shields hang on each side of the doorway, adding to what is no doubt meant to be an impressive entrance.

Twin suits of armor flank the archway between this room and the descending stairway to the north. Each suit is made of polished steel and holds a tall spear with its left glove and a purple and gold buckler in the right. A stone archway leads south from this small landing.

This room contains only a small, single-person bed and a small, wooden dresser. Even so, it seems overcrowded, as if it were not really meant to be used as a bedroom or living space. Two torches provide decent light, hung from the wall on either side of the thin, wooden door that separates the room from the stairwell outside.

Twin torches burn brightly on either side of the stairwell set into the north wall. The brightness of this area plainly shows the dull grayness of both the floors and walls, which is sharply contrasted by the shining silver statue of armor that stands erect to the west of the stairwell.

Long, wooden shelving lines the walls of this small room from the floor to the ceiling. Tools of all sorts are stacked on the shelves, along with assorted mechanical parts. A hefty, metal workbench is set in the center of the room, taking up what little space is left by the shelving. A single, wooden stool stands next to the bench on the side farthest from the entrance.

This small storage room is crammed full of wooden crates, nearly to the entry way. Little space remains inside the room, only enough for one or two people and a few more in the stairway that passes just outside. Two torches have been hung from the wall on either side of the stairwell entry, dangerously close to the stacks of crates.

Lit by torches hung high on the wall, the hallway turns a corner, heading north and east. A short series of steps rises up to the north, where the hallway widens. The eastern branch leads to the entrance of the castle. This part of the passage is devoid of any real decoration, the bare stone walls only broken up by a few shallow carvings.

An enormous, wooden desk dominates this room, nearly dividing it in half. A tall highchair is situated behind the desk, and several piles of neatly stacked papers are spread over the desk's surface, surrounding a book that is lying open. The wall behind the desk is covered by two bookcases in either corner, each filled with books of various sizes, and a broad map of the world that hangs between them.

This storage room is nearly empty. Two stacks of wooden crates have been heaped near the southern wall, one in the southeast corner and the other against the western wall. A few sets of rusty plate armor have been dumped between the crates, along with some spears and small shields.

The ceiling vaults high above this enormous, well-lit chamber. On a platform raised five steps above the floor sits a monumental, luxurious throne facing south. Flowing from the wall behind the throne, down the steps of the wide platform and to the southern entrance is a wide purple carpet bordered with gold. On the east and west sides of the throne, sets of stairs rise to the north, leading into individual stairwells. High on the wall directly behind the throne hang two identical shields of red and yellow.

This landing connects the throne room to the south to the stairway that ascends into the castle tower above. Most of the light on the landing is supplied by a pair of torches on either side of the stairwell. The light is fairly dim and causes everything in the area to be tinted the slightest bit orange.

Two statuesque suits of armor flank the east and west sides of the stairwell on the northern wall. Above the eastern suit hangs a large red and yellow shield emblazoned with the silhouette of a flying reptile. Twin torches burn brightly, illuminating the gray stone walls and floor. A short, compact series of steps head south into a hallway.

This small room has been converted to a library in recent times. Its walls are lined with bookshelves, and two rows of free-standing bookcases fill up the majority of the room. Plenty of space is left around the two torches that light up the room so as to not risk any of the shelves or books themselves catching fire from the torches' flames.

Light floods the courtroom through the humongous stained glass window that is set into the rear wall, illuminating the ample open area. Balconies rise up nearly to the ceiling on the east and west walls, providing a reasonable view of the entire room. Bleachers have been set against the southern wall, opposite the raised area and grand seat that form the judge's bench. A small podium, just large enough for a single person to stand in, is positioned near the center of the room.

A considerable portion of this room is taken up by a large dining table that is surrounded by four wooden chairs. Along the north wall, a counter is stocked with all manner of fare. The walls and floors are made of wood, in sharp contrast to the stone of the rest of the castle. Oil lamps set on small outcroppings around the room provide ample light. The dining room continues to the east, while a kitchen lies to the south. A set of stairs to the north leads to the castle proper.

A sweeping, royal purple rug lies across the rough stone floor, reaching from the entrance gate to a broad set of stairs to the north. The stairs lead to a landing ten feet above. Blazing torches hang in sconces on both sides of the staircase, providing ample illumination throughout the entrance way. On either side of the stairs, grates opening to areas below are set into the northern wall. Hallways lead away from the entrance to the east and west.

This storage room is full of cleaning supplies. Stacked against the eastern wall are a few dozen brooms. The western wall is covered with several wooden shelves, all full of cloths of assorted sizes, small brushes and wooden buckets. A significant portion of the southern end of the room is filled with several barrels, each labeled with "SOAP" in black letters.

A thick, square-shaped rug has been rolled out at the bottom of the northern stairway. The rug is royal purple with gold trim and covers most of the gray, stone floor. Its cushiness and lack of wear suggests this area sees little traffic. A stairwell leads up into the castle tower to the north, and the throne room lies to the southeast.

The flickering torchlight, emanating from either side of the stairwell archway, gives this landing an orange tint. The floor is mostly covered with a long purple and gold rug, which extends to the east as the room continues. The stairwell set in the north wall leads down into other parts of the castle.

Bright sunlight streams into this room from two open-air windows in the north wall. Below each window rests a suit of steel armor stood at attention. Some additional light comes from a pair of torches that hang on either side of the archway that connects the room to a stairway that heads downward. Another archway connects to a room to the south.

The northern half of this room is raised up from the rest of the room by about six inches and has a floor made of smooth stone tiles. A bed and table sit in the center of the raised area, and a desk and small bookcase are set against the western wall. A full-length mirror of polished bronze is affixed to the east wall.

This narrow passage curves here, heading north up a short set of steps and west to the main gate of the castle. The walls on either side of the hallway are largely bereft of any adornment, but a repeating pattern of shallow arches is carved into the stone. Torchlight diffuses throughout the passageway providing plenty of light to see by.

Two dual-colored shields decorate the north wall between the two exits from this room. An open archway west of the shields leads north to a stairwell landing, and a closed wooden double door east from the shields heads into another chamber. The antechamber is lit by four torches affixed to both sides of both exits.

The south end of this landing drops off ten feet into a chamber below. A set of stairs leads down from the middle of the southern edge, while railings line the rest of the edge. An area raised a few feet lies north a short distance from the railings. The raised area connects to the south by a pair of steps, and a suit of armor stands on either side of the steps. A stairwell, set back into the northern wall, heads to the rest of the castle above. To the immediate east and west of that archway are lit torches, and further away hang decorative shields.

This bedroom is divided between a lower section of rough, stone floor partially covered by a purple rug and a slightly raised area of smooth stone flooring, connected by a pair of steps. The raised area holds a bed and table, along with a suit of polished armor that stands against the east wall. The west wall is almost completely covered by an enormous painting of a woman and child.

This well-lit room appears to used for nothing but storage. A few crates are piled throughout the room, along with several empty weapon racks. A handful of wooden shelves have been hung on the wall, though they are all empty at the moment. The light throughout the storage room is provided by twin torches on either side of the entrance, their yellow light more than adequate for this small space.

Mountains of crates are piled throughout this small storage room off the side of the stairwell, leaving only a small amount of space to move around. Neglected suits of armor have been discarded among the crates, all in various states of disrepair. Shelves line the back wall, filled with ancient-looking ledgers and loose papers.

Torches light up this corner of the castle. Set in the north wall, a flight of stairs leads to the basement. An ornamental, multicolored shield hangs from the wall to the east of the stairwell. The northwest corner of the room is filled by a suit of armor that has been posed in the image of a fully armored knight.

The southwest corner of the kitchen is lined with a long wooden counter that holds trays of food waiting to be served. In the southeast corner, several barrels and bags have been stacked, all filled with various foodstuffs. The majority of the kitchen equipment is set against the north wall. A series of stoves abuts a preparation counter that also holds a pair of sinks. The wall above this counter is packed with shelves, and two ice boxes are adjacent on the eastern end. The aroma of fresh-baked bread and numerous spices fills the air. A short hallway to the north leads to the dining room.

Several sets of arm and leg shackles hang from hooks on the walls around this room. Two suits of full plate armor stand up like statues near the center of the room, each gripping a short sword in one metallic glove and a round metal shield in the other. Two rows of weapon racks occupy the center of the room, each filled with a variety of melee weapons.

The wooden doorway leading out of the room takes up much of the north wall, flanked on either side by brightly flaming torches and identical yellow and red shields. A small nook in the wall to the northwest is the resting place of a suit of armor that stands upright, holding a spear and buckler. A long carpet covers most of the stone floor and continues west to a stairwell landing.

A flimsy, wooden door opens into this small room that holds a bed and a chest of drawers. The room appears to be a re-purposed storage area, barely large enough to serve as a basic bedroom. Big enough for just a single person, the bed is covered with plain, white sheets and a thick, purple blanket.

This room serves as an antechamber for the bedroom through the northwestern door. The room is long and narrow, like the thick purple rug that covers most of the floor. The room is well-lit by four torches that hang on the wall, along with some daylight that streams in from the landing just to the north.

An immense rectangular table dominates the center of this area, surrounded by many tall-backed wooden chairs. The western half of the room is taken up by a quartet of identical beds. Each bed is covered with thick, high quality bedding of purple and gold. In the northeast corner sits a sizable wooden barrel or keg, and a pair of tall baskets line the eastern wall. A set of stone stairs leads to a railed platform above.

This area is well-lit by several luminous oil lamps that have been placed on small shelves hung from the walls. The floor is largely covered by a checkered rug on top of which sits a sizable table ringed by four chairs. A counter is set against the northern wall, filled with bottles of ale. More of the dining room lies to the west.

The path through the forest opens to a large clearing here, mostly made of a large dirt patch with some spots of dead grass. Dense, more alive grass grows around the fringe of the clearing, which obviously has no problem thriving. Many families have no doubt chosen this as a frequent picnic area.

The road takes a sharp, sudden turn here as it heads due east towards Guardia Castle. The turn appears to have been so sharp, in fact, that carts going by have scraped against the trees in the inside corner, leaving scratches and dents in the bark.

The path seems to slightly curve here. Small flowers grow naturally in the small space between the dirt path and the trees themselves. Some moss also grows on parts of the trunks, while some small insects crawl about on it, in search of nourishment.

This part of the forest is distinguished by several wide holes, each a few feet in diameter but only a few inches deep, dug right into the path. The holes also have some water sitting in them, which makes the danger and humiliation of falling into them that much greater.

The path ends here in a large clearing, surrounded almost entirely by trees placed so densely that they prevent passage beyond them. There is only one way in or out from here, and it's back to the northwest. The clearing is fairly wide and has a good amount of soft grass around the area.

This small corner of Guardia Forest is much narrower than the area around it, as if the path was cut long ago and has started to close up. Grass grows thick, and it's fairly obvious that this is the path less traveled. There also seem to be some vines wrapped around the trees.

Unlike the rest of the forest to the south, all of the trees here seem to be well-kept and regularily trimmed to prevent overgrowth, making them smaller than the others before them. The top of Guardia Castle is visible from here, to the northeast.

The canopy of leaves formed by the tall trees here prevents most light from reaching the forest floor, but that doesn't stop some small plants and grass from growing here. The path splits in several directions here, some going towards the castle to the north, some going away.

The collection of forestry known as Guardia Forest serves as the last defense between Guardia Castle and the outside world. The massive oaks and maples of the forest rise high above the path. Down low, small shrubs line the dirt trail through the forest towards the castle.

The forest forks again here into several directions. The path to the northwest seems to lead to Guardia Castle, the path southwest appears to lead to a large clearing, and to the east is a part of the path that appears not to be used nearly as much as the others.

The large forest serving as a barrier between Guardia Castle and the outside world, known as Guardia Forest, is the last line of defense to the invaders of the times. From here, the majestic Guardia Castle is easily visible to the north, while the forest lies to the south. While currently traffic through the area is minimal, the dirt path is well-distinguished, suggesting that it is subject to a lot of passers-by.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - West of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: Filled with nothing but sand, the large yard between the surrounding structures is fully exposed to the sun. The intense heat creates mirages in the distance, which offer a minor distraction from the sun above.

Four cells are built into the wall, three of which occupied. Near them, a bucket containing a vile liquid sits within reach of the prisoners. Numerous crates have been stacked in the corner across from the cell with an open door, which has a cavernous opening in the back wall.

How heavily-favored this footpath is for the patrolling guards is immediately apparent when viewed up close. A deep rut has been worn into flattened sand under the shade of the castle's keep. Chittering can be heard, over the whine of the turbines, from behind the massive dunes to the north.

The top of the tower offers an incredible view. Painted by the sun, the Figaro Desert is a blinding and sun-bleached spectacle. Arid winds tear over the tower and the ocean on the horizon completes the ravaged landscape. Storm clouds on the northern horizon drift towards the Narshe continent, pushed away by warm desert air.

Within an alcove framed by flowing tapestries, two magnificent thrones sit at the end of a long crimson carpet. The wall behind the thrones displays two silk tapestries, which have been embroidered with the seal of Figaro. Between them, two crossed swords with golden hilts have been mounted to the wall.

A large green carpet covers most of the room, save for a small landing at the bottom of a set of steps. A small lantern on the northern wall keeps the room lit whenever the desert sun isn't pouring in through the southern door.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - West of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: The desert sand is peculiarly flat, in comparison to the dunes on the horizon. A short turbine silo sticks out of the sand and whines at a constant frequency. The short shadow being cast by the turbine is the only refuge from the blazing desert sun.

This barren room serves as an antechamber for the library above. A small lantern attached to the northern wall provides ample light to the stairs leading up and the area in front of the door on the southern wall. The plain green carpet set into the recessed area by the door seems to act as a sand trap.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - Base of the Eastern Tower

userData.LongDescription: The eastern tower of Figaro Castle rivals the main keep in sheer scale. Attached by a mechanical arm, it has been extended into its current position by the castle engine and has a steel door on its southern face. To the east, large, undisturbed dunes indicate the edge of the established perimeter.

A brisk wind blows through the shade provided by the main keep to the south. Wild, untamed dunes to the north are left unchecked by the patrols that pass through. The whine from the turbines of Figaro is ever-present and is occasionally accompanied by the familiar sounds of the chocobos.

A few stacks of crates take most of the floor space this room doesn't have. A small, empty chest sits in the back corner, under wall-mounted glass lantern. The smooth brick floor of this room lacks the fine coating of dust that most of the castle has. A small sign has been posted near a crate.

The pops and crackles of a fireplace break the monotony of the ever-present whine from the castle's turbines. An iron poker has been set against the firebrick foundation, and a few errant logs indicate a recent stirring of the coal bed. Against the northern wall, a steep staircase leads to the battlement above the western tower.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - West of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: A long shadow from the mechanical arm connecting the castle to the western tower graces the sand below it with cooler temperatures. Against the cooled and shaded bricks, evidence of a sleeping guard seeking refuge in the cool sand remains.

A tightly-designed hallway with machined brick walls connects the stairs leading up to the foyer with the compact dungeon to the south. In the center of the hall, a sturdy wooden desk and chair allow a guard to easily block the passage. The air seems to have a slow but constant flow towards the foyer and carries a musty scent.

Many books and tomes fill the massive bookshelves of the castle library. Only a small walkway exists between the shelves. Many of the shelves loom out of reach; symbolic of the knowledge they contain to laymen that might visit this room. A few small lanterns on the northern wall keep the area well-lit.

Steel doors adorn the northern and southern walls, each set between brick pillars. A simple stone banister divides the eastern side of this barren antechamber from a short set of steps which leads to a small landing below.

A pair of steel doors at the base of a large tower lead north, to the castle's inn. The castle's western curtain wall casts a long shadow over the tower and the southern wall. Gusts of wind from the nearby turbines occasionally carries along sand, which collects near the edge of the courtyard.

Chilled air rushes out of the tower through the vents surrounding the southern door, near the bottom of a small set of steps. Green carpet with a smooth, dense weave fills the area and a small table set for two is tucked into the corner. Long, crimson silk curtains hang from an arch which leads to a bedroom.

Two large tables occupy what looks to be a designated work room for the engineers of Figaro. A wide green carpet sprawls from wall to wall and outlines the landing for the bookshelves to the north. A musty scent fills the air and the muffled sound of wrinkling pages accompanies the familiar whine of the castle turbines. Tucked into the southwest corner of the room, a narrow set of steps leads to an antechamber below the library.

The seal of Figaro is displayed proudly above a pair of double doors which lead into the main keep. The doors are nestled between two brick columns with arrow slits and spotlights integrated into them, making this an easily defended access point. Beyond each pillar, a small walkway leads to a short turbine silo. A wide set of stairs leads south and down into the courtyard.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - Base of the Western Tower

userData.LongDescription: The western tower of Figaro Castle is the King's quarters. This space is reserved for him and displays that he does not hide within the inner sanctums of the keep. To the west, large, undisturbed dunes indicate the edge of the inner perimeter.

Crimson and gold colors fill the room. Vivid red carpet runs from the door on the southern wall down the long hallway towards the throne room. Suits of golden armor line the carpet, each holding an extravagantly jeweled sword. Along the walls and tucked behind brick pillars, there are wooden doors which lead to some small rooms.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - Along the Curtain Wall

userData.LongDescription: The smooth, machined bricks of the castle's walls reflect the heat of the desert sun and make Figaro gleam like a diamond in the rough. In the shade created by an alcove of the outer wall, a small service door leads into the castle. Sand near the bottom of the silo is blasted clear of the exhaust vent, creating a shallow sandpit that refills between gusts.

The single piece of furniture sitting in the center of the room is an over-sized bed with a glorious bedspread. The walls of the room have been draped with crimson silk curtains and completely cover them, save for a clearing left for the small lantern above the headboard of the bed.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - West of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: Dunes near the outer perimeter of the castle show where the patrols stop. A short tower with a turbine whines as it pulls fresh air into the engine below the castle. A large auxiliary structure to the northwest seems to have been pushed into its current position.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - West of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: A small tower at the edge of the patrolled perimeter serves as a demarcation where the guard's responsibility ends. The smooth sand near the castle begins to dune and shift as the distance between the castle and the perimeter grows. To the east, a heavily traveled footpath leads to the shade behind the castle and the castle's western tower is to the south.

Silo-mounted turbines tower over the hot desert sand and double as a massive barbican for Figaro Castle. Nestled between two of them, a short set of sand-covered steps lead up to a pair of reinforced steel doors. Hot exhaust billows from the vents at the bottom of the silos, which occasionally kicks up a cloud of dust and sand.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - Within the Barbican's Foyer

userData.LongDescription: A pristine red carpet covered in delicate gold embroidery lies on the floor which leads between pairs of reinforced steel doors to the north and south. Hanging on the northern wall, regal curtains proudly display the seal of Figaro. Strong drafts of cooled air rush into the western stairwell, towards a thrumming engine room.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - East of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: The sand in close proximity to Figaro Castle has been flattened and looks groomed in comparison to the wild dunes on the horizon. A short shadow from a lone turbine is barely large enough to hide from the blazing desert sun. The main entrance to the castle lies to the southwest.

This small battlement overlooks the western half of Figaro's perimeter. It resides slightly higher than the tower in the center of the yard, though much of the view to the north and south is blocked by the castle's features. A short turbine silo sits atop the corner of the wall and whines as the fan within spins.

The view from the top of Figaro Castle offers a panoramic view of the sprawling Figaro Desert, an immense ocean of sand with miles of jagged dunes, which extends to the horizon in every direction. Heatwaves rising from the sun-scorched earth and dust storms obfuscate the distant landscape. Closer to the castle, the land and wind become tamed by the turbines which have leveled the surface to a clean, flat perimeter.

The room appears to be set up as a guest room and has minimal furnishings. A couple of modest green carpets cover the areas under a small table and a bed. An empty wooden table sits near a staircase which leads out to the desert, while another set of stairs leads to the roof through a trapdoor.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - East of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: The wide mechanical arm connecting the main castle to the eastern tower provides ample amounts of shade to the sand below it. A few small desert creatures have sought refuge in the cool sand beneath the arm. The sandy footpaths from around the yard converge before spreading out again.

Four beds on a simple green carpet fill the room, barely leaving space for the few crates and small table against the eastern wall. A large fireplace is embedded into the northeastern corner of the inn, ensuring the room stays warm on the cold desert nights. A small sign on the table has some writing on it.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - East of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: A faint trail leads between the eastern tower and an alcove along the main castle wall. The high pitched whine of the many turbines throughout Figaro and the occasional gust of wind are the only distractions to be had from the intense heat of the barren desert.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - East of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: A short tower with a turbine at the top provides a little shade in this unforgiving place. The flattened sand near the castle starts to collect into little dunes near the outer perimeter of the castle. To the northeast, a large tower stands, attached to the castle by an enormous extended arm.

The stone crenelation offers an excellent purchase against the whipping wind. For as calm as the air is on the surface, it's apparent the turbines are hard at work turning the wild winds into a valuable resource. Far in the distance, past miles of shifting dunes, the Narshe mountain range dots the northern horizon.

Light from the glass lanterns dances on the golden suits of armor, creating a dazzling display of color. The crimson carpet extends from the hallway to the south and ends after climbing a few steps at the top of the throne room landing. A wide pair of double doors on the northern wall leads into the throne room, while a couple of small passages along the edges of the room lead behind it.

This small battlement overlooks the eastern half of Figaro's perimeter. The shadow being cast by the castle covers much of the eastern yard in a cool shade. At the corner of the castle wall, a short turbine silo whines as the fan within pulls the hot desert air into the structure.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - Behind the Throne Room

userData.LongDescription: Two brick pillars frame a long stairwell, which leads up to the top of the keep. The raging desert winds can be heard through the trapdoor at the end of the stairwell and the howling echoes on the brick walls of this enclosed space. Against the western wall, a small chest sits unopened, Two passageways to the main hall are on the southern wall.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - Along the Curtain Wall

userData.LongDescription: Tucked into an alcove of the outer wall, a small service door leads into the castle. The castle's walls cast a long shadow over the eastern perimeter. At the bottom of a nearby turbine, an exhaust vent has created a small hole where sand has been blasted clear.

A pair of steel doors at the base of a large tower lead north, to the castle's library. The courtyard's cobblestone meets with the castle's curtain wall, where a small amount of sand has collected. Turbines at the corners of the tower and the courtyard wall seem to run perpetually, driven by the massive engine below.

The smell of oil and grease hangs heavily in the air. The heavy thrumming of engines, spinning fans, and random sounds from other mechanical equipment create a cacophonous symphony. Dials, knobs, pressure valves and bells fill the back wall; while networks of pipes run between various gauges, pressure tanks, and junctions before they disappear into the floor and ceiling.

Rows of ivory pillars with intricately carved pedestals extend to the vaulted ceiling. Various paintings have been hung along the outer walls between ornamental swords and wall sconces. An elaborately weaved crimson runner leads from the double doors on the southern wall to the thrones further north.

This relatively small room serves the purpose of the castle's shop to sell equipment and combat tools. Clean and tidy, the items sold here are very advanced in technical design and function. Along the back wall, just below the small lantern set there for illumination, are a pair of opened chests and a crate. The shopkeeper here sits on a chair near the middle of the room, a sign sitting at the foot for all to see. A door to the south leads back out to the castle's main hall.

Funneled by the surrounding towers, the warm desert breeze pushes sand down the broad staircase away from the main hall towards the rest of the courtyard. The whine of the turbines echoes between the towers. The walls are filled with arrowslits, a constant reminder of how well defended this castle is.

The harsh desert sun has baked the sand stuck between the smooth cobblestones that pave the bailey. The sound of spinning turbines echoes off the enclosing curtain walls. Occasionally, shadows stir within the darkened windows which overlook the courtyard and the grand set of steps that lead up to the main hall.

rooms.name: Figaro Castle - East of the Castle

userData.LongDescription: The flattened sand near the castle begins to dune and shift as the distance between the castle and the perimeter grows. A small tower marks the very edge of the controlled zone and the untamed desert lies beyond. To the west, a heavily patrolled footpath leads to the shade behind the castle. The castle's eastern tower is to the south.

The sea of lava below crashes violently against the rock underfoot. Long ago the hot magma splashed up onto this section of platform, igniting what appears to have been another bridge. Wherever it led to is now inaccessible. Stairs lead upward far off in the northwest corner, or another set of stairs leads downward.

An ancient bridge stretches across a chasm with connecting rock platforms on either end. In the middle of the bridge, a column of rock climbs to the ceiling of the cavern. The ramp leads west, down to the sea of lava below, while the platform to the east continues further into the cavern. A sloping curve of rock runs underneath the bridge.

This sandy piece of land is a tiny part of a large archipelago that was created when the Floating Continent crashed into the sea. The beach is marked by rocks both large and small, as well as the occasional bird. To the south a mass of rock protrudes from the sand. Half a dozen islands stretch the north and northwest, while open sea lies to the east.

The platform underfoot sits just inches above the lava level, allowing boiling magma to spill over the edge frequently. A treasure chest sits on a small island that is planted just northwest of the platform. Unfortunately, the bridge granting access to that island was long since burned, and the treasure chest abandoned. The sea of lava rolls northward where it can be heard crashing upon unseen shores. The path runs around a column of rock to the west and continues southeast through a tunnel.

A small platform underfoot is all that prevents one from tumbling into a sea of lava below. Bridges run every which way in this cavern, providing a means of access to other rocky platforms. Another doorway can be seen in the southeast corner of this cavern. The heat is staggering from this vantage point. Stairs here lead upward to fresh air.

Stairs lead from the plateau above onto a narrow walkway that curves to the east. The rocks on either side of the walkway are worn smooth from erosion, making the footing slippery. The path crosses through a tunnel under the plateau and continues further east. The lava level is just below the lip of the walkway, allowing the occasional wave to spill onto the path.

A narrow expanse of rock underfoot cuts through the lava, and rises high into the cavern. The peninsula climbs from the plateau below where it levels off into a circular platform. From here, thin stalactites can be seen protruding from the deafening silence of the dark above. A treasure chest was placed in the center of the platform, but has long since been emptied.

A soft glow from below dimly illuminates the entrance to the cavern. While the damage from the earthquake is less apparent here, thin cracks in the rock run the length of the cavern. The center of the cavern is occupied by an enormous mound of volcanic rock. There is a small treasure chest in the southwestern corner, and the passage continues downward to the southeast.

This platform of rock is an elongated piece that stretches from north to south. The path continues across this rock formation in an east-west manner, while a ramp to the south leads to higher ground. At the northern tip of the rock, the remains of a bridge once ran to a small island, upon which rests an unopened chest. Along the southern edge there is the smoldering carcass of a Zombone, which is partially submerged in the sea of lava.

A thin spire of rock rises defiantly from the sea of lava. Atop, a tiny platform levels off and affords little footing. A wooden bridge reaches westward to a more stable rock formation. There is a rickety wooden staircase descending southward to a plateau of rock.

There is a noticeable drop in temperature here, and a musty stench assails the nostrils. Flight after flight of stairs compose this section of the cave. At the top of the stairs is a dark opening in the wall. Combined with the stooping ceiling and artificial formation of the earth, the staircase suggests an upward direction. The door at the landing of the staircase leads to the main chamber of the cave, and beyond the sea of lava, the outside world.

Two small pillars have collided with each other, forming one larger expanse of rock. The bridge connected the two was subsequently shattered, and debris is scattered across the expanse. A column of rock on the northern pillar once reached the ceiling, but due to the shifting of the pillars, it has since splintered off. More bridges connect to other platforms to the southwest and northeast.

The rock underfoot has worn from millennia of footfall. Due to this, the rock has a clear pathway ground into it. The curve slopes downward, with a set of stairs at the top and passage through a tunnel at the bottom. An ancient wooden bridge runs from west to east, connecting rock formations high above.

In the northeast corner of the cavern stands the most generous and secure outcropping of rock. Bridges run in all directions here, allowing access to any other platform within the cavern. Two metal bindings resting against the eastern wall are all that remain of a treasure chest that has otherwise been burned beyond recognition. Another, possibly more fruitful, chest can be seen perched upon a pedestal of rock to the southwest.

Several stalagmites rise up out of the southern edge of the platform and connect with the ceiling. Another column of rock in the northwest corner ascends and levels off. At the base of that column is a door leading to a dark room. There are more stalagmites to the north and a large stone dais to the west. A maze of bridges and pillars of rock can be seen to the northeast.

A massive stone dais has been constructed here, with a short staircase granting access to the top. Upon the dais, in the center of the platform, a square button has been placed into the ground. This section of the cavern is secluded, with the southern wall extending along the western edge of the dais. A bridge leads east to the large stalagmites while a tunnel in the western wall leads to a wide stone expanse.

This tiny room was heavily damaged in the recent earthquake, and has therefore has been expanded. The northern wall collapsed into the lava below, and is now open to a view of the sea. A lone treasure chest survived the quake, only to be crushed under the weight of a portion of the ceiling which could no longer sustain itself.

At the deepest depths of the cave, a narrow terrace of rock serves as precarious footing. Attached is a decrepit rope bridge, which leads to a distant mass of rock on which two ancient doors loom overhead. Despite being buried deep beneath the earth, a constant air swirls about, gently rocking the bridge to and fro. The suffocating darkness prevents any further investigation of the cave.

The stone balcony underfoot was carefully leveled and worked into a smooth walking surface. As this is the easternmost point of the cavern, the entirety of the sea of lava can be seen flowing to the west. A small staircase at the northern tip of the balcony leads to a small platform. A doorway has been carved into the southern wall.

Waves break softly along the shore, and a patch of grass has begun to take root on what would be an otherwise barren island. Distant islands in the archipelago can be seen to the west and southwest. A gentle breeze blows in from the southwest and rolls east over the open sea. To the northeast, a formation of rock can be seen defiling the serenity of the island.

The long, uneven platform is marked by several stalagmites that stretch to the ceiling. The easternmost stalagmite has two buttons set into the floor, one on either side of it. Attached by a short staircase is a lower platform, with a cracked treasure chest resting upon it. A thin passageway to the southwest leads to a wide expanse, and bridges lead both north and south to other rock formations.

The two-tiered column of rock underfoot is connected via wooden bridges to numerous other rock formations. The lower level leads southwest to another platform, while bridges on the higher level connected to the west and east. A balcony has been carved into the cavern wall to the east. The sea bubbles below, sending fresh gasses into the air.

The main chamber of the cave stretches far to the east of this plateau. Numerous other plateaus and rock structures can be seen across the sea of lava below. The plateau curves southward to a high-rising peninsula while a staircase leads downward to narrow walkway just above the lava flow. A passage in the northern wall leads up to the maze of bridges.

High above the expanse of stone, a narrow walkway of rock runs atop the wall. The western half of the cavern can be seen, with a long drop into the sea just over the lip of the walkway. There is a treasure chest at the northernmost tip of the perch. Several holes mark the ground, more evidence of digging. The ramp leads back down to the wide expanse.

Reopened by an earthquake, this narrow passage runs from the outside world down into a dark cave mouth. As such, shattered rock formations and long stalactites loom overhead, making the passage precarious at best. An alcove rests in the eastern wall of the passage.

A series of three plateaus are connected by ancient wooden bridges. Upon the center plateau sits a treasure chest that was long ago smashed and looted. The bridge leading south was designed to expand and connect with the center plateau, but has caught halfway, making to only access to safe ground to the east. Lava crashes upon the rocks far below, shaking the plateaus with each new wave.

This wide platform stands tall above all other rock formations within the cavern and serves as an excellent defensive position. The entrance can be seen far to the west, and another cavern exit even further to the east. A massive column rises from the northern edge of the bastion, inlaid into which are two switches. Wooden bridges lead west and east, while a set of stairs lead downward and connect to a curving path through the rock.

Sandy beaches stretch to the north and southwest on this small island. A large mound of rock juts out of the sand and serves as the sole landmark on this tiny island. A dark fissure has opened within the mound and leads into the earth. The distant shores of the mainland, the continent of Albrook, lay to the west.

The earthquake caused what was originally a wide platform to splinter into several narrow strips of uneven rock. Because of this shift in the rock, the bridge returning to the northeast is struggling to stay grounded. Stairs leading to a dark passage can be seen to the north. An unopened treasure chest sits just out of reach.

A wide expanse of stone has been constructed at the bottom of the stairs, and is surrounded on three sides by walls of sheer rock with the north open to the sea of lava. While a tunnel has been carved through the eastern wall, a ramp upward leads to the south, and there is a passage around the eastern wall to the northeast. For an unknown reason, there is clear evidence of digging throughout the field.

A plethora of treasure chests were hidden within this small room long ago. Unfortunately, some lucky adventurer has cleaned them of their contents already. There are two chests on the floor and two more on a higher balcony. There is little else in this room, aside from the reprieve from the heat of the lava. The door to the south leads back out.

This is the north easternmost corner of the above-stage catwalk system of the opera house.  The dust is fairly thick here, and the stage lighting below lights the particles as they dance through the air.  The eastern edge of the stage is visible below.

This is a small extension of the lobby, just to the east.  There are stairs here leading up to the lobby's balcony, but more importantly, to the balcony seats of the opera itself.  The same red carpeting from the lobby restarts after a few steps up from the ground level and continues up the stairs. A suit of armor stands, almost as if guarding the stairway.

This is the easternmost edge of the lobby.  It is about a half-floor higher up than the rest of the lobby, and it is similarly decorated with banners and carpeting.  To the north, there is a door visible that most likely leads to some sort of backstage area.

This is the south-easternmost corner of the above-stage area, a small segment of the maze that is the Opera House catwalk system.  To the north, the planks look like they pull a U-turn, leading anyone who would take that path just west of this area.

This room is a small connecting chamber between the main theater and the catwalks above the stage.  There is a small stairway in the center of the room that leads up to another level.  To the south is the balcony seating area.

This T-intersection leads north, south, and west.  To the north, a switchback in the catwalk system can be seen.  To the west, the catwalk curves north and fades into obscurity in a hovering mass of dust and darkness.  The cloud of dust extends in all directions from here, reducing visibility.

This is the center of the opera house's famous stage, where all the greats of the business have performed.  The lights above blind the performers of the audience, helping them maintain their personas better without the distractions of knowing how many people are in the audience.  On the northern edge of the stage is a raised platform.  On the wall are elaborate stained glass windows, depicting great thespians of ages past.

The catwalks merge from the north and east to form a right angle joint here.  The dust being tossed up from below has gathered on the planks in thick layers, and some of the stagehands have taken the liberty of inscribing messages here.  Below, the stage is clearly visible.

The western edge of the lobby's mostly decorative balcony.  To the north, a sturdy wood-and-iron door leads to the balcony seating.  The stairs to the south lead down to the main lobby.  To the east, the balcony extends further.

This is the eastern maintenance room of the opera house.  There is a stairway leading up to an elevated platform.  Against the northern wall is a row of switches.  The balcony seating area is to the south.

The lobby of the world-renowned Jidoor Opera House.  The classical stone architecture is accentuated here by somewhat faded, although still very regal, red carpets.  To the east and west are stairways leading up to the balcony seats.  In the back of the room, there is a desk.  Mounted on the wall behind the desk are banners sporting red and blue starburst designs.

rooms.name: Opera House - Right Front Balcony Seating

userData.LongDescription: The right and forward balcony seating area overlooks the orchestra pit and the stage as well.  To the south, more seating is available.  This section of seating extends all the way to the northern wall, where a door leading to a maintenance room is located.

This is the backstage area of the opera house, the closest one can be to the stage without actually being on the stage.  This area is conveniently connected to the dressing room, which is directly to the south.  There are a few chairs here next to a pile of boxes.

rooms.name: Opera House - Left Front Balcony Seating

userData.LongDescription: This is the forward western seating area of the opera house.  The orchestra can be heard below, tuning.  The stage is visible from here, but at a slightly awkward angle.  The seats here are of fine quality.  To the south, there are more seats and the door to the lobby is visible.  To the north, there is a door that leads to some backstage area.

rooms.name: Opera House - Left Rear Balcony Seating

userData.LongDescription: This is the western rear seating area for the opera house.  To the north and east, there are more seats.  From here, the in-house orchestra can be heard warming up.  Down below, the central stage can be seen.  It looks like there might be some kind of creature on the stage, although it might just be an elaborate prop.

High above the stage, the catwalks creak with age.  The vast web of wooden support structures expands all around, but from here it's only possible to go west or east.  The dusty and dim atmosphere here makes it very unpleasant to linger in one spot too long.

rooms.name: Opera House - Right Rear Balcony Seating

userData.LongDescription: This is the rightmost corner of balcony seating.  From here, the orchestra can be heard tuning their instruments.  The stage is also visible.  To the south, there is a door that leads out of the seating area and back into the lobby.  To the north and west, there are more seats.

The central segment of the balcony which overlooks the Opera House's lobby.  To the east and west are the doors that provide access to the balcony seating area overlooking the stage.  Railing here prevents an overenthused theater-goer from falling to a rather unpleasant demise.  On the northern edge of the wall, there are a pair of alcoves, each one housing a suit of armor.

This is a dead end!  The catwalks stop here, any step forward taken leads down to the stage below.  To the west, the path continues.  The air here is thick with the smell of earth, and the air rife with dust.  Of the dust that has settled, a message has been written in it.

This is the central balcony of the theater, an area filled with rows of seats.  It would appear that the central four seats have been reserved for the Impresario and his guests.  Below, the orchestra can be heard tuning up.  The stage is clearly visible from here.

rooms.name: Opera House - Outside The Dressing Room

userData.LongDescription: Just north of here is the dressing room, where all the greats of Opera prepare for their demanding roles.  There is a small balcony above the door, which appears to be little more than a decorative embellishment.  To the south, the easternmost corner of the building can be seen.  Beyond that is the lobby.

The maze of catwalks has simplified itself somewhat here, as one could only travel west or east from here.  To the west, the catwalks twist around to the north, whereas to the east the boards lay tracks in east and south directions.  The dust here has more or less settled, and it looks like some stagehands wave scrawled out messages in the dust.

This is the southwestern corner of the elaborate system of catwalks which is suspended high above the stage.  There really isn't much to look at here.  The air is filled with dust, and is dimly lit, as the only lighting is pointed down at the stage.

The catwalks are connected to the ceiling with tightly woven metal cables.  Below, the stage is visible.  The orchestra can be faintly heard, although the dust in the air and the planks of the catwalk absorb most of the noise.  It's very poorly lit up here.

Dangling high above the stage, the catwalk system installed in the opera house provides stagehands and technicians access to the various devices that control the technical aspects of the theater, the behind-the-scenes drudgery.  The dust here is thick and the lighting is bad.  It looks like a few boards might be loose.

The stage is more or less invisible from here, as many lighting elements are obscuring the view.  The abundance of lighting here has raised the temperature of this immediate vicinity.  To the east, it looks like the path stops.  To the south, it continues on into a maze like arrangement of boards and wire.

The planks that form the catwalks above the stage are creaky here, but they are still sturdy enough to support the weight of a normal human.  The stage is below, and fairly visible from here.  The dust here is not as thick, but the lighting could still be improved on.

This is the opera house's dressing room, where singers can practice, pick a wardrobe, and relax after a performance.  Against the north wall there is a large book shelf full of the scores of past operas.  There are several chairs against the walls.  There is a large table in the center of the room with an opera score on it.

This is the north-westernmost corner of the area above the stage. It is not very visible from here, as the overlapping planks and boards obscure any good view that would be there in the first place.  This area is dusty and poorly lit.

The easternmost edge of the balcony overlooking the lobby.  To the north is a door which leads to the theater area.  The stairs lead down to the lobby.  To the west, the balcony continues past two suits of armor to another door which also leads to the balcony seating area of the theater.

Just east of the lobby is a small extension.  There are two stairways here, one leading north and one leading east.  The one to the north leads to the balcony seats, perhaps the most desirable seats in the house, and is accompanied by a suit of armor.  The stairway to the east leads eventually to the backstage area.  The carpeting here is faded, due to increased foot traffic.
The catwalks are dangling over the stage, cables draped over pulleys just out of the reach of anyone who might try to tamper with them.  The dust is not very bad here, but the visibility is horrid.

Beyond the main building lies a dirt path, leading up to a pair of ladders.  One is a tiny ladder, almost a stepladder; the other leads up to a larger plateau formed of the same dirt and rock. Atop it is a large skull of some creature long dead, its mouth gaping and leading onto the forest that lies beyond the excavation site.

What appears to be a small excavation site is erected here.  Empty boxes lie in small heaps, next to rather large sets of hollowed-out bones that serve as huts and homes, or at the very least shelter from bad weather.  Dust billows from the occasional wind, causing the air to be very salty and arid, regardless of the lush forest that appears nearby.  The dead, now salty ground is a stark contrast to the flora surrounding the site.

The main 'building' of this shabbily-organized plot of dusty land is in the shape of a huge set of ribs, rising out of the ground like a monument to the dead.  The sounds of hushed voices murmur from the inside, but there appears to be no way past the large yellow-garbed man in front of it, who spends his time scowling and kicking up dust with his boot.

What appears to once have been a series of bones has a small building erected in and around it.  It almost appears to be a boat of some kind, docked in the midst of the dirt and sand that is this village.  Around it, men in bright yellow uniforms pick and dig at the hard soil, attempting to find something, anything of value.

After scaling the ladder to get to the top, a giant skull, its mouth gaping and open, leads into the forest beyond.  Large piles of sand and bone litter this plot of dead land, and the occasional blade of grass stands alone, a tribute to what once was.  The plateau stands roughly eight feet higher than the rest of the land; a sharp cliff, as if the ground below had been dug deep.

Near the large skull lies another plot of land, a series of ribs erupting from the ground jaggedly. the odd bit of dust and dirt trickling down, revealing this to be a recent find.  Something gleams within the cracking bones, an ominous green glow.  A light breeze blows hunks of dirt into the air, breaking off against the bones and causing small dust clouds to waft in the wind.

Beyond the large-mouthed skull lies, strangely, a lush forest, untouched by the violence of the excavators and workers at the Bone Village. Soft, cool breezes flow down from the mountains nearby, relieving the tense, dry heat of the village.  The sounds of creatures chirping and growling can be heard within the dense fauna, unseen by the eye, but most definitely audible.

After clearing the even smaller walkway over the chasm, a platform resides in the middle.  A thick, pulsating crystal stands atop the platform, on a stand which it seems to have been carved around.  The air around it seems a bit thicker, more humid.  The crystal dominates much of this platform, and the humming slowly becomes unbearable for human ears, ringing and crying out.

Even partially buried in the dirt, this conch shell is as big as a two-story building.  It spirals up from the ground with enormous spines circling its edges.  The inside of the shell acts as a ramp, allowing one to walk up to the top of the enormous seashell, offering an excellent vantage point of all of the surrounding coral formations.

The path continues straight across the river, the clouds a bit lighter as the city draws near.  From within the city, the echoes of gunshots and swearing can barely be heard, as if a fight were going on within the city.  Overhead, the occasional helicopter hovers, bearing the Shinra sigil.

rooms.name: Towards the City of the Ancients

userData.LongDescription: Some semblance of life resides here, a series of green treetops, now closer resembling stone.  Harsh, bright light shines down on the dry, dusty hills, and the path branches, once to a dead end, and onward down the path towards the city.

The hole that leads into this cave expands into a huge chamber, radiated by a soft hue of cyan light.   The cave's structure seems orderly and in place, the stairs carefully carved out of the white stone to curl down to a lower level.   The path at the top, where the entrance lies around the cave, vastly resembles a coliseum, with its pillars and archways that descend into darkness.

Before the items that resemble trees the path comes to an end.  The road ends just before a rocky outcropping, and all that lies here is dust, dirt, and the occasional burst of sound coming from within the city.

Past the skull that made up the Bone Village exit, a lush forest slowly pans into view.  Tall, sparse trees litter the area, and a general green glow seems to fill the vision of any who travel here.  The soil is most and firm under the feet, and the sounds of crickets and other tiny creatures sing their songs to the trees.

A series of large green stone outcroppings, closely resembling trees, stand out along the sides of this bridge, which strangely appears to be a hollowed out spinal column.  The clouds are darker along this road, and it twists and turns, leading to what appears to be a city atop a floating isle.

Several tall trees, thin but vibrant with life, stand to offer shade from the sun beating down above.  However, the sun would not shine through the green haze that fills this quiet, magical forest.  What appears to be singing hums farther off, the words muffled by the forest.

rooms.name: City of the Ancients: Winding Road

userData.LongDescription: The harsh light of day suddenly shines down upon the winding road that extends down the hills, back towards the main path into the city.  The road resembles a bone snake slithering downward, occasionally veering off into the mountains into seemingly nowhere.

Several trees stand together in a triangular pattern here, a tribute to the life of the sleeping forest.  The glow of the forest seems to have a steady pulse, vibrating with the very life-essence of the earth.  Small, thin columns of light stream through the treeline, like small arrows of light piercing the gloom.

A small rocky outcropping juts from the soft, moist ground, and small, inconsequential creatures inhabit it, crawling back into the earth.  The soft, pulsing mist continues to glow and consume the forest, the cloud hanging over the forest like a blanket.

rooms.name: City of the Ancients: Eastern Outskirts

userData.LongDescription: A long, winding path takes travelers around the eastern fringe of the city, near a series of small, white buildings.  The ground around the path is a strange lifeless stone, no plantlife, no flora or fauna, just stone and brick all around.

Several glass structures surround a small altar, the only decoration to the strange place being stains of blood along the ground and steps.  Surprisingly, the darkness is gone, left with what looks like a clear blue sky, heading towards a sunset.  Several small steps are standing out of the water like pillars, leading to the end of this place, a blood spattered ground, and the overwhelming stench of death that appears to be coming from the water.  Beyond the presence of death that was dealt here some time ago, it manages to hold an aura of peace and serenity, as the towers watch down over the pond.

rooms.name: The outskirts of the Forgotten City

userData.LongDescription: The thin bridge of land extends further behind the city, into what looks like a cave, with a strange blue light shining from within it.  The cave is made of a jagged brown rock, connecting into the mountain range that surrounds this deep valley.  An odd hum comes from within the cave, an incomprehensible song, it appears.

This is a sparse room, with a flight of stairs that leads up to a small bed.  What little light pours through shines through a pair of makeshift windows carved through the side of the rock, allowing light to peer

rooms.name: City of the Ancients Rear Exit

userData.LongDescription: The bone-paved road through the Forgotten City of the Ancients leads east into a forest of massive above-ground coral formations.  To the east, a conch shell as large as a building spirals up at the end of the road.  Large green stone formations, thin and flat like oyster shells, are layered around the road.

Passing through the steps of stone beyond the Sleeping Forest lies a path into a deep valley, surrounded by steep mountains.  Thankfully, a land bridge connects the forest to the floating isle in the midst of this valley, curiously floating atop a slowly flowing river.  A series of dark clouds seems to hang overhead, just around the isle, but not directly blocking the sun's light upon it.

rooms.name: At the end of the stairs
