userData.LongDescription: Just entering the room lies a flight of stairs, curling down towards an exit.  The room is lit up with a soft blue light, emanating from a crystal.  The light shines from the outside, mingling with the cyan hue, and the platform that leads outside is small.

This house seems to appear like the inside of a massive conch shell.  It curls downward, continuing down what appears to be a long flight of glass stairs.  The inside of this place is lit by small circles of light embedded into the ground, along the walls.  A strange scent wafts up from the stairs, reeking of death or something worse.

rooms.name: The path to the Forgotten Capital

userData.LongDescription: Passing through the entrance through the city, several closed off buildings can be seen in the ruins of this ancient city.  Up ahead is a series of large green rock fixtures in the mountains of this isle, as if a giant tree stood over the capital.  Breaching the tops of these is what appears to be a tree bare of leaves, the sharp multiple branches piercing the mass of jade coloured fossilized plantlife.

rooms.name: Entrance to the City of the Ancients

userData.LongDescription: The city comes into better view, not quite as majestic as from afar.  Three paths split the city apart, after leaving the bridge, off into the city's outskirts, along paths made of the same substance as the bridge across to the island.  Voices can be heard deeper within the city, but the actual words cannot.

Several glass structures surround a small altar, the only decoration to the strange place being stains of blood along the ground and steps.  Surprisingly, the darkness is gone, left with what looks like a clear blue sky, heading towards a sunset.  Several small steps are standing out of the water like pillars, leading to the end of this place, a blood spattered ground, and the overwhelming stench of death that appears to be coming from the water.  Beyond the presence of death that was dealt here some time ago, it manages to hold an aura of peace and serenity, as the towers watch down over the pond.

rooms.name: City of the Ancients: Eastern Path

userData.LongDescription: The long, winding road around the inner city breaks off momentarily at a hollowed mountain, left open by a concrete slab with a door fashioned into it.  The path eventually leads, after some walking, over a deep chasm, a very minor tunnel carved through the rock that would otherwise inhibit motion along the path.

A great city, made of what looks like white stones or bone stretches out here, before a gigantic white fossilized tree.  A trio of paths branch off, after leaving the bridge, off into the city's outskirts, along paths made of the same substance as the bridge across to the island.

Ahead of all the ruins that make up the City of the Ancients, a large series of trees and rock poorly conceal what appears to be a clearing of serene properties.  The branches of the tree seem to extend into the sky, passing several mountain peaks.  The rattling of guns, and faint explosions detonate within the ruins, as if a battle were being waged.

Beyond the trees and stones resides a singular shell-shaped house. Blue light flows down from a hole in the treescape, covering the entire clearing in a soft, phosphorescent glow, vaguely resembling a column of ethereal holy light descending from the heavens.  The entrance is behind a bony railing, and a soft, musical hum rings from within.  What appears to be a small crystallized pond lays in front of the house, the surface ruptured, as if it was not frozen in a quiet time.

The rocks that hold up this path appear to be coated with some green material, almost a mossy substance.  The path sloped, steepening a little as it came closer to the main road.  However, the sounds within the city became more pronounced, as the main road could be seen once again.

The forest ends slowly, the trees giving way to a series of rocks and broken tree limbs.  The green haze fizzles away, allowing the harsh light of day to shine down upon the once again dry stones.  The rocks break slowly up the pass, though there is a log one could crawl atop or through to continue on.  All that grows in this land are what appear to be orange plants that have solidified over ages of life.

The path that leads onward curves along the wall, and small pebbles crack off, descending into a vast, black chasm.  The end of the semi-circled path descends onto a small platform.  Several stones sat along the path on the wall, much akin to chairs.  The soft hum became much louder, and the light almost blinding as it radiated from the crystal.

The flight of stairs is near endless, but it offers a wonderful view of what looks like a room made of prismatic glass.  Surrounding this elabourate scene of a glass room is what looks like a pond.  Something resides in it, but it is hardly visible from this height.  All that surrounds this is a pitch blackness, no light save from the glass structures at the bottom.

rooms.name: West end of the main hallway

userData.LongDescription: The west end of the main hall has seen a bit more wear and tear then the central hall itself but it still is quite a sight to behold.  There aren't any pits on this side of the room and it's quite a bit darker as well.  There's still enough light to make out a door on the north wall with two decorated columns to its sides and another room to the south.  East leads back into the central part of the main room.

This grassy clearing lies in a small forest.  In the center of the clearing there is a huge, hollow stone with stairs leading into it.  Flowers decorate the top of this stone, almost as if the stone were a grave marker.  The opening in the rock and a rough path through the trees are the only ways to leave this place.

The stairs lead into a darkened room.  The floor here is completely covered with a crimson carpet and the walls are home to only two torches which create the room's dismal lighting.  Though it is hard to make out details due to the light, there are some stairs to the south and the ones that lead outside lie to the north.

This room is very simple.  A large cement block with faded, scratched out lettering lies in the center of the room.  It could have once been a tombstone, but it has long since been destroyed.  Fallen rocks carpet the floor here and a large, gaping gateway lies to the north.  The way to the south leads back into the eastern area of the main hall.

This room is very long and straightforward.  Red carpet covers half the floor, while the other half is more of the tiles that are in the rest of the tomb.  Some water-filled pits jut out of the west wall and a glowing save point shines to the north, near the door leading into yet another room.  There are several open chests here, one with what appears to be a shell lying near it.  The turtle is to the south and he can return weary adventurers to the main rooms of the tomb, while a single door leads north.

rooms.name: Room full of water, complete with a turtle

userData.LongDescription: This room is very, very large and this walkway on the western side is the only part that's not nearly completely full of water. A glowing button shaped like a skull decorates the north wall, but it looks to have been pressed a long time ago. To the north, a turtle waits to take weary adventurers back to the main hall of the tomb, ready to take anyone who wants to climb on its back for a ride.

rooms.name: Room full of water, complete with a turtle

userData.LongDescription: A massive basin is completely flooded with water, preventing one from walking east. The lower area has furniture and decorations at the bottom of it, and looks like it was once part of the tomb before it got flooded.  Across the water is a dry ledge with a door. A turtle swims peacefully in the water near the edge of the walkway, apparently to transport needy adventurers across the depths.

This room is well-lit, and in very good shape compared to most of the other rooms here.  Two torches spit blue flames that light up the room, while a treasure chest that apparently was opened long ago lies along the west wall.  There are stairs leading down, deeper into the tomb, while the door back in to the main hall lies to the north.

The stairway ends into a huge room with many doors.  The room looks to have been carved out of rock and the floor is covered with stone tiles. The pathway from the stairs is guarded by thick stone rails to prevent falling into the deep pits on either side of the walkway.  The architecture here is incredible, with the walls carefully crafted to stand the tests of time.  The room expands to the west and east, while a doorway looms to the south.  The stairs lie to the north.

This small room has four deep looking pits filled to the brim with water.  At the north end of the room a glowing skull-shaped switch embedded deep within a column.  The water is fresh and clean, providing a refreshing difference from the death and decay that surrounds this place.

This is easily the most decorated room in the tomb, and for good reason.  A large gravestone covered in purple cloth and adorned with flowers lies in the center of the room, surrounded by red carpet.  A small plaque lies in front of it.  The room is lit up by many torches and is nearly as large as the main hallway.  The only exit leads south.

This room is very cramped.  It is well-lit, though, due to the two torches on the southern wall.  The room itself has the same stone tiling as the main hallway.  A monolith with what appears to be ancient writings carved into it lies against the northern end of the room, red carpeting beneath it.  The only way out of this room is the door to the south.

The eastern end of the huge main hall of Daryl's Tomb is dimly lit, the only light supplied by the two torches from the central room.  Unusual sounds echo off the walls and the only way to find out where they are coming from lies beyond a door to the north or deeper into the tomb to the south.  To the west lies the central part of the hall.

The room is very well-lit, at least when compared to the room to the north.  The only decoration that stands out is an opened treasure chest in the center of the room.  The torches on the wall spit blue flames into the air, lighting the way out through the door to the north.

It's extremely hard to see here, with no torches or any other light source.  Another treasure chest lies in the center of the room, but it, too, has been open for quite some time.  The walls seem a bit weak here in some places, as well.  The stairs, though hard to see, will at least lead into a more well-lit area, and there is a door to the north, though it's been barricaded and is unopenable.

rooms.name: Room with water and a turtle

userData.LongDescription: This room is narrow and undecorated, save for a deep pit of water that leads south.  It doesn't look safe to swim in, so the only passage across is on the back of a turtle.  North leads back into the tomb's main hall, while the turtle can take adventurers across the water.

This room has four monoliths in it, each on a raised section of tile surrounded by red carpet.  The monoliths are nondescript, save for the letters engraved on them. Other then that, this room has nothing interesting in it.  The only exit is to the north, back into the room with a turtle and plenty of water.

This is a magnificent floating continent, high above the surface of the earth.  Nearby is a magical teleportation device that leads down to the surface of the earth, but to the east appears to be a large city of sorts, made up of domed buildings.  It looks like it could be worth exploring a little bit.

This is a balcony in Enhasa, in the eastern part of the city. There is a bed here, as well as a bookcase up against the back wall and a table with a lit candleabra. There is another balcony up north, as well as a staircase leading down to the entrance.

This small alley has nothing much in it but a large potted plant with yellow flowers. The walls have the strange arcane patterns, and the floor is made of grey tile. There is a balcony above that could be reached from a staircase in the main room. To the west is the entrance to Enhasa.

rooms.name: Center of the City of Dreams

userData.LongDescription: This is the center of the city of Enhasa, and there are exits leading in all directions. A set of golden stairs leads down to the entrance, while more staircases lead to rooms to the north and east. To the west is what looks like a shop, and another staircase up.

This room has a woman sitting behind a desk, who seems to be selling something. A sign hangs on the front of the desk. The city is to the north and then to the east. It's possible to see the entrance from the railing. A small stool is in the middle of nowhere here.

At the back of this cave, a strange device gives off a rainbow of colors.  It appears to be another teleportation machine, much like the one used to go to and from Enhasa.  An exit to the south leads out into the harsh, seemingly eternal blizzard.

The ocean stretches out from the east to the northwest.  The blizzard continues beating down onto the land, yet it does not freeze the seemingly boundless ocean.  The beaten path, less snow-covered than the surrounding ground, extends to the northwest and south.  Some frozen and lifeless vegetation can barely be seen to the west.

The ocean stretches out to the northeast, one of the few viewable contrasts to the grey dying vegetation, grey ground and the almost grey snowfall.  Gale force winds continue aiding the blizzard in making travel along the path miserable, helping drop the temperature even farther below the freezing point.  The path extends to the northwest and southeast.

You stand at the door of a dome shaped building at the front of what you can only assume is a city.  The dome that is in front of you seems to be the largest one in the cluster, and you can hear some hustling and bustling going on inside.  To the north seems to be another pad like you encountered on the frozen land.

This is what appears to be an inn of the time. There is a single bed that is occupied, and the innkeeper greets all who enter with a smile. The entire village is visible from this vantage, with its grey tile and red carpet, its books and magical patterns. There is also a table with a book on it and a pretty globe. The stairs lead back down off of this raised area.

The ocean stretches out to the northeast, one of the few viewable contrasts to the grey dying vegetation, grey ground and the almost grey snowfall.  Gale force winds continue aiding the blizzard in making travel along the path miserable, helping drop the temperature even farther below the freezing point.  The path extends to the northwest and southeast.

The blizzard seems slightly weaker here, yet it is still fierce and near blinding.  What limited amount of vision the blizzard allows shows the dark blue waters of the ocean to the east.  It's unlikely that anything could survive in the freezing waters for long, if for any amount of time at all.  The beaten path, less snow-covered than the surrounding ground, extends to the north and south.

Another dome, similar to the one somewhere in the general southeastern vicinity from here, lies to the west.  The blizzard increases in ferocity, almost as if it senses the safety the dome would provide to anyone who reaches it.  The ocean continues offering a contrast in color to the otherwise bland surroundings, although little else.  The path ends to the west, with the only other direction it goes to being southeast.

This is the northern most room in Enhasa. There is a bed here. A bookcase and potted plant are on the northern wall, as well as pair of windows. The only way back to the city is by way of the staircase to the south.

A strange device with a beam of light shooting straight upwards into and through the clouds hums softly, giving off a rainbow of colors.  Yet another teleportation machine, where it leads you to is unknown, yet it is likely to be somewhere on the floating continent, much like the one used to go to and from Enhasa does.  An exit to the east leads back out into the harsh, seemingly eternal blizzard on the lower land.

A grandiose view of the clouds can be seen from this vantage point north of Enhasa.  Yet another of the mysterious teleportation pads lies here, silently blinking a pattern, awaiting its next use.  Odds are it leads back down to the barren and cold ground, allowing further exploration of that region.

The blizzard continues its seemingly endless and rapid descent, severely limiting visibility.  If there are any forms of life out here, it's near impossible to find them.  One of the few things that can be made out in this freezing whiteness are the shimmering rainbow of colors from a telepad dome to the west, while a barely recognizable path leads to the southwest and further north.

The ocean stretches out from the east to the northwest.  The blizzard continues beating down onto the land, yet it does not freeze the seemingly boundless ocean.  The beaten path, less snow-covered than the surrounding ground, extends to the northwest and south.  Some frozen and lifeless vegetation can barely be seen to the west.

A strange device with a beam of light shooting straight upwards into and through the clouds hums softly, giving off a rainbow of colors.  Yet another teleportation machine, where it leads you to is unknown, yet it is likely to be somewhere on the floating continent, much like the one used to go to and from Enhasa does.  An exit to the east leads back out into the harsh, seemingly eternal blizzard on the lower land.

The blizzard continues its seemingly endless and rapid descent, severely limiting visibility.  If there are any forms of life out here, it's near impossible to find them.  One of the few things that can be made out in this freezing whiteness are the shimmering rainbow of colors from a telepad dome to the west, while a barely recognizable path leads to the southwest and further north.

At the back of this cave, a strange device gives off a rainbow of colors.  It appears to be another teleportation machine, much like the one used to go to and from Enhasa.  An exit to the south leads out into the harsh, seemingly eternal blizzard.

This is a high up perch in the northeast conner of Enhasa. The entire city can be seen, along with all of its technological marvels. There are two more beds here, as it seems important for the people here to get sleep whenever they need it. The only way back down is to the west, down a golden staircase.  A book sits on a golden table.

The blizzard continues beating down onto the land and gale-force winds whip through the air, both of which making visibility severely limited.   A dome, similar in appearance to the one housing the telepad used to travel to the floating city of Enhasa, can barely be seen to the north.  A path to the northeast leads further out into the blizzard... but towards what?

The blizzard continues beating down onto the land and gale-force winds whip through the air, both of which making visibility severely limited.   A dome, similar in appearance to the one housing the telepad used to travel to the floating city of Enhasa, can barely be seen to the north.  A path to the northeast leads further out into the blizzard... but towards what?

This is the first room of this strange, and yet intriguing place named Enhasa. The technology here is very advanced, and the society wealthy. There are golden staircases, elaborate looking wall patterns, and the floor has beautiful carpet. There is a table here with books on it, and bookcases against the back wall.

The blizzard seems slightly weaker here, yet it is still fierce and near blinding.  What limited amount of vision the blizzard allows shows the dark blue waters of the ocean to the east.  It's unlikely that anything could survive in the freezing waters for long, if for any amount of time at all.  The beaten path, less snow-covered than the surrounding ground, extends to the north and south.

Another dome, similar to the one somewhere in the general southeastern vicinity from here, lies to the west.  The blizzard increases in ferocity, almost as if it senses the safety the dome would provide to anyone who reaches it.  The ocean continues offering a contrast in color to the otherwise bland surroundings, although little else.  The path ends to the west, with the only other direction it goes to being southeast.

This place is a fork in the path in the western part of Enhasa. To the south is a shop of some sorts, and up the stairs it looks like there is an inn. Back to the east is the center of town. The patterns on the wall look especially ornate, and it is possible to see the entrance from here.

A huge doorway on the front side of the train leads... absolutely nowhere now, as its doors are closed, locked, and double locked.  The same can be said for the doors on the left and right sides of the train.  Additionally, the row of windows on the side of the train are covered by black curtains.  Unusual, since despite the boring view, many of the the passengers in the other cars still stare intently at the forest rushing by.  In any case, there are newly built walkways leading to the cars on the east and west sides.

The walls are covered with wires, switches, dials, gauges, and all sorts of other technological accoutrements that appear to be non-functional and generally out of place here, especially since it appears that whomever decorated the train was attempting to use them as decoration.  Of course, the ghosts don't appear to care too much about the looks of the car, since they're too busy wandering about aimlessly to do much else.

For some inexplicable reason, this car is a wee bit longer than the others.  Of course, it's every bit as shabby, and in fact, there's a bit of profanity spray-painted in glowing paint on the side of the car.  As always, there are doors on either side of the train, allowing access to the inside.  Of course, there are also walkways to the east and west that lead to the neighboring cars.

There are no benches lining the sides of this train.  Instead, there are tables and chairs set up all over the place, and surprisingly, ghosts are flitting in to eat from them.  There are no waiters to serve the food, though.  Instead, meals materialize on the table to be eaten by whomever happens to be sitting there at the time.  Of course, though, no stains or anything are ever left by any of the diners.

A long row of windows offers passengers a view of the forest rushing by, and not much else.  Oddly enough, there are two rows of seats here, and ghosts are occupying a good number of them.  The seats appear to be unusually nice, considering that just about everything on the train is dead.  The other part of the car lies to the west, and the way back to the outside is to the east.

This is the western portion of one of the two cabin cars on the train, and is every bit as logic defying as both the eastern end, and the other car, considering that ghosts generally don't do much resting.  There's a sliding door that leads into a cabin, though the ghosts simply float through without bothering to actually open it.

This car and the one to the west of it are easily the widest ones in the entire train.  Also, the car appears to be significantly less run down than the others, and sports almost intact ladders and a roof with only one hole.  As always, there is a doorway to allow access to the inner portion of the car.

The western end of the dining car is free of tables and chairs.  In fact, besides the doors, the only thing that stands out on this end is a rotten, and long empty wooden treasure chest.  Ghosts occasionally float by, either to exit the train or to feed themselves, though interestingly enough, not a single one of those ghosts looks to be a waiter.  Well, unless that's what they happened to be doing when they died.

Previously, a point of light within this car allowed travellers to magically save their memories, thus preserving themselves in case of disaster.  However, who- or whatever keeps the train running decided that the deceased really didn't need to be able to save their memories, since they'll have those for the rest of their eternal lives anyway.  So the point of light was extinguished, and the door was sealed.  Now this car's just the last normal one before the engine which is doing its steaming and tooting thing to the west.

A small sliding door has been installed into the front side of this car, and it's similar to the other doors on the other cars of this cosmic chariot that hurtles towards realms beyond.  In any case, there's also a ladder here, but of course, it's half-missing.  Not that ghosts would really have much need for a ladder... although maybe if there was one, there wouldn't be a gaping hole in the roof.

Much like the other cars, this section of the train doesn't appear to be very well cared for.  The 'roof' is pretty much non-existant, as it's made up of nothing more than one very large hole.  The ladder leading up there is mostly gone, as well.  Openings on either end of the car allow passage into the train, though the front door is stuck shut.

From the looks of things, this is an economy cabin.  The walls are free of decoration and colour, and the only furniture is a cot in one corner of the room.  Cobwebs adorn the corners, and holes adorn the walls.  Not too many ghosts pass in or out of this room and the few that do look to be fairly lower class.  There is, of course, a sliding door to lead out of this rat's nest and back to the outer portion of the cabin car.

This end of the cabin car is every bit as badly maintained as the other end was.  Worse, really, considering that not even the cabin door works properly.  A dark stain creeps into the rug covering the floor in this part of the car and it seems to originate from the cabin, though it's hard to imagine how ghosts could have created such a stain.  Almost as hard as figuring out why ghosts need cabins in the first place.

A finely woven red carpet covers the aisle between the seats, and as one might expect, there are no signs whatsoever that anybody has ever walked over it.  It's got a gold trim running along its edges, and it seems to be covered with all sorts of unidentifiable symbols.  The few ghosts who aren't sitting in their seats are pacing back and forth through the aisle, though no part of them is actually touching the carpet.

The western half of this train car appears to have been closed off for some reason.  A wall of pale, blue light seperates this part of the car from the western portion, and a sign reading, 'OUT OF ORDER' has been placed against it.  There's a sliding door in the south wall leading to the outside, and it looks as if there was also a way out to the east, but the boards nailed across it mean that somebody doesn't want anyone going that way.

Long rows of plush seats line both sides of the train car, and a few of them are occupied.  Occasionally, a ghostly waiter slowly walks down the aisle pushing a cart before him, and although the cart is completely empty, some of the ghosts are grabbing at the thing as if there's a feast laid out upon it.  In any case, the exit out of the car lies to the east.

A few looted chests line the northern wall of the cabin, and a malfunctioning light swings back and forth overhead.  A couch-type thing sits against the western wall and a table with two simple chairs is against the eastern one.  A rather well appointed room, considering its usual residents.  On top of all this, a dark painting that appears to have been inspired by the woods outside hangs above the couch, giving the room a rather ominous feel.

The train appears to be in a state of disrepair, suggesting that perhaps the deceased aren't very good at all with their hands.  The roof of this particular car is potmarked with holes, and the ladder leading up to it is missing several of its rungs, making climbing up there difficult at best.  An opening on the side of the car leads to the inside, and bridges to the east and west lead to yet more cars.

This car appears to be a bit smaller than the others, and only has one opening, on its left side, to allow access to the interior.  To compensate for the lack of a right-side entrance, though, there's a door right in the front of the car with a weird symbol on it.  Since this car marks the end of the line, so to speak, the only path leading to more train cars is back to the west.

The room is surprisingly well decorated, and quite clean, due to the fact that its main occupants are people who are very much dead, and thus don't leave much of a mess.  The carpet is the same bright red from the dining car, and the chairs look to be as plush as the benches from the first few cars.  All in all, those living here would probably feel rather lucky, if they were alive enough to enjoy it.

This is one of the few cabin cars on the train, though only two of the actual cabins are accessible.  Oddly enough, a steady stream of ghosts moves in and out of both cabins, despite their assumed lack of a need to sleep or rest.  In any event, another cabin car lies to the west, and the engine itself is just three cars in that direction.  Back to the east lies the dining car.

Like the car to the east, this car is unusually wide and very well taken care of, not unlike the average high society debutante.  There are no holes whatsoever in the roof or walls, and the ladder leading to the top is only missing two rungs.  There is a set of double doors leading inside the train, and walkways leading to cars on the east and west sides.  Additionally, it appears that the train's engine is only two cars down.

Despite the near lack of furniture, this is more than likely where the Conductor has his private quarters.  There's a table in the back of the room with an open book sitting atop it, and there's a glimmer of light in the southwest corner.  The walls are covered with switches and what not, although their purpose can't really be discerned.

A sliding door leads in and out of the third of four cabins on this train, though not too many ghosts seem to be entering or exiting it.  Right next to the upper-right hand corner of the door, a number '0' is hanging, and on the ground below are the numbers '0' and '3'.  Apparently, this cabin is about as well taken care of as the rest of the train.  The last of the four cabins as well as a door leading outside are to the west.  The other way out is to the east.

There are two doors here: One on the north wall leading to a back room, and one on the south side leading back to the outside.  A window on the back wall offers a view of the forest zooming by, though it isn't very entertaining.  Pipes, wires, and other such things are hanging off of the wall.  It's unlikely that the pipes and wires serve any real purpose, except perhaps providing a very, very unusual form of decoration.

This is the engine of the train, and the source of its power.  A huge smoke stack rises from the top of it, spewing out the smoke and steam that are the by-products of the methods used to keep this beast running.  There's also a door that leads to the inside of the train, but it's been welded shut, likely to keep curious passengers from entering and screwing with the train's ability to run properly.  Oddly enough, the ground here has a faint, red glow, something that every other part of the train lacked.

This high road overlooks a gently flowing brook which feeds into the open seas. It is a relatively secluded spot where young couples come for a romantic moon-light stroll and for making out. In the times since the end of the world, it seems like this place has been seeing a little less action.

This is the eastern end of the secondary dock. There are several rotting boxes still lined up in neat rows, ever waiting for the day when they shall be taken away. The sound of the waters lapping against the stone walls of the dock mixes smoothly with the sound of the soft breeze, calming the soul. The dock extends west, and there are also several planks leaned agains the ship for ease of access.

This shop is indeed sturdy. There are no indications at all from inside that damage might have occurred. Ornate shields mounted on the wall provide an excellent diversion from the mundane occurances outside, and the stylized armor on the display stands prove that armor smithing is a true art. There is a thick, wooden door in the south wall leading outside. Also, a set of stairs lie in the back, leading to some form of living quarters.

A burnt and blasted building resides here, choking the air with the smell of charcoal and ash. Apparently, this building suffered greatly in the times after the end of the world. Now, it has obviously been neglected in favor of faster and easier jobs. The soft light of the waning sun accentuates the places where the brown of the woodgrain morphs into the black of the ash.

This is the main room of the pub. A large phonograph beside the stage suggests some kind of music will be playing at some point. The stage itself is fairly wide, just large enough for one or two people to dance about, with some flower vases in the back. A microphone sits quietly on the stage, waiting for someone to take it up and begin a sweet song. More of the room lies to the east. Additionally, there is a set of stairs leading down to the main bar.

This small ledge oversteps the small stream that runs through Albrook. The water, though clear and gently flowing, does not appear inviting. The wall itself splits into a high arch over the stream, connecting as part of the ground for the upper city. Against the wall on either side of the stream are two long flower beds. They probably once held beautiful gardens, but now they are home to brown grass.

This alley tracks around behind the main buildings of Albrook, circumnavigating the rear portions. The buildings have no obvious windows on this side though there are holes caused by some form of attack. Also of note is a large section of the guard rail which is missing. In its place are some wooden slats nailed up as a make-shift rail until repair crews can devote some manpower to the job.

There is a mini-bar in the southeast corner of the room, providing a relaxed, out of the way place for a couple of weary people. This side of the room does not get the best view of the stage, unfortunately. There is a microphone set up on the stage, apparently ready for someone to start singing.

While the rest of Albrook appears to be recovering from some form of attack, the inn seems to be completely unharmed. The only sign of damage is that part of the rail along the edge of the wall is missing, providing a hazard for anyone who is not careful. Along the right side of the building several wooden barrels have been lined up, collecting rainwater.

This is a secondary dock, mostly used for the transfer of dry goods between ships. A few discarded barrels are all that remain as evidence of the way it used to be. The cobblestones are somewhat slippery from the moisture in the air, but aren't quite slippery enough to cause anyone to fall. The secondary dock extends to the east. There is also a large wooden plank connecting the ship to the dock.

This quaint building seems to be in better condition inside than out. The shopkeeper has obviously put a lot of time and effort into restoring his store so that he might get back to serving the needs of the townsfolk... and making a tidy profit. The shop is in good repair with a large cabinet on the right side of the shop counter. There are a couple of buckets in front of it, catching rain water leaking through the roof. On the other side of the room, there is a desk with a bookshelf beside, presumably for the shopkeeper to spend time during the slow periods of the day.

The pub is split between two floors. The second floor resides at the top of the stairs that lay in the north of this room. A long bar counter sits on the right side of this room with several comfortable chairs lined up against it. There is also a small table bedecked with a white tablecloth and a bottle of fine wine on the left side of the room. There is also a sign on the wall.

This end of the docks seem to have recently had work done as there are a few small crates with fruit that is just starting to rot. On top of the crates are jugs of stagnant water left behind from some voyage. Nearer to the edge of the docks, it seems someone has left a small pile of belongings. Additionally, there is a large wooden plank laid down for gaining access to the ship currently docked. The city access to the dock is east.

This solid road overlooks a slow-flowing brook. The cold water is crystal clear and reflects the light of the setting sun onto the far wall. A wooden skywalk just above casts a deep shadow toward the south. The metal rail runs along the edge of the walkway forcing travellers to go either west or south.

The weapon shop appears to have been made of sturdy construction. Despite the fact that its walls are a mess and it is missing several pieces of its roof, the building still stands strong, though business seems to have been a mite slow of late. The wooden door is closed, but the sign says the store is open.

The wooden ship creaks eerily as the empty boat gently rocks with the low waves creeping in from the open sea. The deck is nearly devoid of life. Some kind of buildup, likely a combination of dust and moisture, scruffs and streaks. There is a plank connecting the ship to the main dock, and another connecting to the secondary dock. It is also possible to access the rest of the ship, to the east.

The inn is a fairly small building. The main area is just large enough to hold a modest "sales counter" and a hallway leading to the sleeping area. Within the sleeping area are four beds, ready and waiting for someone to pass into a restful slumber. Behind the sales counter is a set of stairs leading to some unexplorable place. There is also a sign on the counter top.

The road converges from west and south into this northeastern corner of Albrook. Over the side of the railing, there is a free-flowing brook. Though the clear water appears safe for a swim, it is no doubt too cold to be thoroughly enjoyed. The chill water serves as a willing tributary for the open sea.

This small back room lies just behind the relic shop. The air is somewhat stagnant from a lack of proper circulation. It really is quite cramped and closed in. The only directions to go are up a set of stairs to another back room or south into the relic shop.

This is the once magnificent city of Albrook. The city is no longer magnificent, of course. Some form of attack has reduced many buildings to rubble while others are missing parts of their roofs and walls. The item shop here also suffered some damage to its roof, though it is still sturdy enough to provide for the populace.

This shop is well-spaced and tidy. A small table with two chairs sits in the left hand side of the shop with a bookcase nearby. A small vase with luscious red roses sits on the sales counter, bringing a homey touch to the shop. A large sign hangs from the wall, waiting to be read.

Soot and ash have mixed with the moisture in the air to form a sticky and gritty muck on the hard cobblestone roads. The ash and soot likely came from fires on the nearby buildings, such as the pub. There are many large holes in the wall just above the pub door, but it is obvious that repairs are underway. A skywalk above connects the pub to a small building, though the small building seems like a shed with no doors.

The Armor Shop stands tall and proud. Though it suffered from some attack, it remained solid and intact. Only relatively small portions of the front wall are missing, making it one of the least damaged buildings in the whole city. Two gentle brooks on either side of the armor shop feed into the ocean. The road makes a southward turn, heading toward the unused docks, as well as heading west toward the town entrance. As well, there is a set of stairs heading up to the upper city.

This is a relatively small storage room. In the south of the room, there is a set of stairs leading down. Beyond the stairs are four sealed crates stacked neatly against the wall. In the north of the room, there is an old grandfather clock, which doesn't seem to be ticking, and an ornate suit of armor, obviously for show. There is also a hallway leading westward to the main room of the pub.

This grassy area exists outside of Albrook proper but is still considered to be within the city's limits. There are several pine trees including a dense grouping that allows children to play games of tag in a small area. To the south is the city entrance and the item shop.

This road leads along the edge of the sea. Looking out over the open waters, the lights of Albrook were a kind of beacon to the seafaring vessels. But no more will the city lights lead ships inward, since the city was damaged so badly. Fewer lights shine now in an attempt to make the city less obvious to raiders and pillagers. There is a set of stairs running up the hole-covered wall to the upper part of the city. The road leads north and east.

This is the northeastern part of the room. There is a wood-burning stove heating a tea pot along the north wall. A large china cabinet beside the stove is locked. There are several tables set with white tablecloths, some optionally having bottles of wine placed atop.

This narrow alley is stuck between one side of a charred building and a waist-height railing meant to keep careless people from falling over the edge. Below, the item shop sits quietly, waiting its turn to have repairs exacted upon it. The cobblestones are more or less clean but for some unsightly footprints drudged in from up the road.

This is the living area for the shop owner. It's small and simple, but roomy for a lone bachelor. There is a bookcase filled with novels and reference books from all genres along the back wall. Beside the bookcase sits a large china cabinet. In the middle of the back wall is a stone, wood-burning fireplace, keeping the whole building warm. There is also a small, circular table with three chairs around it and a bed in the south of the room.

The inside of this shop is doing much better than the outside. Strategic placing of emblems and showcases covers the obvious holes while still keeping the interior fashionable. In the back of the room are mockup suits of armor with various styles of weapons for display, and there are a few boxes in a corner with more samples laid on tidy trays.

Once upon a time, before the Day of Judgment, Albrook's docks served as a sailing port for the Empire. Now, the docks look as if no one has tended to these cobblestones in years. A rope with anchor lies discarded. Several barrels which used to store grains and wheat are now empty and rotting. There is, however, one ship docked, but it doesn't appear to be going anywhere.

The relic shop stands tall and proud with only a few minor scars left over from days of old. A skywalk connecting the relic shop to the inn has been burned by some form of attack, but is still stable and enduring. The road heads east, toward the inn, and north, leading behind the main part of Albrook. It is also possible to walk down a flight of stairs to access the lower portions of Albrook.

This forgotten ship creaks and groans eerily as it slowly sways in the cold water. Two dead suits of magitek armor rest quietly, secured to the main cabin of the ship. Though it is apparent that their power supplies have been removed, it is a wonder the rest of the armors haven't been whittled down by the crafty scavengers. Around the back of the dark cabin, a rusty door seals away whatever dark secrets this old ship once held.

Overlooking a softly flowing brook, this high road provides a cool get-away from the mundane life. Young couples used to come here often, but that was before it became abuzz with repairs. It seems that the safety rail was damaged, as there is a length of wooden slat covering a gap in it.

Wide plateaus dominate the horizon and only the hardiest of plants are able to grow in the hard bronze clay of these canyons. Rocks are occasionally sheared from the cliff faces by the high winds that rip through the area. This unforgiving landscape is home to only the most tenacious forms of life.

Expansive fields of grass extend in almost every direction, swaying gently under the light of the sun. A warm, salt-tinged breeze blows across the plain from the southwest and mixes with the cooler air drifting from the mountains to the east and north, giving a crisp and refreshing feeling to any that feel it.

Expansive fields of grass extend in almost every direction, swaying gently under the light of the sun. A warm, salt-tinged breeze blows across the plain from the southwest and mixes with the cooler air drifting from the mountains to the east and north, giving a crisp and refreshing feeling to any that feel it.

A cool refreshing breeze blows under the canopy far above, rustling the leaves of the trees. Some tall healthy flowers rise above the lush, green grass which sways softly and is full of life. Vines hang down from the trees with flowers blooming off the end.

All the basic requirements of a kitchen are here. A refrigerator, and oven are to the west, while a furnace lies on a stone set ground in the northern corner along with some cupboards. The exit lies to the south.

The scent of lavender washes over you as you enter this room. A picture of a girl in her late teens sits on a desk in one corner next to a mirrored nightstand and an armoire. In the southeastern corner of the room sits a bed and a very expensive looking piano. The exit to the hall leads toward the east. On the desk is a conspicuous pile of suspicious documents...

The light filters in through several large windows on the eastern wall and the smell of curative items fills the air. A sign sits on a counter in front of a bored looking woman. It's odd that this shop has managed to stay in business for this long in a community this small.

Light filters in through a large window at the end of the room, showing a few dust motes floating through the air. The floorboards gently creak with each step in the area, but the wood feels quite sturdy beneath your feet. The room is obviously kept clean, but doesn't show any of the typical clutter expected of an attic.

A metal stove-heater combination sits unused in the corner next to a furry rug. A slightly dusty smell pervades the immediate area and sets a relaxing, calm atmosphere that seems very helpful for sleeping.  A long wooden counter with a sign stands in the eastern corner, and behind that sits an old man. To the east lies the door to the outside.

Stepping inside the master bedroom, you are immediately enveloped in a soothing silence. Two beds sit in the corner next to some other furniture, and the floor is covered with an ornate rug near the entrance. A potted plant sits opposite the entrance and seems to somehow complete the room. The hall lies back to the south.

A dirt covered brick path leads further north towards the center of a miniscule town nestled at the entrance to a mountain range. In the distance you can see a dark and monstrous mansion so large it almost occupies more space than the village sitting before it. In the middle of what seems to be the town square, a haphazardly constructed water tower rises about 5 meters into the air. The path continues to the north and to the south.

This little room is even more cramped than downstairs. A chair sits next to a small table that isn't very high off the ground, and a small box sits next to the table. There is also another larger chest on the other side of the room, next to a short wooden stool. There's nowhere to go here but down the stairs.

The wood flooring creaks slightly here under your weight. The light from a wall mounted lamp shines on a painting hung on the western wall next to the entrance to a bedroom, while to the north lies the entrance to what would appear to be the master bedroom.

Standing in the middle of the village, houses lie in all directions, save north and south. At the center of it all stands a magnificently unstable water tower, with a ladder leading up. To the northwest lies what looks to be a general store, and to the east lies a relatively large house with the door open. There is another house to the northeast and a wooden path to a southeastern house. The inn sits to the west and the path continues north to a large mansion and some mountains, while to the south lies the town's exit.

This house actually seems to have two floors, as there's a staircase in the northern part. A table sits in the middle of this floor, covered in papers. A heater is just west of it, and a kitchen area sits to the southeast.

This house is a very simple one-room place with wooden floor in the main part, and stone floors along the northwestern and northeastern sides. A small set of stairs leads up to the northwestern storage area. Along the northeastern edge of the house there's a kitchenette. The southeastern corner has a pair of beds in it, separated by a dresser. The only way out of this house is back through the door.

To the north, a large deserted mansion, falling down and broken, lies in view. The grass is brown and withered, but vines and weeds on and around the mansion seem to be thriving. Boarded-up windows and a shattered door give a sad look to the face of the mansion, but make it rather easy to get in. A gate leads to Nibelheim proper.

From a rather unimpressive vantage point five meters above the ground you can see all of the town; not really something to brag about, but a quaint view no less. Astoundingly uninteresting, this water tower seems likely to collapse to the ground at any moment. A ladder leads back down.

rooms.name: The Entrance to a Large House

userData.LongDescription: The slow, sleepy atmosphere that seems to be with the entire town is especially pervasive in this house. The sunlight streams through large windows to create a grid like pattern on the ground. A staircase to your right leads up to the next floor, while the entrance to the kitchen area is to north.

The view of the northern Nibel mountains is even more impressive here than from the town center. Just off to the west there is a decaying old mansion, with a gated fence surrounding the yard. To the south is the center of Nibelheim, as vacated as normal, while the path here goes to Mount Nibel in the north.

The vast throne room of Worus has one focal point, and that is the large stone throne that stands against the northern wall.  It appears to be unoccupied now, but this room is presumably where the King issues decrees.  The room consists of a central platform with a large rug leading up to the raised dais that holds the throne itself.  A short path leads west to a small landing that appears to be empty.  There is a similar landing to the east, but that one appears to have a staircase leading upstairs on it.  Every other available space in the room is taken up by sunken pools of crystal-clear water.

From this vantage point, one can truly get a sense of how tall the castle's walls truly are.  A vivid green meadow can be seen rolling far to the east, with only an occasional tree interrupting the green fields.  A slight rushing sound can be heard here, coming from the west, where the waterway continues.  The walls also head back north.

Aside from the movement of the water that flows slowly to the south, the only movement in this area is the occasional passing of a bird overhead.  To the east, the front side of a gigantic tower can be seen, which is a part of the castle's roof.  A massive, thundering waterfall crashes down from the very top, with enough force that it throws up a heavy cloud of mist where it hits that water below it.

The air in this sub-basement is, as is to be expected in a castle cellar, cold and damp.  And judging from the almost complete lack of light, the awful smell and the four jail cells that take up most of the room, this is probably the castle's prison.  The moisture can be attributed to the fact that water seems to have soaked through the stones themselves in some parts of the room.  A few ragged prisoners can be seen through some of the cell bars, along with their meager furnishings.  The only light the room does have is provided by a small flickering torch near the staircase leading back up to the main basement.

Tall pillars crafted of marble rise all around this foyer, supporting the magnificent vaulted ceiling.  The floor is elaborately cobbled with light brown stone, while the walls are made out of gray brick.  To the north, a beautiful woven rug leads into what looks to be a throne room.  There is also a large wooden door to the northeast, and a set of stairs leading down to the east.  The exit of the castle lies to the south.

This small, mostly enclosed area consists of a cobblestone bridge leading into the castle, two large pools on either side of the bridge, and is surrounded by the castle walls on all four sides.  Halfway along the bridge, there are two stone gargoyle statues flanking either side of the path.  A massive wooden door stands to the north, leading inside the castle, while the bridge passes under a portcullis to the south.

Towering stacks of books take up almost the entirety of this room, which is clearly the castle's library.  The many bookcases are in no particular arrangement, but rather scattered about the room more or less at random.  Other than the bookcases, the only thing of note here is a large switch on the ground that appears to have been depressed already.  The northern wall consists of two doors, while a staircase leads back down to the barracks.

This section of the barracks appears to be where the guards sleep, when they are able to.  A series of bunkbeds is set against the western wall, while a roaring fireplace stands along the northern wall.  A table that is much smaller than the one in the main area of the barracks is here, with several stools set around it.  Also of note are the several weapons that are on a display rack, as well as a suit of display armor standing nearby.

The entire northern wall of this room is completely covered with books.  Three massive bookcases are built into the wall, each laden with books.  This room appears to be where the more valuable books are stored.  Except for the bookcases and a small stool, the room is completely barren.  A door leads back into the main part of the library to the south.

The northwestern corner of the castle walls offers a wide vista of the western side of the castle moat.  The waterway continues to the east, where a large waterfall can be seen; and south, where there doesn't seem to be much of interest.  Other than that, the only thing notable here is the huge tower to the southeast that is apparently part of the castle's roof.

This tiny, cluttered room is clearly a storage room for Worus Castle.  Heavy oak barrels are scattered around the room, contents a mystery.  Several pots full of various cooking ingredients also take up space in the room.  There are two large crates against the northern wall, along with what appears to be a very old cabinet.  A staircase leads back up to the hallway above.

This small platform is on a lower level of the castle, and is a bit of a rendezvous between the basement and the castle's high walls, which tower above.  To the north, a small door leads back into the castle.  A small distance to the east, a large staircase gives access to the castle walls.  Between the two of them, a thin waterfall splashes down into a pool below the platform.

Sounds of the laughter and merriment of off-duty guards fill the room, leading one to believe that this area is the castle's guard barracks.  A long wooden table stands here, where the soldiers who protect the King presumably eat their meals.  Weapons hang on the walls, and the clang of steel on steel can be heard somewhere in the distance, possibly from guards sparring with one another.  The barracks continue to the west, while a small hallway leads east.  There is a door leading to the foyer, as well as a staircase leading to an upper floor.

The top of the castle walls is actually a waterway.  Ankle-deep water flows slowly to the south, though the water level never changes.  A stairway leads back down to the castle itself, and a large gargoyle statue stands guard at the top of the stairs.  The waterway continues to the north and the south, and in both directions it seems to turn at right angles almost immediately.

The small hallway from the south has led to a dead-end here.  The hallway forks to the right, and in normal circumstances one would be able to head down into a sub-basement.  However, the staircase down is covered by a heavy wooden trapdoor.  Somebody has stacked several very large rocks on top of it, and has hung a sign on the wall.  The rest of the basement lay to the south.

The sun shines brightly down on this corner of the waterway, causing a dazzling reflection of light on the surface of the water.  A thundering sound can be heard to the east, where there looks to be a waterfall.  From the north, water flows slowly down into this area before being directed to the east.  The castle lay to the northeast.

Rising high into the air to the north stands the magnificent Worus Castle.  A bridge leads into the castle, passing under a portcullis and a guardhouse.  Hanging on the outside of the guardhouse is a small flag, proudly displaying the crest of Worus.  Twin waterfalls splash down from the castle walls to the north, on either side of the bridge.

This small corner of the waterway is fairly mundane, though there is a great view of a sprawling meadow to the east.  A large tower can be seen a short distance to the west, and the soft sound of a waterfall can be heard in that direction.  One of the edges on the eastern wall has fallen into ruin, and a small flow of water trickles off the edge, forming a small pool of water far below.

The most dominating feature of this section of wall is the rather large tower connected to the north side of the castle wall.  It does not appear to be a part of the castle itself, however, and its purpose is not that clear.  The front of the tower is taken up by a large waterfall that crashes down from the roof high above.

This small room is largely dominated by a wooden bookcase, filled with neatly ordered books.  The rest of the room is mostly empty, except for a small writing table and across from that, a desk that is roughly twice as big as the table.  There is a large globe on top of the latter.  The only light in the room is provided by a torch burning brightly on one of the walls.  A door leads back into the main section of the library.

The hallway coming from the barracks to the west heads first east, then south after hitting the eastern wall.  At the end of the hallway is an open trapdoor, with stairs leading to a room below.  The only other thing of note in this hallway is a large tapestry hung on the wall.  The barracks lay to the west.

The layout of this basement is that of a figure-eight almost; two small circular rooms set in a horizontal row, sharing one wall-less side.  Either of the two side-rooms has an ornate column standing in the center of it.  The room to the west contains, aside from the column, two staircases: one is going up, the other down.  In the eastern room there are instead two doors, leading north and south.  Several torches are set into stone sconces built into the walls here, providing ample light.

The path stops heading east here, as it runs directly into the western side castle's guardhouse.  The water that would normally keep flowing east is directed south, over the open edge of the wall, forming a waterfall.  The waterfall sends the water hurtling into the castle moat below.  The waterway can be followed back to the west.

An air of decay hangs in this bedroom, giving one the feeling of being in a sickbay.  A extravagant canopy bed set against the northern wall takes up a large portion of the room, while two massive pillars help fill more of the space.  On either side of the bed, a bookcase has been built into the wall and laden with books.  Other furniture in the room includes a wooden desk that normally could be used for writing, but is now covered with a wide array of fragrant flowers, in a futile attempt to spruce up the room.

The waterway stops abruptly here, allowing no further passage to the west.  The wall runs into the castle's gatehouse, the roof of which is a good bit higher up than the walls themselves.  The southern edge of the wall here is flat, and the water flows off the edge in a cascading waterfall.

The northeast corner of the basement does not appear to get very much traffic, judging from all the cobwebs covering the walls and ceiling.  The fact that spiders can survive in the dampness is somewhat impressive.  To the south and west, a path leads to different parts of the basement.  To the southwest however, there appears to be a raised platform in the center of the basement, but access to it is blocked off from here.

A small stream of water flows down the southern wall, near where it intersects with the eastern wall of the basement.  It appears to trickle down from a large leak in the ceiling above.  The path around the basement continues to the north and to the west, and in this area, a path leads northwest through the blockades to the platform in the center of the room.

Upon entering this room, a scrabbling and squeaking sound can immediately be heard.  Along with the occasional sound of something splashing in the shallow layer of water on the ground, it gives the impression that rats have made their home here.  A large set of stone stairs in the southern end of the room lead upstairs, while another staircase opposite those leads down.

The clear water in this corner of the basement reveals a gruesome sight: mostly submerged and leaning against the western wall is a human skeleton, which is in good condition except for the lack of muscles and flesh.  Slightly above where the skeleton lay, the bricks of the wall have crumbled and shattered somewhat.  A pathway leads northeast, and another path continues around the basement to the north and east.

This small room is understandably damp, considering the path outside leads underneath a waterfall.  The floor also has a small layer of stagnant water on the floor, adding to the dank atmosphere of the room.  A staircase to the north leads down into the gloom, and some of the water trickles slowly down the stairs.

This large raised platform affords a view of the entire basement.  However, it doesn't seem as if that was the original purpose of creating this dais.  A small marble display stands in the center of the platform, and a faded rune is at its base.  Paths lead down to the southwest and southeast.

A couple of torches hanging on the walls of this room valiantly attempt to fight the darkness, but only succeeding in keeping the mild gloom from being pitch blackness.  The torches flicker, and their light is barely reflected on the surface of the water on the floor.  A large staircase leads up, while an identical one leads further down into another level of the tower.

The water in this portion of the tower reaches to nearly knee-level, though it is surprisingly clear.  This basement is rather large, sprawling out in a general southeastern direction.  A staircase leads up to the higher levels of the tower, and paths lead south and east to other sections of the basement.

This cramped steel-gray corridor seems almost like an afterthought in design based on its size and positioning.  To the south, it would have terminated in a dead-end connected to a ventilation shaft, before the Meteor quakes opened it up anyway.  The northern end was designed with only slightly more access in mind; it also finishes in a dead-end, except for a crawlway entrance located in the eastern wall.

A cluster of support beams situated immediately inside the reactor makes for a safe place to stand.  The bulkhead - a three foot steel wall previously designed to protect from immediate threats to the reactor - would make for quite a formidable sight... if it were not for the man-sized breach situated to the south which can be used to bypass the wall.  To the north, across a hollow space occupied by a dense lattice of scaffolding and support structures, the innermost parts of the reactor are barely visible through the dim interior lighting.

The massive wall that separates Sector 6 from Sector 7 has withstood all of the devastation that shook Midgar, and still towers overhead, serving as a barrier between the sectors. However, here at the edge of the city, the wall ends.  The great concrete wall extends from the center of Midgar out to this point, where it once connected the exterior wall of the city; that exterior wall has been torn down, though.  Only empty wasteland lies outside of the city, but it's possible to go around the end of the wall to the northwest.

The shrouded shapes of machinery and a closed-in system of railings, ladders and walkways make for an altogether more cramped atmosphere than the buffer space in the outer areas of the reactor.  The air is stagnant and still carries a tint of smoke to it, further diffusing the dull red emergency lighting.  The exit from one of the many crawlspaces extends onto one walkway which leads off into the murky distance northwest.  Metal and empty space limits any other choices but the crawlspace to the west.

An old ventilation shaft - now collapsed and opened out - makes for improvised access into the reactor.  Whatever instability led to this minor wreckage seems to have faded over time, making this entranceway as safe as any found in these ruins.  The debris curves to the north where it collapses into one of the reactor's many service passages, while to the west, one of the main structural catwalks lies across a three-foot leap.

The main sector wall and the incomplete plate provide unneeded shade along the beaten path.  Exploration elsewhere is discouraged by the jagged metal, broken glass and other detritus lining the trail, leaving just the path southeast to the salvage site and the looming reactor to the west as sensible choices.

Halfway across the buffer space, the scaffolding opens out into a central support platform, wider than most.  Beams and piping converge, just another link in the entire structure.  However, the angle that most of them hit the platform at means that only the central north-south pipe is safe enough for travel.

A canvas tent has been set up here in the rubble as a watchpost.  Corporate markings on the tent and the supplies surrounding it indicate that it is owned by the World Regenesis Organization.  A large computer terminal and some sort of radar console are hooked up to a generator, displaying cryptic data.  A water pump and some surveying equipment sit outside the tent, along with a stash of weaponry.

At barely two feet high and three feet wide, the crawlspace is more inconvenient than cramped.  It is a mercy that the designers were thoughtful enough to reduce the number of sharp edges and stray bits of piping along the sides of the corridor.  The access has held up well in the wake of Meteor and seems much safer than most of the surrounding area.  To the east, the crawlspace opens up into the inner layers of the reactor while west simply leads back along the treacherous route to the outside.

The metal walkway opens up into a circular platform that leads to the very core of the reactor, a towering structure set into the wall of the chamber.  A rusty but servicable wheel valve juts out from the bottom of the core at waist height; in Midgar's heyday, it would have controlled the intake of mako through five major inlet pipes.  Instead, it is just another relic of the city's past.

The precise center of the chamber is here, on the only walkway that connects the service and piping accesses to the very core of the reactor.  With only the supports at either end suspending the walkway above the vat of mako far below, the effect is vertigo-inducing.  Thankfully, the environmental danger is more illusory than real - there appears to be no danger of any more significant structural collapses this deep.

The gantry passes close to a particularly large chunk of electrical equipment at this junction of ladder and walkway.  Compared to the lower gantry, the smoke is slightly denser here, tinging everything visible with the rust-red hue of the lights.  The ladder connects the northern end of this walkway to the upper gantries and looks to be the route to take to approach the core itself, while to the southeast, the latticed grating trails away back to maintenance corridors and ultimately, the buffer space and outside.

Resting against one of the larger pillars, a platform marks the end of one of the main catwalks.  Normally, it would have joined into a west-east gantry, allowing further access to the maintenance walkways; however, the immediate beams leading away have collapsed, and the distance to the next section is too far to jump.  This leaves only the southern walkway leading past the inner sector and back to the bulkhead or a ladder attached to the pillar itself, leading up into darkness.

Normally, this walkway would have progressed further round the reactor to the north-northwest.  However, such access has been violently interrupted by wreckage from the past collapse of many girders and walkways from above taking out a good ten yards of floor with them.  This leaves just a relatively small portion of walkway supported by the eastern wall and the ladder that leads to the lower levels.  Fortunately, this section of the gantries opens up to the northeast into one of the main service corridors of the reactor: eventual access to the core is still possible from this location.

Internal failures located in this part of the reactor have led to a break in the emergency lighting and a subsequent plunge into darkness.  However, the ambient light from the north and southeast sections of the corridor still offers enough to see by.  The floor itself is quite clear of debris despite the problems in this area, and the worst neglect that can be seen is the odd patch of peeling paint from the walls.

Sticky white strands cover the steel wire mesh that the ladder led up to.  Cocoons of various sizes serve as a meat locker of sorts and higher concentrations of the gunk near the rear of the meshed area form bedding.  Grashtrikes, one of the many mako-induced abominations that live in Midgar, have made a nest.  They have likely been preying on the natural fauna, as well as any unwary traveller or salvage worker who happens to be around.  The only way out is down, back into the light.

Once this path led along the interior of the metal wall that comprised the edge of the city of Midgar.  Now that wall is shattered and crumpled, more of a hazard than a true barrier.  Glass shards, once making up part of the barrier, cover the ground.

Comprised of debris from both the derelict reactor and the abandoned construction of this sector, the 'platform' is remarkably solid underfoot.  The debris piles up all around the towering edifice, providing the only possible way to get close enough to the reactor wall.  A couple of ruined girders allow safe descent to a path below, while the platform itself continues west towards an apparent opening in the bulkhead.

This breach in the main wall is only one tiny bit of evidence of Meteor's effect on the city, having created a makeshift entry where before, none was possible.  On the outside, traversable wreckage begins and ends here, with only passage to the east around the reactor available.

The service corridor ends abruptly, with a heavy bulkhead to the northeast completely closing off access to the junction itself.  A large, gaping crack in the western wall where it meets the bulkhead hints at the problem - major structural damage rendering the area impassable.  Twin lines of lit arrows point the way to the southwest, back towards the main service station.

This final chamber is the heart of Reactor 7, once the most important location in the entire sector.  Now the machinery lies silent and the vast mako reserves collected below are left to slowly drain away, back to the earth they came from.  A walkway stretches out across the abyss towards the other side of the chamber, where the very core of the reactor lies.  To the west, an opening in the wall marks the entrance to the nearby service area.  Finally, next to the opening are the torn remains of a ladder that would've allowed access to the piping above: an unorthodox route which would've eventually led - by a far riskier path - to the once safer and less restricted parts of the reactor.

Curving slowly from the south to the northeast, the service corridor continues along the outer edge of the reactor core.  A conspicuous humming sound accompanies the nonstop flickering of the emergency lights in this section of the corridor, making this a less than pleasant location to stay in.  The only other real thing of note are the two lines of arrows - flickering in time with the lighting - that adorn the walls, pointing the way south to the main service station.

A wall of debris leans against the side of the reactor, and to all intents and purposes creates a permanent end to this trail through the ruins, leaving only the eastern route to the salvage site open.  However, some ruined yet well placed girders provide a somewhat stable way to ascend the wall and approach the reactor itself.

A massive, fifteen foot tall, two foot thick shard of broken glass has been driven into the ground, and stands upright in the middle of the path.  It was apparently once part of the barrier around the city.  Now it's just a safety hazard.  Large sections of the mangled metal barrier have been hammered into the ground and covered by dust, leaving the area truly looking like ancient buried ruins.

The main junction of the service corridor opens up into a large, brightly illuminated chamber, a stark contrast to the hazy gloom found elsewhere in the reactor, including around the core visible through the nearby gateway.  Various trolleys, equipment and tools can be found occupying the niches and corners of the room, though their placement is somewhat disorganised from the tremors caused by Meteor.  Corridors lead in both directions around the inner sector to the north and south, while the primary purpose of the service area - the reactor core itself - is accessible to the east.

Without access to one of the other gantries, this is the closest this north/south catwalk gets to the inner reactor.  A three-foot leap to the east is all that's necessary to enter what may have once been a crawlway or ventilation shaft... but is now ruined and open enough to give standing room and a safe way inwards.  The catwalk continues north towards another platform, and south back towards the bulkhead.

The lighting is better in this part of the corridor than in nearby areas, which both highlights the importance of the main service area as well as the relative lack of damage in this location.  It is not untouched however: a bulkhead to the southeast has completely closed off that direction, likely due to extensive damage further along.  Opposite, the corridor curves to the northwest, with a series of lit arrows along each side pointing the way to the main service station.  The only other route is the southwest door that leads out to the gantries overlooking much of the reactor's processing facilities.
