The sandy town is surrounded by palm trees, blocking the way west into the desert expanse.  There is a small, stone building with no actual door, but a trapdoor leads into a cellar below it.  The trapdoor is locked.  Clay pots are strewn about the exterior of the building.

This inn seems somewhat strange.. it is surprisingly well decorated and hardly fits into the blazing sands outside the door.  Stranger still, foreign plants and pots decorate two small desks which sit near the inn's beds.  There is yet another dancing merchant behind the inn's desk.

A huge cannon takes up most of this small clearing.  A short man bounces around in front of it, apparently guiding the cannon so it gets its occupants to wherever they please.. assuming they please to go to the Ice Land, the Empire or Matango, that is.  A short walk west leads back to Kakkara Town, while you can be shot out of a cannon to one of the three locations mentioned.

This oasis can be seen almost anywhere in Kakkara Town and is probably its star attraction.  There are many more flowers here then anywhere else in the town and they surround the sparkling oasis.  It's almost tempting to take a sip.  The main path leads south, back to the town square.

The town square, though small, is somewhat impressive with flowers dotting the pathway and a shop set up to provide tired travelers with some supplies.  The oasis sparkles in the sunlight just off the path to the north.  The path stretches to the east, west and south.

Though it's just a few steps off the path, this section is completely uninhabited.. a stark contrast to the happy, civilized area to the west.  A few flowers dot the sand and the palm trees prevent any further movement east or south.  North, though, leads back to the stony path that leads through Kakkara town and west leads back to the entrance.

A merchant dances merrily in front of a large building, indicating that his shop is open today.  A sign is planted into the north side of the path through town.  The path itself leads west into Town Square and east to an open area while south leads off the path and into a patch of desert.

A stony path surrounded by small clay pots and palm trees leads into Kakkara Town.  The air seems cooler here, it's almost refreshing in and of itself.  To the north, a man is happily greeting anyone who passes by and happiness seems to come naturally here, even though the town is in the massive Kakkara desert.

The inn is, like many other buildings in the town, made completely out of stone.  It has three windows and is conveniently located right next to the oasis itself.  On the edges of the path, flowers have grown in much greater number than anywhere else in the town.  To the south lies a small, uninhabited patch of desert and east leads back to the town square.

A small stone building provides a cool, refreshing shadow on the path as it continues to the north.  A few palm trees lie to the eastern side of the path.  A man is dancing here, greeting anyone that comes by.  To the north lies the town square, where another dancing man seems to be tending to a shop of sorts.  The oasis itself can also be seen, sparkling brightly.  South leads back towards the entrance of town.

rooms.name: A few steps to the west of the path

userData.LongDescription: Palm trees and flowers dot the sand.  A small, stone building with no visible entrances lies a few steps to the north.  Clay pots are seemingly placed at random around it.  Other then that, the palm trees create a barrier or sorts that blocks any further movement to the west or south.  North leads into the main part of the small oasis town, while east leads back onto the path.

The desert clears out, surrounded by cliffs and palm trees, making a wide open area big enough for a large beast to land.  A few rocks litter the ground, but fewer than in other places in the desert.  Kakkara Town offers respite from the desert heat to the north.  There is a drum tied to a pole that could be used to call Flammie...

Nothing but a vast amount of night black extending infinitely far in all directions. Drifting aimlessly through the darkness that is the 'floor' are many points of glowing light: stars and constellations in the panorama that makes up this bizarre temple. Among the stars, the white disk of a distant moon glows brightly below.

Calling this place a 'room' would require a considerable suspension of disbelief. Instead of a floor, there is naught but an endless expanse of dark void extending as far as the eye can see no matter where one turns. Suspended in the inky darkness are uncounted points of faintly glowing light, a galaxy of false stars in this most unnatural space.

This is the Moon Palace's Stage Room, where the Mana Seed of the Moon is kept. The far wall of this large room is adorned with four tall cathedral stained glass windows, with a central window that is circular. Tall white pillars similar to those outside line the side walls, and the Stage is surrounded by six bronze braziers in a half circle. The stage at the center of the room has a palpable aura of power.

Across the Sea of Wonders, the looming expanse of the Moon Palace is visible from this pier-like causeway where Karon's ferry makes its stop. Made of a dull gold brick and lined by white marble pillars, the color of this place gives the impression of an autumn moon's light. A set of large, wide steps lead up to the Palace's double entry doors.

This is an endless expanse of night black extending infinitely far in all directions. Floating unattached through the blackness that is the ground are a number of points of silvery light: stars and constellations for the night sky that makes up this strange place. Among the stars, the mutlicolored swirl of a nebula shines in hues of scarlet and purple as well.

Nothing but a vast amount of night black extending infinitely far in all directions. Drifting aimlessly through the darkness that is the 'floor' are many points of glowing light: stars and constellations in the panorama that makes up this bizarre temple. Among the stars, the white disk of a distant moon glows brightly below.

It is inaccurate to call this place a 'room'. It would be more appropriately called a 'vista'; the ground is not ground at all, but an endless expanse of blackness extending infinitely far in all directions. Scattered among the black are numerous points of luminence, and it becomes obvious that it is not ground, but a night sky! A half circle of violet flames mark the black portal that leads out of this place.

A stark change from the black void of the illusionary Palace, this small square room is made of the same dull gold-colored brick as the outside of the Palace. Huge bronze braziers line the east and west sides of the room, burning with a dark violet flame. In the center of the far wall is an archway and the stairs to the stage room; flanking it on either side are two circular stained glass windows of violet and lavendar panes.

Pure elemental energy suffuses this realm, to the extent that nearly nothing else exists.  There are no perceivable floor, walls, ceiling, just mana.  It is a realm beyond mortal comprehension, and is where the most powerful of elemental beings reside.

Nothing but a vast amount of night black extending infinitely far in all directions. Drifting aimlessly through the darkness that is the 'floor' are many points of glowing light: stars and constellations in the panorama that makes up this bizarre temple. Among the stars, the white disk of a distant moon glows brightly below.

A massive dais dominates the attention of the throne room. Atop the platform, which has been fused into the floor, is the massive Imperial throne. This is where the late Emperor Gestahl ruled his empire with an iron fist. The carpet in the hallway to the south runs up to and surrounds the dais. Two elegant chandeliers radiate a soft glow, which reflects off the carpet and bathes the room in a reddish hue. A small, barely noticeable door is set into the north wall, behind the throne.

The second floor of the stairway is nothing more than a small landing between staircases. At the top of the stairs from the lower level one is instantly confronted by a doorway into the soldiers' barracks. A second staircase leads upward to the third floor and access to the palace rooftop.

As the door opens a horrid stench of stale beer assaults the nasal passages. The bar is decorated from ceiling to floor in Imperial banners and propaganda while a large fire burns in the hearth on the north wall. Aside from soft music playing in the background, the only sounds are the gentle slurping of ales and the squelch of feet tearing away from the sticky floor.

The private quarters of the late Emperor Gestahl are lavish, cozy, and downright excessive. A soft, red carpet covers the entirety of the floor and a warm blaze crackles in the fireplace. A massive portrait of Gestahl hangs above what might be the most plush bed in the Empire. Atop the bedside table rests a small, black, time-worn book.

This large, wide open section of Vector has been cleared of any debris or rubble so that reconstruction efforts may begin. The numerous steel columns and vents that previously occupied this space have been removed and salvaged. Any relatively portable structures are constructed here and shipped throughout the city for installation. Several freshly poured concrete slabs are interspersed among crates of materials and tools.

This brightly lit room is dominated by a massive reception counter and an extravagant chandelier. It appears that a great deal of time and money has been spent repairing the interior of the building. There is a sense that the innkeeper has several high-ranking and wealthy patrons, as evidenced by freshly laid carpet and the Imperial banners displayed on the walls.

A once-proud metropolis, Vector was the jewel of the Gestahlian empire. It has twice been reduced to smoldering ash: once by the rampage of the Espers and another by Kefka's apocalypse. The technology and steel beams that supported the infrastructure of the city now barely stand upright. To the north, the Imperial Palace looms above the city, standing tall as a testament to the might and dominion that was the Empire.

A massive staircase connects the city of Vector to the courtyard of the Imperial Palace. Guard checkpoints are stationed on either side of the staircase while impressively large Imperial banners cover the span of a raised wall. At the base of the stairs the cobblestones of the city give way into elongated metal plates that, when fused together, form the ground underneath.

A balcony in this section of Upper Vector overlooks some tracks underneath. Several wooden crates have been torn apart and used to repair missing sections of the railing. Below, a cart flies by every few minutes, screaming down the rails toward the unloading station in the southeast corner of town. Further to the east the Magitek Factory spouts off the fumes that are polluting the sky above.

A grand total of three cells make up the entirety of the Imperial prison. It was not the policy of the late Emperor Gestahl to capture many prisoners and so only a small prison was built to suit his desires. The prison block is filled with various instruments of torture, several of which are yearning to be used.

The Imperial Courtyard is anything but an actual courtyard. A narrow bridge circumventing the statue of the Guardian serves as the sole public passage between the city and the palace. On either side of the pathway is a railing and, beyond that, a short drop into a rather deep ravine. The metal plates that form the path underfoot creak and groan as one traverses the bridge.

rooms.name: In the shadow of the Guardian

userData.LongDescription: In the invasion of the Espers, the Guardian protecting the Imperial Palace was destroyed. The enormous Magitek creation has been cast in bronze in memory of the brave Imperial soldiers and citizens of Vector who died in the defense of the Empire. It forever stands at the gates of the palace, protecting the Empire and its subjects. Below the Guardian, a plaque affixed to a large concrete slab is inscribed in memory of the decisive epic battle.

The top of the stairwell mimics the design patterns of the visible lower levels; a small, cramped and otherwise ordinary space that provides passage to other parts of the palace. A door in the western wall gives off a slight breeze. Combined with the metallic composition of the building, the temperature in this part of the stairwell is quite chilly.

Unmade bunks and ravaged wardrobes litter all corners of this filthy room. The soldiers' barracks is one of a few rooms within the palace that is not cold and void of all personality. Playing cards and empty bottles cover a small table in the northeast corner of the room while a makeshift bathroom has been sectioned off in the northwest corner.

A large wooden sign bombards customers by reading 'Welcome to Imperial Arms, protect yourself from the Returners!'. A young man, presumably the shopkeeper, watches the store warily from behind a display of fine edged blades. An urn and small painting rest upon a shelf mounted to the wall.

The interior of the armory is just as dismal as the exterior of the structure. In addition to the sizable holes in the eastern wall, a few of the armor stands have been torn to shreds. Despite the horrid appearance of the establishment, business has been rather steady as of late. The army needs to be clothed, after all. An old man is working on a clock in the back of the store and glances up every few moments to recheck his wares.

A single track rail system bisects the street and transports supplies to and from the Magitek Factory. The track begins at a raised concrete platform and trails off to the northeast. Each shipment pauses at a checkpoint to be inspected by Imperial guards. The cart is then unloaded, reloaded, reinspected, and sent back down the tracks.

Warm air rises from below and condenses as it mixes with the breeze flowing in from the rooftop. A soft vapor blankets the area, making the floor underfoot rather slick. Stairs lead down to the lower levels and a small door leads out to the rooftop. A rather unobtrusive sign hangs on the wall.

The plush accommodations present in the outer room do not persist throughout the rest of the inn. A large, dirty brick fireplace encompasses most of the north wall and grimy mattresses populate the room, waiting to be dressed. All in all the back room of the Heart of the Empire Inn can only be described as less than ideal. The most luxurious object in the room is a painting of the late Emperor Gestahl.

This small cramped room is used primarily for the storage of various cleaning and maintenance items needed for daily palace life. Small boxes will all sorts of labels can be found here. One box labeled 'Esper Juice' has been ransacked and left behind. Not much else is in this closet.

A thin hallway and a short flight of steps connect the foyer of the palace with the throne room. A blood red carpet, matching the banners on display about town, disguises the cold metal floor and creates an inviting, albeit tense, environment. At the top of the steps a pair of heavy, ornate metal doors open inward to reveal the seat of power for the Empire, the throne room.

A one-way rail system runs from the back door of the factory and connects the tracks to the south. Every few minutes a cart flies down the tracks at breakneck speeds. It then disappears to the south to be unloaded. The sole entryway to the factory is thirty feet off the ground and only accessible by traversing the tracks. Due to the frequency and danger of carts, entrance here is impossible.

The air here is warm and moist. A small vent gives off steam every few minutes and provides ample heat to the stairwell. A large entryway in the eastern wall gives way to the dark hall where from the darkness within, muffled cries can be heard. The stairwell here leads to the upper levels of the palace while the door to the west leads to the foyer.

The ramparts on the rooftop of the palace overlook all of Vector. Far below, speckles of blood red contrast heavily against the dark rooftops of the city. A thick smog floats about the city, occasionally obscuring the view from the rooftop. Stairs lead to an upper level while doors on either end of the ramparts lead to their respective descending stairwells.

This rundown store appears to be the Vector Armory. A more heavy-handed attempt has been made here by the Imperial bureaucrats in order to mask the building damage caused by the recent tragedies. Imperial banners are affixed to the side of the armory as well as a steel column that formerly held a ventilation shaft. A large staircase leading to the upper level of Vector is laid into the northern wall.

This landing in between staircases has been draped with plush, red carpeting. Two large ornate doors stand guard, exuding elegance and importance. Beyond them lie the personal quarters of the Emperor. Above, the ramparts can be accessed, and below, is the rest of the palace.

rooms.name: In Front of the Vector Weapons Shop

userData.LongDescription: The weapon store sits tucked away in the southwestern corner of Vector. Crates of various shapes and sizes, many marked 'Albrook', stack five-high on both sides of the shop entrance, demonstrating the shop owner's active investment in new merchandise to attract customers.

Blood red banners hang prominently from the roof of Vector's inn, contrasting heavily against the dark, smog-filled sky. Despite the recent catastrophes, active industrial facilities indicate that efforts to rebuild both the city of Vector and its national influence are progressing. The sign next to the inn door reads 'Heart of the Empire Inn' and would appear quite welcoming if it were not propped up upon a pile of rubbish and loose cobblestones. A staircase along the northern wall of the city leads to the upper level of Vector.

Cobblestone streets transform into fused metal plating as they move closer to the Imperial Palace. To the south, one can see all that Vector has to offer: half-rebuilt homes, pollution, broken cobblestones, and bright red Imperial banners. The chaos caused by recent events destroyed much of what Vector used to be, but from here the city looks to be rebuilding.

The upper level of Vector houses the main military compound for the Imperial Army and thus there is a heavy military presence here. The damages here were more severe than those in the lower levels of town as the Espers concentrated the bulk of their attacks around the palace. However, the majority of Vector's repairs have occurred in this area thanks to a little military coercion. Stairs to the lower level lead in two directions: to the southeast and the southwest.

In the center of this small room is a reclining steel table, much akin to a surgeon's operating table. Attached to the table are a multitude of cables running from a control mechanism along the north wall. An occasional squeak or groan can be heard from the pipes as steam is forced throughout the room to power the machinery. The simple existence of this room means that the Empire has reactivated the Magitek program.

Until the officials in charge of reconstruction decide how to dispose of them, crates have been stacked upon crates and abandoned here. A newly repaired air filtration system intermittently discharges a gush of clean, breathable air. This small corner of Vector has become a bit of a secret hangout spot for off duty military, as evidenced by the hundreds of cigarette butts and broken bottles.

The quality of air vastly decreases the further north one travels along the rails. A deep breath causes one to inhale a plethora of unnatural chemicals that surely will eventually kill every last citizen of Vector. The tracks run in a north to south fashion and a cart zooms by every few minutes.

A succulent feast is laid out on the massive banquet table that commands the room. Lobsters, white and red wines, and fresh game birds are but a few of the fancy offerings available for consumption. Such an enormous amount of food could surely feed a hundred of the less fortunate citizens of Vector. Yet, only a few chairs and table settings have been laid out. Clearly this is a very exclusive dining location.

Of all of the buildings in town, the bar has been perhaps the most important establishment in the aftermath of the violent attacks. The barkeep has quite literally housed, fed, and clothed many of the citizens of Vector. As such, the bar is very well respected in the city. Empty crates are piled on top of each other and function as tables for bar patrons wanting to survey the city whilst they drink themselves into oblivion. The whole scene would be very endearing, except that something smells like vomit.

The uppermost balcony of the Imperial Palace provides a complete view of the entire city of Vector. The late Emperor Gestahl would stand tall above his subjects and deliver his propaganda over loudspeakers throughout the metropolis. It is here in this very spot that the exploitation of Espers began en masse.

Two massive doors mark the entryway to the Imperial Palace. Just beyond those two steel behemoths dwelled the Emperor and thus, the most influential man in the world. The symbol of the Empire, a black Magitek Armor, has been proudly plastered over each of the doors.

One might expect the entrance to a Imperial palace to be quite grand and exquisite. That is far from the case. Aside from the main entrance, this small and rather unimpressive room has four doors, to the east, the north, the west, and south back to the city.

Once again fully operational, the Magitek Factory spouts off a thick, dark cloud every few seconds. The source of the rampant pollution blanketing the sky above Vector is obviously this industrial behemoth. After the Imperial Palace, the Magitek Factory was the second structure in Vector to be repaired. It is a vital contributor to the might of the Empire.

This small space at the bottom of the western stairwell is completely covered by metallic panels. Not one piece of organic material was used in the construction of the palace. A soft breeze blows down from the roof access on the upper level and the echo of soldiers can be heard from somewhere nearby. A small door is set into the western wall.

This corner of the Magitek Factory is overbearingly hot, due to the industrial smelter built into the western wall. Materials are shipped here in order to be stripped down to their base compounds before being used throughout the factory. The floor around the smelter is marred and stained black. Stairs lead north and an elevator grants access to a supervisory platform.

Cigarette butts and empty liquor bottles litter this small storage room. Steam pumps rapidly through large, round conduits along the walls. An odd vibration fills the air, as if some machine up above were furiously breathing life into some mechanical war machine. There is a save point in the corner, should an adventurer wish to rest for a while.

A conveyor belt runs into the floor from the north, making passage back to the factory entrance impossible. An old treasure chest rests next to a blocked off ventilation pipe. Stairs lead southward and provide access to more of the factory and a second conveyor belt travels eastward. An outdated deconstruction machine is cast aside here.

A massive generator is pumping steam into pressurized conduits before being dispersed throughout the factory. One such conduit appears to be working overtime and ready to burst. A chute rests about ten feet high, nestled into the northern wall. While the platform continues to the east towards stacks of crates, a wide conveyor belt speeds to the southeast.

A narrow metal platform serves as the landing for the top of the long staircase. A thin railing is all the protection provided between the landing and a short drop down to the trash compactor. The air smells cleaner here, like antibacterial chemicals. Many floors below, something can be seen slithering along the floor.

The elevator consists of a small, rectangular platform complete with a railing and a control panel. The shaft speeds by as exposed wires give of sparks and metal beams groan under the weight of the platform. Up above the Extractor is in full production, and far below a light and a small room can be seen.

The narrow scaffold underneath protrudes from the northern wall and collides with a staircase to the south. From here, one can observe the happenings of the major mechanisms throughout the factory. A clipboard rests against the leg of a folding chair. The scaffold shakes softly as production continues.

A short peninsula juts out from the southern wall and provides a view of the northern half of the factory. Conveyor belts run to and fro, transporting supply crates and other raw materials. To the west the smelter extrudes an enormous heat, which is amplified by the height of this platform. The factory entrance can be seen far to the north, and a door to the south leads further into the factory.

This must be where the voices were coming from! This hidden room is littered with empty liquor bottles and magazines. A small chest lays closed in the corner and the door is the only exit. The machine just beyond the door violently shakes the alcove.

rooms.name: The Other Side of the Tube

userData.LongDescription: A small platform greets those who emerge from the tube. Still covered in dust and debris, this space was not a part of the factory refurbishment. A chest sits here, its contents pillaged long ago. A railing prevents workers from falling onto the conveyor belt below.

rooms.name: The Other Side of the Ravine

userData.LongDescription: A small landing is perched on the opposite side of the ravine. As no one other than factory workers are meant to be here, there is no railing to prevent the short trip to a long fall. Several crates are stacked here, and among them a rather stout chest. The hook that provided access to this ledge dangles precariously from the crane.

In the center of the factory floor, several large machines are producing nearly identical weaponry units. The machines themselves are identical in appearance except for their color identification. The units produced are also color coordinated and separated in similar fashion. The factory floor continues to the west and the north while a wide conveyor belt is located to the northeast.

A wide metal garbage chute hangs suspended in middle of the room by enormous support beams. Industrial waste and other debris is occasionally tossed down the chute where it assimilates into years of mold and decay. Two access hatches are set into the northern wall. It is oddly quiet, despite the muffled noises heard from the factory floor high above.

A small platform marks the entrance to the recently rebuilt Magitek Factory. A short staircase leads down to the main factory floor and another leads out to the city of Vector. From this vantage point, all sort of steam-powered machinery and metallic structures can be seen.

Rows upon rows of enormous test tubes line the southern and northern walls of this rectangular passage. Espers of all breeds and sizes were forcefully captured by the Empire and brought to this laboratory. They were then suspended in a strange, yellowish fluid within these tubes. Other than the occasional thump or monitor blip, is horribly silent.

At the bottom of the elevator is a small yet busy room. Minecarts full of supplies are often launched from here, and run along the tracks to the city outside where they are shipped around the world. The elevator sits along the northern wall, ready to transport back to the Magicite extraction room. An empty minecart awaits.

This section of the factory has been dedicated to supply storage. Crates have been piled on top of each other to the point of toppling over. Even with the high ceilings, this is a very cramped and dangerous platform. Stairs lead down to the southwest and the platform continues east along the north wall.

A massive industrial behemoth dominates this section of the factory. Countless pipes and control panels are on display, and a conveyor belt spits out newly constructed Magitek units. This mechanical goliath shakes the ground underfoot, and without a doubt, the entire factory. Despite the ear-shattering noise of the machine, voices can be heard coming from somewhere nearby.

This industrious laboratory is far from tidy. In fact, this small lab is a complete mess. Half completed experiments and scientific research lay discarded on lab tables and stools, while burners simmer unknown liquids. Crystalline blue shards are being sorted according to size and shape. The larger shards are separated for experiments and the smaller piled and set aside.

A long, metal platform stretches north to south along the wall. Two conveyor belts appear to be the only accessible routes to this platform. The belt to the north feeds into here while the one to the south runs into a wide opening in the factory wall. Some empty chests and a smashed crate rest here.

The southwest corner of the Magitek Factory provides a grand view of the factory operations. To the north a door leads into another part of the factory, while the balcony continues to the east. A massive machine below is constructing Magitek units. Unseen voices can be heard from beneath the balcony. Perhaps there is another room below..?

Long, hollow tubes are stockpiled against the western wall. A complex assembly line is strung out along the southern wall and is manufacturing Magitek missiles. Completed missiles are then carefully loaded into massive shipping containers. A staircase leads up to a balcony where one can see the entire production. More mechanical monstrosities can be seen to the east.

Somehow, trash has escaped from the compactor and now litters this small landing space. There isn't much here other than the soft thrumming of machinery and the occasional steam let off from the pipes overhead. A magnitude of stairs leads upward, away from the trash compactor and the smell that pollutes this room.

This portion of the factory floor appears on all fronts to be the hub of all new Magitek operations. Innumerable steam-powered machines and electrical equipment buzz and whir to create the illusion of a very profitable industry. Large transportation tubes line the walls, one up a small ladder to the north that leads to a conveyor belt, another to the south, and one that leads down into the depths of the factory. Two large cranes loom over a large ravine.

The massive piece of technological ingenuity known as the Magicite Extractor was the driving force behind the reconstruction of the Magitek Factory, as it is able to harness such horrific power. The controls for the Extractor itself are aligned with the northern wall.  Espers of all shapes and sizes inhabit the test tubes here, and appear to be enduring excruciating pain. The occasional soft whimper can be heard from the pitiful creatures.

Every few minutes a factory worker will deposit something into the dark abyss that encompasses the majority of the floor here. To the west, across the gaping hole, enormous machinery can be seen assembling Magitek units. An elevator in the southeast corner leads up to a balcony above. A conveyor belt cuts through the floor, and transports larger pieces of waste into the abyss.

Coming out of the pipe leads to a hidden room containing two empty chests. Someone found this space long ago and walked away with some treasures. There isn't much left except a small scrap of paper left in the corner.

From here most of the factory can be seen. There is a large storage area to the north, the thrum of a machine piecing together Magitek units to the west, and a gaping hole in the factory floor below. The balcony underneath continues along the southern wall to the west. An elevator here will ferry passage to the factory floor.

On the east side of Nikeah, the grass grows thick, slowly overtaking the grey stone road with greenery.  It looks like there's an out of the way shop with large doors to the north.  The front door of the inn, and the rest of town for that matter, is to the west.

Nikeah has a modern, comfy inn available for all travelers at an affordable rate, attended all day and all night by a dutiful employee.  The employee gestures vaguely to a cash register with a sign attached to the front.  The beds look pretty comfy, maybe it's worth it to take a rest here.

The town of Nikeah appears to be very urban and upscale; the entrance is surrounded by modest, sturdy buildings.  The houses are packed so close together that the view around them is blocked, and only two small stone paths lead into the city, one to the northeast and another to the southeast.  A few people walk in and out of town casually, attending to business.

rooms.name: In front of Nikeah's weapon merchant

userData.LongDescription: With several boxes full of trading goods, the merchant here is sure he will not run out of stock under even the busiest of days.  He displays several of his better pieces on the boxes, one being the highly prized and deadly enhancer.  He has a list of what exactly he sells on a box, next to the enhancer.

A pile of trading goods marks the entrance to the cafe even at a distance, barrels and crates on their way out of town leaving just enough space for the door to the cafe.   Travelers enter and leave the cafe, some departing, some arriving, others just taking a break from shopping the busy market.  The majority of traffic comes from the south, towards a large ship, and the east, where the market begins.

Nikeah's market is a haven for traders looking to buy goods.  The stone ground is covered in boxes and barrels, stacked high atop one another.  Several merchants' signs can be seen from here, a lamp sign to the north, a sword sign to the west, and a third bearing a shield to the southeast.

The pier forms a large, loosely horseshoe-shaped enclosure around the sailing ship, and it appears all sides of it are used for storing something or other.  Scattered near the edge of the pier are boxes, jars, a cheap statue, and someone's luggage that was never collected.  The starboard bow of the ship comprises the view to the southeast.

A few barrels here mark the beginning of the Nikeah market, along with the steady stream of passerby looking at objects and gazing out over the open ocean to the south.  To the north, an odd collection of goods stands next to an awfully young storekeeper.

rooms.name: A clearing next to a lake

userData.LongDescription: The south shore of a freshwater lake laps against the ground here.  Vegetation grows thick right up to the edge of the water, and underwater too, judging by the dark shapes beneath the water's surface.  Several small trees grow around the area, but not enough to obscure the view of Nikeah to the south.  The single stream through Nikeah starts here, and can be followed back to the town.

East of the main entrance, the back end of the ship just enters the harbor provided by Nikeah's pier. Cans, bottles, and boxes lay on the ground near the ship, apparently dropped from ship and never collected by anyone, left to the elements.  A grappling hook is also resting on the ground, atop a coil of thick rope used to tie the ship down.  With the impending disembarkment of the ship, the rope must have been removed.

West of Nikeah's cafe building, boxes are stacked to hold the nonperishable goods the Cafe uses irregularly.  The weapon seller can be seen to the northeast a short ways away, and smoke from the cargo ship is blowing on the wind.  The stone paths here are lightly traveled, the flat rocks worn more from weather than from travel.

The bustle of Nikeah's market being left mostly to the east, this side of town is just used for storage of nonsalable goods that the town uses up in daily life.  A few people gather here to talk quietly together, and a reddish brick wall separating the market from the town looms high overhead.  A small stream of water flows between the wall and the grey stone pier.

Set against the swiftly flowing stream from the north, this small area is squeezed between several decently sized houses.  The inn, and a small grassy area are visible to the southeast, and stone paths extend to the north, with a glimpse of trees and a large body of water in that direction, where the urban sprawl ends.  To the southwest, towards the town's entrance, townspeople casually stroll about.

Most of the barrels kept in Nikeah are stored here, dozens of them stacked high with liquid goods.  The surrounding area is heavily traveled, one of the main corridors of traffic between the market and the dock.  There appears to be a person dressed in purple selling defensive equipment to the east.

rooms.name: In front of Nikeah's item merchant

userData.LongDescription: The shops in Nikeah don't seem to be any more than collections of goods, sold in the open air by merchants hoping to get more customers before they leave town.  The merchant here has various jars, potions, and odd herbal cures on display, and many more in barrels and crates around the warehouse to the east.

South of the ship, more boxes of goods are stored and awaiting transport to their final destination.  The majority of the pier is just above water level, with a small area elevated to match the height of the large ship, permitting loading and unloading.  The end of the pier is to the east, by the rear of the ship.

Nikeah has endeavored to add a little greenery in the otherwise drab, industrial township here by planting a little garden in the middle of the street.  The flowers are blooming, and it makes the inn, whose front door opens onto the small space, a little more welcome.  The stream from the lake to the north of town seems to stop at the inn, or goes under it.  The stairs to the marketplace are east of here, with the sellers and buyers spread out across the large converted pier to the south.

In a niche to the eastern side of Nikeah various protective clothes are laid out, displayed in order to show the glitter of the craftsmanship.  The merchant is decorated in colorful clothes and surrounded by numerous boxes of other goods, extras to the display items.  Passerby busily hurry about the market further west.  A list of his items is pinned to the front of a robe.

From here the massive length of the cargo ship at its moorings is just a step away, and people walk up and down the gangplank, loading and unloading goods from it.  Passengers are boarding the boat steadily from the stairs, and smoke rises from the cargo ship as the engines warm up.  Further to the north lies the destination of all new arrivals here, Nikeah.

The large sailing ship carries many travelers to and from the town of Nikeah, and has proven its seaworthiness many times since the world's collapse.  The bow points to the west, to the masonry of the pier.  The aft of the ship is the only side not protected from ocean waves, and is the only way for the ship to sail in or out.  Boarding planks are laid out to the north and south, for loading and unloading goods.

rooms.name: In front of a chocobo shop

userData.LongDescription: The acrid smell of chocobos fills the air before the large building which, by the sign, functions as a stables for the large yellow birds.  The stone street leads right up inside of the building through its widely spread doors.  Thick green grass grows against the edges of the street, flat from being trampled by travelers and steeds.

A building was built off to the side of Nikeah here, with just a thin strip of land between the door and a dropoff into the water.  Perhaps because of its small size, goods are left outside of the building, a collection of wooden crates piled in front of the south side.  The ocean laps audibly against stone, audible memory of how the trading goods came here.

rooms.name: At the top of the stairs

userData.LongDescription: If the northern half of Nikeah is little but housing and the south little but business, it is here where the difference becomes clear.  The town's commercial area spreads out in the view to the south, filled with boxes, barrels and crates along with the displayed wares of busy merchants.  A stone stairwell leads down amongst the merchants, while a path running west to east takes travelers from the entrance of town to a large stables.

Contrasting the view of the drab urban buildings to the east and west, the sea stretches out into infinity, dark blue waters lapping at stones that make up the town's sea wall.  A few people pass by this way towards the ship visible further south, its smokestacks already sending tendrils of smoke up into the air as it prepares to leave.

The chocobo shop smells strongly, acrid odors rising from piles of hay in the corners of the warmly-lit stable.  A small area at the entrance to the stable is roped off from the area where livestock is kept, and several large feathered birds strut around the stable making noises to each other.  An energetic caretaker is required to keep up with the birds, and the owner busies himself brushing down the yellow birds, checking their birds' food and water supplies, as well as cleaning their stalls.

Several boxes have been left here, storing miscellaneous goods for sale on the Nikeah market, while buyers and sellers from other places around town pass by, their footsteps resounding on the hard ground.  The back of the cafe provides a windbreak from the breeze that blows in from the ocean, and dirt collects in the corner against the building.

At the far end of the horseshoe shaped pier, only a narrow portion of masonry encircles the large ship docked here. Waves roll steadily towards town, from places far distant.  Seagulls cry out loudly and circle overhead, skimming over the waves for food.

A narrow stone pathway around the front side of the ship comes within inches of the ship's bow, begging the question of whether the ship is too big for its port.  The vessel is tied down firmly though, preventing it from damaging itself.  Looking over the ship, it's full of people looking off the sides as it gets ready to leave for South Figaro.

A large building blocks sight of the northern area of town, but the view is unrestricted in every other direction.  The inn's door is just to the northeast of the building's corner, and Nikeah's huge market sprawls in a generally southeastern direction.  The town has a tall sea wall separating it from the market and, seen to the east, a set of stairs leading to the much lower market area.

The local cafe is pretty small compared to some around the world, having only a few tables apart from the long bar.  There is only one waitress, kept busy by the steady stream of people entering for beer and other cold drinks.  A large phonograph is up against the north wall, next to a poster.  There is only a single doorway in or out.

Wedged between the cafe and the edge of the marketplace's pier, a young salesman paces back and forth, selling a collection of odd wares designed to protect one from various mystical elements.  He dresses himself in old clothes in a subtle attempt at feigning poverty, and attempts to coddle people into buying things from him with his energetic and engaging manner.

A small stone bridge from the market leads into the shipping area of Nikeah.  A long steam ship with powerful engines occupies most of the view south, and is being loaded with goods for its usual run to South Figaro.  All around the yards, more goods are stored waiting for transportation or money to get them to a buyer.  Twin stairways descend to the dock itself, just above the water's level.

North of the dense cluster of houses in Nikeah the town abruptly ends, leaving the stone path to be overgrown by lush, green grass from the area to the north.  Some small trees are growing well, with a thick grove blocking the view to the west.  A slow stream flows from the north out of a small lake.

The southwest corner of the pier seems to be used as liquid storage, judging from the abundance of barrels here. A few other jars of green liquid stand out from a collection of junk piled up on the ground, alcoholic most likely.  A grappling hook is attatched firmly to the pier by a long coiled rope, which must've been detached from the ship recently.  The ship's south entrance is to the east.

The snow has stopped blowing now, making it easy to see.  To the far north you can barely see a couple huts that might be a small village.  There also is what appears to be a kettle, but you are not sure from this distance.
There is a small sign here that you might want to try reading.  You notice that the clouds are getting darker now, it might be a good idea to take shelter, but none can be seen in all directions.

There is a little dusting of snow on the ground here.  However, there is a huge drift to the west, and there is another drift to the south.  The drifts make it impossible to go in those directions.  To the north there is another huge icicle in the ground marking the path.

This is the cannon room of the Ice Country.  In here there is a cliff with a cannon on top of it, ready to be shot at any moment.  There is a little man here waiting for instructions on where to shoot you.  To the west is the Ice Forest.
You are standing in the middle of a clearing with snow on the ground and trees all around.  To the far north you can see a huge ice fortress. To the west is another small clearing.

To the north there is a small village.  It looks like the village hasn't been occupied in a while.  There is also a small brown kettle that looks good for cooking things. To the east and the south is more ice and snow.

The warmth from the fireplace overwhelms you as you enter this hut.  There is a bed in the corner and a chair besides it.  You also see a workbench with christmas presents scattered all over it.  There are decorations all over the walls and floors.

To the north there are four red icicles in the ground to help distinguish the path to the north.  To the southeast is a small sign. There is also a huge red icicle coming up from the ground to the south blocking the path.

There is a nice festive looking hut here. There are lights on the roof and on the sides of the house, and a snowman right in front.  Also coming up to the house from the sides are several small snow drifts.

This is a freezing cold hut.  There is a fireplace on the north wall which is insufficient to heat the place.  On the east wall there is a bed with frost-covered pink sheets.  Next to the bed is a small table with papers all over it.
As you walk out of the village there are a few red icicles in the ground to help mark the path.  Back to the south you can see the village, and to the west you can go deeper into the forest.

The snow and wind are blowing so hard now that it is becoming almost whiteout conditions.  It has become nearly impossible to tell which way you are going.  You could probably follow the tree line to get around, though.

This is the entrance to the Ice Forest.  Todo Village is back to the east.  The trees in here are covered in ice, making them look very beautiful.  There are also some strange red icicles that come up from the ground in the shape of a pentagon, and there are more of these to the northwest.

The snow is really starting to blow, causing it to drift everywhere.  To the west you see some small icicles in the ground that seem to be marking the path.  To the southeast there is a big icicle that helps define the path also.
To the north of there are tons of red icicles in the ground that seem to be around Neko.  It might be worth your while to go north and see what Neko has to offer.  To the east is another clearing.

There isn't any snow on the ground here, it seems that it is melting away.  There are three more red icicles comming up from the ground, which are surrounded by a dozen trees.  To the west you can see another small clearing

In here there is a cliff that prevents you from going north.  There are also some more red icicles to the east and west of you.  There does appear to be a path to the southwest and the southeast though.

In the snowy forest is a small village that has three nearly-identical huts.  There is a big brown cooking kettle on a raised platform that looks scorched from overuse.  There aren't any people around, so it's a safe assumption that this place has been abandoned.

The snow is not as deep here, making it easier to walk around.  It's really hard to tell which way your going in here though because it almost all looks the same.  To the north you can see a small sign, and to the west is another clearing.
You are completely surrounded by cliffs and icicles here.  There are two huge icicles on either side of you and a couple smaller ones on each side of the huge ones.
The snow is continuing to blow and drift everywhere making it very difficult to see and move.  There are a few more icicles in the ground here that look like they are here to help mark out the path.

There is a huge cliff right in front of you here.  Next to the cliff there are some red icicles in the ground hidden behind some trees.  To the south there is a hut with a reindeer wandering around outside it.

The snow has started up again, but thankfully it isn't coming down that hard at all.  To the northeast you can see some more red icicles in the ground.  Back to the east you can see the path that leads back to the village.

There is a small snow-covered hut here, with drifts leading up to its sides.  There are a couple bushes along the side of the hut that are covered in snow as well.  The hut looks poorly insulated, with large picture windows.

There is a little snow covered hut here that has drifts coming up to it on all of its sides.  There are a couple of bushes along the sides that are covered in snow as well.  The hut looks poorly insulated, with large picture windows.

Seemingly in the middle of nowhere stands the Ice Palace, a large castle in the middle of the frozen tundra. Although it is called the Ice Palace, the interior appears to be more inviting than the bitterly cold winds in the forest. A door serves as the only entrance and exit, and it appears to be fairly worn down from either weathering or use.

This is a nice warm hut.  There is a fireplace on the north wall to heat the place.  On the east wall there is a bed that looks very nice and warm.  Next to the bed is a small table with papers all over it.

There is a huge tree here that towers above all the rest.  It's visible from almost anywhere in the forest, and beneath its thick branches is an area clear of snow.  To the east, south and west there is are three small huts.

This is a freezing cold hut.  There is a fireplace on the north wall which is insufficient to heat the place.  On the east wall there is a bed with frost-covered pink sheets.  Next to the bed is a small table with papers all over it.
The snow is blanketing the ground here and it is so deep that it is hard to walk.  The trees are really dense in this part of the forest, but there does seem to be a path to the north and the east.

There are red icicles surrounding you here.  To the north is a huge ice fortress, but the gate to enter it is locked and closed. Fortunately, someone has pulled some of the gate apart, leaving barely enough room for someone to squeeze through. To the south is back to the clearing.

The path through the forest splits into a three way crossroad.  To the northeast there appear to be some red icicles coming up from the ground.  To the northwest are more red icicles, hidden behind some trees.  To the south is a small clearing, freshly blanketed with snow.

You are at the entrance of a small town called Todo.  There is snow all over the ground making it very hard to walk around.  All around you can see trees towering above.  There is a line of stones marking the way to either side of you.  Off to the east you can see some small huts which would appear to make out a village.

This is a nice warm hut with a fireplace on the west wall.  There is also a counter and a chair behind it.  In the middle of the room there is a big colorful rug that looks like it has been here for ages.

This is a nice warm hut.  A bed occupies the west corner of the room, with a chair beside it.  On the east side of the room there is brightly burning a fireplace, which explains the warmth in the room.  There also is a huge rug in the center of the floor.

There is snow blanketing the ground in here.  To the east there is a stream that has frozen over, which comes from a lake to the north that is frozen over as well.  There is a small hut in here that is covered in snow. The hut looks like some sort of item shop.  There seems to be some other sort of hut to the south as well.

From this road, the ice lake is barely visible to the north through the blinding snow, with the stream heading off in the east.  The snow is coming down hard, and it would be dangerous to stay outside long in this terrible weather.  There is a hut that looks like it could make for some good shelter.

In here there are many small drifts that lead up to an Inn.  To the west and the south are many snow covered trees which make it impossible to go those ways.  To the east there is the frozen over stream.

This is the northeastern corner of the village, and there doesn't appear to be much here.  There are trees to both the north and east of here, and the main part of the village is back towards the west.

This inn is very warm and cozy compared to the blinding snow and harsh cold outside. Warm beds occupy each corner and each looks perfect for a nice rest.  A fireplace on the north wall crackles merrily, keeping this small inn toasty.  A small sign hangs on the wall opposite the entrance.

This is a nice warm hut.  There is a cleanly-made bed in the west corner of the room, and a wooden chair beside it.  On the east side of the room there is a fireplace, but no one has lit a fire inside of it.  There also is a huge rug in the center of the room.

There is nothing more than a bunch of snow drifts leading up to a hut here.  The trees seem to only be to the south of here. To the east you can make out what appears to be another snow covered hut.  The sky seems to be getting darker as if it is about to snow.

Built in the town by an inspired Todoian citizen, this shop has a small variety of mage armor in it, whether it be hoods, bracelets or light body armor.  The shop is very quiet, with a lack of customers.  A gentle fire lends an orangish glow and heat to the room, reflecting the simple yet kind nature of Todoian citizens and of the city itself.  A small Todoian girl sits behind the counter, smiling as she hums a tune to herself.

The snow is deeper and whiter than ever here making it very difficult to walk.  There are trees to both the east and the south in here.  There also seems to be some sort of hut in here.  It has also begun to snow again so it might be a good idea to take some shelter.

This is the entrance of Wutai, a nostalgic town with many little pagodas and a monument to the local gods. The air is calm and fresh and the grassy plains reach as far as the eye can see. No guards seem to be posted outside, thus everyone is encouraged to enter.
This is the western side of the bridge spanning one of the Wutai continent's
The bridge crosses a chasm to the west, connecting two cliffs. Two sturdy

This is an elevated gazebo supported by a square base.  Four posts, one in each corner, hold the roof up and serve as elegant red and gold decorative pieces.  There is a small space around the base, perhaps intended as a walkway.  It is unclear what the purpose of this shrine is; however, one thing can be said.  With it's elegant red and gold design and fragile, gentle architecture, it's an absolutely beautiful structure.

This is quite a stately and comfortable-looking room. It is well-furnished, bearing many valuable and attractive artifacts, trophies, and pieces of art. In the middle of the room is Godo's bed, a small, simple, elegant piece of furniture.  Near the bed there's a small wooden table with some bowls on it, and a medium-sized hutch rests against the northern wall.  The most prominent feature of the room, however, is a large mural spanning the length of the eastern wall. There is one exit in the room, the door to the west.

This is the guest room of Godo's house.  It bears a very comfortable,  homely feel to it, and the three futons lined up across the northern wall look quite inviting.  Above the beds ornamental curtains skirt  down the wall, perhaps concealing something, perhaps just covering a window.  A large painting dominates the majority of the west wall, save for a small, indented area of white drywall.  The only thing of note to the south is a doorway.

The door leads into a smaller room below the house of the old man. It seems that he recently moved a lot of stuff from above down into the basement, including some rugs, futons, some old furniture and even some old magazines. The room is a bit in disarray as someone seems to have ploughed through the previously neatly arranged piles.

This is a large, single-room shop with hardwood flooring and white walls.  A large counter spans from north to south on the western side of this room, behind which a young attendant waits to serve customers.  Random objects, from merchandise like potions and elixirs to rolled-up rugs and crumpled paper, lie haphazardly about the perimeter of the room. There is a sign, too, on the wall.

This short dirt road runs north of the main entrance to Wutai.  At its end, a door leads to a small shack, and to the east, a staircase leads up to another building.  Running parallel to the road on the west is a beautiful stream, one of Wutai's many.  While no part of Wutai can be said to lack tourism, this area is free of the more obtrusive shops and attractions that occupy the western side of town.

Two hallways meet here in a quiet, dimly-lit corner.  While in most places the silence and darkness would create an uncomfortable feel, it serves here only to enhance the mystique of the home and one's respect for that mystique.  This section of the house is completely spotless: not a speck of dust or grain of dirt can be seen. Two doors along the east wall lead to two separate rooms, and another doorway ends the hallway at the north.  The entrance to the home lies to the west.

A breeze seems constantly to be brushing through the treetops on this forested path connecting the northern and southern halves of Wutai. The path itself is a very serene place, with the treetop canopy casting a richly-woven tapestry of shadows onto the dirt road beneath.  As there are few tourist attractions in the northern side of town, the road is perhaps the only place in Wutai that has completely escaped tourism's grasp.  Consequently, it has become quite a popular place for the residents of Wutai to go for relaxation or recreation.

This is the main entrance to Wutai, a small pleasant resort town that, despite its touristy overtones, speaks of powerful ancient traditions. Far to the north is a small wooded area, behind which lies the prominent rock formation Da-Chao.  More immediately to the north is a short dirt path leading to a few buildings.  To the west is a bridge over one of the several small tributaries that crisscross through the town and beyond the bridge, citizens bustle to and fro, acting out their daily responsibilities.

Like several other buildings in Wutai, the Item shop is in an area all to itself.  Streams are present on all sides, and the open air lends quite a sense of spaciousness and relaxedness. The Item Shop itself is a medium-sized building, sporting a few large signs and bearing a large awning supported by red posts.  The main road here forks in two directions.  To the north, the path leads to the Da-Chao monument which suddenly looms overbearingly ahead.  The west path leads to a forested trail.  To the south, a bridge leads to the Turtle's Paradise and to the rest of Wutai's lower half.

In this sparsely furnished house an old man is sitting at a simple round table smoking a pipe and enjoying a cup of tea in private. A paper screen stands on the left side of the room, it's probably a good place to hide behind. The Wutaian sign for 'heaven' is painted on the wall behind the old man, next to a hot springs symbol. In front of the room, stairs are leading up to the next floor.

The weapon shop is a little smaller than the item shop across the bridge. It is neatly organized and the clanging of the smithy can be heard in a back room. This is where Wutai's finest weaponsmith sells his wares. On a counter with a few display weapons a list has been laid out giving the details about the costs.

The foyer of Godo's house is little more than a short hallway. The walls are divided in half horizontally, the bottom half being made of dark hardwood while the top half is composed of white drywall.  On the western wall, there are several windows, through which the garden outside can be seen.  The floor here is hardwood, with thin boards.  To the north, a room with a few beds can be seen through an open doorway.  To the east there is a turn in the hallway.

The area surrounding the Turtle's Paradise is floored in tiled concrete, much like the area to the east.  Most of the ground here is shaded, however, by the Paradise, which is the largest building in this part of town.  Size aside, several prominent signs and posters make certain that the pub will not be missed. The only other prominent feature is a large ceramic pot sitting by the side of the building.  A bridge to the north leads to the item shop, Mt. Da-Chao, and the upper side of Wutai.  A bridge to the east leads to the Weapon Shop.

This is quite a seedy room.  Two small rugs lay slighty skewed on the cold concrete floor, and a layer of dust rests on everything here.  Various scraps of paper and trash litter the floor, and boxes are thrown about wantonly along the side walls.  The lighting, naturally, is dim.  To say the least, it's a conspicuous place, and not at all welcoming. A set of stairs at the north side of the room is the only exit.

This is a large, spacious, room with a high ceiling and wooden floor and walls.  The acoustics of this room are very sharp as a result, and the prayers, sighs, and other noises echoing throughout the room create quite an eerie, mystical effect.  Spaced evenly along the wall all the way around the room are simple square wooden pillars, painted white on the front. The most prominent feature of the room is a large, golden idol to the far north, and there is no overhead lighting- most of the room's dim light comes from large candles affixed to the idol. Several citizens that are here praying to the deity to which this shrine is dedicated stand or kneel on one of the two ornamental rugs in the room- one, a large, elaborate, square rug with a powerful insignia in it's center, the other a small, rectangular mat.  There are two doors to the room- one to the northeast and one to the south.  However, only the one to the south looks like it will open...

This is little more than an elevated platform covered in finely cut grass.  The elevation offers a slightly better view, and one can see most of Wutai from here.  Most prominently, in the distance to the northwest, a large pagoda towers over the surrounding forest. To the north, a small staircase leads to the door of a large building. To the west, a set of stairs leads back to the eastern road.

Trying to climb over a cat which lay down on the stairs without tripping isn't easy. The rooms above are full of cats of all color, the arrival of everyone is greeted by a loud mewing as the little beasts run around playing, tumbling over each other or trying to get each visitor to feed them. The tables and chairs in the room are mostly taken as their possession.

There is quite an air of distinction to this small library.  It is well- furnished, neatly kept, and tastefully decorated, keeping well in line with the standard set by the rest of Godo's mansion and indeed the rest of Wutai. The entirety of the north wall is covered by bookcases filled with a vast array of novels, encyclopedias, and other volumes.  Upon the floor is a red and gold decorative rug, and the southern and eastern walls are quite plain. The only exit to the room is through a door to the west.

This is a large square of tiled concrete surrounded on all sides by water with bridges to the east and west.  The northern half on the square is occupied by Wutai's Weapon Shop, a building similar to the others of this town, yet slightly more martial in feel.  On the ground outside of its doors is a decorative mat, its pattern perhaps a war flag.  To the west is the famous Turtle's Paradise Pub.  To the east lies the town's main entrance.

This is the world-famous Turtle's Paradise Pub, the most popular tourist attraction in Wutai as well as the most elegant and relaxing.  The general motif is a slightly updated rendition of the ancient, dignified feel of the rest of the town, and all the furnishings are glossy and stylistic. A few tables rest in the room's center and several banners, posters, ornamental rugs, and even a fountain decorate the room.  Along the western wall is a long bar at which a few locals sit and behind which a bartender keeps himself very busy.  The entrance to the  bar is on the southern wall along with a large stage, presumably for live bands.  To the north is a bathroom, currently occupied.

This is obviously a very important area of Wutai.  Here, the ground is elegantly tiled, and rich yellow tulips are planted in rows to the south of the main road.  Three major structures dominate the area.  The first is a small but gorgeous shrine to the west.  The second is a large mansion, which can be entered by a door to the east.  Most prominent, however, is the large pagoda to the northwest. A trail to the south leads back to the rest of Wutai. The northern path leads straight to the Da-Chao monument.

The tracks merge at this point from two split paths. One heads northeast to a higher set of tracks, while the second drops down to the southeast. Gusts of wind are a reminder of the craggy rocks below. To the west, the unfinished reactor can be seen.

The rocky surface of a cliffside trail is interrupted by a barricade of boulders to the north.  Beyond the protruding rocks, the trail looks mostly clear of debris, and is covered by little more than a thin layer of dry earth.  The mountain wall rises immediately to the west, where a tree somehow emerges.  Southward, the trail descends the mountain through a more fertile environment.

A large clearing has been created here by a very large bird, evident by the amount of large feathers in the area. A nest the size of a small car is cradled between a few trees and a large pile of bones is over by the edge of the ridge.

A stable wooden bridge supports train tracks, suspended over the area below.  The tracks lead directly south from the mouth of the Mako Reactor, and continue through the mountains in the distance.  Below the railway is the base of the huge power plant, nearly a hundred meters down.

The path aggressively winds its way up the hill, but respectfully veers east to avoid an aging tree.  It also leads down the mountain, but there is a sharp drop-off which would require a quick leap to get past.  The sun can be seen just over the top of the hill as its rays of light illuminate faded yellow leaves.  Green grass and shrubs block any possible attempts to exit to the west.

rooms.name: At The Edge Of A Huge Drop

userData.LongDescription: A single step to the east is the price of a one way ticket to an early grave.  A small rock balances tenuously on the edge of the cliff.  A particularly large crack stretches along the middle of the path, which offers passage up the mountain and also down, to anyone willing to hop over a blockade of rocks.

The train tracks are wedged through a narrow opening, carved into the cliff by humans.  They continue south in a straight line.  Just a few feet below the tracks is a wide ledge, and a set of stairs leads down to it.  The tracks are supported by columns of red bricks.

The embankment is reinforced with steel slabs, which help support the earth while protecting it from the river. A small wooden shack with an old rusty lever overlooks the drawbridge below. A trail of bird droppings leads up to a small ridge.

To the southwest, the trail methodically winds its way down the mountain in a zig zagging fashion.  A few steps to the north a tree proudly stands at the peak of the ridge, absorbing the sunlight which is actually quite blinding.  Just over the cliff's edge, a few body lengths below, two slabs of stone suspiciously protrude from its face.

It was no small feat transporting the amount of wood that it took to build this railroad hundreds of feet off the ground and in the middle of nowhere. Small imperfections in the build have taken its toll on the structure and many gaps have appeared in the tracks. Some debris has fallen onto the track here from one such gap directly above.

The train rails end abruptly near the water's edge. It appears this was intended to be a small service station that was never completed. The opening in the cliff face looks like it was only hollowed out but never finished, leaving a small cave.

A round metal platform surrounds a high reaching tower, which is immediately to the north, and is connected to two bridges.  One bridge leads northeast and the other to the northwest.  Near the top of the tower, a number has been painted in white where a loud engine is emitting fumes.  The entrance to the tower is framed with a bright border.  From inside, a wide railway emerges and leads towards a valley through a mountain range to the south.

The tracks conjoin and immediately split again, granting traffic from the reactor access to either station at North Corel. The track gets higher on both northern paths and lower on the southern options.

A large sheet of thick concrete serves as a landing pad for helicopters.   To the southeast, the mouth of a wide bridge opens and leads towards the tall central engine tower of the reactor.  Down over the edge, three nearly flat surfaces of metal can be seen stretching from the inner tower all the way to the outer wall of the reactor.

This ledge forms a circular platform which is surrounded by a white waist-high fence.  The fence is falling apart, and has large gaps where pieces of it have broken off and fallen down the cliff.  Although this area gives an excellent view of the Mako reactor, there's nothing actually up here.  Some of the dirt has been dug out into trenches, as though construction on something were begun but abandoned.

Thick and fluffy moss is beginning to overtake the stone drawbridge, but the iron rails are preventing a total victory. The river periodically slaps against the side of the bridge, providing the moss with a constant supply of water.

rooms.name: A Bend In The Rocky Ledge

userData.LongDescription: A small rocky platform immediately to the southwest looks over the trail from above; but there is no apparent access to it.  Somehow a few small patches of yellow weeds are growing up there.  A glance over the cliff's edge to the east presents a panoramic view of the landscape below.   The trail leads to the southeast at a decline, as well as northeast to the peak of this exhausting mountain range.

The tracks have a layered structure, and this set of rails is far above the ones below. The landscape is lifeless, with only sparse coniferous trees on the mountains in the distance where Corel used to be. The tracks have fallen apart and left a small gap that looks like it can be crossed easily.

The blackened husk of a city, once known as Corel, can be seen in the valley below this cliff.  Every single building, without exception, has been burned to the ground.  A dirt road can be seen leading from the ruins of Corel north to the Mako Reactor.  There is no path down to the city.

On top of the tracks, its possible to see for miles. The mountain range in the distance is pitch black with snow white peaks and trees line the base. Below, to the southeast, the tracks rejoin the the lower bypass and continue towards the river. A large break in the tracks to the northwest looks like it can be crossed.

Northward lies a hazardous rocky cliffside path, which winds its way to the true peak of the mountain range's altitude.  Large mature trees tower high into the sky on either side of the trail.  Some of their roots, which can be found emerging from little scattered patches of overgrowth, provide convenient footholds.  Down the trail to the southeast, a very small clearing awaits.

There is a small clearing on the path here which would serve as a great spot for a weary hiker to take a moment's break.  An impenetrable rock wall blocks movement past the eastern boundary of the trail, leaving only the two canonical options.  It appears that a handful of paces to the northwest will lead to the top of the mountain.

The rails have a very steep grade and make progress difficult, but the rusted rails provide decent traction. A small drawbridge can be seen to the east and the smell of the river bank offers respite from the coal dusted rails.

Heavily rusted tracks follow the bends of the river and mountainside. The rails divert and a short section leads down to an opening in the side of the cliff. To the southeast, the tracks cut into the mountainside towards North Corel through a pile of old oil drums and stacked rail ties..

A very steep set of stairs leads up to a higher ledge to the north.  The stairs are made of old, cracked wood, and look like they might collapse at any moment.  The tracks stretch south into the distance.

The bridge bends here, leading both northeast and southeast.  Directly to the north, through the misty fog, the outline of a mountain range can faintly be made out.  To the southeast the bridge leads deeper into the mist, which fades to the north.  Below the bridge, hundreds of levels of scaffolding have been built from aged lumber.

The orange sky against the coal rich mountains is framed beautifully in the wooden support beams of the track above. There is an impassable break in the tracks far above, making this the only safe passage. A small gap to the west should make for an easy jump and the tracks continue without incident to the east.

In the center of this small room is an elevator, designed to raise and lower both employees and resources in and out of the depths.  A set of railway tracks leads from the elevator through the open doorway to the south.  A giant, red operating lever protrudes from the floor.  On the wall, there are arrow-shaped lights pointing up and down.  But they are not illuminated, and do not appear to be functioning.  A train engine sits idly against the north wall, which has been removed from the tracks.

The tracks are raised hundreds of feet off the bottom of the valley below. The old wooden supports and trusses creak slightly with the stronger gusts of wind. From this distance, the ravaged town of Corel is nothing more than a charcoal pit on the horizon.

The badlands below are a mix of craggy rocks and coal dust. Oddly, there is a chest stuck to the tracks here, but it's empty. The tracks continue but there is a broken section ahead, creating a gap that is far too large to jump across. The only way to continue on is by using the tracks below.

rooms.name: A Little Cave by the Water

userData.LongDescription: A random collection of construction equipment is being stored in this cave. It almost looks as if the project was abandoned mid-build. A few replacement parts for the train that used the tracks are against the far wall. A large bulldozer takes up a majority of the floorspace.

rooms.name: A Stone Bridge Near North Corel.

userData.LongDescription: The only river in the region runs far below this high-rise bridge. A drawbridge to the southwest indicates this river was once a passage of commerce. The tracks lead east towards North Corel and a beyond a small break to the west, they continue towards the Corel Reactor.

A massive break in the tracks marks the end of the line for this section of track. The track far below looks like it continues to the west towards the reactor. The only path available is to leap back across the gap.

Up the hill to the north, a steep climb awaits.  A few large boulders block the path, but could be easily passed with a good leap.  A pair of healthy trees lie on the eastern side of the path, flourishing with rich green leaves.  The soft brown earth makes for comfortable hiking.

Just a few feet above this ledge is a set of train tracks, and some stairs lead up to the tracks.  The tracks are supported by columns of red bricks, but it's possible to walk under the tracks to the northeast.  There's a simple rope bridge, held up by wooden posts hammered into the dirt, leading southeast to another ledge.

rooms.name: A Stone Bridge Near North Corel.

userData.LongDescription: A large gap blocks the path to the northeast, but it looks like it can be crossed. The landscape here is a painted mosaic of black coal, green trees, white snow, and an orange horizon. Far beyond the leap to the east a river can be seen.

The tracks are situated below the overpassing tracks from above. The tracks below were likely a siding for passing trains, although the design seems superfluous. Fortunately, the design has imparted extra stability not found elsewhere. A small break in the track can be jumped across to the southeast and junctions with the overpassing rails to the northwest.

A high reaching tree with no growth of any kind watches silently, as a bridge from the southwest and the mountain trail from the north collide here and join together.  They both lead down the mountain in their respective directions.  The sun sets gently over the ridge to the north.  A mist of vapors spans along the south, blocking any line of sight into the distance.

A heavy and unpleasant smog of humidity flows from the southwest, through which one can make out a giant factory from which it is produced.  The bridge leading towards it is lit up with heavy duty fog lights, which give an indication of how far it goes.  Far below, directly beneath the bridge, a large structure tunnels deep into the ground.
Frigid mist coils and churns around the edges of this open field, making the island feel much smaller than it really is. The peak of the mountainous island is nearly visible to the north.

The connecting chain vanishes into the frozen mist as it descends to some other portion of Mt. Woe. The expansive stone island sways only a little despite the howling winds that assault it. A path goes both east and west along the northern cliff.

The ground shifts and rolls with the rapidly changing winds, like a ship tossed in a storm. A heavy chain groans in protest of the swaying island's movements on the northern edge of the island. The narrow ridge of stone, jutting oddly out of the ground, interrupts the otherwise level field.

Constant, volatile weather has worn away at the western edge of the island, narrowing the already slim trail at the base of the cliff. The trail suddenly widens out to the southeast, before turning south out of view.

rooms.name: Mt. Woe -- A Turn in the Path
