userData.LongDescription: A small batch of yellow flowers flails in the harsh winds. The thin layer of crunchy snow has built up on the ground nearly covering the scrubby grass completely. The narrow path hugs a bare cliff face as it continues northward into better weather.

A mighty chain stretches an unknown distance through another gathering mass of clouds. Somewhere in the flowing mists below the overpass is the worn dirt trail that travels the entirety of the mountain.

The slim path splits around a wedge-shaped cliff. A small, secluded field continues around the cliff to the southeast. Following the cliff southwest, the steep path continues to climb up the mountain.

The field descends into a quiet grotto on the northern side. Strange sounds echo out of the large hole on the southern end of the field. The noises are, likely, the distorted echoes of the wind. Exactly how deep the hole goes is entirely up to speculation.

A long forgotten treasure chest, nearly overgrown with flowering scrub brush, sits near the northern cliff of this small butte. The details of the large island's slope rapidly fade from view under a building haze of fog.

The minuscule island is mysteriously more stable in the gusting winds than it aught to be. Two battered treasure chests have been left open to the weather by a careless explorer. From the vantage of the small island a much larger formation can be seen to the south.

The numerous batches of bright yellow flowers littering the northern region are a harsh contrast to the darkening clouds that surround the mountain. A short ridge of stone along the southern border is split by a slender path heading up to the mountain peak.

The fog rolls off the western edge, driven by a gentle breeze. A battered trail starts at an enormous chain and meanders eastward into the thickening fog. Despite the chain's immense weight, the two islands are pulling so hard that it has virtually no sag.

The frigid mist laps over the jagged eastern edge in a mimicry of the sea, obscuring the uneven ground. The whispering echoes of the gusting wind are the only sounds that grace the desolate landscape.

An overpass has formed over the delicate mountain trail. From underneath, it shows its sides and underbelly as rocky and uneven, as if it were yanked right out of the ground and set down here. Fog disperses and coalesces below the overpass, creeping down across the ground and beyond like a ghostly river.

A pervasive fog shifts about, enshrouding everything. The borders of the rocky, misshapen ground are almost impossible to discern. A single, heavy chain is visible, anchored right into the ground, and leading off into the foggy unknown.

This portion of the mountain path opens up into a large swath of open ground. The ground gently rises as it turns to the south. Despite afforded space, the center of the path is clearly the preferred and trusted route, evidenced by brown patches where even the tough short-bladed grass has been worn away.

Sharp stones are littered across the grassy landing on the western side of the island. To the north a small wooden chest lays half buried by rubble. The ground climbs steeply eastward before leveling out again.

A worn trail in the pale green grass winds across the top of a short rise on the moderately sized island. Cloud-capped cliffs rise up on the eastern side, framing in the steep path to the lower fields.

The elevated field offers a prime view of the various fragments of Mt. Woe that float amidst the  roiling storms. The swirling clouds roll over a seemingly countless pieces of Mt Woe. From this view the arrangement appears as if an explosion was frozen in time.

A broken chain clinks uselessly off the western edge of the large field. The yellow flowers continue their flourishing domination of the northern slopes of the mountain. A deep gouge in the terrain prevents any travel to the south, so that the only way to continue the climb is back to the east.

The narrow peninsula of stone extends westward, away from the safety of the cliff. The dancing clouds obscure the true edges of the narrow strip of stone, granting it a forbidding beauty. Even the hardy native grass has largely abandoned the exposed location.

The cliff overhangs a portion of the trail, protecting it from the harsh weather. Several dark masses floating in the eastern clouds bobble in the severe winds. To the north the path tapers as it nears a large stone arch.

rooms.name: Mt. Woe -- A Fork in the path.

userData.LongDescription: The ground rises to a level plateau which stretches far to the south. To the east an extremely steep climb rises up, becoming the topside of a winding overpass. The meandering mountain path travels up the steep ramp, and north into a fog covered field.

Jagged shards of splintered stone surround a gaping wound torn into the earthen surface of the summit. The shards, sharp as fragmented glass, hem in a small path to a meager outcropping that stretches over the vast abyss. A glowing altar rests at the furthest point of the outcropping.

The petite landing is hardly larger than the heavy chain anchored into it. Hunkered against the short cliff, the ledge ascends southward into the churning fog. That same fog obscures the precarious drop on the western side of the small climb.

Tendrils of mist glide over the rocky edges of the field, obscuring anything in the distance. The worn trail of trampled grass cuts westward, through the field, fading into the surrounding mist. The the north the trail climbs up a short, steep hill.

Lumpy spirals of brown stone sprout from either side of an enormous chain embedded into the ground. The stone columns stretch far overhead before arcing towards each other. The land beneath the skywalk spirals up the western column allowing access to the topside of the arc.

A mysterious magical phenomenon has generated a small haven among the unstable weather patterns that plague the mountain. While a storm swirls all around the island, the conditions on the small field is relatively calm, bordering on pleasant. Passing through the wall cloud is another fantastically large chain.

rooms.name: Mt. Woe -- The Mountain of Woe

userData.LongDescription: The ancient chain groans in its contest with the swaying island of floating rock.  The array of floating islands, called Mt. Woe, spirals higher until they vanish in the clouds. To the west another massive chain bridges the gap to another island.

The path along the island narrows as a cliff presses in from the west. Another gargantuan chain set into the stone island vanishes into the obscuring cloud bank on the opposite side of the path. The westward cliff offers some cover from the frigid winds of Mt. Woe.

A small outcropping of rocks, partially covered in bright yellow flowers is a lively splash of color on the short climb to the peak of this small island. A massive chain stretches from the peak to another island to the west confining the swaying islands.

The sun breaks through the clouds onto a steeply pitched grassy plain rising from the mists that cover the lower portion of the island.  A few scrubby brushes, sporting their lively yellow flowers, dot the landscape.

Fierce winds rage against the exposed western face of the large island, tossing snow and slush in its fury. The winding mountain path turns into a sliver of uneven ground, barely visible in the onslaught.

Overhead, a partial arch of stone reaches into the clouds. The underbelly of the arch is a lumpy mass of khaki stone. The vague shape of another enormous chain extends from the arch before vanishing completely. The only way north is across a narrow bridge of stone.

A precarious stone arch extends from the peak of the island. The arch is broken off part way through it's rise and a massive iron chain is embedded in the resultant stub. The chain reaches out over the cloud filled nothingness to a neighboring island.

The extended walkway looks like a panhandle for the floating mountain fragment. Hints of the island's true mass are hinted at through the ebbing clouds as they float past. The walkway broadens out onto the main portion of the island, only a short walk from the chain that leads west to another chunk of the mountain.

Patchy grass grows like lichen across the wind scoured plateau. Near the shelter of a cliff a small batch of yellow flowers grows from a dubious looking scrub brush. To the south the cliff pushes in on the small plateau.

The rudimentary trail, that treks the entirety of the woeful mountain, crosses the rime covered field to end at the base of an immense chain. The iron fetter is pulled so taut that the frost covered links nearly appear to be frozen in place.

The swaying island rocks and rolls unpredictably, tossed about by the stormy weather. An arctic wind blasts across the barren landscape of this exposed ridge. To the north, a titanic chain rises heavenward into the stirring clouds.
The narrow ridge dead-ends with a colossal chain rising precipitously into the clouds. An immense shadow can be seen through the heavy overcast, likely the other anchor point for the titanic chain.

rooms.name: Mt. Woe -- Before a Narrow Ledge

userData.LongDescription: The snow-laden winds howl against the large island, reducing vision to just a few feet. To the south the stone surface suddenly stops, making the path against the cliff quite prudent. The path continues northwest, where it narrows considerably making travel that way difficult at best.

A spiraling path on the western end of the skywalk is the safest means of descent. Under the constant assault of the weather, the proud rock formation has withered to a mere echo of its former mass. The chain that dangles off the eastern pillar sways slackly in the wind.

Tucked neatly against a towering cliff face, the hidden glade is overrun by scrub grass. In the middle a large boulder stands alone, surrounded by flower brushes. The eastern edge of the field is a sheer drop of dubious height.
Thick, undisturbed hoarfrost covers the stubby grass. Even the bright yellow flowers sprouting from the scrub brush is encased in a thick layer of rime. The frosted field continues to the north.
The slender stone ridge climbs rapidly away from the main body of the small, swaying island. Embedded deeply into the rocky peak, a heavily pitted chain sways gently with the rocking of the island.

A large patch of grass has been worn to nothing but dirt in the center of the open field. The mountain path continues westward, where the rising slope meets the shrinking cliff. A heavy-duty chain ascends to a relatively small hunk of floating rock.

Two titanic chains are anchored into the stone foundations of this field. The northern chain leads to a massive rock formation. The other chain is tossed wildly by the unpredictable movements of something hidden in the fog.

Countering artist expectations, the peak of the island is a wide, flat plateau. Nestled above the storm currently invading the mountain island, the weather on the peak is comparatively demur. To the east a massive chain is anchored into a partial arch of stone.

On the west side of the room lies a number of large, fluffy mattresses with purple comforters. On the east side, several barrels full of rations lie behind a large table surrounded by several chairs.  Tucked away in the northeast corner is a cask of mead. A staircase lies to the north, at the foot of which is a matronly servant, offering visitors rates for the night.

The floor becomes much more delicate in its texture as the passageway leads into the room. The cold stone is met with a fine carpet, the fabric extending towards a series of steps that lead to the Queen's bed and table. The steps above end the rough, stone path as the floor is laid with tile thereafter, another carpet spreading along the pristine tiling underneath the bed and along the table. A spinning wheel sits next to the Queen's bed and looks to have seen very little use in its time, the wooden device serving as mere decoration.

Two torches illuminate the room from their mantles along the stone archway and leave the room exceptionally well-lit, save for the very corners of the room, its walls casting small, errant shadows that shift as the torches become further and further removed. A weapon rack lies next to the stairwell and is immediately adjacent to a large, wooden table capable of seating four, all of its chairs empty.

Two large casks of mead lie against the wall in front of the table and the crest of Guardia above one of them, shining brightly as two torches burn on both sides of the emblem. The table itself is littered with plates. The plates are full of food and are being brought from the kitchen while empty plates are being taken out. The plates that are newly arrived may receive special and very prompt attention.

Two clay pots sit on top of equally large, clay ovens. Despite the lone torch in the corner of the room, the cooking fires provide the most light to the kitchen. There are two cooking stations, pots sitting at each of them while the flames of the oven below scorch their bases. A cask of mead sits in the far reaches of the room, unattended and unaccompanied where it lies in shadow.

Knightly regalia is placed in this stone chamber by the quarters of the Guardia Knights.  Two mannequins are equipped in shining steel breastplates, helms, kiteshields, and pikes. A large ornamental shield bearing Guardia's crest is high on the northeast wall.  Flanked by torches, the staircase down to the knights' quarters pierces the northern wall, while a stone hallway treads towards the south.

Two windows allow light to seep in and brighten the spacious residence. Stone steps lead to a resting area, the bed brought closer to the window with the increased elevation.  Next to the bed is a table draped in a cloth with a clay pitcher atop of it. Purple carpets lie at the door and beneath the bed, the fabric's quality and condition both superb. A mannequin is positioned adjacent to the bed, its lusterous steel reflecting the light from the windows.

rooms.name: Guardia Castle - Hall to Knight's Quarters

userData.LongDescription: The muted sound of steel upon steel echoes at this large, stone corner of the ground floor of the castle. Footsteps clatter on the flagstones in rhythm with the flickering torchlight coming from high above the ground. The hallway opens eastward into a grand foyer, whereas to the north a cramped, stone staircase may be seen.

As the steps progress further upwards, light can be seen reaching down from further above the stairs, the beams illuminating the steps. Shapes and figures can be made out from within the darkness but detail escapes the objects due to the poor lighting. The only exits lie in the stairwell, the steps extending both up and down.

A royal purple carpet expands to cover the ornate, stone entryway to the great castle Guardia.  A large stairway divides the wall to the north, leading up to grand mahogany double doors.  Arching stone hallways extend to the east and west.  A fresh, earthy scent wafts in from the gates to the south from where the misty Guardia Forest lies.

Torchlight illuminates the room, reflecting off the crests of Guardia lining the walls and the spare suits of upper body armor near the banister to the south.  A staircase leads down into the practice and rest areas of the Guardia knights, while a smaller flight of stairs climbs the north wall, leading to the ground floor of Guardia Castle.

rooms.name: Guardia Castle - Hall to the Kitchen

userData.LongDescription: All sorts of wonderful smells linger at the end of the stone hallway and permeate upwards from the small staircase in the north wall. Armed mannequins flank the stairs, their equipment glinting in the torchlight.  Guardia's crest is also featured prominently on a large heraldic shield high on the wall.  To the south, a hallway curves back towards the entryway of the castle.

The regal carpeting stretches from the doorway and reaches to the center of the room. Two thrones tower from the room's center, each throne draped with luxurious, red, padded material. The King's throne stands taller than the Queen's seat. Beyond the throne, two stone staircases rise from each side of the room. Guardia's crest hangs high from above each of the thrones.

The large front gate of Guardia castle is wide open, allowing visitors to enter.  A flag hangs over the stone wall on either side of the metal gate.  Through the entrance is the interior Castle Guardia, with stone floors and walls.

The floor is rough with its lack of carpeting, the stone surface coarse and uneven. Armaments hang on a rack next to the entrance. Boxes are stacked along the walls on every side of the room, the crates in the corner are covered in shadow. Steel mannequins mingle with the wooden containers lying about, their plating dull and aged. The only way out is the stairway leading into the room.

Two spear and shield clad statues guard the entrance to the tower's stairwell. Passage opens through an archway to the south. Windows and a pair of torches shine their light into the room and through archway. A chandelier hangs from the ceiling, its candles unlit.

rooms.name: Guardia Castle - Before the Throne Room

userData.LongDescription: The narrow stairway opens up as it ascends, the railing turning to create a balcony on both sides of the passageway. A purple, golden trimmed rug softens the floor above the stairs and before the door. A pair of torches light the area, each of them on either side of the door. Alongside each torch resides a crest of Guardia wedged in between great pillars of stone.

rooms.name: Guardia Castle - Hall to the Royal Bedchamber

userData.LongDescription: Two archways occupy the room, the west arch offering open space and passage to a staircase and the east arch sealed by means of a door. The hallway is long, purple carpeting with gold, decorative borders rolled along the floor's surface. Four torches hang, two on each side of both arches with a crest of Guardia elevated above and beside each outer torch.

The room is cramped with its small space and its large, quantitive contents. The storage space is used by means of stacking the crates in a giant pile, the wooden containers stacked on top each of other until they just barely brush the ceiling. Where a little space that remains unoccupied by the crates sits a wooden spinning wheel and a weapons rack, both awkwardly placed and difficult to reach without squeezing in between some boxes.

The corners in between the walls are dark and dreary. The torches are weaker here, the small amount of light not strong enough to relieve the large space of darkness. Wooden crates are stacked up along the wall with a pair of old, rusted mannequins standing adjacent to the containers. Next to a weapon rack adorned against the wall is an open chest, its contents long removed. The stairwell offers the only exits.

A square plot of regal carpeting is laid along the floor after some stone steps, leading to a flight of stairs encased in a stone archway. A pair of torches hang on each side of the arch, the staircase within spiraling upwards and leading to the tower above.

rooms.name: Guardia Castle - Hall to the Kitchen

userData.LongDescription: The scent of spices, woodsmoke, and cooking meat waft from north of this stone corner of the castle, contrasting the smoky oil smell of the torches lining the walls.  The entrance of the castle looms to the west. The path ends and a new one opens northward, leading to a stairwell encased within an archway.

The walls around the room have several shelves constructed into them.  There is a pile of whetstones and buckets and on the wall adjacent to them is a series of paintings, the canvases leaning on each other and onto the wall. The corner contains a large, stone block, a chair, and a bottle polishing oil atop of the block's surface.

Two torches shine their light onto the small, musty space, the floor cluttered with boxes that have accumulated dirt on their surfaces over time. A weapon rack is aligned on the wall next to the stairwell, spears and battleaxes hanging from its shelves. An old, wooden spinning wheel lies at the end of the room, collecting dust from ages of disuse.

Carpet is laid along the floor after the stone steps and lead to another set of stairs within a stone archway. A pair of torches hang on each side of the archway, the staircase within cascading upwards to the tower.

rooms.name: Guardia Castle - Hall to the Royal Bedchamber

userData.LongDescription: A long roll of carpet treats the rough stone floor and extends from one end of the hall to the other. A door lies towards the west side of the hall while an arch to the east, two torches on both sides of each passageway. A crest of Guardia is mounted above each passage, one adjacent to the arch and another to the door.

Natural light pours from the two windows and fills the room. Two mannequins stand guard from below each window.  The stone walls open up opposite to the staircase, an archway of space granting access to the hall beyond it.

The path into the village continues running north and south through this part of the grove. Except for the wide dirt path and some grass, there really isn't much here. Unexpectedly, finely cultivated tulips run along the east and west sides of the path in a variety of colors.

A bit cramped for a human, this hut is nevertheless pretty spacious for a goblin, fitting for the home of the village's head shaman. The furniture is very sparse: a small bed with some dirty blankets, a crude iron stove, and a large and likely stolen armoire with the doors flung open. The floor is actually wooden planks laid down, and on top of that is spread a large brown bearskin rug. A table in a corner hosts a bunch of the same totems found hanging outside.

This central part of the goblin's village is also apparently the meeting place, as the path becomes a ring of well-tramped dirt. At the center of the ring is a large iron cauldron over an immense cooking fire that's always kept lit. Small straw huts are scattered about, and four totem poles similar to those found at the village entrance surround the cookpot as well.

There's not much room in here, but the view is terrific. Except for a single chair and a box with a book and some red and white semaphore flags in it, there really isn't much IN this tower, save a single goblin attendant of some form every once in a while. In almost every direction, an unparalleled view of the forests and landmarks of the Pandora area is possible. A ladder to the rear of the room leads back down to the ground.

This area is a long stretch of cleared land. The grass here is a total write-off; it looks like goblins have had a marathon run on it every day for years, and the soil is tramped-down and a bit muddy. Off to the east is a short wooden watch tower of some form, and to the west is a large structure that looks like a gallows without the hangpost. A wooded path leads south to the sapper field.

The short wooded path runs through this village, a large grove with a few huts and goblins of all shapes and sizes. Near the end of the path are two tall totem poles which stretch toward the sky. All around goblins go about their daily business in their own fashion, and any interlopers get disapproving looks. The path continues on into the village in a number of directions, while leaving to the south returns you to the Pandora trail.

Set in the southeast corner of this small village is the tribal longhouse where the goblins eat and sleep. A very large wooden building covered in tribal masks dominates this area. Goblins frequently move in and out of it, going to and from their daily business. Outside are also some archery targets. A small group of Chobin Hoods is practicing their marksmanship upon them.

As might be expected of goblins, this is one giant mess. Row upon row upon row of bunks covered in filthy blankets line the walls, with windows between each letting some sun in. Dirty clothing and other messes dot the floor, and thrown somewhat randomly the between rows of bunks are a few brass stoves and chimneys reaching toward the ceiling.

In the northwest corner of the village is this field, a blasted and rocky mass of trenches, wood targets, and occasionally the cackling of goblin sapper teams as they practice their craft on this proving ground. The sound of explosions is common here, as are flying dirt, rock, and other shrapnel. The path continues through the trees to the north.

The ground in this area is very loamy, and in the southwest corner is a fenced-in pig sty where the goblins keep their favorite food: pork. Inside the sty the ground goes from loamy to just plain muddy, as the pigs prefer to play around in the cool mud, especially on hot days. A feeding trough is set up next to the sty, and a little west of that is a small shack.

rooms.name: Goblin Village -- Outside the Shaman's Hut

userData.LongDescription: This part of the village is surprisingly peaceful. A simple but well-constructed hut of wood and straw is the dominant feature, and outside are some lovely tulip beds. On the outside of the hut are a number of what look like shamanic totems, and on the roof of the hut a crude iron chimney emits puffs of smoke intermittently.

This hill is clear of debris.  A ledge is directly below the south edge of the hill.  The forest is fairly bright, as the trees are relatively sparse.  The hill stretches a short distance to the east before sloping away into a path.  A portal on this hill leads to another part of the forest.

The ledge is about halfway up the hill, which crests about twelve feet higher.  The lowest level of tree limbs is about eye level.  Small, green bushes dot the ledge leading to the east, hindering travel slightly.  Just to the south, a staircase leads to the forest floor.

The hill ends, sloping down into the forest to the south and east.  The ledge is dotted with a few bushes and rocks.  The bushes are stunted, due to the lack of light passing through the overhanging limbs.  The ledge follows the contours of the hill around to the east.  Just north, there is a staircase leading to the top of the hill.

The forest is dark and foreboding, closing in from the south and the west.  To the north, a hill rises high above the forest floor.  There is a short staircase leading about halfway up the hill to a ledge.  The ground is covered in dead leaves, while a few bushes dot the terrain.  A portal beckons travellers to enter.

Two paths join, and continue deeper into the forest, which grows steadily darker to the south.  A few leaves have fallen to the ground on the path, but it is still mostly clear.  A few rocks line the western edge of the path.  To the north and east, paths lead back out of the forest, while south leads still deeper within it.

The forest is lighter to the east, as though there were open land a short distance away.  The ground is surprisingly clear of debris.  A single rock sits in the middle of the path.  To the west, the path disappears around a corner.  To the south, it splits then disappears.

The path takes a sharp turn.  A layer of leaves covers the ground, while a solitary bush grows along the edge of the path. The path itself is extremely dark, and only seems to get darker further along. To the west, there is a low ridge, while to the north the path leads deeper into the forest.

This ridge extends eastward, then slopes gently down to a path. Only a few leaves have fallen across the path.  The forest is much darker, and the air is stale from the lack of a breeze.  The darkness doesn't seem to let up any, even down the path to the east.  A portal leads to another part of the forest.

Trees rise just above the crest of the hill, which is virtually clear of debris.  The forest floor is clearly visible.  A lack of overhanging branches makes this part of the hill rather bright.  Stairs lead down to the south, while a portal invites travellers to explore other parts of the forest.

The path has darkened considerably.  A hill lies just to the north, shading this spot even more.  The smell of decay rises from a layer of leaves along the edge of the path.  To the south and west, paths lead through the forest.  To the north, a staircase ascends the small hill.

This ledge is clear of debris.  The forest closes in from the south, making it extremely dark.  A hill rises slightly above this ledge before cresting.  A staircase leads north to the top of the hill, while a portal leads to another part of the forest.

A small gap splits the hill in two.  There is a pair of whipping posts to allow passage across.  Fortunately, a large tree has fallen across so there is no need of a whip.  To the south, the forest stretches as far as the eye can see, although that isn't very far due to the thickness of the vegetation. To the south, a staircase leads to the forest floor.  A portal leads elsewhere.

The path, lined with thick bushes, turns at this corner of the forest. The ground is littered with leaves and rocks.  The smell of decay wafts up from the leaves.  The forest to the south is very dark.  To the north, a clearing is visible, while a narrow path leads a short distance off to the west.

This ledge is fairly small.  There are a few bushes along the edges.  To the north, there is a ridge, inaccesable from the ledge.  A switch is on the ground at the base of the hill.  A few loose stones are scattered across the ledge.  A portal leads to another part of the forest.

The forest closes in from all sides, ending the trail.  A few leaves have fallen across the path, but not too many.  The forest is dark all around, since the trees have become more numerous.  A portal leads to another part of the forest.

The forest closes in from the west to end the path.  Only a few leaves have fallen over the path.  A row of white stones lines the end of the path.  To the east, a path disappears into the forest, while a clearing is visible to the northeast.

The path turns a sharp corner, and is covered in dead, decaying leaves as far as the eye can see.  The forest is quite dark to the west, and shows signs of growing even darker further to the south.  A large stone is sitting to the north of the trail.  To the south and east, the trail leads away.

The path runs straight, north and south and is clear of any debris.  The forest has grown to almost midnight darkness around the path.  Even the small sounds of animals have faded into nothing, leaving only silence. To the north, there is a hill.  To the south, the path turns away into the forest.

A clearing opens from the south edge of a hill to the forest a short distance to the south.  The ground is clear except for a few leaves near the treeline.  A staircase leads north, up a hill, while two paths diverge into the forest to the south and southwest.

This hill is in the deepest part of the forest.  The forest has darkened to pure black.  Only the hill, the path, and a portal are visible in this darkness.  The portal on this hill leads to the castle of Elinee.  To the south, a path leads back through the forest.

The forest is quite dark along the path, owing to the fact that the trees are much thicker in this part of the forest.  A large bush bisects the trail neatly.  A thin layer of decaying leaves carpets the forest floor along this part of the path.  To the northwest, a hill is visible, while to the north a path leads deeper into the forest.

The road forks, leading to different parts of the forest.  There are few leaves, while a large stone sits in the middle of the path.  The forest seems to lighten to the north, while darkening to the west.  One part of the path goes west, the other north.  To the south, the path disappears around a corner.

Large mushrooms line the path.  The forest is fairly sparse around this hill, and light passes freely through the canopy to the forest floor.  A few leaves have fallen on the trail.  The trail splits, southeast and southwest, leading to opposite ends of the hill.  A portal leads to another part of the forest.

The path turns, and is clear to the end.  The forest to either side is extremely dark.  Over the trees, the towers of Elinee's Castle are visible.  A short distance to the north, a hill is visible.  To the northeast, a path leads back through the forest.

The rocky cliff and dense forest come together, creating a small cove.  From the cliff to the edge of the forest is a row of blooming, light blue and red dandelions. The bright colors fade in and out as the blood red clouds pass by overhead, casting broken shade over much of the forest.

The trees break for this natural clearing, where a number of large nests on the ground are home to what look like chocobo eggs.  From the trees around the clearing, thick green vines extend over the ground across the clearing.  The vines are thick and make it difficult to walk without tripping.

Bright light illuminates this cave, and the greenish glow is intensified by natural light from the west.  Obviously, the exit is quite near now.  To the west, a set of stairs connects to yet another cave, which seems to lead outside.  There is a huge pile of bones here as well.

The path splits up around a large pit through this tunnel.  Its edges are rough, but the cuts appear sharp.  Both sides around it lead to a set of stairs, and a gigantic stalagmite towers due north.  The majority of the caves lies to the southwest

In this cave, a path has been literally smashed through the stalagmites.  It does not appear as if any mining activities have ever been performed here.  Also, the distant cave walls seem to lack the intermittent glow of mythril ore which can be seen everywhere els
This stone platform towers before a deep pit.  From far below, a faint eerie green glow shines up.  Maybe it would be wise not to step too far towards the edge, unless you can fly...

This is an intersection connecting three caves.  It must have been well-traveled in the past, as there are still traces of a mining railway to be seen here.  Nowadays, though, only the occasional dripping of water can be heard in the distance

This is a huge cave which marks the end of the mining efforts in this direction.  Apparently, most of the cave is of purely natural origin.  All of its walls are dripping with moisture, while the ceilings, spiked with tiny stalactites, lose themselves in the darkness

A tunnel lies quite close to the mine entrance, winding itself in a sharp curve.  Many small stones lie on the ground, and more gravel seems to fall down from time to time.  To the east is an intersection, and after a turn, the tunnel opens on a stone arch going due south

Below a stone arch, the path opens upon an intersection between three directions.  The area was apparently well-traveled in the past, but now only a dim, faint echo answers the sounds of human presence.  The arch leads towards the mine's entrance to the north, to the east, the tunnels fade into darkness, while the west path seems to open upon larger caves

This tunnel winds itself into the southernmost part of the mines.  There are many more streaks of mythril ore now, although it still remains sparse.  This section of the mines seems to be darker as well.  To the southeast, another cave opens up, while the west path leads back to an intersection

Situated at the crossroads of several larger caves, this one marks a large, rather natural passageway between different section of the mines.  Straight to the north, the light seems to get dimmer, whereas to the west, it seems much brighter than everywhere else.  The path to the southeast winds itself back into the rest of the mines

A narrow ledge leads to the north-eastern part of the mines.  To the south lies a cliff reaching deep into the earth.  Below, far in the distance, a green glow shimmers faintly... What could possibly produce that light?  The ledge winds and turns to the north-east or west back to the entrance

The eastern-central part of the mines, as in the rest of the cave, is illuminated by a soft and dim glow.  It functions as a large conduit, with the western end leading to the mine entrance and the eastern path leading deeper into the mines.  Encased in the walls, some sparse remains of mythril ore can be seen.

rooms.name: The entrance to the Mythril Mines

userData.LongDescription: This is the entrance of the Mythril mines.  It immediately strikes any traveller that the cave is not completely dark.  On the contrary, a green metallic glow dimly lights the whole area.  The cave walls are dripping from moisture, and some occasional sparks indicate the presence of former mythril veins.

In this cave, most of the old mythril ore apparently has been mined out.  Only sparse remains glitter poorly in the natural, dim light spread too thin throughout the mines.  There are some rusty bits of old tools littering the ground that look as though they were abandoned long ago.

This spot marks an intersection in the Mythril Mines.  It must have been well-traveled in the past, back when the miners were still extracting the ore.  Now, most of the mining equipment has disappeared.  Was it removed when the mine was closed or simply looted?  None certainly could tell by now... The path splits to the east and to the west, while the entrance to the mines is back north

This cave marks the end of the galleries in this area.  Apparently nobody has cared to dig any further.  One can't help noticing the remains of a former adventurer lying on the ground... Just how safe is this place really?

This is an oval-shaped platform located above the cave you just left.  The walls are bare but dripping with moisture, showing some sparse remains of poor-quality mythril ore.  There is a huge stalactite here, leading down

This place opens upon another cave to the east, near the mine's entrance.  It looks like the curvature of the walls and gradual incline was enough to obscure this opening from below.  From here, the path winds itself back into the heart of the mines to the southwest.  Another spur leads into another cave located northwest

Offering a strange mix between nature's influence and human efforts, the cave seems intact for the most part, while to the east, one can clearly make out the relics of formerly intensive mining efforts.  It is assumable that every bit of ore available has been dug out here

Here, a large, stony alcove opens to the south, which was obviously dug out by the mining company, probably to contain mining material and such.  Now it is just empty, and moss has started covering the ground, creating a somewhat depressing sight...

This marks the end of the Mythril Mines.  Certainly the largest and brightest cave of the underground installation, it opens up on a huge, natural passageway to the outside.  A half-demolished shack leans against the cave walls.
This is a grassy, windy ledge outside of the mines.  It is possible to climb down here, but unfortunately time has withered the path so much that it is almost impossible to get back up from below

This part of the cavern connects two caves; it must have been a passage between the main section of the mine and a great excavation area.  The walls are rounded and quite smooth, a testament to a very active past.

Emerald grass grows out over the hills and plains. A gentle wind breezes through, making the appearence of waves flowing through the endless blades. Perked ears, and a wriggling nose of a rabbit can be seen before it hops off into the fields.

Rocky foothills rise and fall along a high mountain range. Billowy, white clouds cover the mountain tops as others whisp on by. A few loose rocks tumble down as a goat trudges through, hiking up the rocky ledge with ease. Fort Condor can be entered here.

A small enclosure sits just offshore, housing a small submarine. From the shoreline a couple walkways lead out to the enclosure as smooth rock lines up where the submarine pulls in. The only place the sub goes to now is the sunken Gelnika, forever trapped in the oceans maw.

Rocky foothills rise and fall along a high mountain range. Billowy, white clouds cover the mountain tops as others whisp on by. A few loose rocks tumble down as a goat trudges through, hiking up the rocky ledge with ease.

This particular room definitely causes those inside to have feelings of claustrophobia. The walls here are very close together and the ceiling is slightly slanted. Everything is sturdy and does not appear to be needing repair, but there is still something very ominous about this particular place. The northern wall has a heavy-looking wooden door embedded into it, and the path to the south seems to lead to a large study.

rooms.name: Ice Palace: Lair of the Frost Gigas

userData.LongDescription: An old throne room rests at the end of the long path through the Ice Palace, but the Frost Gigas that calls this place home isn't willing to give it up. The fine decorations that once made this place beautiful have been destroyed by the monstrous occupant. There is something in the back of the room that appears to be, on closer inspection, the remains of previous adventurers.

Somehow, this room has no ice on the floor, or any other moisture. It's a small room, shaped like a cube, with large stones making up every wall. Even though there isn't any ice and it is closed off by two doors, the room is still bitterly cold. The floor seems to be a bit uneven, though.

Not only is the path here narrow, icy, and cold, but there is a deep pit on the eastern side! Looking down, the bottom is not visible, which means that if the heart attack during the fall doesn't kill you, the sudden stop should. The path twists around the perimeter of the room and then goes out into the center, where some small torches give dim illumination to the room.

This hallway really isn't much of a hallway, it's more like a walk off the plank on a pirate ship. The icy floor is surrounded by very deep, very unforgiving pits. The bottom isn't visible at all. Falling here is surely fatal, so it might be a good idea not to do it.

The hallway here is dimly lit and has the atmosphere of a prison escape tunnel. The walls appear to be highly unstable, as they are starting to crumble in a lot of places. Pieces of block litter the floor, which provides some traction on the ice. A small breeze blows through from the north.

While many of the rooms in the Ice Palace are cold, this one takes the cake. A swift, biting wind blows down a long flight of steps, making the temperature seem much lower than it is. There are candleholders on the walls, complete with candles, but there isn't any way a flame would last here due to the wind.

Here the walls of the hallway are replaced by deep pits, which don't look too safe to fall into. Normally that wouldn't be a problem, but the path is icy, and one bad movement could cause a fatal slip. There is a door here, leading to yet another room to the north.

The hallway opens to a set of stairs leading up to what appears to be another hallway. The stairs are slightly damaged, and ice covers them in some spots. As if that wasn't bad enough, there is no handrail to hold on to. Somewhere off in the distance, the sound of water dripping can be heard.

Aside from being in the darkest place in the room, this part of the path is pretty nice. There's more ice-free footspace than in other places and the temperature doesn't seem so cold. Although the place is nicer than the surroundings, it's still not an ideal place to take the family for a picnic by a longshot.

Both the eastern and western sides of this hall are walls made by bookshelves. Both shelves are covered with a thick frost and have small icicles hanging from the shelves. Most of the books here look ruined, their covers torn and sagging. The sight of it all is fairly depressing. Hopefully the rest of the library isn't in decay as well.

The hallway here is more like a cold, blue tunnel. The lighting is very dim, but at least there's carpeting to provide some traction against the ice. It seems that the walls here have been cracked, and water has somehow frozen into ice inside the cracks. Everything here looks to be fairly stable and in no danger of collapsing anytime soon.

This room is almost exactly like the one before it, the only way out is a door to the south, the same way in. It is also quite a bit colder here, and the floor is covered in ice. The northern wall is also covered. It smells as if something has died here, but there's not enough light to be able to see if something did.

Upon setting foot on this already crumbling section of walkway, some small pebbles pop out of the side of the ledge and plummet to the ground below. It's obvious that this section can't support much weight, and hanging around here could prove to be a very fatal decision.

Compared to the southern section, this part of the library, besides being a dead end, is a bombhole. Hell, compared to any other place in the library, this section is a bombhole! The floor is covered with dust, as is every book and every other space. Mostly everything here appears to be either destroyed or extremely old.

Never before has there been a more nicely organized shelf of books as there is here. Compared to the damaged rows around this one, these books seem to be not only in perfect condition, but all are aligned and in alphabetical order. It's almost as if they were all just a big painting. The floor is in good order, with all the tassels of the carpets in rows as well.

The hallway makes a small turn here, making a corner to the southwest. The corner is full of what appears to be destroyed books, some with nothing but empty covers. Their destruction doesn't appear to be accidental, and there are some books hanging off the shelves and on the ground. There was obviously some kind of conflict here earlier...

The library branches into three different paths, all of them appearing to be dead ends. There is most likely a bend in the path further down one or more of them, but it isn't easy to see far ahead with the way the bookshelves are positioned. A cool breeze blows through, occasionally changing direction in a seemingly random pattern.

This section of the library looks more like a hallway. The bookshelves are completely bare and have stone walls for backings. The floor, instead of being carpeted like the rest of the library, is made of icy stone. While the environment to the south is much more like the rest of the study, the northern path appears to lead to a door.

Amidst the icy surroundings, there is a set of steps leading down, a break in the hallway, and a small trickle of water going down the wall. The water quickly freezes into ice after hitting the ground, making it a bit slick. The air here is cool, crisp, and refreshing, but it's still very cold.

The walls seem to be sturdy and holding up against the pressure of the aging castle upon them, despite a few cracks here and there. It's slightly warmer here than in the surrounding areas, but it's still very cold. There is a small picture on the eastern wall.

The path suddenly stops with a bookshelf blocking the way. There is a path behind it, but the shelf won't budge because of the weight of the books on it. Even if there weren't any books on it, the shelf is probably fastened to the floor. There is nothing to do here but go back and see if another path leads to somewhere useful.

In a place with so much ice, it's truely rare to find a room with a regular, stone, non-ice covered floor like this one. Unfortunately, it's still cold in here. There are only two ways in and out, and they are two doors, both of which appear to be identical.

While much of the library is crammed full of books, this section seems to have almost none. Some small novels sit on the shelves, but these are few and far in between. The entire room has that "Brand New, Never Removed the Shrink Wrap" kind of feel. Never before has there been such a desolate and lonely collection, and the mere sight of it is painfully depressing.

A warp tile here sits in the center of what appears to have once been some kind of altar surrounded by a large chasm. Four raised torches border the tile and bring light to this otherwise dark space in the palace. A thin walkway in a severe state of disrepair connects the altar to an entrance in the corner.

This small room deep inside the Ice Palace is pretty plain and generic, with the exception of the beautiful door in the northern wall. The door is bigger than others found in the Palace, and it is a lot nicer on the eyes. Even with all its beauty, it seems to suggest that there's something important behind it...

It's almost as cold inside the Ice Palace as outside. The ice walls provide a sturdy shield against the wind outside, though, which takes most of the chill away. The floors in the dimly lit palace are a bit slippery where the carpets end, and the interior is almost completely blue. At least the air is cool, clear, and refreshing to breathe.

A set of stairs leading down into a hallway serves as an exit from the Ice Palace library. Rows of shelves with books are arranged in such a way that they seem to create a maze. A small pile is visible through the small gaps in the shelves, but what it is or if you can get to it is not known. Finding a good way through here should be interesting, to say the least.

This is one of the corners of the fairly large chamber. Several chunks of the side of the walkway are missing and other parts are loose. The ceiling of the chamber seems to slant towards the inside as well, as if it were about to collapse under it's own weight. Using extreme caution and choosing steps carefully is a good idea.

The hallway suddenly stops into a dead end, and there's nowhere else to go but back. This room is blue, like the others, and very dimly lit. The air here is old and hard to breathe, and smells like burning plastic. The walls here are also cracked, but more than earlier. It's easy to see that the ceiling could cave in at any time from the lack of anything holding it up.

The Nibelheim Mako reactor sits atop a plateau high up in the mountains.  A stainless steel walkway leads to the raised entrance of the reactor.  Caution lines frame the open doorway leading further into the reactor.  The plateau reaches north on both sides of the reactor, while a path leads southwest down the mountain.

A few desperate rays of sunshine poke through the dark clouds and glance off the mountain peak.  The rock is cracked, revealing a cave leading deep within the mountain.  A wooden bridge slopes down to connect to another mountain in the southeast.

Stalagmites and pillars ring a depression in the ground in the middle of the cavern.  A small tunnel connects the depression to the upper landing.  More rocky growths dot the base of the walls, while a glowing green chamber beckons through an opening in the northern wall.  A path along the eastern wall leads to the southern part of the cave.

The Nibelheim Mako reactor sits atop a plateau high up in the mountains and casts a shadow to its north.  Though largely abandoned, some machinery hums along the reactor tower as it rises upward.  A metal door occupies a space hewn roughly out of rock wall to the northeast.

Rails run the length of the platform, reaching the wall to the south and a sizable landing to the north.  A single lamp hangs down from the distant ceiling, though the green glow from the bottom of the tower makes electric light superfluous.  A chain leads above.

The southern edge of the mountain is framed by a long path.  The path winds wildly to the northwest, though it widens as it reaches a plateau to the southeast.  Below the path, two limestone outcroppings uncharacteristically break the steady wall of sedimentary rock.

The bridge becomes quite steep as it approaches its connection point to the northwest mountain.  The mountain's face is incredibly smooth at this height, as though some spikes were shorn to make room for the bridge.  The black peaks of the northern mountains poke through the dark fog.  A glint of metal shines from behind the mountain, a sign that Shinra's reactor is near.

The path narrows, connecting the base of the mountain in the north to a small island-like plateau in the south.  Deep chasms to the east and west are hungry to swallow any adventurers who misstep, while a light glows on the west bank of the path.

A strong green glow lights the cave to the south and parts of the current cavern.  Rock pillars shape numerous paths through the cavern.  There is a ledge to the northwest, while the southern wall curves sharply to the northeast, leading to an intersection.

A purple marker rotates within a blue sphere of energy in the middle of the rocky floor.  A pool of Mako energy to the east reflects off the various pipes in the area, making this part of the cavern brighter than those higher up.  A large rock blocks vision to the west, while a large pipe reaches down from the top of the cavern.

The middle section of the long wooden bridge leaves one a long way from safety.  A green glow marks the cracks in the southeast mountain's base and the valley below.  Spikes from the northwest mountain stab the air around the bridge and resemble a claw ready to snap up a fallen adventurer.  A narrow path is visible below the claw-like rock formation.  Far to the north, the fog twists the shapes of the mountains.

The end of the path nestles tightly against the mountain, slightly hidden by a claw shaped series of spikes to the west and an overhang above.  Corroded fog spawns a washed-out light show past the cliff at the eastern edge of the path, but the silhouettes of other mountains can still be seen through the glow.

A sand-colored plateau hangs out over the southeastern edge of the mountain.  As the plateau moves further into the mountain, it is divided into two paths by a cylindrical rock formation.  The path narrows and curls along a cliff to the northwest, while it ascends into crags as it goes north.  A small opening in the rock formation leads into a cave.

This part of the path is enclosed by spikes.  The path appears to plateau a bit further up.  A fork traverses the mountain and leads east under a spike coming off the plateau.  South leads back down to the claw-shaped crossroads below.

A rickety-looking wooden bridge spans the impressive distance between mountains.  An obsidian monolith pierces the fog off the north side of the bridge, while a number of smaller stone formations ring the far edges of the valley.  Faintly, a green glow seeps out from cracks in the rock below, and a path leads northeast.

The trail bows out to the east as it leads to the base of the mountain.  West leads towards stable ground, while southwest presents a narrow path out over the chasm.  Far to the northeast, more of the spike-shaped mountains characteristic of the range are visible.

The northeastern corner of the cave connects three distinct paths that wind through the rock pillars characteristic of the cavern.  Natural light to the south indicates a connection to the outside, while the green glow of the west and southwest passages beckons deeper into the caves.

The stone trail to traverse the Nibelheim Mountains curls around the edge of a misty chasm.  Spiky rock growths jut out from various places within the chasm.  It almost appears as if the mountain was once wounded and has evolved defenses.  The town of Nibelheim can be seen to the southwest.

The path widens greatly at this point, forming a circular landing on the mountain's southwest face.  A rock wall blocks some of the view to the north, but some fading sunlight glows from behind it.  The edges of the landing to the west and south are smooth and offer a sheer drop to any misstep.

The distinct green glow of Mako energy shines down on a forming crystal in the center of the room.  A network of gnarled roots to the south parts only briefly to allow access to the outside.  To the north, a crack in the stone wall leads deeper into the glowing cave.

The floor is comprised of panels bolted onto the metal frame of the reactor mechanisms.  There are still some gaps between panels and no railings even though the structure was ostensibly completed some time ago.  Stairs lead up to a more natural rock plateau, while the panels continue west, winding their way between a series of pipes descending from the above plateau.

A large spike points nearly straight up on the east side of the path, while a claw shaped rock formation stabs the air to the west.  The path descends to a landing in the southwest, and extends along a gigantic canyon to the northeast, narrowing as it gains altitude.

The narrow trail curves here, leading to Nibelheim in the southwest and further into the mountains to the southeast.  A bright light reflects off of the rock wall to the northeast, perhaps amplified by the mist.  Across the chasm, another part of the trail turns deeper into the mountains.

The rocky floor is cracked and uneven underfoot, with two large pipes reaching down from the mechanical structure above.  Support girders for the structure reach through the ground to the west and north.  One ladder leads up to part of the structure, while another ladder leads down to the base of the cavern.

The path spirals around a spiked peak.  More structures of a similar shape are visible far to the northeast.  A higher vantage point can be found further up the spiral, while the main path through the mountains is to the south.  The spikes adorning the peak appear unnatural and there are some signs that the path may have been man-made.

The path forks here.  North leads up a mountain while southwest goes further into the mountain range.  The path curves to the east, and then becomes more dangerous as it narrows.  While the path here is more stable than in other parts of the mountain range, the chasm still lurks to the south.

Mako energy cracks the earth to the south and west and lends a faintly green hue to the surrounding area.  A large rock obscures vision to the east, but a path makes further passage possible.  There is a breeze blowing in from an opening to the south, leading out of the cavern.  A ladder leads to a plateau above.

A numbered set of very large pipes offers purchase to destinations further into the ruins.  A few smaller pipes run through the northern rock wall, while a staircase to the east offers an alternate means to descend.

The path plateaus here, enclosed by spikes above and below.  Another part of the path runs below, eventually leading further up the mountain, though the peak looks too difficult to reach without specialized equipment.  The only way to leave is down.

A number of flat rocks stack neatly along the northwest wall.  Varying shades of green flicker across the surfaces of the rocks, changing appearance by the moment.  A yellow chest stands open a short distance from the rocks, while a path leads east.

The trail widens for a moment, fortifying itself before continuing across the narrow parts.  A bright light can be seen reflecting off the rock wall of the northern path leading to the base of the mountain.  The path curves to the northwest, leading away from the mountain range.

Myriad conduits and electrical cables drape off the walls of the reactor like parasites gorging on the abundant Mako energy.  A very pale, but intense, green glow illuminates the tower from its source, hundreds of feet down.  The only footing remaining at the reactor entrance is a parallel pair of pipes that leads ahead to more stable ground.

The paneled flooring bends in accordance with the contours of the rock wall on the western side of the cave, but there is still a gap between the two.  The path continues to the east, between a crowded area of large pipes, and a ladder leads down to another platform comprised of panels.

The path comes to an abrupt halt along its northern edge, though it is still possible to return southeast.  Numerous flat rocks are piled below the ledge and flicker varying shades of green.  A yellow chest has been cracked open to the east of the rocks.

Three concrete panels and a wooden one form a hollow rectangle of floor,  A small gap between the panels reveals a steel support girder.  A dark wooden board bridges the height difference between the panel flooring and the natural rock shelf to the west, leading to a metal door in the cavern wall.  Two ladders lead to other plateaus above and below.

A small ledge juts out from the side of the mountain, unprotected from the elements.  There is tremendous fog going further down the mountain, but a path and an opening are visible below.  It is possible to leap down, but there is no visible means to climb back up to the ledge.

The path forks to the west, resembling the shape of a claw, and goes down a slight hill to the east.  The southwest part of the fork leads to a long bridge spanning the chasm, while the northern part leads up the mountain.

A long path curls east around the base of the mountain range.  A sheer cliff of sandstone drops into the reddish depths along the southern edge of the mountain.  Around a bend to the northeast, a large mechanical tower peeks out from behind the rock face.

Magnificantly crafted gears trundle in a column on the east side of the platform, while a series of valves can be controlled by wheels on the western side.  A set of rails constrains the way south, while an open doorway leads further into the reactor.

The path becomes very narrow as it traverses the area between two large spikes to the east and a sharply sloping rock face to the west.  The descent to the south happens in two intervals, culminating in a large plateau at the southeast edge of the mountain.  North brings more switchbacks as the path ascends.

This platform stands atop a support beam bored into the rock wall to the north.  A yellow chest stands ajar in the middle of the platform, while a large pipe above provides the only access to the platform.  It is necessary to leap to a ledge to the east to avoid being swallowed by the Mako pool below.

This part of the path nestles into a slight depression in the mountain.  The path curves gradually up as it goes east, eventually coming perpendicular to a ledge.  To the west, the path branches, claw-like in its shape.  A great chasm beckons to the south.

The altitude of this plateau affords a view all the way to Nibelheim in the south.  Though there are some handholds in the rock, attempting to climb any further up would be reckless due to the height and unevenness of the spiky peak.  A spiral path leads back down.

A thin path curls around to the southwest edge of the mountain, while incredibly thick fog hides any trace of the mountain's base.  On a ledge above, a cave leads into the mountain, but looks inaccessible.  A second cave at path level beckons inside, its darkness standing out against the light rock of the mountain's face.

A metal support beam and wall bolts keep a wooden platform rigid despite the dearth of flooring at the top level of the reactor.  Gears and valves churn along the far wall, providing mechanical power to the structure.  A large chain is the only means to go further into the reactor, while two parallel pipes lead back to the entrance.

The rock of the walls and floor is very smooth within this cavern.  Various stalagmites and growths block most of the way north, but a path leads along the eastern wall.  There is a small alcove on the western wall reflecting a faint green light emanating from the northern part of the cavern.

Pale green light seeps in from an opening at the south end of the passage, mixed with a slight breeze.  Rock columns shape the way north, where the light dims, but does not become dark enough to hide the intersection ahead.

The path ascends sharply to the east and then levels off abruptly.  It dips as it goes west, as if to accomodate the spike-rimmed plateau overhead.  The fog at this altitude makes the fading sunlight flicker unpredictably, making estimates of the distance to the peak unreliable.

The path curls along the edge of the mountain, cradled by spikes as it ascends.  Enclosed on nearly every side, this position could just as easily cause feelings of safety or dread depending on whether it is the enclosure or the cliff that is in view.  It is possible to go up, to a possible plateau, or west, leading back down the mountain.

A ledge to the west slopes gently down and continues the path.  There is no choice but to jump down to proceed in that direction.  To the east, the path snakes to adapt to the edge of the chasm.  A large spike looms overhead, hiding the top of the mountain from view.

The path turns north into an s-shape and curves around the edge of the chasm.  A large, spiky mountain looms to the north and dwarfs the one to the east, while the trail forks to the east.  A narrow section of the path can be seen across a gap to the south.

Crimson fog reaches up from the depths of the mountain, shrouding the western edge of the path as it curls southeast along a cliff.  Far below, the mountain has been worn down to its sedimentary layers, its brown contrasting with the bright gray rock above.  East leads in from the cliff, though the path quickly switches back along the other side of a gap to the north.

A path leads outside from the base of the cavern, spanning the distance between two glowing pools of Mako energy.  Three large pipes pump out energy from the pools.  Claw marks litter the rock floor, indicative of a large beast in the territory.  A large rock dominates the landscape to the northwest, but another path leading out of the cavern is visible to the west.

This cavern is a maddening synthesis of natural rock and Shinra's machines.  A rotting wood bridge leads out, through the chilling breeze blowing in from the mountain path.  A mess of pipes exists to the west, while some stairs offer a far saner way to descend into the ruins.

The path rounds over a slight bump as it goes to the north.  Large, spiny outcroppings frame the path on both the east and west sides and cause the path to snake as it ascends.  To the south, the path widens into a plateau extending over a cliff.

The ground forms an imperfect plateau as it slopes downward towards the edges.  The mountain rises higher still, but the sheer face prevents climbing further.  Some distance to the northeast, another mountain range is visible.  The only path goes down the back of the mountain.

Rows of pods line the room as it rises to the north, broken only by a red staircase in the center.  The wall at the top of the stairs is cracked and damaged around a closed door, though a green light remains intact enough to glow above the door.  A network of pipes clusters along the ceiling and then diverges to connect to the pods.  The word 'JENOVA' is written in red at the top of the northern wall.

The Nibelheim Mako reactor sits atop a plateau high up in the mountains and casts a shadow to its north.  Two large pipes connect the reactor tower to what appears to be a pumping station along the rock wall to the west.  The reactor entrance is to the southeast, while the plateau wraps east around the back of the reactor.

The path forms a horseshoe beneath gigantic rocky protrusions that jut out of the eastern side of the mountain.  The northwest component of the path ascends, while west curls further down the mountain.  Another path runs along a cliff on the other side of an outcropping to the east.

The base of the mountain range is framed by a narrow path going east and west.  The south side of the path is open to the air, which becomes a reddish fog at lower elevations.  A limestone cliff rises high to the north, but does not manage to completely hide a large mechanical tower on the other side of the rock face.

Covered in cobwebs, there isn't much inside the room.  The only three objects in the room are a bed, a bookcase, and a drawer.  The walls are stripped bare, as were the rugs, as if somebody had removed all objects of material value here.  The bed has an outline pushed down in it, like someone had been bedridden for a long time.

Overlooking the ocean, a fresh sea breeze is coming in from the north.  A steep rocky cliff blocks most of the way eastward.  To the west is the post office, surrounded by a small picket fence.  There are small paths to the southeast and to the southwest.  The item shop lies half submerged to the south, but the water is too deep to get to it.

Dark and foreboding, the entrance of Mobliz is overshadowed by the submerged item shop to the west.  A steep rocky cliff blocks most of the way north, but there is a small foothold of land that allows access into the center of Mobliz.  A small graveyard can be seen to the southwest, but appears to be blocked by a foul-smelling swamp.

A small outcropping of land serves as a path around the fence surrounding the post office.  The fence is in a bad state of disarray, with a few of the wooden slats freely swinging in the wind and others lying on the ground.  A few feet within the fence is the post office.  One of the broken windows of the item shop to the southeast has been left open.  The sea breeze from the north gently sweeps the path, replacing the stench of the southern swamp with a fresh salty smell.  To the west is the center of town.

A bare counter sits to the left of the entryway.  The owner of the relic shop did not survive the light of judgement, and all his wares have been pilfered.  A metal drain runs through the top of the ceiling, made to collect rainwater and automatically water the outside garden with it.  Other than the counter and the drain, the walls are completely bare.  There is a door in the back of the room and another near the front of the shop.

Uphill and upwind from the swamp, the nasty stench is gradually dissapating along this incline.  A small garden lies to the northwest, surprisingly bountiful given the poor condition of the land.  An abandoned house is immediately to the west, while to the northeast is the former relic shop of Mobliz.  Although there are a couple small holes in the roof, the relic shop seems to have survived the age of Kefka.  The center of Mobliz lies downhill to the south.

The post office stands immediately to the north.  In front of it and slightly to the east is a rotted mailbox.  Children play in the center of Mobliz to the west.  A foul-smelling swamp lies to the south, a watery tomb for lower Mobliz.  A path around the telegram sender's house is off to the east.  There's a wooden picket fence surrounding the telegram sender's house.  Half of the wooden slats from the house lie on the ground beneath it.

rooms.name: In front of the Relic Shop - Mobliz

userData.LongDescription: A wooden sign hangs, loosely supended on one chain, above the door to the relic shop. To the west, a small garden is growing quite a bit of food.  There have been some repairs made to the relic shop, as the door looks fairly new.  A sharp dropoff prevents travel to the east or southeast.  The post office lies down the cliff to southeast.  The sound of kids playing can be heard downhill to the south, towards the center of town.

rooms.name: In front of a house - Mobliz

userData.LongDescription: The house of the wounded soldier lies immediately to the north.  Surprisingly, it is relatively unscathed.  However, it is covered in cobwebs, leaving the impression that nobody has been there in a while.  Only the faint sounds of the chirping crickets to the south can be heard.  The center of town is directly to the east and the swamp is a few feet to the south, its stench more powerful here than anywhere else.

The inside of the post office looks to be in much better condition than the outside.  A gentle breeze blows in through the window on the right.  The smell of kerosene emanates from a lantern that sits on a nearby table.  A staircase is on the left side of the room, leading down.  Some voices can be heard downstairs.

All kinds of crops are growing in this small garden: lettuce, carrots, peanuts, potatoes, and squash.  The slime from the swamp is brought here and used as fertilizer.  To the immediate east is the former relic shop.  There are metal drains guiding the rainwater that leaks in from the roof into little canals dug in the garden.  The center of Mobliz lies downhill to the southeast.  A steep drop prevents any travel south.

The stench here is unbearably bad, as this room is right over the middle of the swamp.  Piles of mildewed rags are strewn about everywhere, soaked in the nauseous swamp water.  There is a bed here, but it has also been claimed by the stagnant muck.  Remnants of potions, ethers, and other items are on the shelf at the other side of the room, but they look unusable.

A neatly turned bed lies in the corner of this room, near a lamp sitting on a table providing light.  This room is either a very large closet or very small bedroom.  Regardless of what it used to be, it has been turned into the babysitter's bedroom.  The only other furniture is a dresser next to the table.  The only exit to this room is the door through which it is entered.

There are many children here, playing games and sleeping in the sleeping bags that are scattered about the room.  The old work basement of the post office has been converted into a children's dormitory.  There is a door on the opposite side of the room from the stairs.  Books, toys, and plates of leftover food are scattered around the floor.  It is difficult to walk without stepping on one of the many children sleeping in the room.

A small window overlooking the ocean lets in the nice, peaceful seabreeze.  The only object in this room is a small bed that lies in the corner, unused.  There is a sign on wall.  The exit from this room is through the door used to enter it.

Months' worth of dust and soot completely hide what used to resemble a clean floor.  Aside from the cobwebs and dust, the room is completely bare.  Before Terra came to take care of the town's orphaned children, they would hide in this room when monsters would invade the town.  Built into the side of a rock cliff, this room is completely protected from weather and monsters alike.

The most notable trait of the center of Mobliz is that the nasty stench associated with the swamp is at its worst.  A narrow dirt walkway forms a small circle and a gradual incline leads north to the former relic shop.  The putrid-smelling swamp is directly to the south.  There are crickets chirping in the swamp, but the dark haze emitted from it, makes it difficult to see.  To the west is the house of the wounded soldier.  A wooden fence is to the east, and contained within it, the post office.  A small, flickering light can be seen inside the windows.

The shores of this small island are covered in stones and a large patch of dead grass covers its center.  A large mountain sits in the center of the grass.  At its base is a large hole in the rock, big enough for a person to fit through.  Strange growls and screeches of unknown creatures emanate from the hole in the mountain.  The Falcon sits on one of the larger patches of grass nearby.

This cavern was dug by... something.  The walls are covered in deep scratches and cuts that are far too deep and numerous to have been caused by human hands.  One passage in particular is sheared through the rock, leading north.  Near the entrance to that passage lies a treasure chest, one that's apparently been open for quite some time.  There's a warp tile on the ground - perhaps it would be a safer choice than the passage to the north.

Another dark cavern and another room to explore.  The cave is lit up by natural light, the source of which cannot be determined, but it does help to illuminate the paths to the various passages through Ebot's Rock.  To the south is a warp tile, leading back towards the entrance of Ebot's Rock.  The cave has several other exits - one to the west, another to the northeast and a final one to the east.

rooms.name: Passage leading to the final cavern

userData.LongDescription: This passageway is very dark.  It is also damp, oddly enough, considering the cave to the south was dry as bleached bones.  The whole passage has an air of danger to it, and it gets thicker to the north.  The passage leads north and south.

rooms.name: Yet another cavern with a warp tile

userData.LongDescription: This cavern boasts many of the features of the one leading into it.  It is dark, though it has some odd form of natural light, and it is quiet.  It does have one notable difference, though, a warp tile embedded into the ground at the north end of the room.  The larger cavern lies back to the southwest, but the warp tile probably leads farther into Ebot's Rock.

Things are much different here than in the entrance to Ebot's Rock.  The cave is lit up by some form of natural light.  The cave walls appear untouched by any sort of creature and seem alive to the touch.  The cavern floor, however, is very dry.  The floor shows signs of quite a bit of wear and tear, and a thin sheet of gravel covers it.  In fact, there are some footprints from the warp tile leading into this room to another one on the far northern side of it.

This cave shows signs of many battles.  Destroyed weapons lie flung into corners of the room and wrecked armor lies upon long-dead warriors who were unable to survive the assault of whatever creature lives here.  The stench of rotten meat is nearly unbearable in this place, and whatever lives here probably doesn't appreciate the visit.

Any further movement west is blocked by a large pile of stones.  It looks like something that lives in this cave did this, however - the walls show signs of multiple impacts, as if some monster was ramming into it.  The cavern continues back to the east.

It is extremely dark in here, and impossible to see more than perhaps ten yards in any direction.  The natural path leading through here ends abruptly and there are no apparent exits aside from the entrance.  The cave does possess one oddity, however - on the end of the pathway, there is a strangely decorated tile that is just large enough to stand on.

The cavern ends suddenly, the passage leading directly into a cavern wall.  The wall has claw markings from some creature, perhaps from a battle from long ago, but there's no sign of the thing that caused the markings now.  There are no signs of any warp tiles here, and the only way back is to the west.

Rocky mounds jut bluntly from the wasted earth before the town of Thamasa, creating a natural but crude pathway in. Coniferous trees dot the land, coming together in tighter groups around some of the town's borders, providing but a mediocre barrier. Easily bypassing the trees, dust and larger debris blown through by coastal trade-winds lend greatly to the aged and unkempt appearance of the town. Stretching southward and away from the habitation at its bulbous tip, the narrow peninsula feeds into a small continent.

This small, dank, but not too dark cave is the home of the almost legendary Sage Joch of Lofty Mountains.  All around are small pillars of stone, though they don't seem to be put to any use.  A set of stairs lie to the north and atop them rests a small, insectoid creature.  Further to the north lie a set of large stalagmites, obviously there to impede progress forward.

rooms.name: Lofty Mountains -- Entrance to Joch's Cave

userData.LongDescription: This final part of the peak path consists of three small platforms, each vertically connected by short sets of stone stairs. The view here is perhaps the best in all the land; hundreds of miles of landscape are visible from this point on the mountain.
