At the top of the mountain is a tall, dome-shaped rock formation with a cave entrance, around which the grass is well cared for and dotted with yellow flowers.

This wide stone platform is adorned with an ornate rug, atop which a short insectoid creature in robes is resting.  It seems to be in a state of calm at the moment, though it likely won't mind being disturbed.  From here, the beginnings of the path after the large stalagmites can be seen, though it seems un-populated.

This plateau in the Lofty Mountains sits directly outside Mandala Village, perhaps the only settlement for scores of miles; above and below are simply expanses of mountain stretching seemingly into infinity. A dirt track lined with golden flowers leads into the town, while rough stone stairs head southeast toward a cave entrance.

Parallel to the village entrance to the west, this small series of plateaus is northwest of the gaping cave entrance. The breezes from the east side of the mountains make the grass wave slowly here. Stone stairs to the northeast lead to a dirt path marked with two stones that leads to another path to the peak.

rooms.name: Lofty Mountains -- Peak Path First Tier East

userData.LongDescription: This first grassy plateau is one step closer to the mountain's peak. The higher you go, the more of the vast Tasnican forests you can see extending below in almost every direction. The path here isn't as narrow as it was below, so there's less risk of falling off the mountain. The plateau ends at a break in the cliff face. Wooden poles on each side are connected by a crude rope bridge.

rooms.name: Lofty Mountains -- Peak Path Second Tier West

userData.LongDescription: As one continues to climb the peak toward Sage Joch's cave, the path up the numerous grassy plateaus becomes narrower and more treacherous. However, the breathtaking view of the forests below is becoming more and more extensive; the faint glint of the spires of Tasnica Castle can be seen to the west now, as well as the blue ribbon of a river. Another break in the cliff is crossed by another crude rope bridge to the east.

rooms.name: Lofty Mountains -- Peak Path Base East

userData.LongDescription: This narrow ledge is the beginning of the path leading to the peak of the mountain and Sage Joch's home. At this altitude, the expansive forests of the Tasnica kingdom are visible as a carpet of green below. Without much room to walk, travelers need to watch their step around this area. A set of stone stairs to the east leads up to the next plateau.

rooms.name: Lofty Mountains -- Outside the Shade Palace

userData.LongDescription: This trough in the series of small plateaus leading up to Sage Joch's peak always seems to be surrounded in a strong breeze that chills to the bone. Below you can see the vast craggy expanse of the mountains stretching toward the horizon, and the cliff wall here is especially high. A large cave entrance is here, and stone stairs head up the mountain to the northeast.

rooms.name: Lofty Mountains -- Peak Path Third Tier East

userData.LongDescription: The path is getting close to the peak now, and as such the sudden turn up a set of stairs to the third plateau tier comes very quickly after the end of the rope bridge from the west. It seems as if fewer travellers make it up here, as the grass is longer and less tramped down. A final rope crossing lies to the west.

Inside, this house may not be large, but it's obviously comfortable. To the west a warm fire burns in the hearth, warming a teapot that sits atop it. Two beds are just south of the hearth, and just inside the entrance is a small wooden table on a faded violet rug. The far wall has a violet-draped window, some drying herbs, and a small portrait.

Inside the temple is a tall, wide room and very little else. The stone floor is a symmetrical array of dark tan floor tiles, each decorated with the same cross pattern as the ones outside at the entrance. In the center of the room atop a very tall dais are seven arranged orbs of clear crystal. A small etched sign sits on the floor in the center of the orbs. In the far east back corner of the room is a small door.

Here at the top of the mountain is the Mandala Temple, a small edifice of grey stone that overlooks the vast expanse of Tasnica in the valleys to the west. At the very entrance is a short set of stairs flanked by two lion statues, leading up to a dais decorated with floor tiles in a cross pattern. Heavy double wooden doors lead inside.

This small, pastoral mountain village is entirely visible from here. Short green grass is blown about by pleasant breezes from the top of the Lofty Mountains, and the gentle bubbling of a clear blue mountain stream emphasizes the feeling of lazy tranquility. The stream makes a U-shape here at the town's entrance, with three small wooden bridges to the south, east, and west. Over the stream to the north is a water mill which also appears to be the town's item shop.

This high balcony overlooks the temple entrance and affords an unparalleled view of the Tasnican lands in the western valley below. The doors leading to stairs back inside sit recessed behind a wide, near-pyramidal stone pillar that rises even further into the sky. Numerous stone settings holding candles dot the pillar, as well as two more lion statues at the base of the pillar.

As the cobblestone path continues north along the stream and then turns east, it passes a white shack here at a bend in the stream. The grass is a little longer and wilder here than it is down south, giving the impression the shack used to be a house. Small groupings of flowers dot the path, as well as a small pot of daffodils. A wooden bridge across the stream lies to the east. An unmarked path also leads north.

After a long climb from the village one can reach the temple which sits to the far north atop a peak. Except for a few clear areas for viewing the endless landscape of green trees and blue rivers below, the natural stone of the mountain is unworked here except for a set of stairs that lead up to the temple entrance.

The small room in which you stand doesn't seem to fit the size of the building from the outside; most of the place must be taken up by the water mill. A wooden shop counter separates the room in halves. Behind it the shopkeeper has many shelves of goods and a small desk where he manages the books. Candles burn on the counter next to a vase of orange flowers.

The cobblestone path ends here at the northeast corner of Mandala Village. The mountain stream continues on in the north, and just to the south the item shop's water mill is visible. Groups of tulips and a pot of daffodils are scattered around a small white house with a sign reading 'Inn'. Tall pines circle the building on the north and east sides.

Here in the southwest portion of Mandala is a small house bordering some tall pines. The green grass continues to wave about, though the sound of the brook to the east fades a bit since it's farther away. A cobblestone path runs from the bridge to the east up north toward a shack, and a manicured bush of bright pink flowers lies beside the path.

This narrow stairwell at the back of the temple leads up to the roof. The banister is decorated at the bottom on both sides with the same lion statues that were found at the temple entrance. To the right of the bottom of the stairs is a small altar flanked by two lit candles and at the top are double doors leading outside.

This comfortable home serves as the inn for Mandala Village. Just inside the entrance is a wooden counter, behind which sits the innkeeper and a small cabinet with bottles and dishes. To the west is a set table with three chairs, and three identical beds pushed against the north wall, where two windows let sunlight stream in. Hanging pots of orange flowers decorate the entire place.

Pure elemental energy suffuses this realm, to the extent that nearly nothing else exists.  There are no perceivable floor, walls, ceiling, just mana.  It is a realm beyond mortal comprehension, and is where the most powerful of elemental beings reside.

This room has no notable features, and only one exit.  The walls are made of an odd black stone, as they are throughout the entire Shade Palace.  The walls are undecorated, making the tiny room even more plain.  The floor also shares this black stone setup, and the only exit is to the south.

rooms.name: Dead end in a large, dark room

userData.LongDescription: The walkway ends abruptly after a right turn leading into a wall.  It's too dark to get a view of the rest of the room - there isn't a single torch or blue flame to guide lost travelers.  There's nothing to follow aside from the path itself, which leads back to the west.

This room is small enough to cause claustrophobia and is plenty dark as well.  There are no notable features here except for two pillars at the northern end of the room and perhaps the darker color of the stone floor in this room.  The exit is to the south.

The walkways that traverse this room seem to come to a point here.  There's not much room to stand here. There is a set of blue flames that lead up to a doorway in the wall to the northwest.  Another path, to the southwest, leads back to the center of the room.

This room is gigantic, but the only way to navigate it is on various walkways, all of which are straight as an arrow and lead directly into the wall or a doorway.  This walkway leads north to a door, while south leads back to the three-way path room.

Similar to the section to the east, two large runes are inscribed on the walls in between stone pillars.  A doorway leads to an inner room of the palace, with more doorways back east.  The black and gray room is oppressing.  The way out of the palace is back to the east, then south.

This cave is a major part of the Shade Palace, with exits leading every which way... well, except for this side of it, where there are only two exits, one to the north and one to the south.  To the east, there is some kind of rock outcropping that looks to have once been two seperate rock 'islands' over the deep pits that surround the natural walkways.  The north exit leads out of the cave, but it's impossible to tell where it leads without going that way.  The south exit returns to the raised walkways.

This room is made up of stairs leading to another set of walkways above the main hall of the Shade Palace.  On the upper floor of the room there are decorated walls like those in the hallway leading to this area.  There are three seperate exits to this room - one is to the southeast, past the stairwell leading to the upper floor.  Another exit is to the north on the second floor.  A third exit to the southwest leads back into the hallway.

This side of the room is little more than a passageway leading into another cave within the rock walls of this place.  The 'path' has sheer cliffs on the western side, and any fall from them would surely be fatal.  To the north is a hole big enough to walk through, while to the east, through the oddly shaped stalagmites, is the main part of this cave.

This room is very large.  There's barely any floor to walk on at all, and what is there is barely wide enough to support three people.  There's a button completely compressed into the floor. The narrow path around the room leads east.  To the west, there are two rows of blue flames surrounding... something.  It's impossible to tell what.  South leads back from this strange room.

There's only one path through this room.  It leads past the northern wall to the west.  The wall has two window-like structures on it, but they reveal only darkness.  Two torches jut out from the east and west walls of the room, but there is no way to reach them as they are seperated from the main path by the pits around the walkways.  The path leads off to the west or back to the east.

The walkway opens up into a large central area.  The central area has three exits.  The northeast path is surrounded by two rows of flame, another leads north, and a third to the east leads back to the beginning of this room.  The central area and paths are surrounded by blackness, making the designated paths the only ones that can be followed.

The walkway terminates into a wall.  There are no additional paths or even blue flames that would suggest that this path leads somewhere.  There aren't even notable symbols on the walls - this is a dead end.  The only way to go is back to the south.

This area is a GIGANTIC cavern, lit up by unusual crystals that appear sporadically on the floor and ceiling. Even with the lighting, it's very hard to see in here, as the walls, floor and ceiling are all nearly black in color and seem to emit a darkness of their own.  There are exits to the north and south.

This hallway turns sharply at several points.  Much like other rooms in the Shade Palace, there are deep pits surrounding the walkways here, forcing travelers to follow a specific path.  The hallway continues to the west and some stairs to the south lead out of the hallway.

This 'room' is actually just a pathway set up on top of the walls of another room in the Shade Palace.  The pathway splits in two, one way leading west towards a doorway and the other leading south to the walls above the main hall.

This area is merely a large outcropping of rock that was once, apparently, two smaller 'islands.'  The northern part of this area has an odd stake of sorts buried deep into the black gravel that makes up the floor.  The southern part contains a button that was apparently pressed some time ago.   The pit that surrounds the outcropping is apparently infinitely deep.  The only exit from this room is to the east.

This room is bright and regal, much different from the rest of the Shade Palace.  In the center of the room is a large stage with a Mana Seed on it.  Six large braziers surround it.  The white tile floor is a stark contrast to any of the previous rooms in the Palace.  The only exit is to the south.

This walkway leads straight into a wall.  There are no ways in or out except the exit to the northwest, and the room is nondescript outside of the pits alongside the walkway and the two unlit torches alongside the northern wall.  The exit to the northwest leads back to a more interesting room in the Shade Palace.

This room's most notable features are the gigantic torches which extend from the floor almost to the ceiling.  The only other decoration this room possesses is a gigantic hole near the south entrance.  The hole has no visible bottom, much like the other pits in the Shade Palace.  There are exits to the north and south.

This walkway towers above the other walkways below it in this room.  The room is very large and the only passage through it is across various walkways, some of which lead into the main hall.  This walkway leads north to a doorway in the wall.  The walkways make paths across some deep pits, and are the only way to cross the room.  The only exits are to the north, through the doorway, and to the south, back into the room above the main hall.

This room is huge and at the same time drab.  Passageways of stone are the only way around this room, seeing as a huge pit makes up the floor where the walkways aren't present.  This passageway, unfortunately, leads directly into a large wall.  The only way out of here is to the south.

This room is a bit decorative, with two large runes inscribed on the walls in between some large pillars.  The room itself is split up by several doorways, each leading off into some deeper part of the palace.  The whole room has a grayish color to it and the floor is jet black.  The doors are the only way to go further into the palace, but the way out of the palace is south.

This is another dead end in the Shade Palace.  It's hard to see, and the walls only help contribute to this, as they are made up of some kind of dark stone.  There's no notable features in this room, and the only exit is to the south.

The hallway ends after several more turns, leading through a long passageway to the south.  This room is almost exactly the same as the room at the other end of the hallway - the only difference is that the walls here have an odd decoration on them.  The exit to the northeast leads deeper into the Shade Palace while the hallway continues back to the east.

The eastern side of the cave reveals more of the gigantic hole that makes up the cavern's main body.  A few scattered rocks decorate the ground and there is a gaping hole cut into the rock to the north.  Another pathway leads to the south, while west leads back towards the main part of the huge cave.

This walkway is set up one floor above the main, three-doored hall of the Shade Palace.  It doesn't lead anywhere in particular, but there are some stairs to the southeast that lead to a long hallway.  The walls here are covered in fancy designs and a button lies pressed deeply into the dark stone floor to the west.  The only exits from here are the stairs and the doorway to the north.

This cave is very small.  The cave is made up of dark stone. It is apparently a natural formation, albeit one that has two distinct exits.  The exit to the south leads back out onto the mountain, while the one to the north is very dark and leads into the depths of the Shade Palace.

The palace takes a radical change from the apparently man-made constructions to the south.  This place is a huge cave. Stalagmites block off pathways and also prevent the unwary traveler from tripping and falling into the various bottomless pits that the walkways lead across.  This room's lighting is very poor, so it's hard to make out anything in particular.  South leads back towards the exit, while west and east lead into different parts of this open cavern.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: The stairs leading down the mountain appear as if they've been slammed into the side of the mountain by a falling boulder. Long cracks spread from the top of them and spread down to the next level of the escarpment. The trail extends northeast and west before it disappears into the surrounding cliffs.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: Clouds directly overhead are being split by the peaks above. A dense mist fills the area, covering the area in a thick fog. Although the plains beyond the cliff's edge and far below can be seen without an issue, the top of the nearby staircase to the north is obscured.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: The trail from the southwest abruptly ends with a long descent to the chasms far below. The wind whips up from the depths, carrying the odor of death. Tucked against the exposed bedrock of the mountain, a small red chest sits in bold contrast against the ancient strata.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Above a Sea of Clouds

userData.LongDescription: The clear sky above is offset by an undulating canvas of dark storm clouds expanding out from the shoulder of the mountain below. A fierce wind howls, pushing the clouds into the mountain which cuts them like a knife. A dark tunnel set into a crevice leads down to lower ledge.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Above a Sea of Clouds

userData.LongDescription: A thin ridge is the only path between a long drop to a rocky shelf below and the tunnel leading down the mountain. To the north, the path drastically widens as it converges with a similar path from the east. The peak of the mountain pierces through the clouds to the northwest.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Along a Precipitous Cliff

userData.LongDescription: The plateau of the cliff widens the closer it gets to the mountain. Fallen from above, large boulders are scattered throughout the clearing, the unfortunate side-effect of the increased surface area. A pale green and sickly looking bush has managed to find enough nutrients within the rocks to survive here.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Along a Precipitous Cliff

userData.LongDescription: A small flat clearing to the side of the stone staircase overlooks the rolling green plains of the Mysidian landscape, a stark contrast to the deathly gray mountain. The treacherous trail follows the jagged cliff to the west, winding towards the mountain's peak and north towards the base.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: Dark clouds cover this section of the mountain. The large cracks in the path extend from the slope leading south and reach into the cliff face to the north. The path widens to the east and to the west a small platform can barely be made out through the fog.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: A long stone staircase is covered in gravel and shale. Incredibly dense clouds reduce visibility to only a few feet and obscure the top and bottom of the stairs to the north and south. A sickly stench carries on the heavy mist as readily as heat on flame.

From the top of a great set of stone stairs, the sea of clouds seems to extend for miles in every direction. Occasionally, glimpses of the grassy plains of Mysidia can be seen for a moment before the clouds reconnect. To the west, a sun-bleached wooden bridge connects to the peak.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: The trail narrows as it weaves between the chasm to the north and the drop-off to the south. Deep gouges in the path reveal where rocks have fallen from the cliffs above before continuing their journey down the mountain. The northwestern trail begins to bend sharply as it navigates the terrain.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: The trail extends towards the horizon and reaffirms the tremendous stature of the mountain. Chunks of shale from the nearby cliffs have fallen and shattered after smashing into the paths below.  An ancient staircase leads up the mountainside, granting access to a higher level.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: The winding trail widens as it rounds the jutting precipice to the north. A set of stone steps carved into it leads up to the next plateau. Intermittent blasts of wind kick up small dust clouds that crash into the boulders scattered on the trail. To the south, after a short drop, a footpath leading to the trailhead can be seen.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Along a Precipitous Cliff

userData.LongDescription: The narrow trail between the staircase and the edge of the cliff is all that exists between this precarious vantage point and the base of the mountain far below. A dark stairwell leads into the mountainside, supported only by rotten beams of wood.

A strange collection of small stone pillars surround a granite pedestal. Although it appears to be an attempt to create a sanctuary, any magic that was once held by this formation has long left. A vast expanse of clouds extends in every direction but west, which leads across a small wooden bridge.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: A monolithic rock juts from the ground like a stone pillar. The base of the mountain can be seen beyond the edge of the cliff, but the horizon is quickly obscured by the rolling clouds. To the south, a long set of stone steps disappears down into the heavy mist.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Along a Precipitous Cliff

userData.LongDescription: A fog-filled and darkened tunnel through the mountain leads up towards the peak. The trail skirts by an absolutely-sheer cliff towards the west. The rocky descent that lies beyond the edge extends below the base of the mountain and down into a chasm that reaches into a dark abyss. An unnaturally cold wind rises from those depths.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: Clouds brush against the mountain as they travel by, leaving behind pockets of fog which mask the cliff's edge. The ground is extremely craggy, filled with cracks, and shattered slabs of shale make the path unpredictable. A thick forest far below and to the south blends in with the rolling plains.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Above a Sea of Clouds

userData.LongDescription: The sun-baked plateau has massive cracks which branch out in every direction. A large section of the path to the north has fallen to the depths below, leaving only a thin walkway. A sloped path the west leads to a tunnel set into a crevice, which leads down the mountain.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: At the top of the short set of stairs, a thick rolling fog has obscured any view of the horizon. A small opened chest sits against the cliff face, its contents pilfered long ago. The platform disappears into a tight crevice, meaning the only exit is back down the stairs.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: A sheer crag of bedrock towers over the trail. A massive boulder that has fallen from it has found its final resting place on the path. Tall stone bluffs to the north can be reached with a set of stone steps to the east. To the south, an oddly straight line of charred earth travels from the cliffs to the ravine.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: The path widens at the base of a large set of steps which lead north and up the mountain. A thick layer of clouds behaves like a ceiling, concealing the top of the staircase. Far beyond the edge of the cliff, the rolling plains of Mysidia appear like a deep green canvas of life in comparison to this dead mountain.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: The trail narrows unpredictably as it junctions with others. One trail heads north, up to a set of craggy platforms. Another heads east, down towards the trailhead. The last trail heads towards a stone staircase and its destination is hidden in fog.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: A gigantic boulder has fallen onto the path near the top of the stairs. Large cracks in the ground spread from the impact site like a spiderweb. Deep striations along the cliff face to the north indicates this part of the mountain was created violently.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: A large opening in the side of the mountain has been reinforced with wooden beams. The sickly odor of death is carried on the breeze traveling through the passage. A small set of decayed wooden steps within the opening winds into the mountain, its destination shrouded in darkness. To the west, a large stone staircase leading down the mountain barely avoided destruction when a boulder fell nearby.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: The thin path from the north ends almost immediately on a broad, rocky platform. A small chest sits in the center of the clover-shaped terrace. Thick cloud cover obscures the view in every direction, and the choking stench of decay hangs on the mist like a humid smoke.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: A long and twisted trail leads up the mountain to the west and a pungent smell of rotten flesh carries from ravines below the jutting cliffs. Recently fallen from far above, a massive slab of rock has upturned fresh earth on the pathway and come to rest near the trailhead.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Above a Sea of Clouds

userData.LongDescription: At the northern end of the wide and flattened section a long stone staircase leads up to the summit. A short wooden bridge to the east leads to an immense natural pillar. To the west, a deep chasm separates this platform from the peak of the mountain.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Along a Precipitous Cliff

userData.LongDescription: A massive crack in the cliff threatens to drop the entire rocky formation down to the base of the mountain. To the south, a thin path covered in a fine gravel reaches up to the next crag. The trail widens to the east as it approaches the staircase which leads to the trailhead.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: A decrepit wooden bridge connects two platforms together. Each plank looks as if it's decades beyond its last leg. A thin sloping path leads south to a lower level. To the east, a stone staircase can barely be made out, which leads down the mountain.

Below the summit the mountain parts the clouds like a ship on the sea. The forests that surround the mountain are intermittently visible in the wake. However, those howling winds which are driving the clouds below have been replaced by a zephyr and a sense of calm emanates from the massive stone shrine nearby.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: The trail dwindles as it hugs the side of the mountain and becomes little more than a small outcropping. Fortunately, the escarpment connects with the next level by a set of stairs to the southwest. Near the edge of the path, a fresh crack has formed where rockfall has collided with it before continuing its journey to the bottom of the mountain. Almost hidden in the shadow, a small red chest lies abandoned near the craggy wall.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Overlooking the Plains of Mysidia

userData.LongDescription: Large crevices in the path have cracks which extend out to the cliff's edge. The narrow path meets up with an outcropping which has a cave-like tunnel leading through the mountain and up towards the peak. Thick cloud cover obscures the drop-off to the southwest. A decaying bridge to the east is barely visible through the mist.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - At the Base of the Mountain

userData.LongDescription: The path turns sharply as it runs into the cliff and promptly reverses direction. A wide section of the path leading north has been left charred by a fire which no longer burns. To the east, a narrow ravine separates the trail from itself as it connects the ascending path to the base of the mountain.

rooms.name: Mt. Ordeals - Along a Precipitous Cliff

userData.LongDescription: Miles of rolling green plains can be seen from this scenic overlook. A cool breeze travels up towards the peak. Tumultuous clouds overhead appear to be closer than the ground below. A thick rotten tree trunk lies on it side, roots fully exposed.

An oblong plateau occupies the middle third of the cavern's northern wall, illuminated by a single brightly burning torch.  Wooden bridges of varying fortitude connect to other such plateaus to form a makeshift upper level, the nearest bridge leading to the southwest.  Stairs carved from the southern ledge of the plateau lead to the lower floor.

Flickering torchlight reveals stairs leading deeper into the cavern, while the slightly open area around them quickly tapers into two paths.  A pair of beams braces the walls to the west, while the eastern path curls underneath a much more elaborate construction.

A narrow path winds through the rock to the south, leading down some stairs and through a thin passage in the wall.  Light from a torch on the northern wall illuminates the way northeast, while a wooden chest rests in slight shadow to the west.

A modest plateau nestles tightly into the northeastern corner of the cavern.  Some wooden planks bridge a serpentine gap as they exit the small exposed section of the plateau, quickly splitting in a perpendicular fashion as they lead to other plateaus west and south.

Plateaus ring the cavern, accessible along the northern and eastern walls and connected via a network of platforms.  A large staircase on the northern wall ascends to another cavern level while a shorter set of steps, slightly to the west, carves the way over the nearest plateau ledge.  The cavern expands west, beyond the plateau, while the eastern path forks below some scaffolding.

Stairs lead down the southern plateau edge, joining a narrowing path as it carves through the rock to the south.  A wooden chest leans against the western wall, left in slight shadow by a torch on the northern wall.  The plateau continues east, where two paths trail off its corners.

Two torches on the northern wall brightly illuminate a plateau in the northwestern corner of a constrained cavern.  A wooden bridge exits to another landing east and quickly takes a perpendicular fork south over a winding path, leading through a narrow strait into a larger, dimmer section of cavern.  Stairs leading up split the rock face between the two torches.

A wide plateau formed out of the southern wall chokes the winding path at its base.  A small set of steps leads north, towards some scaffolding, while the remaining path curls south through a passage in the western wall.

The southwest area of the cavern is oval shaped, enclosed on all sides except for a narrow path leading up some stairs to the north and a thin passage through the eastern rock wall.  A small wooden chest occupies the center of the oval.

The eastern section of a narrow passage appears to end abruptly, pinned against a rock wall.  A wooden bridge of simple scaffolding connects to a similar elevated section to the west, illuminated by strong torchlight.

A long bridge, braced by extensive scaffolding, exits the cavern's southeastern plateau and forks perpendicularly, connecting to two small plateaus nestled against opposite sides of the northern wall.  The plateau extends west along the southern cavern wall, eventually connecting to others in the upper level of the cavern.

A broad plateau sprawls east as it dominates the southeast corner of the cavern.  Smaller plateaus ring the cavern, one of which, in the southwest portion of the cavern, is accessible via a wooden bridge to the west.  A lone torch above the northern plateau provides illumination for this section of the cavern.

A small plateau nestles against the eastern wall of the cavern, accessible via jagged steps carved from its side.  A narrow path leads west from the base of the steps, bounded by a larger southern plateau as it snakes towards a fork beneath a scaffolding-supported bridge.

The western area of the cavern terminates in a jagged edge along the northwest wall, while a plateau to the south truncates the lower level.  Remains from a wooden bridge jut from the wall overhead, while other platforms connect a ring of plateaus as the cavern continues east.

A dim lantern reveals a sizable basalt cavern, made stable by some wooden scaffolding bracing the walls.  Small stone steps lead up to each of two platforms to the north and northwest, leading to other caverns.  Two holes break the otherwise smooth floor of the northwestern platform, while a third cave can be reached to the northeast.

A narrow, zig zagging path terminates against the northern wall of the cavern.  Wooden planks bridge the gap between high plateaus bounding the path along its east and west edges, as well as a much larger plateau to the south.  The path follows the southern bridge for its entirety, eventually turning towards an intersection slightly to the southwest.

A narrow passage stretches east, a divot in its middle bridged via wooden planks and basic scaffolding.  Torchlight at the center point of the northern wall lights the area well, revealing one skull shaped switch on each of the passage's upper levels.  A jagged staircase on the southern wall leads down into another section of the cavern.

A solitary chest is the only adornment upon a wide plateau occupying the southwesten reaches of the cavern.  Wooden bridges of dubious quality reach out to the east and northeast to connect to other plateaus.  The remnants of another bridge connecting nothing hang off of the west wall of the cavern.

Stone age tools and the skulls of various creatures litter the reaches of a spacious cavern, lit in triplicate by torchlight.  A straw mat provides the centerpiece of an elevated section, while a long staircase leads out the back of the cave.  Judging by the stench of a few decaying corpses, something has been living here and preying on other denizens of the caverns.

The second half of the armory is just as unimpressive as the first.  The old brown brick building is rather simple-looking with a sign depicting a sword hanging next to the door.  Back to the east lies the other half of the shop, while through the door you will find the armory.

Books are scattered about this dusty, old house.  A desk littered with ancient scrolls sits alone in the center of the room.  Two bookcases filled with books on monsters and other information of the occult rest in the back of the room. Rickety stairs off to the right lead on into the Elder's home, and the door leads back into Thamasa.

This side of the armory is stocked with various armors.  Behind the counter sits an old man who appears to have been working here for ages.  To the left of the counter is a suit of armor on display.  To the west is the other half of the armory, while through the door is the town of Thamasa.

Wonderous weapons from around the world adorn the rack behind the counter.  An old guy stands behind the wooden counter glaring at any who pass by.  A flower basket and register sit on the counter though both are covered in dust.  To the east is the other half of the armory and the door leads back out into the town.  An important looking sign is here, begging to be read.

In a small clearing surrounded by trees sits the grave of the fabled hero, General Leo.  His crystal sword is jabbed in his burial mound as a reminder of his bravery and strength.  In front of the mound is a grave marker with intricate writing on it. Flowers are scattered around the tombstone, but a bouquet of red flowers stands out.  Back to the west is the center of town.

This is a small village, but somehow it gives an air of some mystical importance.  Rock walls are to either side, giving the town a natural barrier.  Surprisingly, the grass here is green, even when the outside world is bleak and dead.  A cobblestone road leads to the town's center, and to the east and west are shops of various kinds.

rooms.name: In front of the relic shop

userData.LongDescription: Another marvel of simple design, the relic shop stands before you.  Barrels sit next the shop gathering dust from years of non-use.  Dead bushes wilt, proof of the great tragedy that happened so long ago.  Back across the bridge is the item shop and beginning of town.

Glorious relics from the past sit behind the counter.  A large, old man sits behind the counter waiting on someone to purchase some of his relics.  Flowers in a basket sit on the counter to help bring some color to this otherwise drab room.  Two crates sit next to the counter holding unknown items.  Back through the door is the town of Thamasa.

rooms.name: In front of the Magus Residence

userData.LongDescription: The largest house in Thamasa, the Magus residence, stands here. This simple, two-story house became the largest house in Thamasa when the old-largest burned down under mysterious circumstances.  Dead bushes sit around here as they do all around Thamasa.  A strange-looking man stands outside of the house, staring at people as they walk by.  Back to the south is the center of town, and to the west is the Elder's house.

rooms.name: In front of the item shop

userData.LongDescription: To the front is a plain looking building that appears to be the item shop.  Next to the item shop sit three barrels whose purpose is not known.  To the east lies a bridge that crosses over a small ditch to another shop.  Back to the west lies the entrance to Thamasa.

By far one of the oldest houses in Thamasa, the elder's home rests alone on top of a hill.  A garden that is surprisingly green and full of vegetables lies beside the house.  Barrels full of food sit in front of the elder's house so that anyone in town can get a snack if they are hungry.  To the east one might find the home of the most famous citizen of Thamasa.  Back to the south is the inn.

rooms.name: In front of a burnt house

userData.LongDescription: A house long ago destroyed by fire sits here.  The roof has collapsed, the door is sealed shut, and blackened spots cover various spots on the rest of the house.  Rumor has it that a youngster set this house ablaze while experimenting with his magic.  Back to the west is the center of town, while to the east through some trees lies a grave.

Despite being a peaceful town, Thamasa possesses an armory. The building doesn't look like much, but who knows what wonderous armor could be inside?  Dead bushes sit as a reminder of the devastation that happened not so long ago. To the east lies the entrance of town, while to the west is the other part of the armory.

Another simple building, the inn of Thamasa sits here.  It has the air of a simple bed and breakfast, and smoke rolls from the chimney.  The town well sits a little to the south of the inn in a prime location for the residents to get to it.  To the north is the house of the village elder, and to the east is the town center.

A young man stands behind the counter, merrily waiting on customers.  Two buckets sit between a desk and the counter.  Three chairs and a table sit in front of the buckets.  Next to the table, on a huge rug, lie four empty beds.  Next to the beds is a stove that has recently been used for cooking.  Back through the doors is the town of Thamasa.

A checkered carpet sits at the entrance to Strago's house. A table surrounded by four chairs sits in front of a stove.  An ancient-looking record player plays an unfamiliar tune.  A cabinet full of dishes is in the corner of the room, and a desk with an open book is in the opposite one.  Up the stairs is the upper level of Strago's house, and back through the door is the town of Thamasa.

A lone tree stands marking the center of town.  People wander the area and converse with one another.  Cobblestone paths extend in all directions.  To the east is a burnt house, while to the west is the inn.  To the north one would find the home of the great lore master Strago and his granddaughter Relm.  Back to the south is the airship.

rooms.name: In the home of the Elder

userData.LongDescription: A fireplace dimly lights this parlor.  A simple wooden table surrounded by chairs seems to be the center of attention.  Plates and other dishes from a recent meal are still sitting on the table.  A window to the outside serves to help illuminate the room, and provides a cool breeze.  Back down the stairs is the Elder's study.

Two beds sit in what appears to be the sleeping quarters for Strago and his granddaughter, Relm.  In between the two beds is a nightstand with a clock on it, and next to them is a bookcase.  A small desk sits next to a table with two chairs.  A vase of red flowers sits on the middle of the table.  Stairs lead back down to the lower level of the Magus household.

A clock on the wall ticks, as a young man behind the counter works on mixing up an item.  A plaque on the back wall signifies that this is indeed an item shop. A bookcase filled with books on items and their uses is near the back of the room.  The wooden counter serves as a place for exchanges of item and money, and an old register also rests on it.  Back through the door is the town of Thamasa.
Trees grow so thickly to the south they prevent passage to any but the smallest of animals.  The air is filled with the sounds of native wildlife, ignoring the passage of man through the forest.

A fallen tree lies upon the ground like a conquered foe as small shoots of different trees grow from the bark of the rotting trunk.  A hole of light, unfiltered, blindly slams into the ground like a laser pounding into the soiled earth.

The clearing is a little larger than it appeared.  There are only small shoots of grass and moss that grow below.  Overhead are blue sky, clouds, and pure amounts of radiant light.  The grass seems to enjoy this rare and elegant light.
Deep within the forest, there is barely a sound to be heard, but the rustling of small animals in the bushes.  From this deep in the forest, it is possible to go any way desired.

The trees look rather common, except for one, which is covered in dried blood and smashed on one side. It appears as though some massive creature was thrown against it with such force that it broke open both the ancient tree, and the beast that was battling.
A small snake slithers by, and its larger cousin drapes over the branch of a nearby tree.  Both peer about when they feel the footsteps hitting the earth, but don't appear to be dangerous.

Infesting the area are junglelike plants with moss and bushes containing emerald green leaves that shove their way towards the precious light.  The birds are somewhat silent around the rainforest, but can still be heard.

The way eastwards is blocked by the sheer amount of trees crisscrossing the area.  Many paths cross the ground, showing that many animals go through here.  No birds circle the area, as they tend to stick closer to the center of the forest.

To the west the forest thins out a little and looks brighter as more light makes it through to the ground.  The wind, having less resistance, picks up a little and blows around a few leaves mischieviously.

The trees are beginning to look a bit abused in this area, some having branches broken off as far up as about forty feet. A cool breeze blows through the area, carrying along with it a horrific, overpowering stench. The pathway from the east comes to an end, leaving one to have go through the forest unguided.

Birds sing thoughout the foliage of the forest.  Emerald green dew drops and beautiful flora reside everywhere.  Drops of water come down from the high trees and twisting palms of the forest.  Only the sounds of the forest echo though here.

A small lizard scurries away at the sound of footsteps crunching on the ground.  The brief flash of color streaking into the bushes is the only indication it was ever there.  Otherwise, the forest is still.
A broken twig is on the ground.  The leaves crowd everything in this forest, blocking the view in almost all directions.  The water vapor given off by the plants are kept in by the protective canopy.

The trees in this clearing are significantly more healthy than in most of the rest of the forest, and for an obvious reason. Laying in the middle of the clearing is a huge nest made out of broken off tree branches. In the nest are several broken eggs, each nearly two feet long. The eggs appear to be somewhat old, but still in somewhat good condition.
At the southern edge of the forest, the vines get too thick to continue.  Small animals rustle in the bushes, and a bird can be heard singing its song somewhere in the distance.

A brightly plumed bird circles overhead, calling out to its mate with beautiful song.  The nest of the bird stands in a tree not far away.  The trees surround the area, giving a sense of peace and tranquility.

Sitting up in the tree, all of the Dinosaur Forest is visible. The forest stretches on in all directions, and the roars of angry Tyranosaurs can be heard. There is a spot in the tree that looks as if it is a focus of energy of sorts, and as if something important is nearby.
The trees stretch far up into the air, seeming to scratch the sky with their branches.  Birdcalls and other animal noises fill the air, making this a noisy part of the forest.

Leaves bursting with a light green color grow almost everywhere.  The plants in this forest are crowding other plants out of their spots in order to survive.  The foliage reaches out to snatch the rare and flavorful light that falls though the forest.

The trees in this area are looking highly abused, with huge claw marks embedded deep within them. The claw marks stretch half the width of the ancient trees, and are about a foot deep. Furthermore, the marks are about twenty or thirty feet up.

The forest is so dense in this spot, the sky can barely be seen through the canopy.  A few rays of sunlight sparkling down between the dense trees is all there is to light the area. The trees are also broken and battered, however they are so tall that they reach far above where the beasts that attacked them can reach.
A small mound with a hole in the middle has many tiny black dots moving around it.  The insects are carrying small bits of foliage into their kingdom.  Birds chirp around the area, flying high above.

With its humid atmosphere, the forest gives off an apprehensive feeling.  Up above is a carpet of lush green leaves, absorbing all light possible that shines down to the ground of the forest.  Around the spot are rays of light that burst out of the holes in the jungle covering.

Surrounded by countless huge, dark brown trees looking as ancient as the ground they're coming out of, a strange, but strong aura of power can be felt coming from this area.  A huge pathway is cleared, leading into the forest.  A trail out of the forest has been marked to the east, waiting to take travelers away from this place. In the mud south of the path are massive, three-toed footprints, made by a beast of unimaginable size.

The rainforest reeks with a potent odor that the humidity in the forest camouflages some of, however, it presents a distinct smell.  The leaves of the jurassic forest seem to shine off the filtered light like a mirror.

The village of Kalm is a tiny one, several shingled two story homes clustered together behind a brick wall under a plain blue sky.  The quiet little city bustles with villagers in small spurts, but generally seems to be uninhabited, save its tiny populace.  A blue cobblestoned path leads into the city, towards the town square.  Directly at the town's entrance rests a building with a sign upon it, gently swaying in the wind.

Leading up to the Kalm shops is a large flight of stone steps.  Just a few paces away lies the Town Square, and the monstrosity that is the gloom that encases nearby Midgar. The corruption and polluted stink that is the encased Midgar has not oppressed the small town of Kalm yet, though its tiny visage pales in comparison.  The smell of gunpowder seems a bit stronger here, not overpowering, but slowly making its way down through the town.

Past the shops in the Kalm plaza stands a darker tower, with its four pointed spires, one on each corner.  A black mist seems to pour from somewhere nearby, but slowly dissipates, misting into nothingness.  The cobbles are blue, as are the rest of the towns, and well kept, regardless of being far away from Kalms hustle and bustle of citizens.

rooms.name: A House in Kalm: First Floor

userData.LongDescription: This appears to be one of the many two-story houses in Kalm.  The floor is covered in orange tile.  Cupboards and shelves line one of the walls while a clock hangs from another.  Pipes can be seen running along the ceiling going who knows where.  An ornate dining table is in the middle of the room with a single green chair pulled up.  A staircase leads to the second floor and a door leads out into the streets of Kalm.

Lined against the tall walls that guard Kalm from the outside world is another series of houses, pushed together by a lack of space, constantly confined behind the towering white bricks.  Off in the distance a wide set of stairs leads up to a street along the wall, and another way out of the town, via a tunnel through the wall.  On the walls under the buildings rest a few posters pasted for all to see.

This store seems to be dusty and ill-used.  Behind the counter, in a locked display case, are several shiny glowing stones, giving off a faint magical aura, some potent, and some less so.  The man behind the counter seems to be asleep, but has left a sign to be read.  This building is just like all the others, in regards to set up and colour, with the stairs behind the counter.

A faint trail of oil, gunpowder, and grease is found in the air of this shop.  Weapons of all types are proudly displayed, guns, staves, swords, claws, glaives and more.  However, only a few are in the "For Sale" display case.  The man behind the counter brisky rubs his hands and offers a rather dubious smile.

The vague smell of smoke wafting down from the northern watchtower can be caught on the wind from here, almost the scent of gunpowder.  The stones here are a bit worn and cracked, though this is hardly noticable with their tone of blue.  Several barrels are stacked beside the houses here, in groups of three.

The interior of the item shop is a very clean and well-kept one, with bottles, boxes, and vials neatly put away, though within reach of the customers.  The counter dominates the back of the downstairs, which is otherwise littered with various boxes of stock. Behind it a flight of wooden stairs lead up to another room, which is however off limits to the normal customers. A sign also sits on the counter-top.

At the top of the stairs, the plaza is a bit clear.  A trio of buildings, each with a sign above their door, is here.  One bears a sword of rather large proportions, the other a claw and katana, and the other appears to have a potion bottle upon it.  The buildings are designed the exact same as the remainder of the town, and also seem to be a bit more populated, as adventurers from all over shop to here to begin their quests and crusades.

rooms.name: A House in Kalm: Second Floor

userData.LongDescription: The second floor of the house has an old but well-kept wooden floor.  Two beds sit side by side on a plush pink carpet.  Between the two beds is a night stand with a lamp sitting atop.  Pictures hang on a few of the walls along with shelves that hold an assortment of objects.  A tan colored trunk sits on the ground next to one of the beds.  A staircase leads down to the first floor of the house.

The monotone blue cobblestone leads on the short path, and extends off to the rest of the town, but not before pausing on the strange 'statue' that rests in the center of the town.  A row of houses, closed off and bunched together like dominoes stretches to form a circle of white houses, all nearly identical in size, shape, and proportion.

The interior of this otherwise severe looking building is cozier than its appearance would depict.  Scents of roast duck, ham and other foods waft through the air, and quiet murmuring of the few patrons can be heard somewhere in the back.  A painting hangs on the wall behind the counter, picturing, of all things, the Kalm overland at sunset.  On the counter is a small white sign.

The brightness of this room is surprising, considering how dark the rest of the mansion tends to be. Three windows light this room, revealing an old dirty rug, an even older picture over in the corner, and shelves with all sorts of books and bottles on them. However, what really draws attention is the shining golden chest in the room. There is nowhere to go out of this room but back west.

These caverns under Nibelheim Mansion look artificial, carved out of the rock. However, the bats and guano are completely natural, and the intermittent screeching sounds real enough. Down at the end of the cave you can see a door in the wall, as well as a room that seems to glow a dim green. There is also a way back to the somewhat better lighted pillar room.

The caves continue towards the lighted room, which looks like a lab, or library, although there don't seem to be any bats around. The lab still has a strange green glow, however, which is providing what little light there is around here. Off to the north is a door embedded in the wall. Way back to the east the pillar room's light is just barely visible.

The room is absolutely still. Nothing moves. A window lets in some light, making everything visible. There is a layer of dust on the floor, with footprints dotting it. There is an occasional breath of wind, from an unknown source, but, oddly enough, the dust is not moved at all by it.

This room has quite a few decaying bookcases in the corner. Two stools sit in front of them, and there is a small shelf near the northern door. A lamp hangs off the northern wall, and a picture hangs on the eastern wall, as well as another lamp. The door into the bedroom is east as well.

It is almost too bright to see anything, due to a large window that lets in a lot of sunlight. Two other, smaller windows are set on either side of the large one. They don't bring in nearly as much light, though, due to the curtains that are drawn shut in front of them.

This room is even darker than the rest of this cavern, as it can't get light from the library or outside. There are 5 black coffins in this room, 4 of which contain old skeletons. The fifth one, in the center of the room, is open. There are various skulls and bones stacked along the walls, and a massive pile of them at the back of the room. The entry door is the only exit.

This hallway opens up into a few doors. It appears to have been built somewhat haphazardly. The walls don't quite seem to match up at some points, but are connected by some wood and wallpaper, and somewhat shoddily at that. It is fairly dark, even though a window is not far away.

This hallway has neat piles of books on the floor, and most of the bookshelves are empty. In contrast to the comparative organization of the last room in this library, this is a mess. There looks to be a room filled with even more books at the end of the hall.

This mansion is much larger than it would seem from the outside. The air is stale, and the boards creak and groan with every step. A wind blows through from an unknown source. Dust is everywhere, and visibility is low due to the lack of light. Ghostly noises intrude from all directions.

rooms.name: The Entrance to the East Wing

userData.LongDescription: The stairs leading up from the main room look warped, and this floor doesn't look much better. The wallpaper is peeling, adding to the decrepit look this whole mansion has. To the north is more hallway, lighted only by a grimy window. There is a door to the south leading to a sitting room, and to the west is the somewhat better lighted main room.

A window, set far away, is the only thing that gives any light, and even that light is miniscule due to the size of the room. A piano sits in one corner, while a circular sitting area is in another. A table with a few worn chairs is near the sitting area.

The floor slopes in an upward direction, ending at a door. There seems to be some carpet remains on the floor, but it looks like it has nearly rotted away. The doorway has a door hanging off of it haphazardly, missing two of the three hinges that used to be on it.

Plants of all shapes and size reside in the room, large and well watered. The green-tinted windows are actually clean, and let in plenty of light and heat to keep the foliage growing. The room is not very large, though, and the plants take up almost all of the space.

The hallway wall leans to the right, and a broken board sticks out of the wallpaper. Plaster litters the floor, and every once in a while, more comes falling down from the ceiling. The floor, at least, is in good condition, only slightly worn and not at all broken.

rooms.name: The Other End of the Library

userData.LongDescription: This room's bookcases are neatly filled with books, and the floor is covered in even more of them. A light hangs above the desk here, illuminating the open books on it. The books and the desk make it hard to get around this room, but there are more than enough available bookshelves, and books on them, to sate the knowledge of the curious. The book-filled passage leads back out of this room.

The bottom of this pillar is almost overrun with mold and muck, probably from years of rain. However, the boards are still holding up well despite the bad conditions. The sounds of the bats are even louder here. Walking back up the spiral leads to the passage's entrance, while continuing down leads into a purplish glowing cavern.

This small room has only a few items of furniture sitting around, a carpet on the floor, and a painting on the wall. All of the items, though, are clean, well used, and in nearly perfect condition. The room itself is fairly small, though, which is most likely the reason for so little furniture. For some reason, among all of the neatness in the room, the painting is ajar.

The floor is littered with glass, most of it long ground into powder. The window itself, though, is cracked but whole, the glass probably having been replaced at some time. The wallpaper is peeling away in strips, and falling off in some places. The air is stale and dry, even with the window.

This spiral rampway on the inside of the secret passage isn't in any better shape than the house. You can hear the echoing screeches of bats and the wind outside whistling by. The rampway goes all the way down to the bottom of the pillar, and one could go out of the entrance to this passageway as well.

Books, books, books, this room is filled with books. They sit everywhere, on shelves, and tables, and even some on the floor. A small window lets in a bit of light to help avoid tripping over the books, and probably to allow some light in to read. A large, steel safe sits in one corner, sealed tight.

The light from the window illuminates this area decently well. Unfortunately, it doesn't look any better in the light. The boards here creak under the unfamiliar weight of your presence. There is a doorway off to the east that leads into another well-lit room, while south along the hallway leads towards the main hall again.

The odor of rotten food wafts around, coming from the food long past spoiling and now into the bacterial culture stage. Even the normally non-perishable items seem to have rotted. The food was held in some large refrigerators, which seem to have all broken long ago.

rooms.name: In A Blinding Shaft Of Light.

userData.LongDescription: The huge windows are letting enough light to light up the room, but it is dark enough to look at the windows without being blinded. The windows, from what is visible, appear to be gold wrought, and look very expensive. The gold shows signs of age, and the glass of the windows are filthy.

It seems that there might have been robbers in this room at some time in the recent past, as the room is completely bare, yet there are shapes in the dust that suggest furniture was once on the floor. There are some paintings on the wall still, and a few lonely pieces of furniture stand, too heavy to take.

A broken window lets in a chill, the boards that had kept it closed long broken. Aside from the howling wind coming in from outside, the room is absolutely still. The floor is splintered and broken, making walking treacherous. Dirt shows through where the floor splits.

The ceiling, walls, and floor of this hallway all seem on the verge of simply falling apart. The floor is covered in ceiling plaster, and bits of shredded wallpaper. There are a couple of broken lamps on the wall, hanging halfway to the floor, tarnished and depressing.

It is nearly impossible to see in this hallway, due to the fact that there are no lights, and the nearest window is around the corner. The only light is coming from a door in the western wall, and even that is pale. It is, though, just enough to be able to see that there are no obstacles.

rooms.name: The Top Of A Flight Of Stairs.

userData.LongDescription: The light from the windows makes it tough to see, being so bright. A couple of hallways go both east and west, once twins but now as different as night and day. Yet another flight of stairs, this one smaller than the large spiral staircase, lies in the northern wall.

This bedroom on the second floor has two windows, casting their light on the rug beneath your feet. An oversized bed sits here, perfectly made, if a bit dusty. There is a chair next to the bed, and a bookcase on the far north side of the room with many dusty old books on it. The stone wall next to the pillar seems to open up to a staircase.

A large spiral staircase, still showing some of its former glory, leads to the second floor. A hallway leads to the back part of the mansion, leaning drunkenly to one side. Light pours in from some dirty windows on the second floor, enough to see any obstacles in the path.

This laboratory is an absolute mess, with books all over the floor. There are shelves with test tubes, glass containers, and more scientific implements. Two very large glass tubes sit on the southern side of the room, and a table covered in books and glassware is in the middle of the room. Bookshelves line the entirety of the room, with scores of green and gold books. To the north there is a hallway with more books and bookcases, leading to another room.

This room appears to be a kitchen, with all the cupboards and the stove. Everything in the room appears to be disused and broken, though. Some of the doors of the cupboard are missing, and the jars inside seem to be cracked as a general rule. The stove is a large, old iron one, pitted by rust.

A grandiose view of the clouds can be seen from this vantage point.  The city of Enhasa can be seen on a small island to the east, as well as two domes, both of which contain telepads which send their user down to the barren land below.  One of the aforementioned pads lies here, silently blinking a pattern.  A lake flows gently to the west, but its origin cannot be seen from here.  A series of bridges grant passage over the lake in the same western direction.

The entirety of the colossal floating continent and its three islands are clearly visible from this high point atop the mountain. Below, an endless blanket of fluffy white clouds crisscrossed by a royal blue drift by. The Kingdom of Zeal's many structures can be spotted as well, each of their exteriors are a fine ivory with tastefully set gold detailing. The marvelous city of Kajar lies near the western base of the mountain; neighboring Kajar rests the mighty Blackbird upon its equally impressive dock. Established on the western island is the Sun Palace, with its bulbous apex defining its presence. The eastern island maintains a mysterious pyramidal glass structure, its contents hidden by the sun's reflections. Dwelling upon the lowest of the three islands is the city of Enhasa. Above all Zeal's glorious creations stands Zeal Palace, twin spires reaching prominently toward the heavens.

Water vibrantly flows from a small outlet; its descent is rapid and its termination smooth as it feeds into the bright blue lake below. A small bridge has been constructed, allowing passage across the face of the nearby waterfall. At this mid-point of the mountain path, the mouths of two caves can be reached; one sits adjacent to the waterfall's outlet, the other is more recessed just around a bend in the path to the east.

Everything within this cave is bathed in a pulsating yellow glow. Sectioned rays descend from the ceiling forming a small circumference of light upon an earthen platform, thereby providing the genesis of the invasive glow. Distal to the platform, lush vine-like plants thrive in all directions, as if the rays of light were facilitating their incredible fertility.

Two waterfalls, one dwarfed by the other in flow, steadily feed a nearby lake. Despite the intense bluish hue of the lake's water, sight beyond its surface seems impossible. Overshadowing the scenery is a moderately sized mountain; at its base an archway has been carved allowing passage into a small cave. Far atop the mountain stands an ivory castle, whose spires seem to pierce the heavens.

A large black table remains in sight to the southwest, with its myriad books and magical tabs. A stairway leads up to the north, to the back of this large room. Never blinking, a Nu continues to stare at the bookcase in front of it close to your left.

rooms.name: In Front of a Healing Pad

userData.LongDescription: In the southeastern corner lies a strange, dimmed blue pad, surrounded by more green carpeting. There is a small note by the corner of the pad, apparently explaining what purpose it serves. A mysterious book lies on a desk, with undecipherable lettering on the front cover.  There are two halls here, one leading to the west and one leading to the north. Yet more of the strange wall designs are present on the back wall.

Kajar can now easily be seen not far to the northwest, while all signs of Enhasa have faded from view to the east.  A breathtaking view of the clouds spreads out to the south.  The origin of this area's lake appears to lie some distance to the north.  The end of this bridge is a short distance away, leaving only a beaten path to guide visitors towards Kajar.  The path branches off towards the north leading toward a small cave.

The path affords very little room to navigate, as the mountain rises steeply in a dark crook on one side, while it drops sharply on the other. Despite this precarious location there are no safety nets or guardrails; only luck and coordination will protect those who pass. A small floating island sits some distance to the east, with seemingly no conceivable way of reaching it short of flight. At the center of the island a pyramidal glass structure stands, though its contents are masked by the reflection of the sun's light.

Up close, the sheer number of books on the twin bookcases is staggering. A nu stares at a book on the bookcase, but does nothing to move towards picking it out from its place on the shelf. There's not much room to walk around, seeing as a black table is placed just so that a lane to walk back and forth is barely possible.

A large black table remains in sight to the southeast, with its myriad books and magical tabs. A stairway leads up to the north, to the back of this large room. Never blinking, a Nu continues to stare at the bookcase in front of it. Something far to the southeast flashes a bright blue briefly, much like one of the tabs on the table.

This narrow hallway stretches east to west, with wall designs on both sides. They closely resemble stained glass art, commonly seen in a cathedral. Heading to the west leads back to Kajar's entrance, while heading east leads to the southeastern corner of the city. For such a small city, the amount of art and technology is amazing.

Barely visible over the banister to the north lies a large black table. Stairways to the west and east both lead up towards it.  Designs can be seen on the wall supporting the banister. A way out is easily accessible to the south.

rooms.name: Entrance to Kajar, the City of Magic

userData.LongDescription: A quartet of large stone demons at each corner of the room greet any and all visitors with a baleful and foreboding red-eyed glare.  A small carpet is laid out by the entrance.  A few small purple stools lie to the left, presumably for winded travellers to sit down on.  The floor seems to be made from a brownish rock, smooth to the touch and slightly shiny.  A pair of stairs lie to the north, leading up towards a bookcase.

rooms.name: North of the Entrance to Kajar

userData.LongDescription: A few bookcases are a short distance to the north, possibly part of a small library of sorts. A few books lie open on desks to the west, one of which looks more interesting than the others. A metal globe lies alone in the southeastern corner of the room. Stairways lead to the east and south, while a plush green carpet leads further north.

A window to the north lets in the blinding and warm light of the sun, giving the room a bright glow. This appears to be one of the more vibrant areas, with a few potted plants and flower arrangements by the northern wall. The windows have some designs, similar to the ones seen on walls elsewhere in Kajar. From here, it's possible to get a view of outside Kajar by looking out the window.

The surroundings in here are a little underwhelming, with little to reflect any research in the stars, or for that matter, research in anything. Were it possible to interpret the writing the citizens here use, perhaps insight into what goes on here could be made. A steel globe stands in the middle of the room, flanked on the west and east by tables with books.

The bookcases viewable from the south loom overhead now, their varied choice of books easily apparent. A small hallway to the north leads to the observatory. The back wall shows off yet more of the geometrically styled designs present elsewhere in the city.

This shop is the only one in Kajar, with the shop itself surrounded by a thin strip of green carpet. The variety of items is somewhat varied, concentrating mostly on life restoring ones, but also available are weapons and armor of different kinds. A nu tends the shop, but it appears to be asleep. Yet another mysterious book can be seen here, this one with the picture of a flame inscribed on the cover.  A bookcase lies to the east, as does another part of Kajar, while a staircase leading up to a higher level lies to the west.

Enhasa starts to fade from view to the east around the same time Kajar starts to appear to the west.  The dome housing the telepad which brings visitors to this side of the continent continues to be readily visible to any who care to look for it.  Another bridge lies a short distance to the west, while the lake of unknown origin flows under those who pass across this bridge.

Although narrow at its entrance because of thriving plant life, the cave widens greatly to accommodate a raised stage. At the stage's center a column of yellow light continually forms. In its entirety, the cave could easily be described as a large light bulb made of natural material with a touch of the unknown. A set of stairs has been carved into the anterior of the stage, allowing for greater ease in traversing the stage's elevated position.

A window to the north lets in the blinding and warm light of the sun, giving the room a bright glow, thankfully not reflected due to the dull wood-like floor. This appears to be one of the more vibrant areas, with a few potted plants and flower arrangements by the northern wall. The windows have some designs, similar to the ones seen on walls elsewhere in Kajar.

A large black table spreads out to the east, with a variety of books and strange shimmering blue objects upon it. The floor here changes in design and in material, while the carpet remains the gentle green type present elsewhere in Kajar. A Nu can be seen not far to the north, apparently engrossed in a book from a bookcase in front of it.

Due south of here is what passes as an inn in this advanced town, while its item shop lies to the west. There is little of importance around this area, short of yet more of the smooth, shiny floor and green carpet. Perhaps heading up the northwestern stairs will lead to something of interest.

The item shop can be seen below, with its shopkeeper, a plump blue Nu, seemingly out cold.  A pair of bookcases lie to the east, although no books are visible. There is a stairway to the southeast leading down, while a small hallway to the north leads to a pair of staircases.

Erected at the back of the cave sits a stage; its circumference and height are appropriately scaled in consideration for the small volume of the cave itself, yet still allowing for several adventurers of moderate size to stand on it comfortably. At the center of the stage a pillar of light forms almost constantly; its perimeter is composed of individual pulsating yellow beams whose glow serve as the pillar's cohesion. All about the cave dense florae flourish, narrowing at its entrance but never crowding movement.

A small set of stairs lead up to a man-made platform of solidly packed mud at the cave's rear. Upon this platform, a circular field of light continuously descends from the ceiling, formed by multiple flashing yellow beams. The walls of this small cave seem to be covered with a lush abundance of vine-like plants, which for reasons unknown have failed to grow at all near the beams of light.

A large black table spreads out to the west, with a variety of books and strange shimmering blue objects upon it. The floor here changes in design and in material, while the carpet remains the gentle green type present elsewhere in Kajar. A Nu can be seen not far to the north, apparently engrossed in a book from a bookcase in front of it.

A window to the north lets in the blinding and warm light of the sun, giving the room a bright glow. One of the more vibrant areas, there are potted plants and flowers flanking the window, which has designs similar to ones seen elsewhere in Kajar. A black table, a centerpiece to this large room, lies to the south, with its varied books and glimmering tabs.

This corner of the city is relatively quiet and free of activity.  A pair of bookcases lie upon the back wall, stacked full of books.  A stairway lies a short distance to the west, as does a hallway which leads north, further into Kajar.  Close by the northeastern corner of the ceiling, some strange glimmer can be seen.

Kajar lies directly to the north, its splendor easily viewable by all who approach and visit it.  The design behind its buildings is similar to that of Enhasa, but not enough so as to make them indistinguishable.  From here, it can be seen that the source of the river along this side of the continent lies in a pool, high on a mountain to the northeast.  The path back towards the dome leading downwards lies back to the southeast, while the view of the clouds continues uninterrupted.  A trail leads eastward, out of the view of the guards to the southeast.

A huge wall towers over the western edge of the Armor shop.  The shop itself has half of its roof covered with what appears to be earth, while the other is covered in the more typical tiles.  To the east is a small ledge which gives a good view of the city.

Grass grows in abundance in this corner of the clearing.  The small canal that flows through here has some slight spill-out in the area, thus causing a great deal of plants to grow here.  Off to the corner a few windows are placed until they can be put into the buildings that require them.

Recent fires have reduced the once proud city of Maranda to almost complete ruin.  Upon a brief estimate only three or four of the buildings that once filled the city are usable now.  To the north stands the inn, blackened and burnt, but still serviceable.

The entirety of the Armor Shop is located within this small room.  The only things of interest here, aside from the shopkeeper looking at you expectantly, are a number of crates scattered along the floor, and a vase of roses sitting on the counter.  There is also a small sign here.

The outside of the Weapon Shop was largely destroyed by the fire.  Large, gaping holes poke through its walls like a sponge, and the shopkeeper smiles widely at you from the inside when he catches your glance.  To the east and south is a small clearing with a few citizens beginning on some repairs to the city.  Further east is a small house.

An even more impressive display of flowers are spread about inside the house than on the outside.  Numerous baskets of flowers are virtually everywhere: on the suit of armor in the main hallway, surrounding the bed, and circling the desk.  One particularly large basket lies at the corner of the bed.  A small letter lies opened on the desk.

The eastern side of the landing is covered completely with grass and the occasional small flower.  A few citizens are here having a picnic and generally throwing their cares to the wind, at least for a few hours...  The walkway lies to the west.
