This corner of the clearing overlooks a small platform built down a set of stairs to the northeast.  The platform looks out over the inlet from the canal, and a small rowboat is docked there. To the north and west the clearing continues.

A single tree stands to the west of the walkway in this corner of the landing.  A few birds chirp nosily, and some squirrels can be seen running around searching for acorns.  Very few marks can be seen here regarding the recent fire which devastated the rest of the city.

The Weapon Shop is in a large house, decorated with many of the shopkeeper's trophies from his old adventuring days.  A staircase leads to the upper floor, but it is behind the counter and is largely unaccessible.  A large record player sits behind the counter playing a rousing musical number geared to inspire those who enter the store.

A large stairway dominates the otherwise plain features at this end of the landing.  Another tree stands here, with a lone pigeon perched in it cooing softly to herself.  To the south lies a small stairway leading to the inn, and going up the stairs lands one at the entrance to the Armor Shop.

At the northeastern section of the clearing a group of citizens are reconstructing what appears to be a roof.  A few of them glance upwards at you, but most just ignore you and continue working away.  The clearing continues on to the south, and a small house lies directly to the east.

This platform overlooks a large inlet accustomed to seeing large frigates sail in with good from around the world.  It looks like it hasn't seen an outside ship in quite some time however from the disrepair the docks are in.  A small rowboat is tied here.

A small house, largely unravaged by the recent fires stands here.  Around the house, arranged almost in a design of some sort, are dozens of flower baskets.  No sign adorns the house, but the door is open.  A flight of stairs leads down to a platform overlooking the inlet.

The exterior of the inn is in sad shape.  Burnt walls are crumbling down, revealing small parts of its less than stellar interior.  One particularly large hole gapes above the right-hand window, which creates a draft on the inside.  To the south is the city's entrance, and a flight of stairs lead to a landing.

At the bottom of the staircase is a small grass landing.  A few citizens walk around aimlessly enjoying what little beauty remains of their city. Two trees line either side of a small walkway to the north.  At the end of the walkway to the north lies another staircase leading to another level near the Armor Shop.

A large staircase leads down towards the weapons shop.  To the east of that, past a small clearing, stands a small house largely untouched by the recent fires.  Directly north is a small alleyway with a broken statue of an old woman seemingly staring calmly.  To the south is a ledge with an excellent view of the city.

A small, but well-lit, alleyway extends off from the staircase to the south.  Leaning against a wall is a ruined stone statue of an old woman, broken on one side.  A wonderful view of the ocean can be seen from here, but aside from that, there is not much else of interest here.

The Grand Maranda Inn was once a place of absolute splendor.  The recent fires, however, have reduced its once glorious decor to mere rubble.  Holes poke through to the outside causing quite a draft, and the smell of smoke permeates everything in the room.  A small alcove here has a small dinner table for the guests to eat at, and a few of the locals still come here to chat.

The ledge provides an excellent view of the city.  To the south lies the city's inn and entrance.  Down the flight of stairs to the north places one at the entrance to the Weapons Shop, and east of that, past a small clearing, stands a small house.

This is the rebel headquarters in Northtown, a valiant little group plotting the downfall of the corrupt Empire. The headquarters itself is small, still a part of the seafood restaurant. A row of tables has been placed in the center of the room, with a large map on it. Stairs are on the north and southern side of the room.

A large building rests against this corner of the city, composing of the upper platform walls and the forest barriers on the east side. The label of an item bag is placed next to its doors, and through the windows, armor and items are placed in a display stand. Roads lead to the west and south, to different sections of the city.

This junction looks to be one of the most important in Northtown, leading three directions, all to important places. The street to the north leads further onto the drawbridge of the Emperor's Castle. East leads to a platform with a good sight of the city below, and to the south is a set of stairs leading to the lower portion of the city. Nearby is a large white building with the Inn symbol on it. There's another building close by that looks like a clinic of sorts.

This is a charming little cafe and restaurant with a bit of a seaside theme to it. The blue walls and floors and all-seafood menu are a definite plus, and the sweet aroma of baked fish lingers around the air. To the north is a set of stairs, leading to the second floor.

This is a fairly simple house in Northtown, lavish decorations and expensive furniture abound. The owners of this house must be at least fairly rich, as noted by the location and contents of the building. The windows on the north wall provide a clear view of the Emperor's Castle.

rooms.name: In front of the Northtown Ruins

userData.LongDescription: The eerie courtyard is cut off from the rest of the city by high, pointed walls.  Scattered candles add to the mysterious atmosphere, and a horrible stench fills the air.  Statues of mythical, horned beasts have been placed in columns, and the central column leads from the southern gate to northern stairs that head into the ruins.

This is a fairly silent edge of town, surrounded by trees all over, with the forest edge to the south. The paved path seems to loop around the trees to the north and east, leading closer to the more active part of town. A few benches are placed about, creating the image and feeling of a quiet park more than anything else.

This store is brilliantly decorated, with signs and posters of all sort around. On the racks are weapons and armor of all kinds, foreign and local. The walls contain shelves which house the hottest, latest items of gossip. Medicine cupboards are placed behind the clerk's counter. This store, though nameless, truly has a lot of odds and ends.

The sea-themed cafe includes a second floor with a gorgeous large window for the customer's viewing pleasure, with a nice sight of the Angel's Headstone park. A door marked 'stock room' is on the northern wall, but it seems to be locked. There are stairs on both ends of the room.

This room is filled with a medical scent, typical of a doctor. A small receptionist area is near the entrance, with a bed and an array of medical tools on the other side of the room. A large cupboard hangs against the wall, filled with medicinal supplies and the sort. A few potted plants are around, lavishly decorating the room.

This is the highest street in Northtown, geographically, providing a nice view of the city below. In particular, buildings with white walls and red roofs can be seen amidst cobblestone roads. Large oak trees are planted about and out of the city perimeter, creating a nurturing feel of nature all around.

This fine inn is one of the leading lodging establishments in Northtown. A sleek black marble counter is near the entrance, with a clerk keeping tally of customers booking in and out of the inn. Past a decorated doorway is a long row of beds to sleep on, with dividers and curtains for privacy.

The sun flares brightly upon the aptly called Northtown, the northernmost city in the Empire. Cobblestone roads stretch out in different directions, leading to different parts of the city. A triple-pronged series of roads lead out to the north, south and east. The Empire's large castle lies to the north, and to the east is a long road leading to some big ancient ruins off in the horizon. South leads to a set of stairs trailing down to the lower portion of town.

Probably the highest highlight of this junction is the large two-story cafe nearby, with attractive designs and a standing blackboard sign listing today's menu. A small fountain is placed in the center of the cobblestone path, looking beautiful. To the north is a set of stairs, while other roads to the east and south lead to different sections of town.

This little corner of town is what the citizens of Northtown call the 'Angel's Headstone' park, because of a large beautiful monumental fountain depicting the statue of a fallen angel who questioned God's love and was banished in a coffin of ice. Benches are placed around the fountain, with cobblestone paths stretching out to the north and west. Large oak trees are planted all around, giving the park a nice shade.

This is a typical one-room citizen house in Northtown. Two beds are against the corner, with a nightstand in between them. Curtained windows are against the northern wall. A few miscellaneous pieces of furniture such as a table set and a sofa are against the walls of the house. A small kitchen is on the corner of the house.

The road of cobblestones takes three different turns from this junction, leading west, south and east. West leads to another T-shaped junction with the Emperor's castle nearby. South leads to the southern part of the top layer of town. The passage east leads further away from town to the ancient ruins.

rooms.name: An eastward-winding path to the Northtown Ruins

userData.LongDescription: Unlike the rest of the streets in Northtown, this long and winding pathway is conspicuously devoid of citizens.  The elevated cobblestone walkway leads only in two directions, and a quick glance along the street reveals why it is never used.  A dark, decaying ruin sits to the north, formidably surrounded by a hazy grey cloud.  To the west lies the central commercial area of the city, bustling with activity as usual.

The eastern wing ends in a large room. The walls rise up to a high ceiling, but no adornments cover the cold stone walls or the floor. The only objects of any note within the room are two chests, which have long since have had their contents removed.

Cold stone comprises the entirety of this stairwell. The floor tiles echo with every step, the stone walls reverberating each sound so effectively that one would be hard pressed to pass through this way without drawing attention. A draft blows through the room, drawing the stale air out from the cells below.

The stone walls of the prison open into this circular room. A narrow passage to the north leads into the deeper portions of the prison, while a small ledge on the east end of the room leads towards the upper levels of the castle. An ornate tile is embedded in the floor in the center of the room.

The predominant feature of this room is a large hole in the floor with a short platform extending to its center. It looks to have been used to send unfortunate prisoners to their doom, as the bottom of the pit cannot be seen. Gargoyles watch over the pit menacingly, as if standing sentinel over what lies below. Several switches can be seen on the floor, though they appear to have been rusted with age and no longer function.

The bottom of the pit is bound into the shape of a heart. The walls around the edge of the room are designed to prevent prisoners from attempting to climb their way out. Two gargoyles are on the north wall of the room. A pool of water surrounds the south edge of the room, forming a barrier at the edge of the floor. A patterned tile is at the edge of the water.

The eastern wing curves around in a stairwell. On the north wall, a pair of fearsome gargoyles stare down at passers-by. The deep blue carpet covers the floor, muffling footsteps of anyone going through the hallway. The path to the south leads further into the eastern wing, and the stairs lead to the grand stairway.

This landing connects to the eastern wing of the castle. A large wall with a gargoyle looming above divides the landing from the central level of the castle. To the south are a narrow flight of stairs that lead towards the entryway of the castle.

The third floor curves around a drab brick wall, heading off to the north and the west. The carpet, present in other parts of this level, is nowhere to be seen, causing footsteps to echo loudly. The inner wall forming this corner has two arched insets, though nothing rests on either of them except for a thin layer of dust.

The narrow passage to the south connects the hallway entrance to the quarters. Several beds are spread throughout the room, immaculately made and evidently untouched for a long time. A small wall jutting out breaks the quarters up into a western and eastern section.

Ornate blue carpeting runs down the center of the room, covering most of the stone tile floor. A pair of steps to the north ever so slightly elevates the area. Walls on either side of the steps mark passages to the east and west, spreading further out into the third floor of the castle.

The passageway snakes around from the entrance off to the south. The north has an opening that leads out of the prison area. A small landing in the northwest corner looks over the rest of the room.  Several pots on the floor line the narrow passage to the south, leading further into the prison.

The pathway curves around at the south end of the room, leading to an elevated platform. The pathway divides the platform in two, but not so much that it cannot be crossed. A small yellow orb-like spring sits at the edge of the platform, which could provide enough jumping power to cross the divide.

rooms.name: A bend in the eastern wing

userData.LongDescription: The eastern wing bends around in a twisting fashion. The deep blue carpet here runs down the path, keeping any footsteps from echoing off of the stone walls. The narrow corridor to the north leads out towards the grand stairway, while the stairs lead further into the east wing.

A hallway opens on both the north and south sides of the room. Near the middle of the hall, the walls narrow, constricting the ability to pass through the area to a single file line. The door on the north end leads further into the eastern wing, while the door on the south end leads outside to a landing.

The southwest corner of the third floor turns into a dead end. Two pillars stand on either side of the path to the north back into the third floor. A small engraved tile is set on the east side of the floor, though it no longer appears to have any function.

The high walls around the landing keep a strong breeze continually blowing. A complex and ornate archway surrounds a gate that leads into the inner castle. Two gargoyles stand on either side of the top of the arch. A narrow path on the west side of the archway leads to a door that leads back into the outer portion of the castle.

The hallway splits into two distinct paths. The wall on the north side has several arched insets, each decorated with ornate buntings and lit with a sconce set in the center. The hardwood floor here creaks with age under each step, though they are well maintained.

A small stairwell behind the Great Hall connects to the higher levels of the castle. Directly opposite the door into the Great Hall is a nook on the northern wall. The blue carpet runs throughout the area, with ornate patterns near the western side of the room. A flight of stairs on the west side lead further up into the castle.

An enormous table dominates the presence of the room, clearly designed to impress guests at state banquets. The table has ornate candelabra set up between each place setting, causing shadows to flicker to and fro. It extends to the north end of the room, which ends with imperial banners hanging on the wall.

A flight of stairs leads up to a landing, which splits into two further stairways. Banners of the Empire drape either side of the first stairway, which has ornate railings on either side. The stylish blue carpet here muffles footsteps, despite its obvious wear from age.

The northeast corner turns around the interior wall. Without the carpet that is common throughout the castle, the stone tiles echo with footsteps. At the west end, an engraved tile sits in the middle of the floor.

This small landing leads towards the western wing of the castle. The walls tower skyward, dwarfing the door to the north. Underfoot the stone flooring has been worn by time, and any design has been long lost. To the south are the stairs back towards the entrance to the palace.

The northwest corner of the third floor bends around from the main hall to the south. An arched inset on the north wall looks to have once held some sort of ornamentation, though now sits empty. A switch rests on the west side of the north wall, though it no longer appears to function.

The hallway ends to the north at the double door entrance to the throne room. Deep blue carpet runs along the path from the entrance south to the northern end. The path to the south, which runs between two stone gargoyles, has ornate engraved tiles dividing the hallway in half.

The hallway, which curves north, is ended abruptly by an unfortunately placed credenza. The bunting continues on from the rest of the hallway, and though the pathway is much narrower, it seems as though it was originally intended for actual passage.

The throne room has a large elaborate carpet running down the center, more ornate than the rest of the carpeting in the castle. Freestanding pillars on either side create a hallway right up to the throne. At the north side of the room, the throne resides on an elevated platform, and a small door leads out to the roof.

The west side of the quarters has a number of pristine beds spread throughout. The wall juts out slightly, dividing the room from the eastern part of the quarters. On the west end of the room are a flight of stairs that lead to the highest parts of the castle.

A small pit splits this room into two forks at the north wall. Footsteps echo throughout the dungeon, though there seems to be no discernable source. A ledge to the west side of the room gives a view to the rest of this level of the dungeon. The southern passage leads back out of the dead end.

The entrance to the inner part of the castle has many tables on either side of the hallway. A podium atop a small flight of stairs at the far north end of the room is clearly designed for speakers to hold the attention of everyone in the room. A small door on the north wall leads further into the castle.

rooms.name: A bend in the western wing

userData.LongDescription: The western wing curves to the south towards a door leading to the upper levels of the castle. The stone floors echo with footsteps, though the source of the sound is not clearly discernable. On the southern wall, a door leads out to the second floor landing of the castle.

A narrow corridor leading towards stairs that lead out of the castle dungeon, this room is designed to prevent many people from leaving all at once. To the west is a large hole that was once used as a trap door, as well as the cell that was used to hold prisoners.

The hallway that connects the grand stairway to the west wing twists around. Two menacing gargoyles reside within the northern wall. The path bends off to the south, leading to the further parts of the west wing and deeper parts of the castle.

The gigantic castle looms ominously above the town. Two stone gargoyles sit next to the castle doors, appearing to be an extension of the castle itself. The grass sways gently in the wind here, and the path splits off towards stairs on either side. The bridge to the south leads back towards town.

This small stairwell leads downward into the basement of the castle. The area is cramped, feeling as though it was designed as a means of restricting access to the lower levels. The walls seem faded and worn from continued use, as does the rest of the room. Stairs lead further down, while a door leads outside.

The room here has dark stains on the walls and floor from the blood of prisoners of the Empire. There is little room to move around, and shackles on the walls indicate that those who occupied this cell before would have had even less freedom. To the south, an ominous pit awaits those kept here against their will.

Wind blows sharply across the roof of the castle, buffeting anyone who stands here. The roof extends off widely to the east and west, though runs narrowly along that path. Tall pillars rise far above the castle, casting a long shadow over the area.

Apart from the breathtaking view of the town, there's a lot to see here. The eastern part of the monument is dedicated to one of Da-Chao's followers, a stern looking person about two thirds his size. He wears an ornament on his chest which is very similar to the one on Da-Chao's hat. His loosely fitting robes are open at the front. Looking closer, his mouth seems to be twisted in an angry frown, his teeth look almost as if he were constantly gritting them. There's not much to do here but return to the main path to the west.

rooms.name: Entrance of the Da-Chao fire cave

userData.LongDescription: Entering the fire cave the damp and hot air is noticable. Even with the roaring fires extinguished it is still hotter inside than outside in the sun. The cave turns to the northeast leading into a larger cavern. It is hard to breathe here. The walls don't seem to have been worked on any, it seems this cave is a natural one.

rooms.name: At the foot of the Da-Chao monument

userData.LongDescription: Leaving Wutai behind you're standing at the foot of the Da-Chao monument. The mountains behind Wutai have been used by the locals to create a truly breathtaking work of art to honor the water god Da-Chao. Several huge stone statues have been carved into the sand rock. Looking up, the rope spanning the central figure's belly is prominently visible. Its two pairs of arms are still far above. The path gently rises up to the east.

Beside Da-Chao's head a path leads along his upper left arm ending in the palm of his hand to the east. Some manacles are still dangling in his face. This is the place where the dastardly Don Corneo tried to make a choice between Yuffie the ninja girl and Elena of the Turks which he had chained to Da-Chao's eyes whom to use as his lady for a night. He regretted kidnapping the two when Reno and Rude made him fall to his death. Near the mountain's summit the path leads around the massive head.

The mountain summit offers a great view all around. Beyond the mountains there's a carpet of lush forests which nearly reach up to the horizon. On the other side the small town of Wutai lies peacefully, its inhabitants looking like tiny ants from this height. A slight breeze is blowing over the mountain while the shadows of some clouds brush over it.

The cave turns from the south to the east here leaving the hotter tunnels to the south behind. To the east the tunnel leads through a larger cavern before turning back to the south in the distance. It's a bit darker to the east without the glowing lava to illuminate the area.

Passing Da-Chao's head with his priestly hat, the path leads around it descending over his right shoulder to the west. The fire cave is close but cannot be reached except by going around the chasm between the statues and then climbing up a bit. This is nearly the highest point of the mountain except for the hand of another statue which seems to be mischieviously showing the 'V' sign behind Da-chao's head. But regarding this is a spiritual monument, it is sure to have a deeper philosophical meaning.

The cave opens up in a T-crossing here. To the east the source of most of the illumination in this cave is visible. Mostly cooled down lava still has some hot and glowing embers lying around. It seems one of the great fires in this cave burned there before it was extinguished using the Leviathan Scales. To the north the cave leads around a bend deeper into the mountain.

To the west, Da-Chao's girdle which is tied around his waist can be seen. A little futher up the mountain trail branches so it is possible to either take a tour directly upwards around Da-Chao's head or circle around his large belly. The lower left arm of Da-Chao is close to the path, but no trail leads up to it.

The tunnel twists and turns reaching the last caverns of the fire cave. A long passage leads southwards towards the biggest cave in the whole system. The telltale glow of nearly extinguished lava can be seen to the south. The Da-Chao fire cave ends to the south.

The cave takes another turn and passes by an old metal chest which lies opened and abandoned at the wall. Following the path further it seems both illumination and heat are increasing by the minute. It seems old lava paths are still running under the caves, just the roaring fires which used to rage here were extinguished long ago.

The path ends at a dead-end. Looking at the embers and glowing rock and judging by the heat it might still be dangerous to touch the walls even though the fires were extinguished. Examining the rock, a fire wall must have blocked the north/south path to the west.

The cave widens here forming a natural cavern. The air is still hot and humid making breating difficult. The light shining in from the entrance can still be seen shining through the entrance to the southwest. The only other source of illumination is the faint glow which parts of the wall emit. Streams of lava have long since cooled down and hardened into slabs of stone though.

The path leads along the mountainside twisting a few times finally coming to an end on Da-Chao's lower right hand. From here visitors can watch the statue of a flame-haired warrior best. He's the only figure in the mountainside actually wearing armor. The hairstyle and fierce expression nearly makes him look like a demon. Him standing to Da-Chao's right side indicates him being an ally of the water god though.

The tunnels open up here into a wide open room. Bats fly around here which have been roused by the noise of the footsteps echoing through the caves. The air is a little cooler here not being that close to the lava fields. To the east the cave bends to the south as the tunnel takes a turn to the right.

rooms.name: Entrance of the Da-Chao fire cave

userData.LongDescription: Close to the statue of the demon-like warrior there's the cave entrance of another of Wutai's attractions, the infamous fire cave. The large cavern in which fires roared until a group of adventurers extinguished them using the Leviathan Scales can now be visited without additional protection. A path leads upwards past the cave to the highest point, the hand behind Da-Chao's  head. Going downwards, the trail reaches the upper right hand of the water god from which Don Corneo fell to his death long ago.

The path turns around here, leading further up to the west. This trail is just below the statue of one of Da-Chao's followers, a strict looking man holding up a hand in greeting or warning. One of Da-Chao's hands is directly above. Some activity is noticeable up there, shadows of moving figures are dancing over the rock surface.

The dusty path leads around Da-Chao's belly. Wutai is already far below, the roofs of its pagodas glitter in the sunlight. The main Da-Chao statue which reaches from the top to nearly the foot of the mountain in height is truly an amazing display of human craftsmanship. To the west the path leads towards Da-Chao's lower right arm. Climbing upwards it is possible to wander around the head, upper arms and also visit the Da-Chao fire cave which lies behind the huge central statue in the upper regions of the mountains.

The path leads up the mountain slowly. The sun is shining brightly letting the shadow of one of Da-Chao's huge hands fall down on the rocks. It grows noticably hotter after reaching an altitude higher than nearly all of  Wutai's buildings, except for the Pagoda of the Five Gods of course.  Looking upwards two statues of other followers of Da-Chao can be seen which are nearly hidden by his massive figure.

The last cave is well worth visiting, being one of the last of the few fire caves inside the tunnel system. An empty treasure chest which has been forced open lies in a corner, the rocks are charred and the walls have molten into slabs of rock. Most of the lava is cold by now, but there are still some very hot parts which shouldn't be touched.

This hand is directly under Da-Chao's face. It is big enough for several people to gather and enjoy the view. From this hand the entire town is visible, including the towering pagoda, Godo's Mansion and the Turtle's Paradise. Da-Chao's meditative face is above and seems to watch with a benign expression.

This bridge is incredibly slick, with some ice formations like none ever seen before.  Just before the bridge, there is a sign with some sort of writing on it, and what appears to be a little doll standing next to the sign.  The ice is cracked and worn, and looks very unstable.  The noises can now be heard much louder, almost as if something horrific is just ahead.

The air has cooled down a great amount due to the rise in elevation and increased wind activity.  The ground is very dense and covered in a very thick layer of snow, making each step quite an exhausting process.   The ladder extends further up, closing in on the peak of the mountain.  The fog appears to have settled in again, making things much harder to see, and making navigation harder.

The bridge narrows down to barely enough space to stand on both feet.  The slushy winds are strong enough to knock and unsuspecting person off of the narrow walkway to a fall of certain doom.  The view from here is very limited due to the foggy strong winds carrying an abundance of snowflakes around.  Far down below, the entrance path to this horrid mountain can be seen just before it disappears into the mass of fog.

The ground is covered in a thick layer of ice, making it very slippery.  The wind blows fiercely in a southeastern direction, with enough force to knock an uncautious traveler off the bridge to certain death.  The ground below is not visible through the dense fog.

The steep path leads down a little bit more, then it disappears to the west. The Krakkers continue sliding down the slope, which leads to the bottom of the path.  The Krakkers then scramble onto other parts of the mountain, slowly invading each crack and crevice of it.  The roars of some monstrous creature are very loud, and come from what appears to be the peak of the mountain.

The hollowed out cave provides a nice shelter from the harsh outer environment.  An opening to the south provides an exit to a platform overlooking the snowy meadow area.  The puddles continue streaming south through the exit and back into the snow where it freezes into ice, making the ground slick and hard to walk on.  The layer of ice slowly thickens as more water drains down and freezes.

Soft white snowflakes drift throughout the air, eventually falling down to the ground.  The soft white snow glimmers in the faint daylight, illuminating the area with an iridescent glow.  The cave is visible to the west, carved out of the side of the mountain.

The jagged spikes protruding from the walls and the light snowfall produce quite an extraordinary environment.  The pathway is encompassed by these walls, creating a harsh atmosphere. The dense fog layer lowers visibility in all directions, and makes travel difficult.

The bottom of the slope has leveled out, and the path turns to the west.  The steep dropoff at the end of the cliff looks perilous, but still the Krakkers hop off of the cliff.  The sharp protruding rocks and the extremely long fall are quite a damaging combination.  To the west, there is a small open area.  Up above, one can see that the peak is not too far away.

rooms.name: The top of a steep slope

userData.LongDescription: The mountain itself appears to block much of the wind, making it somewhat clear.  The path slopes downward at a steep angle, stopping a few hundred feet to the south.  It is quite apparent what the hole in the wall is now.  Thousands of little Krakkers stream out of this hole to infest the mountain like a group of parasites.

The beam of light traveling through the hole in the wall creates an amiable source of light.  A snowy bridge can be seen through the hole, leading off to the east.  The atmosphere outside looks relatively placid.  The loose gravel on the ground makes each step difficult.

The pure white snow slowly gains in elevation as the steady fall of snowflakes continues.  The sunlight reflects off of the snow, brightening the surrounding area.  To the west, some sort of sign can be seen, as well as a large bridge connecting two parts of the mountain.  Very small footprints lead to the west, slowly eroding away as the fresh snowfall covers up the tracks.

This area is a small open space, the northern side of which has a ladder heading up the side of a cliff.  There are some markings in the snow, it looks like something was sliding around on the ground not too long ago.  They appear to lead over to the ladder.  The thick snowy layer, freshly fallen, is ideal for tracking these creatures, whatever they may be.

The path circles around near the top of the mountain, the northern way leading straight up to the peak.  As the path gets higher and higher, a massive presence can be seen far to the northeast.  Long protruding spikes and an overall hideous form can be seen wandering alongside the upper cliffs of the mountain.  It must be guarding something very precious if such a massive beast was sent to be the protector of this mountain.

The insides of the cave are extremely barren, just dirt floors and a wall.  To the east, there is some sort of giant crevice, and then the cave continues far over to the other wall.  The only visible source of light is from a hole in the northern wall, with a clear blue sky on the other side.  This hole could serve as an alternate exit to the cave.

rooms.name: The eastern end of the bridge

userData.LongDescription: At this end of the bridge, there is an entrance to another cave.  The narrowed path towards it looks as if it could barely support any weight.  The snow melts at the entrance to the cave, exposing a rocky dirt floor.  Sharp jagged rocks and long icicles line the walls of the mountain.

Upon further inspection, the cave appears to be a massive canyon in the mountain, formed out of rock.  The snow leads into the cave, where it drifts off into an area of blackness.  The cave's entrance is made of solid rock with icicles drooping from the edges, barely wide enough for one to squeeze through without being pierced by the razor sharp icicle points.

The bridge has connected to a large open plot of land, covered in a layer of immaculate snow.  The ground is a pristine white color, obviously untouched for a long period of time.  Nearby to the west, a small hole can be seen in the mountain side, not nearly large enough for any human to fit through. Occasionally, some sort of small blob can be seen drifting out of it and sliding down the mountain.

The land is flat and open, covered in a thick layer of freshly fallen snow.  To the far northwest, a ladder can be seen leading up to yet another level of the mountain.  Far up at the peak of the mountain, occasionally some sort of vicious looking spikes can be seen barely poking over the edge of the cliff, but then disappear back beyond visibility.

This platform provides a beautiful overlook of the giant snowy meadow. One can get a great view of the lower parts of the mountain, as well as the upper parts.  The sparkling object can be better seen from here, as it glimmers and floats above the white snowy layer, and it reflects off of the icy covering of the rocks and snow.

The hovering bunch of sparkles turns out to be a save point.  Upon arriving in the meadow, snowflakes float through the air, gleaming in the light as they flutter around.  Beyond the meadow, to the north, there is a hole in the wall leading to some sort of canyon inside the mountain.  Some tracks can again be seen here, leading to the north.

The hazy fog and heavier snowfall make walking a strenuous task.  The enormous icicles hanging off the cliffs and the stench of death amidst the air is sure to impose upon any traveler.  The only visible thing is a ladder off in the distance.  The snow on the ground is very soft, obviously untraveled for a long period of time.  A strong gust of wind could easily knock someone off course and to a perilous fall of certain doom.

rooms.name: At the peak of the bridge

userData.LongDescription: The view from the top of the bridge is both extraordinary and frightening.  A cave can clearly be seen to the east.  A small cyclone of snowflakes swerves its way around the bridge, pacing back and forth between the two ends.  The cave serves as a shelter from the snow.  The ground inside the cave is a rocky dirt floor.

The damp and dark climate, combined with the terrors from within the mountain, produce quite a peculiar environment.  The small water streams on the walls, and the puddles from dripping icicles flow down to the other end of the cave. Near the southern end of the cave, there is an exit back to the outer parts of a mountain.

rooms.name: The far end of the canyon

userData.LongDescription: The northern part of this passage is rather dull, except for the small hole in the wall. The hole appears to be just barely wide enough for a person to fit through.  The ground is covered in mud, making it difficult to travel across.  The hole provides just enough light so the bumps and rocks sticking out of the floor don't trip an unsuspecting traveler.

The fluffy white snow covering the rocky bridge is quite an exquisite sight.  The bridge is merely an extension of the mountain, and the icicles drip down far below the bridge base.  The bridge continues farther to the east, where it rejoins with the mountain, at another cave entrance.  The bridge is in a stairstep type pattern, peaking at the middle of the bridge.

This walkway is barely wide enough for someone to venture across.  There are razor sharp walls on one side and a perilous fall on the other side of the walkway.  To the far east, a huge meadow area is visible, but the journey there looks far from easy.  The loose snow on top of the ground makes walking very unsteady.

rooms.name: Along a windy snow covered path

userData.LongDescription: The path here is covered in slick ice, making travel difficult. Snowballs gradually fall down the mountain, growing constantly as the loose snow clings to its outer layer.  The rich white color of the snow very diligently illuminates the area, adding to the overall experience of the mountain.

Small pieces of ice pound down onto the ground, then tumble down the slope of the path.  The peak is not far to the northeast, and the massive guardian beast grows nearer.  The path has created a circle pattern, spiraling around the top portion of the mountain.

The path continues its circular pattern, with the northern way leading up to the peak of the mountain.  Strong wind storms and mini cyclones of snowflakes make travel quite an exhaustive process.  The beast ahead still seems to be roaming around the mountain, alert and ready to defend against any intruders.  The peak appears to disappear up into a high cloud, making it hard for one to decipher what lies past all of this.

The last cliff of the mountain is nearby to the east, where the massive beast protecting the mountain roams around.  The snow rains down like a blizzard, pelting the ground with each and every little ball of snow.  The peak of the mountain is not visible through the cloud cover.

The pathways here are slick and icy, creating a very slippery walkway. The cliff continues further on to the east. The hanging icicles creak and crack, as if they were going to fall.  Any misplaced step could possibly lead to a fall to the death.  There is a ladder visible to the southeast. The steep and narrow cliffs are quite a disturbing sight.

Massive rock formations tower above on either side of the passage. On the wall to the north, erosion has created a small hole.  The roughly surfaced walls protrude into the canyon area, making the pathway barely large enough for a person to travel through without serious injury.  The narrow passage continues leading to the north, where it is nearly pitch black other than the small hole in the wall.

rooms.name: On top of a snowy cliff

userData.LongDescription: This is the very last cliff of the mountain, where the massive guardian roams around the open space. The air is thin and the wind is strong, making each and every step an exhaustive process.  The peak above is unreachable, due to the fact there is no path or ladder leading to it.  Perhaps there is another way to get up there.

The snowy path has split into different directions.  The eastern way heads to a large, open meadow area blanketed in snow, the northern way leads to some sort of cave, and the western way leads to the beginning of the mountain.  The ground is covered in a thick layer of ice.  A rumbling noise can be heard from inside the cave, creating attention towards it, but also there is a small sparkling object floating around to the southeast.

From this location, both the peak and the base of the mountain can be seen. The fog rolling off the mountain exposes even more of the mountainside than could be seen before.  Occasionally, an icicle will fall and tumble down the mountain, shattering into a thousand pieces as it impacts with a massive rock formation from the mountain.

A massive cave entrance stands before you, but its insides are pitch black.  The only obvious way to see inside is to venture in.  The howling from within the cave may just be the wind, or it may be some other force.  The snow appears to have melted at the entrance to the cave, exposing the rocky dirt floor.

This family was thinking about moving out once but they must have decided against it. Old boxes are crushed and thrown into a corner of the room; apparently there's no need for them anymore. Also discarded are some heavy suitcases; they're also laying in a corner of the room, unused. A lovely chandelier has been hung from the ceiling, making the whole house seem much brighter. A wood-burning stove provides all the warmth in here, and some much needed light to boot.

Loud, boisterous cheering and singing can be heard outside the inn; it's apparently become quite a popular spot for the townfolk since the world was saved. The inn itself is a pretty large building, measuring about twice the size of the largest residential house in town. It's also a two stories, which is also notable when only one other house has this feature. A merry glow illuminates the windows of the inn, making it seem that much more welcome to a weary traveller.

rooms.name: Icicle Inn - Along the Northern Path

userData.LongDescription: Here the path begins to take a northerly turn and head towards the town's popular snowboarding spot. This path also appears to have seen the most use out of any path in the entire town; this section of it is a bit lower than any of the other paths around. The evergreen tree that sits in the center of town is now off to the south. A child's sled is off to the side of the path; it apparently has seen heavy use over the years. Over to the west is the former house of the late Professor Gast.

Northwest of the main area of the inn is the cafe. This small room was formerly just a storage room with a furnace, but it was converted into a full service cafe when business started to pick up. A large counter seperates the room in two; the ordering section and the cooking section. The cooks are massively busy cooking on a stove that looks like it was recently converted from a furnace. The person taking the orders is also very busy, but still has time for a quick smile before returning to serving the customers. A small door is off to the eastern side of the room, presumably leading to the inn's Bar; that is, if the mat at the foot of the door is at all accurate.

A cozy-looking house lays along the path here, quite unsurprisingly, covered in snow. A small snowman sits in the front of it, completely devoid of features. Also of note is the homely-looking dog sitting adamantly beside the snowman. It's almost as if the dog is guarding the snowman.

The path now leads all the way to the north of town. Large snowbanks have built up along the edges of the path. Off to the west of the path is a bunch of evergreen trees, the type commonly found here. To the east is the beginning of the town's popular snowboarding course. While the course is not recommended for beginners, it might still be possible to descend the icy slope safely.

rooms.name: Icicle Inn - Entrance to a Large House

userData.LongDescription: This is the entrance area of the large house on the eastern side of town. It has a few odd things on the walls, most notable among them a mounted deer head. Perhaps the family obtained this somewhere else. Also here are some old planks, an old table and chairs, and an odd fake tree. While the planks and table and chairs may have some use, the purpose of the fake tree is a total mystery.

This is Icicle Inn, a rather small town that is always in a never-ending winter. As the name would suggest, the entire town is covered in a layer of snow. Near the entrance to the town is a small evergreen tree, also covered in snow. A small shop can be seen to the northwest, while the rest of the town is off to the northeast.

This is the very eastern edge of town. A single house sits here, slightly apart from all the rest. The most eyecatching feature of this house is the snowman sitting out front. Unlike the snowman to the west, this one is much larger and has all the features one would expect a snowman to have. The house is also fairly large for the town; it seems as if a pretty large family lives here. A yellow welcome mat out front greets all visitors that happen to drop by.

This is the upstairs section of the inn, where all the visitors go to sleep when they get tired. It once only had a few beds, but it was expanded when the inn began to get better business. Now beds positively cram the room, filling up every space possible. The beds all look alike, a typical twin size bed with a green bedspread, but the beds aren't what attract the customers. The true draw of the inn seems to be downstairs, with the people currently partying. The only other object in the room besides the numerous beds is a small clock hanging on the wall. Oddly enough, the clock seems to have stopped working.

A large counter takes up the majority of this room, behind which sit an old man and a young girl running the shop. The man appears to be asleep, but the girl is wide awake and ready for business. A staircase is also behind the counter, presumably leading to the family's living quarters. A glass case displaying various weapons sits to the left of the counter. Above the case is a small sign. An old chair is also nearby, but it looks to be there for lack of a better place to put it. Also of note is a small chest sitting in a corner of the room. It appears to be locked, however.

This is Icicle Inn's Inn. The main room is packed with people partying and having a good time, so it can be hard to maneuver. Scattered about the room are various tables and chairs; some of the occupied by chatting people, some not. A counter is off to the northern end of the room, behind which stands the innkeeper. He is currently booking people left and right, but still has time for a quick gesture to a sign on the wall before going back to checking people in.

Icicle Inn's bar, unlike its inn, is nothing to write home about at all. As upbeat and cheerful as the inn is, it's a surprise that the bar could be this dank and depressing. Maybe it's all the depressed drunks hanging down here. Some of them are sitting at tables dotted around the room, but most are hanging at the bar counter, ordering drinks. The bartender is only too happy to oblige, the drinks look like they're very expensive. A small furnace off in a corner provides the only heat in the room, a small grate surrounds it to keep the bar's patrons from burning themselves when they get too drunk.

This is the room of Icicle Inn's snowboarding child prodigy. While most of the town thinks of snowboarding as old hat, this kid has continued to work on it, and has become the best in town. His room displays his dedication to the sport; the walls are positively plastered with posters and pictures about snowboarding. There are some random toys scattered around the room, but his prized snowboard sits delicately in the corner, away from everything else. His large bed is, oddly enough, the only one in the house. The windows beside his bed offers him a terrific view of the snowboarding course on which he spends most of his time.

This is the former house of the late Professor Gast. It has been abandoned since he was killed when the Shinra invaded. The room is very dark and dusty; it doesn't look like anyone has been in here for years. Not a lot can be seen besides rubble, but it looks like a couple of things did survive the Shinra attack. A table and chair sit at one end of the room, while the various instruments Gast used while he was alive are at the other end. None of them appear to work, including Gast's prized video recording system. The only scientific item that was left untouched was a globe, but maybe the Shinra didn't consider it scientific enough to be worth destroying.

Further inside the house is the area where the family can usually be found. Along the northern wall stands a wonderful fireplace, currently lit with a roaring fire. The whole area is filled with the warmth coming from the fire. A particular wood must be burning, for a pleasant scent permeates the room filling it with a heavy, winter-like smell. A stack of this wood is bundled up off in a distant corner, ready for use. Another table like the one found in the entrance area is here, but this one looks to be in better shape than the other one. One of the chairs from the set is also near the table. Accenting the room is a large, Persian-style rug set right in front of the fireplace. The family cat is also sitting in front of the fireplace; enjoying the warmth.

rooms.name: Icicle Inn - Platform Above the Bar

userData.LongDescription: This small platform overlooks the inn's bar. While it's not as popular as the inn itself, it still gets a fair amount of business, mostly from adults looking for some type of alcohol. From this vantage point it's clear that there's not nearly the amount of people in here as back through the door. The bar's also not as family friendly as the inn; curse words are muttered here fairly often. Fortunately, it's much too loud outside for anyone to be able to overhear them. A set of stairs lead to the actual bar itself, which is odd, considering how difficult it is to climb a set of stairs when intoxicated.

This building would appear to be an item shop.  At the far end of the room is a large counter, behind which stands a tall man, wearing a fishing hat.  A coat rack stands to the left, but it doesn't seem to get much use.  A large window provides the dusty shop with some light, while a lamp on the counter does its best to help.  Several boxes, probably of wares, stands behind the man.  A fishing rod and a few weapons are mounted on the wall behind him as well, but neither seem to be for sale.

A tiny bar is set under the weapons shop. The lighting is dim, quiet music plays as a few patrons sit at the scattered tables, and stools. A couple potted plants sit in each corner, giving some decoration to this place. A large counter curves around a case full of beer, and different other alcohols as the bartender stands there, holding a shot glass, and cleaning it quietly.

A small, quaint little shop sells potions and other wares. A dual row of lights illuminate the room, and a clear display case. Inside, many of the shopkeepers wares are shown. Behind the counter the shopkeeper stands, smiling brightly, and waiting to help any of her customers.

A wide stretch of road runs along from west to east, all raised up on a large bridge. On the western side, the road curves to the northwest, heading off towads the cargo shipping area. A small platform can be seen to the south, leading to some sort of lift, broken down from lack of use. Further east the road heads under a small enclosure.

Bright lights, and upbeat music fill this small diner. A row of flourescent lights line along the walls, as well as a neon sign showing: 'Diner'. A few tables are set up, and kept clean as lamps hang down, brightly illuminating over the surface. A small L-shaped counter stands against the back wall, with the owner of the diner tending to her daily duties.

Bright and cheery best describes the Junon Inn. An L-shaped marble counter top runs along a side-wall, with the innkeeper sitting quietly behind. In the next room, nicely made beds await in a warm, clean room.

A large fireplace and several lamps combine to provide a complete change from the dark, cold, town outside.  A long couch is set up against one wall for casual relaxation, while several bright orange beds are available for sleeping.  A large cabinet filled with precious china is by the door, next to a tall grandfather clock.  The center of this small inn is a table with a few chairs set up around it.  A small sign sits on top of it.

A large cargo boat has backed into this loading bay, taking up nearly the whole room. Its loading ramp is lowered down, giving access to anyone inside for a trip to Costa del Sol. A large door leads back out into Junon.

This small branch of the road heads to and from a small beach, which was once the most important part of the town.  Catching the eye here is a large, wooden model of a fish, held up by a nearby pulley.  An old building sits near the fish, but it doesn't seem possible to go in.

The gentle lapping of the waves against the rocks is the first thing that comes to the ears here.  The water stretches forth as far as the eye can see, eventually becoming an ocean.  However, the view is obscured by a huge framework of red metal.  Below the blue-green water a metal structure is visible.

Beneath a metal overpass, two paved roads intersect. A wide, asphalt road runs east to west, heading out from the overpass. Another road branches off to the south, descending in grade steadily. A row of lights provide illumination in this enclosed area.

A small hallway runs from east to west, between the Junon airstrip to the north, and the main part of Junon to the south.  A small door leads to a locker room to the west, with larger doors leading north to the airstrip, and south into Junon. Down the hallway to the east leads to an elevator to Lower Junon.

This once-prosperous fishing town known as Junon is now completely shadowed by the sprawl of the city above.  The whole area is in a perpetual dusk, and the streets and buildings appear very dusty.  A large one to the left appears to welcome visitors freely, as its door stands wide open.  The main street of the town heads towards the northwest.

A horseshoe-shaped counter centers the room, all sorts of papers and junk scattered across it. A few lights within the walls illuminate the room, showing a few clear-cased cupboards along the far wall. An old, balding man sits behind the counter, tending to paperwork. Behind him, a few awards and memorabilia from what only could come from an ex-SOLDIER can be seen.

Upon entering this weapon shop, a fanfare of applause and music fills the room. A couple models of various weapons are on display before a large glass station. Behind this station the shopkeeper stands, awaiting to give any assistance. Behind him, the real McCoy's are held waiting to be bought.

A wide stretch of road runs along from west to east, all raised up on a large bridge. On the eastern side, the road curves to the northeast, heading off towads the airstrip. A small platform can be seen to the south, leading to some sort of lift, broken down from lack of use. Further west the road heads under a small enclosure.

A massive, old, house stands here, showing many signs of age.  A fence runs around its perimeter, with a few barrels sitting behind it.  The house seems to be empty and boarded up.  To the side of it is a small cement pool, filled with stagnant water.  A water pump is set up near the pool; however, it looks extremely rusty.  The street meanders northwest and southeast.

This section of the road is as close to the center of Lower Junon as one can get.  To the northwest, a large stone wall can be seen.  To the southwest, a path leads to some sort of watery area.  A small building stands here, its old sign swinging gently.  On either side of the building is a towering pillar, which most likely supports the city above.

A well lit display case is at the center of this shop. It seems to be the only thing really in the whole store. Various types of weaponry are on display in the clear case. The shopkeeper sits off in the far corner, inside a small room surrounded by glass.

Wide, flat, metal makes up most of the airstrip that the Highwind hovers over, holding the grand airship at bay with a couple tow lines attached to concrete moorings. A row of spotlights line along the runway, and around a couple smaller planes. A small doorway to the south leads into Junon itself.

This tiny house has a heavily feminine decorum.  A red and pink plaid rug has been laid out in front of the door, allowing visitors to clean their feet.  An oddly shaped fireplace warms up the room, sending out a cheerful glow.  Against one wall is a heavy cabinet, while a desk stands near the middle of the room.  In a far corner stands a tall bed with a ladder leading up to the mattress.  A wall clock has been hung up, ticking endlessly.

A huge cement wall rises into the air here, fading into part of a large structure above.  A small door at the bottom of the wall appears to be an elevator, and probably leads to the area above.  Mounted a little ways above the door is a large red symbol.  The road leads back southeast, to the rest of the town.

The sound of distant music can be heard from here, most likely coming from the small door at the bottom of the wall to the northwest.  A large, wooden staircase stands here, leading to a small house at the top.  The house seems to be inhabitated, as lights are shining through the windows.  The small stretch of cobbled road here leads northwest towards the wall, and southeast to a shop.

A small locker room with, of course, lockers lined up along the walls. Various Soldier uniforms and equipment are stored atop the lockers, and around the room itself. Some done neatly, others not. A couple benches are also here, with various items sitting underneath.

A wide expanse of concrete and asphalt forms into a road running from the northwest to southeast. A row of tall buildings rise up along the eastern side with long, twin red banners hanging down from the roof. Large metal 'curtains' hang just above the buildings, ready to be brought down for protection against any attacks. A door can be seen in the holding area to the northwest, leading to the cargo shipping area while the road continues to the southeast.

A wide expanse of concrete and asphalt forms into a road running from the northeast to southwest. A row of tall buildings rise up along the western side with long, twin red banners hanging down from the roof. Large metal 'curtains' hang just above the buildings, ready to be brought down for protection against any attacks. A door can be seen in the holding area to the northeast, leading to the airstrip while road continues to the southwest.

This moderately open section of cave is decently lit with torch light coming from the northern exit. The ground is littered with mounds of rocks of varying height and width. An extremely large cave painting dominates the entirety of the south wall, and the only visible exit is to the northeast.

This cave is covered in a reddish brown layer of rust, or what looks like rust, scattered in patches on the walls, ceiling, and floor. Several human skeletons, as well as reptilian skeletons are littered about the floor of the cave. The cave widens out as it goes deeper in, and several stalactites and stalagmites almost strategically seem to form the shape of a wide open dinosaur mouth.

The cave comes to a dark tunnel, leading to an exit inside the north wall which is adorned with broken stalactites on the ceiling above it. The cave becomes brighter to the east, lit with dim, flickering light. An old, hollow, human skeleton rests against the southern wall.

The tunnel comes to a large platform above a seemingly bottomless pit to the north. The top of this area of the cave is very high as well. However, because there are shafts of light pouring in from the surface, the ceiling becomes hidden behind the light. They all are illuminating one particular place on the platform, giving the impression that this is some sort of altar.

Light shimmers throughout the place, barely illuminating the area. The walls are extremely rough and rocky, and look climbable, but unfortunately, there is a ceiling overhead, filled to the brim with stalagmites. Water drops steadily on the ground in several places, in an even rhythm. The cave stretches to the north and east.

A large spiral staircase holed into the north wall stands prominently in the room. Its threshhold is adorned with engravings along the top, with some strange symbols carved in. The floor is made up of old, gray, rough bricks, which lead from the staircase further east.

This platform sits high above its surroundings, and is decently small, leaving not much room for movement. On the south side of the platform, a long rope ladder leads down into a small hole, shining faintly with light. Another rope ladder on the west edge of the platform leads down to the path below, but is cut off halfway, making a return trip impossible.

Green light shimmers in from the north, keeping this room fairly bright. The walls, and floor are made from solid rock, and are covered with debris. A ravine lies to the south, preventing passage in that direction. The cave stretches to the west and to the north lie the stairs.

This room is very small, but its stone, gray and green floor signifies that it is part of the castle. The ceiling is unusually low, yet there are high torches on the east and west ends of the room that are probably made out of dinosaur leg bones. The walls are covered in bones as well. On the ground, there is a small, but rather shiny egg laying against the north wall.

The most important thing about this room is a small, sparking magic circle commonly known as a Save Point, placed in the southeast corner. The room is lit up by torches on the wall burning a bright green fire, and the gray walls are cracked, seemingly barely holding up the mountain above.

Torches illuminate this region, casting an eerie glow. Also, a lot of noise can be heard. Various animals making noises echo throughout the room. The floor is very hard and rocky, except for some smooth ground near the north exit. The cave stretches to the west, while a staircase leads down.

This hallway comes to an end, with an exit at the south leading to more dark caves. On the north wall, there is a thin window outlined by dinosaur bones through which nothing but rocks can be seen. On the floor near the southern exit a switch has been installed some time ago, though it is now rusted and defunct. The hallway continues on to the west.

Waves wash ashore, thrown against the land by the cruel tide. Directly north lies the entrance to the Giant's Claw, a legendary place once said to be inhabited by prehistoric people. To the immediate west, the Epoch awaits.

This small platform is accompanied with tall cliff walls on the north and west sides, and a seemingly bottomless pit on the south. The platform extends further to the east where a small rope ladder leads up to the top of the rocky cliff walls. Tucked away in a nook of the cave on the west wall, there is an opened, black, treasure chest.

The cave is lit faintly by the torch light coming from inside the northern exit that leads to the castle. The ground is cracked open, revealing small fissures underneath. The area is closely surrounded by rock walls, except for an opening to another area to the west.

Walls lie on only two sides of this room, as the paths to the north and south are clear. Rows of torches line the walls, keeping this place lit. The floor, walls, and ceiling are all made from stone, and have been cut perfectly. All of them are remarkably smooth, each without flaw. A set of stairs lie to the north, and to the south, the cave continues.

Light shines brightly from the north, casting an eerie green light over this region. The floor smooths over near the northern exit, while everywhere else it is very rough. Also at the northern exit, the rock walls are much smoother. The cave stretches to the west and north.

This small platform is accompanied with tall cliff walls on the north side, and a seemingly bottomless pit on the south. There is more to explore further to the west, and a small rope ladder leads up to the top of the rocky cliff walls. There seems to be a crude drawing on one of the walls as well.

Shadows dominate, casting its black glow across the cave walls. Light shines in from a distant source, but fails in its fight to provide good lighting. A corpse of some unidentifyable animal lies on the debris-ridden ground. The walls are made of solid rock, with signs of age. The cave stretches further to the east and north.

This room is a rather cramped room in the castle part of Giant's Claw, made of gray, stone walls, and a green, almost jade colored floors. On the north wall, a giant tyrano skull rests, almost peering around as if it were still alive. There are two switches on the floor, but they look rather defunct.

Light shines from all directions, except north. Several torches line the walls, emitting an eerie green flame. The walls and floor are made from a very smooth stone, and are nice to the touch. Also, there is a huge throne just sitting in the middle of the room, waiting to be sat on. Only the throne and two empty chests are noticable aside from that. The source of the noise is directly south.

This tunnel is the back end of the Lair of the Rust Tyrano. The entire cave is covered in a brick-red colored rust. The only source of light is coming from the area to the north. More skeletons of many different kinds are piled up against the cave walls.

This hallway comes to an end, with an exit at the south leading to more dark caves. The north wall hosts a slim window lined with dinosaur bones. However, only rocks can be seen through it. On the floor near the southern exit a switch has been installed and pressed by somebody some time ago, and there is a gigantic hole in the floor at the east end of the hallway. The hallway continues on to the west.

The source of both the light and noise lie to the south. This region is very well lit, as there is no darkness at all. There is very little debris on the floor, especially near the southern exit, where the ground becomes smoother. Also, under a rock, something crumpled is slightly visible.

Light shines brightly from above, casting a yellowish blaze. Air blows in from several directions, but none more than from the uncovered portion of the ceiling. The walls are made from rock, and are unusually smooth. A rope ladder lies overhead, just out of reach. There seems to be no way to get there, as though it were made for return trips only.

Torches illuminate this room with a strange green light. To the north, there is a large skeleton head of a dinosaur, with its mouth shut. The walls have been crafted from stone, and seems to have been done perfectly. The floor consists of several stone tiles, all of them perfect squares. There are three switches lying on the ground, however, they seem broken and unusable. There is a gaping hole in the floor.

It is VERY dark. Light seeps in from little cracks in the walls, but it is not enough. Vision is just about useless, but fortunately, the exits are still slightly visible. Somehow, a set of rock stairs has been formed. The inhuman voices are even louder from down the stairs.

Torches crackle on the walls, providing ample light for vision. The ceiling, floor, and walls have all been crafted by a strange white stone, which is remarkably smooth. A set of stone stairs lies here, allowing pasage deeper into the earth. To the south, the hall continues.

Torches on the walls illuminate this room. The fires from the crackle as they burn the oil away quickly. Also, the floor is extremely smooth, and is made from stone tiles, similar to the ones in the throne room. Walls lie on opposite ends of the room, each carrying one torch. The cave stretches to the east, and down a set of stone stairs.

This platform is the middle of a series of ledges connected by rope ladders. One rope ladder leads up, and the other leads down. There is a bit of a downward incline to the south on the ledge, with a significant separation in the middle of the platform, making it consist of two layers.

The cave is lit faintly by the torch light coming from inside the northern exit that leads to the castle. The ground is cracked open, revealing small fissures underneath. The area is closely surrounded by rock walls, except for an opening to another area to the west.

The hall continues the gray and green stone scheme found in the rest of the ruined fort. This is the middle of a completely symmetrical hallway that stretches out from the west to the east. On either side of the exit to the north, there are dinosaur-leg torches that illuminate the hallway.

This is a spacious section of the cave that is lit up by torches from the west. The rope ladder to the south leads down a series of cliffs, and it is a decently long way down. Pinned to the north wall, another ladder leads upward to a hole in the ceiling surrounded by claw-like stalactites.

The northern exit is adorned with large bones that form a large gate, covering over a dark hole, surrounded by cave walls and sinister stalactites. Empty egg shells litter the floor before the exit and a warm draft comes from inside, but only once every so often, in almost a rhythmic pattern.

This section of the cave is particularly wide compared to the rocky cliff edge up the rocky, slanted path that leads north. The cave is dark and the air is cold and dry. On the southern wall, a pile of castle rubble has collapsed into place.

All along the north wall, a series of ledges leads upward, with dangling ladders made of rope as means of transportation between them. To the west, the cave continues down a tunnel obscured by darkness. On the southern wall, a rather large cave painting has been made.

Several torches placed about the room, both large and small, standing and hanging, are burning brightly in this part of the hallway. They are spaced symmetrically on either side of the hallway, leading toward a stairwell. The stairwell is in a small alcove in the north wall and is well lit.

Stalagmites jut out from the floor of the cave near the exit to the south, slightly curving and forming an archway that leads into the interior of the ruined cave. Along the east wall, a disused and ancient treasure chest rests, completely stranded. The thick darkness to the west covers over the pathway, obscuring it completely.

The exit to the north is adorned with a couple of torches that are ensconced on the dusty cave walls. They illuminate the immediate area and cast shadows against the various stalactites that dance as the flames flicker. The cave below tunnels downward, with various rope ladders connecting the layers of ledges. This ledge continues to the east.

The room is very dark, making it very difficult to see. Light seeps in through the cave entrance, granting minimal vision. A huge crevice lies to the north, which doesn't seem to have a bottom. This part of the cave seems abandoned, however to the east, many strange, inhuman noises can be heard...

The scene opens up into a grand hallway. Ancient, gray stone covers the floor and the walls of these ruins of the Tyrano Fort. On either side of the main path, signified with lighter gray tiles, is a large stand-up makeshift torch emitting an ever-burning green flame. The torches seem to be made out of leg bones of some ancient dinosaur.

The cave comes to a slight corner above a bottomless pit, its unending darkness engulfs the terrain below. To the north, a small plateau below the rocky cliff edge is visible, where an opened treasure chest collects dust. The path continues on to the east and the west, reaching to the the interior walls of the cave on either side.

Light shines brightly from the east. Debris adorns the floor, weaving a pattern of sorts. A couple of bones lie in the corner, completely fleshless. To the west, a huge crevice lies, which seems to have no bottom. Some strange inhuman voices can be heard, and they are very loud.

The cave comes to a corner, splitting off to the east and to the south. The ground is particularly uneven at this corner, slanting downward as the path heads south. A smaller platform with a treasure chest is barely visible below in the darkness. Rocky formations on the ceiling loom over the area like giant, outstretched claws.

It is very dark here, as the only light comes from the throne room. The ground and walls look jagged and rough, and very unappealing. Water drops steadily from the ceiling, maintaining an even rhythm, and striking the exact same spot each time. A flight of stairs lead up, while to the east, the cave continues.

Casting an almost flashing green light across the room, several torches line the stone walls. The floor is smooth, except for near the southern exit where the ground seems to be crumbling. A set of stone stairs lie to the north, and to the south, the caves begin anew.

There is a narrow cliff that leads to an exit on the north wall, which is adorned with peculiar stalactites that look like the claws, or a hand. There is a ladder that leads down and the narrow cliff platform stretches on to the west, further into the darkness of the cave.

The dinosaur leg torch in the center of the hallway gives an eerie, green aura to the entire hallway, whose dinosaur-bone decorated walls and dusty air only add to the eerieness. Several green torches hang on the walls, seeming to light up the east end of the hallway a little bit more than the west end.

Stalagmites loom overhead, making travel slightly difficult. The floor and walls are of solid rock, and signs of age are showing. Water drops from the ceiling, splashing against the surface of the floor. The cave continues to the east and south.

This hallway of the ruined Tyrano Fort comes to an end with what appears to be two giant dinosaur skulls on the north wall, wide open, with staircases behind them that lead up on the left side, and down on the right. The tiled path splits off into both of those chambers. To the south, torches made of dinosaur bones burn a bright green fire.

There is a lot of noise in this room. Crickets chirping, bats flapping, even noises from outside can be heard. Everything has been built with stone, from the staircase to the floor. The floor starts to break up near the southern exit, and to the north, the throne room is visible.

This is a cell within the Tyrano Fort, signified by the tininess, darkness, and bareness the area exhibits. The bones that would normally block the exit to this room, however, are wide open. The bones seem to be made out of a dinosaur's ribcage. A pile of shattered egg shells lies in one of the corners.

The cliff juts out for a short distance away from the rest of the sky islands. Glowing stones all around the area radiate with the intense energy felt from the most powerful of Eidolons. The clouds below the cliff have mostly parted, though it is near impossible to gauge how far down it is to the surface.

The smooth walls of the bend in the path suggest this narrow section was made by something, but there are no signs of tools or marks on the walls to indicate what carved out the passage.  The bend continues to the north, and opens to the east to a larger cavern room.

The deepest part of the underground tunnels, the only light is provided by the crystal veins running through the walls, their dim glow lighting the way.  Their light stretches down the path, showing that the tunnel leads to the south and to the northeast.

A small corridor leads off to the north, winding its way into the depths of the mountains.  To the south, an exit lies, opening out to the moon's surface and providing ample light to the cavern.  The opening seemes to have been widened by tools, as small marks and chips show where the rock was struck.

This intersection leads off in three directions.  An exit to the surface can be seen farther to the south, while another path leads to the west.  More of this large room extends to the east.  Debris is scattered about the floor, looking like it has been hacked off the walls.

The cave exit leads north and out, the stars shining outside brightly.  This small room has a passage to the west that leads to the other side of the mountains.  Footprints in the moondust near the entrance show signs of previous travelers.

This small subchamber is merely an extension of the much larger chamber to the west. This area looks like it was once used for storage, as a few empty chests lie discarded and unused, pushed against the wall.  The only exit from the storage area is back to the large western chamber.

This curve in the underground road is a small widened pathway between two narrow passages, one leading south to a well-lit exit, the other leading east to deeper inside the mountains.  Small grooves in the ground mark the passage of some clawed beast.

This tunnel runs from southwest to northeast, with the southwest leading farther under the mountain, and the northeast connected to a large chamber that leads out of the underground passages.  The light is dim, with only curious looking crystals in the walls softly glowing as a source of illumination.

A bend in the passage makes the path run from the east to the south, with the east side lit still from the outside exit that lies in that direction.  Shards of rock and crystal litter the ground, signs of a struggle evident from the scars on the walls.

The corridor looks to bend around a corner to the north, and narrows to the south.  Veins of crystal running through the walls gleam softly, twinkling with an inner light and providing illumination enough to traverse the path with ease.

The dessicated and mostly eaten corpse of a giant worm lies at the end of this passageway's dead end, giving a clue to how the path was formed long ago.  The worm's work was unfinished, though, and the only way out of this passage is to the west.

A large chamber under the mountains, this room has an opening to the north to lead back out to the moon's surface.  To the east, a small subchamber lies, and to the southwest a small tunnel leads deeper into the depths beneath the mountains.
