A small path trails off to the east, while to the west lies the other side of this cavernous room.  This room appears to be hollowed out from the rest of the passage, with toolmarks etching the walls.  Stone and rubble from the walls lies on the floor.

This passageway leads through several of the untraversable mountainous regions of the moon.  The exit to the moon's surface lies to the south, while to the north the passage continues.  The starlight from the land above shines in through the opening.

The passage is so narrow, both walls are able to be touched simultaneously without effort.  It widens to the north, and turns a corner to the west to a different wider passage.  Small pieces of rock lie scattered about on the ground.

The eastern wing of the Lunar Palace ends in a small room, bare except for a single glowing tile set in the middle of the room. Though it once restored the magic of any who stepped upon it, the tile's power has long since been exhausted. The path to the west leads back to the palace entrance.

The stage room of the Lunar Palace has a platform situated in the center, with a simple chair seated atop the platform. Four pillars surround the platform, supporting the roof while narrowing the paths on either side of the platform. To the north, a doorway leads deeper into the palace. The entryway is accessible through a path to the south.

The northernmost room in the lunar palace houses eight platforms, each holding a Lunar Crystal. The light emanating from the crystals fills the room with an ethereal aura that is focused in the center of the room. The tile in the center glows underneath the aura, allowing travel into the subterranean caverns. The door to the south leads into the stage room.

The western wing of the Lunar Palace ends in a small room, bare except for a single glowing tile set in the middle of the room. Though it once restored the health of any who stepped upon it, the tile's power has long since been exhausted. The path to the east leads back to the palace entrance.

The entrance to the Lunar Palace branches off in three directions. The paths to the west and east both turn north after a short distance, while the path north here leads into a larger room. The door on the south wall leads out to the lunar surface.

The path of the lunar subterrane splits off to the southeast and southwest. The crystal walls of the subterrane block further passage to the north, while stairs to the south lead back to the entrance platform.

The path curves around the chasm here, heading either northwest and southwest. The platform with the entrance warp tile can be seen across the gap. A faint breeze can be felt coming from the eastern wall.

This hidden path twists around the southwest wall. The darkness prevents one from seeing much of anything, though a faint light to the west can be seen. The path to the south leads further through the passage.

The path opens into a smallish, triangular room. The north wall slopes southwest, while the corner in the southeast is a right angle. A chest sits up against the northern wall. To the west, the path narrows, while a gap in the east wall leads into a dark passage.

The path stops to the north at a small nook in the wall. An empty chest sits at the end, rewarding those who came first and taunting those who came after. The path to the south leads back to the fork in the cave.

The hidden passage has led out to a platform that is separated from the rest of the walkway by a chasm. On the southern end of the platform is a tile that leads deeper into the subterranean caves, and there is a passage through the wall to the east.

The third floor of the lunar subterrane opens into a large cavern that branches off in multiple directions. A huge pillar in the middle of the room has a small cave that leads further down, while a cave on the north wall leads up to the second level.

The subterrane comes to a small opening, the walls circling around to create a cul-de-sac. On the north wall is a small cave, leading to deeper parts of the subterranean caves. To the east, a narrow gap in the wall leads towards the rest of this level of the caverns.

The platform is bordered by the abyss to the north and west. To the east, another section of the platform can be seen across a gap too wide to be crossed. The platform extends south into a dead end, and a small ledge juts off to the west. The stairs to the northeast connect to a higher platform.

The east side of the ring stretches in a mostly straight line to the north and south. Further east is endless abyss, while to the west the lower platform can be seen. The path to the south curves west towards the series of rooms, and to the north the path eventually curves east.

The west end of the lower platform opens to the south but provides no other path further into the subterrane. The abyss can be seen off to the west, and the path back to the east will lead to the flight of stairs going back up to the ring platform.

The caves come to a T-junction in this part of the subterrane. To the west is a dead end, though a passage appears to have existed there before it collapsed. To the north, the path widens and leads to another T-junction. The path east twists south, preventing anything further from being seen.

The path through the lunar subterrane winds through a narrow gap to the west, then twists north leading further into the third floor of the caverns. On the west side of the northern wall, a small cave leads up to the second floor.

This small room within the lunar subterrane connects the first and second levels. A tile at the south end of the room leads towards the first level, while a cave at the north end leads deeper into the second level of the subterrane.

The platform narrows to a point at the south end. A chest sits along the eastern wall, picked clean of its contents. The abyss along the western side separates this platform from one of the many others in the subterrane. The only path open is back to the north.

The entrance to the lunar subterrane begins on a small platform. Stairs to the north lead off the platform, and the path leads off to the left and right, circling back around the landing. A warp tile leading back to the lunar palace is in the center of the platform.

The end of the ring is blocked by a wall on the far west side. The path runs back to the east, leading along the ring to the lower platform. The platform connecting the seventh level to the sixth can be seen from here, but the gap dropping into the abyss is too large to cross.

The subterrane opens here into a vast cavern. A series of platforms are staggered over each other, with stairs interconnecting them. A large pillar sits in the middle of this platform with a cave leading back to the third floor. To the east is a small bridge connecting to another platform.

The west half of a large platform wraps around the western pillar in the fifth floor. Another large platform is above this one, and to the east the platform encases the eastern pillar. A cave in the large pillar leads into the smaller tunnels within the pillar.

The lunar subterrane path leads to the northwest, northeast, and south at this junction. The walls here shine lightly with light from an unknown source. A chasm to the north separates the entrance platform.

A small circular room opens up within the cave situated inside an enormous pillar. On the southern wall is a small passage that leads out into the massive cavern. A gap in the northern wall leads to a small room that curves to the west.

The path twists around a corner into a narrow corridor. To the west, it curves north, leading to a small cave that connects the first level to the second. To the east is a dead end, though a faint breeze is coming from the wall.

The southern tip of this platform has a small outcropping on the east side, giving a slight hint of the invisible bridge connecting this platform to the one to the east. The path runs along the wall to the northwest, wrapping around out of sight to the north.

The platform opens to a wide area with two large wall segments. An open chest sits at the southwest side. The abyss borders the platform on the south and west sides, but the path continues to the east. A long flight of stairs runs through a narrow gap in the walls leading up to a higher platform.

The path curves around, connecting a cave to the path towards the entrance. The cave turns quickly to the east, obscuring what lies deeper within the lunar subterrane. The path to the north leads towards the entrance of the lunar subterrane.

rooms.name: The Lunar Subterrane: B5 Save Point

userData.LongDescription: This room is surrounded with an aura of calm. Four small metal obelisks are situated in a square around a glowing orb in the center of the room. A warp tile sits on the north end of the room, and a small exit on the south end leads out of this room and into the larger cavern.

A large platform wraps around one of the two main pillars on the fifth floor. Above this platform is another shaped just like it. To the northeast is a small chest, though its contents are long since gone. A small cave in the large pillar leads back into the twisting caves within the pillar.

A small room in the tunnels opens up. The path to the south runs through a narrow gap in the walls into a fork in the tunnel. On the northern wall, a small opening leads deeper into the subterranean caves.

The platform comes to a T-junction, with the path running east, west, and north. The southern edge is bordered by the abyss, while the path to the west leads towards the stairs that connect this platform to the higher ones. The north appears to be a dead end, and the east path stretches on for quite some distance.

The southwest side of the ring has a large wall running along the east side. To the north is the beginning of the ring and the seventh floor, while to the east the ring runs alongside the wall with several openings into smaller caves.

The path comes to a dead end. A chest sits in a nook at the far west end of the room, though it was long ago cleaned of its contents. The path to the east is the only exit from this room, leading back towards the rest of the lunar subterrane.

This room is a dead end cave. The room is mostly round, though a small section of wall in the southeast corner juts out. An opened chest sits on the eastern wall. The tunnel in the southern wall is the only exit, leading back to the cavernous main room.

Two columns stand at the entrance to this room, forcing anyone who wishes to enter to squeeze through, A single pedestal stands in the middle of the room, ornately carved. Whatever used to rest on it has long since vanished. The exit to the south is the only way out of the room.

The east end of the lower platform opens up to the south, but provides no other means to go deeper into the subterrane. The eastern ring segment runs high above. The path to the east will lead to the flight of stairs going back up to the ring platform.

This small room is tight, though slightly larger than the narrow hidden passage that connects it to the rest of the third floor. A long since looted chest sits in a nook on the north wall. A faint breeze comes through the eastern wall. A hole in the wall to the west leads into a secret passage.

The subterrane opens into a small room, roughly circular in shape. A small nook sits in the southern wall. The wall to the east has a faint draft coming from the passage. To the west lies a narrow passage that leads to another room.

The path runs along from east to west. To the south of the path is a large wall, and to the north is the deep abyss. The path at the west end turns south, while the path to the east runs into the darkness of the abyss, unable to be seen clearly.

The path comes to a peninsula pointing north. To the northeast across the abyss, a separate platform can be seen. The path runs to the west, leading back towards the main portion of the platform. A small warp tile sits on the side of the peninsula.

This room is a small niche in the cave. It holds an opened chest in the center of it, and wraps around it tightly on the east, north, and south sides. The only path out of this area is back to the southwest.

The path runs through a hidden tunnel in the wall, making it nearly impossible to see anything. The ambient lighting is nearly gone, but there is still enough to make out a path to the north. A faint light to the south can be seen coming from the exit of the tunnel. A light breeze comes from the west.

This section of the hidden passage twists around a corner to the southeast. The light from the northern section of the passage has faded, but a glimmer can be seen to the west, indicating the end of the dark tunnel.

The narrow path runs along from east to west. To the south of the path is a large wall, and to the north is the deep abyss. At the east end, the path wraps south towards an apparent dead-end, while the path to the west runs farther than can be seen in the darkness.

Two columns stand on either side of the entrance to this room, forcing any who wanted to gain entry between them. Two chests sit in the back of the room. Whatever their contents once were, all that is inside them now is a thin layer of dust. The door to the south is the only exit.

The northeast portion of the ring curves, mirroring the platform below. To the north and east, nothing can be seen beyond the abyss. The path to the west leads to a flight of stairs connecting the ring platform to the lower one, and the path to the south narrowly stretches on.

A small circular room in the cave opens up here between two narrow passages. A chest sits along the north wall, though it has long since been picked clean of its contents. Passages to the east and west lead through twisting narrow corridors into the rest of the lunar subterrane.

This enormous platform sits at the bottom of the vast cavern. A huge pillar on the north end has a small hole that leads to a connecting cave. A chest on the east side of the platform has long since been opened. To the south is a set of stairs that leads deeper into the subterrane.

The lunar path twists and turns here, wrapping around the western wall to the north. At the southern end, it ends abruptly, with a narrow cave entrance on a short outcropping leading towards the upper levels of the subterrane.

A narrow split in the walls allows the path to continue. On the east side, the path abruptly ends, but a path to the southeast allows one to go deeper into the subterrane. To the west, the path opens up and looks to split off in several directions.

The smaller caves split into two paths to the north. The path to the northwest appears to lead to a dead end, while the path to the northeast has a small opening in the wall. A tunnel in the southern wall leads out to the larger cavern.

Two small, ornate columns stand on either side of a majestic pedestal. Though nothing sits there now, the carvings on the pedestal indicate that this was once the home to a most powerful weapon. The platform has no other exit than the small tunnel leading back into the cave.

The subterranean caves split in a T-junction. To the east, the path twists around towards a warp tile. To the south, the path, slightly wider, splits once more. The west holds a dead end, though it appears there used to be a passage before it collapsed.

A gap between two pillars leads to a large open space in the subterrane. The room has a small protrusion from the south wall, creating a slight curve in the shape of the room. The only exit from this area lies back to the east through the gap.

The seventh level of the lunar subterrane opens up. The large cavern appears to consist of two platforms, the higher a large ring encircling the lower one. The wall on the north end blocks the ring going northwest, but the path extends south. A tunnel in the wall leads up to the sixth floor.

The main feature of this platform is the gargantuan pillar holding up the platform above it. The path forms a crescent shape around it on the south side. Stairs on the far east end lead down to another platform, while the path to the west connects to a smaller platform.

The lowest point in the fifth floor cavern, this large platform wraps around the eastern pillar. A small path to the east turns into a dead end, while to the south a staircase leads deeper into the subterranean caves. A small opening in the pillar leads into more twisting caves.

The path of the lunar subterrane heads off to the southeast and northeast. The entrance platform can be seen to the west, though it is separated by a chasm that seemingly has no bottom. A faint breeze comes from the western wall.

A central pillar defines this room, shaping it in a diamond formation. The path curves around it in either direction, rejoining on the east and west sides. To the northeast is a small room that fades around a corner. The path to the southeast leads to an open circular area, and the west side leads to another open room.

The second level of the subterrane continues to wind around. At the north end of the path, a cave leads up to the first level. In the other direction, the path curves east around a corner deeper into the subterrane.

A large ledge wraps around one of the two main pillars on the fifth floor. To the northeast is a small chest, though its contents are long since gone. A small cave in the large pillar leads back into the twisting caves within the pillar.

A hidden path leading through the western wall leads towards the entrance to the lunar subterrane. To the east, an endless chasm spreads out, certainly spelling doom for any who fall off. A narrow path heads to the north before turning out of sight to the west.

A long flight of stairs connects the large cavern of the fourth floor to the even larger cavern of the fifth floor. The stairs run between two enormous platforms, each supported by a large pillar. An open chest sits on the west end of this platform. A small cave leads into the central pillar.

A narrow tunnel runs north to south in the subterranean caves. At the south end is an exit leading back to the larger cavern composing most of the fifth level of the subterrane. To the north, the cave twists and opens to another room.

Curving around the wall to the southeast, the path comes to a dead end. However, a path has been blasted open through a small nook in the wall, leading to the northwest. The path to the north turns around a corner and heads east.

A narrow corridor runs north-south, restricting the subterranean path tightly. To the south, the path continues on, leading to the cave that connects the second and third floors. At the north end, the path turns west sharply. A strong aura can be felt coming from that direction.

A large room within the cavern comes to a T-intersection. To the north is a small passage that leads to a lower section of the large fifth floor cavern, and to the south is a different passage leading out to a higher portion. A small passage in the wall on the west side twists around into the cave.

An immense aura can be felt from this dead-end in the lunar subterrane. Two columns rest in a nook on the south wall, and a pedestal stands between them. Evidently, a powerful artifact used to rest on it, but has long since been taken away.

This platform circles around a large pillar with a small opening in the center. On top of it rests the platform with the connecting cave to the second floor. The path to the west leads towards another platform that has multiple stairs leading up and down.

A small gap in the wall leads through to a small open area. The wall to the north comes out sharply, leaving a small passage to the east, though it suspiciously ends abruptly. A faint breeze can be felt from the east wall. The gap to the north leads to the larger section of this floor with passages both up and down.

This platform is near the bottom of the vast cavern. A long flight of stairs at the east side leads up to a higher platform in the cavern. A small cave in the central pillar of this platform can be entered.

A large platform wraps around the base of the western pillar in the large fifth floor cavern. To the east, a narrow path leads towards the eastern pillar. The path to the west curves to the north. A small opening in the pillar leads into the narrow tunnels.

The hidden tunnel runs in a relatively straight north-south path. At the north, it abruptly curves west, leading out of the tunnel. Far to the south, a faint light can be seen coming from the other entrance of the tunnel.

The platform runs narrowly from east to west, the abyss spreading out on either side. To the west, the platform turns into a T-junction. The eastern side of the path curves slightly north, turning to a dead end.

A long flight of stairs extends upwards into the darkness, surrounded on all sides by the dark abyss. A platform can be seen off to the east, though it is inaccessible from here. A small warp platform sits at the base of the stairs.

A hidden path within the hidden tunnel itself twists around in strange ways. A chest can be faintly seen at the west end, though it appears someone else has long since passed through here and availed themselves of its contents.

The path runs up to the north into a peninsula, surrounded by the abyss on the north, west, and east. At the very tip, the two protrusions where the invisible bridge is can be seen. The only path open to adventurers is back to the south.

This room has an aura of calm. Four metal obelisks surround a glowing orb in a diamond pattern. The orb seems to be the source of the calming aura. A small open area in the wall sits to the north of the obelisks. The only exit is the door on the southern wall.
The tunnels turn into a dead end at the south side of this room. A small, empty chest sits in the corner. To the northeast, the tunnels curve back and continue their twisting tangle of pathways.

The path wraps around to the north, turning into a dead end. An empty chest sits squarely in the middle of the narrow path. A gap in the platform to the west separates this platform from one of the many others in the subterrane. The only exit is back to the east.

The southern side of the ring platform starts to curve north at the west end. The wall on the north holds a door to the most eastern of the rooms. To the west, the path continues along the series of doors. The path turns north, leading towards the section connecting the lower platform to the upper ring.

The northern end of the cave curves around the wall to the southeast. A small niche is cut out in the northern wall, and the path to the south opens up into a wider part of the cavern. The path ends abruptly to the east, though a faint breeze can be felt.

This room has a large pillar sticking out of the northern wall, right next to a cave that leads deeper into the subterrane. A chest on the west side of the pillar has been pillaged. A path to the east leads into a small, circular room.

The northern section of the ring runs somewhat straight from east to west. A flight of stairs connects the ring to the lower platform and deeper into the subterrane. The path continues west, running into a wall preventing the ring from being a complete loop. The path to the east curves to the south.

A short flight of stairs connects this lower platform to the first platform of the sixth level. Immediately at the bottom of the stairs, the cavern walls abruptly turn north, wrapping around in a horseshoe pattern. The path continues around the protrusion to the south.

The path here curves east and ends up against a large crystal wall. The northern edge of the path has a small gap separating another platform, though the distance is too great to jump. A chest rests on the ground here, though it has long since been cleaned out. The path runs back to the northwest.

A long staircase runs up through the fifth level of the caverns. The massive pillars surrounded by multiple platforms that hide a maze of twisty passages can be seen. At the top of the staircase is a small platform followed by more stairs. The bottom of the staircase has receded into the darkness.

The path along the south side of the ring continues in either direction. The middle door is on the north wall, while the endless abyss is to the south. To the east and west, the path continues, curving north on both sides.

The entrance to this cave within a cave opens broadly. The room runs mostly along a northwest line, though the south wall wraps around, forming a circular area. A hole in the south wall leads out to the larger cavern, and the path to the northwest leads into the rest of this cave.

The lunar subterrane path runs south here, splitting away from the wall on the east side. A small landing can be seen across the abyss on the east, and nothing can be seen to the west in the inky darkness.

The lower platform branches off to the east and west from this narrow landing point. A flight of stairs leads up to the ring platform encircling the area. Pillars extend up from this level to the ring, supporting the higher platform. A small cave is set into the northern wall, though it is sealed with some unknown force.

Two large wall segments open up at the base of the stairs connecting the fifth and sixth levels of the lunar subterrane. To the south, two sets of stairs connect this platform to another. Narrow paths on the east and west side wrap around the walls.

The cave curves around the western wall, the path to the northwest leading to a T-junction and the path to the west leading to a smaller opening. The wall extends almost to the point of restricting passage to the west, but still leaves enough room to pass through single file.

The path runs east to west, with a small pillar jutting out of the wall on the north end. An emptied chest sits in the alcove created by the pillar, showing signs of a fight nearby. The path twists south at the west end and gently curves southeast on the east side.

The path curves around the wall, turning north into a dead end. A chest, emptied of its contents, sits in the middle of the path. The abyss of the subterrane spans into the darkness to the east. The path back west appears to the be only exit.

The path runs north-south between the wall and the abyss. To the west, a flight of stairs can be seen, though there appears to be no discernable way to get to them, as the abyss separates them from the platform. The path ends to the north, though a strong breeze can be felt from the wall.
The small cave turns in a horseshoe pattern. It has two paths to the south, one leading southeast and one southwest. The northern wall has a small tunnel that leads further down into the subterrane.

This small cave sits inside a large pillar. A lone chest rests in the middle of the room, though from its state it looks like it was plundered a long time ago. The only exit from this room is the small opening in the southern wall leading back out to a large cavern.

The path turns north, leading to a dead end. The darkness at the edge of the platform is impossible to penetrate. A chest sits at the north end of the pathway, long since looted. A small column rises from the floor to a higher platform far above. The only path open is back to the east.

A long staircase continues up to the top of the fifth level of the caverns. The large cavern composing most of the fifth level can be seen quite clearly. At the top of the staircase is a small platform, on which sits a warp tile. The stairs down lead to a tiny platform and then again to more stairs.

A rectangular area occupies the far west end of this cave. A small nook in the southwest corner of the room contains a previously-opened chest. On the south wall is a small opening that leads out to the larger cavern. To the east is a room with a wide pillar in the center.

This platform sits near the top of a vast cavern in the subterrane. A huge pillar rests in the middle of it, to the east of which is a chest that long ago gave up its secrets. Stairs to the south lead down to another platform, most of which is occupied by the pillar holding up this one.

The path comes to a dead end, ending at the far east wall. A pillar juts out of the north wall, and the south wall curves up, bringing the room to a curve at the northeast side. The only path is back to the west.

The path runs along the south side of the ring between the abyss and a series of small doorways. The westernmost door is on the north wall. The path to the east continues along the wall, while the path to the west curves north and leads to the start of the seventh level.

The subterranean path runs narrowly between the wall and the abyss. Across the gap to the southeast, another platform can be seen. The opposite wall has a small opening at the end, leading into a smaller maze of tunnels. The path to the north wraps around the wall, obscuring the path out of the caves.

A pulsating, blue star fills the chamber with its soft glow, its ancient enchantments protecting all within. The grotto itself is a picturesque landscape of beautiful, towering stalagmites and a mineral spring, artfully arranged as only nature can. In the northeastern and northwestern corners, subtle passageways lead away from this peaceful scene.

rooms.name: A Maze Of Treasure Chests & Bridges

userData.LongDescription: In a horrible state of disrepair stands a winding bridge, curling in upon itself as if 'twere a snake seeking to bite its own tail and not quite reaching. At its northmost end, it collides most unceremoniously into a wall and decides to terminate with little fanfare. No sane man could have designed this travesty of a passageway.

The cave's floor drops off sharply to the west, where several old, wooden bridges stretch out across a yawning abyss. Jagged stalagmites pierce the darkness like skeletal fingers, adding further risk to crossing the already unstable platforms. Stairs lead away through entrances both to the north and the south.

A pillar of white light shines down upon the northmost section of this chamber, bathing the cavern's warm stone floor in brilliant luminescence. Two sets of roughly hewn stairs lead away to the south, the landing between them branching off into an empty side area. The second set, definitely not a natural occurance, descends into a dark opening.

A sparsely wooded hillock offers an excellent view of Triangle Island, a wasteland of scorched earth and dead grass obscured only by the ugly crags in its center. East of the knoll, a ravine cuts through the outcropping, allowing passage to the beach. A rope ladder leads up into the Falcon, southeast of which a cluster of trees awaits.

This remarkably sturdy span of bridge connects to nothing at all on either end. The surface is covered with scratches and pits, the wear and tear of regular use, an oddity in so exotic a locale. Flanking the partially crumbled platform on either side are two more, which a sufficiently athletic leap may be able to reach.

Pale green light shines through deep fissures in the earth, filling the chamber and bathing the ascending stairway in its glow. Atop this stair lies a circular platform coated in a thick layer of dust, long ago abandoned by whatever used or occupied it. In the opposite wall, a slightly ajar door of heavy iron protects what once was.

rooms.name: A Maze Of Treasure Chests & Bridges

userData.LongDescription: Plainly standing out from the surrounding rock is a door of solid iron, set into the northern wall and quite clearly representing one of the maze's two endpoints. To the south, a great pit of blackness is compromised only by a plethora of bridges and chests, the latter of which's spring-loaded nature makes jumping the gaps between a fun endeavor.

The formerly lush greenery comprising this grove is struggling to survive, much of it having already lost the battle against such a harsh environment. Several of the trees are uprooted completely and there's a strange lack of wildlife, as if the island were dying.

Thin fog hangs over this tepid landing, accompanied by the distinct scent of mildew emanating from the southern entryway. A slight breeze wafts through the balmy cavern, as oddly warm as the nearby stone, seemingly originating from far below, beneath the thick, obscuring cover of darkness.

Flotsam and jetsam litters the sandy shore, scattered across the sparkling white sand. Crimson waters stretch out as far as the eye can see, reflecting the glare of an angry sky. Strange sinkholes dart the landscape, some of which are stuffed with debris from the frequent shipwrecks, a constant threat to the inattentive.

rooms.name: A Maze Of Treasure Chests & Bridges

userData.LongDescription: A small ledge protrudes from the northern rock face, holding a treasure chest and, a rare sight in this gauntlet, enough room to stand. Myriad chests are scattered about the chamber, all of them open and seemingly either rusted into position or spring-loaded. Assuming the latter, leaping from chest to chest might be possible.

The ground is strewn with loose rock, debris from the fall of what appears to be a great piece of the ceiling. Most of it is intact in the form of a single, solid layer, its support having given way long ago. Though the going will be treacherous, the properly prepared explorer could climb around atop it with minimal injury.

rooms.name: A Maze Of Treasure Chests & Bridges

userData.LongDescription: This bridge extends just a little ways to the west, ending there without joining to anything, and curves southward a bit to the north. Despite sturdy construction, time has taken its toll and brought low parts of this mighty, yet humble, construct. It's safe enough to traverse for the time being, but how long it will hold is anyone's guess.

The passage of many feet has worn smooth the stone floor, lending extra treachery to any travel across the precipice. Thick, parallel cracks separate a small, protruding segment of the ledge from the surrounding rock. A depressed switch is set into the ground just to the west of the upraised portion, rusted into position, and a set of stairs ascends into darkness to the north.

Spanning the length of several men, the bridge terminates sharply to the east and west, ravaged by the steady march of time. A few poles stand to the south, having once held a bridge, and the nothern one has held surprisingly well over the ages. Despite the gap between its two sections, either could be reached with a little care.

Jutting out from the floor's warm stone is a rickety structure of wood, ending abruptly before reaching any real destination. Near it are two more bridges in various states of disrepair, easily within jumping distance. Off to the west and south, roughly hewn stairs descend into a well-lit chamber.

The air grows stale in this small chamber, exacerbated by the pungent odor of mold from the southern tunnel. Rather featureless, the chamber itself is, boasting little but a dull brown floor and similar walls. Were it worked by human hands, which it shows no sign of, the place would be naught but a hall or antechamber.

The floor is rough, untraveled, and the occasional pit reveals a separate, smoother layer of rock below, occasionally covered with splinters of wood from shattered chests. The light, musty scent of mold permeates the air, growing ever stronger along the ledge to the west.

An unkempt assemblage of rotten planks extends haphazardly over a great pit, a length of bridge whose center has collapsed. Two bridges run parallel to this one, each missing several sections of its own. With careful leaps, it may be possible to traverse this architectural travesty.

rooms.name: A Maze Of Treasure Chests & Bridges

userData.LongDescription: An island of rock floats serenely in a cloud of darkness, isolated from the surrounding treasure chests and islands by an expanse of nothingness. Futilely attempting to bridge these gaps are a trio of ramshackle platforms, not long enough to serve their proper purpose and, instead, becoming naught but springboards for foolhardy acrobats.

rooms.name: A Maze Of Treasure Chests & Bridges

userData.LongDescription: A surreal number of empty treasure chests rest securely upon evenly spaced pillars, like stepping stones within a vast, black river. Bridges unknowably ancient stand interspersed between them, peppering the air with their unmistakable scent, and a man-sized hole leads off to the north.

Repeated impacts have formed a shallow pit in the floor over the ages. The simple beauty of natural stone is marred in its center by myriad scratches and even the occasional fracture. A pair of empty treasure chests further detract from the earthy ambience, aided in their efforts by an ugly metal switch.

A series of platforms, in actuality just three bridges that are missing large portions, stretch out across a gaping chasm in the rocky floor. The pungent scent of old wood fills the dank cavern and several of the bridges' planks are missing. Dangling from a protruding nail is a scrap of cerulean cloth, still clean, adumbrating the recent passage of someone else.

rooms.name: A Maze Of Treasure Chests & Bridges

userData.LongDescription: Rusted into the surrounding metal is an iron switch of the variety one activates by foot. It seems that somebody passed through long ago and saw no reason to reset the button, if even it can be, leaving its effects a mystery to any future travellers. Adjacent to this island are a pair of bridges, quite possibly within range of a good leap.

The bottom of the sea is filled with exotic life.  There are schools of fish swimming around in the distance, weaving between the colorful plants, sponges and anemones that cover the ocean floor.  The water's surface is high overhead, the light of the sun blurred and barely visible.  A hatch leads back into the submarine.

This tiny U-shaped room is the control hub for the submarine.  The swiveling captain's chair in the middle of the room has a good view of all the flashy monitors hanging above the consoles that the other chairs are positioned in front of.  Irregular rectangular panels of dark gray metal are bolted onto the walls, which are slanted to make the ceiling smaller than the floor.

A steel walkway surrounded by grated flooring runs through the length of the tiny submarine.  Numerous metal pipes cover the walls, some connecting to exposed machinery and others disappearing behind the wall plating.  The ceiling hangs very low.  Flourescent lights are set into the starboard wall.  Next to some glowing meters and dials is a tiny trap door leading down to an airlock room.  It's currently sealed.  A ladder affixed to the wall leads up to the upper hatch.

Near a bend in the northern wall is a rotating purple and green monolith with a shining aura about it.  Another of the light gratings is on the north wall just next to a dark pathway leading to the west.  A door with the Shinra logo upon it leads north.  The steps lead down into the water to the east.  There is an open crate in the corner.

This is a platform overlooking a storeroom below.  A railing on the edge to the south prevents one from accidentally falling off.  There is a message of some sort posted on the wall here, but damage from moisture has rendered it unreadable.  Another fan is on the northern wall.  A crate is at the end of the platform, but it is open and empty.  The only exit is back to the west.

A strange purple light fills this two-level room.  A grating stretches south towards a door on the other side of the room.  This platform also leads east to a green box which has already been opened.  A green box can be seen below the platform as well.  North of the platform is a large device of some sort with the Shinra logo upon it.

The storeroom is large and expansive.  A mass of broken crates and dented drums occupies the southwest corner of the room.  There are a few drums under the staircase leading back up to the platform as well.  There is more of the storeroom to the east.

This is a platform overlooking a storeroom below.  A railing on the edge to the east prevents one from accidentally falling off.  On the wall to the left is one of the ever-present fluorescent lights, but this one appears to be nonfunctional.  An overturned steel drum has rolled against the railing.  There are three crates here; one has been opened and is empty, and all three are covered with algae.  A fan on the northern wall is not moving.  A staircase leads down into the storeroom and the platform continues east along the northern wall.

A strange purple light fills this two-level room.  A grating stretches north in front of the door; it can be walked on to the other side of this room.  The platform also leads east to a stairway leading down into the bottom of the room.  A green box is at the foot of the stairway.  A door also leads out to the south.

rooms.name: A room in the Gelnika, bottom level

userData.LongDescription: A strange purple light fills this two-level room.  A platform goes around the room above.  A green box is sitting in the corner near two grimy drums, and like the other boxes in the Gelnika it has been opened already.  An odd device stretches towards the ceiling to the north.  The Shinra logo can be seen upon it.  The sole exit is the staircase going back to the platform.

The metallic walls are grimy and showing spots of rust in this narrow passage that is flooded with about two feet of water.  Just above the water level are two grates behind which still functioning yellow fluorescent light bulbs provide enough light to see.  A ladder leads up through a hatch and out of the crashed Gelnika.  The passage leads only to the west up some steps.

Most of this half of the storeroom is occupied by a large, mangled, wrecked helicopter.  There is a single open crate along the south wall.  What little of the room isn't occupied by the helicopter is flooded with water, and impassable.  The only exit is back to the western side of the room.

This room seems to border the side of the plane, as evidenced by the sloping west wall, along which two thick pipes run.  There are two light gratings along the west wall as well.  A large drum is by the eastern pathway, as well as one on its side in the corner of the room.  On the north wall is another door with the Shinra logo on it.  A red light is on above the door.

The corridor splits into two paths, an eastern and a western direction.  A series of three pipes runs along the floor, disappearing beyond a distant corner.  Large metal catwalks and wires can be seen all around the ceiling of Geno Dome.  A small computer is imbedded in the wall, with broken wires and a smashed in display screen.

The room is nothing more than a giant conveyor belt, wall to wall.  There are some strange pipes along the wall, and the conveyor belt leads far to the north.  From some panels above, buzzing noises can be heard, like some sort of electrical current is running through this whole place.

The pulsing red lights that comprise most of the floor continue flashing as one passes through the area, along with several glowing yellow protrusions from the ground.  The floor is made of dark grey panels, and one destroyed panel reveals some sort of circuitry beneath.   In the southeast corner of the room a chest sits on the ground, open and untouched for quite a while.  To the north the elevator is in view, while a pool of green goo seems to be forming against the west wall.

Large mechanical arms and assembly areas are running along the far wall.  A large box full of scrap metal and machinery is attached to the floor.  An exhaust vent is on the upper left corner of the room, cooling the area down so the robots do not overheat during production.

The belt moves faster, taking all of its occupants to the north.  Tiny robots fly around the area, with sparks trailing behind them.  The conveyor belt appears to continue on for quite a while.  Larger robots are coming out of the walls, flying towards the center of the belt to rid the area of any intruders.

A motion activated steel door is on the northern wall, with a giant red and yellow sign above it.  To the west, a small conveyor belt takes over what would be the pathway, to easily transport large objects or equipment around Geno Dome better.  The paint on the walls has been scratched off of the floor from moving large things all about this place.

The door to the north is visible now, but a horde of monsters are guarding it.  Small surges of electricity flow throughout the walls, lighting up the area.  A series of large pipes run through the walls and along the ceilings of the area, disappearing into the main portion of Geno Dome.

This room was originally designed to be a viewing area for the experimental robots.  One of those one-way mirrors is on the western wall, allowing sight into an adjacent room.  A small switch is on the Southern wall, with a sign above it.

A short flight of steps joins this section of the walkway to a much wider area of the dome.  There are a few of the glowing yellow protrusions here, but far more a short distance to the north.  A ladder is visible through a small break in the wall, leading down into the darkened dome.  A narrow path of dirty floorspace heads off east.

Used to control the huge steel door, this room has a small glowing pedestal which looks rather important.  The room itself is small, dirty, and fits right in with the rest of Geno Dome.  Looking to the east, another matching pedestal can be seen a short distance away.

The corridor makes a turn for the north, where it soon after dead ends.  Some broken pipes run along the walls, with an occasional electrical spark leaping out of them.  The floor is old and worn, with some spots not having any grate coverings on it.  Some sort of worn down defensive matrix can be seen on the floor, but does not appear operational.

On the north side of this walkway, the floor is simply missing, providing glimpses of an isolated catwalk below.  The edge of the pit is walled off, and there is a red emergency light set into the end of the wall here.  An abundance of glowing yellow lights can be seen over the wall as it bends north, along with a large door.

rooms.name: A large room full of technology

userData.LongDescription: The room is very simple, with a massive computer on the far wall, and a door next to it.  The computer is very old and large, but appears to still be working, with all the flickering lights and switches on it.  The door is heavily bolted shut, no human could possibly open it without aid.

This room is in a state of energy flux.  A giant field of energy emits from it, and electrically charges all of the objects inside of it.  Waves of electricity are emitting from all of the objects in the room, spasmatically moving around and fluxuating in the air.

Used to control the huge steel door, this room has a small glowing pedestal, and looks rather important.  The room itself is small and dirty, which fits right in with the rest of Geno Dome.  Looking to the west, another matching pedestal can be seen a short distance away.

Geno Dome is dismally underfurnished and not very well maintained.  The ground is consistent with the rest of Geno Dome by being particularly unswept, and the ceiling near the walls drips some sort of green fluid into a puddle.  A laser forcefield was placed between this area and the one to the north, but is currently nonfunctional.   A switch high on the north wall presumably controls the forcefield.  The rooms east lead back to the elevator, while those to the west head deeper into the dome.

The exit side of the conveyor belt is clear evidence that the human victims are dead, the belt is stained red.  Ear-piercing shrieks of pain fill the room at odd intervals, and it seems like a very unsafe place to be.  An electrically-protected set of steps accesses the conveyor, but is impossible to pass through.  A doorway leading out of here could provide some much more welcome sights.

This giant hallway in Geno Dome seems to be filled only with the red glow of blinking lights, though the scant illumination makes it difficult to be certain.  Cables are in view along the tops of the walls, transmitting communications between the mother brain and the rest of the dome's robots.  Far to the north the end of the hall is identifiable only by the end of the long chain of lights, and a doorway leads out.

This small claustrophobic chamber features four glowing ovals of light on the ground, which function as an elevator.  It is illuminated by these and several other lights in the room, whose purpose is unknown.  The wall to the north pulses slightly with power from the Dome, in two tall stripes of oscillating red light.  A doorway leads out to the second level of Geno Dome.

The long hall here features more of the same old glowing lights as the areas to the north and south.  Where the floor is not covered in lights, there is a light crisscrossing mesh that provides traction for wheeled robots.  The hallway is so lightly traveled, it is a mystery why it exists at all.

A small panel is on the wall, with two buttons.  A sign is above the door, reading 'Elevator'.  A faded green arrow is on the western wall, now dull with age.  Some flashing red and green lights can be seen under the floor grates, as well as a thin blue line.

The elevators in Geno Dome are of the same standard design, four glowing ovals of light on the ground sense when passengers are present.  The soft light cast by these reveals that the rest of the room is stark, panels and slits in the walls are the only features.  A doorway leads out to the first level of Geno Dome.

This room is an old storage unit for Geno Dome.  There are lots of shelves and boxes, but they are all empty.  A small table is seen on the distant north wall, recently cleaned off.  A few hand trucks and hammers are lined up neatly along a wall, as well as some some other miscellaneous tools.

There are two more path choices in this room, off of the conveyor belt.  To the East, there is a sharp bend to the north, followed by some stairs.  To the West, there is some sort of locked door with a large red light above it.  A small disposal chute is to the north, but it is too small for any person to fit into.

A massive door towers up all the way to the ceiling.  A flashing red light and a large sign are right next to the top of the door.  Large pipes run through the wall into the closed off room.  Some pieces of scrap metal lead a trail that ends right at the foot of the door in this room.

The corridor continues on to the west, where it disappears behind a corner.  Immediately to the west of here, there is a small passageway leading farther into Geno Dome.  There is a door in this room, sensor activated.  It leads into a small room inside of the walls.

The path continues on to the west, as well as a small walkway to the north.  There is a huge pipe running beneath the floor, heading to the north, where it leaves view behind a door.  To the west, the floor changes to a brownish cover, and there are cameras tracking movement throughout the area.

The platform below the upper level is made of a lower quality material than the area above, but seems to be sturdy enough to support the weight of the robots around here.  The ladder leading back to the deck above is metal, but looks scarcely used.  The narrow scaffold-like catwalk leads west, deeper into the dome.

The snakelike, unprotected corridor continues from the east through this area, and further north to a door off in the distance.  An old chest lies on the ground here, lid ajar.  In the dark, still air to the west, a green oval of light grows darker and lighter, almost like an eye opening and closing.  There is no guardrail protecting the careless adventurer from falling into the void here; watch every step.

This area of Geno Dome features much of the same flashing red and yellow lighting found all over, illuminating the dingy metal that comprises the entire building.  There are several large pipes set into the wall to the east, along with a ring of sparkling lights, indicating a save point.  Two doors are set into the north wall, one to the elevator and the other to a hallway.  The current room continues south, to some turret fixtures.

The floor is covered in shrapnel and old metal parts that were once used in Geno Dome's time of production.  Some sort of electronically sealed door is in this room.  A warm green glow emits from under the floor grates here, almost as if something radioactive was buried in this place.  Fully operational surveilance cameras are hanging from the ceiling, moving back and forth to record all movements in the area.

rooms.name: The end of the conveyor belt

userData.LongDescription: The conveyor belt comes to an end where the cold metal floors begin.  A massive door can be seen just north of here, leading into Geno Dome.  The sound of robots actively moving around the dome can be heard echoing through the long steel corridors.  Angry robots spread throughout the area to protect their home from enemy intrusion.

rooms.name: A lonely room made of scaffold

userData.LongDescription: The conveyor room opens up into more darkness and squeaky scaffold.  The area here is only a few feet across, with a dusty, opened treasure chest along the wall.  The scaffold touches all walls, but the only visible door is to the north.

The metal floor comes to an end at a massive steel door.  It is electronically opened and shut, with a small panel to the left of it.  The robots are even more abundant within the dome.  Going the opposite way on the conveyor belt does not appear to be possible because of the speed at which it is spinning.  The only obvious exit would be the door.

Finally coming to an end, the sections of metal that make up the corridor squeak underfoot in a most uncomfortable way, luckily there is a door to the north which may lead to more solid ground.  The sounds of machinery penetrate through the door, giving you some clue what to expect on the other side.  More unsteady scaffold is to the south.

Some sort of sparkling chest can be seen to the north, but it is very well guarded by this robot.  It mimics actions exactly to the left and right, removing any chance at getting past it.  To the north, there is a dead end, with no other obvious exits.

The catwalk from the south has grown into a real corridor, slightly lessening the danger of taking a wrong step and plummeting through the darkness of Geno Dome.  Small sections of scaffold link the corridor to the eastern wall, bridging a small gap over thin air.  The corridor continues northwards, to a door.

The metal floor narrows down to just about the size of a human to fit through.  A water pipe above has a small leak and is every so often dripping onto the floor, making a small puddle.  A lot of safety warnings and signs are on the walls, as well as an old faded map of the floor.

rooms.name: In front of a big steel door

userData.LongDescription: This large area goes in all four directions, east and west to some glowing circles of unknown origin.  A really big steel door is here, closed to prevent unauthorized access into Mother Brain's room.  The dark grey floor back down the steps can barely be seen from this room.

This room is a four way intersection.  To the northwest, a door with a bright red light can be seen.  To the east, there is a massive wall with a giant computer screen on it.  To the south is the main corridor of Geno Dome, and to the north there is a wall with three switches on it.  A maze of pipes and electrical wires covers the ceiling, splitting in all directions.

Glowing yellow lights on the floor are the only indication that this area is of any particular importance, though what exactly remains unclear.  There is a low wall in place beside a great void to the west, keeping robots from slipping on any of the piles of goo around here and sailing over the edge.  The dark grey paneled floors extend to the east and north.

Small lights are imbedded into the ground, flashing with a green illumination.  Far to the north, a door can be seen.  Some old broken laser motion sensor alarms are on the walls, but are obviously out of service now.  Some broken blue floor tiles line the sides of the path.

This small storage room could concievably be used as a holding cell with the laser forcefield set into the exit, but seems to be unused for the moment.  A chest lies against some pipes bolted to the west wall, and an uncharismatic puddle of green goo lies in the northeast corner.  The only exit is to the south.

The northern wall of this room is covered in old, broken switches.  Occasionally, a light will flicker on one, because of a few loose wires rubbing against each other.  Pieces of old levers and switches scatter the floor, creating small piles of rubble in some places.

This room is very simple.  It has three walls, one of which is a giant computer.  The computer takes up the whole wall, from floor to ceiling.  Some microphones are lining the perimeter of the screen, to allow voice activated sensors.  Some white text is on the screen, giving instructions on using the device.

This inner sanctum controls all of Geno Dome through a huge artificial intelligence, called Mother Brain.  The room containing 'her' is covered in flashing lights, with brightly pulsing oval-shaped holoprojectors on the ground, and three displays on the north wall, which display something that seems to be random data.  The only way out is to the south.

Far to the north, a door can be seen, which probably leads to the main floor of Geno Dome.  The belt begins to spin faster, and more robot fiends appear to protect their territory from intrusion.  The whole place is beginning to look like a technological nightmare.

This hall is filled with blinking lights, with stripes of glowing red material placed at regular intervals across the floor.  The steadily blinking lights here seem to indicate nothing at all, except perhaps the dome's alert status.  The floor's surface is an unremarkable mesh, swept clean by maintenance robots and untrammeled by organic life.  The hallway turns to normal steel floors again once through a door to the north.

The blue light source is very visible. There is a glistening blue object down the ladder, laying on the floor. A few stairs mark the northern path, where a small conveyor belt can be seen. Yellow caution lines and directional safety arrows line the walls of the path in this room.

This room is an old storage unit for Geno Dome.  There are lots of shelves and boxes, but they are all empty.  A small table is seen on the distant north wall, recently cleaned off.  A few hand trucks and hammers are lined up neatly along a wall, as well as some some other miscellaneous tools.

This room is very barren except for the north wall.  There are three pod structures in the wall, which appear to be some sort of assembly area.  There is a small plaque over each pod, with a bar code number on them.  Small pipes run along the perimeter of the room, providing electricity for the assembly of robots.

A large computer and space-age monitor cover the outside wall of the killing machine, facing towards the center of the room.  The same regular interval of screams can be heard here as the conveyor keeps rolling.  The beginning and end of the conveyor are to the west and east, respectively. A doorway out can be seen in either direction.

This small claustrophobic chamber features four glowing ovals of light on the ground, which function as an elevator.  It is illuminated by these and several other lights in the room, whose purpose is unknown.  The wall to the north pulses slightly with power from the Dome, in two tall stripes of oscillating red light.  A doorway leads out to the first level of Geno Dome.

One of the wonders of advanced technology does not seem to be windows, as this stark room demonstrates.  The walls are made of dull grey metal, featured only by dents in its surface and the glowing lights so common in the interior of the dome.  Two charging stations for robots flank the door here, along with a pair of turrets.  The door behind them features two very impressive metal bars across it, just as most of the other doors here.  To the south a glowing red hallway is visible.

The elevators in Geno Dome are of the same standard design, four glowing ovals of light on the ground sense when passengers are present.  The soft light cast by these reveals that the rest of the room is stark, panels and slits in the walls are the only features.  A doorway leads out to the second level of Geno Dome.

The area here is surrounded in flashing yellow lights, making the area much more brightly lit than previous ones.  Several turret mounts have been placed here, apparently to guard something important beyond.  To the north, a huge metal door is shut tight, while to the south more of the dome beckons.

This room appears at first glance to be a production facility, by the large conveyor belt and monitoring equipment above it, but very soon its purpose is revealed to be much, much more sinister than that.  A huddled, unmoving human dressed only in rags appears on the conveyor belt, disappearing into a small enclosed machine in the center of this room.  The person lets out a terrible scream soon after they disappear into the opening, and a minute later another person meets the same fate in the killing machine.  The steps leading up to the conveyor are guarded by a powerful electric field, but perhaps another way to save the people can be found to the east, at the controls for the machine.

This small conveyor belt that was intentionally put here to help transport large objects easily around Geno Dome.  Some sort of dropoff into an underground storage area is at the end of this belt, but the space is far too small for any person to fit through.  A split path going left and right is visible to the north.

Some broken wall panels expose the electrical interiors of Geno Dome.  Metal grate floors and chain railings surround all of the walkways.  Some bright blue light is illuminating the area from the East, enveloping the area in an iridescent blue glow.  The light appears to be coming from some sort of ventilation shaft.

The cobbled road through town loops around to the east, passing the armor and weapon shops before heading back to the town's entrance. Water wheels churn the water that flows under the town, keeping it from becoming stagnant. The weapon shop is to the north, and the road east leads past a central water wheel to the armor shop.

As the road continues towards the northern end of town, it passes under one end of the large building that houses the inn. The sun can not reach the midst of the passageway, and so a damp darkness chills the area. Bright light can be seen to the north and south. The faint sound of water rushing underneath the town echoes faintly through the tunnel.

This part of town is the closest Worus has to a town center. To the south is the bridge that goes over the moat and out of town. A massive building runs the width of the town, housing residences as well as a few shops. The town's inn lies directly ahead, while roads to the east and west eventually head north towards the shops.

The sound of splashing water rings through the area. Waterwheels of all sizes are turned by the swiftly moving water that flows around and under the shops and other buildings. Just ahead is a small building with a sign proclaiming it to be the armor shop. To the west is a shop selling armor. Citizens of the town wander through the streets, enjoying a gentle breeze. The exit back into the wilderness is southward, as is the inn.

Tucked into the far north end of Worus is the armor shop. An older man stands behind the counter, ready to serve his customers. Behind him, a fire roars in a stone hearth. The warm glow from the flames bathes the shop in a dim, ruddy light. There are no windows to provide more light, and the smell of smoke permeates the room. The shopkeeper sells a few different types of armor that might be of use.

Just inside the inn is this little item shop. Vials and crates of all sorts of useful supplies line the walls behind the counter. The warmth from the fire back in the inn reaches this small shop, keeping the chill away. A shopkeeper looks up over the counter, startled after being absorbed in his work. The only exit is back into the inn.

A bridge overlooking the moat leads off to the east. Woods begin to close in on the narrowing path, and less of the sunlight is getting through the leaves overhead. A cool breeze rustles through the trees, and the birds twitter softly as they go about their business. The path leads back towards the town to the west, and east it ventures further into the forest.

A warm, welcoming feeling permeates the atmosphere of this inn. A bright fire is crackling in the hearth beside the counter, giving off a welcome dry heat in this eternally damp town and warming the beds for weary travelers. The innkeeper stands behind a high wooden counter, whistling a little tune as he looks over his books. There is an item shop nearby, where necessary supplies can be purchased.

Only a small bit of sunlight can reach this far under the building above. This tunnel leads to the back of the building, which faces the north end of town. The passage is damp, as the sun can not reach the ground to dry it out. To the south is the entrance of town, and a small forest is visible to the southwest. Farther north, on the other side of the tunnel, are the shops.

rooms.name: The woods to the east of Worus.

userData.LongDescription: The path, completely surrounded by the trees on either side, turns towards the north here. The dense vegetation makes it difficult for the light of the sun to reach the pathway, leaving travelers to find their way in a musty darkness. A breeze occasionally rustles the leaves overhead, causing the little bit of light that makes it through to shiver and dance. A small clearing can be seen to the north.

The deep moat that surrounds Worus continues here, heading to the north and east. The view to the south is of the water and the distant road out of town. Worus Castle is just barely visible over the moat to the west. The road continues north, winding under a second story made into a bridge between two buildings, and towards the shops.

The road continues north and east here. The northern path passes under bridge between the inn and another part of the large building as it heads for the shops. The road east disappears into the woods just outside of the town proper. The moat that surrounds Worus is wide and deep, protecting the town from unwanted trespassers. Far to the south, the road out of town is visible.

The pathway deadends into a little clearing. In the center of the clearing rests a small building with a sign in the window. Thick ivy has grown up the walls of the building, finding plenty of footholds in the old, cracked walls. The forest around the clearing is too dense to walk through, leaving the southern path towards the village as the only exit.

Water surrounds the gentle, quiet town of Worus, protecting it from the wild beasts in the surrounding countryside. One of the many bridges over Worus's waterways leads further north, towards the inn at the center of the town. Water laps softly at the heavy stone pilings that support the weight of the bridge. The road appears to fork in the distance.

The doorway opens into a room much darker than the outside roads through town. Just enough of the glaring sun from outside shines in to show that this is a weapon shop. The shopkeeper himself is just ahead, standing behind a wooden counter. Above his head is a pair of polished crossed swords.

The massive central water wheels of the town tower above everything else. They help to circulate the water around and under the town, preventing the channels from becoming stagnant. Any noise that anyone might be making is drowned out by the sound of water crashing down from the wheels just above. The road, slippery from the cool spray of water that is continually thrown into the air by the wheels, leads east, toward the armor shop, and to the weapon shop, west of here.

This cafe is large and spacious. White tables with fancy chairs are placed around in a large area for customers. Along the northern section is a long counter, filled with food and an attendant behind a cash register. A kitchen is towards the back, though only staff personnel can enter.

This is the center of Porre. Cobblestone roads stretch out in different directions, particularly in the four main cardinal directions. To the north is the inn and the store outlet. The tavern is to the east, the mayor's house lies to the west and the ferries are to the south.

This inn is one of the finest in all of Porre. Red, lush carpets roll along the ground, covering it. Marble pillars support the ceiling, and lamps emit a yellowish glow to the room, adding to the luxurious atmosphere. To the west end is a long hall leading into separate private guest rooms. A sign is placed right next to the receptionist desk.

rooms.name: By the Porre Inn and shops

userData.LongDescription: A fine road made out of stone lines the pathways of Porre village. Buildings with green rooftiles are placed around, each serving its own purpose. In particular is the inn, a large two-story building on the northern end of town, and right next to it, a flashy-looking hut with glass windows showcasing weapons and other sorts of merchandise.

The natural path leads in two directions from here; north and east. A large cathedral-like building can be seen in that same direction; it looks almost divine, located in the heart of the forest. Large trees form an almost psychological barrier, keeping most travelers on the main path and out of the wilderness of the forest.

This is the great bridge that spans the channel between Porre and Truce. Large, long logs are placed and tied together with thick rope. The Guardia and Porre crests can be seen on the railings in a wooden design. The water below laps and overlaps gently as the wind blows through.

This house just seems to be the pinnacle of luxury. Carpets roll along the ground, exquisite and exotic in their own right. The walls are made out of cut marble, nearly wrapped in fine tapestry. All the furniture seems to be expensive and good quality, almost crossing the line of good taste into gaudiness. A large staircase leads up to the second floor.

This long pier is one of many piers that make up the Porre harbor. The ferry is docked here, ready to take adventurers all the way up north to Truce. No ticket office is in sight, though, it appears that the ferry is a free service. Back to the north is the town center.

This large building is shaped much like a cathedral, probably showing praise to some God or magnificent being. The walls are made out of limestone, carved smooth. The rooftiles are painted blue, and the elegant design really shows. The building looks fairly new, like it was erected by people of this age, not long ago. A grand set of double doors serve as the entrance to the place. To the south is a short path that leads into the village of Porre.

rooms.name: South end of the Zenan Bridge

userData.LongDescription: This is the southern end of the Zenan Bridge, and the northwestern corner of the Porre continent. Most of the continent is wrapped in the beauty of trees, with one straight path leading adventurers and the sort through safely to the village of Porre. Mountains are on the northern border of the land.

rooms.name: A bedroom in the Mayor's house

userData.LongDescription: This large bedroom is simply grandeur. A large king-sized bed rests against the back wall, with long red curtains to hide the actual bed. The floor is a fine, lush carpet that stretches all over. A large door-like window is to the northern wall, with a balcony with a good view of the beach and the seas.

The house of the Mayor of Porre is simply large and elegant. It must have cost him a fortune to build. Two stories high, this wide house is made out of a granite stone, with fine wood in between as supporting pillars. Glass windows are dotted about, and the style of the house is simply marvelous. To the east is the village center.

This shop is well stocked and kept. Weapons are finely stocked on racks against the wall, polished to a luminous shine. Armor pieces are placed in a neat stack, and against the back wall is an impressive array of medicine vials, in a glass cabinet. The shopkeeper flutters about, looking busy.

This cathedral-like building is large, calming, and serene. The floors and walls are a bluish tint, with a greyish carpet leading up to what seems to be a circular stone pod. A large rectangular stained-glass window is placed high above, letting blue light pass through into the room, surrounding the pod with the glow. A sign hangs on the wall.

This is a typical house in Porre Village. The floor is made of refined stone tiles, a bit cold on the bare feet. The walls are a fine stone, grey in color. A table stands in the center of the room, with wooden chairs as a set. A couch is on one end of the room, with what seems to be a television set in a corner.

This is a small road before a building that looks much like a cafe. Large glass windows are placed on the walls with the cafe logo, a red and white symbol with the words 'SNAIL STOP' on it. A plaque version of the symbol also hangs above the doorway, with a mat with the word WELCOME on it.

This is the entrance of the village, marked by a wooden gate and a small sign. The path leads further down to the east, where several buildings are visible. Trees are all around, nearly like walls as an addition to the path. To the north is a small path leading to a cathedral-like building.

The control center of Lunatic Pandora glows with a soft purple light. The ceiling has a jagged metal formation pointing down towards the helm controls, which are on an elevated platform. At the front of the room is an enormous view screen that circles around the helm. Smooth metal walls diverge from the helm, eventually connecting back at the exit on the south wall.

This is a large semicircular chamber with three massive pillars. Each pillar is a dark blue with different trim colors, and has a door at the base leading into the deeper portions of Lunatic Pandora. At the center of the base of the semicircle is a stairwell leading down towards the entrance hatch.

This hallway in Lunatic Pandora is cut directly out of crystal. Streaks of green and blue mix throughout the crystal walls, and they glow faintly. The hallway continues to a junction at the north end, and at the south end hits a corner that turns east. A small niche in the western wall has been cut out, though whatever was in it has long since been looted.

rooms.name: Lunatic Pandora: Transport to Landing Deck

userData.LongDescription: A long yellow tube connects an elevator to the primary landing deck on Lunatic Pandora. Dim lights glow along the walkway, and a long pipe runs along the top of the tube glowing faintly. At the west end of the tube is the elevator leading to the main section of Lunatic Pandora, while to the east is a doorway leading to the landing area for smaller ships.

rooms.name: Lunatic Pandora: Before the Control Room

userData.LongDescription: A metal bridge connects the crystalline hallway to the control room. A large circular frame surrounds the door leading into the main control room, where Lunatic Pandora is piloted from. Dozens of cables can be seen running into the wall above the circular frame. To the south is the crystalline hallway.

This part of Lunatic Pandora is made entirely out of a strange crystal. It is streaked with veins of green and blue, and pulses with a faint light. At the end of the hall to the east is an elevator leading down. To the west, the hallway continues before turning north around a corner.

A crossroad junction connects the crystal and the metal sections of Lunatic Pandora. The walls are a dull blue-green, with little of the light seen elsewhere in the crystalline structure. A large hole in the tunnel floor blocks passage to the west, and an elevator is embedded in the northern crystal wall. To the east, a metal tunnel extends away from the elevator, while a ladder leads down into the crystalline structure.

The landing deck of Lunatic Pandora could easily fit hundreds of fighter ships. Dozens of openings leading back into the main area can be seen, each separated by enormous steel fire barricades. A short set of stairs leads down to the landing zone, which is currently blocked by a steel wall. The opening to the west leads into the main body of Lunatic Pandora

rooms.name: Lunatic Pandora: End of the Ravine

userData.LongDescription: A ravine in the crystal ends here, with a slightly rusty ladder leading up and out of the chasm. A metal circle is embedded on the east wall, providing structural support for the crystal wall. To the west, the ravine curves around and out of sight. The crystal walls glow bright green this deep in the crystalline section of Lunatic Pandora.

A long metal tube connects a sealed external hatch to the interior of Lunatic Pandora. The tube has translucent yellow crystal running along the sides, allowing a view into the deep chasm that separates the deeper interior of the structure from the external shell. The exit hatch at the east end has been sealed shut, and the west end of the tunnel opens into a crystal pathway

A long flight of stairs connects the entryway hatch to the main portion of Lunatic Pandora. Panels on either side of the stairwell glow with a pulsing red light. At the top of the stairs a large room can be seen, while at the bottom is the hatch leading out of Lunatic Pandora.

The ravine has three small chambers carved out along the northern wall. Each chamber has a metal frame built into the wall to provide structural support. They appear to have been emptied of whatever they may have contained long ago. To the west, the end of the ravine can be seen, and to the east the ravine continues on around a gentle bend around the crystal walls.

The walls of the ravine seem to rise up endlessly. The walls, being made of the same crystal throughout Lunatic Pandora, are impossible to climb. The area is filled with a blue-green glow coming from the crystal all around. In the middle of the floor, a deep hole that would have otherwise been impassable has been filled with a large boulder. To the east, the end of the ravine can just barely be seen, while to the west the ravine continues on.

rooms.name: Lunatic Pandora: End of the Ravine

userData.LongDescription: The end of the crystal ravine turns into a short tunnel with a steel frame at the end. It appears that something of value used to be stored at this end. The tunnel glows faintly with a blue-green light. A thin strip of lighting has been strung along the top of the tunnel, though the ambient lighting from the crystal seems more than sufficient. To the east, the ravine runs around a slight bend in the crystal.

You stand before Lunatic Pandora, a giant weapon created during the first Sorceress War. It is shaped like a massive obelisk, and made out of a smooth, light purple metal. Lights glow along the side where bands of obsidian streak through the wall. A small hatch appears to be the only entry point into the massive building

A long narrow bridge runs across a deep chasm, connecting the crystalline structure to the metallic part of Lunatic Pandora.
