Hundreds of beams of light can be seen coming out of the metal structure and going into the crystal, somehow holding the two together. A ring of blue and red lights sits at the end of the bridge on the metal side. It appears that it leads out of the structure, but the exit has been sealed shut.

A T-intersection connects the crystal hallways in this part of Lunatic Pandora. Structural rings made of a golden material support the connections on the north and east, while the crystalline hallway runs open to the south. The walls glow with a pale green and golden color.

The only light in the heart of the meteor is emanated by a radiant green panel in the middle of the floor. The light swirls and wavers, causing the roughly carved walls of the meteor to shimmer. The only other exit beside the strange green panel is the door in the northern wall, through which daylight can be seen.

A huge meteor has crashed to a landing here, plowing through the otherwise featureless plains. The only other interruptions of the rolling grass are the occasional glimpse of trees and ocean in the distance. A warm breeze teases and ripples the grass around the massive rock while the sun beats down from above. Oddly, the faint smell of the ocean that is on the breeze is mingled with the scent of fire and charred wood, though no smoke or fire is visible.

Beams of light from outside shine through the arched entrance, making the rough hewn corridor visible. The weight of the heavy stone is palpable as it presses down. The passage curls around the inner perimeter and a doorway leading towards the center of the meteor is just barely visible in the dim light. A strange green glow emanates from the northern doorway.

The common, feathered friend known as the chocobo comes in abundance. Some of said birds rest behind a large stable made of dark brown wood. The floor is made of flat, tiled stone, and half of it is covered in bright yellow hay to accomodate the chocobos' needs. A counter on the west side of the room signifies where one can go to rent one of those birds to ride.

rooms.name: In Front of the Chocobo Rental

userData.LongDescription: The path of grass in front of the Chocobo Rental Shop is relatively narrow. Navigating outside of the short wooden fence that encircles the rental place to the west seems difficult. It leads to an untraversable stretch of land between two small rivers that go their separate ways. Inside the fence, the lawn is spruced up with a few patches of bright pink flowers. Chocobos from the inside are warking loud enough to be heard outside.

This stretch of the grass pathway spreads out in many different directions, as it is the center of the village. Directly north of the path is a small, tranquil pond, and buildings are visible in all other directions. Some delinquent children seem to be swimming around in the pond to the north.

Corrugated wooden slats have been layered along the walls of the tiny room. Two ducts, installed near the ceiling on the southern wall, likely carry the music from the piano into the pub. A large, old piano takes up the northern end of the room and begs to be played.

Rugor's Pub seems to be decorated with the intent of hosting a lively scene. Framed pictures of B-list celebrities hang all across the north wall. The floor is made of stone, and on it, a few tables are scattered about, where likely social gatherings would take place. On the west side of the room is a counter where a barkeep serves beverages, and on the east side of the room is an empty stage, with stairs leading up to it. There is a small, wooden sign next to the stage.

This side of the store is where armor is sold, and the weapons are sold on the other side. The two stores are divided by a wooden counter. The walls are painted an ivory color, accented by wooden framework that supports the roof. The floor is made of a rocky, gray, and uneven stone pattern. Behind the large armor counter are a few stands of shiny new armor.

A narrow, but sturdy wooden bridge entangled in bright green ivy has been made here to serve as an entrance to the village of Rugor. Crystal clear water constantly flows in the underpass as part of a quaint stream. Tranquil sounds from the slowly moving river muffle the sounds of the villagers of Rugor moving about their daily business.

This path consists entirely of grass and natural contours of the land. The armor, and weapon shops, whose roofs are bright blue, are visible, almost directly side by side. The tranquil sounds of the river flowing underneath the wooden bridge to the south are still audible as well. Villagers doing their shopping and other business pass through this path frequently.

rooms.name: In Front of the Item Shop

userData.LongDescription: The path of grass in front of the Item Shop is quite spacious and open. To the east, a wooden fence propped up between a stream and a cliff marks the border of the city. The building itself, with its cerulean roof, rests in the cliffs to the north, but since it is not symmetrical, one of the sides comes down almost to the ground, making the entire building look lopsided.

This building contains both a weapon store and an armor store, but only one store can be accessed at a time due to a large wooden counter in the middle of the room, separating the two. The walls are painted an ivory color, accented by wooden framework that supports the roof. The floor is made of a rocky, uneven stone pattern that is quite difficult to walk on. Behind the large weapon counter are a few racks of unsold weaponry.

The area outside the inn is a spacious path of bright, green grass. Underneath a balcony of the inn is a fenced off portion of grass where a lone sheep walks about to and fro. The inn itself looks rather grand, its blue roof stretching high above any other building in the village. Next to the entrance of the building, there are a few crates and barrels that supply the grand inn with copius amounts of food and beverages.

The interior of the inn is decorated with a shade of dusty beige paint and slightly rotten framework for an accent. The ceiling stretches extremely high, but the paint only rises up to about the second storey, exposing bare walls and giving the inn a very unfinished or lazy look. At the entrance there is a set of stairs that forcefully carries anyone entering onto a wooden platform that covers the entire floor. As for furniture, the grand inn is furnished with a small table with three chairs, and four beds stowed away on the east side of the room. Considering the large appearance of the outside, the inside seems inappropriately small and empty.

The walls of this building are painted a soothing cream color, and the floor is of a dark gray stone pattern. A large wooden counter encircles the area in which one enters to help guard against theft. Behind the counter, various items like a bookcase filled with trinkets, some barrels, and some gray cauldrons are visible.

A serene looking lake rests slightly below and to the east. At the edge of the land, a small picket fence is propped up, with several caution signs painted near it. There is a decently large garden that is decorated with bright pink flowers and dark green stems. The grandiose inn can be seen far to the west as well.

A large building with a sign on it reading, "Beginner Hall" stands here. Unfortunately there seem to be many old men picketing outside of the building, complaining that they are not receiving enough pay for their services. They appear to be blocking the entrance to the building, not letting anyone pass. The flowers around the walkway have been trampled by these formerly helpful sages in the midst of their protest. The walkway leads both east and north.

The bedroom is quite large, having room for more than one person to sleep. There is a king sized bed, large bookshelves, a table to eat at and stools that surround it. A large area rug with a picture depicting a tiger laying in some grass is on the floor. A glowing ball is embedded into the wall, providing its own light without fire.

The upstairs area of the pub houses two large rooms that patrons may rent. This section is a large hallway that leads to the two bedrooms. The floor is freshly waxed, giving the wood a nice luster. Two high quality lamps sit atop a table, lighting the hallway.

An odd smell wafts through the air of Tule's Item Shop. It is a mixture of various herbs and spices. Many vials of liquid hang from the wall, with small labels beneath them to designate what each one is. An older woman stands behind the counter. She points to a sign below her and smiles.

The Tule inn is comfortably decorated with large beds and tables. The fireplace crackles with intense heat, filling the room with warmth. A woman stands behind the counter, smiling and waving at anyone who comes into the business. A small cat lounges in the middle of the floor, not being disturbed by anything in the room. There is a door in the back of the room, and beside it, a small sign that says "Tule Item Shop".

Zokk's mansion is very elegantly decorated. A large crystal chandelier hangs from the ceiling, illuminating the large sitting room. There are two couches with footstools at the end of them, used for sitting or reclining when tired. Another room extends off of the sitting room. A stone fireplace with a crackling fire is against the north wall, and a small man in some green robes is standing there, observing everything. Why don't you say 'hi' to him?

The northernmost building in Tule is the grand mansion. This building is lived in by a single sage, Zokk. It's quite tall, with a low fence surrounding the property. All of the windows are neatly washed, the upkeep on the paint is immaculate. The entryway into the building is a lattice archway, covered in ivy leaves.

This is the Armor Shop. Many varieties of decorative armors hang on the walls everywhere.  There is a young man here taking care of the shop, and he points to a sign as you enter.  The only exit is the door that leads back into the town.

rooms.name: The Village of Tule - A Bridge

userData.LongDescription: This is a wide, wooden bridge that spans the river running through Tule. It covers the path between the mansion and the other areas of town. The planks are in high maintenance, with none of them being loose or missing. A large sign is on the northern side.

An unusual shop, with an assortment of swords and other weapons hanging from wall to wall.  Most of them look simply built, but they will get the job done.  At the front desk, a young lady in unusual clothes sharpens a small sword, seemingly absorbed in her task.  Without bothering to look up, she points to a sign on the counter.

A building once stood here. It has been ravaged by flames recently, leaving the entire area a large mess of ashes and fallen down boards. The frame of the house still stands, although wobbly. People who walk by the area keep their heads down, not looking at the wreck of the business that was previously here.

The bedroom is quite large, having room for more than one person to sleep. There is a king sized bed, large bookshelves, a table to eat at and stools that surround it. A large area rug with a picture depicting a wolf laying in some snow is on the floor. A glowing ball is embedded into the wall, providing its own light without fire.

Zokk's bedroom is quite sparsely decorated. A small bed rests in the corner, with a small pair of slippers tucked underneath it. There is a medium sized bookshelf on the west wall, holding his most important books. Two chairs with high backs rest in the corner, with a woven rug between them.

The northwest corner of Tule is covered by many flowers. Children can be seen playing in a small field, surrounded by a fence. A lone armor shop stands here, open for business. There is a large line of trees blocking access to the river from this point, as it is a danger for the children of the village to play around it.

The pub in Tule is comprised of one large room. A wooden bar rests on the back wall, being tended by an older man. There is a stage in the northern corner which can be used for dancing and a piano sits on the far end of it. A fireplace sits to the left of the stage, providing heat to the bar customers. Many tables, surrounded by chairs sit in the room. Pirates seem to patronize this bar frequently, as there is seven of them sitting at the various tables, making a lot of noise. A set of stairs leads to the upstairs rooms.

The entrance to the village of Tule is lined on both sides with large spruce, pine and cedar trees. There is an abundant amount of flowers dotting the outskirts of the walkways as well. The buildings are made with white brick and the roof of each is shingled in red. The sounds of people going about their daily business can be heard from all around.

A large building stands here with several banners on it stating, 'Grand Opening'. There is a sign on it depicting a harp, indicating what the shop sells. A large statue of a bard stands outside of the building, carved out of marble. The flower beds are arranged around the building in a way that it depicts a picture of a harp as well. There is a wooden bridge that spans the Tule river, and also leads to a large mansion on the other bank. The walkway leads to the bridge and west.

An inn stands in the southeastern corner of Tule. Many trees surround the area, providing plenty of shade. The flowers seem especially bright in this part of town. A walkway leads north, towards a rather large mansion. The other walkway leads west, towards the town entrance. A few birds fly around the area, watching for any food that gets dropped on the ground.

This is the wooden pier where the pirates' ship is docked. Its planks are stable enough to hold a large amount of weight. The ship looks like it could survive quite the storm on the sea and would still remain afloat. There are no forms of sails on the ship.

The cave extends both east and through the doorway. To the southeast, there is a pile of large rocks with a small space between them and the ceiling. It looks as if another doorway once stood there. A makeshift bridge has been built across the large crevice in the eastern floor, making a walkway for someone to cross.

This is the entryway to the pirate lair. It appears as if the entire lair has been dug out of the stone. The chiseled look of the walls stands out quite nicely. There are numerous pirate flags adorning them, showing grinning white skulls with crossbones underneath.

The humidity has dropped, making the cave quite cool. The lights that are embedded into the granite emit a dim glow. There are a few bats hanging from the ceiling now, apparently sleeping. A short distance to the north, there appears to be a doorway.

This appears to be a dead end. An empty treasure chest sits on the ground, picked clean by whoever last raided it. There are a few flags adorning the walls, and a real skeleton is hanging on the western wall, chained up in shackles.

The walls in this area are quite far apart, giving the room an open feeling. The ceiling has a few dangerously sharp stalactites hanging from it, that could easily crush the skull of a careless traveller if they were to fall. The lights seem a little brighter than normal at this point, illuminating the area and making shadows bounce off the spikey rocks above.

This is the main area of the Pirate Lair. To the east there is a large pier to dock incoming ships. There are two separate doors on the northern wall, leading to other parts of the hideout. There are no pirates around this section. Judging from the sounds coming from all around, they appear to be nearby.

The walls of this belowdecks room are lined with large wooden shipping crates. There are two lamps hanging on the walls, pouring light into the small room. A small table is in the corner, although there are no chairs anywhere to be seen. The smell of oranges and other citrus fruit wafts through the air.

This is the barracks of the pirate lair. There are many bunk beds lining the walls, complete with plenty of loud, snoring pirates sleeping in them. There is a large table in the center of the floor, that has numerous plates and sets of cutlery on it. Many chairs surround the table as well.

There are many empty shelves and bags in which gold was held in this room. There is a large amount of dust and cobwebs covering this place, showing that the room has not been used for anything important for some time. Some lazy pirates are in here sleeping so that they don't have to work.

This ship is used to transport between various areas near the pirate lair. The vessel is completely crafted from balsam wood, making it durable and buoyant. The crew is performing their daily tasks on deck. They don't pay attention to anything other than their jobs though. No one is at the wheel of the ship, and it doesn't look like it'll be going anywhere.

This room splits off in three directions, two ways leading into deeper into the cave and one going to the entrance. The walls in this section seem damp and cold to the touch. To the north is a doorway. It's rather difficult to see what is on the other side of it.

The walls of the cave appear to be closing in, making the area seem slightly narrow. There is a doorway in the north wall that leads deeper into the cave. There aren't many rodents that can be seen, but some small scratching noises can be heard.

This is the southeastern corner of the pirate lair. It seems that there are quite a few pirates in the area, although they appear to be sleeping instead of keeping watch. There is an excellent view of a small inlet where the pirate ship can dock, although it is unreachable from this point in the cave. The ship appears to be at the dock right now.

This is the captain's quarters. A large bed lies in the corner of the room, covered with many thick warm blankets. There are four lamps hanging on the walls, providing more than enough light to see. A table sits in the middle of the room, with a chair on both sides of it. A chest is in the back corner of the room, heavily locked.

The ceiling slopes to roughly eight feet in height here. It is fairly smooth, with no stalactites showing. Instead, a smooth stone surface is showing from all sides. There appears to be no exit other than west, but a small button sits on the northern wall, hinting that there could be more.

A dark cave stretches out north. A few large gaps are in the ground, making the area almost impassible. There are small walkways that could be used to bypass them. It is very humid inside the cave. Some odd looking lights have been embedded into the granite shedding light on the ground, and outlining where the pitfalls are. There are a few small rodents scurrying along the floor.

rooms.name: A Spring in the Pirate Cave

userData.LongDescription: There is a large freshwater spring bubbling up from the ground. A few small fish can be seen swimming in it, but nothing else. There are no other forms of life in the spring. This water looks like it is good enough to drink. A few bats cling to the ceiling.

This is a small room just below the deck's surface.  Barren of almost any furnishings, a lonely oil lamp hangs from a wall, illuminating the area. Two large wooden doors can be soon, both leading towards the north.

The majestic Bal Castle rises up visibly above the high stone wall that surrounds it.  Flags fly from the top of the wall.  Wind drakes circle the castle high in the air, some riderless and others mounted by soldiers.  A moat, diverted from a small river, surrounds the castle to help protect it.

The western end of the massive structure known as the Big Bridge is marked by a large, stone building, built partway onto the bridge itself from the Bal continent.  The brown-tiled peaks of two towers rise above either side of the building, while a single door set into the building's wall allows for entry.  Two torches burn at either side of the door.  The bridge extends into the distance to the east, over the ocean.

The bridge continues both east and west here, the span seemingly endless.  Cracked stones and cuts scar the bridge's surface, as well as the walls on either side.  The ocean can be seen stretching off to the north and south, a cool breeze blowing across the bridge from the ocean air.

Waist-high walls stand at either side of the Big Bridge as it extends into the distance both east and west across the vast, seemingly endless ocean.  A large section of the bridge's surface here is black and cracked.

A small island can be seen in the distance to the east, its low mountains rising up from the ocean beneath the bridge as it continues beyond the horizon.  To the west, the bridge continues to stretch over seemingly endless ocean.  The walls rising on either side of the bridge still allow an excellent view of the ocean beyond.

The bridge continues onward, with no visible end towards either the east or west.  The walls on either side allow a view of the ocean beyond, though the wall to the north is riddled with small holes.  Many of the stones are cracked or broken, and a large crack is visible along the length of the bridge for several feet.

This small room serves as a checkpoint, and is designed to limit travel.  The walls are sparsely decorated, with only banners on the north and south walls adding any color.  Two columns partition the room further and allow the room to be more easily secured.  A door stands in a small recess in both the east and west walls, allowing entry into or out of the checkpoint.

A small island lies under the bridge, a ring of mountains with a temple of some sort in the center.  The support pillars on the bridge seemingly extend deep into the island itself, rising up to break the walls at the sides of the bridge.  A rope hanging down from one of the walls offers a means to reach the island temple below.  The bridge extends far to the east, while to the west, a door opens into a stone building of some sort.

This small room serves as a security checkpoint, and currently stands bare aside from two columns near the center of the room.  The walls are unadorned, save for a pair of banners.  Matching doors set into the east and west walls allow passage in or out.

This section of the bridge appears to be near the center.  The bridge extends off into the distance to the west, while to the east a small stone building stands upon the bridge, a single iron door allowing entrance.  The stone walls to the sides continue, broken only by the support pillars extending below.  A small island of mostly low mountains, with what appears to be a temple visible in the center, is visible below the bridge.

This section of bridge shows fewer signs of battle than the others, but still is marred by the fighting that took place long ago.  The stone walls to either side, wide enough to stand on, do nothing to hinder the view of the ocean beyond.  The round stone pillars that support the bridge interrupt the walls occasionally.  To the west, the bridge appears to pass over an island, while to the east it continues to stretch off into the distance.

The bridge continues over the ocean, stretching far to the east and west.  The wide walls to either side are short enough to allow a view of the ocean beyond.  Scorch marks and slashes mar the surface and walls of the bridge, but the great span remains intact.

The bridge has several broken stones, and scratches and burns mar it.  The walls that rise to either side of the bridge are mostly undamaged, but are not entirely unscathed.  The pathway extends off into the distance to the east, while to the west a stone structure can be seen standing at the end of the bridge.

The bridge continues to both the east and west, marred by the scars of battle, and a building is visible in the distance to the east.  Walls stand at both sides of the bridge, broken by rounded pillars on occasion.  Beyond the walls, the ocean extends in all directions.

This grassy field forms the tip of a small peninsula overlooking the ocean.  A stone checkpoint stands here, the building serving as an entrance to the Big Bridge.  A lit torch sits at either side of the door, while a tower rises at each corner of the checkpoint building, pointed roofs stretching above the checkpoint.

Stretching into the distance both westward and eastward, the Big Bridge stands high above the ocean below.  The walls and bridge both bear gashes and cracks in the stone.  Massive pillars rise from the ocean below, the supports joining with the walls at either side of the bridge.

The Big Bridge stands high above the ocean, extending off into the distance to both the east and west.  To the east, a small stone structure can be seen, taking up the width of the bridge, while below the bridge an island rises from the sea, not quite reaching the height of the bridge itself.

The Big Bridge is a truly massive construct, stretching to the west seemingly without end.  Waist-high stone walls stand at the sides of the bridge, broken only by the rounded tops of the pillars that support the massive structure.  Beyond the walls, the ocean extends for miles along the edges of the eastern continent.  A door opens to the checkpoint building to the east, and the pointed roof of a tower juts out above either side of the building.

The bridge continues to travel to the east and west here, with signs of battle visible.  Beyond the walls rising to either side, the monotony of the ocean is broken by the appearance of a small island to the west, directly underneath the bridge.

Continuing off towards the horizon both east and west, the Big Bridge truly lives up to its name.  Though the bridge, and the walls on either side, shows signs of battles having been fought, the structure is still as strong as ever.  The walls are partitioned by massive support pillars extending from the ocean's depths below.

The eastern entryway to the Big Bridge sits in a small grove of trees, an open path passing through the grove for easy access to the bridge itself.  Mountains rise to the east, blocking passage to the Tycoon continent.  A narrow trail leads into the mountains to the east, winding upwards.  A checkpoint stands at the end of the bridge, preventing any view of the bridge.  A torch burns to either side of the single doorway of the bridge's eastern checkpoint, and a small tower stands at either corner of the checkpoint itself, each spire just stretching beyond the height of the checkpoint's roof.

This small room was constructed as an added security point.  The room is empty, but bears signs indicating that a significant battle has taken place.  Gashes along the walls, scorch marks on the floor, and the shredded remains of what once were tapestries fill the room.  Doors lie within the walls to both the east and west.

A small entryway provides a glimpse of the interior of this castle.  The walls are a pale, fleshy color, and torches line them, mounted in what appear to be skulls.  Pillars at the corners of the walls are adorned with skulls as well, with the space between resembling skin stretched across bones.  The walls themselves seem to pulse regularly, as if the castle itself has a heartbeat all its own.  A large door to the south leads out of the castle, while a door to the north leads into a separate chamber.  The hallways to the northeast and northwest extend around the chamber.

The hallway here turns a corner, extending to the east and north.  An alcove opens to the west, near the northern end of the hallway, into a narrow path which leads to a bone staircase continuing deeper into the castle.  A torch flickers on the wall of the alcove, while the skulls decorating the pillars and walls seem to watch blindly from beneath a layer of pink flesh.

This narrow hallway runs to the north, where it opens to another hallway to the east and west.  It extends to the south, where it intersects with another hallway.  The brown, stone walls here are jagged, with the stone appearing to pierce through the fleshy, pink membrane that covers the ceiling, edges and base of the wall.  Pillars covered by the membrane stand at the corners of the walls, with skulls pushing against the pink substance as if trying to escape.

This room is long, and strikingly warm, with large pools of a thick, red liquid boiling at either end of the room.  The torches burning along the walls add to the heat of the room even as they offer light, while the room itself seems to quiver almost as if alive.  The only exit is a door, seemingly made of large, sharp teeth, that sits along the south wall.

A short, narrow hallway extends north and south, leading to a similar three-way intersection at each end.  The southern wall extends unbroken beyond the corners.  The northern end of the hall opens to the east, leading to a corner where the path turns north again, and to the west, where the hall branches off to the north and continues onward.  Jagged stone pierces through the pink flesh of the walls, and the skulls adorning the pillars seem to be locked in an agonized silent scream.

Running east to west, a narrow passage follows directly behind the large chamber that is the center of the castle's first floor.  The walls, pink and fleshy, pulse almost as if displaying the heartbeat of the castle itself.  The passage opens to a large room on either end, while a single door stands at the center of the northern wall.

A large cell stands in the northern section of this room, two gates made of what appear to be bone blocking it off from the hallway.  The pillars at the corners of the walls, separating the two gates, pulsate as if with the castle's heartbeat.  The brown, jagged stone walls are distinctly different from the pink, fleshlike substance stretched over the pillars.  A set of stairs at the west end of the hall leads up, while a similar set of stairs at the east end descends further into the bowels of the castle.

The hall continues to a small alcove at its western end, which holds a torch burning brightly.  The eastern hall leads past the branch to the north, towards the stairway leading to the higher levels.  Skulls push against the pink flesh at the base of the stone walls, as if trying to break through, while pillars of flesh stand at the corners of the walls, quivering rhythmically.

This room is small and mostly round.  Though torches line the pulsating walls here, the light in this room is softer than the number of burning torches would suggest, and seems to emanate from the center of the room rather than the walls.  Doors on the north and south walls provide the only points of access to the room - making it seem a safe place to rest.

A hallway stretches both east and west here, the scaly, brown walls looming over it.  Skulls set into the walls seem to hold a silent vigil, watching and waiting.  The pillars, grotesque imitations of a somewhat human torso, throb continuously.  A set of stairs at the east end of the hallway leads up, while the hallway continues along to the west, and another hall branches north.

Stairs of bone descend into a narrow hallway, twisting to the south and the east.  The walls of the hallway are lined with a combination of grotesque, pulsating pillars and blazing torches set within skulls.  The stairs lead back up, while the hallway opens into a large room to the east.

The center of this hallway holds a three-way intersection.  To the north, the hall continues a short distance to a dead end, while to both the east and west, the hall extends out, passing a southward branch, before finally turning a corner to the north.  The walls here are a jagged, brown stone, with what looks like pink skulls lining the bottom.  The corners of each wall are carved - or perhaps grown - into pillars, pulsing rhythmically.

A large room stands here, with the hallway to the west leading back towards the stairs, and a small alcove in the eastern wall.  The room extends to the north, where the centerpiece is a prison cell, sealed by a doorway of bones.  The cell walls are solidly formed from brown, jagged stone, while the walls outside the cell are lined with torches.  Pillars stand along the paths to either side of the cell, with more torches burning along them.

A wide, flat clearing opens within the mountains, a small forest within.  Rising above the trees is a monstrous red castle, radiating an aura of evil.  The plant life surrounding the horrible place has died and turned black, as though the castle were siphoning the life energy out of the surrounding land.  The castle is very tall, towering over even the tallest trees and only barely obscured by the highest mountain peaks, and looks as if it could be staring down at the forest in hatred.  A narrow trail leads down through the mountains towards the west.

The narrow hallway here extends north, leading to an impassable wall of what looks like brown scales at the northern end.  Just before that end, a small alcove opens up in the eastern wall, a niche extending into the wall briefly before running southward, parallel to the hallway.  The alcove itself is empty, save for a couple of torches mounted on the walls to provide light.  The hallway opens up to the west as well, with several branches visible along it.  Skulls adorn the walls and the pillars visible at the corner of each wall.

Two pillars stand as the focal point of this room, pulsing in time with the walls.  Torches line the walls, making the room far brighter than the surroundings might suggest, and the walls themselves are a fleshy, pink color.  A narrow passage extends to the east, while a hallway curls southeast, with the castle's entrance visible at its end.  To the west, a short, winding hallway ends in a staircase leading down.

The hall is large enough that it is almost a room in itself.  The fleshy, pink walls seem almost to wail in silent agony, and the light is provided by torches resting in skulls.  Pillars stand in an open section of the room, and a small alcove at the hall's eastern end holds an open chest.  A narrower hallway to the southwest leads towards the entry hall, while to the west another narrow passage is visible, leading behind the central chamber.

A crossroads inside the Underground Palace of the Earth Seed, there is a stairway to the north, and passages to both the east and west.  Torches keep this room brightly lit, burning without consuming themselves.  South leads to a well lit platform that goes out of the palace.

A small platform stretching one way into the darkness, it continues to the south a ways, climbing down a small set of steps, before stopping at a switch set in the floor. The switch appears to already have been depressed, and locked into place by another person.  The only way from here is north.

Giant braziers circle this platform, lighting brightly the stone catwalks around a deep, dark hole in the center of the platform.  The hole's bottom cannot be seen, and the light does not seem to penetrate it.  A stairway to the south leads out of the palace, and a door to the north leads deeper within.

Small torches dot the walls, allowing enough light to see a great chasm to the west.  It has a tightrope stretching between two pegs set in the ground on each side to allow crossing.  The floor consists of tiled stones in what first appears to be a random pattern, but on closer examination, the oddly shaped tiles repeat themselves.

A small walkway crosses a ravine in the middle of the room, allowing access to to an open archway to the south, and a staircase to the north.  A pillar rises from inside the ravine, suggesting that it isn't that deep, but looking into the ravine only reveals darkness.

A great brazier burns hotly in the middle of this small room, illuminating brightly two stained glass windows flanking a great door set in the northern wall.  Smaller torches line the walls, only serving to brighten the room even more.  A staircase southwards leads downwards.

A small catwalk hugging the eastern wall leads down a small set of stairs,  leading to a small switch embedded in the floor, long activated.  The switch no longer looks usable.  The catwalk is small, and the area beyond it disappears into deep darkness.  The only way from here is north.

This is a circular room, with pillars surrounding the area.  The room looks somewhat like an arena, with a small dirt pit in the center of the room only adding to the effect.  Stained glass windows are between every pillar in the room, glittering brightly.

Looking much like the other side of this crossroads, a giant stained glass window glows softly with its own light on the northern wall.  The source of the window's illumination is not visible, but torches keep the room lit.  A door to the south leads to a small pathway, and west leads to the crossroads.

A chasm splits this room in two, with two buttons on each side of the chasm, surrounding a narrow walkway.  The buttons are stuck in their current position, and presumably move the walkway.  There are stairs to the south, and a doorway to the north.

Pillars line the walls, tall and imposing.  A giant brazier lies to the south, burning brightly, and a beautiful stained glass window in the north wall shimmers in the light cast by it.  The ground underfoot is damp earth, well-tramped by other beings walking.

The cave is filled with lava, making this area very warm.  The lava flows sluggishly, almost cooling in spots, but remelting the rock and continuing on its slow course through the earth.  A raised section of rock functioning as a pedestal has a small orb sitting on it, glowing softly.  The Dwarf Village is to the south, and to the north, the Palace of the Earth Seed.

Pure elemental energy suffuses this realm, to the extent that nearly nothing else exists.  There are no perceivable floor, walls, ceiling, just mana.  It is a realm beyond mortal comprehension, and is where the most powerful of elemental beings reside.

The grandest room of the palace, giant braziers that burn brightly surround the stage of the Mana Seed of Earth.  The stage itself glows with an eerie green light, and has stairs leading up to the seed itself, which looks like nothing more than an oversized plant seed... yet is filled with a perceptible power that fills the room.

The chasm in the floor has small fires burning within it, only serving to further accentuate its depths.  A catwalk wraps around the western wall to an open archway in the north, and a tightrope crosses the chasm to the east, tied to a peg on both sides.

The stone ground present in most of the palace gives way to plain earth, giving the area a smell of damp earth.  Another stained glass window is set in the northern wall, and giant pillars hold the ground above from collapsing down and destroying the palace.

A wall stretches from the middle of the northern wall, mostly splitting the room in two.  The edge of the divider wall has another stained glass window set in it.  On the western side of the room, a door leads north, while the eastern side has a door leading south.

The ground underneath is damp and well-trodden, obviously showing that people or things have been here before.  The ceiling overhead looms dangerously, giving the impression of being ready to collapse, yet pillars are set in place to keep just that from happening.  A door is set in the southern wall.

This dimly lit passage made of damp earth, and two torches flank a staircase in the north leading upwards.  To the south is a door leading out of this narrow, cramped corridor.  The earth seems to feel more surrounding in this area than in the rest of the palace.

A giant stained glass window set in the stone walls glows eerily with its own light to the north, for underground, there is no light to shine through the window.  A door to the south leads to another section of the Underground Palace, and east leads to a crossroads.

rooms.name: The Underground Palace - Before the Stage Room

userData.LongDescription: Pillars surround this room, majestically looming overhead.  The room is well lit, but the light sources cannot be seen.  The Stage Room for the Mana Seed of Earth lies beyond the northern door, while a staircase to the south leads downward.

This ledge overlooks the cave's entrance, the sun's rays lighting the scene in a cheery glow.  There is a broken switch on the ground.  Visible are the exits from the room below, however, the only way off the ledge is back to the north, as it is too far to jump down to reach the other exits.

A narrow passage, this hallway leads north and south.  Plant life festoons the walls; some are vines, others are glowing mosses giving off enough light to see by.  The path north seems to lead into darker areas, while the path south leads to a more open chamber.

This ledge overlooks a debris filled chamber.  Set into the floor is a large panel, revealing nothing about its purpose.  To the west, a steep drop prevents passage down off the ledge, but a few large pillars span the gap to allow passage to the ledge across the chasm.  Stairs to the east lead down into the chamber, and south goes along the ledge.

The river of lava flows through the room, radiating heat like an infernal furnace.  The bridge is surprisingly sturdy, considering it has been suspended over lava for countless years.  However, the bridge cuts out to the east, leaving only some rocks to jump across to the small stone ledge on the other side.  Stairs lead upwards to cooler regions of the cave, while south leads to more of the lava areas.

A small ledge in between and overlooking two very narrow passageways running parallel to each other, it is extremely hot in this area, as the lavaflow runs swiftly to the south.  From this vantage point, it is easy to see that the rock platform to the south used to move between the two passageways, but that function has long since expired.  The only exit is to the northern stairway.

This is a large cliff, where it seems that grass has been able to survive, despite the cool climate and high altitude.  The cliff rocks make it almost impossible to climb either up or down.  Even though the altitude would normally make the air cold, a stream of warm air blows out from the cave, blocking the chill from coming near.

A long stairway leads north and south, with the north leading to the upper levels, and the south leading down into mostly cooled lava.  The lava is dark and rocky, looking to have been recently cooled, giving enough purchase to walk across without fear.

This is a small room within the cave, where the rock walls climb upwards towards the general cave above.  The walls are too sheer to climb, however, and the only exit is a stone stairway to the north, that appears to have been carved out of the rock.  A broken switch lies on the ground, its previous function unknown.

A comforting blue light suffuses the area, emanating from a small campsite to the south, tucked away in an alcove.  It is safe to camp here, as the small ring of charred stones suggests, others already have.  To the north, a small bridge leads to a broken switch, its purpose unknown.  To the west, the cave continues.

The air is damp and laden with the earthy smells of moss, rock, and fungi.  The shadows cast by the rock formations deepen into a pitch black darkness.  A bridge leads to an empty treasure chest, and there is no hint as to what used to lie within it.  Heat issues forth from the stairs leading downwards, while cooler air flows from the east.

A small set of steps leads into a large chamber of the cave, with exits in all directions.  Charred rocks litter the ground, singed black by the heat of some fire long ago.  Some of the rocks are large enough to impede passage, however, it looks as if someone cleared some of the larger rocks out of the way of the exits.

A giant island amidst the surrounding lava, there are bridges to smaller islands to the east and northwest.  The air shimmers and twists as the heat off the lava causes the air to quiver.  The stairs to the north lead upward to the top level of the cave, and cooler air.

Several collapsed bridges make climbing up to the ledges surrounding the lavabed a manageable task.  Both the northern and eastern bridges leads to stairways stretching out of the chamber, while the southern bridge leads to the southeastern section of the lava sea.

Long bridges span over the lava, with only small rock sections jutting out from the river to support them.  To the northwest, the bridge leads to the riverbank.  A small side bridge to the west leads to an empty chest, and to the south, larger rock islands seem to surge out from the lava, resisting nature's attempts to melt them down.

Crystals glisten within the walls, shimmering as light flows from them.  The light also shines upon an empty chest, dusty with disuse.  Chunks of rock litter the floor, perhaps a result of a battle, or the earth's shifting.  Northwest leads back into the main part of the caves.

One of the rock pillars in this room is shattered, causing stone debris to be scattered around.  Pits and pockmarks scar the ground, as if something large went on a rampage.  Holes dot the ground in an eerie pattern, but their purpose is unknown, as is the purpose of the large broken switch that is part of the floor.

Bridges connect this island to others, with the west bridge connecting to a large rock island with a stairway, and the northern bridge is exceptionally long, stretching out over the lava for a good distance.  The heat of the lava permeates the area, offering no escape to cooler air.

The lava looks unstable, as if it could release the entire area back into the depths of molten rock.  A stairway leads up to a small rock island with nothing on it but a single lonely chest.  The stifling heat of the lava fills the area, refusing to give way to whatever cooled the lava to this hardened state.

Heat flows upward from the depths of the earth, filling the area with its warm embrace.  To the south, stairs can be seen in the distance leading downwards, while to the west, a path leads along the cavern wall, dotted with a pattern of holes that could not be naturally made.

An extremely narrow passageway, the walls seem to press in and move slowly, the heat twisting the air around them and making them seem alive and breathing.  To the south, the passage opens up to reveal the banks of the river of lava, and to the northwest, a stairway leads to the upper floor of the cave.

The steaming vents, gaping cracks in the floor, relentlessly blast hot air out of the ground and heat this passageway with the warmth of the lava from the chambers underneath.  Out of reach above is a higher ledge, which seems as though it were rent in two to form this lower trench.  On the other side of this rift, embedded high in the wall, is a metal box lying out of reach, the steps leading to it having crumbled long ago.

Steam billows forth from cracks in the ground, making the air hazy and thick.  Moss grows on the rocky walls, thriving in the steamy environment.  The stairway leading upwards suggests some relief from the muggy air, while the north leads to hotter regions of the cave.

Steps go north out of the lavabed, while east and south lead to other sections of this strange cooled lava sea.  Even cooled, the lava still puts out a sweltering heat, and the ground is uneven and precarious, as if the lava underneath could break through at any time.

Heat fills this huge chamber, sweltering in its strength.  In the distance, across the lava flows, a large island can be seen, right in the center of the lava lake.  A long stairway leads out of the chamber, and the path to the west leads to a bridge.

An extremely long bridge stretches northward, out over the lake of lava, connecting this path to the large island in the center of the lake.  The heat is stiflingly hot, pouring off the lava in torrential waves.  The lava itself glows like the fiery pits of hell.

Deep grooves mark the floor, leading into the wall and stopping.  Perhaps at one time, this wall was meant to be some sort of mechanism that moved, but no longer.  The air is distorted by the heat rising from the lava below.  To the southeast, a bridge leads out over the lava.

A switch is built into the northern cave wall, with a skull-shaped handle.  A small stairway to the south leads into a debris-filled chamber, which appears to lead off in many directions from there.  The larger set of stairs lead down to the lava regions of the cave.

The lurid glow of the lava gives plenty of light to see by, illuminating a series of spikes sticking out of the ground, a trap long ago triggered.  The trap seems out of place, however, if it ever guarded anything, it doesn't anymore.  A bridge leads northwards, and to the south, in the distance, a stairway leads upwards.

A small ledge on the outside of the lava lake, there is a giant rift in the air here, with an image of the grassy ledge outside of the Phoenix Cave appearing within it.  A cooler wind issues forth from the warphole, bringing with it the smell of fresh air.

It looks like someone or something smashed many pillars that used to impede progress, and the remains of those pillars has been left scattered on the ground as evidence.  On the southern side of the chamber, there is a narrow passageway to the south.  A small stairway to the west leads up to a ledge overlooking both the chamber and the southern passageway.  North leads back into the chamber.

An empty chest sits near the northern wall, with no hints as to what it used to contain.  Small holes surround the chest, suggesting that whatever was within the chest, it was important enough to put behind a trap.  The floor drops off into a small area to the west, but the climb is too steep to try to go downwards.  The only exit is back to the southwest.

Overlooking the large sea of cooling lava, this ledge in the southeastern section of the chamber has two bridges that seem to have lost their supports long ago.  These ruined bridges now serve as ramps to lead north and west back down to the ground level.

The path going north to south ends, as this ledge is located high above the chamber, with sides too steep to navigate.  However, several pillars span the gap between this ledge and a ledge to the east, giving enough footing that a person could jump from pillar to pillar.

This small island has debris littering the floor, mostly looking like small bits of lava had splashed out of the bottom of the chamber, hardening into rocky lumps on the ground.  The stairway leads north and out of the chamber, while the broken bridge to the south leads down into the cooled lavabed.

A set of stairs leads north and away from the debris-cluttered large chamber that lies to the east.  Water drips from the ceiling, forming puddles on the ground amidst the small chips of rock.  Moss and fungi thrive, the moisture and warmth giving them the perfect conditions to grow.

This ledge on the eastern side of the great chamber has only one broken ramp leading down to the lava bed.  Debris is scattered across the ground, mostly rocks broken off the walls.  Hot winds blow from the center of the chamber, going north, up the stairs that lead to the upper level of the cave.

A bridge on a rock formation up above to the east collapsed at some unknown time, making enough of a ramp to scale it and climb to the top.  Going to the east leads to the rocky ledges above the expanse of cooled lava, while west goes back across the lavabed.

Bursts of heat pulse from the stairs leading downwards into the depths of the cave.  To the east, the path along the wall has an interesting section of flooring dotted with holes.  The rock walls have been worn down to a smooth finish by the passage of time.

A small ledge of rock overseeing the river of lava, the heat here is almost unbearable, rising up from the lava in torrents.  Rocks that cut the current of lava are the only way off this ledge, and two sets of them lead west, one to the northwest, and one to the southwest.

A narrow passageway leads north, away from the swiftly flowing river of lava to the south.  The lava moves swiftly and smoothly through the channel cut deep within the ground.  West leads down to the banks of the river, where the heat is even more intense.

The temperature seems to be climbing, with heat issuing forth from the stairs that lead down into the deepest part of the Phoenix Cave.  This ledge overlooks passageways to the east and west, but neither of these can be reached.  Besides the stairs, the only pathway is north.

This section of the river is dotted with small outcroppings of rock connected by bridges.  The westernmost bridge leads to a small, empty chest.  The heat is unrelenting, pouring off the lava in an unending torrent.  To the southeast, a larger bridge leads back to a big rock island in the middle of the lava flow.

Stairs to the north lead upwards to the higher chambers of the Phoenix Cave, where slightly cooler air can be found.  The heat here is still incredible, owing to the fact that going south leads back to the lava river that flows through the bottom levels of the cave.

The cave entrance is still lit somewhat by the daylight from outside, but is quickly replaced by a reddish glow of heat.  On the ground, a curious large button appears to have been wedged into the pressed position.  A ledge high above appears to have an exit north, but is unreachable from this position.  Northeast and northwest lead to different sections of the caves.  The cave exit looms to the south, with daylight shining brightly.

A bridge leads southeast out over the lava, but a portion of the bridge collapsed, leaving only debris.  However, enough of the debris looks stable enough to jump on to cross the burning river.  The cave extends to the east, along the banks of the lava stream.

A breeze of warmer air blows from the stairway leading down into the dimly glowing depths.  A switch sits on the wall that lies across the gap to the east, however, it is out of reach from this ledge.  There is a stairway leading south to get off this rocky ledge.

Debris from collapsed rock covers the floor.  To the north, the floor drops off into a small self-contained area, however, the walls are too sheer to safely enter that room.  To the south, a stairway leads deep within the cave, and waves of heat billow out from it.  A grand arch of stone looms over the passage to the southeast.

The pillars of rock join the ceiling and floor, creating giant columns.  Heat flows upward from the depths of the earth, coming from the stairs descending deep into the cave.  Stone litters the floor, making footing precarious.  Small curious holes line the passage south, while the passage to the east looks normal for a cave.

Tucked away in the northwestern side of this large chamber of cooled lava, this small rocky outcropping leads up and out of the lavabed.  A stairway lies to the north, going completely out of the area, and south goes back down into the main room.

Two stairways to the south lead to the lower, lava-filled areas of the cave.  North goes across a small natural bridge that spans over what appears to be an empty lake.  Vines crawl across the walls in intriguing patterns, and the floor is blanketed with a thin steamy mist.

The lava underfoot has recently solidified, making traveling across it a simple task.  However, debris and spurts of lava that hardened into pillars are scattered everywhere, blocking off most routes except to the west and north.  North goes to a stairway out of the lava.

Small lumps of rock are melded with the floor, as if something splashed lava over the ground playfully.  Two floor panels sit next to each other, their functionality long since broken by the heat and the decay of time.  The only exits are to the north and south, as the ledge is too steep to climb off of.

The fresh air from the entrance barely makes it this far, stirring the air just a little.  To the northeast, there are holes in the ground that do not look natural, as they are too perfectly shaped and spaced apart.  The southeast leads to the entrance and fresher air.  To the west, a small bridge and an empty chest lie, proving that something has been here before.

A dark area of the cave, most of the light making the area visible is coming from the soft red glow emanating from the stairs leading down into the bottom of the cave.  Dimly lit, a small passageway gradually bends around a corner and leads south.

The dark recesses of the cave offer no hint as to what lurks within them.  Depressions in the floor make footing treacherous, some large enough to fall into, others only enough to twist an ankle.  A carved stone stairway leads southward, but it is a small stairway that doesn't lead very far downward.  There is also a passageway to the west.

A large island in the center of a lake of lava, the heat here is nearly overpowering.  Stones circle the island in a strange symmetrical pattern, suggesting that they did not randomly appear.  The island appears to radiate power as much as it does heat.  A chest in the center of the island is charred nearly beyond recognition.  A line of rocks bridge the lavaflow to the east, where a glow different from the lava can be seen.

The east/west passage just leads to more cave as it stretches deep into the earth.  A skeleton lies on the floor, becoming one with the rock.  Twisted and misshapen, the bones are obviously not human.

A light shines brightly with a cold blue glow.  It is safe, no monsters will enter this area of the cave.  Even the stench of decay has cleared from the region, and the moss seems to shrink away from the light.

Illuminating the paths south and west, the moss is bright enough to see a rather large boulder in the middle of the path.  Other than the boulder, only a few spires of rock dot the area, shooting into the empty air of the cave.

A set of crudely hewn stairs leads down into the darkness below, which is only mildly mitigated by the moss that grows and glows all around.  The paths north and west lead only to more cavern, giving the impression of immense size to the cave.

A small chest lies against the western wall, open and empty, with a small pool of water collecting in it.  Cold, clear water is in small pools all around the area, with ways to the northwest and southeast.
This passage stops at an old oaken door, built in the wall of the cave.  The dripping of water is audible again, and the passageway goes to the north back towards Figaro.

The ground is rocky under your feet, and the only light is from glowing moss on the walls and ceiling.  By the dim light, you can see several exits, northwest back to the Castle Figaro, east, and south deeper into the cave.

The passageway north and south is shrouded in darkness, as very little of the moss has survived in this area.  Pitted and scarred, the walls look like they have been through many battles, and the moss did not survive them.

The caves open up to the southwest, into a giant cavern, dimly lit by the moss. The light, however, isn't strong enough, for the ceiling of the cavern is not visible.  A passageway to the east leads into a section of the caves closer to Figaro.
At a deadend in the cave passage, a small chest sits here.  Overhead are huge walkways that presumably connect higher sections of the cavern.  The only way is back to the south.

The cave seems to stretch out forever, and has entered a three-pronged crossing, all going some direction of east.  The western wall is slick with condensed moisture, but nothing else of interest is in the area.
Splatters of red decorate the area, and a chest can be seen over a ledge, but is too far down to jump to it.  A few rock formations jut out from the walls, making the wall rather sharp.

On this sloping path, there is only a way upwards to the southeast, and downwards toward the exit of the cave. Snarling and growling can be heard distantly, something else must be in this cave besides you.
An east-west passage, just like many others within this dark maze, is dimly lighted by the always present moss.  Water drips slowly from the ceiling high above.

Looming overhead is a stone walkway, leading to another section of the cave.  However, since you can't reach the walkway from here, the only choices are to go north towards Figaro, or southeast, deeper into the cave.
The cavern remains huge, but jutting rocks from the ground prevent easy passage.  The stone allows passage west towards a great hole in the cavern, northeast towards Figaro, and south to more stone.

The passage to the west goes under a great arch of stone, giving the impression of an entire new area of the cave.  Coated in moss, the arch gives off a faint unearthly light.  The passageway east leads to more familiar areas of the cave.

A door set in the north wall has been marked many times with a series of slashes, making no discernable letters or runes, but looking more like the carvings of a madman.  To the south and southeast passages lead.

This east west passage has a small stream running through the middle of it, that has dug a small channel in the floor, and a hole in both walls too small for anything but water.  Splashing sounds suggest that it is deep enough for fish, however.

A door leads deeper into the cave, which seems endlessly long.  A small chest is here, but the lock has been sprung on it.  A passageway to the northwest slopes upward rather steeply, and the passageway north is level ground.

The walkway you are standing on is a naturally formed one, stretching out over the middle of this grand cavern.  It is sturdy, and wouldn't crack even if a bomb was set off.  It leads northeast and southwest.

Moss lights the paths to north and south, giving enough illumination to pick the way past giant columns of rock trying to reach the ceiling, like grasping hands.  Reaching downwards from the ceiling are their brethren columns, and over the ages, they will meet in the middle.

On top of the walkway, you can see under you a small passageway running north to south, and the end of the walkway to the southwest.  The light is rather dim here, making it difficult to see anything beyond that.
Light comes from all around, but the top of the cave is not visible, making it seem like the ceiling is off somewhere in infinity, and the cave is enshrouded in a sky of endless, starless night.

Stairs stretch far to the north, with a slight incline to them, marking something different from the endless amounts of rock.  A faint breeze flows from the stairway, suggesting that something more than mere cave lies beyond the stairs.

The walls are covered in moss, giving off small quantities of light, and illuminating the passageway, which leads north or east.  Puddles of water have gathered, and drops of water echo through the cave as they drop from the invisible ceiling.
This stairway climbs slowly, and a light shines from the top.  The stairway appears man-made, for water could not have cut such steps, though water has smoothed the steps, making them a bit slippery.

A giant formation of rock dominates the view of this area, covered in glowing moss, looking like a pillar of light.  The pillar is covered with moss all the way to the ceiling, giving a clear view of how high the ceiling of the cave is.  To the north and west is more cave.
This slope leads upward to the north, near the walkway that stretches across the cavern, and southeast leads downward.  The dripping of water is the only noise you can hear, it is otherwise quiet.

Outside of the jail cell is a mysterious underground cave, full of twists and turns.  Looking around, there are exits to the south and southeast visible, with the southeast passage gently sloping upwards.

Columns of rock appear to block the path that goes east to west, but are easily weaved through.  Chips of rock scattered about, chipped from the columns, suggest that someone or something has been irritated with these rocks.

In the middle of the cavern, a hole leads deeper within this giant maze of stone.  A crudely carved stairway leads downwards into the darkness.  Stone spikes from the ground block most ways, but the east and west passages remain clear.

The cavern is spread out before you at the top of the paths, and looking out, you see many different paths to take all through the labyrinth.  There is a rough-hewn stairs down, and passages to the northwest and southeast, and a walkway to your southwest that crosses over several rooms.
A ridge of stone arches overhead, and the passage to the west splits to north and south.  A small trail of red is on the floor, leading to the southwest...
A deep pit in the ground leads down into darkness.  With no way to get into it, and no moss inside it, it could be a very dangerous idea to go down.  Northwest and southwest lead to more of the cave.
Many ways lead from this area, sprawling out all over the cave.  You can hear water dripping, but no water is in sight.  The ways are numerous, but the way leading back to Castle Figaro is north.
A T-section passageway, the western path goes down a long stretch of passage, the north passage leads toward a giant hole in the ground, and the southern passage leads to more endless cavern.

This T-junction goes north, east, and west, with the southern wall blocking any passage that direction.  The moss grows faint in the western direction, and a giant hole is visible to the northern direction.
Water flows through a small channel into the floor, disappearing under the southern cavern wall.  A pillar of rock bars passage to the northeast, but ways to the northwest and east are available.
At the bottom of the staircase lies an open chest, probably looted by an adventurous spelunker.  A small stream trickles through here, making little sound as it travels into a wall.

This east-west passage stretches for a while longer to the west.  A small jumble of rocks seem to be piled in small pyramid like structures, with moss ripped off the walls to cement the rocks together, for no apparent reason.

On this end of the walkway, the southern path slopes downward, and the combined light of torches along the wall and fungus on the walls make it possible to see where you are.  However, it is just rock walls, rock floor, and rock everything.

A small ledge looms over part of the cave, and you think you see wood instead of rock to the south.  The light is too dim to be sure, however.  West will take you on the passageway out of the caves to Figaro.

Moss growing abundantly lights the path, making the paths to the south and west visible.  Dripping water falls all around, dripping from the downward thrusting rock spires, and landing on the upward jutting spires of pointed rock.
A stone staircase rises to a higher level, and is roughly hewn.  A flickering light comes from up ahead to the east, and west leads under a giant walkway.

Water falls like a gentle rain from the formations of rock high above on the ceiling.  Small puddles support life, mostly plants, like the everpresent green moss that glows softly.  East and southwest lead elsewhere in the cave.
Deep inside the cave, this is a small room with a chest in it, the chest has been opened already.  The door to the north is made of sturdy oak, and there is a corridor to the west.

The smell of the glowing phosphorescent moss permeates this part of the cave, giving an earthy flavor to it.  Rents and tears on the moss suggest that something uses the walls to sharpen its claws.  To the east leads deeper into the cave.

A T-section of the cave, the southern wall is coated with the everpresent moss, lighting the paths north, east, and west.  Puddles of water have welled up from the ground.  The moss glows softly, making the cave feel like another world.

The moss on the ground has footprints in it, some human, some inhuman.  It is difficult to walk on the moss, and the dampness suggests water nearby.  Northeast leads deeper into the cave, while west leads outwards.

A faint glimmer of blue light can be seen at the top of these long stairs, while at the bottom of the stairs, only the faint glow of the phosphorescent moss shines dimly.  The sound of water dripping is the only sound the cave makes.

A torch flickers on the wall, and reflects off of an oaken door to the south.  The passage runs back to the north towards Figaro, or through the door.  Grumbling of something, and a creaking sound can be heard beyond the door.

A giant arch towers overhead, stable as the rock composing it.  Water drips from the arch, making the air feel damp and clammy, and the chill in the air doesn't help matters.  North and south are the only ways from under this arch.

A flickering torch is here, lighting the way enough to see the stairway down, and that a passage south leads deeper into the cave.  Northwest of you, the passage slopes upward, leading to a walkway high in the caverns.
Drops of water rain down from the ceiling, splashing about and creating many puddles on the ground.  The moss thrives here, and the rocks shine wetly in the phosphorescent light.

A dead end in the cavern's endless passages, the only exit is to the west, which leads back to a T-junction is the passageways.  It is rather dimly lit, as the moss does not grow well here for unknown reasons.

Looking up, there is a natural walkway overhead, and ways to the north, south, and southeast.  This place is a maze of ways, sprawling out everwhere.  The rock this cave is made room is never smooth in any place, but you hear a drip of water in the distance.

The door that leads towards the exit is to the north, and southeast leads deeper inside the cavern.  Dripping water comes from rock formations in the ceiling, that are growing larger throughout the millenia, and will, after eons, connect with formations on the floor.

The northeastern side of the throne room has little of note, except for a set of openings that seem to lead somewhere deep into the heart of the castle. Most of these entrances have been blocked by rubble, but there is one that is clear. The thrones are to the west, while a path of stony pillars lead to the south.

A heavily adorned door leads to a different part of the castle at the eastern wall of the throne room. Suits of armor and shields line the walls on this side, providing a rather decorated feel to the castle. To the west is a long line of carpet, and to the north and south stand stone pillars.

The thrones are here, at the northern end of the throne room. There are two large-sized chairs that look rather regal and comfy. The left chair seems to be larger than the right, as it is the throne of the King. To the south, there is a long path covered with a royal blue carpet. There is a large painting by the back wall as well.

This is a fairly sparse room with not much in it. There is a single suit of armor standing tall on the northern wall, as well as a few buckets. In the corner is a regally adorned treasure chest, though its contents have been emptied out. To the south is an exit leading back to the courtyard.

The northwestern side of the throne room has not much to note. A few entrances have been exposed on the northern wall that lead to other parts of the castle. These entrances don't look really safe to enter, however, since they are stacked and blocked with debris. The thrones are to the east, while a path of stony pillars lead to the south.

This hidden basement seems to have been a shelter of some sorts, for important personnel during raids upon the castle. There is a long path of blue carpet by the middle of the room, with countless suits of armor lining the sides, as if to serve as protection. A set of stairs leads up to the castle proper.

This is the majestic throne room of the ancient castle. Royal blue carpets are rolled out along the middle of this very wide room, with countless pillars supporting the sides. Visible to the north are the double thrones. To the south, there is an anteroom used to contain guests and halt invaders.

This is the center of the throne room. A vivid blue carpet is rolled out along the ground to the northern and southern sides, covering the entire length of the middle of the area. Straight to the north, the thrones can be seen. There are doors leading to other parts of the castle to the sides as well.

A hallway opens on the left wall of the throne room, leading to a set of stairs heading down somewhere. There are two shields hung on the wall just beside the hallway, indicating that the entrance may be of some importance. South and north lead to corners of the throne room, while east points straight to a carpeted path.

Wrecked columns fill the courtyard, and a small moat lies to the east, blocking off passage.  This part of the archway has crumbled down completely, revealing the rest of the courtyard.  Pieces of the castle walls lie all around, grass growing up to cover them slowly.

This is what remains of one of the cells in the ancient fort. The ceiling is high, and it is impossible to tell what there is up there. There are many iron bars placed along the southern wall that make visible the other side of the room. A busted prison door leads to the hallway eventually leading to the throne room.

This is the northern end of the castle's basement. There are metal grates attached to alcoves on the wall, as well as decorative swords placed in between. The only object of worthy note here is a life-sized statue of a very beautiful woman, wearing an elegant royal dress...

The center of the courtyard is clear of most debris, with most of the columns not falling inward to scatter pieces of themselves everywhere.  A small pond is to the east, but it is small enough to walk around with no difficulty. The doorway to the castle looms at the northern end of the courtyard.

The ruined columns ring this area, shattered to pieces as if a giant hand had just swept the area.  The stonework to the north contains a column in slightly better condition with a small window in it.  The grass grows all around, and small rocks and debris are scattered everywhere.

The stairs to the south open up to a brightly lit area.  The light source seems like sunlight, but that is impossible, since this is an underground cavern.  A castle looms to the north, crumbled and ruined, but still majestic, somehow.  The stairway underneath is crumbled and decaying, but still apparent that it was carved from stone by human hands.

This is an elegant room in the castle, whose beauty has not faded even with the flow of time. The floor is smooth and made out of marble, unlike the rough stony floors common to the castle. There is a large bed on the corner of the room, and an expensive-looking bookshelf by another corner.

This is a room used as a divider as well as a waiting room before something much more important. There are chairs lined up in the sides of the room, as well as suits of armor on the corners as decoration. To the north is a great hallway leading to the throne room. South leads to the castle courtyard.

Crumbling columns of the once awe-inspiring castle lean forward or are cracked in half, spilling debris all over the ground.  Grass grows in between the stonework, adding to the atmosphere of this long-forgotten place.  An archway looms to the north, intact enough to be passed through, and to the southwest lies a stairway leading to the caves.

The western side of the courtyard is in no better condition than any other part. Some of the walls have been torn down enough that a person could walk down into the moat with ease.  At this point of the wall there are openings that lead deep into the prison cells of the castle.

This room appears to be one of the prison cells in the castle. The ceiling is very high, and hard to see. There are bars placed along the northern wall that make visible the other side of the room. There is an opening to the south that leads to the courtyard of the castle. It looks as if it was busted open forcefully.

The wall to the east is in good enough condition to block passage. However, the rest of the area cannot have the same said for it, as junk from ruined columns lies everywhere.  A pond to the west contains a few fish swimming around happily.

The basement expands to the north and south. Placed in perfectly constructed lines are suits of armor that form almost the image of an army battalion. To the north, there seems to be a statue of some sort, though details are impossible to make out from this point. A set of stairs is to the south.

This is the southwestern corner of the throne room. A seemingly endless array of stone pillars make for a confusing, maze-like structure around the sides of the room. There is barely any light here. East leads to the carpeted path, while north leads further closer to the throne along the pillared path.

This is the corner of the throne room. While there is not much here except for the seemingly endless array of stone pillars, this location makes a good hiding spot for soldiers and invaders alike. West leads to the carpeted path, while north leads further closer to the throne along the pillared path.

A desk is here, unoccupied.  Evidently, the guards dislike coming down here because of the noise.  The stairs up will lead to a higher part of the engine room, and south through a door leads deeper into this odd place of machinery.

You can see the stairs that lead back to the castle across the room, but the channel dividing the room makes it impossible to reach.  The door inside the channel leads to the engine, but it too is unreachable.  To the north you see a door, and down the stairs leads deep inside the engine room.

This is the channel leading to the engine.  The throbbing of the engine comes and goes, sounding like something is clogged in it.  The door is a little ways to the north, and the door south leads out of the channel.
You can still see the stairs out of the engine room across the room, but to get to them involves a bit of walking.  A door stands in front of you, and stairs are visible to your south.
Several empty chests are in this room, as adventurers have been through here before.  Other than that, there isn't much in this room, and the only way out is back to the north.

This side of the room has a door to the north that is flanked by two dusty suits of armor, an opening to the south, and the rest of the room is to the east.  The throbbing of the engine can be felt in the soles of your feet.
Two empty chests are in this room, with dust inside them, showing that they've been open a long time.  Not much else to be seen this room, and the only way out is back to the north.

The machinery in the area is still working, and can be heard below you.  A door is right below you in a channel, but cannot be reached.  The stairs down into a lower section of the engine room are here, and south of you are the stairs back into Figaro Castle.

This is the Engine Room of Castle Figaro.  A writhing mass of worms covers the room, and it is obvious that these things have been causing the problem with the engines.  The door to the south leands out of the engine room, and a door to the north is barely visible behind the weaving tentacles.

The channel extends through the basement towards a metal door which leads to the engine.  The sound of the engine comes and goes, sounding like something is clogged in it.  The door to the north leading to the engine is a thick steel plate covered in rivets, while a regular wooden door further to the south leads out of the channel.
