A big open room, you see openings around you, and the north one leads to a door that might lead to the channel that was seen in the first part of the engine room.  The throbbing of the engine sounds odd, as if something was stopping it from working properly.

This is the treasure room of Castle Figaro, but all that is here is a ring of empty treasure chests that surround a suit of armor.  Obviously, the treasures have been removed for safekeeping somewhere else.

The first part of the engine room basement; there are lots of sounds of machinery working in the area.  Another walkway is on the other side of the room, but it is unreachable due to a channel cutting through the middle of the room, with a door at the end of it.  The door is unreachable, the only exits are up the stairs to the castle, and north towards another set of stairs.

Two suits of armor flank the door leading out, and sounds of machinery are rather loud.   A deep thrum can be felt from the engine nearby.  There is an opening to the south, and west is more of the engine room.

A box is in the corner of this room, and some machinery can been seen within the wall, moving and clanking about.  The stairs upward lead to above the channel, and the door south lead towards the exit.
All that is in this small room is an empty chest collecting dust in the middle of the room.  The door out leads to the main chamber of the engine room.

This spacious cavern is the entrance to the Lunar Trials.  Pale light from the moon reflects into the cave from outside, giving the walls a pale, blue glow.  An opening in the cave leads back to the moon's surface.  Two passages to the east and west lead further into the cave.
The current trial for this week
Inside of a spacious cavern lies the heart of Lunar Ramuh's trial.  Lightning arcs from stalactites
The current trial for this week
The current trial for this week

A path runs through a chasm underneath an uneven land bridge and seems to only lead northward, deeper into the large cavern.  The only other direction of travel is up a staircase, to a hardscrabble landing containing an open, wooden door.

Fallen rock debris is scattered about and scuff marks on the ground indicate travel by some larger creature.  Stairs lead to an upper level, and there is a dark passage to the west.  A pulsing blue light shines to the northeast, reachable via a narrow path underneath a small bit of land from the upper level that runs overhead to the east wall.

The torch hanging on the brazier in this part of the cave provides stoic illumination to otherwise drab terrain.  The stairs to the south cause the torch's light to produce the illusion of flickering shadows on the lower level.  To the east is a dark, cavernous tunnel through which nothing is visible.

This junction is dimly lit by a torch hanging from a brazier set in the far north wall.  To the east a cavernous tunnel has bored through the rock, while to the north is a set of stairs which lead towards the light. To the west is a passage which seems to arc to the south, and from which a gentle breeze can be felt.

Darkness strains to cover a narrow tunnel through the rock, but light encroaches from two torches in caverns to the east and west.  The flickering light reveals a dim passage to the south that ends upon carved stairs leading to a lower level.

This large expanse of mostly flat terrain overlooks a chasm, and provides an almost safe haven for the refugees who have set up camp in the sheltered southeastern corner.  They huddle around the fire, reminiscing and telling stories of hunting trips in the wilderness outside.  To the west is a land bridge, while to the north is a man-made door.  A small treasure chest seems to still be holding up in the northwestern corner.

This crudely formed land bridge crosses from west to east, above the chasm below which stretches from north to south.  To the east, a few refugees who dare not venture deeper into the cave huddle around the light of a camp fire.  A dark, cavernous tunnel leads to the west.

A dark passageway dead-ends in a small chamber with a torch hanging in a brazier on the northern wall.  It looks like there is a treasure chest here, but the lid has been pried completely off.  The only visible exit from this room is through the dark tunnel back to the east.

The harsh winds of the ruined world subside to an eerie whistle inside the cave entrance.  The ground is craggy but passable.  It seems that this is the only refuge on the entire Veldt.  To the north, the cave bears to the east; the only other accessible direction is out onto the Veldt.

From this small landing, most of the cavern is visible.  A narrow land bridge juts out from a much more expansive area of flat land to the east but stops just short of connecting to the landing.  There are stairs which lead down to a slightly lower level of the cavern, which seems to form a path through the chasm passing under the land bridge.  An open door shows a passage through the rock.

A narrow path fans out before meeting walls in the northeastern corner of a cavern.  In contrast to the path, the widened area is flat and clear of debris.  Warm, blue light radiates out from a fixed point in the center of the alcove.

This room is well lit by a brightly burning torch hung in a brazier on the northern wall.  There is a set of stairs leading down to a lower level, which seems to twist and bend before continuing west into the rock.  The only other exit in this room seems to be south, through a door in a darkened tunnel.

This juncture is well lit by a torch hanging from an amply shining brazier in the northwestern corner.  The southern wall to this room is inlaid with a door, while an eastern passage looks like some rocks have been moved to make it passable.  There are steep stairs to the north, which lead upwards and out of sight.

A profusion of claw marks, scratchings, and tracks from a large type of beast have left little else upon a large mass of mostly flat land.  This area is nearly devoid of debris as its extends into a small, unstable bridge to a landing on the western edge of a chasm.   Remains of old animal corpses and skeletons form a neat pile in the corner, near a dark passage heading east.

A wide chasm cuts unders a land bridge, outlined by several rocky, craggy cliffs.  The chasm stretches from north to south, in a large room which seems to have ample lighting from a source near the ceiling of the cavern.  The northern end of the chasm leads into a tunnel, while at the southern end a few stairs lead down to a door.

The passage opens up slightly into a narrow, natural room, with a burning torch set in a brazier on the eastern wall.  There is a slight cool breeze entering into this chamber from the southern entrance.  Tunnels exit the cave to the north and south.

There seem to be stairs in every direction: a smaller set leads down to a path, while around a bend in this landing, a steeper stairwell descends into a dark tunnel punctuated by a door.  The landing runs all the way to the east wall.  A lone torch hangs from a brazier along the north wall, seeming to be running out of energy.  Down in the chasm below, debris litters the ground.  An undulating blue light shines to the east.

This terraced room ends at the bottom of three levels; two sets of stairs lead down to another set of stairs, which leads to a desecrated treasure chest.  On the northern wall is a large and bulky switch.  A door leads through the northern wall.

A passage ends, overlooking a chasm, over which several naturally formed bridges wind deeper into the cave.  There is a dim light flickering to the northeast, across the bridges, where some faint sounds can be heard.  The ground down below seems rough and craggy.  The only way out is the cavernous tunnel back to the west.

At the north end of a chasm is a steep stairwell which ascends into dimness, only to reach a landing with a door set into the cave wall.  The chasm runs south, under a land bridge making up most of the upper level of flat land in the large cavern.

A huge wall of rock blocks the direct path to the north but there is a path stomped on the ground that goes around the wall and continues northeast. Green grass and different colored flowers border the path, almost as if they are welcoming the random adventurer to the forest in their own way. The tree growth is not as thick as it has been but there are alot of trees everywhere.

Venturing deeper and deeper into the forest, the landscape seemingly stays the same. Few variations in the coloration of the flowers and the shape and sizes of the trees can be noticed. But one thing can be seen easily; the trees are beginning to close in. It is starting to get darker since the trees are blocking the light from the sun.

A myriad of lights constantly flash through this room.  Mana of all varieties flows freely through this room, the only real structure in the entire Elemental Realm.  All of the mana slowly makes it way towards a solitary stone altar in the center of the room.

A dark, thin passage bends its way through the rock below the surface of the ground.  A small crack in the wall leads back into some unreachable crevice.  Water slowly drips down from the ceiling and collects in small muddy puddles on the floor.

A wide underground cavern spreads out in all directions, making a large single room.  Cold drops of water drip from the high ceiling, falling into puddles on the ground with plinking sounds that echo around the room.  Two flat ledges of rock sit at opposite sides of the cavern.

The temperature is cool between the two cliffs lining the path.  Trees grow high up on the tops of the cliffs, their branches casting only a light shade on the path far below.  Soft light glances off the rocks, filling the valley with their pale blue tone.

A narrow path runs through the dense trees and forks into three different directions.  The air is still, with no wind.  The whole forest feels frozen in time as each leaf, flower and blade of grass stays motionless.

A shrine of pure white rock stands among the trees in a very small clearing.  The ground all around the shrine is also made with white bricks.  Although the grass has almost completely overgrown them, large sections of brick still show through to the west and south.  An entrance between the shrine's pillars leads to another area of the forest.

A path leading south meets with another path that bends around a large mountain.  A tree grows by one side, casting its shadow on the steep slope of rock in branching patterns.  A trail of worn spots in the grass leads from south to northeast.

Many short, leafy bushes have grown over this part of the path in large clusters, one right next to the other.  Their leaves remain covered in dew from the cool moisture of the Pure Land's cloud barrier.

A vast forest rarely seen by human eyes stretches out for miles.  Tall, majestic trees with mighty roots and beautiful, blue-green leaves are all around as far as the eye can see.  A soft floor of grass grows along a thin path through the trees.

This is the center of the whole clearing, a round piece of land on the top of a ridge.  Some large rocks and a tree stump sit at one end.  Purple and yellow flowers grow in abundance.  Two branches of a stream flow by on the west and east sides.

A narrow path coming north through the rock suddenly widens into a narrow grove of trees.  On the other side of the cave-like opening, a clearing can be seen to the southeast.  A tiny waterfall trickles over a pile of rocks before flowing into the forest where it can no longer be seen.  The trees are spaced apart, making many deep places for something to hide.

The path opens up to a peaceful clearing that has a shrine standing amidst the trees. The shrine looks to be built of white rock. No monster dares set foot upon this sacred land. There is a big flock of birds here. Chirping happily the birds seem to ignore everything that happens around them and just keep to themselves. Four pillars that hold up a block form an entrance of some sort, but the entrance looks to be blocked...

The path runs through a valley in between two cliffs.  The valley widens as it goes east until it opens into a wide clearing.  A large tree stump stands near the middle of the path, its roots overgrown with yellow flowers.

The path runs between the sea of trees to the west and a high cliff to the east.  Light shines in from above, illuminating the natural garden growing in the path.  The ground is almost covered in blue-green grasses, rich green bushes, and deep purple flowers.

Most of the wide tree trunks grow so closely together that there is no way to get through.  A thin path curves and branches through the dense forest like a stream, splitting off in different directions.  Interlocking tree branches almost completely cover the twisting path in deep shade.

A long underground corridor bends around sharply and comes to a small staircase.  Its stairs are carved right into the wall of the corridor and lead up towards the surface.  The passageway through the mountain is dark and narrow, and loose pieces of rock on the floor make for hazardous footing.

The path to the west is lost as a massive clearing opens up around a crystal blue stream.  A branch of the stream flows from north to south over a small ridge of pale blue rock, making a waterfall that sparkles in the light, slowly trickling to the ground.  The shallow stream makes a path to the southeast.

The path comes to a dead stop at a small grove covered in grass and surrounded by a wall of trees.  Crossing branches stretch out over the path on all sides, covering the ground in rich blue-green shade.  At the ends of the branches, the outermost leaves shine in the light.

Water from a waterfall to the north has spread out into a large pool of clear water.  The west side of the pool narrows into a stream that bends around the rocks to flow southwest.  A few bushes have grown up around the edge of the pool.

A branch of the stream, originating at a large pool to the north, flows south through the clearing.  This northern end of the clearing lies on top of a ridge of rock, overlooking the converging streams and pool to the south.  A taller ridge to the north walls this place in.

The vegetation has grown really dense and is obscuring and hindering sight. Even seeing the sky is starting to get really hard. The sun is slightly shining through the thick roof of leaves and branches. Majestic stone stairs can be seen to the north. They seem to lead high above the trees into an arena-like structure.

Tall rock cliffs circle a starkly empty round clearing.  Snow sticks to the sides of the cliffs and blankets the ground with white.  Only a few frozen flowers and some patches of grass are left poking through the snow.

A beautiful circle of trees is nestled between high mountain walls, covering the ground in shade and almost completely hiding a large opening in the rock.  The edges of the mountain curve around on all sides until they nearly touch, leaving only one small pass to the north.  Dozens of tiny yellow flowers grow among the thick bushes.

A tranquil looking clearing complete with a gently flowing brook. Strangely, there are no flowers growing around here. There is even a tiny waterfall causing a faint rumbling sound. The sounds from the waterfall is not enough to cover the ever present chirping of birds. A twin set of pedestals are standing on the both sides of the small brook.

The ground suddenly sinks, making a ridge of rock, then becomes a dead end surrounded by trees.  Two ledges are carved into the rock, shaped like steps.  Leading to and from the steps is a road made of flat blue rocks, overgrown with grass and only faintly visible.

The path arcs to the left, somewhere east. It runs through an old ruin of some sort. Pedestals still stand proudly and by the looks of it, they are really old. Moss has been growing on the pedestals for some time now. It must be the barrier around Pure Land, that is preserving the old structures as if they were new and allowing everything to grow so freely. There are birds sitting on the pedestals. The cheery little birds are chirping happily to each other and peering curiously at the occasional adventurer.

Light from outside dimly reflects off the shining rock walls of a room-sized cavern.  The inner walls of the mountain are a cool shade of blue.  Tufts of grass grow on the floor near the walls of the cavern.  A stairway, carved into the rock, leads down into the roots of the mountain.

There is an opening in the trees as the path follows the side of a high, pale blue cliff to the east.  A single tree stands beside the wall of rock, its many roots stretching out into the path.  Yellow flowers grow scattered around it in its shade.

In the midst of the green trees, beautiful flowers still bloom. These flowers seem to enjoy the vast shade the trees offer them. A narrow path has been stomped on the soft grassy floor. It runs up a stony cliff and continues north, past the flowers and under the majestic trees. A faint glitter from rain dew shines in the sun shine.

A small shrine built of white rock stands in this small clearing, bathed in warm light.  A decorated platform lies open to the sun, adorned with pillars that make an entrance to some separate part of the forest.  Nothing disturbs the sanctity of this shrine except the grass that slowly grows over its stones.

The air is unusually cold.  Grass and flowers still grow along the path, but are fully covered in a layer of frost.  Glittering snowflakes lie on the rocks and leaves, making them sparkle like blue and green crystal as pale light reflects all around.

A flat rock ledge sits near the west side of a huge cavern, up against the northern wall.  A very tall flight of stairs has been painstakingly carved in the wall of the cavern, leading up towards the surface.  The rocky floor below is covered in puddles of water.

This cavern in the mountain's inside is more like the center of a raging furnace.  The air is searingly hot, and the walls glow intensely, filling the room with a glaring orange color resembling molten steel.  The rocks in the floor are dark and scorched.

The path follows along the west side of a large mountain.  The densely packed trees make way for the towering rock, letting bright light pour in.  A few loose rocks lie in the grass, warmed by the heat of the sun.  The center of the path is covered with thick patches of leafy bushes.

Short grasses somehow manage to grow all over the floor of the dark, underground passage, in between puddles of muddy water.  The path narrows into a corridor leading south, and a large hole in the northern wall leads to a bigger part of the cavern.

There is a path going through a low rocky hillside. The path zigzags through the seemingly safe terrain to the other side. Not even one tree grows on this clearing. Sure, there are trees in the edges, but not in the middle. Even the flowers have made room for this rock 'structure'. Only the ever persistent moss grows on the rocky hillside.

A grassy path ends at the southern side of a mountain, blocked by the dense trees that grow all along the east side.  To the south, the trees move away from the mountain, and their leaves shine brilliantly in the light.  A worn trail in the grass leads to a large, dark opening in the mountain's base.

The narrow path travels in a perfectly straight line, from north to south.  Bare patches of earth are scattered around the path, as well as many purple and yellow wildflowers.  Light shines in through a larger opening in the trees to the north.

Two branches of the stream, one from the northwest and one from the northeast, come together in a graceful curve and make a wide, clear pool.  The water flows over a tall cliff to the south, making a waterfall.  A small grassy area lies beside the pool, to the east.

A large clearing sprawls out to the east and south.  Two paths lead out of the clearing; one wide path to the west and a faint, narrow path to the northwest, heading towards a large opening in the rockface of a cliff.  A sparkling stream flows by, heading south.

The thin, grassy path follows alongside a flat mountain that resembles a plateau.  Bright yellow flowers grow all over the path, their petals gleaming in the sunlight.  An opening near the end of the path leads to a cavern inside the mountain.

The shade is deep and intense as the overhanging branches above weave a tight mesh of leaves.  The grassy floor makes way for a patch of bare earth here and there, where there is no longer enough light for it to grow.

The walls of this cavern shine with dim specks of light from the forest outside.  The veins of pale blue rock deepen in color near the bottom until they reach the sapphire blue floor.  A long, narrow stairway in the south wall leads down into the darkness.

This grassy area by the side of the stream is closed in by the pale blue rock ridges to the north and the great trees to the east and south.  Tree branches hang overhead, completing this sheltered hideaway.  The ground is covered with soft, tall grass and tiny yellow flowers, whose colors stand out in the darkness of the shade like stars in the sky.

A rocky clearing that has only a little of the green grass in the edges. Something has destroyed the nature here, scorched marks everywhere. Broken down pedestals and tree stumps that look like they have been struck by lightning a few times. Signs of battle can also be seen everywhere around the clearing.

A wide, clear path runs directly north to south through the forest.  Rows of trees grow right next to each other, their branches crossing and entwining into a tightly knit ceiling of branches and leaves.  In the center of the path, light sneaks in through a crack in the ceiling as the branches on each side of the path stretch out towards each other.

This clearing looks like it is made for battling, almost like an arena of some sort. There are no obstacles to hinder fighting in sight, not even a loose pebble on the ground, as if has swept clean by a strong gust of wind. The ground is charred black in some spots, almost as if struck by lightning, but lightning doesn't strike the same place twice... or does it?

A shallow pool rests in the ground, fed by a wide waterfall that falls from the northern cliff.  The water looks crystal blue and is icy cold.  Large chunks of rock stand near the south edge, forcing the water to branch off into two streams, each on opposite ends of the pool.

The path forks into two paths. The one that leads northeast is a dark one, shrouded with vegetation, it is not an easy path to even notice. The west one is a bit lighter one. The sun is shining high above the trees and lighting up the dew on the flowers. Some bushes have grown in the path but it is nothing a few swings of a sword can't fix.

The northeast corner of the cavern is taken up by a flat ledge of rock, which is covered in small tufts of grass.  A small flight of steps, carved into the side of the ledge, leads back down to the ground.  Stalactites in the ceiling drip water down to the cavern below.

Many leafy bushes grow in the shade of the trees.  To the east, the trees suddenly disperse as a large, bright clearing and a stream come into view.  Yellow flowers in patches of tall grass are scattered around the edges of the path.

The narrow path seems to be changing from the stomped grassy ground to a more harder terrain. Somehow, even the rockier terrain around here seems to be fertile enough to be able some life to plants. There are numerous flowers growing on the rocky surface and not to forget the normal moss that grows on rocks. It might truly be that the barrier around the Pure Land is giving every living organism a fair chance to grow anywhere they wish to.

As the east branch of the stream flows from a large pool to the north, two miniature waterfalls ripple over a stair-shaped path between two rock ridges, making a gentle current.  On top of the ridge to the west, a risen piece of land splits the stream, forming a small circle as it flows southwest.

Before you is a large building bearing a sign of a sword and a shield over the doorway, which must be the general store. The building, however, continues a little to the east, where another door can be seen. The path here splits three ways.
A small place in the general store dedicated to the selling of armor, you may purchase a variety of equipment here. The man behind the counter points to a sign.

This is the item shop section of this general store. There is a table with three chairs just inside the entrance, allowing you to take a reprieve while you look around. The man behind the counter points to a sign.

The inn here looks hospitable, and the combination of lighting and pleasant-smelling flowers makes it even more inviting. The man behind the counter smiles genuinely at you upon your entrance, and gestures towards a sign.

In the center of this room is an empty bed which is surrounded by many golden vases holding sets of red roses. The room is otherwise barren, down to the brick floor and walls. There is a sense of uneasiness here, as it appears to be a deathbed.

The path from the entrance splits two ways: one to the north, towards another bridge; the other to the west, which leads past the inn next to you. The grass here is mostly dead, and the bushes' leaves are brown, indicitive of the slow healing process seeking to undo Kefka's damage.

This segment of the path ends before a small, wooden bridge, similar to the one at the entrance to town. Past the bridge, a single house can be seen sitting across the creek. The small patch of flowery bushes that adorn this place are obviously well-kept, and an elderly lady stands in the nearby shade, remembering pleasant days from the past.

This is the eastern side of the general store, along with a second entrance leading to what appears to be the item shop, judging by the sign over the doorway. The path continues east, towards a bridge, and west towards a three-way junction in the path. While the path does not extend north, there is a grassy walkway that direction, where a small group of people have gathered.

This house is well-furnished: a pair of beds, a bookcase, and a grandfather clock, among other things. Despite being in good upkeep, it doesn't seem that anyone lives here. The town residents must be responsible for maintaining this place, though for what reason they go through the trouble is anyone's guess.

The grassy path leads into a ridge here, stopping northward movement. However, a small bridge is to the east, crossing the creek at another bend. A couple people have gathered here around a small sapling, admiring it as it steadily grows in this slowly recovering land.

The cobbled path ends, leaving a small grass path to a small house. The house seems to be vacant, yet also appears to be kept in good shape. There is no indication of who used to live here, or who takes care of the house now, but it is obviously in good hands. With the forest surrounding the rise the house sits upon, this appears to be a dead end.

A little bridge covering the small stream beneath you serves as the entrance to this town. Just before you is the village of Kohlingen, which has suffered under the power of Kefka along with the rest of the world. The flow of time has brought new life, however, and the lives of the people begin anew.

This, apparently, is the house's kitchen. Furnished with a table, chairs, and a small stove, this area also does not appear to have been used; although it seems that someone has been taking care of this place. There is a desk in the corner, with a book on it.

There is a single house in front of you, residing alone on this side of the creek. There are a couple barrels in front of the house, adding to the simple look of the place. The house sits upon a small rise, created by the bank of the creek, and is surrounded by trees. The exits are across the bridges to the west or to the south.

This is the room that contains the beds for patrons to sleep in. Aside from the beds, the simple table, and the rug, the room is rather unfurnished. Small lanterns hang from the walls, illuminating the room and providing warmth. The sound of people talking can be heard to the east.
This house is in pretty bad shape.  It seems a fire must have hit the house, or perhaps it's a remnant from Kefka's reign of destruction.  It's certainly not inhabited, or at least, not permanently.

This lounge acts as the town pub. It is a gathering place for locals who wish to talk with travelers, or amongst themselves. A couple tables with chairs are in the room, while behind the counter, the bartender carries on a conversation with a customer.

A tiny clearing is here, a small cavity cut out of the forest next to the town. Many tree stumps dot the ground, but is the lesser of the displays of devastation here. Scorch marks marr the ground, and in the center of the clearing is a badly damaged house. The small path continues north and east.
This section of the store is the weapon shop. Behind the counter, you see many different types of weapons. The man behind the counter is pointing to a sign.

This room is plainly furnished with a bed, a table with two chairs, and a crate. The exception to this is a rather ornate-looking set of armor, standing upright against the far wall. There is a set of stairs on the west wall, leading into a basement.

The largest building in town is here, and judging by the sign, it is both the local inn and pub. The path that runs along here continues west, and also curves north to the east. Several citizens are milling around here, talking about good times from the past, and the rebuilding for the future.

The sounds of the sea are faint, although little other than water can be seen. While a small bit of the path sticks out, overlooking the endless blue below, it otherwise becomes quite narrow as it bends and snakes its way around the mountain. The trail leads down to the base of the mountain, and it continues up a steep incline to the peak of Solitary Mountain.

A badly damaged house, although still standing, has seemed to withstand abuse by nature enough to serve as viable housing for someone. A few dead bushes and a dilapidated fence serve as an appropriate kind of scenery for a house on an island that, some day in the past, may have been beautiful. To the south, a serene beach is visible.

A large mountain rises amid this desolate wasteland, and even more strange than that, it seems to have no problem supporting life, as the trail that leads up the mountain gradually becomes more and more grassy in contrast to the wasteland it comes from. The mountain appears to be a great scouting point for the island as well as the sea. A slight scent of salt water can be detected in the air and on the breeze.

The trail up the mountain ends at the summit, high above sea level. The edges of the peak break off into cliffs all around, providing an unobstructed view of land, sea and sky. The sun shines above and off of the water, hitting the grassy floor swaying in the breeze, giving this small area the illusion of a strangely magical glow. The entire island is visible from this spot, while nothing but an endless sapphire blue is visible beyond, stretching into the horizon in all directions. The trail heads down, the only sane way to exit the mountain.

Oddly serene, this beach seems capable of fully supporting life, both on the land and in the water. The gentle waves edge upon the shore before retreating back into the sea, while a gentle breeze cools the area and carries moisture to land. Small plants break through areas of less sand, while schools of fish can be seen not far from the shoreline. To the north, a scorched house is visible.

The rocky cliffs of Solitary Mountain overlook the vast, sapphire sea beyond its edges. Wind whistles through the crags as waves crash into the mountain, sending up sea spray to dampen everything around. The grassy trail upwards is littered with stones and boulders, while the land slowly turns to wasteland down the trail to ground level.

Contrasting with the damaged appearance of the outside of the house, the inside of the house has been taken care of well and shows little to no sign of disarray. There is a working stove, a spacious bed, and a table with a chair and vase of flowers. A flickering light on the wall makes visibility in the room difficult, but not impossible. The only way out is through the door to the south.

A sturdy, smooth floor spreads out in a well-lit, enclosed area. Lights shine brightly along the ceiling as the walkway runs from north to south. A soft humming sound can be heard coming from around the hallway leading south, while an elevator door leads up to the city.

Compared to the rest of the machinery-filled reactor, this room is fairly quiet. A few large pipes lead across the ceiling. Multiple display panels and controls line the walls, giving readouts and reports of almost every aspect of the reactor. Lights shine and flicker from displays everywhere in the room. A sliding door sets on the eastern side of the room, with another smaller one on the southern wall on the western side.

A red arrow is painted on the floor pointing north.  A red 'exit' sign hangs from the ceiling, visible when one is looking north.  A yellow number '02' is painted on a large, aluminum ventilation tube running along the eastern wall.  Additionally, 'L.2-16' is painted in yellow on the tube further south.  Another arrow is painted on the floor leading south.

A metallic docking area extends out over a mostly calm body of water. A large crane can be seen hanging down from a track on the ceiling. The dock itself is clear, save for a few crates stacked up in the far corners. A catwalk can be seen going along the southern wall high above, leading to a couple doors out of reach from here.

Metal pipes run along the bottom of the tunnel walls, connecting ventilation units with one another. This smooth, paved road is enclosed in a concrete tunnel, with lights hanging from the ceiling, and dual rows of small lights also shining along the sides of the road. A steel door at the base of the grade leads off to an underground area.

Beneath the waves, a clear glass tunnel stretches along the ocean floor. The ocean life is visible through the glass. Arches of metal hold up the clear dome along the path, supporting the massive weight of the ocean somehow. Coral reefs, seaweed, and different marine life float about on the ocean floor. The fish do not seem afraid of the tunnel and many of them swim right up to the glass.

The clear glass tunnel extends beneath the waves, along the ocean floor, leading to the Underwater Reactor. The metal arches that hold up the glass dome do little to detract from the beauty of this undersea paradise. Various types of fish swim through the ocean amidst the coral reefs and seaweed on the outside of this tunnel.

Loud, constant humming fills a small, cramped room. It might not seem so small if not for the fact that most of it is taken up by large machines. Only a small path leads through from one end to the other. A metal grate covers the entire floor. Underneath the grating, water can be seen flowing quickly as gusts of steam blow up from within.

The stone and cement floor continues to slope downhill to the south, leading further underground. On the ceiling, a light flickers on and off. A mechanical humming sound can be heard constantly, growing louder as one descends deeper. A couple sets of stairs break the smoothness of the floor.

A skinny, grated metal walkway extends along the wall of a large room, with metal handrails rising up along the sides to prevent any needless accidents. The room below seems to be some sort of docking area, with a large basin of water filling most of the area. A large crane can be seen hanging down from a track on the ceiling, which leads to an adjoining room to the west.

Outside of the glass walls that make up this underwater tunnel, sea life frolicks beneath the waves. Small signs are attached to the inside of the glass, identifying some of the more common fish that one might see. The larger fish seem to be drawn to the reactor at the north end of the tunnel, which rises up from the ocean's floor above the clear dome.

A large structure which once was the storage place for a Huge Materia dominates the area between the submarine docks and the reactor.  Many red lasers surround the perimeter of the structure, acting as a security system.  Metal pipes jut out from the walls of the structure, connecting with the reactor in many locations, and submerge deep within the ocean under the walkway which provides travel between the reactor and the docks.

Pipes, and lots of them. Small pipes, long pipes, wide pipes, any size and shape imagineable criss-cross throughout the room. They all converge in a bubbling pool of water below the grated catwalk. The catwalk leads to a large mechanical structure ahead that apparently used to be the core of the mako reactor. Now it's been converted to a steam generator, and there's plenty of water for it to use.

Metal rails rise from the floor providing structural support to the walkway, allowing easier travel throughout the reactor. Handrails surrounding both sides of the catwalk exist to keep those walking on it from falling off. Below the catwalk are two submarine loading bays, complete with ramps for providing crew members with a high enough point to enter even the largest submarines.

Once used as a loading and unloading port for submarines, this dock is seemingly abandoned.  A metal guard rail is in place along the wooden bridge to prevent dockworkers from falling into the ocean.  A passage to the west leads the way up to Junon, or further below to the Underwater Reactor.

Poor lighting and a lack of space make this room a not-so-comfortable place. The ceiling is not very high overhead, and various wires pipes hang from along its length. The sound of rushing water can be heard constantly in the pipes. Condensation drips from the piping. Below the grated floor, nothing much can be seen, save for a lingering mist and fog. The grated path exits out on either side in a west-east direction, with the western side taking a northern turn.

A long staircase takes up most of this end of the walkway. Tiny lights glow on each metal step. At the bottom of the stairs, an elevator waits to take passengers down to the next level. The base of the stairs has a large amount of machinery around the elevator door, which seems to lead to the source of the incessant humming.

Stone blocks form a perimeter around the cement floor throughout the path. A red arrow is painted on a block of stone, pointing north towards the elevator. A ventilation duct is set in the floor along the southern wall and the path continues to the south.

rooms.name: An Intersection of the South Hall

userData.LongDescription: The hall from the north seems like it almost didn't stop here. A short path leads south from the intersection, though it quickly halts as the open path becomes a brick wall. A pillar resides at each corner of the intersection, holding a flaming torch for light. This intersection is formed by a path leading east, one leading west, and still another leading north.

This ledge skirts the edge of a deep pit. The pit spans most of the room in fact, only leaving this small walking space along the north and west walls. A bridge extends out from the southeast and circles around through the middle of the room to reconnect with a staircase to the southwest. Ghostly flames float in mid-air tracing the bridge. A doorway here leads north, and the ledge extends to the east.

Three paths branch out from here to explore the extents of the area. All of the paths traverse the heights above a dark pit from which there is no return. The first path leads east to a staircase. The second leads southwest to a weird ball. The third leads south toward the other side of the pit.

The cavern is very warm and humid. A mist permeates through any coverings to saturate the skin of those who travel below the structure. The red, glowing floor suggests it was once running magma, although it has been cooled recently. The parts of the cavern to the southeast are somewhat obscured by the mist. However, a staircase here leads up and out of the pervading substance.

This room is barren and empty. The north wall has odd patterns of metal nailed to it. In several of the corners, a buildup of dust sits quietly, growing with the passage of time. It is very likely that this room hasn't been used in a long time. The only way to go is south.

From this vantage point, the short walls seem to be a kind of filter to force an orderly progression to the dais in the back of the room. Unfortunately, since most of the paths are blocked by fire, there is very limited access.

rooms.name: A Hall in the Fire Palace

userData.LongDescription: Strong heat appears to be common to this ancient building which seems to be caused by a large number of burning braziers scattered throughout the halls. This brief hall leads to an arched doorway in the north wall. The path follows through, passing between two large braziers, and it also passes to the west, leading to the main entrance.

This small platform lies at the base of a staircase. To the west is a minor dais. Another, lower level platform to the south cuts sharply around a wall, forming an unseen path. A waft of cool air passes through, suggesting the entrance is not far off.

The northwest corner of the path edges near to the pit. The path shrinks slightly as it passes along a diagonal before proceeding on its way. The south path leads to one of the accesses to the room while the east path leads to another corner of the path.

rooms.name: The South Side of a Pit

userData.LongDescription: Two walkways intersect, forming a small platform along the south wall. A dark pit greets those foolish enough to look down. The walkway which extends to the east runs between two walls, leaving the pit behind. The walkway which extends to the north runs over the pit to the north wall of the room.

This is a wide and open room, taking up most of the entire fifth floor. The red walls are scarred with a number of gashes. The brown floor is littered with many gouges. Apparently, something extremely big and heavy has spent a great deal of time stuck here, and it seems to have been bored for a long time.

rooms.name: At the Edge of a Pit

userData.LongDescription: A walkway begins here, bordered on one side by a pit, on another by a wall, and on still a third by a staircase. The dark pit seems like just a small chasm cutting off a platform which lies a short distance to the east. The walkway continues west to intersect another. The staircase would lead adventurers down, nearer to the way out.

A dark corridor greets travellers and would-be adventurers leading into a deepening darkness. Through the other side, a small point of light is visible, though movement within the corridor is completely shadowed. A walkway lined with strange, floating flames leads south while the corridor leads north.

The desert has given way to a veritable oasis. Many lush palm trees grow unchecked along this path. The heat of the desert is eased, slightly, by the shade that the trees provide, and the hot winds have been slowed nearly to stillness. Even so, the bright sun intensely beats down on the area. The path leads south to Kakkara Desert and also extends further east to a set of stone stairs.

This room is empty and barren. The red, brick walls are dulled in colour compared to the strong reds in the rest of the building. Cobwebs in the corners of the room are evidence that this room has not been used in quite some time. The only exit from this room leads south.

This ancient structure is marked with hints of a strong relationship with fire. Hot air and red walls are just two clues which manifest the ancient mysticism of this place. A pair of large braziers stand to either side of the entrance, holding brightly burning flames. Two paths lead east and west, while a third leads north to an impassably steep incline. The main entrance is here, allowing swift travel to the outside.

rooms.name: East End of the South Hall

userData.LongDescription: This end of the south hall leads into a dead end. A number of pillars at this end hold braces with torches which provide light, but there is nothing more to this closed-off little corner. The hallway extends to the west, leading into an intersection and further.

This hallway follows a north-south orientation leading from one intersection to another. An intersection used to exist at this point, but two braziers containing hot flames have been placed to block the west and east paths. The hallway continues to the north and south.

As the walkway runs along the southern wall, it widens into a small platform. From this platform, three paths extend; one leads west, another north, and still another east. The north path is lined with mysterious flames floating above the pit. The west path runs safely along the wall, while the east path immediately halts at the base of a staircase.

This is a fairly small room which holds several walls of unknown purpose. Each wall runs north-south, and, except for two, the paths are blocked by flames. One of the southbound paths is traversable while there is one northbound path visible to the east.

This room is enclosed by walls on all sides. The east and west walls, however, stop short of the ceiling, forming ledges to walk upon. Going north and climbing a set of stairs leads to the top of a high platform. There is another set of stairs which leads up to the third floor.

rooms.name: An Intersection of the North Hall

userData.LongDescription: At this intersection, it seems like the builders wanted to make a path headed north, but it quickly runs into a brick wall. Torches in pillars at the corners of the intersection provide light for the area. The hall is made of a path which extends both east and west as well as a path which extends south.

This is one of two accesses into this room. The south path runs into a corner before turning northwest. The north path circumnavigates the edge of a fiery pit. The other access point is across a small chasm to the east.

The main entrance is directly to the south, but a steep, slippery slide stands in the way. The slide is made of some smooth, black rock and coated with an odd kind of grease. While it is possible to slide down, it would not be possible to climb back. The only other way to go is north.

Rising up from the floor, this dais cuts through a wall to connect two rooms. Centered upon the floor of the dais lies a rather large, depressed button. Its purpose is not immediately obvious, but the fact that it is depressed suggests the mechanism has already been activated. Along the west side of the dais, a path runs southward through a doorway. Apparently, the other side is accessed from another part of the structure.

The hallway runs into a corner coming in from the east and south. To the south, the eastern wall takes a short leave of absence opening out into a lower chamber but leaving no immediate point of access. To the east, the hallway turns south. A light waft of air circulates within the area.

rooms.name: A Hallway in the Fire Palace

userData.LongDescription: This appears to be the east end of a hallway. Humidity in this area is high, likely coming up from the basement. A doorway in the north wall leads to a barren room. The corridor otherwise continues to the west. A staircase leads down into the basement.

The path runs along the top of a wall separating two distinct rooms. The path runs north, into an intersection, and it runs south, ending in a staircase leading downward. On the other side of the west room, another ledge can be seen running north-south along a wall.

A path would normally lead west, except that it is blocked by a burning brazier as big as oxen. Two staircases serve as a means of travelling onward - one leads up, the other down. The close proximity and lack of air flow cause the smell of burning sulfur to dominate in the air.

Atop this landing, another landing to the west is visible across a short chasm. Someone has rigged a rope between the two, connecting each end to an oddly placed rod atop each platform. The rope serves to connect the platforms, providing a means of travel across the gap. There is also a staircase leading downward.

This small room is simple and empty. A pattern of metal on the wall acts as a meager decoration in this otherwise unremarkable room. Pillars in each of the corners of the room holds a torch to light the room. The only direction of travel is south, through the dark corridor.

This room extends to the north in the form of a wide hall with two thick walls splitting it into three distinct paths. At the far end of the outer paths, large red flames can be seen burning strongly. There is also a set of red-tinged stairs leading upward.

This room seems like more of a cell; it has no decorations and no furnishings. The walls are bare brick, leaving nothing to appease the eye. As well, the lack of ventilation has made the air hot and stale. The only way to go would be through the south doorway.

This massive room engorges the whole of the fourth floor. Within it are two score bronze braziers. Strangely, two by the southeast corner are the only ones alight with fire. A staircase in the south area of the room leads downward while a staircase in the center of the room leads up.

rooms.name: East End of the North Hall

userData.LongDescription: This is the east end of a hallway. A slight indent in the northern wall is sided by two pillars, each holding a torch for light. The hallway continues west to, and past, an intersection. A downward-leading staircase takes its place in the south wall.

The cliff face rises high, looming over this ridge and blocking out the hot sun. Several vultures perch atop the cliff, waiting, watching for some poor soul to lose his strength in the desert. A path extends to the west, and an odd set of stairs provides a means of getting down from the ridge.

The ceiling and walls of the large recess stop suddenly, giving way to red brick and white wood which forms a wall with a door in its midst. The door is formed of the white wood and sits atop a minor stage. Two white pillars flank the door, and four small steps lead up to it. The opening of the niche lies to the south.

rooms.name: A Hall in The Fire Palace

userData.LongDescription: Strong heat is the most prevalent sensation in this hall. The air is heated by two immediate braziers containing crackling flames. The hall itself is fairly small, simply serving as a branch between the main entrance to the east and an arched doorway to the north.

rooms.name: West End of the South Hall

userData.LongDescription: This end of the southern hall forms a corner between two paths. Several pillars here hold torches which provide light. The path to the north seems to go a distance then halt and take a turn to the east. The path to the east leads into an intersection which also leads further east and north.

Atop the ridge, the cliff face has broken apart, leaving high and wide a recess within the mount. Of particular note are four white pillars which appear to be holding up the ceiling of this oversized niche. Toward the north, a large door is visible in the darkness. Toward the east, the ridge leads to some stone stairs.

From atop this landing, another platform is visible to the east. A chasm separates the two, though someone has erected a rope connecting a short rod on each landing. A staircase leads down from the landing to a lower room. Below the chasm, a ledge can be seen running atop a wall and serving to separate two rooms.

An odd set of stone stairs is an unusual find in the midst of a desert. The stone is chiseled and smooth meaning someone carved the stairs, so they must lead somewhere. For now, all that can be seen is that they lead to a higher ridge. A path stretches out to the west, leading toward the open desert.

The hallway opens up on the east side, looking down at the base of a staircase coming in from a higher floor. Across the room, a short wall separates another room, while also acting as a walkway. The rest of the path leads southwest, into a corner, or north, into an east-facing bend.

rooms.name: At the base of a staircase

userData.LongDescription: There is not much to this path. A staircase leads sharply upward to the second floor while the path runs around a southward-leading wall. The western wall generally blocks this area from all sight, and a scraping mark on the ground suggests the wall extends and retracts to hide this staircase entirely.

The stage of the Fire Seed is a five-tiered pyramid with the seed sitting atop the highest tier of all. A semi-circle of bronze, burning braziers surrounds the stage symbolically protecting the seed. Along the back wall, a yellow, stained glass window filters in light, providing a bright atmosphere.

This narrow walkway is sandwiched between two very deep pits. The pits are so deep that their bottoms cannot be seen. Small fires float in mid-air, surrounding the walkway and providing enough light for this room. The fuel that keeps those floating flames burning is a mystery. A staircase just a few paces south leads into the depths of this building while the walkway extends to the east.

Two burning braziers flank a staircase in the midst of this hallway. The heat of the braziers has caused portions of the wall behind them to char and become black with soot. The hallway extends both east and west while an arched doorway leads south. The staircase leads up.

This is the east access into the pit room. The northward path travels in a rough circle around the room until it passes southward through the other access which lies just to the west. A small chasm separates the two accesses. The southward path leads to a corner before turning, again.

A dark pit envelopes a great portion of this room. A long ledge hugs the wall along the north and west walls, while another ledge runs from the southeast portion of the room around through the middle to the southwest portion of the room. Unfortunately, the ledges are not connected. This ledge extends to the west, and an arched doorway leads north.

The west and south paths converge, creating a diagonal path to connect them. In so doing, the diagonal path is slightly thinner and brings the wall dangerously close to the edge of the fiery pit. To the south is one access into the pit room. To the west, then south is the other.

Dropping slightly below the rest of the level, this platform wraps around a wall, following it back northward. Unusual scrapings on the ground suggest this wall retracts and extends in order to block the progress of travel. To the northeast lies a staircase leading upward. To the northwest lies another staircase leading upward and a small, raised dais.

The hallway forms a minor T-intersection with the east branch quickly running into a dead end. The west branch turns southward, while the south branch runs along the top of a wall which seperates two rooms. The two walls that border the south branch form two platforms just beneath the ceiling. A rope can be seen crossing the intervening gap, above.

rooms.name: A hallway in the Fire Palace

userData.LongDescription: This appears to be the west end of a hallway. There is a heat buildup in this area, likely caused by a lack of circulating air. A doorway in the north wall leads to a barren room while a doorway in the south wall leads onto a ledge. The corridor otherwise continues to the east.

rooms.name: West End of the North Hall

userData.LongDescription: This is the west end of the hallway. Two pillars flank a staircase, providing light from torches which are held in mounted braces. The torches provide enough light for sight, but are obviously not the source of the warmth within this structure. The hall extends east to an intersection while a staircase leads down.

rooms.name: The Lower Side of a Dais.

userData.LongDescription: This deadend path runs around the base of a dais with no way up. Atop the dais, four braziers alit with flames stand in each corner. Apparently, the Dais runs between two separate rooms as noted by the walls that stop at the its edge. A doorway to the south leads back toward the main entrance.

A deep, dark pit greets any who would fall off the sides of the narrow walkway. Although this room is fairly wide, there is no connection to the other path which skirts the wall on the north and west sides. This walkway does, however, curve around to a staircase to the west. Otherwise, the only way to go is to the south, toward the main entrance of the building.

This small platform runs along the wall of the room and holds enough space for just a few steps in any direction. The edge of the pit runs close, though far enough away to hold some measure of comfort. There is only one walkway leaving this platform, and it leads northeast.

The floor of this cavern is coated by a pool of magma. This area of the cavern lies in the south portion, but crossing to the north portion requires some ingenuity. To the north, another staircase, which leads up, is visible. A staircase here also leads up.

The hallway comes in from the south to this place. A staircase leads down, deeper into the bowels of the structure. A large brazier holds a brightly burning fire, giving off more than enough light to make the entire area visible.

The dais is raised up as high as a man is tall with finely cut stone stairs leading up to it. Atop the dais nothing is visible but for a large, sun-shaped, ornate, stained-glass window. From up here, the whole room is clearly visible. The placement of the fires almost seem as if they follow some kind of pattern...

Having come from one staircase, another continues the journey. This landing is a break in the stairs. The stairs leading upward stop at a platform while the stairs leading downward end in dimness. The western wall does not run all the way to the ceiling, leaving a ledge along which to walk.

This short hallway comes in from the southeast and ends in an upward-leading staircase. The repugnant smell of hotly burning sulfur lightly flutters through, cruelly stealing away from the fresh air. Fleeting shadows, created by flickering lights, can be seen dancing wildly to the southeast.

Pure elemental energy suffuses this realm, to the extent that nearly nothing else exists.  There are no perceivable floor, walls, ceiling, just mana.  It is a realm beyond mortal comprehension, and is where the most powerful of elemental beings reside.

This is a corner before a circular room. To the north, the path can be seen twisting around the outside of a fiery pit. The smell of burning ash and sulfur invades the air, choking the breath from anything living. The stairs to the northwest suddenly appear slightly more inviting in that they must lead away from the stench of sulfur.

The hallway forms into a corner, leading both north and northeast. The north path leads into a room smelling of putrid sulfur while the northeast path leads to one side of a large room. The rank odor of burning sulfur chokes the air.

This large bedroom most likely belongs to the king of Tasnica. Wide and wrapped in a plush purple carpet, the room glows slightly due to the kindle fire burning in the fireplace. A large king-sized bed stands with velvet curtains on the corner, and a small table with chairs provides a place to eat breakfast in the morning. A majestic armoire is against the wall for kingly wardrobes, and a door-window leads into the balcony, providing a nice view of the beach and sea.

All around are long rows of wooden tables with stools placed next to them. To the south end is what seems to be the cook's outlet for people to collect their food when it is time. A passage decorated by advertising banners is placed on the eastern wall through the raised platforms, leading to the Tasnican store. A small door is to the northern wall, leading into the Throne Room hallway.

Under a regal stone archway is a set of steps leading into the northern castle portion. To the south is a long road of cobblestone serving as the castle's rather boxed in courtyard. This area seems to be more a hallway than a meeting point, however, with the lack of room needed to assemble an army.

The peripheral walls, made from gray stone bricks, are octagonal in shape.  This entire floor is one large room, with a staircase in the middle of the room leading upward.  The ceiling is quite high, maybe thirty feet.  The windows are positioned too high to look through and see anything but the sky, but they effectively let light in during the day.  Massive double doors lead out to the beach.

The roof is above this floor of the lighthouse, which is much narrower at this height than at ground level.  Similar to the lower floors, a pair of balconies reaches out to the north through open archways.  The spotlight is on this floor, and shines out through an opening in the south wall.  There are no wires feeding power to the giant light; it must have an alternate method of energy.

The walls slope inward as the tower rises, though not nearly enough to have converged by the time they get to the roof.  A flight of stairs leads up and down, connecting this room to the nearly identical ones above and below it.  Two openings in the north wall lead out to short stone balconies, overlooking the picturesque beach.

rooms.name: Tasnica Castle, West Wing Storage Room

userData.LongDescription: This is a fairly small room apparently used as a storage area. Large wooden crates are stacked up in the corners, with a small bed and desk made for the warehouse guard on duty. A few lanterns are hung on the wall, providing some light to this otherwise dimmed room. A set of stairs are on the northern wall, and an opening on the east, leading into the throne hall.

rooms.name: Tasnica Castle, Hallway of Fame -- North End

userData.LongDescription: This long hallway was originally fairly empty, only designed as a connecting hallway between key destinations in the castle. However, it has since then been used to hang portraits of past Tasnican warriors who have done great deeds. Doors are placed on the northern and southern sides of the rooms.

The northern wall of the mess hall includes a large row of windows to peer further north, giving an excellent view of the forests. The large windows also allow plenty of sunlight to enter, giving adequate lighting to the room. The platform leads west and south, west leading down to the mess hall and south to the courtyard past a wooden door.

The eastern end of the main hallway contains a small wooden door with glass tiles upon it, showing a glimpse of the long paved courtyard outside. Flags and banners are hung high above with vivacious colors emblazoned upon them. Royal blue carpets cover the ground, pointing the pathways through Tasnica Castle.

This long hall is both used as a passageway and as a storage room. Large crates are stacked on top of each other, filling almost the entire room's space. Lanterns are hung on the wall, barely providing light to the room. To the north is an archway containing a set of stairs leading to the second floor. South leads to the main hallway of Tasnica Castle.

This long hall is almost entirely made out of stone, both from the cobblestone of the floor and the white concrete walls. A large set of steps leads north to a majestic set of doors into the Throne room of Tasnica. Off to the side of the hall is a little passageway branching into two doors.

Nearby is a set of stairs leading down to the mess hall proper. Large windows with excellent views of the bushy forests around are placed on the northern wall. East leads to a corner point in the raised platform, and to the southeast a wooden door leading into the castle courtyard.

This ferry is spick and span; unusually so, even for a passenger ship.  A trap door in the deck leads to quarters below.  The boat is bouncing gently in the waves, awaiting its captain's approval to head out.  This ferry uses sails rather than a motor, and the sails are currently down while the vessel is docked.

This is the main hallway of Tasnica Castle, impressive in size, functional for a meeting or speech hall before a battle or some such. To the far east is a wooden door leading to the eastern wing and courtyard of the castle, and to the west is an archway heading deeper into the storage area. Double doors are placed to the south, leading outside to the wharfs.

rooms.name: A ferry, docked at the lighthouse

userData.LongDescription: This ferry is spick and span; unusually so, even for a passenger ship.  A trap door in the deck leads to quarters below.  The boat is bouncing gently in the waves, awaiting its captain's approval to head out.  This ferry uses sails rather than a motor, and the sails are currently down while the vessel is docked.

The western end of the Main Hall contains a large, grand archway of stone that leads north into a storage room stacked full with crates. A path to the east leads into the main hallway. The walls are limestone, the floors cobblestone. Blue banners with the Tasnican logo are hung as a morale booster and for national pride.

This little room is home to Tasnica Castle's only store, though a pretty well-stocked one at that. Different kinds of merchandise, from swords and spears lined up in racks to magazines placed in a basket near the counter are available for sale. A wooden sign hangs on the wall nearby.

rooms.name: A raised deck atop the lighthouse

userData.LongDescription: This smaller platform is raised a good fifteen feet above the rest of the roof.  The view is prime, but the small floor area and lack of guardrails could be a bit unnerving for the queasy.  From this platform's position in the center of the roof, no part of the tiny island can even be seen, giving the illusion that the lighthouse is floating in the middle of the sea.  The steps back down to the main roof area are unsettlingly steep.

A pair of balconies in the north wall allow for a few steps out to see the ocean.  A pair of torches are present next to each of the balcony platforms, but are unlit.  In the center of the room, which has the same octagonal shape as the ground level, a stairway leads up, and another one directly below it leads down.

This gray stone tower stands tall on a tiny island in the middle of the sea.  The lighthouse itself looks to be several stories tall, four rows of windows being visible from this side.  A cobblestone path is leading to the entrance, but doesn't exactly lead from anywhere; the path just kind of ends at the beach, a short distance from the door.

This is the western corner of the throne hall, with three different paths available. A wooden door is to the north wall, a hallway to the west. To the southeast is the raised platform leading up to the throne room. The walls around are decorated with large banners and flags.

The Throne room of Tasnica is large, spacious, and majestic, of much what is to be expected from a regular throne room. Thick, lavish red carpets are rolled across the room. The throne is made out of pure gold with soft cushions, large and comfortable. Banners are hung all over the walls, and potted plants stand in the corners of the room.

This raised platform appears to form the borders of the Tasnica Castle mess hall, perhaps to keep the lunch hours in check should a fight break out. A set of stairs are to the northwest corner, leading down into the table rows proper. A wooden door is to the south, leading into the castle courtyard.

This small room does not hold much, only the stairs on the right side and a wooden door on the southern wall. A small wooden sign is hung on the wall as a guide for visitors. Portraits of past Tasnican heroes Jema, and Serin are hung on the wall as a commemoration of their past deeds.

rooms.name: Tasnica Castle, Hallway of Fame -- South End

userData.LongDescription: The Hallway of Fame is a long hallway built to commemorate the past warriors of Tasnica as a memorial service to their deeds. The passage stretches north-south, brightly illuminated by lanterns hanging on the wall. Portraits of Tasnican warriors are hung on the walls in an array with beautiful golden frames.

The roof of the lighthouse is paved with a blue stone, shaped into a pattern of hexagonal bricks.  It would be a long fall to the ground below, but a waist-high border around the perimeter is in place to prevent people from slipping.  The sky is wonderfully clear.  A steep flight of stairs leads up even further to a raised platform in the center of the roof.

This long courtyard is paved out of grey cobblestone, stretching north-south among limestone walls topped with blue roofs. On the northern and southern ends are grand stone archways with sets of steps leading up to wooden doors. A soft breeze blows through the castle, the air slightly salty with the smell of the sea.

Nearby is a large and strategically placed castle by the ocean shore, called Tasnica. It is the main headquarters of the rebels fighting against the Empire, and a powerful ally to the rebels. A naval-based castle, the main front of Tasnica castle resembles a large array of wharfs with battleships. To the north lies a paved road leading into the castle proper.

rooms.name: Tasnica Castle, Before the Throne Room Doors

userData.LongDescription: The large set of doors stands tall nearby, their intricate craftsmanship showing as a sign of royalty. Golden lion door knobs are attached on expensive mahogany doorleafs. Large blue flags and banners are hung all around the wall, showing the crest of Tasnica. The set of doors lead into the throne room, and south leads to the branching point in the throne hallway.

This large room serves as the outer of Owzer's two basement galleries. It has a rather high ceiling for a basement room, and the tall north wall houses two paintings in shallow alcoves. The central alcove hosts a wooden door, and above it hang two barely-lit lamps which give the room a brighter look than the rest of the basement. Three support pillars dot the southern half of the room, and floating in the air are... treasure chests? Their shadows are scattered across the floor, another testament to the bizarre nature of this place...

This is a narrow, somewhat Z-shaped corridor leading between the outer and inner basement galleries. Besides the plain brick walls and the continued slate grey pattern of the floor, there really isn't much here except a pair of identical wooden doors to the north, one lower and one upper. However, there is no trace of the entryway *into* this room; simply the two exit doors to the north. The darkness throws suspicious shadows everywhere.

This room, at the top of the stairs, is home to Owzer's many collected paintings. The rug from the upper gallery off to the north continues here. The gallery itself is made of alcoves, with two pedestals in the center of the room for displaying as well. There remaining four paintings are displayed here, and at the south end of the room is small bar and chairs, presumably for receptions.

This is the entrance foyer just before Owzer's innermost gallery, where his most treasured paintings are kept. Just inside the entryway is a small swath of the same carpet found in the house upstairs and a wooden door. Beyond the door is a wide, empty room and a double staircase that leads up to a raised dais where the gallery proper is located. The darkness and shadows here seem particularly... sinister.

rooms.name: Owzer's Mansion -- Top of Basement Stairs

userData.LongDescription: Just inside the secret door from the gallery is this small, square room. A large staircase with a thick oak bannister leads down into the basement, while the door in the south wall leads back out into the gallery. Some light comes in under the door, but otherwise this room is remarkably dark.

This extremely narrow corridor cuts through the dark basement like a scar. It's barely wide enough for a single person to stand in shoulder to shoulder, and there's hardly room for more than a handful of people single-file. At the end of the corridor is a treasure chest sitting flush against the far wall; it is open and has been open for some time, the contents long gone. The only way out is the door on the back wall.

This U-shaped room is the entrance to Owzer's basement. At the foot of the stairs hangs a trio of lamps and a short left turn through a hall into another perpendicular corridor. Heading down that corridor leads to another branch off to the right, at the end of which are two wooden doorways. Two paintings hang here: one of a door at the far end of the hall in an alcove, and one of a chair on the wall at the 'bend' of the U.

This room, at the top of the stairs, is home to Owzer's many collected paintings. At the top of the stairs is a bookcase and a suit of decorative armor, and the rug from the entry hallway resumes. The gallery itself is made of alcoves, with two pedestals in the center of the room for displaying as well. Four paintings hang here.

This room is the deepest gallery in Owzer's spacious basement. A wide, tall room, it is well-furnished and comfortable. On the left side of the room is a small fireplace and a suit of decorative armor; on the right a bookcase, an old urn, and a bucket. The center of the room has three rectangular rugs arranged in an arrowhead shape. The left and right rugs each have a table and chairs, and the center rug has a short stepstool. On the far wall, in a central shallow alcove, hangs a very large painting.

A narrow corridor, barely wide enough for one person to stand in it, runs straight ahead. A bucket lies on the floor where the corridor opens up to the left into a slightly wider area with three matching doors, a single lamp hanging on the wall between each. Somewhat unusually, behind the doors is a crawlspace, barely accessible through a small opening. The wall between the doors and the crawlspace is barely thick enough for any of the doors to go anywhere...

This dark, shadowy corridor is a little unusual. Entering from a portal in the back wall, one is immediately presented with a wide, short room. Immediately opposite the entrance is a door... one built so that it actually floats above the floor. Strange, but par for the course in Owzer's unusual home. The wall protrudes a bit to the left of the hanging door, and then retracts into another alcove, where a second, normal doorway leads out through a narrow hallway.

The entranceway of the giant mansion is actually nothing more than a long hallway leading to a wall. Two sets of stairs, one on the left and one on the right, lead up to slightly raised areas. A multicolored rug runs halfway to the wall; the remainder of the floor is done in slate grey tile. On the far wall is a hanging electric lamp, and a desk sits to the left. The lamp provides a nice warm glow all around when turned on.

To the east, south lies more sand, while to the north and west lies the impassable barrier of this desert.  Always a hostile and barren area, an open and empty treasure chest lies here, as well as the decaying form of a skeleton. A staircase leads back to the entrance.

Among the dry, unforgiving desert, an open treasure chest lies here. A lone cactus stands, shaking in the wind. To the east, south, and west lies a prodigous amount of sand. To the north, the treacherous barrier of this desert can be seen.

Many skeletons are here, warning of the danger. The caves seem to be carved out by a massive monster of some sort. Five opened treasure chests aren't sinking at all into the quicksand, as if some magical force is keeping them above. The staircase leads towards the surface.

Tumbleweed slowly rolls around. To the north, the tyrannical barrier of this desert can be seen. To the east, south, and west lies more sand. Among the arid, depraved desert, a battered treasure chest is submerged within the quicksand. In this desolate wasteland, plant life is all but unable to grow.

The dusty sand blows about, making sure nothing escapes its tyranny. The maroon barrier blocks the passage to the east and south. To the north and west lies a path to the rest of the desert. A vulture picks upon the dusty skeleton of a human. Tumbleweed rolls quietly across the desert.

Among the dry, unforgiving desert, an enormous, sandy rock sits on top of the open, half-submerged treasure chest. The wind is stronger than at the surface. A lone cactus is decaying. To the south, east, north, and west, a path is dug out in the sand.

To the south, east, north, and west the paths are slightly marked in the sand. The wind is blowing sand everywhere. The air seems to shimmer brightly. A prodigously-sized rock is fighting to stay above the sand. The golden treasure chest lies here, opened. A lizard disguises itself to blend in with the sand.

To the west, an insurmountable barrier is too difficult to cross. To the east, south, and north, a path to the rest of the bleak, impoverished desert is dug in the sand. Among the desert, a cactus flows with the wind. Another eroded, aged, opened treasure chest is slowly falling apart into the sand.

Tumbleweed tumbles about the dusty desert. The forbidding barrier of this desert makes travel to the south impossible. To the east, north, and west some sand dunes stand proud. Among the arid, depraved desert, a battered treasure chest is submerged within the quicksand. Plant life is struggling to survive in the barren wasteland.

To the east, the earthy obstacle stops any hope of passage. To the south, and west and north, a path to the rest of the bleak, impoverished desert is in the sand. Among the desert, the cactus stands tall. Another eroded, aged, opened treasure chest is empty.

The water-deprived desert looks to be in need of help. A lone cactus is decaying while a scorpion skitters around it. The aged rock sits on top of the empty, half-submerged treasure chest. To the south, east, north, and west, a path is dug out in the sand.

A vulture is feasting upon the corpse of a traveller who apparently fell into the quicksand. The cactus is brown and dry as the ground. The scorpion is resting from the effects of the heat. To the south, east, north, and west, the rest of the desert beckons.

There is a staircase leading to even more sand. The cactus is decaying while a lizard sleeps beneath it. The barrier makes travel to the south impossible. The sand is blowing everywhere, literally covering the area in sand. The treasure chest is slowly sinking into the quicksand.

The dusty sand blows about. To the north and east the maroon barrier blocks the passage. To the south and west lies a path to the rest of the desert. Among the baked, depraved desert, the remains of a human lie here. Tumbleweed dances across.

Tumbleweed slowly rolls around. To the west, the barrier of this desert can be seen. To the east, south, and north lies more sand. Among the arid, depraved desert, a skeleton is submerged next to the battered treasure chest. A desolate, parched wasteland stretches for miles.

To the east, north lies more sand. The southern and western edges have the impassable barrier blocking transportation by foot.  Always a hostile and barren area, an open and empty treasure chest lies here. The slowly decaying, sandy form of a skeleton is sinking into the sand.
