The brown barrier stops any hope of passage to the east. A path to the rest of the dry, forsaken desert is marked in the sand. Among the desert, a lizard sitting on a rock is sinking into the sand. Another eroded, aged, opened treasure chest is empty.

The main lobby of the inn is spacious enough to accommodate a moderate number of people. A large, vividly-colored rug covers much of the stone floor. On the western side of the building is a set of stairs leading to the second floor. The innkeeper is here, snoozing behind a desk with a sign and some flowers on it.

This small shop sits on the second floor of the inn, which leads down to the inn's lobby. The room is quite small and mostly empty, save for a crate by the top of the stairs, the vendor's counter, and a placard on the wall signifying an item shop. The item shopkeeper stands behind the counter, eager to peddle his wares. A small notice has been posted on the counter.

This small storage room nestled on the ground level of the town serves as the storage room for the pub upstairs. Several barrels are stacked up against the wall, presumably filled with alcohol. A bright rug has been placed in front of the southern door, while a staircase in the northern wall leads upstairs to the pub.

rooms.name: Mirage: Outside of the Weapon Shop

userData.LongDescription: Anchored in the lower levels of the town is the weapon shop. The area out front of the store is lined with soft green grass that has been well maintained. A dangerous drop off prevents safe movement south, although it gives a lovely view of the forest outside the town. A building identical to the weapon shop can be seen to the west, though passage to it has been blocked by some oversized crates.

rooms.name: Mirage: At the Base of the Stairs

userData.LongDescription: Surrounded by stone walls on three sides, this small area between the inn and the rest of the village is covered in lush green grass. Stone stairs built into the northern wall lead up into the village, while to the east is the inn, waiting to welcome weary or lost travelers.

Devoid of furniture, this building shows no signs of permanent residency. In fact, the only object in here is a large, precariously placed urn in the center of the room. The lack of furnishings hasn't stopped the townsfolk from coming in here for whatever reasons they may have, in fact the place seems to get a fair amount of traffic. On the north end of the building is a staircase leading down below the ground level, while on the southern end of the building is a door leading outside.

Overlooking the southeastern corner of the upper part of Mirage stands the armor shop, as is made clear by the sign next to the shop's door. The forest outside the town can be safely seen, from behind a railing, which is quite high off the ground. The sky above is clear and blue, with no trace of wind. To the northwest is the center of town.

The forest opens up just outside of the town of Mirage into a peaceful glade. The surrounding trees begin to flicker in and out of existence, as they represent the barrier between worlds. Fresh tracks of some rather large bird can be seen in the area, meaning it was either trapped here when the worlds were split, or has found a way to travel between them. The only obvious exit out of here is a set of stairs that lead underground on the southern end of the glade.

The clank of dirty dishes and empty mugs rings throughout the room, as the staff of the pub place them onto shelves to be washed at a later time. Next to the shelves sits a large urn. The bartender can be seen casually walking back and forth between the bar and a row of barrels which presumably hold this establishment's alcohol. A wooden door sits at the northern end of the bar, serving as an employee entrance, while a set of stairs along the western wall lead downward.

A long bar stretches from near the entrance of the pub all the way to the far wall. Stools line the bar while additional tables for patrons to dine and drink are placed throughout the room. The floors are wooden, while a lavishly colored rug has been placed in the central dining area. On the far wall a stone hearth is used to create ambiance and warm up the establishment should it ever get cold.

A forest lies just outside the phantom village of Mirage, the Town that Time Forgot. The inn is settled here at the town entrance to welcome any visitors, as unlikely as they may be, while most of the village sits elevated upon a large platform of brick and stone. There is a large set of stairs to the west of the inn, granting access to the rest of the village.

Nestled in a dark area of the building with no windows sits another room full of armor and accessories. The floors here are wooden, as opposed to the stone floors in the other part of the shop. A shopkeeper sits behind the counter on the southern side of the room, along with many crates, barrels, and chests. It is unclear why anyone want to hide their store.

This tiny secluded room is empty and seems to serve only as an entryway. The wooden floors look well worn, indicating they've seen much traffic. The stairs in the northern wall appear to lead directly outside, while the passage in the east wall leads to more hallways.

A large, wooden placard with the image of a staff sits squarely above the door of the town magic shop. Lovely pink flowers on the lateral side of the shop, medial to the center of town, decorate the entrance. A stone railing runs along the length and western side of the shop, overlooking the forest and lower level of the town. To the east is the center of town, where the majority of traffic passes through.

Two parallel buildings mark the most southwestern region of the town of Mirage. The buildings run long ways with a gap in the middle for passage north and south. Access to the eastern building is blocked off by absurdly large crates and barrels. The western building can be accessed by its front door, if one takes care not to slip off the ledge to the south. Traveling north between the buildings leads under an archway to an area directly below the pub.

Deceptively smaller on the inside than it appears on the outside, the armor shop is little more than a hole in the wall. A wooden crate sits in the lower left corner of the room. To the upper left is a counter with a shopkeeper behind it. A small sign with a shield insignia on it identifies this as an armor shop. The only obvious exit is to go outside.

Nestled deep out of sight, and presumably out of ear shot, this little room is tucked away from the rest of town. What little space was initially available has been mostly occupied by a piano of substantial size. A stool sits in front of the piano.

A large, stone building inlaid with wooden beams, a tasteful red roof, and a wooden sign placed in the front, the town pub has served as Mirage's only source of escape for the past thousand years. A stone staircase leads to the town entrance, while a landscaped strip of fully bloomed flowers lines passage south. Many crates and barrels are dangerously stacked up behind the northern side of the pub.

Empty space and plain wooden floors greet the customers of the weapon shop of Mirage. An already small room to begin with, the shopkeeper's counter cuts the room in half, leaving little space for any potential customers. Behind the counter is an open doorway, with two identical signs hanging on either side of it. Through the open doorway, an enormous stockpile of crates and weapons can be seen.

Originally a fairly spacious room, this area of the weapon shop is extremely crowded with crates and weapons. Dozens of lances are lined up on weapon racks, and various crates are crudely marked with words like 'Swords' and 'Hammers'. Standing amongst the weapons is one of the shopkeepers, taking inventory of his wares.

Serving as the unofficial town square, this busy cobblestone intersection connects all the major points of interest in town. To the north, the town pub can be seen, while to the south lies a set of stairs leading down to the weapon shop. To the southeast is the armor shop, while to the west is the currently closed down magic shop.

A large, gaudy rug greets guests and covers much of the wood floors of the magic shop. Two symmetrical wooden counters line the eastern and western walls behind which are numerous bookcases filled to capacity with books. A black square sign with the image of a golden staff, similar to the sign outside, hangs on the northern wall between the counters. The shopkeeper is not present, but has left a note on one of the counters.

Underneath the town, this passage is shaped like an inverted horseshoe. The air down here is still and cool, as are the stones that make up the floor. On either end of the passage are stairs leading back up to the surface level, while halfway between the two ends of the hall there is a mysterious looking door. The western stairs lead up to an empty building, while the eastern stairs lead to the back of a shop. Occasionally a slight breeze drifts through, disrupting the otherwise lifeless passage.

Encircled by stone walls and tall trees, this small clearing is a nice quiet respite from the town above. A door in the northern wall leads under the pub, while an archway built into the wall under the magic shop to the south leads to some more buildings.

rooms.name: Library of Ancients - Second Floor Entry

userData.LongDescription: The second floor of the Library of Ancients isn't nearly as big as the first.  The major feature of the second floor is the stairway that leads up to the third.  A few tables adorn the research areas closer to the books.  On the west side of the room, there is a large table with a globe on it, and a clay pot.  A couple long tables sit on the east side the room.

Two long tables run parallel to each other on the eastern wing of the second floor.  Some chairs surround the two tables, which are buried under tomes of ancient texts.  There are a few rows of books within the bookshelf in the northern wall.  The stairway leading to the roof rises from the center of the second floor.

Overlooking the lower floor, the main foyer consists of a large wall of books to the north, interrupted in the middle by a staircase leading higher into the library. The library exit lies to the south, across a wide stone walkway. Tall bookshelves playing host to a wide variety of books can be accessed to the northeast and northwest. A couple of wooden stools sit up against the bookcase to the east, most likely used to reach the upper shelves.

The unnerving silence that permeates the basement level is only disturbed by the occasional rustling of books as if someone is taking one off a shelf, though there is no evidence anyone has been down here recently. The basement stacks continue south.

Two more dust-caked bookcases create a barrier across the northern section of the dim room dividing the area cleanly and providing a small gap between them for access. During more active years this decision likely helped keep the ambient noises under control. Given the current state of affairs, however, further deadening the noise mostly succeeds in adding to the creepy atmosphere.

A small study area rests below the entranceway into the library.  A square table with a small pile of books on it is in the center of the room.  A steep stairway leads back up to the main foyer.  Within the large bookcase that makes up the northern wall, there is a door leading deeper into the library.  A bright yellow sign is nailed to the front of the door.

This small study room is beneath the entranceway.  Stairs climbing up to the main foyer area are on the west side of the room.  Dozens of books are scattered across a wooden table in the center of the room.  A small stepladder is pushed up against the northern bookcase.

The broad tops of the bookcases make for a handy walkway on the western edge of a well-lit study room. While the titles of the books cannot be read from this distance, the dazzling array of colors of the bindings makes the room look more like a piece of art than another forgotten storage area. There is a gap between the books on the bookshelf that occupies the northern wall that was probably once a door until there was ever more pressing need for places to store various tomes.

The narrow balcony barely has room for two people to pass between the large heavily built bookshelf bolted to the northern wall and a gray stoned railing rising up from the southern edge. A multitude of large books occupies every one of the four shelves. The stone railing, while pretty, is primarily there to stop distracted scholars from falling into the quiet study room below. The more practical way to get down to the study is a steep set of plain stairs on the western wall.

Two small stools are set before a bookshelf bolted onto the northern wall, stuffed with person-sized books. While most of the book covers are faded red in color, occasional green or blue covered books also occupy the four shelves. A stone railing traces the edge of the foyer, until it meets a plain set of stairs, protecting the often absent-minded scholars from taking a tumble to the study below.

A narrow passage widens out into a small alcove hosting yet more bookcases. Cobwebs drape over the open lid of the large treasure chest in the center of the room, its contents long since pilfered. The thick wooden walls of the chest look to be in good shape, if the stacks are ever used again it is unlikely to remain disused for long.

A wide table sits in the middle of the western wing.  A globe of the world rests on top of the table. Pushed up against the bookcase to the north is a ladder.  A low clay pot sits on the floor to the south.  The stairways are to the southeast.

The floor rapidly transitions from marble to wood, to nothingness. Likely there was supposed to be a balcony, though, why that project was abandoned is anyone's guess. The wooden ledge, it turns out, is a gap in the books on the excessively sized bookshelf in the main room. Small balconies can be seen on other shelves, though from here there is no safe way to get to them.

This small study is hardly the extensive collection one would expect of the lauded Library of Ancients. Old dusty tomes may cover every inch of the haphazardly placed bookshelves, however the area is quite small. The only apparent exit is the door leading back to the upper levels of the library.

The sheer size of the eight-story bookshelf built into the northern wall is baffling from this vantage. This small wooden ledge is actually the top of an ornately carved doorway accessible from the ground floor fifteen feet below; its use as a walkway seemingly an incidental opportunity. Several better-planned outcroppings jut out from the preposterous bookshelf in a haphazard fashion. Two gaps in the books are the only feasible exits, one to the west and the other to the east.

The small peaceful balcony was likely once used by scholars to take a break from their feverish studies. Leaning back against the wrap-around stone railing provides an impressive view of the eight-story bookshelf built into the northern wall. Massive books bound in a staggering variety of materials and colors, are carefully arranged on every shelf from floor to ceiling. Other balconies are arranged in a haphazard fashion higher on the bookshelf. It is an engineering marvel the whole thing has endured centuries of use.

At one point in time, the red-veined marble floors would have been a stunning sight to see. Time and disuse have dulled the once high polished gleam into a dreary dull gray stone with very little character. Likewise, the fine wood paneling that covers the walls were likely once polished and oiled are now dull, dry, and lifeless. Large cobwebs currently drape across the opening of a disused wood and iron chest at the end of a small alcove on the southern end of the room. Enough light to reveal the details of the room is pouring in from an open doorway in the eastern alcove.

The large open balcony is the highest platform in a cavernous room filled with an arrangement of books that dwarfs any other known collection. Staggering in scale, the bookshelf is nearly eight stories tall and the view over the railing is vertigo-inducing. The stone railing acts as a safety measure against the fatality of a fall. There is a plain wooden door set into the bookshelf that leads to the upper levels, and a simple set of stairs leads down.

An almost normally proportioned, finely done bookshelf is built into the northern wall of a small alcove. More sparsely burdened with volumes, the shelf feels nearly empty by the rest of the library's standards. Five books on the second shelf are placed with such careful intent they draw attention. There is a simply done dark wood door on the southern wall.

The vast collection of books is briefly interrupted by a small wooden door set into the large bookshelf. Set on the left-hand side of the door; a ladder resting against the bookshelf allows for tomes above the third shelf to be accessed. Though the placement of the ladder seems unwise, since the stone railing is unlikely to stop a rapid descent should it tip over.

The large well-lit study is surrounded on all four sides with bookshelves stuffed with a stunning collection of historical tomes. A single bookshelf occupies the northern wall with only two gaps of missing books, at least one of which is a passage further into the stacks. The other gap would only be accessible by standing atop the bookshelves on the western wall. The warm bright light of the study allows for easy reading of the collection, provided you speak the right language.

It is easy to imagine how busy this balcony may have been while still in use. There is plenty of room for people to pass each other, a couple of corners for quiet conversations, and a small study placed under the stairs help paint the picture of a busy hub of excited scholars. Now, however, the abandoned balcony hosts no discussions, the desk with books strewn across it covered with dust.

This larger room is broken up into a zigzagging path by the placement of several bookshelves. The majority of the books on these shelves appear to be written by the same author: Alazlam Durai. His exhaustive collection of histories of various lands was apparently important enough to claim an entire room in a library where doors are considered less important than finding space for more books. The only apparent exit is back out the doorway.

A great view of Karnak Continent can be seen from atop the roof.  A large furnace is here, constantly being fed books.  A pile of books is in front of it, and two scholars work feverishly to throw the books into the flames.  Several books of notable interest stand out conspicuously in front of the pile.

A single massive fifteen-foot tall bookshelf marks the northern wall of this area. The ample collection of books continues on several smaller bookshelves which create an impassable border for the area. The only apparent exit is to the south towards the upper levels of the library.

Something about this room speaks of a sacred place. The walls and floors have been cleaned to a careful polish, while two marble columns stand on either side of the only exit. The only thing looking misplaced is a book placed on the floor in front of the ornate curved bookshelf that is the focal point of the entire room.

The bright light of the study is a harsh contrast to the gloomy lighting found elsewhere in the basement. The light allows a clear look at the varied and brightly colored tomes carefully packed onto each shelf. The room has been kept in good order, being free of the dust that plagues the rest of the stacks. This small alcove, sectioned off by the bookcases, only has two exits; the gap between two bookcases leading north, and a door on the southern wall.

Blessedly free of the books and the spirits that possess so many of them throughout the library, this small room is the perfect place to set up a cot and get some rest. The soft pink light illuminating the whole room is coming from an inscribed circle on the marble floor in the center of the room. Eight large stone pillars are arranged on the perimeter of the pink light. A set of stone stairs on the eastern side of the perimeter head down, further into the library.

The wood paneling continues to line the walls of the passageway, only giving way for a narrow set of wooden stairs. Covered in dust and cobwebs the stairs descend deeper into the long-abandoned basement. The dead still air combined with the absolute silence and lack of light makes it hard to determine if occasional glimpses of movement are figments of imagination or haunting spirits.

The three bookshelves, facing the only entrance, cause the room to feel staged for something. Two of the bookshelves stick straight out from the walls on opposite sides, providing a gap between them barely large enough for a person to fit through. The third bookshelf is in the sectioned off portion of the room. Though there is nothing menacing about the odd arrangement, something about this particular collection feels restless.

A motley array of books, so old the covers look like they would turn to dust at the touch, fill the lowest three shelves of the preposterous bookshelf. A grand door frame occupies a full third of the ground floor. Intricately carved designs depicting a variety of historical moments fill every inch of the large frame. Peculiarly, the door set into such a frame is of simple design lacking any of the embellishments lavished upon its surroundings. There is a set of stairs through a gap in the books that leads up.

A narrow hallway framed by more bookcases connects the small nook to the ladder leading across the top of the bookcases to the rest of the basement. This small quiet forgotten room in the library appears to be the end of the basement collection.

Completely lacking direct light sources this room is nearly pitch black. The walls are made of smooth, wood paneling, as opposed to more bookcases, though the reason for the change isn't apparent. The hard marble flooring, at least, is smooth and even allowing for good footing in the dark. The empty hallway is even devoid of the random noises of books shuffling, making the passageway feel truly abandoned.

A long granite walkway marks the entrance of the Library of Ancients.  A stone railing lines the edges of the walkway and keeps absent-minded scholars from falling down a floor.  The room is extremely large, and the wall to the rear of the room is filled with numerous large books.  Over either side of the railing, scholars pour over the books, mumbling to themselves in ancient arcane languages.

A lattice of incredibly resilient orange metal beams stretches across the sky, forming a framework upon which the pride of the kingdom of Zeal, the Blackbird, rests. The platform extends from a white gateway, which leads out to the rest of the isle, to the underside of the ship itself. There, a ladder leads up into the craft's smooth, green hull.

The room is designed in two parts, an actual storage area and a small hallway branching off of that with a doorway at the end. The former holds a modest collection of crates and cans, accompanied by an empty treasure chest, and the wall juts out unceremoniously to divide the two sections.

The exquisite beauty of the Blackbird's design is marred terribly along this section, where deep gashes tear into the surface. The damage shows distinct signs of recent repairs, though the work is nowhere near complete. This being the tip of the wing, the rest continues to the east and southeast.

The east end of the passage halts at this spot, connecting the nearby door to the rest of the craft and showing distinct marks of damage recently repaired. The Blackbird's quiet hum reverberates through through the walls, interrupted occasionally by mechanical beeps from deep within the ship.

A sea of machinery can be glimpsed through large gaps in the floor panels. With little concern for safety, a conveyor belt stretches across a yawning chasm of gears and flashing lights, connecting the northern door with the passageways to the south. Being a dead end opposite an intersection, the entrance is lent an air of prominence.

The room is dark and small, a few lonely strands of soft blue light illuminating the entryway and the base of the ladder opposite it. It isn't easy to gather much about the space, being as poorly lit as it is, not that there's much to see in the first place.

A number of boxes are crowded against the east wall of this room, all made of the same mysterious metal and sealed tightly. The storage room itself isn't very large, meant to hold little more than the present crates, the currently empty treasure chest, and the ladder on the far wall. Fragments of metal litter the floor, intermingled with shards of glass.

This intersection branches out three ways - to the north, over a conveyer belt; to the east and west, into what appear to be dead ends. The belt isn't operational at the moment, nor is the adjacent console which would normally control it. A pile of metallic rubble and wiring is heaped beside the controls.

Where three paths meet, the south one actually being a conveyor belt, the scattered remains of many machines cover the floor. Deep gouges in the walls hint at a catastrophic battle fought long ago, supported by the wreckage of countless automatons. The northern and western halls appear much cleaner.

The west end of the passage cuts off in perfectly measured forty-five degree angles, connecting the nearby door to the rest of the craft. The thick metal walls are interrupted regularly by bronzed girders and, at one point, by the twisted wreckage of a ruined ladder. All is lit by the same yellowish light found elsewhere in the Blackbird.

This intersection is made from conveyor belts and passageways, facilitating movement between them and the nearby rooms. To the south, along a deactivated belt, another crossroads is visible. To the north, along a similar belt, a door leads elswhere. East and west lead to bends in halls, each with a door of their own.

The southwest corner of this area holds a powerless control panel, clearly linked to the still conveyor belt that leads north. There is also a door set into the wall close by and, far to the east, another door with a similar console.

This is only really a room on a technicality. There are four walls, connecting at forty-degree angles, and a door. The floor is made up of three ascending levels, each with a ladder leading to the next, the final rising into the ceiling to meet a sealed grate. The only other noteworthy thing to be found is a partially opened box on the second tier.

The east/west hall meets the north conveyor belt, forming a T-shaped junction. At its northernmost point, the belt appears to end in an intersection mirroring this one. The west and east sections of the hall appear very similar to one another, each branching off in opposite directions. An unobtrusive door isn't far off, the only one in sight.

East of this corner, the corridor becomes an intersection. To the south, it continues along for a brief stretch and turns back to the east. Near at hand is a cluttered stack of boxes and cans, set carefully beside a door in the northern wall.

The view from atop the Blackbird is magnificent. Off the northern edge, a vast sea of clouds float below, occasionally revealing glimpses of snow-covered landscape. A slight, constant breeze prevents the pleasant warmth from becoming uncomfortable, the utopian conditions a result of magical engineering. The wing continues along to the west and south and, to the east, a hatch leads into the Blackbird itself.

Filled with stacks upon stacks of crates, the room's only walkable path follows the wall itself. Behind the menacing ziggurat of sealed boxes lies a smaller collection of empty ones, either discarded or left to be refilled. The southwest corner features a gray door, presumably leading to the Blackbird proper.

This is the northmost point upon the Blackbird itself, the apex of the semicircular corridor whose curve is simulated through carefully placed forty-five degree angles. A belt of conveyance leads southward, the southeast and southwest passages sloping out of view. A short ways to the west, a ladder leads upward.

The room's many various containers are in haphazard piles, strewn about with little rhyme or reason. The storage room shows signs of constant inhabitation, though all of the containers are still sealed. A cluster of glowing green stars hover about, ensuring safety for weary travellers through their mysterious magic. In the northeast corner, a hatch in the floor leads to a descending ladder.

The hallway takes a ninety-degree turn, forming the northwestern corner of this circuit. A nearby ladder leads upward to absolutely nowhere, the shaft having been sealed long ago. Near this frivolous ladder is a northern door, presumably leading into a room.

High in the sky, the southwest corner of the wing ends to reveal another floating island not far off. A majestic palace calls the isle home, with no visible means of reaching it. Beyond the architectural wonder, an endless ocean of clouds spread out as far as the eye can see.

Where two paths terminate, a corner is formed in the corridor and, near it, is a door. To the north, a second door is visible and, to the west, an intersection flanked by strange devices. A light showering of debris covers the floor along the northern hall, having fallen from a badly damaged ceiling.

A network of metal lines spread across the sleek elegance of the Blackbird's wing, navigating around deep grooves in the seafoam green surface. From this vantage point, far above the land and even the clouds themselves, the world stretches on into the horizon, where they eventually become one. To the west, east, southeast, and south, the wing stretches onward.

This narrow room, whose floor is twice divided into consecutive levels in half-story increments, features naught but a few crates and an empty treasure chest. A pair of ladders link the three platforms together and the chamber itself is immaculately clean. A gray door is set into the south wall, the room's only exit.

The northern corridor consists of a number of forty-five degree angles, giving the illusion of a broad curve sloping off to the northeast. Directly to the east is a straight path interrupted by a couple of conveyor belt consoles and side passages. South of this intersection is an inactive conveyor belt, whose path turns when the belt terminates.

A white tower looms nearby, from which emerges a long platform of ugly orange metal, the dock at which the Blackbird currently resides. Beyond it, the rest of the floating continent of Kajar can be seen, in all its verdant glory. To the north, west, and northwest, the rest of the wing awaits.

Boxes, cans, ladders, and an orange chest are the main features of this three-level room. The steady glare of a yellowed light gives everything a bronzed, oily appearance, reflecting off of the metallic walls and the various containers clumped together on the second platform. A rectangular opening in the floor reveals the Blackbird's inner workings, an intricate conglomeration of seemingly random parts from which many strange sounds emanate. The south wall is interrupted by a single door, the only escape from the incessant clicking and whirring of machinery.

The hallway bends to form an 'L' and continues along to the north, where a door and a similar bend can be seen, and to the east, where one would find a cross-shaped intersection. Immediately at hand is another door, presumably leading into the attached room. A small green light pulsates in the corner, a sign of activity in this otherwise static metal paradise.

The hall turns sharply to the north and west, the northern section replaced by a long strip of ridged rubber, clearly meant for the transport of goods. Past it, the path turns forty-five degrees and leaves sight whilst, to the west, it passes a couple of doors and cuts sharply to the north. There's also another close by, just begging to be opened.

This cross-shaped intersection, where the corners of four rooms meet, consists of conveyor belts to the north and south and a hallway heading east and west. The two belts, like their controlling consoles beside them, are currently powerless. Four long, parallel grooves lead from one to the other, making the transport of heavy objects easier.

The Blackbird's military motif, an emphasis on efficiency over appearance, is very evident in this room. Stacks of tightly sealed crates, in neat rows, fill most of the free space and leave little room for navigation. Between and beyond them, a few ladders are visible, allowing access to the other floors. In the southeast corner, the door stands as the only way out.

At the center of this straight passage, the walls open to form a slightly wider, octagonal space. The southmost side of this shape holds a single door that looks similar to the two at either end of the hall. The pathway is remarkably clean and the architecture bears little in the way of aesthetics, lending the ship an air of military precision.

The entranceway to the ruins of a large manor house sits here, while deep, impenetrable forests run to the east and west barring any attempts to traverse them.  A mountain looms beyond the ruins, but no path seems to reach it.  This dirt path runs to the south, leading towards a small village in the distance.  The Epoch sits parked here, sparkling in the sunlight.

A young, purple-haired woman sits behind a long wooden counter, while a door to the south leads out of this small inn.  Several beds lie in a room to the north, providing a place for travelers to sleep.  A yellow plant sits in a vase on the counter while several pots have been left lying on the floor.  Two chests sit behind the counter, but there is no way to reach them.

This is a small market, containing only a single merchant behind a wooden counter.  A door to the south leads out into the village.  Another door is in the back wall, behind the counter, but there is no way to reach it from here.  Numerous other items sit behind the counter, such as fruit, plates, chests, and a bundle of wood.  A yellow plant sits on the counter, in a small vase.

A small fountain sits in the center of the village, water splashing out of it.  The village is otherwise sparse, with only a few planted trees adorning it.  Two small houses can be entered from here, one to the north and one to the south.  The village ends shortly to the west, with a small market marking the western edge.  To the east lies the town inn, as well as a small cafe.  Dense forests surround the town on almost all sides, preventing travel across much of the island.

Bright sunlight spills in from a window in the north wall, while even more illumination is given off by a small fireplace near it.  A wooden table holding several pieces of cookware sits in front of the window, while a side chamber to the east holds several beds for this house's inhabitants.  A door in the south wall leads outside, into the village of Choras.

Numerous tables and chairs, as well as numerous people eating and drinking, mark this building as the Choras Cafe.  A man behind the counter serves people at the bar while a waitress walks from table to table.  Two tapped barrels sit up against the northern wall, containing some liquid.  A small basket of fruit sits in front of the barrels, while a white rug runs under the tables.

A small fireplace burns in the north wall, casting a soft glow over this house, while even more light spills in from a small window in the wall.  A small pot containing a yellow flower sits on a table under the window.  A door in the south wall leads out into the rest of Choras Village, while a wooden staircase leading to an upper floor runs upwards from the western side of the room.

An isolated market is the only building nearby, while dense forests and steep cliffs prevent any travel westward.  The rest of the village of Choras lies to the east, where various buildings can be seen.  The market itself is a small, red-roofed building set on a raised foundation.  A peninsula lies to the northwest, but it is unreachable due to the thick forests blocking the path.

The center of the village of Choras lies to the west of here, while a dirt path runs to the north, towards what appear to be the ruins of a large manor house.  The Choras Inn can be reached from here, as can a small local cafe.  Freshly-planted trees are scattered about the town, and deep forests can be seen in the distance.

Light floods this room through two wide windows in the north wall.  A bookcase rests on the eastern side of this room, while a pair of unmade beds sit up against the south wall.  A small cabinet sits at the top of a staircase, which leads down to the ground floor of the house.  A vase holding a bouquet of yellow flowers sits on the cabinet, as well as a small jug.

Three long beds are here, ready to accommodate weary travelers.  A young woman with purple hair stands behind a counter, prepared to check in customers.  A small guest book sits on the counter, as does a bouquet of yellow flowers in a vase.  The floor is made of hardwood, but is largely covered by white checkered rugs.  A door in the south wall leads outside, while a small bar area lies to the west.

A lone tombstone dominates this cape.  Ancient writing covers the surface of the tombstone.  A dirt path leads to the southeast, away from here and towards the village of Choras.  Sharp cliffs surround this cape on all sides but the southeast, thwarting any attempt to traverse their steep slopes. Small flowers grow near the tombstone.

A small manor house belonging to the mayor of Choras sits here.  A dirt path leads north, towards the dilapidated ruins of an older, larger manor house.  The center of the village lies just to the south, marked by an old stone fountain.  Thick, impenetrable forests lie to the northwest and east, preventing any travel in either of those directions.  To the west, a path leads towards a solitary grave, just visible in the distance.

Water spills out of an ancient stone fountain here, the center of the village of Choras.  A large inn can be entered from here, as well as a small, private residence.  The house of the village mayor is to the north, while a path runs to the northwest towards a peninsula containing a lone grave.  The thick forests block any movement to the southwest, while the island ends in a sharp cliff to the south and west.

The crumbling ruins of a large manor house sit just to the north of here, while deep, impenetrable forests run to the east and west, barring any attempts to traverse them.  A mountain can be seen beyond the ruins, but no path seems to reach it.  A dirt path runs to the south, leading towards a small village in the distance.  The Epoch sits parked here, shining in the light.

A man wearing a blue hat walks back and forth behind the bar here, serving customers.  Numerous patrons are crowded in front of the bar, eating and drinking.  A merchant to the west of the bar tries to sell wares to anybody he can get his hands onto.  Numerous plates and cups sit on a rack behind the bar, while to the east lies the local inn, and the door leading to the town beyond.

A radio sits on a small cabinet in the northwest corner of this room.  Two beds rest up against the south wall, while a window is set in the north wall.  Bright sunlight spills in through the window, illuminating this room.  A potted plant sits up against the eastern wall, while a wooden staircase leads down through the floor to a lower level of the house.  White checkered rugs cover much of the wooden floor.

This dirt path runs to the northwest, towards the end of the peninsula.  A single, slightly crumbling tombstone can be seen at the very edge of the peninsula.  The path also continues to the southeast, towards the center of the village of Choras.  It is also possible to travel eastwards to the northern edge of the village.  Sharp cliffs prevent travel in any other direction.

A white checkered rug covers much of the floor of this small house.  A kitchenette rests up against the north wall, just under a window through which bright beams of sunlight pour.  Two beds sit in a small chamber to the east, while a food-covered table sits up against the south wall.  A door to the west of the table leads out of the house, into the open air.

Bright sunlight spills into this manor house from several windows in the north wall.  A bright red couch sits in front of the largest of the windows.  A small kitchen takes up the northwest corner of the house, while a large table dominates much of the center.  Food is spread out on the table, as well as a small yellow flower in an ornate vase.  A staircase on the eastern side of this room leads up to another floor of the house.

This small chamber is illuminated by a trio of torches set in the north wall.  Also set in the northern wall is a small alcove containing a set of stone stairs, which descend into inky darkness, as well as a wooden door leading into another room.  Rough, chipping stone covers the floor.  The walls are made of chipping, carved stone that seems to have suffered the effects of long disrepair.

Shadows drape much of this room, dispelled only by a pair of torches set to either side of an alcove in the north wall.  A set of stone stairs runs from a landing just outside the alcove down to the floor of a hallway several feet below.  Cracked stone rails run along the edge of the landing to either side of the stairs.  A set of stairs set in the alcove lead upwards into darkness.  The hallway runs to the east, soon becoming almost totally covered by shadows.

Rotting wooden doors are set in both the northern and southern walls of this small chamber, leading out of the room.  A pair of torches is set to either side of the northern door and their blue flames illuminate the chamber.  The chamber itself is rather small, with only a small amount of floor space.  The walls and floor of this chamber are made of rough, cracked stone, which shows signs that it may once have been carved.

Shadows cover much of this cramped room, as there is no visible light source to dispel the darkness.  A small green rug with red fringe sits in the middle of the floor with an indentation that suggests that something once rested upon it.  The details of the floor and walls are not clear due to the shadows, and the only means of exit from the room is a wooden door placed in the south wall that connects to a hall leading west to a larger room.

The stone walls of this hallway are chipped and cracked, appearing ready to fall apart at any moment.  A pair of torches in the northern wall burn with a blue fire illuminating this end of a long, narrow hallway running westward.  A small hole has formed in front of the northern wall, but it is too small for any human to enter.  An alcove rests in the eastern end of the northern wall, containing a set of stairs running up into the blackness.  The hall runs to the west, where beams of daylight spill in from an opening in the south wall.

A short set of crumbling stone stairs run from the floor of this room up to a small landing containing a door.  Another door is set in the south wall, and small streams of light trickle in from grills set in both doors, providing the only illumination for this shadowy chamber.  The parts of the floor not covered by shadows show that faded carvings run all across the floor.  The walls are too draped by shadows for any details of their surfaces to be seen.

An old wooden door in the north wall leads into another room, while the hallway runs westward, where it quickly becomes covered by deep shadows.  Torches mounted in the walls to either side of the door provide illumination for this room.  A set of stone stairs runs from a landing just south of where the door stands, down to the floor of the hallway several feet below.

Numerous crumbling staircases fill this room, running upwards and downwards.  Short metal braziers sit next to many of the staircases, providing dim illumination for this chamber.  Small red-fringed, green carpets run up each set of stairs, lending a sense of eloquence to the entire room.  The portions of the floor not covered by carpets are covered with intricate, swirling carvings.  A door in the south wall provides exit from the chamber, while the stairs continue to the north.

Two torches in the northern wall burn with a blue fire, illuminating this end of a long, narrow hallway running eastward.  A green rug with red fringe runs along the floor, ending just before the western wall.  The walls of this hallway are crumbling and beginning to fall apart.  Small bits of debris from the walls rest on the carpet.  An alcove rests in the western end of the northern wall, containing a set of stairs running down into the darkness.  The hallway continues eastward.

Doors set in the north and south walls of this small room provide the only adornment, besides a pair of torches set to either side of the northern door.  The rough stone that comprises the floor and walls of this room appears to be in an awful state of disrepair, and has begun to heavily chip and crumble.  The walls and floor are both covered with the faded remnants of carvings.

Several short flights of crumbling stairs run up to an open platform at the northern end of the chamber, while more sets of stairs run back down to the ground below.  Sets of rusty metal braziers sit to the sides of several of the staircases, burning with a blue flame which illuminates the chamber.  Green carpets with red fringe run up and down each staircase, while a large carpet rests on the platform.  Two square indentations on the platform suggest that two box-like objects once rested there.  The only means of exit from this chamber lies far to the south, where a door leads out.

A pair of doors, one set in the north and the other in the south wall, provide transport out of this chamber, while a pair of torches placed to either side of the north door provide illumination within the chamber.  The rough stone walls slope diagonally inwards towards the northern door.  The ragged stone that comprises the floor is in bad shape and is lined with cracks.  The remains of wave-like patterns carved into the floor's surface create a slight swirling effect.

This hallway is almost completely covered in shadows, covering much of the ground and the walls.  The portions of the hallway to the east and west are better lit, and a faint glow from some light source can be seen from around the corners of the northern wall.   The details of the walls and floor are too shrouded by shadows to be clearly seen.  The hallway continues to the east and west, to better lit areas.

A solitary torch set in the northern wall illuminates this small, square chamber.  An open treasure chest sits on a small red-fringed, green rug in the center of the otherwise barren room.  The walls and floor are all rough and ragged and hold the remains of very old carvings.  A rotting wooden door set in the south wall opens to a hallway that leads east towards a larger room.

The stone floor of this open chamber stretches out in all directions, leading to several doors set in the stone walls.  A pair of burning torches sit embedded in the walls to either side of each of the doors, except for one set in the southern wall.  The walls of this chamber are carved, and the floor is ragged with the remains of numerous carvings.  Many small piles of debris lie scattered about the room, and the entire place seems to be in bad shape.

A large tombstone sits in the center of a raised dais in the center of this room.  A torn green carpet with red fringe rests underneath the tombstone, with bits of debris scattered across it.  A short set of wide, stone stairs lead from the ground up onto the dais.  To the right and left of the stairs, metal braziers give off deep blue flames, while four small torches are set in the northern wall, giving off the same blue flame.  The stone walls of the chamber are cracked and chipped, but the tombstone itself seems to be in a state of perfect repair.   A door in the southern wall leads to a small antechamber.

A long, narrow hallway runs to the east and west, with a red-fringed, green rug resting on the ground.  The walls are made of stone that was once ornately carved, but has since begun to fall apart.  Debris from the walls and ceiling lies scattered across the floor, while several small holes have formed in the floor.  Sunlight flows in from the south, leading out into daylight.

A solitary torch set in the northern wall illuminates this small, square chamber.  An open treasure chest sits on a small red fringed, green rug in the center of the otherwise barren room.  The walls and floor are both smooth and covered with ornate carvings, and both seem to have been repaired recently.  A wooden door set in the south wall  opens to a hallway that leads east towards a larger room.

Shadows drape this portion of the hallway, covering much of the ground and the walls.  The portions of the hallway to the east and west are better lighted, and a faint glow from some light source can be seen from around the corners of the northern wall.  The northern wall slopes slightly inward at the center of the hall, forming a slight depression.  The details of the walls and floor are too shrouded by shadows to be clearly seen.  The hallway continues to the east and west, to better lit areas.

A pair of doors, one set in the north and another in the south wall provide transport out of this chamber, while a pair of torches placed to either side of the north door provide illumination within the chamber.  The smooth walls slope diagonally inwards towards the northern door.  The smooth stone that comprises the floor is in a state of perfect repair, and has wave-like patterns carved into its surface, creating a swirling pattern.

Two torches in northern wall burn with a blue fire, illuminating this end of a long, narrow hallway running eastward.  A green rug with red fringe runs along the floor, ending just before the eastern wall.  The walls themselves are made of ornately carved stone, which seems to have been recently repaired.  Small bits of debris sit on the carpet, and a small hole has formed at the base of the northern wall.  An alcove rests in the eastern end of the northern wall, containing a set of stairs running up into the blackness.  The hallway continues westward, with daylight spills in from an opening midway down, and continues on, ending far to the west.

Wooden doors are set in both the northern and southern walls of this small chamber, leading out of the room.  A pair of torches are set to either side of the northern door, and their blue flames illuminate the chamber, revealing a pile of large stones that once belonged to the ceiling, now blocking the door.  The chamber itself is rather small, with only a small amount of floor space.  The walls and floor of this chamber are made of smooth, ornately carved stone which seems to have been recently repaired.

Doors set in the north and south walls of this small room provide the only adornment, besides a pair of torches set to either side of the northern door.  The smooth stone that comprises the floor and walls of this room appears to be in a fine state of repair, with almost no chipping or decay.  The walls and floor are both covered with fine carvings, creating slight, swirling patterns.

A short set of stone stairs run from the floor of this room up to a small landing containing a door.  Another door is set in the south wall, and small streams of light trickle in from grills set in both doors, providing the only illumination for this shadowy chamber.  The parts of the floor that are not covered by shadows show that intricate carvings run all across the floor.  The walls are too draped by shadows for any details to be seen.  A short stone rail runs to either side of the staircase on the landing, preventing any means of ascent or descent other than the stairs.

Three torches illuminate this small chamber, resting in the north wall.  The north wall also contains a small alcove, containing a set of stone stairs, which descend into inky darkness, as well as a wooden door leading into another room.  Smooth stone covers the floor, and seems to have been recently repaired.  The walls are made of finely carved, smooth stone, apparently made by a skilled artisan.

Two torches in northern wall burn with a blue fire, illuminating this end of a long, narrow hallway running eastward.  A green rug with red fringe runs along the floor, ending just before the western wall.  The walls themselves are made of ornately carved stone, which seems to have been recently repaired.  Small bits of debris sit on the carpet, and a small hole has formed near the northern wall.  An alcove rests in the western end of the northern wall, containing a set of collapsed stairs running down into the darkness.  The hallway continues eastward, with daylight spills in from an opening midway down, and continues on, ending far to the east.

Several short flights of stairs run up to a open platform at the northern end of the chamber, while more sets of stairs run back down to the ground below.  Sets of metal braziers sit to the sides of several of the staircases, burning with a blue flame which illuminates the chamber.  Green carpets with red fringe run up and down each staircase, while a large carpet rests on the platform.  Two square indentations on the platform suggest that two box-like objects once rested there.  The only means of exit from this chamber lies far to the south, where a door leads out.

Shadows drape much of this room, dispelled only by a pair of torches set to either side of a wooden door in the north wall.  A set of stone stairs run from a landing just outside the alcove down to the floor of a hallway, several feet below.  Stone rails run along the edge of the landing to either side of the stairs. The hallway runs to the west, soon becoming almost totally covered by shadows.  The walls and floor of this room are made of ornately carved stone, which shows signs or recent repair, despite some chipping and deterioration.

Shadows cover much of this cramped room, as there is no visible light source to dispel the darkness.  A small green rug with red fringe sits in the middle of the floor, with an indentation that suggests that something once rested upon it.  The details of the floor and walls are not clear due to the shadows, and the only means of exit from the room is a wooden door placed in the south wall that connects to a hall leading west to a larger room.

This stone floor of this open chamber stretches out in all directions, leading to several doors set in the stone walls.  A pair of burning torches sit embedded in the walls to either side of each of the doors, except for one set in the southern wall.  The walls of this chamber are ornately carved, and the floor is smooth with very fine carvings.  Small piles of debris lie scattered about the room, but otherwise the room is in good repair.

A long, narrow hallway runs to the east and west here, with a red fringed, green rug resting on the ground.  The walls are made of stone that was once ornately carved and was recently repaired.  Debris from the walls and ceiling lies scattered across the floor, while several small holes have formed in the floor.  Sunlight flows in from the south, leading out into daylight.

A large tombstone sits in the center of a raised dais in the center of this room.  A torn green carpet with red fringe rests underneath the tombstone, with bits of debris scattered across it.  A short set of wide, stone stairs lead from the ground up onto the dais.  To the right and left of the stairs, metal braziers give off deep blue flames, while four small torches are set in the northern wall, giving off the same blue flame.  The stone walls of the chamber are cracked and chipped, but the tombstone itself seems to be in a state of perfect repair.  A door in the southern wall leads to a small antechamber.

Shadows drape much of this room, dispelled only by a pair of torches set to either side of an alcove in the north wall.  A set of stone stairs run from a landing just outside the alcove down to the floor of a hallway, several feet below.  Stone rails run along the edge of the landing to either side of the stairs.  A set of stairs set in the alcove lead upwards into darkness, broken only by a faint trace of blue light.  The hallway runs to the east, soon becoming almost totally covered by shadows.  The walls and floor of this room are made of ornately carved stone, which shows signs of recent repair, despite some chipping and deterioration.

Numerous short staircases fill this room, running upwards and downwards.  Short metal braziers sit next to many of the staircases, providing bright illumination for this chamber.  Small red fringed, green carpets run up each set of stairs, lending a feel of eloquence to the entire room.  The portions of the floor not covered by carpets are covered with intricate, swirling carvings. Short rails run to either side of each set of stairs, blocking any means of quick ascent or descent.  A door in the south wall provides exit from the chamber, while the stairs continue to the north.

The southernmost of the two north-leading doors in this room is very brilliantly decorated, with huge pillars, stacks of gargoyles, and intricate designs on the walls on each side.  By contrast, the northern door past the long hallway is extremely uninteresting, with only a large cat statue peering over the top.  The door is slightly open, and fog pours out unrelentingly.

A decaying corpse of a fellow adventurer rots in a western corner of the hallway, pinpointing the source of the horrible smell.  The odor is nauseating, and the level of decomposition suggests he died fairly recently.  The hall extends far to the east of the rotten body, offering an expansion from the main center hall to the west to the hallway to the east.

The entrance to the eastward-expanding hallway on the second floor of the ruins is bathed in light due to a multitude of candles adorning the northern wall.  Small gargoyle statues surround the door that leads north, signifying the possibility of danger beyond.  A horrible scent seems to permeate the air, but nothing appears to be the source.

The north wall of this tiny, useless room is entirely covered with gargoyle statues.  Not a single square inch of the wall can be seen behind the statues the way they have been built.  A small button rests in the corner of the room as well, but years of rust have stopped it from pressing into the ground.

This corner of the haunted ruins gives more depth to the theory that the ruins once housed a cult.  A large stage is set in the northern section of the room, surrounded by glowing candles and fearsome statues.  The presence of still-lit candles gives support to the feeling that perhaps the cult hasn't yet disbanded.

Smack dab in the middle of the room is a massive pyramid, constructed from three large pieces of stone, decreasing in size as they stack atop each other.  Surrounding the pyramid is a skinny metal grate, and sounds of splashing water come from below.  The door to the north is surrounded by massive dragon statues, bigger than any other statues in the ruins.

This cramped room features a large dining table with room for at least fifteen people.  Shelves full of aged wine and assorted dishes adorn the corner.  The room is lit by a few lanterns on the wall and just two candles on the table.

This poorly-designed hallway has maybe enough width to hold two people walking side by side.  A shaggy, worn-down purple carpet covers the floor, with pieces of stone laying exposed where the carpet has torn away or rotted.  The heavy, metal door to the north lays on the ground in front of the exit, broken from its hinges long ago.

The faint fog that has been present in the rest of the ruins picks up both speed and thickness in this narrow hallway.  The mist permeates every aspect of the room and seems to come right from the walls.  The door to the north features a fierce-looking demon's head, intricately designed to come forth straight from the center of the door.

Large, intricately-carved stone pillars try to support the ceiling in this gigantic open hallway.  Each of the pillars is indented to hold a single candle, though most of the candles have been extinguished.  A large part of the ceiling has fallen to the ground, revealing the sky above and lighting the room.  The candles were likely blown out by a breeze from the damage to the roof.

This nondescript room serves as an entryway into the west hallway of the second floor of the ruins.  Aside from the usual candles adorning the walls, the room is virtually empty.  Various gargoyles surround the door, acting as a warning once again.

One massive room has been turned into two long rooms by a dividing wall.  The path curves in the shape of a U, with an extremely narrow path to the west and a winding path of retracted spikes to the east.  Fortunately, the spikes can be walked across safely due to the button to the east being completely rusted down, forever drawing the spikes beneath the metal grates.

A sprawling, open hall serves as the gateway to the rest of the ruins.  Not only does it have paths leading to various rooms with different functions for the ruins, but it tracks back towards the ruins' entrance and goes even deeper into the many basements.  The room is very dark, as no natural sunlight can find its way in.

Five pillars of stacked gargoyles greet unsuspecting visitors entering from either entrance.  Between each stack is a single candle, causing this room to be much dimmer than others in the ruins.  The hallway runs west to east, with a door heading south from each end.

A shaggy, purple carpet is a veritable graveyard, marred by hundreds of separate bloodstains and a large number of bones.  The piles of remains have been deliberately swept into the corner to clear the way forward, and among the bones are various weapons and backpacks from fallen warriors.  The room is dank and smelly, and a sudden breeze cuts to the bone.

The first floor of the ruins can be seen over the edge of the long balcony atop the stairs.  Candles flicker menacingly as a cool breeze floods the room.  Surrounding each of the two doors are two raised platforms, each holding a small, odd, and hungry-looking cat statue, signaling that there might be danger beyond.

Dust scatters through the room as a cool breeze floods in from the open door to the south.  A rumpled, golden rug is all there is covering the damp and cold stone floor of this room.  It seems like any renovation that may have once come to the ruins never made it as far as the end of this hallway.

Stacks of sneering gargoyles pile along the north wall, shadows dancing with the light of the candles mounted along the wall beside them.  A stone staircase goes deeper into the ruins, where the fog grows even thicker, and a path to the south heads back towards the entrance of the temple.

The path takes a curve, leading both north and west.  The path is well-lit by many candles on the walls and a hole in the ceiling that is letting some light in from the rooms above.  The hallway has been formed out of two separate rooms that became one as the wall between them either crumbled or was torn down.

The hallway turns sharply at a right angle along the path in this room.  Steep stone stairs lead deeper into the ruins, while a path to the south turns 'visitors' back towards the main foyer.  Menacing statues sneer from their stone positions on the wall, each holding a single lit candle in its mouth to light the path.

The fog thins out heading off to the side of the corridor from the center of the ruins.  Over the balcony is the entrance to another basement, accessible via the stairs to the north.  From this vantage point, it is clear that a large pit is on the lower level, and it shows no sign of stopping.

Oddly enough, this dining room within the ruins looks as though it has never been touched.  Stacked china and bottles on shelves in the corner of the room appear brand new and untouched by dust.  In front of each seat at the large table is a full place setting, with dishes, wine glasses, and silverware.  Flawless unlit candles stand upright in their holders on the table atop the unwrinkled tablecloth.

A refreshing breeze blows past the precarious overlook of the ruins.  A fall to the courtyard below could be crippling, but fortunately somebody had the foresight to construct a fence made of pointy stakes to keep people from falling over, or even climbing over.  The only option is to return to the ruins through the door to the north.

The subtle light from decorative candles on the wall reveals that the floor in front of the northern door is in fact a mesh of metal wire with spikes.  The spikes have since been retracted, allowing passage north, but at one point the door to the room was blocked off for whatever reason.  A path to the east leads back to the center of the ruins.

The circular room abruptly ends upon entry.  There is still the same purple carpet that inhabits much of the rest of the ruins, but set in a spiral pattern is another odd, silky, yellow carpet.  The stench of death looms heavily in the air, much like the rest of the deepest basement of the ruins.  Shadows dance along the wall as candles dance in a slight breeze.

The only light in this damp and odorous room comes from the open door to the south.  Unlike the rest of the ruins, no candles have been placed on the walls.  Shackles on the wall show that the room was once used as a prison, as do the various chains scattered about on the floor.

The fog on the upper levels of the ruins has definitely been drifting in from the basement downstairs from this small room.  Only the top two steps can be seen before the entire staircase gets absorbed in the thick mist.  The northern door can only be seen because of the two candles on either side...were the candles not there, nothing in the room would be visible.

A large, wooden table sits at the top of the giant pyramid, cheerfully adorned with shackles, gears, and other murderous devices.  A skeleton rests upon the table, there from years gone by, arms and legs each in their own individual cuffs.  The device stretched this poor man so thin that nearly all of the limbs have been pulled from their sockets.  From the looks of it, the device was used often, but something must have happened to keep this particular man from being freed.

Cluttered detritus on the ground is evidence that this area was once two rooms connected by a door in the middle and the wall has since crumbled to the ground to form a long, dirty hallway.  Most of the rubble is clustered in the middle of the room, but there are remains of statues scattered about the room, and dust flies about.

The candles in this room have all been extinguished thanks to a constant breeze blowing in from the open door to the south.  Besides the fact that it obviously hasn't been used in awhile, the room looks fairly new.  Unlike the rest of the ruins, this room is carpeted, though it ends abruptly before it reaches the northern door.

Grinning cat statues with gigantic tongues rest at the bottom of each side of the staircase.  To the south, surrounded by gargoyles, is a door that leads deep into this basement.  A pile of large, sharp spikes sits to the south, protecting a button on the floor.  The button, however, seems to already have been activated.

Two delicately-carved pillars with candles help support the balcony of the center of the ruins.  A ferocious-looking stone dragon pokes its head over the heavy metal door to the north, while a passageway leads even further south.  Above is the long hall in the center of the ruins that lead to all corners of the floor.

rooms.name: A large antechamber in the Northtown Ruins

userData.LongDescription: The frayed, purple carpets of the center staging area of the haunted ruins lead into thick dust piles in the corners.  The room is dark, provided with light solely by scattered candles on the walls and pillars that support an upper section.  Dim light from the eyes of the scattered statues of creatures about the room would not be visible were the room better-lit.

Strange posts surround this small balcony overlooking the courtyard, forming an odd fence.  Were it not for another set of posts, it might be possible to climb on the roof, but as it stands, the only way off the balcony is to the north.  The entrance back into the ruins is set under a small canopy to protect from any rain.

A sizable chunk of porous rock has landed in the trees alongside the path, knocking several of them down.  This strange rock that has been launched into the path does not match the native stone of the mountainous path at all.  There are other similar disruptions further down the path to the east, where the source of these phenomena is apparent: a massive meteor.

The grassy path that leads between the trees and bushes is overrun with briars and other small plants.  Though not a real obstacle to travel, the weeds are a nuisance to step over.  A pair of very dense trees, surrounded by boulders and rubble, prevent passage east, but it seems possible to get around the obstacle by heading north first.  The mounds of loose dirt and rock that cover the ground seem oddly out of place, as if they were thrown there by a massive impact.

Sunken deep into a crater, entrenched at the end of the groove cut into the earth by its own landing, the gigantic Tycoon Meteor is the origin of the calamity that has disturbed these woods.  The porous exterior of the meteor is broken only by a single artificially created opening leading to the meteor's cold interior.

This ruined spot in the forest is the site where the Tycoon Meteor first landed, leaving a massive crater.  After falling from the sky, the meteor drilled north through the trees, wrecking everything in its path and cutting a blackened trench.  The burnt rut that begins at this crater remains as a scar in the land.

As the massive meteor which now rests to the north landed, it apparently skidded across the ground before coming to a rest.  As a result, this charred trench was dug into the ground.  The trees and soil that used to reside along this stretch have been displaced, walling up into a barricade around the edges of the scarred pit.  The trench is at least forty paces wide; the same size as the meteor at its end.

Soil and debris have been pushed up into a wall above the edge of the trench dug by the meteor's landing.  When the meteor skidded to a halt, the landscape must have been displaced.  Dirt and broken trees make up the barrier, which is piled several feet above ground level.  With a little bit of climbing, though, there is a way down into the trench.

Towering trees fill this valley, but the mountain ranges of the Tycoon region still dominate the skyline to the east and west.  The path through the woods is hilly, much of it not traversable due to the steep mountainside cliffs.  The grassy, overgrown trail leading through the trees is matted with briars, weeds and wild flowers.

A narrow path leads through the middle of some dense brush in this field.  This region may once have been a tiny forest, but something has burned many of the trees and bushes.  The mouth of the trail leads out to the southwestern valley, but to the east one can travel into the thicket.  Small animals can be heard in the brush alongside the path.

The cold walls of the meteor are made of porous stone.  Bizarrely, the area inside the meteor appears to be completely natural, rather than carved out by man.  There is a suspicious hole directly across from the entrance, but it is empty.  Yet the most unusual feature by far of this chamber is the vortex of swirling energy on the center of the floor.

This pile of rubble beside the Tycoon Meteor was unearthed by its violent crash landing.  The building-sized meteor presses against the west side of this mound of shattered rock.  The only safe way off of this rubble is to climb down into the crater below, where a strange entrance into the meteor beckons.

Shards of the giant meteor have been flung across the trail, turning what used to be part of a small forest into the edge of a scorched and burned mess.  At the end of the path, just to the east, soil has piled high, forming a wall at the edge of the meteor's landing path, which digs into the ground beyond.

Through the thick trees, what appears to be a huge meteor is visible to the northeast.  Debris has erupted out from the crash site of the meteor and covers parts of the trail.  A huge chunk of a fallen tree lies to the north, knocked over by the meteor's crash.  The meteor's landing has caused quite a disturbance in the earth, leaving a sharp ridge of splintered earth, which walls off the east side of the path, along the edge of its wake.

This peninsula of land rises above the rest of the center of town. The Cosmo Candle gives off its continuous, warm glow of light. What fuels the flame is either unknown, or its people simply refuse to tell, forever burning with the hopes, and desires of all its people.

Just outside the center of town a couple shelves lean against a cliff, holding many types of containers and bottles. To the south, the main entrance into town and a large staircase leading up to the west can be seen. From the east a raised peninsula of land is seen with a faint, warm glow coming from its center.

High up on the cliff of Cosmo Canyon's town, the view becomes wider as the canyon spreads out over the horizon. A set of stairs leads up further along the cliff, nearing the observatory sitting at the top. An opening leads into the cliff as well.

High above the main area of Cosmo town, the plateau overlooks most of the area. The other plateau in the middle of town gives off a warm glow, where the large flame can be seen burning steadily. A set of stairs leads down into the valley, with another set leading up to an opening in the side of a cliff.

Lights and monitors blink, and display all sorts of different information throughout this small room. The domed ceiling has a small rectangular opening as the telescope peers out into the heavens, and descends into the room. A small eyepiece bends up just before a padded stool, for those long nights of clear stargazing...and focused listening.

Rising into the heavens, a large building towers from the top of Cosmo Canyon. A dome at its top is open, with a large telescope protruding from the center, peering into the infinite sky. All around the cliffs drop off sharply at its edges, giving a spectacular view of the entire canyon. A ladder leads down a small crack, back down the cliff, as well as a small door, heading into the observatory.

This is the edge of Cosmo Canyon's town center. It drops off suddenly into a deep ravine as the rest of the canyon spreads out ahead.  Warm updrafts come up from the canyon floor, spinning the windmills spread out around the edge. A peninsula of land rises in the center of town as a warm glow comes from the flame at its center. A small path heads southward along the peninsula's eastern edge, as well as one heading northwest along the northeastern edge.

A peninsula of land rises just to the northeast as the path splits around it, heading to the north toward a ladder leading up along the cliff, to the east along the peninsula, and westward toward the main entrance of town. A few whisps of a flame can be seen coming just over the ridge of the peninsula, giving of a steady glow.

This path travels between the sheer cliff of Cosmo town, and the peninsula of land rising in the middle of the town. The glow of some sort of light can be seen flickering against the walls. There's also a ladder here, leading up to a house built into the rock face further up.

Climbing up from the ladder, the house spreads out to a wide room. Various items for sale are spread about on display. The shopkeeper sits behind the counter awaiting to serve his customers. A sign is propped up next to him as a brief gust of wind drifts up from the ladder, leading back down to the ground.

A small ways off from the entrance into town stands a pillar of rock, rising from the ground and tapering to a smooth tip. At its base is a long shelf that holds varied types of containers and jugs of all colors. Most are empty or hold water for general use.

A small incline rises from the ground along the peninsula to the north. At its base a small sign sticks into the ground. The glow from the Cosmo Candle is strong here as it is also fairly visible. A gentle warmth can be felt washing over from the peninsula, brought from the Candle through gentle breezes.

Entering into the cliff, a small room opens up, various boxes scattered about here and there before a counter carved out from the inside of the cavern. A large sign hangs above with ' Tiger Lily's Accessory Shop ' scrolled across. A young lady sits there, presumably Lily herself, smiling brightly. An opening leads out of the cavern, as well as a set of stairs just to the left of the shop, leading up to another opening.

Climbing up the long ladder, this house built up on the cliff is really nothing more then a storage shed, holding various boxes, and crates full of different items. From here, a nice view of town can be seen, as well as part of the canyon surrounding the town.

This flattened landing separates two sets of stairs. One set leads down to the southeast towards the town's main area, as well as its exit. The other stairs lead up to the northeast, toward another landing more towards the observatory. It can be seen sitting on the highest peak of town.

A medium-sized room, serving as the center-point to the rest of the Observatory. A long wooden picnic table with four stools is at the center, with a couple glasses on top, and a barrel set near the back edge. A small cupboard is set near the wall heading toward the door out to the canyon, with a small lamp lighting up the room. A refrigerator and sink are by another corner, with a small alcove leading to a metal ladder, heading up further into the area. Another door is set before the ladder, with a small sign tacked on to its front.

The ground spreads out to a flat, wide plain that leads off into different areas of town. To the west, a small path can be seen leading along side a staircase that lies to the northwest. The north and northeast lead further into the open area of town, as well as the warm glow coming from the peninsula.

A fairly large room opens up inside the cliff, various lamps scattered about the walls, giving it a warm cozy atmosphere. A few boxes and barrels are stacked here and there, though they're mostly around a large opening to a cave. A ladder leads up from here, as well as another small opening leading out.

A small little room for the most part, with an odd looking contraption set in the middle. Above, the ceiling rises into a dome-shape with a backdrop of the stars. Also in the room, on a small table, an old phonograph sits fairly well preserved, and most likely still useable.

This is the main entrance into the town of Cosmo Canyon. A large sign is here, held up by two wooden pillars. Further in, citizens can be seen bustling about town, or at least the ground portion of it.
