Most if it seems to have been built into the limestone walls of the canyon itself, with only ladders and sets of stairs giving access to to the various areas. A warm glow can be seen to the northeast upon a raised peninsula of land.

A wide ramp of stairs leads up to the northwest. Above that, the observatory can be seen atop the highest peak of the town.  The main center of Cosmo Canyon lies to the east with a soft, warm glow coming from the raised peninsula.

The path leads along the southern edge of the stairs that rise up the cliffs towards the observatory. A long shelf is set against the wall holding various bottles and pottery. A sudden dropoff falls into the rest of Cosmo Canyon. No apparant paths lead any further.

An elaborate doorway is here, made of wood as it leads into the side of the cliff. Two large torches stand at either side, burning steadily. A large tapestry hangs above the door, with a few designs scrawled on it. The light from the torches cast shadows over the tapestry as a slight gust of wind does the same to the flames.

A small plateau high up on the cliff atop Cosmo Canyon. Just above the observatory sits, looming large over the canyon. The perfect setting for a lookout to the stars. Just below an opening leads inside the cliff, and a set of stairs leading down along the cliff.

Walking alongside the large cliff, a small setup of different breads, and pastries is displayed in a little booth. Overhead, a house has been built against the cliff, held up by various wooden support beams. It continues to the east, bending around the cliff edge. A gentle waft of warm air also comes from the east, drifting in along the cliff walls.

This is the edge of Cosmo Canyon's town center. It drops off suddenly into a deep ravine as the rest of the canyon spreads out ahead.  Warm updrafts come up from the canyon floor, spinning the windmills spread out around the edge. A peninsula of land rises in the center of town as a warm glow comes from the flame at its center. A small path heads westward along the peninsula's southern edge, as well as one heading north along the eastern edge.

A simple inn is here, with various lights illuminating the inside in a soft glow. A slight breeze creeps in from the outside, only giving a momentary chill to the quietness. The innkeeper stands behind a desk that's just to the side of a door, leading to the rooms to stay in. A small sign is set upon the desk as the innkeeper presents a warm smile.

rooms.name: Ladder up to the Item Shop

userData.LongDescription: This is the northeastern most point in Cosmo Canyon. Just to the east, a set of three fans collect the updrafts from the canyon down below. A ladder leads up here to the house built overhead, held up by wooden support beams right into the cliff. A small sign sticks in the ground by the foot of the ladder reading 'shop'

High rock walls line a smooth, rock path leading northeast, and south. A large opening can be seen to the south, leading into another wall of rock. To the northeast the path widens to a more open area as a warm breeze filters in. Criss-crossing back and forth from wall to wall, sticky fibres make a strong webbing. Their creator could be nearby...

It is dark, cool, damp and fairly cramped within this small cave. There appears to be nothing inside of it, lending the impression of a dead-end. Smooth rock lines the inside, making a completely flat wall on the far side. The only way out is to go back through the entrance.

A thin ledge stretches along the wall of the cavern, dropping off suddenly to jagged rocks below. A little further west the entrance to this cavern can be seen, though from here there seems to be no way to get to it. Spotty patches of green light dimly glow from the rocks along the walls of the cavern. Back to the east there's another light source spreading its light as well as a gentle warm breeze.

rooms.name: Upper cavern in the Cave of the Gi

userData.LongDescription: This area is just east from the door leading back out to Cosmo Canyon, and the Planetarium. A single light-bulb shines brightly as it hangs down from the wooden rafters set in the ceiling. Various sized boxes and barrels are scattered about, stacked atop each other, and against the rock walls of the cave. There is a ladder here, leading further down into the rocky cavern. A gentle breeze can be felt coming from through the cave's entrance, kicking up clouds of dust as the warm air filters in.

Solid rock paths converge from different directions. A high rock wall rises on the eastern boundry as the paths fan out to the north, south, and west. A light green tinge gently glows from the rock, spreading out in small patches. A gentle draft of air carries the building heat around the caverns, barring any relief from the sweltering onslaught.

Three solid rock paths converge into a flat plain. The paths head off to the north, south, and west, with some sort of cave just visible to the north. Bubbling pools of lava churn just over the edges of the paths, making the surrounding air almost unbearable. To the east, another path can be seen snaking along the eastern wall.

Solid rock forms to a flattened pathway, heading toward the northeast and south. A warm, humid breeze drifts in from the northeast, making the air a tad uncomfortable. Heading toward the south, rock walls start to rise along the edges of the path as a cooler breeze comes from that direction.

Molten pools of bubbling lava surround a solid rock path, various bumps forming here and there from the heat. The path comes in from the south, then takes a turn to the northwest. The path continues on to the south, bisecting through the lava pools. The lack of any wind doesen't help to alleviating the heat.

Rock rises up from the ground just to the southeast, the path bending around either side of the pyramid-like structure as small veins of green coalesce from the rock here and there. Along the northern wall a skeleton hangs half imbedded while a large arrow is impaled into its chest, and into the wall behind.

The path takes a slight incline, and flattens out, as a light fog sweeps in from a gentle breeze to the northwest. To the north, a little niche has been cut out in a wall of rock. A lone skeleton sits there hunched over, silent in his eternal slumber.

The path rises sharply to the northeast along the rising walls of the pyramid-like structure. Small patches of green can be seen within the walls, and spreading out steadily. A warm, bright light shines in from the west, as well as a light warm gust of air.

A flat landing of solid rock comes out from the cave to the north. Another path can be seen going east to west over the cave. All around the landing, molten rock and magma bubbles and flows, making the air nearly unbearable. To the west another path can be seen running north to south.

A vast pool of molten lava spreads out in a seemingly endless reach. Solid rock forms to a flat plain above the undulating flowing rock. The air is still, and stagnant, not giving any relief from the simmering heat. The rock path leads south, the only way out of this area.

The path widens, and splits out in three directions. To the north, an opening can be seen in the side of an outcropping of rock, to the west, the path leads behind a spine of high rocks, and to the east, leading deeper into the caverns.

Coming around the spine of rocks, the path is cut off by jagged boulders, glowing with a green tinge, and getting stronger deeper in, stopping any movement further. Along the backside of the spine of rocks, there appears to be the figure of some sort of warrior, holding a large dagger. The only way to go is back to the east.

High rock walls line a smooth, rock path leading north, and south. A large opening can be seen to the south, leading into another wall of rock. To the north the path widens to a more open area as a warm breeze filters in. Criss-crossing back and forth from wall to wall, sticky fibres make a strong webbing. Their creator could be nearby...

rooms.name: Plateau just below entrance to the caves

userData.LongDescription: A small plateau juts out from the ledge of rock. A ladder leads up to the entrance of the caves, and a thick rope hangs over the edge, tied securely as it leads down further into the caves' depths. A gentle breeze can be felt coming from above, warming the stale air.

A long stone pathway runs from north to south, paralleling a large wall of rock to the west. Just over the eastern edge, the path falls off into a large pool of bubbling lava. The heat radiating from the pool makes the air humid and thick throughout the cavern. To the east another path can be seen out over the lava, but how to get to it isn't apparent.

A solid rock path bisects though the area, heading east and west. Just over the edges twin pools of lava bubble, and flow underneath, making the air opressive, and nearly unbearable. Just along the edges of the path, a faint green glow is visible, building eastward in small patches. A faint acrid smell drifts in from the west. Not too strong, but not unnoticeable.

A solid rock path runs east to west through the oppressive heat of the cavern. Its edges fall off to what looks like another path to the south, though how to get there isn't readily apparant. Another path stretches northward on the other side, through the bubbling pool of lava. To the west, the path widens slightly as a rusty goop coats over the ground.

The path widens out, splitting off into multiple directions. The most noticeable aspect here is the opening in the northern wall, leading out to a more open area of the caverns. The path strays off to the west, leading toward a darker opening in another wall, as well as a valley between two rising rock formations. To the south and east, the path splits around yet another rising formation, its opening not seen from this perspective.

Molten pools of bubbling lava surround a solid rock path, seeming to wrinkle from the oppressive heat. The path comes in from the north, then takes a turn to the southwest, inclining slightly. The path continues on to the north, bisecting through the lava pools. Gentle winds don't help in alleviating the heat.

A solid rock path runs north to south, leading over a bubbling pool of lava to the east. A large wall of rock and stone rises on the western side of the path, marking the boundry for the cavern. A light shines through a passageway to the north, leading deeper still into the cavesof the Gi Tribe. To the south, the path starts to curve a bit to the east as it spreads out into the cavern.

A dense patch of fog covers the area, although a bright light can be seen shining through to the north. A small wall of rock rises around the path, diverting down an incline to the east, passing just south of another rising rock structure.

Solid rock spreads out from a path to the north, making a small plateau amidst the bubbling pools of lava. The said lava pinches up at the plateau's edge, threatening to wash over at any moment. A constant barrage of heat comes from the molten rock, with continuous wave after wave of thermal energy. Just to the east, another path, built up high upon a large wall, can be seen.

The heat here is sweltering as twin pools of lava bubble steadily, taking up most of the area of the room. On the far wall a giant troll-like face grins menacingly. From the ceiling, stalagtites hang down, dribbling beads of water into the lava pools. The troll's mouth is open slightly, though the lighted path behind it has been blocked off.

Smooth rock forms the interior of this cave, albeit a bit cramped in size. Light shines in from from the south, while a faint breeze comes from a skinny passage to the east. From the south a warm breeze filters in, giving some confort to the cramped conditions.

A solid rock pathway comes in from the north and bends around an outcropping from the eastern wall, towards the southwest. Just over the western edge, the path drops off into a bubbling pool of lava. A steady heat rises, making the air quite warm and thick. From the rock outcropping small patches of green glow silently, spreading towards the southwest.

Solid rock forms into a path, splitting through a large pool of molten lava. Just over the edges, the molten rock can be seen flowing freely, with intense heat rising up into the vast cavern. A small plateau of land can be seen to the east, but any way to get there does not present itself. The path leads through the cavern, heading toward the north and southeast.

A fairly wide rock path runs from east to west through the cavern. A pool of lava bubbles steadily to the south, just off of the path's edge. Looking northward, another pool of lava spreads out into the cavern. Another path can be seen, though getting to it from here is not possible. Along the southern edge of the path, a fairly bright green glow can be seen coming from the rock, spreading westward.

The path curves as it heads off to the southwest and east, passing by a rather large opening in the northern wall. The breeze picks up a bit, scattering  a bit of dirt along the path, and around the opening. A fairly bright light shines in from the east.

A large peninsula of land juts out from the large wall of rock to the west. A large pool of bubbling lava flows just below, and throughout the cavern. A raised path can be seen just to the north, though getting to it would be impossible at this distance. A steady heat rises from the lava all around, with no relief from the hot breeze coming from the north.

A high rock wall rises along the western edge of a solid rock path, running southward along its length. A pool of bubbling lava flows along the eastern border, threatening to to ooze over the edge. The main path comes in from the south, and coming to an abrupt halt to the north. The heat is especially noticeable in this stagnant corner, with no wind to fan its effects.

A thin ledge stretches along the wall of the cavern, heading east and west. It drops off suddenly, spikes of earth growing up from the ground below. Spotted here and there are dim green patches, glowing silently out from the rocks. A dim light can be seem coming from the east, as well as a warm breeze washing out over the ledge.

This enclosed room's walls glow with a green hue, getting brighter toward the opening in the ceiling. A rope hangs down, allowing to climb up into the shaft. There is a steady breeze here coming from the eastern opening, leading further into the caves. It has a slight warmth to it, hinting of a similar climate further in.

The walls of the cave glow brightly with a light green hue. There isn't really much of a foothold here, hanging onto the rope. The only options are to continue up or down. A chilly breeze picks up slightly, seeming to come from both above, and below.

The path splits off into three directions as a slight breeze picks up from the north, coming from between two rising rock formations. Each one sporting an opening inside them. The one to the west is shrouded a bit from a light fog, being a little further away compared to the one just to the east.

The inside of the rock opens up into a fairly well illuminated room, the strange green glow coming from all around, casting shadows here and there inside the enclosed room. Faint whispers can be heard echoing off the walls, through the still silence.

A solid rock path curves between pools of bubbling lava. The intense heat washes over quite strongly, even from the raised height of the path. A dull glow of light comes from the north as the pathcomes to parallel a wall on the eastern side. To the southwest, another pool of lava separates from another path, and open area.

A solid rock pathway runs along the eastern wall. Small ripples and valleys rise and fall over the surface as the path bears north to south. A pool of bubbling lava flows just off the western edge. In the pool, the beginnings of another northward path can be seen, though getting there from here is not possible.

Turning around the bend in the path, the outcropping of rock reveals an opening into a small cave. Along the outer edge of the opening, a faint green glow coalesces, and runs up to the tip of the pyramid-like structure. The path splits off in three directions, giving much more to explore in the caverns.

This precipice of rock sticks out from the wall of the cave, taking on a dim green tinge, growing brighter as it makes its way down, and over the ledge. A metal loop hangs over the left edge of the ledge, with a thick rope tied to it, snaking its way deeper into the caves depths. A ladder is also here, leading back up.

rooms.name: Cave of the Gi-A tiny plateau.

userData.LongDescription: This ledge of rock undercuts a larger landing just above it, seeming to grow out like fingers from the ledge of rock. A rope hangs down, leading to the landing above, while a ladder leads down further  into the deep chasm. The breeze from above doesn't filter down here, keeping the air fairly stale, and cold.

A solid rock pathway bisects through a large pool of bubbling lava, running north to south. To the north the path leads deeper into the molten rock, with a high plateau of rock running parallel with the path. To the south, the higher path take a curve, coming right across the path, and continuing to the east. A cave has been cut out in the crossing path, eventually leading through to the other side.

The path is quite wide here, and splits off into three directions. Northwest leads back to the entrance of the area, while to the northeast a cliff can be seen rising high from the cave's floor. To the southeast, the path continues deeper into the caves, bending around an outcropping of rock.

A small section of the eastern wall juts out into the solid rock path running north to south. Along the wall patches of green light glow from within the rock here and there. The air thick and damp as heat rises from the pool of bubbling lava just over the western edge. Amidst the lava another path can be seen, but no evidence of how to get there is apparant.

The inside of the rock opens up into a fairly well illuminated room, the strange green glow coming from all around, casting shadows here and there inside the enclosed area. Faint whispers can be heard echoing from the walls through the silence.

Molten pools of bubbling lava surround a solid rock path, with another path seen running parallel to the west. The main path comes in from the southeast, then takes a turn to the northeast. The path continues on to the northeast, bisecting through the lava pools. Waves of heat rising from the pools distort the view slightly.

The sounds of churning lava can be heard all around, flowing throughout the caves. Waves of heat wash over the solid rock path, making the air uncomfortable to most. There is no real breeze to help with the stifling air, only managing a brief gust now and then. A path splits through the intense heat, leading toward the northeast and southeast.

A solid, rock path runs north to south, with a slight bend here and there. The edges fall off into a pool of bubbling lava, making the air thick, and stuffy. A wall rises along the western edge, the rock smooth over its face. To the south, the path widens a bit as a rusty goop coats over the ground.

Cut out from the wide path crossing overhead, this small cave provides little shelter from the intense heat of the cavern. It's relatively dark, except for a slight green hue coming from the smooth walls. Small batches of silk webbing are scattered about, showing signs of other inhabitants in the cavern. The ave cuts through completely, with a path leading towards the north and south.

Smooth, flat rock forms the inner walls of this cavern, widening out at the center.  To the north and south, the cavern leads out, with light coming from both directions. The light is a little brighter from the north, along with a constant gust of warm wind.

A solid, rock path runs north to south, the edges falling off into a pool of bubbling lava. A wall rises along the western edge, the rock speckled over with patches of a faint green glow. To the north, the path widens a bit, and has some sort of rusty goop coated over the rock. A faint cool breeze filters in from the south, giving slight relief from the room's oppressive heat.

Smooth rock forms the interior of this cave, making a comfortable passage through the rock wall. Light shines in from from the northeast, and the south, illuminating the path. From the south a warm breeze filters in, and from the northeast a softer gust can be felt every so often.

A stone stairway rises up from the rock walkway cutting east to west through the sweltering cavern. It leads to another path built up a bit higher then the one here. The heat is almost unbearable as the lava pools flow almost right up to the path's edge. Small pockets of air escape from the molten rock, assailing the senses with pungent sulfuric scents.

The inside of this structure isn't as big as the outside portrays, only giving a few feet of headroom. It's rather dark, except for the dull green glow coming from the walls. A faint breeze comes in from the outside, slightly warming up the cold atmosphere.

A small plateau of solid rock spreads out into the bubbling pools of lava scattered throughout the cavern. The heat strong, and constant as it radiates from the molten rock. The plateau shrinks down some as a path heads off to the south, and a large cave opening becons to the north. Around the edge of the cave opening, patches of green light glow dimly from within the rock, scattered about in no particular pattern.

Solid rock spreads out to a flat landing as three paths converge onto it. The landing narrows a bit as paths lead off to the north, south, and west. Over the eastern edge, hot lava bubbles throughout, making the air hot and stuffy. Further to the east another path can be seen running north to south, but how to get there is not openly apparent.

A plateau of solid rock flattens out to a wide plain as four paths converge. Between the paths it drops off suddenly into a bubbling vat of molten lava, flowing throughout the cavern. A path branches off on the northeast side, splitting to two paths heading east and northeast. Two other paths also branch off, heading off to the northwest, and southwest.

A solid rock pathway widens a bit along the eastern wall. Wave after wave of heat washes up from the pool of lava bubbling just over the western edge of the path. Another path can be seen a little further west admidst the lava, though getting there isn't possible from here. It parallels the current one heading north to south.

A solid rock path cuts through the blistering air of the cavern. It runs east to west, splitting off to the northwest. A set of stone stairs descends down into the sweltering heat rising from the bubbling pools of lava running throughout the cavern.

A solid rock path runs from north to south, with a high wall rising on its eastern edge. The western edge falls off into a ravine, filled with molten lava. Just past the ravine another path can be seen curving around the wall to the west, but how to get there is not openly apparent. To the north, the path continues deeper into the caves, while to the south a hot breeze whafts in from another section.

A wide rock path leads in a north/south direction, paralleling a high wall along the western edge. A large pool of lava bubbles continuously just off the eastern edge of the path, making the air swelter with heat. A little further to the east another path can be seen cutting through the lava, though how to get there remains unclear. Near the base of the western wall, a dull green hue glows from within the dense rock.

The path descends from west to east, starting to flatten out at the eastern side. The walls of the rock structure raise up from the east to west as small, green blotches dot over the surface, letting off a soft glow.

Rock rises up from the ground just to the northwest, the path bending around either side of the pyramid-like structure as small veins of green coalesce from the rock here and there. A warm whisp of wind filters down from around the structure, the only break in the area's silence.

Rock walls rise up around a widening rock path, enclosing the area and not helping with the stifling air. A larger stone juts out from the rock walls on the wast side. The path leads to the north and south, with the southern path looking a little brighter. The northern way leads to to a dark opening among the rock.

The path leads down to another opening set into a rockface, a green tinge scattered around its top edge. Bones are strewn about at the opening, not making it the most inviting place to go as a slightly chilly gust of wind sweeps down along the path.

Smooth rock walls widen out into a larger cavern as three openings converge here. Two openings are embedded into the walls to the south and southwest, dim light filters through the other side, along with a warm breeze. A brighter light comes from the opening to the north, leading out of the caves. A stronger breeze can be felt, swirling around in the room.

High walls of solid rock and stone rise along a flat rock path. To the southeast, a small opening appears in a high wall of rock, a cool breeze coming from its depths. The path continues to the north as the surrounding walls steadily descend, widening the path in its wake. A warmer breeze comes from the north, swirling about softly.

A long rock path stretches out to the northwest, bending around a wall of rock rising up high into the caverns. The air is warm as heat rises from the bubbling pool of lava just off the western edge of the path. The heat is deterred somewhat as a cool breeze drifts in from the opening to the south, leading into another area of the Gi Caves. A strange green glow can be seen coming from within the rock walls, getting more intense to the north and west.

Smooth rock forms the interior of this cave, making a comfortable passage through the rock wall. Light shines in from from the northwest and the east, illuminating the path. From the east a warm breeze filters in, and from the northwest a softer gust can be felt every so often.

A relatively wide expanse of solid rock spreads out amidst a large pool of bubbling lava. The plateau of land contracts to a small path leading south into a cave, cut out from the path crossing overhead. The lava depth is a bit more shallow here, but doesn't stop the intense heat rising all around. Another small plateau can be seen just to the east, with a path leading to the one coming over the cave.

Walls of solid rock encase the rock path leading north to south, forming a dark little cave inside the vast cavern. A faint breeze comes in from the outside, making any relief from the oppressive heat minimal at best. Scattered here and there, little clumps of silk webbing cling to the cave walls, waiting to grab its next victim. A couple dry husks are already trapped inside.

A solid rock path forms a small plateau, jutting out from a high rock wall to the west. The path continues on to the north, running parallel along the wall. The eastern edge of the path falls of suddenly into a deep chasm, where bubbling pools of molten lava flow throughout the caves. Waves of heat billow up from the depths, washing over the path.

Footsteps echo from the solid rock pathway running east to west through the cavern. Looking over the northern edge, a path can be seen coming out from under the current path, leading further north. The same can be seen looking south with a path coming out from an opening underneath.

Rock seems to be the theme element for most of the Gi caves, as it surrounds in all directions. A high wall of such rock rises on the path's eastern edge, continuing along to the north and south. To the west, the path drops off into a ravine, where molten lava bubbles and flows, sending waves of heat washing through the area. To the north, another wall of rock can be seen, though multiple openings can be made out.

A solid rock path runs along the eastern wall, coming in from the south before dropping off abruptly. The eastern wall curves around to the north just past the vast pool of lava, bubbling constantly just over the paths edge. The wall glows rather brightly with a green hue fanning out towards the north. Another path can be seen amidst the lava to the west, but from here there's no way to get to it.

Solid rock cuts through a large pool of bubbling lava, forming into a path that leads to the south and east. The molten rock flows up just to the edge of the path, constantly melting, and reforming the sides. Waves of heat blow across the path, refusing to give any relief from the torrent of the cavern. Just to the west a high ledge can be seen running parallel with the path.

The path here gets very skinny, the rock walls closing in tight as a warm, gusty wind comes from around the bend to the northeast, swirling up little dustdevils here and there. A dim light can be seen coming from there as well, casting shadows behind jutting out rocks.

The path leads up between the two rising pyramid-like structures, creating a mini valley. The wind picks up a bit as it rushes into the relativly cramped space. A mix of cool gusts from the south, and warmer ones from the north as the path continues deeper into the valley.

The path declines steadily from west to east as the wall of rock to the north rises, and reveals an opening, leading inside the structure. A faint breeze can be felt from the west as a light fog rolls into the area, casting a blanket of silence throughout.

A solid rock path runs in a north/south direction. A high wall of rock rises along the eastern side, marking the boundry of the cavern. A constant barrage of sweltering heat comes from the pool of bubbling lava just over the western edge of the path. Another path can be seen amidst the magma, though getting there isn't quite clear.

Three solid rock paths converge to a wide flat plain.  Along the surface, small rises and dips are scattered about as the paths split off to the north, west, and south. The air is hot, and thick as breezes from every direction blow in quite warm. Any relief from it seems rather distant.

Rock walls rise up along a smooth, rock path leading north and south. A gentle breeze of hot air blows in from the south, giving no relief from the stagnant air. Criss-crossing back and forth from wall to wall, sticky fibres make a strong webbing, shifting slightly with the gentle breezes. Their creator could be nearby...

Nestled away in what seems to be a little corner of the caves, a small cave opens into a large rock wall to the northwest. A solid rock path leads the way between the cave, and further away to the east. Just to the north, a plateau can be seen on a higher plane, and a large gap in between. Looking down, a hot blast of heat washes up from the bubbling pools of molten lava, flowing throughout the caves.

A rocky cliff rises here, leading up a steep incline before flattening out a good distance away. A soft light filters down from above, giving a hint of a possible area. It's further accented as a mix of warm and cool drafts filter down into the area. A flattened path leads back to the southwest as there's no apparant other way to go.

The cave opens up to various paths, and caverns. Stalactites hang down from the ceiling in fluctuating lengths, some nearly reaching the ground. The breeze continues gently, coming from the northeast, a mix of warm and cool gusts washing over.

Smooth rock encloses this small room, making it comparatively darker to others nearby. Uncomfortably warm winds bombard the room from the north and south, not giving any relief from the oppressive heat. Two openings lead out of the room to the north and south, into the rock walls.

Molten pools of bubbling lava flow along the eastern border of a solid rock path. A high rock wall rises along the western edge, running north along the path. The main path comes in from the southwest, then takes a turn to the north. The path continues on to the north, with waves of heat rising from the pool.

A sharp cliff rises up from the ground, a faint green glow coalesces from the smooth rock, fading up along the incline. A dim light comes from above as the cliff flattens out out of reach. A gentle warm breeze washes over, giving a hint of an area to explore, yet unreachable from here.

The walls of the cave glow with a light green hue, growing steadily brighter as they descend down further into the shaft. A thick twine of rope hangs down from above, leading to another ledge. A large metal loop is embedded into the side of the plateau, hanging over the edge, with another thick strand of rope tied to it, descending down into the deep trench. The glow of the rocks doesn't show any ledges nearby to hop to.

A solid rock pathway bisects through a large pool of bubbling lava. Waves, upon waves of heat dance across as they come from the molten rock. The path runs north to south, with the lava lapping up at its edge every so often. A plateau of rock runs parallel with the path to the west.

Keeping along the path set in the cave, it splits off in two directions. To the the northeast, a cliff can be seen rising up, while to the southeast the path continues. Stalactites hang down from the ceiling, sending small droplets of water down to the cave's surface.

A thin ledge stretches out to the west along the wall of the cavern. A good view of the Gi Caves can be seen spreading out through the dim light. The ledge drops off suddenly to the cavern below, showing no way to get down. An opening to the north is the only means of exit as a warm breeze filters in.

This is the highest part of the path, leading sharply down to the southeast, and southwest around the pyramid-like structure. Within the far wall, and the structure itself, patches of a dull green glow can be seen. A faint light is also seen down the southwest path.

A solid rock pathway bends around an outcropping of rock from the eastern wall. It comes to a point on the western side before dropping off into a bubbling pool of lava. Just over the edge of the path, a trail of green light glows down from the rock. The same glow can be found in the outcropping of rock, radiating quite brightly from within the solid stone. A cool breeze filters in from the southwest, doing its best to counter the intense heat of the cavern.

rooms.name: Further down in the Cave of the Gi

userData.LongDescription: A larger plateau juts out from the ledge of rock. A ladder leads back up out from the caves, and a large metal loop is embedded into the side of the plateau. Hanging over the edge a wide of rope is tied to the loop, descending further into the caves. The chill in the air is a constant reminder of why these caves were cut off.

Smooth rock forms the interior of this cave, making a comfortable passage through the rock wall. Light shines in from from the north, and the south, illuminating the path. From the south a warm breeze filters in, and from the north a softer gust can be felt every so often.

The incline flattens out here a bit as the wall of rock to the north continues to rise. Through the fog, a light green hue can be seen upon the walls. The path leads down to the east, and up toward the west, with a faint light filtering through the fog.

Solid rock forms into a flat plain, widening from the cave entrance to the north. The plain drops off suddenly into a deep gorge, the bottom not seen as hot air rises from the depths. Far to the southeast a path can be seen running south to north, but there's no way to get there from here directly.

Solid rock forms to a narrow path, running from north to south. Another small path breaks off to the southwest, with a growing pool of lava in between. A larger pool runs along the eastern edge, billowing waves of heat throughout the area.

Three paths converge into one, covered over by a rusty oil slick. To the north, east, and south, the path splits to the rest of the cavern, and out of the mess in the room. A large wall rises to the west, with small holes here and there, most of which at waist level.

Constant gurgling of molten lava can be heard flowing throughout the caves. Waves of heat wash over the solid rock path, making the air stifling, and hard to breathe. There is no real breeze to help with the stifling air, only managing a brief gust now and then. A path splits through the intense heat, leading toward the northwest and southwest.

A solid rock path spreads out before a higher rise of rock to the north. In the rock, five different cave openings stand, receding into darkness. Where they lead is anyone's guess. To the south, and west, the path drops off into a deep ravine, where molten lave bubbles, and flows under the area. Just past the ravine, another path can be seen coming from a tiny passage to the west.

Solid rock forms into a flat path, curving its way around a rock wall to the south and west. It runs parallel along the tall outcroppings as the path drops off to a deep crevice to the north and east. Pools of bubbling lava flow through the trench, and out through the caves. Waves of heat rise up, flowing over the path and rock.

A jagged stone cliff, bare of life, faces the northern wastelands that lie outside the canyon.  The ground outside the cave is a sheet of black stone, warm from the magma that flows beneath it.  Steam rises from the rock, dispelling into the cool air.  Dusty red landscape stretches north as far as the eye can see.

This small foothold of rock grows out from the ledge, widening to a confortable landing as the light starts to fade.  A ladder leads down further into the darkness, and a wide length of rope is leading up into the higher areas of the caves. The already stale, chilly air becomes even more still as the light fades.

The path rises from east to west along the northeastern edge of the rock structure, as its walls rise steadily with small veins of green seen glowing from within. The path takes a turn northwest around the growing structure, and to the east a figure can be made out on the far wall in the next area.

A firm rock path stretches out underfoot, leading north into the open cavern, and an opening to the south. Along the western wall, a bright patch of green coalesces from within the rock, to just before the opening. To the east, over the edge of the path, a pool of lava bubbles steadily, spreading throughout the cavern. The air is thick, and humid from the intense heat, with no signs up it letting up anytime soon.

Smooth rock forms the interior of this cave, making a comfortable passage through the rock wall. Light shines in from from the north and the south, illuminating the path. From the south a warm breeze filters in, and from the northeast a softer gust can be felt every so often.

A large rectangular rug covers the checkered floor. On either end of the large rug are a set of stairs; one ascends to the third floor, the other to the palace's foyer. A very heavy looking bookcase conveniently rests upon the rear portion of the immaculate rug, keeping it firmly in its place. Various colorful objects and small chests are nestled neatly upon the bookcase's shelves, their purpose beyond that of decoration would be hard to identify.

On either side of the hallway a figure of a goddess stands, hair and dress flowing in a long curling wave which come to rest at the top of a small cube shaped pedestal. Between the goddesses runs a narrow rug with a sapphire hue. The rug leads up to and seems to feed under or terminate at the base of a wide stairway, whose steps span the very width of the hallway itself. Off to the left side of the hall several sparkling stars hover above the ground in a small circle.

This southeastern corner of the second floor forms one point of a perimeter overlooking a small reading room upon the first floor. Vividly distinguishable is contrast between the wooden slats of the floor below and the darkly checkered stone which spans the entire second floor. A distinct lack of any balustrades surrounding the large rectangular opening gives the impression the architects wanted easy access to the small room below, or possibly a painful fall should one lose their balance.

Two eerily demonic figures have been placed against either wall cramping the already narrow hallway, both look inward with disturbingly lifelike magenta eyes in an attempt the frighten away those lacking the courage to pass. Large posters adorn either side of a dark doorway, depicting in gold and purple the powerful Mammon Machine. Above the doorway the crest of Zeal projects forth symbolizing the height of power the kingdom has attained.

Sequestered comfortably in the far east corner of the bedroom is a small bed. A vermillion blanket covered in gold stitching, with what appears to be an angel at the center covers it quite neatly. Between the stairway exiting the room and the bed is a small table and stool resting at the center of a large violet-red rug. Sunlight pours into the room through three closed windows. A large plant with flowers in full bloom has been placed intelligently below one of the clear windows. The only storage space in view is two large bookcases, filled only with various objects and a variety of colorfully bound volumes.

Atop this high level of the palace it becomes readily apparent that the flooring schemes are alternating from wooden slats to darkly checkered stone. Propped up against the western wall is another of the heavy bookcases regularly in use throughout the palace. Three stools sit in a triangular formation around the bookcase, obviously comfortable research was not a consideration in the choice of seating. A stairway of impressive girth leads further upward to the final floor.

The library walls are lined with cold gray stone bricks. There are two bookcases beside a golden angelic sculpture within the wall. A violet-red rug is laid in the center of the room, with a lacquered mahogany table placed in its midst. Atop the table, a royal purple tapestry with prominent gold embroidery has been spread out and generously hangs over the table's smooth edges. A green book has been placed on top of the tapestry.

rooms.name: The Hall Of The Mammon Machine

userData.LongDescription: At the center of the platform two demon-like statues sit on either side of an empty mechanical base, presumably where the Mammon Machine once stood. Large bright purple carpets surround the base, their edges covered in intricate gold stitching. Six metal beams seem to secure the circular platform in place. Along the lower sides of the platform monstrous faces protrude, with large purple eyes, and sharp-toothed open mouths. Silhouetting the entire platform is an immense reddish-orange shape pulsating as if alive in some way.

The lower western corner of the palace is occupied by an immense table. Golden grooves carved upon the table's dark surface form two identical symbols, one of which is partially obstructed by an open book. A candelabra holding three tall candles sits off center on the table; though the flames brightly illuminate the corner they never seem to flicker or move in the slightest. Seating is limited to two small stools.

Standing below the marble balustrade of the floor above is a large bookcase; its shelves evenly filled with red and green bound books no doubt of the highest scholarly measure. Juxtaposed beside the bookcase stands a bizarre metallic sculpture. It rises from a small square base through a whirlwind of thick metal wires and ends in a large globular head. Opposite the furniture is a view of a colorful reading room lying on the first floor.

Stairways are visible leading both higher into the palace and lower towards its exit. Acting like a guide, a long violet-red carpet runs along the center of the stairways, never rumpling as if held in place by unseen magical forces. Huge potted plants, yellow flowers in full bloom, lie decoratively at each side of the center platform.

The long and elegant violet-red carpet ends before a large open doorway. At the top of the doorway Zeal's shield-like crest rests in suitable prominence, overlooking the palace's entirety. Two beautiful stone statues resembling goddesses stand on large pedestals on either side of the doorway. Large golden potted plants rest against the walls, large yellow flowers in full bloom, only further enhancing the beauty of the palace's peak.

This narrow platform at the third floor nears the peak of the palace's primary stairwell. What's different at this point is the juncture of stairways allowing normal passage to the eastern and western sides of the palace. Importantly acting as guide, the long violet-red rug continues beyond the base of the stairwell and still further forward, beyond the final stairway north.

The complete surrounding of a marble balustrade gives a distinct air of protection to this area. Two plants sit upon a large violet-red rug; one grows from a golden pot and is much larger than the other, its flowers in full bloom and its leaves nearly touch the floor; the smaller emerges from a plain brown sack and has but a single stalk with only two tiny leaves sprouting from it. Parallel the carpet is a strange golden-framed square, an intricate array of lines form an indigo symbol at its center.

A large circular platform suspended by six metal beams form the majority of the room. An incredible throne wrought in gold and upholstered in purple fabric sits mightily at the rear of the platform. Complementing the throne is an extravagant purple carpet covering the bulk of the floor, with intricate gold stitching running along its sharp corners. Grotesque faces project from the lower sides of the platform, light emitting from their open jaws and deep purple orbs serving as eyes. A spotlight forms a large circle at the axis of the platform. Within the spotlight a small black circle floats motionlessly, at its center a small white-blue light flashes constantly between the shape of a diamond and star.

Near the center stairwell stand two large bookcases side-by-side, their shelves completely filled. A surprisingly large rug covers the floor leaving almost none of the darkly checkered stone floor below in view. Sitting near the eastern wall before a high marble balustrade is medium sized wooden table; upon the table only a small golden angelic statue and candelabra sit. Recessed at the back of the northern wall is a high doorway, above it Zeal's crest is prominently displayed.

The walls narrow inwardly toward a high opening. At the proximal end of each golden wall beside the opening a tall pillar has been carved; a rounded ball simulates its apex while its base is a small square with a gold emblem on a pea-green background. At the eclipse of the opening a fanciful gold design heralds the shield-like crest of Zeal. Even the sapphire rug at the center of the hall accentuates the importance of what lies north as it comes to a pointed end before the opening.

A dark sapphire rug runs through the center of the hall ending under the base of a long stairway. The floor maintains its dark checkered appearance, except that the dark and light squares have become much grayer in tone. Before the stairway, two large demonic statues perch upon golden bases. Behind the statues large gold and purple posters can be slightly discerned.

Along the L-shaped corner overlooking the foyer runs a thick marble balustrade. Within the protective boundaries of the balustrade rests a large wooden table where a fully lit candelabra clearly illuminates the table's top revealing a map-like series of lines. Closed, a lone green-bound volume rests near the center of the table's surface.

As expected of a royal bedroom, this one is extremely neat and mature. Two closed windows let in the bright glowing rays of the sun. A small bed has been set directly under one of the windows; the bedding upon the gold-wrought frame is a beautifully made vermillion with gold stitching. A small stool and desk have been placed a few feet from the foot of the bed. The opposite side of the room houses two large bookcases, both completely filled with books and various ornate objects. Allowing passage from the room is a stairway, convenient albeit precarious in function.

The introductory decor within the palace presents an odd mixture of possible themes. Evenly distributed upon the walls are gold inlaid designs which appear to be a simplistic representation of an angelic body. A tall regally carved wooden bookcase stands in one corner, its shelves almost completely filled with colorfully bound volumes. Rectangular panels of wood set in a diagonal formation compose the floor. Various paths are available from the foyer; standing out in particular is a violet-red carpet leading under an archway to the north.

An elegant violet-red carpet laid at the center of the floor begins from the mouth of an archway to the south, and extends up a series of stairways toward the highest floor of the palace. Set in the walls on either side of the first stairway are a pair of ornately carved angelic representations. Rounded moldings run along the walls allowing for a smooth transition to the diagonally slatted wooden flooring.

Simple in design, this rectangular antechamber is focused solely on the prominence of Zeal herself rather than those who dwell within. At the extreme right and left sides of the northern wall two archways permit passage into the royal bedrooms. Above each the crest of Zeal sits, thick gold outlining a purple shield. Between the openings are two large potted plants. Centered upon the wall two posters of the Mammon Machine standout brightly.

A large bookcase is positioned against the northern wall: its shelves have been filled with an odd assortment of colorful shapes and boxes. A lone stool has been placed beside the bookcase, presumably to allow the vertically challenged access to the upper shelves. Noticable is the instance of a balustrade solely along the southern edges of the floor, where in all other directions they are dangerously non-existent. This point seems to serve as a junction with stairways leading to the first and third floors.

Two very demonic looking figures crouch upon large metallic pedestals, appearing very much like keenly watching gatekeepers. Beyond the figures lies a darkened opening at least eight feet in height. Zeal's crest sits in high prominence above the doorway, while large purple banners on either side portray the Mammon Machine in bright gold stitching.

Sequestered at one end of this platform a large violet-red rug rests beneath a small table and two hearty bookcases. Upon the table beside a closed book, a small golden stand with a rounded top cradles a brilliant red orb, its purpose beyond decoration is unclear. A small squat stool has been placed near each of the bookcases, no doubt to facilitate the reach of higher shelves. At the proximal end of the platform the center stairway comes clearly into view.
A roly-poly Mystic Pet rolls around.
A woman, eyes closed, mumbles various incantations.

The small yard is enclosed on two sides by a short, golden fence and on the other two sides by the wall which encircles the city. There is nothing of interest in this yard, but it is shaded, providing a bit of relief from the beating sun. To the north is a road which leads either to the city center or to the item shop.

This corner of the wall peers into the yard just outside the inn where King Manmon lives. It is difficult to see much past the golden branches of the two large trees, but this place is on level with the second floor of the inn making it quite easy to peer inside. The walkway forces travelers to go either east or south.

This is the top of the eastern side of the gateway which leads north to the tower. Below, many tourists can be seen milling about, but strangely none are moving anywhere near the tower. From this close, the golden tower is intimidating with it's shadow edging very near to the wall of the Gold City.

This room is pretty sparse with naught but a single shrub and a small, hanging picture for decoration. There are also no windows, leaving it comfortably cool. It appears the staff working in the building use this as a rest area. A set of stairs leads down to the main floor, and another leads up to the top floor.

rooms.name: Gold City Tea Shop, Second Floor

userData.LongDescription: This is the second floor of the tea shop. There are several windows peering out into the city below, framed with drapes. The windows which face west have been closed to reduce the strength of the ambient light. There are also three small tables and one long table set up to have guests seated at them, though there are no guests in the shop.

The inn is the largest building within the walls of the Gold City. It is three stories high with several windows on the south face. All of the drapes are shut, but for one set that is open on the top floor. Apparently King Manmon enjoys looking out upon his wealth.

This entire city is a magnificent construction and testament to the wealth of the king who built it. Everything is made of gold, including the tower to the north. To the east lies the three-story royal palace which also doubles as an expensive hotel for tourists. West leads to the item shop, and south leads to the center of the city. There is also a set of stairs here, leading up to the top of the wall which encompasses the city.

This section of the wall looks westward over the open seas. Many gulls can be seen performing aerial displays far from the city. The courtyard below the other side of the wall seems very small and contained from here, though the single golden tree makes it look inviting. The path continues north and south.

rooms.name: Gold City - Outside the Item Shop

userData.LongDescription: The item shop is a quaint little building with the right half of it set a short distance back from the left half. The left half has two windows peering out, while the right half only has an arched, french-style doorway leading inside. To the south is a golden tree. Eastward is a road which leads back to the center of the Gold City, and further east is the inn in which King Manmon resides.

This point in the wall is at the southernmost edge of the golden isle. There is a sharp dropoff just before the wall with crags and rocks jutting into the open air ready to skewer anything that falls. Within the city, the tea shop lies directly below, it's door facing toward the wall. The path goes onward west and east.

The item shop is a quaint little building set up for comfort. It has a loveseat sitting by the counter and a table setup for tea time just off to the left of the entryway. In addition, there is a bookcase with reading material and a small shrubbery to make the place look homey. Behind the counter, there are several containers holding the goods to be sold.

The wall here is bright and sunny, unobstructed by barriers. The light glints and glares off of every surface, making it seem even more blinding. A window can be seen on this side of the inn, peering into the staff-area of the inn, but the window, itself, is barred to prevent unlawful entry. The path runs west and south.

The wall forms another angle here, as it makes room for the armory. The armory is about half as high as the wall, making the wall seem larger than it really is. Looking out over the city is quite breath-taking as the large golden tower seemingly juts right out of the water. The path continues west and south.

This area is marked with a single, large, golden tree. It's unsure whether the tree is living and painted or just a golden sculpture, but the shade it provides is comfortable. The item shop lies to the north. To the south is an enclosed yard or some sort. The city center lies to the east.

This open alley is brightly lit by the ambient sunlight reflecting off of the many golden surfaces. Despite the obvious wealth, muggings are very rare. The road turns south, leading toward the southern wall and the far side of the tea shop. The alley leads west to the center of the city.

rooms.name: Gold City - Outside the Tea Shop

userData.LongDescription: A building stands here holding a sign that marks this as a tea shop. There is very little decorating the outside of the shop except for a window at chest height. Above, on the second floor, a few smaller windows dot the walls, but the drapes are closed. An arched double-door stands as the entryway.

There is a shop here with a sign over the door. It is a single-level building with a window on either side of the door. On the sign is a delicately emblazoned shield. The drapes prevent the bright sunlight from getting inside. The door is arched and primarily glass with a gold frame. To the east is the tea shop, and the road to go back to the center of town.

rooms.name: Gold City Weapon and Armor Shop

userData.LongDescription: The armor shop is a small building with just a simple, gold painted, wooden counter separating the sales area from the clerk area. Rather than having expensive armors displayed for viewing, there is a filing cabinet along one wall with pictures of the items for sale accompanied by their respective prices. Behind the counter, there are a few book shelves packed with books and baubles.

This is the northwestern corner of the wall. It stands directly over the item shop, providing a crisp view of the building's roof. The sparse rails allow the wind to sweep the wall clean of any debris, making the wall safe to walk upon. The golden tower is still a captivating sight from here, but it is not quite so magnificent.

This is the residence of the famed King Manmon. Sometime in his youth, he stumbled upon a secret method of turning rocks into gold. He not only sold enough of the gold to pay for the construction of this city, but he had more than enough left over to use as construction material. Nearly every structure around has at least a majority of gold in it.

This portion of the wall is deeply shaded by the girth of the inn. It is noticeably cooler here than in other areas of the city. There is an empty water bottle laying on the ground, as if someone had taken a rest recently and doesn't know how to use garbage cans. The path continues north and west.

The inside of this quaint shop is brightly colored, probably to match the strong yellows of the outside city. There is wooden counter surrounding the saleswoman with a small clock on it against the back wall. A simple stove lies in the back corner, presumably used for making the teas which should be sold here. There is a set of stairs leading up to the second floor, and a french-style, arched door leading outside.

The Gold City appears to be an amazing place. The ground sparkles as the sun reflects off the soft gold, which glows a tantalizing yellow. In fact, the road is paved with gold, the buildings are constructed of it, and even the trees are sculptures made of the soft metal. A large wall, also made of gold, encircles the whole city. The populous appears to be moving around excitedly, bewildered by King Manmon's audacity to build an entire city of gold.

The inn is a fairly large building. The inside holds the same strong yellows and golds contained in other buildings, making the whole place seem bright. Several beds are lined up in the western part of the room. There is a sign leaning on the counter. There is a set of stairs here, leading up to the second story. A door in the south wall leads to the courtyard, outside.

This section of the wall lies above the armory, though it is separated by a short distance. From here, anyone entering the armory can be seen clearly. The Gold Tower looms large in the distance, providing an excellent landmark. The path on top of the wall continues north and east.

This corner of the city is shaded from the sun, though all of the gold reflects the sunlight keeping this area almost as bright. The wall looms large, and provides a strong surface against to lean against. To the west lies the entrance to the tea shop, and further, the armor shop. To the north lies a brightly lit alley.

The view from up here is amazing. Looking out over the ocean, no land is visible. Looking in over the city, everything is visible. From this vantage, any defenders could spot pirates, or other enemy ships from many leagues away. The wall, itself, is composed entirely of gold mixed with certain other alloys to provide great strength and endurance. This particular portion of the wall forms one end and also holds the stairs to go down. The path continues to the west.

This portion of the wall angles sharply east to avoid running off of the island. There is a small yard just below this point of the wall. It seems few people come up here because nearly everyone is too preoccupied with the golden construction on the ground level. The walkway continues north and east.

Below the outer wall, there is a small piece of land which appears to be untouched by the golden finger of King Manmon. It appears lush and green with a duet of trees standing straight and firm, peering off into the open ocean. This portion of the wall forms a ninety-degree angle, driving the wall north and west.

Standing here, amid the golden-colored trees of Gold City, is the Light Palace. The walls are made of mismatched bricks, each a dull gold color that makes the entire building shine metallic in the light. A short stair leads to the gate: a heavy yew door surrounded by an ornate archway. Along the grassy path grow neat rows of sky blue and pink flowers.

As with the second floor, the fourth floor consists of a single large room. The stairways are actually in the middle of the room as opposed to the north and south ends, in the middle of a large pedestal. A seam in the floor gives the impression that the pedestal used to rise or fall to hide access to this floor, but the mechanism must be broken. High on the wall, torches cast long shadows over the otherwise empty room.

Beyond the gate outside is this small room, a foyer of sorts. The brickwork from outside continues inside the palace, though without sunlight the metallic glare isn't as prominent. The room widens from the entrance, and then narrows again at the far wall, in the center of which is a door leading further into the palace.

A rather open and plain room, this is the stairwell between the third and fourth floors of the tower. The light of the two green flames burning astride the door cast long shadows on the stone floor. The west side of the room is dominated by the wide stairway leading up to the next floor.

Apparently the second floor consists of this room and this room alone. It's rather expansive as a result, but with no windows to judge how high up the place is. Only the green torches give the room any light whatsoever. At the back of the room are two very high and very thick pedestals. In the room's center, north and south stairways lead up and down, respectively.

The long, narrow corridor that runs from the west continues here. Once again the north wall features the room's major decorative device; a stained glass window, ornately decorated and colored with all shades of gold. The small green flames which provide light for the room are also present. A supernatural light shines from the entrance back to the west, but does not continue through the rest of the tower. To the south is a white wooden door leading onward.

This rather open and plain room serves as the stairwell between the first and second floors of the Palace. Twin green torches burn on either side of the entranceway, casting shadows on the grey stone floor. On the west side of the room is a slight curve in the wall, and the stairs leading up to the second floor.

This room is at the top of the stairs from the second floor, and is almost identical to the foyer just inside the gate on the first floor. In the south part of the room are the stairs leading back down to the previous floor, while to the north is a wooden door leading onward. The ever-present green torches provide their warm glow as well.

The east corridor is almost identical to its counterpart on the first floor. As always the north wall has the room's only  decorative object; a cathedral stained glass window, ornately decorated in shades of gold. The green torches which provide light for the palace are naturally present. To the south is a white wooden door leading onward.

At the top of the Light Palace is the grand Stage Room, where the Mana Seed of Light rests. This wide room faces north, and the north wall is dominated by four of the stained glass windows found elsewhere in the palace, with a central window that is round instead of cathedral. Tall white pillars with engraved gold bases line the east and west walls, and the Stage is surrounded by six huge torches in a half circle. Light pouring through the stained glass gives this room an intense, hazy golden aura.

This is a long, narrow corridor that run the breadth of the tower-like palace. The north wall is the feature of prominence, here; directly opposite the entrance to the foyer is a stained glass window, ornately decorated and colored with all shades of gold. Colored patterns of light shine through the window and decorate the floor. Sconces high on the wall hold small green flames, but are unneeded; there seems to be an all-encompassing supernatural source of light.

Surprisingly, this corridor is almost exactly the same as the one two floors below it. The stained glass window on the north wall is the same style as before, but is higher above the treeline, allowing more light to shine through. Sconces high on the wall hold the green flames which provide light for the room.

Pure elemental energy suffuses this realm, to the extent that nearly nothing else exists.  There are no perceivable floor, walls, ceiling, just mana.  It is a realm beyond mortal comprehension, and is where the most powerful of elemental beings reside.

The house in which you stand is deserted.  However, a bed, a bathroom, and a kitchen are visible.  The owner of this house must be at the bar or the beach.  If so, they've been gone awhile, because the bed doesn't look like it's been used in a while.

The whole place is nicely decorated with a beach decor, probably just another attempt to trick tourists into renting it.  There's a posh bed in the corner, as well as a bathroom, and a fridge.  A table not in use stands near the entrance.

This is the entrance to the beach tourist town, Costa del Sol.  The sun is shining brightly, the wind blows slightly, and the weather is perfect.  Many people wander about the streets.  The street meanders to the east, while above, there is a small bridge leading to a house and the harbor. Westward leads to the field outside.

To the north stands a comfy looking beach-side villa.  There's also a lovely view of the town from here.  One can see the harbor, the beach, and the people crowding the city streets.   To the south lies the harbor, while the stairs lead down to the entrance of the town.  More tourists stand around here, and the entrance to the house stands ajar.

The street goes both east and south from here, and it seems to head towards the beach to the east.  To the south, there is a bar, and then the street turns sharply.  A large house can be seen to the west, as well as a large seagull flying overhead.

The street here turns northward, and also leads to a bar.  The windows of the bar are tinted, but light still shines through them.  The bar seems to welcome any and all tourists.  There is a tall, wooden sign outside the tavern.

This portion of the street seems to be a little less cemented, and the rocks are giving way to patches of sand here and there.  There are a few trees here, providing some cover from the heat.  There is also a shop here, with a sign out in front.

rooms.name: Costa del Sol's Bar and Equipment Shop

userData.LongDescription: This bar looks to be well-kept, and is a definite tourist trap.  The walls are beautifully decorated, and the floors are mopped and polished.  There are trinkets displayed on the counter, and the barkeep is overly friendly.  There is a pinball machine in the corner, too.
The street ends here, and a small path leads south towards the beach.  A lot of people are running towards it, with lotion in hand, while some people are running back, wrapped in towels.

Seabells clang in the distance as boats dock and depart the busy harbor.  Costa del Sol, being a busy seaport and tourist location, has many boats going between it and Junon, bringing tourists, Shinra employees, and other goods.  You could probably hitch a ride yourself.

The street leads east-west here, west heading towards a house, east to a beach.  The street is made up of randomly-sized rocks, cemented together.  Before you is a shop of some sort, with a sign standing to the side of the door.

All around, gift and souvenir items are being peddled, such as perfumes and key chains.  A large fake shark fin is displayed on the counter, while a large surfboard leans against the wall.  The proprietor of the store is wearing a gaudy shirt, which is complimented by his ridiculous shorts.

You stand on a sandy beach.  The waves ripple back and forth as the tide rises and falls.  A few palm trees stand, adding a touch of green to the rather beige area.  There are many people swimming in the water, and others laying out on the sand sunbathing.  And please, if you're gonna hang out here.. GET A CHAIR!

Brilliant colors assault the eyes as one looks around this small shop.  Shirts made up of green palm trees and beige beaches splashed onto a blue background hang on neat racks, while various shapes and sizes of sandals are displayed below.  A friendly salesman greets you at the counter.

Surrounded by boxes on two sides, and a towering set of stairs on the other, this small portion of the cabin remains accessible.  The space is very small and cramped and offers little room for comfort.  However, the placement of boxes make this section an excellent hideout for a lazy worker trying to take a break.

Complementing those on the ground floor, many more controls are situated in the wall.  Splitting up two sections of controls, a large ventilation duct is also fixated into the wall.  Additionally, a railing has been set up on the ledge to prevent the clumsy from having an accident.

Dozens of crates of several different sizes clutter the floor of the ship's cabin - lines of boxes stacked to the ceiling fill most of the interior, leaving very little space for movement.  Blocked off by gates are two generators situated in the corners of the ship, providing power for the lighting.

Much like the section immediately below, this platform also grants a spectacular ocean view.  However, this platform is constructed of wood and has a rail around its perimeter.  Additionally, a series of ropes hangs about, used to manipulate the mast.

Differing from the majority of the deckhouse, a few boxes and barrels - some leftover cargo that wouldn't fit in the cabin - are stacked up next to the ship's fore-mast.  The fore-mast rises many feet above the floor of the deckhouse, used as a mounting point for radar antennas.

Two sets of stairs extend to the ceiling, parallel to one another, both serving different purposes.  The first serves as a means of stacking and retrieving boxes at the highest elevations, while the second allows workers to go to the deckhouse.  Like much of the cabin, this portion is also cluttered with boxes.  However, it differs in that a small nook is left boxless, creating an intersection.

Two large generators dominate the majority of this small room, one on each side of the ship's controls.  A window is in place at the bow of the ship, allowing a helmsman to see where to steer the ship.  A ladder near the corner of the room leads up to a walkway, and a set of stairs leads into the main area of the cabin.

A large structure, used as the ship's command center separates the bow of the ship from the stern.  The structure is encased in bulletproof glass, with only one door available for entry and exit.  However, a large gate has been constructed in front of the building, making it impossible to enter or get to the back of the ship.

Offering a marvelous view of the ocean, this is the ideal spot for cargo workers to take a break.  The upper deck has no siding, making it possible to have a seat while still being able to see the ocean.  A ladder leads down to the main floor of the deckhouse and a set of stairs leads to a slightly higher section of the upper deck.

Contrary to much of the cabin, this section has relatively few boxes to hinder movement.  However, several barrels of water are situated in a corner, next to a large door leading to a back room and series of stairs leading to the deckhouse.

Used to check for unexpected conditions, this platform is one of the few sections of the ship that offers any sort of ocean view.  The platform is very small, having only enough space for a few people, and has a wooden barrier to prevent any 'Man Overboard' situations.  On the side away from the ocean, a ladder leads below to the main area of the deck.

Situated at the bow of the ship, a series of stairs leads below to the cabin where all the cargo is stored.  Across from the stairs, on the starboard, an elevated deck allows a better view of the ocean to gauge the path more carefully.

Connecting the bridge to the bow of the ship, this thin walkway offers little hope of an ocean view.  The ship's siding extends well above the floor, creating difficulty for even the tallest of creatures to see over it.  However, a ladder across from the siding leads to an upper section of the deckhouse.

The tower's dark magic pulses like a heartbeat, filling the room with its barely felt throbbing.  The room itself is very nondescript, with nothing in it but an empty chest collecting dust on the far side of the wall, opposite the door leading out.

A chain of snow-covered mountains can be seen far off in the distance. Dark clouds cover the sky, and a gusty wind blows. The musty stairs appear to go on forever, perhaps a trick of the magic aura seeming to radiate from the very tower itself.

A door in the side of the tower breaks the monotony of climbing the endless stairway, inviting people to come inside, away from the harsh elemental forces that surround the tower.  The magical pulses of energy seem stronger in this area, as if the tower itself wants people to notice the doorway.

A set of spiraling stairs seem to reach from the ground to the heavens. A strong wind blows dust and gravel around the tower in eddies and gusts, darkening the air all around. Magic pulses in a barely felt beat, seeming to echo throughout the tower.

The tower seems to darken, apparently the result of its powerful magical aura.  The only true light is provided by the constant flashes of lightning in the sky.  The wind howls between lightning strikes, but the wild storm never actually strikes the tower itself.

Ornate armor flanks the chest that sits in the back of this room, as if to guard it.  The entire room is more extravagant than the rest of the tower, with arcane runes scrawled across the wall that slowly pulse with light.  There is only one exit, the door that leads back out to the roof.

Enormous mountains surround the seemingly neverending tower, and a howling wind blows eerily from them. The rocky ground leaves very little space for grass to grow, and has several tracks of small footprints going around the tower. The spiraling stairs seem to reach to the sky.

The steep spiraling stairs stretch far up and down, penetrating the musty clouds that stretch out as far as the eye can see. The tower seems to be pulsing quite strongly with latent magics. A forceful wind pounds at the tower, perhaps strengthened by the powerful magic.

The stairs of the brick tower stretch as far as the eye can see. The black clouds surrounding the tower seem to get darker and darker, perhaps as a result of the magical energies coming from it. Flashes of lightning can occasionally be seen in the distance.

A set of spiraling stairs seem to reach from the ground to the heavens. A strong wind blows dust and gravel around the tower in eddies and gusts, darkening the air all around. Magic pulses in a barely felt beat, seeming to echo throughout the tower.

Clouds circle the tower in a vaguely menacing manner, pressing around the walls to give a chill, damp feeling to the area.  A faint, almost unfelt throb of malice emanates from the tower itself, as if to warn people to stop their efforts to climb to the top of the tower.

The top of the tower is so high, that the ground directly below the tower cannot be seen, masked by distance and swirling dark clouds that gather around the tower itself.  A penthouse building sits in the middle of the tower's roof, and arcane symbols are etched all around the penthouse's doorway.

The stairs of the brick tower stretch as far as the eye can see. The black clouds surrounding the tower seem to get darker and darker, perhaps as a result of the magical energies coming from it. Flashes of lightning can occasionally be seen in the distance.

A chain of snow-covered mountains can be seen far off in the distance. Dark clouds cover the sky, and a gusty wind blows. The musty stairs appear to go on forever, perhaps a trick of the magic aura seeming to radiate from the very tower itself.

A door in the side of the tower breaks the monotony of climbing the endless stairway, inviting people to come inside, away from the harsh elemental forces that surround the tower.  The magical pulses of energy seem stronger in this area, as if the tower itself wants people to notice the doorway.

The platform throughout the palace arrowheads here as it leads elsewhere, exiting this enormous and stifling chamber.  Two bronze pillars conspicuously stand on either side of the platform, marking the chamber's far exit. Just across a fiery channel of magma, a lone gargoyle crouches, guardedly surveying in the exit's general direction.

The magma within the lake rises and falls lazily against the pathway and separates it adequately from two small outlying islands.  Staring back at the pathway from the islands are a pair of statues, one of a woman and the other a gargoyle.  A doorway with amazingly gaudy decor leads beyond the pathway and out of the magma-filled chamber.

From the northern wall, this platform projects as a minor outcropping above a massive lake of magma.  All along the wall's upper exterior, lights blink rapidly between sets of metallic torches, but with the presence of the magma the light they produce together is but a trivial effort.  A tasteful burgundy rug with a golden box at its center has been set across the platform's black floor.  A circle of twinkling blue stars floats peacefully about, imbuing a sense of safety here.

Everything here is symmetrically placed, but with a pointed emphasis on the northern wall.  A pillar stands from floor to ceiling at each of the four vertices along the northern half of the room, each with a brightly burning flame at its top.  Metallic golden lines reflecting the flame's light cross the floor in each cardinal direction forming a singular square at the center, and within the square exists a prominent ciel blue button.

Shocking in its enormity, the elevator seems easily capable of moving large numbers or large objects.  Four hexagonal plates of glass have been built into the elevator's surface allowing a clear view of the equally enormous shaft the elevator is descending through.
