The light on the control mechanism is no longer twinkling at this point.

Much the opposite of the first descended platform, is the statue of a woman greeting the arriving stairway.  Good omen though this may appear, the statue of a demon quickly casts doubt with its watchful pose near the next and final descending stairway.  Along both stairways and platform the golden lines gleam brightly continuing to lead brave adventurers onward, towards a fate unknown.

The eastern pathway is pincered by annoyances on both sides of its narrow body; white-hot magma from the lake rises and falls against its edge, emitting foul vapors and heat, while the walls on its inside reflect back a sickly green color applied over insectine carvings.  Statues of a woman and a gargoyle have been placed in watchful positions upon two small islands within the lake.  Just ahead the pathway ends at a dark doorway, its frame so ornate that it approaches gaudy.

Simply gigantic in size, this platform stretches almost the full length of the equally large room housing it.  A stationary bridge-like path attached to the platform's side leads east.  Two square pillars have been situated parallel to each other, both with partially exposed lighting at their bases showing off the deeply carved golden grooves that decorate them.  Along the very edges of the room's walls runs a narrow ledge.

An elegant blue marble pathway outlined in emerald green runs from the doorway directly north where it ends below a pulsing red lever.  On either side of the pathway, intricately etched lines form step-like patterns whose inlay reflects a bright gold. Dividing the room is a channel of hot magma that flows in from the northwest and works its way downward toward the southeast.

Various paths convene here, forming one of the larger platforms existing throughout the palace.  Much like a completed puzzle, chunks of black in awkward and unidentifiable shapes squeeze together flushly, creating randomly set golden lines and intersections across the platform's girth.  Looking upon the scene from a small island isolated by magma, is the figure of a kneeling woman holding something curious before her chest.

Grandiose in its enormity, the elevator seems easily capable of moving large numbers or large objects.  Four hexagonal plates of glass have been built into the elevator's surface allowing a clear view of the equally enormous shaft the elevator ascends through.  Serving as some form of control mechanism is a large steel ball, a blue light twinkling rapidly from its center.

White-hot magma surrounds this small platform, rising and falling steadily as if alive.  The air is incredibly humid and blisteringly hot, yet the platform's floor remains cool, somehow completely unaffected.  Metallic golden etchings cross the floor, gleaming brightly, forming simplistic panels and shapes.  A tall stone post stands alone near the platform's edge.

Four pillars with torches at their tops extend from each corner of the northern wall.  Their flames clearly illuminating the wall's dull metallic surface and the room's main attraction.  Surrounding a steel lever sticking forth from the wall's center are two large green beetles; a mantle high above the lever heralds a bright blinking orange light, only further calling attention to that spot.

A massive lake of fiery magma is the dominating substance within the room.  Pathways run along the outside of the magma, giving just enough room for one person to walk safely.  Near each pathway is a small island, each quite isolated within the magma and impossible to reach.  The statue of a kneeling woman is present upon the limited surface of each island.  A small square platform protrudes perpendicular to the pathways directly over the magma; at its center is a large blue button.

rooms.name: Save Point Below The Many Stairs

userData.LongDescription: Steel walls in odd and even angles form this room's boundaries, the odd exception due to the rising stairway on the eastern end of the room.  Various exposed panels, circuits, and lights are embedded throughout the walls creating an intensely mechanical feel to the room.  None of these machines appear to be functioning however, leaving a ring of floating stars as the only purposeful presence.

On either side of the pathway the magma rises up like an indomitable wall of death, held in place and completely separate from the path by some incredible unseen force.  Stone gargoyles stare down upon the pathway from stone pedestals within the lake, their maws hung open hungrily as if waiting for the magma to make a quick meal out of any who should pass.

The lower half of this platform is dominated by a dark blue marbled rectangle, its center cut away revealing a small square of the familiar metallic black floor.  Another smaller square of the blue marble is nestled between two large golden pillars; at the square's center a diamond of malachite glows beckoningly.  An ornate chest rests abandoned behind one of the pillars, dust visibly flittering about its open mouth.

Grandiose in its enormity, the elevator seems easily capable of moving large numbers or large objects.  Four hexagonal plates of glass have been built into the elevator's surface allowing a clear view of the equally enormous shaft the elevator descends through.  Serving as some form of control mechanism is a large steel ball, a blue light twinkling rapidly from its center.

The walls are lined with various computer panels reminiscent of advanced scientific laboratories, clashing starkly with the antiquated ground.  The rather bland black floor is decorated with ornate etchings of rich amber.  In the center of the room is a cross that has taken a shape inspired by a complex circuitry of inextricable golden-brown wires.  Extending from each end of the cross, is a segmented walkway, of which its square tiles are outlined by the same amber.

Pulsating red lights run throughout the steel machine-like walls.  The eyes of two demonic statues pulse in disturbing sync and color with the lights.  Between the watching statues, a shaft of sickly greenish-purple light slowly brightens and fades at its own tempo; the shaft allows a quick departure from this foreboding mechanical nightmare.

A warning of immediate notice lies in the larger than normal demon statue positioned in a corner of the platform; the obvious reason rests with the dangerously erratic red halo circling its face. With the innumerable number of stairs and the surrounding darkness, it has become hard to gauge just how far descended this platform is.  Yet more stairs appear at the southern end of the platform, descending even further into the depths.

This kidney-shaped platform acts only as a connecting point between the two larger platforms neighboring it.  Its metallic surface is pitch black and fails to even slightly reflect the bright emanations from the magma surrounding it.  Only the angled edges running the perimeter and a simple square design etched in its center seem to be affected, gleaming brightly as if they were always intended to do so.

A channel several feet wide runs along the entire border of this immense platform.  The only source of light and heat here comes from the white-hot magma that fills the channel nearly to its brim.  Golden lining along grooves in the platform's surface gleam perfectly in the magma's presence, as does the dull sickly-green of the room's walls; a harsh but harmonic co-existence.

A long, oblique fissure cuts across the sprawling black surface of this platform.  As the fissure comes into contact with an edge, it splits and begins running along the outer sides of the platform, completely encircling it.  Within the fissure is a gold inlay that gleams brightly and then dims with each rise and fall of the surrounding magma.  However, it is the magma's ubiquitous heat and haze swirling through the air that truly assaults the senses.

Only a short ledge exists here for walkable space, its surface covered in a dark blue marble.  An enormous angular shaft of incredible depth drops down just beyond the edge of the ledge.  Cold machine-like linearity describes the walls of the shaft; its structure that of steel parts and blinking lights throughout.  Overhanging the only survivable exit, a dark doorway, is a large and menacing steel skull.

The black snaking paths that converge upon this dark metallic platform mirror in construction all the walkable parts of the palace; yet like the rest, this place holds its own unique flow of shapes and design.  Twin pillars stand across from each other on either side of the platform, their heads glowing in magenta unison; two more similar but squat pillars jut forth from a pool of magma nearby.  These four symmetrical pillars provide an architectural harmony to the otherwise abstract appearance of the various walkways.

Pervasive darkness envelopes the platform on all sides.  Fortunately, throughout the comparatively black floor, glowing golden lines provide a unique and powerful source of navigational light.  At the platform's center the lines form a massive and very complex pattern.  Bordering the complex pattern are two small squares, each with a set of four pulsating magenta lights.

Large blinking lights and numerous metallic torches thoroughly illuminate the room and assault the senses in unison.  The mass of light clearly displays a large pattern covering the floor; its design is maddeningly labyrinthine, this effect only intensified by the reflecting light on its golden lines.  Quite out of place in this fantastic setting is a single chest, it sits alone in a corner of the room.

A crude tree-like design decorates the black floor; its inlay of gold shines brightly, clearly revealing every detail no matter how small.  Torches line the room at each of its corners, generously giving clarity to not only the tree, but to the walls' various carvings and colors.  Near the tree's trunk sits a small object, perhaps a present?

The large platform seems to fit much like a puzzle piece within the confines of the room.  Reaching the actual walls of the room would seem to be near impossible as a channel of magma buffers the platform on all of its edges.  Though there is a large amount of heat in the air, the platform itself seems completely unaffected by the thermal reactions produced by the magma, its surface maintaining a strangely cool temperature.

Gone from the walls are the dull metallic green and insectine shapes, replaced by steel plates of different sizes, all fitting together neatly but in no particular order.  Four ten-foot high pillars stand along the southern end of the platform, at their top magenta lights slowly pulse in unison.  The platform itself is rectangular in general shape, its sides however, are cut in strange angles that create various symmetrical indentations and protrusions.

Pillars are set evenly across all the walls of this octagonal room.  Small cavities at the tops of each pillar house tirelessly dancing flames that perfectly reveal all aspects of the environment they overlook.  A simple burgundy carpet covers the middle of the room, while short stretches of dark blue marble extend from its sides to the room's exits.  An ornate treasure chest sits open in the northeast corner.

Waves of heat blast across this pathway, the one product of the magma that seems able to pass through the invisible force holding it aside.  Just ahead, a short set of gold-plated steps provide a welcome escape from the magma bordered trench.  Stranded on islands within the magma are the figures of two women, both kneeling forward, a magenta orb within their cupped hands outstretched towards the steps.

Heat washes over the room in incredibly oppressive waves.  From within two diamond-shaped holes, blindingly bright magma rises and falls, the source of the incredible swelter.  The dark metallic floor seems completely unaffected by the magma flowing beneath it, indicating it must be crafted of some amazing materials.  With the presence of the magma, one could safely assume that the palace is below even the ocean's floor.  A strangely conspicuous circle of stars floats just above the floor, beckoning a passing adventurer toward it.

The first set of stairs terminates at a large platform, marking the initial sub-level within the Ocean Palace.  Near the ascending stairway sits the statue of a kneeling demon; not the most pleasant of greeters.  Opposite the demon and on the other side of the platform is another statue, this one of a woman.  Her gaze is directed towards the next stairway, this one heading downward.

Flames jump wildly in unison from four small chambers high upon the walls, illuminating just how barren this large room is.  Three peculiar shapes resting on the center of the northern wall would probably be missed by most if not for the overall plainness of the room.  From the wall's base a golden line appears, eventually becoming the outline for a square button at the room's central point.

Seemingly random lines zigzag across this large platform, terminating at various points along its edges.  Canals full of a white-hot magma ebb and flow against the platform's sides, lending a bright golden glow to the lines throughout its otherwise opaque black surface.  A flame against the eastern wall illuminates the outline of a large open archway.

As the platform comes to an end, it does so with a set of elegant rugs; one is rectangular and set long ways, the other overlays it as a long traditional cross, both are burgundy with double golden stitching around their borders.  A narrow path leads northward toward a dark open doorway; on either side of the door frightening bronze demons crouch, a bright magenta flashing from within their eye sockets.

Focus here falls on three squares, the predominant characters in the floor's design.  Thick lines of gold connect and lead to the squares in step-like patterns and diagonals originating from the room's walls.  Torches mounted throughout truly bring to life the floor's golden pattern; at the same time however, they reveal the sickly metallic green and insectine carvings that compose the room's walls.

Octagonal and square shaped platforms interconnect here to form a bridge between the two larger platforms.  At the center of the bridge a ciel blue button protrudes importantly from within the floor.  Four identical statues of a kneeling woman have been situated around the bridge, each cupping a small magenta orb within its hands.

A dancing fire warms and lights the room, casting shadows along the walls from within its fire pit. Over the fire, some fruits hang, drying in the warmth of the fire. To the right of the fire some rough furs used for bedding are strewn out over the corner. A small pot near the door holds some grain to be used for the next meal.

A pair of antlers looms over the hut from the far wall, lit from below by a warm fire. A hanging set of fruit dries in a corner of the room, giving the room a sour but fruity smell. Beneath the fruit, a pair of pots hold some grain and some already-dried fruits. The floor of the hut has a few leaves on it from previous dryings.

The snow has completely taken over the northeastern portion of the island. It is impossible to move any further against the howling white wind. The temperature, already low on the rest of the island, is unbearably cold in this area. The imprints in the snow made by the few who visit out here are obliterated before one can even turn around to look at them.

A few meager huts lie to the west, east, and north. The village commons are to the northwest, sheltered from snowfall by both a mountain and a small forest. This area is nothing more then a pathway between all the important parts of the village, with no evidence of any building beginning here soon.

The village commons run up to the edge of the mountain itself, where a small chair has been thoughtfully placed. A tree's gnarled branches also run over the chair's position on the ground. The cliffs on each side of the small field start to round off before become unassailable walls of stone, slanting away from the mountain in a manner which makes them impossible to climb. Snow is almost completely absent from this area, although the ground is still frozen solid.

The frozen landscape extends only a short distance further to the west, where the cliffs extend over the frozen sea. Prints in the snow are quickly obscured by the heavy flakes falling to the ground, a permanent fixture of this blasted world. A short cape extends to the north of the island, and past that, more frigid water. A mountain obscures the vision of the meager village to the south and east, as well as shielding the village from the snowfalls.

Just before the northern cape, a magnificent view can already be seen; on either side of the promontory, the small bits of ice out in the sea give an illusion that the entire ocean glitters with silver or diamonds, and, for some reason, the howling wind ceases near this point, becoming calmer and more peaceful. A bit of green is even visible as the ground starts to slope gently upward, hinting at a refuge from the harshness; but at this point, there are only the white plains behind, and the green cliff ahead.

Just outside of the village inn, the land has been completely cleared of snow, while the dirt is still packed as hard as cobblestones. The hut nearby is set up as a resting spot for those on the way to the village commons; the fire inside appears to be a welcome respite from the harsh reality of the ice age. The village grounds to the north are directly beneath the towering spire of rock. There is not even the slightest breeze here in front of the inn, which looks like it might be destroyed by a medium-sized storm.

A fire crackles off to the side of the entrance to the hut, providing the hut with some light but more importantly heat. The ground illuminated by the light consists of dry packed dirt with a few still melting flakes of snow blown in from outside. Sitting beside the fire across from the entrance is a potted flower. Off to the other side of the fire are two more pots, as well as a few bits of metal glinting in the light.

Free of the blanket of snow which covers the rest of the island, the north cape seems like it could be a good place to escape from some of the hardships of the village. Grass covers the ground instead of snow, even if the small blades are still coated in ice from the cold and the flowers are dead of frost. To the north, the setting sun reflects back off the small pieces of ice floating in the water, causing them to sparkle and give the illusion of an ocean of precious metal. The view is absolutely spectacular.

This area is just outside the area shielded by the peak to the east, where the snowstorm divides the island into the inhabited region and the wilderness. Small hills of snow keep people from seeing the water to the north, as most people who wish for a view head west, towards the northern cape, or to the east. The result is a depression in the snow to the frozen ground where people frequently walk; however, it disappears rather quickly, as most people who leave the village decide to return before reaching their destination.

This hut is the easternmost in the village; any further to the east would be too far away from the mountain which protects the village from the wind. Thus, only a few dozen yards from the huts, the ground is piled ten to twenty feet higher with snow, and the temperature drops below what can sustain human habitation. The hut is used as a common sleeping ground for the entire population of the village; an unpleasant smell wafts from it, unsurprisingly.

This small gathering place just southward of the highest mountain is comparatively warm, as the snow is old and mostly melted. Most of the trees in this pitiful forest are long since dead of the cold, their withered branches reaching overhead. Stone occasionally shows through the snow, to give people dry land to rest on after standing for too long. The village commons extend a little further to the north, butting right up to the mountain itself.

The snowfall in the village is light; the mountain above shields the village from the vicious northwestern storms, the ones that result in the most snowfall.  There is nevertheless more than enough snow and ice to make habitation difficult.  A weak-looking hut has been established in spite of the bitter frost.

Seeing seagulls dive from the sky and straight into the water for a small snack, or diving smack down to a hidden rock below the surface is very interesting. North is covered in a dark forest and not even a peep of a bird or a squirrel can be heard, it's totally desolate. A gloomy fortress or a castle can be seen above the forest, and it doesn't look like a nice place at all. The Giant's Claw is located southeast.

The waves are hitting the shoreline with its tranquil and peaceful effect. Nothing could ruin this nice effect upon people; except those damn seagulls again, crapping on everyone near the shore... North is covered in a dark forest and not even a peep of a bird or a squirrel can be heard. A spooky fortress or a castle can be seen above the forest, and it doesn't look like a very nice place to visit. The notorious Giant's Claw is southeast. A green forest has risen in the north.

The deep blue ocean with foamy waves encircles the island. The normal sights of a shore are seagulls, and boy are there a lot of those around here.  The waves are gently hitting the shoreline with its tranquil and peaceful effect. Northeast is covered in a dark forest and not even a peep of a bird or a squirrel can be heard, it's totally desolate. The gloomy fort can be seen above the forest. Also, the dreaded Black Omen can be seen. The notorious Giant's Claw is somewhere southeast.

The deep blue ocean with foamy waves encircle the island. The normal sights of a shore are seagulls, and boy are there a lot of those around here. On the other hand, north is covered in a dark forest and not even a peep of a bird or a squirrel can be heard, it's totally desolate. A gloomy fortress or a castle can be seen above the forest, and it doesn't look like a nice place to visit. The notorious Giant's Claw is southeast.

In the midst of forests, the weary wanderer feels at peace and not even the dark forest can disrupt this feeling of tranquility.  Unlike the darker version of nature's lungs, this one doesn't look like from someone who smokes.  A lone mountain looming over the isle can be seen, and it is quite astonishing. Some kind of blueish light is shining from the northeastern parts of the forest.

Surrounded by forests, the weary wanderer feels at peace and not even the dark forest can distrupt this feeling of tranquility.  Birds are flying around and squirrels are scampering from tree to tree. A lone mountain looms over the isle, and with its snow covered top, it's quite astonishing. Also, some kind of blueish light is eerily shining from the northeastern parts of the forest.

The deep blue ocean with foamy waves surrounds the island. Nothing could ruin this positive effect upon people, except those seagulls again, crapping on everyone near the shore... Northeast is covered in a dark forest and nothing can be heard. A gloomy fortress or a castle can be seen above the forest. The dreaded Black Omen can be seen hovering above an isle to the west.

The west is covered in a dark forest and not even a peep of a bird can be heard nor a squirrel seen, it's totally desolate. A gloomy fortress or a castle looms above the forest. Unlike the darker version of nature's lungs, this one doesn't look like from someone who smokes. Birds are flying around, chirping happily to the weary adventurer. Some annoyingly cute squirrels are scampering along the path, occasionally stopping to take a peek at the new sight in town. From the midst of the green trees, an ocean can be seen. Also, some kind of blueish light is shining from the northern parts of the forest.

The deep blue ocean with foamy waves encircles the island. The normal sights of a shore are seagulls, and boy, are there a lot of those around here. Seeing them dive from high above sea level and straight into the water for a small snack or diving smack down to a hidden rock below the surface, very interesting. Northeast is covered in a dark forest and not even a peep of a bird or a squirrel can be heard, it's totally desolate. A gloomy fortress or a castle can be seen above the forest and it doesn't look like a nice place to visit. Also, the dreaded Black Omen can be seen. It is hovering above an isle to the west. The notorious Giant's Claw is southeast. The Epoch has landed here.

Surrounded by greenish trees, the weary wanderer feels at peace. A gloomy fort-like structure can be seen above the trees. Birds are flying around, chirping happily to the weary adventurer. Some more annoyingly cute squirrels are scampering along the path. The waves are gently hitting the shoreline with its tranquil and peaceful effect. To the north above the trees, you can see a snowy mountain top and a glimpse of a blue ocean on the horizon.

Foamy waves of the blue sea encircle the island. The gently hitting waves caress the shoreline with its tranquil effect. A dark forest looms in the northeast, it's totally desolate. A fort like structure stands in the midst of the forest. Also, the feared Black Omen can be seen, hovering gloomily on an isle to the west. The Giant's Claw is located southeast.

Another one of these dark corridors. This place is filled with them. Must be a normal thing in dark fort-like places. There is a little flicker of a candle to the northeast and in the west dwells yet another murky passageway. Also, there is a balcony with golden railings just above eye level. A winch can be seen on the balcony. The floors are quite dusty; footprints are visible on the floor.

A really narrow, dark passageway. There are no light-providing lanterns. In both ends of it, a dim light of hope shines its blessing of... well, light. The northern end has something shiny and curved hanging from the roof, which could be a blade of some sort. Before that, however, candles cast shadows from another direction. The floors are quite dusty; footprints are visible on the floor, venturing deeper into the Fortress.

A small dark room with a very deadly looking blade hanging at the end of chain, which is connected to a weird mechanism. The blade has been elevated back up after it fell. There is a balcony on the east side of the room. Glimpses of a winch can be seen on the balcony. That must be the winch that operates the blade!

The room has weird holes in every corner and a treadmill on both sides of the room. It is a bit narrower than the rooms before, but still not a friendly looking place. Dropping into the northern holes are metallic chains of some sort; it might be best to leave them alone. Above an eerie passageway is a balcony with a beautifully decorated golden railing. The floors are quite dusty; footprints are visible on the floor, venturing deeper into the Fortress.

A dark and empty room. There is nothing worth noticing, excluding the two lanterns that are providing the dim light for the whole room. The lanterns are making the walls dance with shadows. The play of light and shadow offers a display of beauty unique to the effect of lanterns in dark, empty rooms. The floors are quite dusty; footprints are visible on the floor, venturing deeper into the Fortress.

This room is pretty dark and empty. Nothing really worth noticing, except those two lanterns that are providing the dim light for the whole room. The light from the lanterns is making the walls dance with shadows. The playful shadows on the walls and floors are displaying a magnificent view, unique only to dark rooms with lanterns. Footprints are visible on the dusty floor, showing a trail deeper into the fort.

This is room looks bigger than the rest. Not even the two lanterns can light this one up. The lanterns are trying to make the walls dance with shadows, but due to the size of this room, not quite accomplishing it. There are two open chests in the far right corner of the room. The floors are quite dusty; footprints are visible on the floor.

Yet another one of these dark and empty rooms. The only difference is that this room is a dead end. The two lanterns in the far wall are lighting up the room a little. With the little light the lanterns are providing, some shadows are doing the dance thing all around the room again. The trail of footprints in the dust ends here.

The shadows on the floor and wall are coming from the east. There might be a candle or some other means of lighting in that direction. The room due north looks like a dead end, though it has something shiny and curved hanging from the roof; which could be a blade of some sort. A dim light is shining from the south. The floors are quite dusty; footprints are visible on the floor.

A quite small room with lanterns on each side of dark passageway leading upwards. There is no end to these dark passageways, is there? Bet there is even a dark and empty room at the end of that passage. There is a slightly visible crack in the southern wall. To the west is the balcony with the winch on it. The floors are quite dusty; footprints are visible on the floor.

This is the front hall of the Great Ozzie's fort. There are two identical, creepy-looking statues on each side of a red-carpeted staircase that leads to higher grounds. In the far north wall of the room are lanterns, giving the only light to this unholy dark place, shining the deepest shadows away. There is a sign near the entranceway.

The path here coils around much like a chopped up snake with the gliding posts covering the gaps in the path of lit platforms. A trademark of the fortress, everything is metallic and showered in light, even the floors, walls and ceiling. The path leads south and north from here.

This odd platform is shaped like a large triangle, mostly black, with green on its borders. The platform itself doesn't seem to be made out of metal, but a strange plastic, yet another oddity the fortress seems to hold. The path leads to the southwest and southeast from this point.

This room just seems to glow with energy, with bluish lines of light streaming in the walls. There are lights everywhere; the room is flaring with energy. The floor is made out of an odd greenish metal, placed like plates on a suit of scale mail, with the same lines of light going across it. The main path takes a turn to the west here, eventually looping quite a bit in a helix pattern before ultimately keeping the main track to the north.

A three-point intersection in the confusing maze of solid stone walls, floors and ceilings. There are three paths to take. To the north is a short path leading to a sharp corner with a turn to the west, and to the south is an apparent dead end. To the east is what seems to be another intersection...

This is the western end of the catwalk. A set of twin doors is to the north, fairly simple in detail. The walls around here seem to shimmer bright with energy, almost with an odd colour pattern to it. A large arrow on the ground points dead on to the doors, almost an all-too-obvious sign that something is of great importance behind it.

Though the corridor is nearing its end, the spectacular view of the ground below is still visible. The bluish floors and walls reflect the glow of hundreds of tiny colored lights. Highs winds threaten to hurl an unwary traveler from the safety of the pathway.

This is a truly odd room, if it could be called a 'room'. There's no ground here, only the vast and eternally black void. Two spheres of light float around, one at this point, and the other to the north. Images of stars, suns and other planetary objects fill the room, creating a near simulation of outer space, though breathable air seems to be present.

rooms.name: The Path Through the Fortress of Mana.

userData.LongDescription: The passage through the Fortress twists and turns. Winds careen about the Fortress, creating a high-pitched whistle. Lights set in the floors and walls here give off a dim radiance. The structure consist of the same bluish metal as before.

The path stretches further along the outer edge of the Fortress. The floors and walls here consist of the same bluish metal as before. Winds howl and whistle through the pipes that have a tenuous hold on the Fortress wall. A brief glance over the edge reveals the pipes, and the constantly changing view of the ground far below.

This is the northern end of the symmetrical room. To the north is a path leading to yet another symmetrical room, and to the south is an array of odd paths leading eventually to a small speck that looks like a double set of doors. The room glows with light from the lines that run along the floors here.

This room is certainly shaped in an odd way. Two rows of platforms make the length of the room, with a sole connecting piece in the left side, and two bridges on the northern and southern sides lead elsewhere in the Fortress. The walls and floors glow slightly, because of the lights emanating from it. The power of Mana is very vibrant in the Fortress.

A large circular room, brighter than most others in the fortress.  The lines of light on the walls and platforms seem to run in an organized manner, leading into a large circle in the middle of the platform. From within the circle arises a veil of light, reaching up to the ceiling.

This room is circular, with no floor except for the large purple platform in the middle, oddly floating. A green translucent glass bridge fills the gap between the entrance and the actual platform. Large glowing stones are floating around, seeming to channel power into the portal in the middle.

The platforms take on a wider approach here, with a nearly squarish appearance. A small path leads to the southwest, looping up to the eventual north, into the next room in the fort. The metal walls and floor still glow bright with energy here, giving the room a bluish tint.

This is the western end of the helix-shaped looping room. The doorway is just to the southeast, within close reach. The western wall here has identically shaped thin lines that throw energy beams back and forth over it, creating an odd but amusing scene. To the northeast is the path leading closer to the entrance and exit of the fortress.

This is another three-point intersection in the maze, with three different paths: north, west and south. To the south is another dead end, and to the north is a turn in the path, even should it make no sense at all. To the west is another intersection. The presence of stone is practically everywhere around.

This is another intricate doorway, as with all the others in the fortress. This one is made out of many carvings of turtle shells, with two turtle heads sticking out at the top, connecting to a large green orb that glows with energy. Past the doorway is a large circular platform, almost equal in intricacy.

This is a large, open room with massive platforms attached to each other. The room is very vast; it could be used for a large-scale meeting or celebration. A doorway is on the northern end, and a small field of crystals to the east. The floor and walls glows brightly with a shining essence.

This is another decision point in the fort, providing access to many of its twisted and odd halls. To the south is a large hallway leading to an unknown place. The set of gliding posts provides a passage north to another intersection. The path west leads to yet another intersection, to make things unneccessarily complex.

This is the eastern side of a very odd room. A large hole lies in the middle, like the result of a large explosion, though strangely the platforms seem to indicate that it is more of a purposeful hole than an accident. To the northwest is a doorway leading further north somewhere.

This is a long catwalk that stretches out to the far west, ending at a curve leading into a large set of doors. To the north is a set of gliding posts and a vile purple gate that seems to be radiating dark energy. The metal on the platform seems to be a bit out of the ordinary, glowing with a fiery, reddish light. Arrows are placed on them, pointing to the west.

This gate is truly seraphic, shaped like a high majestic arc with the large wings of an angel jutting out of it. The entire gate is made out of a soft white material, akin to pearl. Two small angel-like statues are placed on the top, holding a milky white orb that shimmers with holy powers.

This is the northernmost part of the large, elegant crescent-shaped hallway. The flooring is almost designed to recognize the crescent shape, with patterns that decorate it much like a boomerang or a throwable weapon. The path leads into two directions from this high point, to the southeast or to the southwest.

This platform is a perfect circle, connecting two paths in the fortress together. Glowing walls and little orbs on the floor seem to be the main attraction of this room. To the east is a bridge leading to a mirroring circle platform. South leads to a set of doors.

This is a small platform connecting the entrances to three hallways together. To the north is a short hall that leads to a large room, while the southern path branches off into two, leading southwest to a path filled with light, and southeast to a rather dark path.

The path breaks into three here; west, east and south. TO the west is a short path leading up to a gap and a set of gliding posts. To the east is a path that seems to lead to a dead-end. To the south is a long array of strange rooms leading eventually to a set of double doors; the exit and the entrance to the fort.

The catwalk branches off in an L-shaped twist, leading northwest past the doorway and then east. To the northwest is what seems to be a crescent-shaped hallway, and to the east is a long platform leading to a misty gate at the end. The platform glows as light seems to course through it.

The path continues along the outer edge of the Fortress. The floors and walls here consist of machinery, complete with little blinking lights. The deep blue colored metal shines dully in the dim light. Far below this pathway, the constantly changing ground can be seen.

This is the northwestern corner of a humongous platform, set on top the entire Mana Fortress, possibly on its rooftop. A marvellous view of the fortress sectors below can be seen, with domes and buildings of all kinds glowing light. To the east is a crude path leading to another portal. Nearby is another portal leading into the fortress.

A pair of gliding posts are adjusted to the edges of the platform here, for ease of gliding across the gap. To the direct south is a set of rooms, each with possibly its own obstacles and such to help defend the fort from possible intruders. The light glimmers around the room, emanating from the floors and walls.

This large gate is pearly white, with two sets of thin  faerie-like wings embedded onto it. The pillars glimmer like glitter, sparkling with a light energy. On the top is a beautiful carving of two faeries holding a large, white orb that glows with radiance. To the north is a long path with an intersection a fair distance away.

There are three separate ways to take from this point, in the form of doorways to the west and east as well as a teleporter active in the middle of the floor. The walls here are made out of metal, cut into large pieces between each supporting pillar. On each wall slab is a unique runic image, whether the form of an ancient relic of power or just doodles a bored ancient being might've carved in his idle time.

This is the northern end of the Gate of Ice, a truly marvellous piece of ice sculpture, made to last eternally under the influence of Mana. It resembles a large swan, all crafted in ice. It gives off frosty puffs of air, adding to its beauty. A large frozen orb rests on the top of the structure, part of its preservation equipment. To the east is a set of gliding posts before a large room, and to the southeast past the gate is a long coiling path.

This gate seems to sparkle bright with electricity, static flowing through it. It's made out of a dark metal, almost charred with the lightning sparking about. This large gate is shaped like a six-sided, hexagonal thunder drum. A large purple orb sparkles with energy on the top.

This long path takes a bit of a zig-zag pattern to it, with a few gaps along the way to complicate matters. Green crystals line the borders of the platforms, creating a glowing path of green light through the darkness that wraps the fortress. The path leads up to the northwest and to the south.

A long corridor, dimly lit by small colored lights set in the floors and walls, continues through the Fortress. The surrounding structure is composed of a strange metallic material. The view of the constantly changing ground below is interrupted only by the occasional cloud drifting under the Fortress.

This is the northern end of the looping path. A large piece of the wall here seems to have been torn out, and a splendid view of the fortress section below can be seen. Other than that, the always present lines of light still course through the veins of the floors and walls. The path leads to the southwest and southeast from here, with the doorway visible to the direct south.
This small corridor itself is fairly ordinary, providing

This is the northwestern corner of the array of thin adjoined platforms. From this point, three paths are available, like a large arrow pointing northwest; east, southeast and south. Light seems to emanate from within the platforms and walls, glowing with a bluish tint. To the south is a complicated twist of platforms.

This is the eastern corner of the rooftop. The sight is not as splendid as it was from the other side of the roof, being mostly enclosed with walls and railings. A large slab is placed on the wall, glowing slightly with runic energy. A set of energy stairs leads high up to a floating platform above.

This room looks like an utter disaster. Large holes dot the floor like pockmarks, for whatever reason. Some platforms are still surviving, hanging through like straws over the endless, bottomless pit. The platforms are a sharp contrast to the jet-black pit, glowing bright, shimmering with energy. To the south is a doorway leading into the room beyond.

The path takes on a bit of an odd shape here, leading both north and northeast. The two separate paths nearly merge with each other, creating lots of room to walk around on. To the direct north is another room that looks particularly odd. To the south is another odd room, and the set of double doors that serve as both the entrance and the exit to the fort.

This is another impressive doorway in the Mana Fortress. This one is set with yellowish metal, with two tigers coiling around it. A red orb rests on the top of the arch, glowing bright with energy. The intricacy and detail of the doorway is just marvelous. A path of platforms lead to the south, ending at a double set of gliding posts.

This is a large, red-colored gate. The metal seems to glow with a fiery passion, emanating a temper-like blaze. The tails of the phoenix bird seem to be carefully placed upon it, though only carvings. Metal wings spread out far from the doorway, to demonstrate the wings of the phoenix. The head is above the doorway, holding a large orange-colored orb in its mouth. To the south is a large field of crystals.

The hall continues along the outer edge of the Fortress. The floors and walls here consist of the same bluish metal as before. A brief glance over the edge reveals some pipes and the inconstant ground far below.

rooms.name: Entrance to the Fortress of Mana.

userData.LongDescription: The most notable aspect of the Fortress is the lack of any natural material. The floors and walls are made of some bluish metal, unidentifiable in origin. The dizzying height combined with the winds from this high up make the journey through this section of the Fortress treacherous. The scenery far below is constantly changing as the Fortress repeatedly transports itself.

This is a reverse L-shaped corner in the catwalk leading north and west. To the north is what seems to be a nearly concealed gate, due to heavy mist enveloping it. To the west, the catwalk stretches far, further into the long room. Darkness looms around, both due to general lack of lighting and the bottomless pits that lie around below the platform.

This is a large, odd room. A small platform rests on the southern wall, with a small circle of glowing light on it. To the wide, open north is void. There is void all over, here and there. Though the void looks unsafe to walk upon, it has a particularly inviting feel to it... Another platform is to the extreme north.

The maze takes a sharp turn on this corner, leading two ways: south and east. To the east is yet another turn, showing no hint as to where it leads. The walls, floors and ceiling are all made out of stone in this puzzling maze. To the south is a long path leading to the entrance and southwestern exit of the maze, marked by a large gate.

The hall continues along the outer edge of the Fortress. The floors and walls here are machinery, consisting of the same bluish metal as before. A brief glance over the edge reveals the pipes, and the inconstant ground far below.

This intersection splits into three directions: north, east and south. To the north is a corner leading into a hallway. Another hallway lies to the south, and to the east is yet another path stopping at yet another intersection with gliding posts.

This room is very odd indeed, with platforms so irregularly shaped that travelling it isn't a simple matter anymore. From this point, rough paths to the west and south can be seen, along the little strips of metal that compose this gigantic but odd-shaped platform. The walls seem to be hooked, line-wise, to the flooring, helping it glow terribly bright like a christmas tree.

There seems to be a large black hole tugging in the background, with swirls of debris flowing around, though all is just an image and not real. Stars and bits of light are scattered everywhere else, creating a fairly impressive display of artwork. To the north and south are small spheres of light that give off just about the only source of real light in this room.

The maze breaks into two paths at this point, south and east. To the south is a three-point intersection of stone, and to the east is a long path leading to a bright light, presumably an exit of sorts. Stone wraps basically everything in this god-forsaken maze, curse the designers.

This is a rather narrow corridor, surprisingly dark with the lack of lighting, despite the rooms around glowing with light. The walls and floor here are metal, though specific details about them are not known for sure. To the north is a room shaped in perfect halves, and to the south is a room filled with a mess of platforms.

This circular room is fairly ordinary, with the usual compliment of metal platforms and glowing walls. However, a long rope bridge is set to the west, as a device to help cross the long gap that separates the two sides of the room. To the south is a short staircase beyond a doorway that leads to a large field of crystals.

This is a large, round platform. Runic patterns are engraved all across it, glowing with energy. Large pedestals containing huge stones of power, possibly Mana Stones themselves, are placed on the edges. The skies seem to be tossing around full of confusion. This place emits a radiant aura of evil.

This is a dead end. The path ends with a sharp cut in the row of green metal platforms. Only the endless pits around the platform and the way leading back to the west make up the options here. The walls and floors glow with bright energy, nearly filling the room with brilliance.

This is the focal point of the confusing maze. Everything seems to revolve around this point, with two main paths leading northwest and east, going in zig-zag like motions. Light glows all throughout the platforms, both as little creases among the metallic plating and as large, glowing guidance arrows.

The stone here is smooth and fine, without flaws in it. Three out of four of the cardinal directions are wrapped in a stone wall, causing a bit of a claustrophobic grip. Other than the everpresent stony influence, there doesn't seem to be much else other than the path leading north, to an intersection.

The path takes a two directions here; west and south. To the west is a long hallway with an ornately crafted gate in the middle. To the south is a lone platform between bottomless pits with an intersection in the middle of it. This corner is fairly empty by itself, only serving as a middle room to more interesting destinations.

This large gate seems to be emanating a venomous aura. The metal is designed in the form of of a snake's skin, with a coiling design up to the top, where two ferocious cobra heads seem to lunge at each other. A large, purple orb rests on the top, glowing with an almost dark energy. To the south is a set of gliding posts, and to the east is a rope bridge.

Where there is a beginning, there is an end. The start of a journey, however small, will eventually end. This gate marks the embodiment of such journeys, particularly the one taken through this fortress of pure evil. It resembles a gate of purity, with white pillars and a brightly shining white orb. To the north is the deepest section of the fortress.

This is the western end of a fairly long hallway that stretches out to the far east. The walls shimmer with energy, light coursing through them like blood in their veins. In the middle of the hallway is what seems to be a large, important-looking gate. To the south is a small room before an adjacent hallway.

This is a large-sized circular platform, with swirls of light going in thin lines all around in a helix-shaped pattern. In the middle is a large glowing pink orb, seeming to channel light all around the platform. To the west is what seems to be a similar platform after a short bridge, and to the south is an intricate gate of turtles.

This is the left side of the symmetrical room. Lines of light run rampant all around the floor, creating a dim bluish glow. Yellowish metal walls contrast sharply against the blue light. The green shine of the platforms creates a nearly sickening color combination that runs rampant all around the fortress.

This is a large, golden glowing gate that seems to shine bright with pure power. Its pillars don't seem to be made out of a solid, worldly material, but more pure energy. The wide arc comes to a closing at the top, with a floating yellow orb shining bright on top of it. To the southeast is a path leading further deeper into the maze-like trail. An intricate-looking platform lies to the north.

This is the southern tip of the western platform. To the northeast is a path leading into a small doorway, and to the east is a bridge encompassing the gap between the two large platforms. Arrows seem to be placed on the platforms, one pointing to the northeast, the other to the east. On the wall is a message, looking to be almost carved by a sharp object.

The ground here is composed of nothing but seemingly solid void, even though it should not make sense. Blackened walls of energy are on the perimeters, creating the boundaries of this magical room. To the north and south exist metal platforms with a circle of light upon them.

This is a dark path, with nothing much but the exits on the northwest and southwest giving a bit of light into it. Not much of the features on the walls and floors can be seen; it's too dark to see clearly. To the southwest is what seems to be the entrance to a gate, and to the northwest is a small platform.

rooms.name: A sharp turn in the corridor

userData.LongDescription: This is a small corridor, built more to give space between two large rooms of more value. Runic patterns are embedded onto the wall, this particular one resembling a large design-laden circle into it. The corridor takes a small bend to the south, before ultimately leading further east into the room beyond. Alternately, a path to the west is also available into the Gate of Ice.

This is the entry point to a large circular room, with a set of steps leading up to a glowing circle of light. It looks fairly important, and probably leads somewhere deeper into the fortress. To the north is a long hallway, connected by a walkway, ending at a large gate of stone.

The path winds through the artificial landscape of the Fortress of Mana. The machinery that the floors and walls are made of is the same bluish metal as before. A glance over the edge reveals the inconstant ground, hundreds of feet below.

There's nothing in this dead end, except the path to the north, to an intersection. Stone wraps practically everywhere here, in the ceiling, the floors and on the three walled sides, creating a bit of a closed atmosphere. The stone itself is smooth, without a single dent or flaw to it.

This lone platform leads to a large gate with two identical openings, leading northwest and northeast. The gates resemble identical halves of a face, one resembling an innocent, pure face with no trace of evil whatsoever, the other a demonic face with purely evil intent. The white and black surely contrasts, with the crest of the Gemini constellation upon the forehead, creating a rather... creepy image; that of a cold, expressionless mask. On the forehead, between the constellation is also a glass orb with two soul-like objects within them, one white, one black, swirling around.

This room would be completely floorless if it weren't for a plus-shaped platform of glowing metal replacing it. The walls wrap in a cylindrical manner around the platform, glowing bright with the patterns of light carved through it. To the west is a large mound of crystals, and to the south an intricate gate of light.

Large quartz-shaped crystals fill the floor here, making travel a major hassle. The room is a roughly circular shape, with a large doorway to the north, and a set of platforms beyond it. The crystal field extends to the east as well, with another doorway on its adjacent north.

This is the western end of the looping path. A set of gliding posts is to the east, the only means of going further north into the path. To the southeast is the south end of this long coiling road, leading somewhere else. A strange pattern glows on the wall, resembling much of a large helmet. Crystals line the borders of the path, glowing a shimmering green.

The path winds around the outer edge of the Fortress. Lights set in the floors and walls here give off a dim radiance. As in the rest of the Fortress, the structure here consists of a bluish metal. The winds howl around the Fortress, and a brief glance over the edge reveals the constantly changing ground far below.

This unique gate was truly designed along the corner of the room, with the path leading southeast. Small individual gates, each with a flat horizontal beam attached to two pillars, line the platformed path, creating an interesting series of gates. They each have little orbs of glowing light upon them. To the north is a rather plain road leading to the northwestern corner.

This side of the room looks very odd, with closed in corners that have shaped patterns of light on them. One looks like a large vertical eye, with vine-like lines coming out of it. The other looks like a large hexagon, with short lines on its sides. Other than the wall patterns, there's not much else here other than continuing the path, which comes in two directions: south and east.

This large gate marks one of the entrances to the maze of stone. It's large and crafted out of solid earth and rock piles, looking fairly crude and primitive. A large orb is half-buried on the top of the arc, glowing with a gray light. To the south is a metallic walkway that leads into a large hallway.

This is the easternmost end of the large platform, with the bridge close to the west. The wall is rather odd in looks here, with almost no light glowing on it except for the almost archaic text inscribed on it, like a large slab. Two paths exist to take here, one to the west past the bridge and the other to the southwest.

The Fortress of Mana is simply amazing, almost seeming to be alive. The floors are all a greenish metal, placed in a strange pattern that shapes a large skull on the ground as a walkway, as holes fill the room otherwise. On the edges are streams of shining light, and the power of technology just seems to pulse all throughout the fort.

This round platform was designed to resemble a snail, with lines of light swirling around it much like the features of the shell. In the middle is a circular hole, so small it can't obstruct much, probably more for decoration than anything. To the west is a set of gliding posts.

rooms.name: Before a set of gliding posts

userData.LongDescription: A set of gliding posts are nearby, placed to ease the task of leaping across space left by the missing platform. To the near south is a three-way intersection, and to the north another junction of triple paths. Glowing metal and green are the key themes of the Fortress of Mana, apparent by what the walls and floors show.

This room is long, wide and filled with crystals. Green crystals of different shapes and sizes fill the floor, making travel fairly difficult, especially for bare feet. The crystals glow with energy, as if each and every single one had an ounce of mana energy in it. The room extends far to the west. To the north is an intricate-looking doorway of phoenixes.

The large glowing platform takes two turns here, north and east. To the north is a dead-end in terms of walkable platforms, though a pink set of gliding posts may prove otherwise. To the east is the doorway leading to the entrance and exit to the fort. The room glows with sparkling energy, even the platforms are glimmering.

This is the connecting point between the metal walkway connecting the entrance to the maze and the hallway leading south. The walls glow bright, carved with lines of light through it. Little orbs are placed on the sides, seeming to channel into the lines themselves. It certainly is much different from the bleak stone walls in the maze to the north.

There are more strange symbols on the wall, here on the southwestern corner of the path. One of them resembles a strange-looking face with a sad look on it. The other resembles a kind of round shield, with a crest upon it. These abstract, almost runic-like designs seem to do nothing, but they are peculiar at the most. The path splits in two, to the north and to the east from here.

This gate is barely visible, what with thick mist surrounding the area. The vague silhouette of two pillars and a closing arc on the top is visible to the south, signifying the misty gate. A large orb filled with magical mist glows on the top of the arc. It is too misty to see what lies around, though glowing arrows on the floor point to the south and east.

This is a pretty odd room, in its own right. Three metal platforms are isolated in the middle by a large gap, almost like a castle surrounded by its moat. The flooring around it is created in a nearly symmetrical sense, with beams of light running in adjacent positions both on the left and right side.

This platform is designed to be a large square, mostly black with pink on its borders. To the general north is a rather pretty arrangement of small strips of platforms. The walls and floors glow bright with energy here, possibly due to the wiring and lights placed through it.

rooms.name: West section of an odd room

userData.LongDescription: This is the western part of a very odd room. There's a pretty large hole in the middle, about the room's center in size, leaving a doughnut-shaped platform to go around. A lone tile seems to jut out from the southern end, almost like a diving board serving for the hole, although jumping in might not be a good idea.

A small gap separates two otherwise parallel and almost identical metal platforms. A set of tall, pink gliding posts is placed to ease the arduous task of leaping through the gap. The bluish light of energy runs through the walls and platforms, creating a bit of a luminous glow in the room.
A large, angry yellow Fiend Head floats here.

This is a fairly odd-shaped platform, mostly black, with a large ring of red around it. Around are different paths, particularly northwest to a triangular-shaped platform, southwest to a cross-shaped platform and north to a crescent-shaped hallway. Many different shapes and destinations altogether are in the Fortress...

This room looks rather... messily placed. Two identical chunks of parallelogram-shaped platforms are placed on the southeast and northwest sides of the room, with a small bridge connecting them. However messily cut and placed, the platforms still seem sturdy and channeled to the walls, glowing with a bluish light.

This is a small crescent-shaped platform that rests against the cylindrical walls. An opening is in the middle, revealing a short set of steps and a path leading north into a larger room. On the walls are strange, almost runic-like patterns. On the left side, a large crescent scythe-like weapon pattern can be seen, and on the right side is a large shuriken.

This doorway is very intricate in detail, with the design of two long dragons coiling each other. A large gemstone rests on the top part, glowing bright with energy. Lines of glowing light run through it, creating a nice effect. To the north the path breaks into two, leading left and right.

Past the doorway is an L-shaped bend. To the east is an extremely long path, with multiple doorways upon it. North leads to an intersection breaking three ways. The metallic floors and walls glow bright, with lines of light flowing through them much like blood through its veins.

This large room looks fairly odd, with four large holes near the center. It looks more made out of six platforms cross-hatched together in a hasty manner, with the lack of furnishing and refinement that most other rooms in the fortress have received. To the south is a small doorway leading down to a catwalk, and to the west is a small corridor.

This room was probably created with the annoyance of its travelers in mind. A large square hole lies in the center of the room, with a path of thin platforms looping around it, eventually leading south, deeper into the fort. The flooring is composed out of smaller platforms adjoined together.

This very peculiar room is large and circular in shape. It's mostly a large, gaping bottomless pit that fills almost the entire room, with thin, narrow platforms to walk along the sides. In the middle of the room is a small pillar-like platform, its purpose unknown. To the north is a dark corridor, and to the south is a large, open room.

This is a rather devilish gate, as the name implies. Demonic wings of black and red stretch out from the gate, which is made out of a black material, probably damascus. A large demon head rests on the top of the gate, with a large orb in its mouth, glowing with a purely negative energy. To the further north is a maze of stone walls, and to the west a small intersection.

rooms.name: Before a set of gliding posts

userData.LongDescription: The row of metal platforms branches out to different sections from here. To the north is a short path leading up to an intricate-looking doorway. To the west is a long path leading somewhere, and nearby is a twin set of gliding posts, to make crossing the gap to the south easier. The walls and floors glow bright with Mana, a trademark of the fortress.

This is a fairly regular intersection, with three different paths to take. The northern road leads into a large room filled with holes, the eastern path a long hallway ending at a sharp curve, and to the south a set of gliding posts. A small piece of machinery seems to be attached to the ceiling.

Stars, small planets and other sorts of outer space objects dot the background around, creating a nice planetary image. A small sphere of light floats nearby, creating a dim glow and providing access to another section of the fortress. To the south is a wide star ocean and the image of a black hole.

This platform is a true oddity, shaped as a large raised X on the ground. Around it is a large black platform, circular in shape. The X itself seems to be made out of a plastic material, for a reason unknown. The path splits into two from this point, to the northwest and to the northeast.

This is the odd room's northern side, with a square platform hatched onto the walls. A circle of light glows in the middle of the platform, with an almost inviting feel amidst all the darkness present in this room. To the extreme south is a similar platform, creating north-south equivalents.

The walls of the room seem to slope in like an alcove in the northwest corner, allowing for a circular-shaped platform with a glowing red orb embedded in it. It certainly stands out as the northwestern point of the maze. South takes a long straight path to the southwestern corner, and to the southeast is a path leading to the very center of the maze.

This is the final room before entering the Fortress itself. Small lights shimmer on the floors and walls, reflecting dully off of the deep blue metal. As the Fortress glides slowly through the air, the ground below can be viewed from a dizzying height.

rooms.name: Near the north end of the loop

userData.LongDescription: The path takes a sharp turn at this point. There are two immediate directions: northwest to the doorway of the loop and to the west across the gliding posts. A runic pattern rests on the eastern wall, resembling a large suit of platemail. The floors glow bright with energy, channeling into the almost chaotic crystals, with their bright emerald green glow.

This large gate is rather comical in looks, wrapped in white moogle fur, with many different faces of moogles carved onto it! Happy faces, sad faces, angry faces and dancing faces, all the different natural facial expressions of the moogles are placed upon it. Some text seem to be carved upon the sides, and on the top is a large orb with the image of a dancing moogle within it.

This is the easternmost point of the large maze of platforms. Platforms swirl around like noodles in a ramen bowl, though clear paths leading to the west and northwest seem to stand out among the rest of the confusion. The walls and floors here glow bright with a certain blue tint of light.

This railed platform is small providing only a nice view of the space below, but otherwise leading nowhere. Far below is a large circular platform, almost like a ritualistic altar with a raised mound in the middle. A circle of light seems to glow from within, sending a pillar of light shooting up to the ceiling high above.

All around the fortress is a color combination that is almost sickly in taste. The green shine of the platforms and the yellow metal of the walls certainly do not contrast well with the bluish glow that envelopes this room, due to the lines of light that run rampant all around. This is the right side of the oddly symmetrical room.

The corridor takes two turns here, north and east. To the north is a short bend leading further west somewhere, and to the east is a large room filled with holes. This section of the corridor seems to even be more interesting than usual, with a large glass screen embedded onto the southern wall. Other than the usual compliment of glowing metal, there's not much else here.

This large, twisted maze is built not to intimidate, but more to confuse and annoy, with its walls, floors and ceiling in perfect unison. It's all made out of a greyish stone, showing no difference. The path leads to the north, leading deeper into the maze, and to the south is a large gate marking the entrance of the maze.

This path is filled with bright light. Bright overhead lamps are placed on the ceiling, and strips of light on the walls and floors help illuminate this narrow path. On the corners are green orbs that glow, outlining the already bright path. On the upper top of the walls are what seem to be narrow screens, with text outlining them. The path leads both to the northeast and southeast.

This room is fairly uninteresting, judging from what it contains. A medium-sized hole is in the middle of the metal platforms that make the fortress' floors. The walls are fairly standard, with beams of light that link up to the ceiling, making the place glow like a firefly festival at night.

This is a small corridor made out of metal, lines of light glowing about it. To the east and west are larger rooms with gates of amazing and unique powers. The walls and floors glow brightly in this small hallway, due to multiple strips of light that are placed around.

This small corridor has barely any lighting in it, though the shape of the passage is clear; it's a straight hallway leading north-south. To the north is an intricate row of gates, and to the south is a doughnut-shaped room. The walls and floors here are barely visible, preventing any more particular details to be seen.

This is a truly interesting gate, shaped in a high arc of solid ice. Frosty puffs of air seem to emanate from it. Pillars of cute penguins in pirate outfits in ice-sculpture form line the arc. A sky blue orb rests on the top between two heads, glowing with energy. To the north is a fairly straightforward path leading to another hallway.

This gate seems to be made out of fire, and nothing but fire. Tall infernous pillars wrap in a high arc with a large, fiery red orb resting on the top of it. Everything around it seems to glow with a reddish shade. To the north is a twirling path, while to the east is a short path, ending at a point leading south.

A long hallway stretches out to the south from this point, with an intersection in the middle. To the west is a short path leading to another corner. There's stone here, stone there, stone everywhere; stone fills the maze. The floors and walls are made out of a dark stone. The ceiling is made out of stone, and only small wisps attached to the wall give light to the maze.

rooms.name: The Pagoda of the Mighty Gods - 7F

userData.LongDescription: This is the final floor of the pagoda, and its final trial as well. On the back wall, two glass display cases sit.  Along the other walls, masks depicting the three faces of Godo, the pagoda's final god, hang.  Behind these masks, candles are flickering, giving the eyes of each mask an eerie look. Noone is allowed to leave without braving the final challenge of fighting Lord Godo for the recognition of beating the Pagoda of the Five Gods.

rooms.name: The Pagoda of the Mighty Gods-1F

userData.LongDescription: A beautiful looking strip of red carpet leads from the Pagoda's entrance to its attendant.  Above hang strings of paper lamps decorated with dragons, various symbols, and other designs.  Just past the attendant sits a staircase, leading to the Pagoda's 2nd floor, and its first challenge. Wutai citizens who have attained a sufficently high martial arts prowess are free to challenge the gods of the pagoda. This decision should never be made lightly.

rooms.name: The Pagoda of the Mighty Gods-3F

userData.LongDescription: In each corner of this room, bird-shaped statues are attached to the walls and are holding lanterns to provide the place with illumination.  A red, square carpet, the only real color, sits in the middle of the room.  Above the stairs leading to the upper floor, a portrait depicting a small, penguin-like creature hangs.

rooms.name: The Pagoda of the Mighty Gods-4F

userData.LongDescription: All around, glass eyeballs float, held in the air by some invisible force.  These eyeballs glow, giving off a rather eerie light.  A blue carpet, bearing a rather unsightly stain, lies in the middle of the ground. Above the stairs leading to the upper floor, a picture hangs, depicting a hideous mass of flesh with 8 eyes.  It seems the guardians of the pagoda are getting uglier each floor.

rooms.name: The Pagoda of the Mighty Gods - 6F

userData.LongDescription: All challengers of the tower who have braved the lower floors are allowed to rest here. This part of the pagoda seems a good respite. Several straw mats lie about the room, and a few paintings hang on the walls. A simple lantern hangs overhead to light the room, and a staircase lies ahead, leading to the final trial of the pagoda.

rooms.name: The Pagoda of the Mighty Gods - 5F

userData.LongDescription: A faint chugging noise is heard while climbing up the staircase. Upon reaching the 5th floor itself, the first thing that strikes the eye is the huge, wall sized portrait on the wall next to the staircase to the 6th floor.  Above the room, a pair of brightly glowing orbs circle, providing light.  This floor is the last real obstacle before challenging the master of the pagoda, Lord Godo himself.

rooms.name: The Pagoda of the Mighty Gods-2F

userData.LongDescription: A large, square green carpet is located in the center of this room, providing it with a bit of color.  In each corner of the room, there is a table with a small Buddha statue atop it.  A lantern is held by each of these statues, providing some illumination.  Above the stairs that lead to the upper floor, a portrait hangs, depicting a ferocious looking winged creature.

The small passage connects with a big cavern to the west.  The waterfall from the entrance can still be heard, although barely.  A small cubbyhole sits on the north side of the passage, big enough for a person to fit in.  The ceiling recedes upwards, giving way to darkness.

This is a narrow path that runs over an underground stream.  The stream is full of rocks and debris, which slows the flow of the water.  Much of the grotto can be seen from the path, and it extends into darkness to the north and south.  Flapping noises come from above.

The cave entrance is nearby to the south, and the cave continues on into darkness to the north.  There are patches of rough grass on the ground where water is falling from the ceiling, and some bones are strewn about the floor.  There are also some rocks protruding from the ground that could be easily tripped on.

The tunnel curves somewhat to the right, before leading to a flight of stairs.  The floor is half covered in rough grass, and slopes downward towards the stairs.  The ceiling is lower than most parts of the cavern, and is also sloping downward.

The room is a large cavern that extends to the south, with a smaller passage to the north.  A large stalagmite and stalactite meet in the center of the room, forming a column.  Some rocks are lying about, forcing passersby to watch their step, while a spot of soft ground lies to one side.

The bridge is made of rock, and looks as if it was formed before the cave was found.  To either side of the bridge is a large chasm.  Off to the northeast, a different part of the cave can be seen.  That part of the cave is too far across the chasm to reach, though.

This is a smaller cave, but it opens out to the west more.  It smells like fresh air, and some small patches of grass grow in random spots on the ground.  There is also lots of rock littering the ground, and a soft spot of earth next to the eastern wall.

This is a circular platform, with a small rock pillar standing right in the middle and a thin rock bridge leading somewhere to the north.  The platform is a part of the small cavern that extends east from the platform.  On each side of the platform there is a deep chasm.

Outside of the cave to the south, the waterfall flows into a shallow pool.  Some water from the waterfall flows inside the cave, creating a grotto.  The cave looks small at first, but farther in the ceiling opens up into a larger cavern.  A set of steps leads up onto dryer ground to the north.

A view of a large cavern can be seen from the landing.  Most of the cavern extends westward, and south a bit.  The floor of the landing is spotted with rocks, as well as bat droppings.  A musky smell pervades the room, and the sound of dripping water can be heard in the distance.

This is only a small portion of the grotto.  To the east, a large underground stream passes through the cave.  The smell of fresh air comes from the water, though the source of the water can't be seen.  Some noises that sound like bats moving come from above.

The landing is in the western part of the cavern.  A passage to the north leads into darkness, but the rest of the cavern is well lit by an unknown force.  Some large rocks lie on the floor, waiting to stub someone's toe.  The wind can be faintly heard howling through the rocks above.

The path is basically a small tunnel.  It is very thin, leaving hardly any room to walk.  It has a slight curve to it, and there is a small opening at one point.  The opening looks out into the underground stream, which is flowing at a steady pace.

The rooms opens up into a large cavern that extends northward.  A large rock pillar stands in the middle of the cave, supporting the ceiling and taking up half of the room.  Some large stalactites can be seen hanging from the ceiling, coming down from the darkness.

The room is square shaped, and of a decent size.  It smells of goblin, as some have obviously made their home in the cavern.  Signs of goblins are all about the room, and there is even a pile of trash in one corner.  The floor is uneven and rocky, except for a space in the center.

The underground stream flows by unimpeded to the west, and some large rocks block passage to the east.  Some stairs lead further down into the cavern, where some faint noises can be heard.  The ground is uneven and rocky, while the walls seem to be made of smooth, flat rock.

The cavern is in a circular pattern, with the western and southern sides blocked off by large rocks that are impassable.  There is a rather odd large hole in the center of the cave, leading straight down into another part of the underground.  Some noises can be heard from the hole.

This is the lowest part of the cavern.  From this position, the ceiling can't be seen because it's so high up.  The walls tower up the sides of the cavern, and the floor is colored with different shades of rock.  It is also evident that the floor was once not in the place that it is now.

The room is a small cul-de-sac, and is shaped like a circle.  The ceiling is low, but high enough for a human to easily walk in.  Some ashes lay in the center of the room, evidence that there might have been an intelligent being in this area previously.

The hallway curves from the stairs into a larger chamber.  There is a small alcove to one side of the passage, and some intricate drawings are barely visible on the wall there.  A small patch of grass grows on the opposite side of the passage, but it is impossible to tell how it got there.

This is the western side of a small chamber.  There is a sharp upward slope in the ground at one point, leading up to a platform at the north point in the chamber.  It looks as though there has been a quake recently, as the place is a mess.

The platform is the highest part of the cavern, and everything can be seen from that point.  The platform curves around into a semi-circle, with a hole in the middle.  There also isn't much room to walk, so steps must be taken carefully in order not to fall into the hole.
