The passage curves north, but is blocked off by some large rocks.  Past the rocks a large room can be seen, and possibly reached from some other passage.  Water drips from some point on the ceiling onto the floor, creating a small wet spot on the rock.

Part of the path leads across the stream, while the other part splits into two paths.  There is a thin ledge between the wall and the stream that leads north, and a large corridor in the other direction.  The ceiling gets lower, and there are holes in the wall which appear to be natural.

The passage leaves little room for people to walk, nonetheless fight.  There is a small cubicle off to the west side of the passage that would be an ideal place for a monster to hide. Rock from the wall has fallen off, and lays on the sides of the corridor.

The passage starts curving in a semicircle, and also gets a bit wider.  The ceiling opens up to reveal a platform that sits high up, which can't be reached.  The floor of the passage is very rocky, so steps have to be taken carefully.  A musky smell also creeps through the air.

This is a small corridor at one corner of a large cavern, that ends before a deep chasm.  Across the chasm, another passage can be seen coming from somewhere else in the cave.  There are also lines on the floor where the rock had once moved from a different level.

The corridor leads further into the cave to the west, and out across the underground stream to the east.  The walls tower over either side of the passage, until they reach a high ceiling.  The sound of running water can be heard, and above it the sound of flapping wings.

The platform is actually a large rock, although it is extremely big and flat.  The whole chamber can be seen from the rock, which isn't very much.  A slope leads up to the platform, and some rubble lies in piles on the ground.  The sounds of a village come from the north.

This is a dead end, and a very small space at that.  More loose rock from the walls has fallen onto the ground, mixing with some bones.  Some water methodically drips from above, making a small pool on a rock that lies to one side of the passage.

Rubble lies in piles on the ground, and an old set of steps that once lead up to the platform in the north part of the chamber no longer does.  There is a large rock in the middle of the chamber that allows access to the platform from the western side of the cave.  Without the rock, there would be a large gap between the platform and the slope that leads to it.

The beginning of the path into the trial is relatively clear..disregarding the bones and occasional puddle of slime, that is.  Every now and again, an inhuman cry or groan can be heard, adding to the darkened atmosphere of this area.  Back to the south, the stalagmites are still clear, although it's unsure whether or not they'll stay that way.

The path takes a sharp bend, continuing to the northeast and to the southeast. Across the chasm to the west, earlier parts of the trial's passageway can be seen, but the jump would be impossible to make. Aside from a few scattered bones, little else of interest can be found.

Cracked bones and scraps of armor lay scattered on the floor among debris unearthed from a fierce battle. A large humanoid skull sits in the center of the path, a large section caved in. A chasm is visible to the southwest, while the path begins to wind towards the north.

The path leading north stops abruptly at a cliff that leads to a rather long drop down into nothing.  A skeletal hand grasps the edge of the cliff, as if hanging on for dear life... or, it would be if it had any life left to hang on for.  This spot is a bit cleaner than the rest of the cave, though all that really means is that there aren't as many dried pools of blood or chips of bone.  To the northeast, one can advance onwards towards the Test of Courage, and back to the south, the exit lies.

Apparently, a huge magical cataclysm of some sort occured here, as the rest of the path to the east was somehow sheared away.  Evidence of this cataclysm's magical nature is apparent, as the floor and walls glow with traces of mana.  Something very desperate... or sinister... must have caused whomever is responsible for this to do do as they did.

More of the small craters present to the west are here as well, though there aren't nearly as many.  A series of hairline cracks run down the walls from the ceiling of this small section down to the floor, evidence of some great struggle.  Additionally, a whole, human skeleton has somehow been melded to the wall, covering some of its cracks.  A black outline surrounds the skeleton... perhaps it was burned on?  Further down the path, to the west, a large hole is present in the wall of the cave...

More graveyard than test of courage, mountains of bones and skeletons from several types of beings are piled up along the entire floor. Many are chipped, cracked or charred, and it is impossible to tell which were slain by adventurers, and which are adventurers themselves. The path bends, leading to the north and to the west.

The path continues westward with the same bits of bone littering the way.  The bones are joined by small pieces of stone, possibly broken away from something by a rather large force.  On top of that, old and long dried blood covers small portions of the walls.  Joch really needs to do a better job of keeping this place clean.

A large humanoid skeleton sits in the center of the path, blackened and burnt, a victim of a powerful explosion, pieces of its bones laying scattered among shreds of armor. The poor individual's skull sits a few feet away from the rest of itself, evidence of the severity of the blast that claimed its life. The passage continues to the northwest and southeast.

Shards of scorched metal are scattered all about in this little part of this decidely unkept cave.  Here, small masses of what was once metal has hardened, and now sit in lumps on the walls and floor.  In addition, a battered helmet rolls around the ground here, yet another sure sign of the vicious combat that must occur here.

Several charred, rocky craters can be found along the ground of the pathway, although they can be difficult to see through the layers of ash kicked up after any movement. Whether the ash is scorched earth or the cremated remains of an unlucky adventurer is impossible to tell. The path bends around to both the southeast and the northwest.

More sharp, dangerous looking stalagmites poke out of the ground.  Near them, shattered chips of rock are scattered all around, joined by a few white features and bits of tentacle.  An obviously human arm is stuck on one of the stalagmites, having recently been chewed off by something at the shoulder.

The most outstanding feature here is the rather large hole in the wall of the cave.  It allows one to catch a glimpse of the Lofty Mountains, and the City of Mandala, both of them far below here.  Sunshine pours in through the hole, giving a little bit of light to the otherwise dark, and gloomy cave.  There is a small, rounded cliff outside the hole that's not quite big enough for a person to stand on, but big enough for small animals and plants to live on.

The path bends slightly, leading to the southwest, where it further curves, and to the north, where any further passage is blocked by a massive rocky barricade. Standing beside the barricade is Sage Joch, ready to test the courage of any adventurer through his trial.

A few rather large rocks are scattered all about, littering the area.  Two rocky stumps where stalagmites once blocked the path are here as well, hacked away crudely by a group of adventurers.  Broken arrow shafts are lying about as well, the heads nowhere to be found.  A large pool of blood covers a fair portion of this area as well.

The pathway abruptly ends, cutting off into cliffs that overlook the massive abyss below. The endless pits surround the dead end to the west, north and east, and the only way back to the main path is through the south. To the far northwest, beyond the void, another part of the cave is visible.

The darkness and gloom of the cave is lessened somewhat by the sunlight coming in from the west.  Though it isn't nearly as bright here as right next to the hole, it at least temporarily alleviates the constantly dark environment.  An old wooden coffer... or the bottom of it anyway has been tossed to the side, its top nowhere to be found.  Obviously, it's long empty, not counting the finger bones lying inside of it.

A few stalagmites poke out of the ground here and there, with sharp points threatening to seriously injure the careless.  Blood stains the walls here, something that should be familiar by now.  The hilt of a once expensive sword, sans blade stands against one of the walls.

As the path bends, it becomes impossibly and dangerously narrow at the corner, bits of the edge of the cliff falling down into the abyss below with every slight vibration or movement. The path leads two directions; to the east, it opens up to a larger room, while to the northwest, it snakes and bends around the cave.

Stone rubble lines the rocky floor, remnants of a stalagmite barrier that may have blocked the pathway once upon a time. The blockade looks to have been broken by a powerful swing from a sharp weapon. Paths lead to the east, towards a large chasm, and to the north, where scattered bones litter the terrain.

A large amount of rubble lies on floor of the passage, which has narrowed considerably. Perhaps once a barrier to prevent the unworthy from finishing the trial, the rocky wall has since been knocked down. Now traversable, the path continues and widens considerably to the northwest and to the southeast.

A cool breeze blows from the chasm as the path abruptly ends to the east, carrying with it a stale odor. A large stalagmite rises from the ground at the cliff edge, worn away in the middle. A platform can be seen across the chasm, where another stalagmite sticks in the air.

The fragments of a jack-o-lantern are in a small pile on the west side of the path.  It's much thinner here than it is just to the north, like most of the cave.  Next to the pumpkin pieces is a pile of white feathers with an army helmet sitting atop them.  Covering both are bits of an odd, silverish liquid and shreds of what used to be little yellow tentacles.

Extending to the northwest and southeast, this straight path contains little of interest. Across the expanse below, to the north, another section of the path is visible. Continuing northwest, the path bends to the northeast, while continuing southeast, the path leads into a large, stalagmite-filled room.

Small craters scar the floors and walls of this small portion of the pathway. Within a few of them, small puddles of dried blood lay as they have for quite a while.  Thin trails of it run down the walls, its dull crimson color off-setting the starkness of the rock.

The floor beneath this part of the passageway is full of cracks and craters, as this narrow section of the path was, perhaps, the scene of a fierce battle. The section of the northern cliff's edge is worn away, as the path stretches towards the east and towards the northwest.

A pile of bones are in a pile with an obviously inhuman skull on top.  A rather old and rusted sword is stuck in-between its ribs.  Nearby, fragments of bone and half of another, more human skull are scattered about the ground.  A path leads to the east, though there doesn't appear to be much in that direction.  To the south and east is another path leading towards a massive pile of rocks.

More sharp stalagmites stick up from the ground, posing as a natural but ineffective barrier.  Many of them have been hacked away, thanks to the efforts of past explorers, though a few still remain.  Those that are still here are covered with a slimy, silverish liquid that oozes slowly to the ground.  Between the stalagmites, charred bits of what were once seeds are scattered about.

Another pile of bones is buried in the ground here, sans skull.  These have been picked VERY cleanly by the denizens of the cave... or perhaps by other explorers with no other means to feed themselves.  Though it was probably once possible to go southwest, that is no longer so, as a large part of the path is no longer present.  Past the large gap there, however, there is more path leading to just north of the cave's entrance.  There is a small gap between those two as well.  Going north, northeast, and east is possible, fortunately.

The occasional rat scurries cautiously about, sometimes poking at the remains of a poor, long dead adventurer whose skeleton is embedded into the earth with a skull sitting atop it.  Occasionally, a bat flies by overhead, hunting for one of the many insects inhabiting this cavern.  There's an impassable gap to the east, and yet more path to the north and south.

Bits and pieces of rock line the floor as the path curves, continuing to the southeast and southwest. To the north and below, the bottomless chasm is seen stretching out infinitely across the cave, fading to complete darkness before any end is visible.

As the cave path forks with branches leading to the north, northwest and south, several stalagmite structures rise out of the ground. There are small piles of rubble along the floor of the pathway, appearing to be stalagmites that have been broken into many pieces by an immense power.

The pathway thins out here, barely allowing enough room for the very bottoms of a few stalagmites that previously blocked the way forward.  Scattered around them are chips of rock, presumably the result of someone hacking their way through.  None of the sunlight from the east is visible, now.  To the southeast, the path widens a bit.

Rubble and debris cover most of the floor of the bending pathway, scorched marks visible underneath. Rocks are still standing on the northeast protrusion of the passage, ending at a cliff and out of the way, as the path stretches towards the northwest and to the south.

Aside from a large stalagmite near the edge of the cliff, very little of interest can be seen nearby. A large platform is visible across the chasm, where a similar stalagmite rises from the ground, while another path leads to the northeast.

This part of the path is rather wide, allowing for advancement in several directions.  The rather large, rusted, and metallic head of an axe is buried deeply into the ground, a hand still attached to it.  Though it is mostly bone, a few shreds of flesh still cling to it.  It is possible to continue to the east, south, or southeast, though the paths to the south and east seem to end rather abruptly.

The path curves to the northwest here, and its condition continues to be subpar.  A large, inhuman skull looks up at the world, despite having half of its top crushed in.  Randomly strewn about are broken pieces of bones that closely resemble ribs.  Perhaps they belonged to the same creature as the crushed skull.  Perhaps this test wasn't such a hot idea after all.

The path is considerably more narrow than to the west or southeast, where it continues and widens, and the edges of the cliffs are worn away and cracked. Charred bones and blackened scraps of armor litter the small area. The winding path is visible across bottomless chasms to the southwest and northeast.

Taking a sharp bend, the path to Sage Joch's Trial leads to the northeast and southeast. Further along the northeast path, a large barricade is visible in the distance, while the southeast path eventually opens up into a larger room with many stalagmites.

Advancing any further east is impossible, due to the large chunk of ground that is no longer present.  Some poor sucker left his skull buried in the ground near the hole, his body nowhere to be found.  A blast of heat occasionally rises from the hole... it must be a deep one indeed.  To the west, southwest, and south, the way is clear.

This is a large hut acting as the island's only inn with a long row of straw beds placed over white mats. Crude windows are placed in set increments on the walls, causing sunlight to fill the room. On the eastern side is a wooden counter, and a sign hanging on the wall near it.

This round hut in the island belongs to the elder of the village. A white, coarse mat is placed over the wooden floors of the house, with straw beds piled in the middle. On the edges are wooden table-like counters, with miscellaneous belongings placed on them. An open doorway nearby leads outside.

The island's northern edge seems to be more packed than any other spot in the area, being the unofficial 'commerce' zone. Crates filled with dried fruit and other foodstock are piled next to a wide, large hut with a gourd plaque attached to its doorway. South leads back to the center of the island.

This round hut is rather sparse. It's not furnished with straw beds, white mats or little ornaments. Instead, there are lots of fishing rods lined up against the walls. Unfinished rafts are piled in one stack, and rope scattered all about the floor. There are also some baskets filled with all sorts of bait in the corner.

This small island is located in the middle of a vast sea, off from the commotion and events of the rest of the world. Apparently some people have inhabited this place, since there are small wooden huts scattered about the island. Nearby is a particularly large hut with a white cloth cover, making it stand out among the rest of the huts.

A large, round hut filled with different kinds of merchandise: those salvaged, bought, grown and stolen. The counter is drawn straight across the middle of the hut. Hung all about are the very items that the island is named after: the Sea Hare Tail. A doorway is to the south, leading outside. A sign is hung on the wall nearby.

A sharp cliff ends the southern border of the island. Just down below is a rope ladder leading to a small wooden dock, a small boat tied to it. Trees are planted around, wavering in the breeze. A wooden hut is built nearby, looking fairly hidden between the trees.

The western end of the island seems to be very bright and sunny, with the most exposure to the sun. There are almost no trees in the grassy field around, only wooden poles with laundry lines attached to them. A large hut with a bed sign attached to it is nearby. East leads to the center of the island.

This is a regular circle-shaped hut made out of wood. On the log-like pillars are strange, cultural masks. Baskets of food are placed on the sides of the hut. Straw beds are laid in the center of the hut. Overall this hut is fairly comfortable for a hut in the middle of a small island of a vast ocean.

The eastern end of the island overlooks a vast, endless ocean horizon. The grass wavers gently in the tropical breeze, the sun shining brightly in the blue sky. A wooden hut with peculiar painted designs stands nearby. Large trees are planted around, providing some cool shade from the sun. West leads to the center of the island.

On the south end of the city is a wide courtyard where citizens can come to relax and socialize. The grey stone road makes a brief turn north here, then turns to a large two-story building in the same white-walled style as the rest of the city. Two large oak trees provide shade, and the grey walkway circles one of the trees in a walking route. Scattered groups of red flowers dot the well-kept grass. To the north, past a small white marble fountain, a tree-lined path heads north along the raised stone wall.

Southtown's Inn isn't terribly roomy, but like the rest of the city, it is tastefully decorated with violet curtains and has a homey feel, thanks to the overall wealth of the empire. The smell of cooking food wafts in from behind the desk and beams of sunlight give the room a warm glow. A sign sits on the check-in counter, while a set of stairs at the west end of the room leads up to the item shop.

Made of grey stone, this raised walkway extends from the northeastern corner of Southtown to the center of town. The view of the small city is excellent, but considering Southtown is a sleepy burg there's not much to see. A thin railing made of the same grey stone runs along the sides of the walkway. Stairs here lead down into the town proper.

12290: 0say the password is mara sent me

userData.LongDescription: This narrow path leads north between the raised stone walkway on the west and the expansive treeline surrounding the city on the east. The grass isn't very well cared for here, but it's obvious that some people do walk this far back on occasion. The path comes to a sudden dead end when the wall takes a turn toward the forest, and a barred portcullis is set into the wall. Thanks to the height of the wall, this place is swathed in deep shadows.

Made of grey stone, this raised walkway extends from the northeastern corner of Southtown to the center of town. The view of the small city is excellent, but considering Southtown is a sleepy burg there's not much to see. A thin railing made of the same grey stone runs along the sides of the walkway, which continues to the southwest.

This second-floor room is rented out to the shop owner by the innkeeper. It's small, but it seems to serve well enough, as it's got a monopoly on the dry goods business in Southtown. A waist-high counter separates the shopkeeper's work area from the rest of the room, and a single wooden chair sits off to the side for any armor fittings that need to be done. The stairs at the back of the room lead back to the inn.

Standing here is a small one-story house of white wood with double doors and a tasteful red and white-striped awning that sits on a foundation of the same grey stone that the walkway is constructed of. Along the west border of the property a low garden wall runs, and beyond that the expansive forest of pines that surrounds Southtown. A large oak tree sits in the yard. To the east you can see a small courtyard, while to the southeast is the main road of the city.

Running south from the raised walkway that runs to the center of town from the northeast, this central road is a grey cobblestone street that runs south, then turns easterly toward the inn and the southern courtyard. The western edge of the road is lined with tall green pines. A path in the grass runs to the northwest toward a small house, while the road continues east and stairs lead back up to the walkway.

This courtyard in the northern part of Southtown presumably belongs to the owner of the house to the west. The grass lawn is well-manicured, though, so it may be in the care of the state. A bubbling fountain of white marble flows quietly in the shade of a large oak tree, and the entire yard is dotted with groups of red flowers. A waist-high garden wall stands between the surrounding forest and the courtyard.

This wooded area is yet another in a long line of world-famous Cannon Travel Centers. Tall pine trees surround a raised earthen platform into which has been carved a short set of stairs. At the top of the platform is a highly ornate black and gold cannon. At the foot of the stairs, small stones litter the path into the Empire's Southtown, and a happily bouncing Cannon Travel attendant smiles as you pass. A wooden sign stands next to him.

This peaceful stretch of grass is the entrance to Southtown, a small city on the southern edge of the Empire. From here, only the city's raised walkway is really visible, blocking your view of the rest of the city. Surrounded by tall pines and dotted with small red flowers, this peaceful, grassy path gives no indication the the residents live in the cruel grip of the Empire.

The interior of this small house isn't terribly roomy, but the occupant obviously takes good care of it. The floor is a simple wooden panelling, while the walls are covered in a tasteful grey wallpaper and one landscape painting next to a window with light violet drapes. Inside the door is a small potted shrub. The furnishings include an easy chair of the same violet as the drapes, a bookshelf with a desk clock on top of it, a small bed, and a dinner table with two chairs.

This long, flooded chamber is where the sewers on the south side of the network pool before draining into the drain room below. The murky brown water is nearly waist-high here thanks to the number of small square platforms that dot the center of the chamber. Small torches set into the walls provide the only real lighting in the room, a dim red glow that fits the sewer's crypt-like ambience. Stairs leading down to the south and up to the north lead out.

This drainage room is at the very bottom of the Imperial sewer network between Northtown and Southtown and is practically flooded with the disgusting brown water that pervades the entire sewer, pouring in continuously from dragon-headed cisterns positioned everywhere along the walls. Two walkways rise above the water near the exits: a narrow ledge to the south stairs and a wider ledge to the north stairs.

Spiralling down through the sewers is the northern drain corridor, where the cloudy brown water pouring from the dragon-headed cisterns at the south stairwell pools and then rushes down to the drain chamber below. Two platforms at the south and north ends of the room surround the stairwells, and a narrow trough filled with water leads between the two.

This entrance to the sewers echoes with the sounds of dripping and water rushing from dragon-headed cisterns down to the floor and then down further through the sewer network. At the south side of the room, near stairs up toward the surface, is a shallow expanse of cloudy brown sewer water which extends nearly halfway through the room, where two separate paths lead to a raised stone walkway. At the north end of the walkway is a set of stairs leading further down into the sewer.

This chamber is the first in the downward turn to the central drain chamber between Northtown and Southtown. Stone platforms sit at the foot of two sets of stairs, one in the northwest corner and one in the southeast corner. Between the two platforms is another stretch of the murky brown sewer water that the dragon-headed cisterns continue to pour in from high on the walls, and the only light provided is from dim torches set aside the stairwells.

Here at the northern side the sewers are a deep trough of the sickening brown water, presumably running from Imperial Northtown on the surface above. The dragon-headed cisterns set into the walls continue to pour the putrid water in from above. At the northeast end of this trough are two sets of stairs: one out of the water, and one down further into the sewers. A ladder leading out appears to have been set up, making an exit.

A short hallway from the main lobby leads to a counter with two werewolves behind it. They stand ready to take your money in exchange for weapons of various sorts. Behind the wolves on the back wall of the shop is an open door-frame that presumably leads to the actual workshop. It is possible to go west and speak with the armorsmiths.

Fed well by the bright light of the sun, the grass here is a vibrant green, unblemished by excessive travel that should exist in on a primary thoroughfare. To the north is a massive closed gate, while to the east inviting music can be heard. Looking west there is another grassy clearing; more captivating, however, is the two story mansion to the south, so large it bridges over the main path through the village.

rooms.name: In front of the equipment store

userData.LongDescription: The equipment store is a quaint little building built into the northern cliff. On either side of the front door are two signs; the left one depicting a sword and the right with a picture of a shield. To the west is the magic shop, and the rest of Quelb is to the east.

A short hallway from the main lobby leads to a counter with two werewolves behind it. They stand ready to take money in exchange for armor of various sorts. A large fireplace occupies most of the northern wall, providing heat to the entire building.

Light dances cheerily from several lamps on the walls giving the main room of the inn a warm, welcoming feel. The floors are cobbled stones fitted so well it feels like tile. A long counter divides the room in half. The inn also features an item shop for those who are in need of such things. Three werewolves stand ready to serve. The door on the north wall provides access to the sleeping chambers. There is a sign on the counter.

rooms.name: In front of the Quelb inn

userData.LongDescription: The village's inn has little to differentiate it from the other local buildings. There is a large wooden sign with the word "INN" written on it in bold letters to dispel any confusion about the nature of the establishment. One of the werewolves has left the front door open in response to the warm, sunny weather.

This sunlit grassy patch of Quelb has two moderately sized pine trees and tall cliffs to make up the southern edge. To the west is the equipment store, while further the same direction is the magic shop. The front door of the local inn can be seen to the northeast.

The northern wall in the first room of the Quelb's equipment shop occupies the middle two-thirds of the room. It is decorated with two signs, the one on the western edge is embossed with a large shield, while the one on the eastern edge has a pair of swords. As further evidence for the direction of the weaponsmith, there is a rack of spears on the eastern wall.

This robust hall is huge by comparison to the other buildings of Quelb. Here on the southern end, richly colored area rugs cover much of the smooth stone that comprises the floor, giving the room warmth it would otherwise lack. Tall ceilings and stone walls provide clear acoustics throughout the room. There is a large wooden table occupying the center of the room, while smaller tables occupy smaller alcoves. A large sturdy door leads outside to the rest of Quelb.

Only a few feet down the suddenly narrow pass leading north out of Quelb, a massive grey stone frame has been built nearly seamlessly into the sheer rock walls on either side of the idyllic path. Supported by the large stone frame is a proportionally large iron gate that serves to maintain the peaceful atmosphere of Quelb to the south.

Two windows on the northern wall provide a surplus of light in the small industrial kitchen. A wooden prep counter dominates the eastern wall, and is covered with a variety of vegetables. Placed next to the prep counter are two wooden chairs, which are currently vacant. An industrial wood stove takes center stage on the northern wall, upon which a cauldron of stew has been set to simmer.

At the northern end of the large wooden table rests an over-sized chair, marking this end as the head of the table. While no fire is currently lit in either of enormous fireplaces, it is clear they would be capable of heating the entire hall. On the northern wall there is a humble looking wooden door that presumably leads further into the mansion.

The primary path through Quelb is covered by the second story of the large mansion, as it stretches across from one side to the other. The ever present grass in Quelb grows unabated through the underpass, and there is a comfy looking bench for anyone who wanted to take a moment to rest. To the north is the main gate, and the path south leads to an open courtyard in the center of Quelb. Faint music can be heard coming around the corner to the north.

The hallway stretches on here with only a small painting on the wooden walls to break up the area. The smells from the kitchen to the east are tantalizing from this distance. To the west is the other end of the hallway providing access to the dining hall. A long and narrow well worn carpet dampens the sound of footsteps through the area.

A spacious courtyard where the youth of Quelb can often be found enjoying the warm sun, and soft grass inherent to Quelb. The courtyard is on the south side of the large mansion, which has two windows on the second floor, but curiously only a heavy wooden door on the ground level. The southern edge of the courtyard is largely blocked off by the western portion of the inn protruding from the cliff. A small path to the south squeezes between the edge of the inn and the nearby cliffs. To the west is a shaded clearing with two large trees.

Shade extending out from the tall cliffs on the western edge of Quelb offers a brief respite from the hot afternoon sun. In spite of the shade, the area clearly gets enough sun to keep the grass impressively healthy. The eastern edge of the clearing is framed by one wall of the massive mansion, and to the south the clearing continues interrupted only by a pair of large pine trees.

On the eastern edge of Quelb is a spacious alcove with some of the only shrubbery found in Quelb. The quiet area is surrounded on three sides by sun warmed cliffs. The eastern wall of the mansion encloses the majority of the passage west, adding to the seclusive nature of the alcove. The music heard from here is being made for the werewolf villagers to dance to.

The guest room of the inn is a spacious number, with a high ceiling supported with large wooden timbers. Six beds are set up in a barracks style arrangement, the emphasis being on the number of beds rather than privacy. A massive fireplace on the north wall keeps the room warm and well lit in the evenings, while a window on the same wall provides light during the day.

Quelb is a busy little village of werewolves high up on the mountain pass. Though the buildings are designed for harsh winters, fortunately it is currently summer time and the sun is out in full force making the grassy basin a very comfortable place to spend time. Travel north is restricted by the western wall of the inn protruding from the cliff face. The entrance to the inn can be found to the east; while to the south a pair of pine trees disrupts the otherwise flawless blanket of grass.

rooms.name: In front of Quelb's magic shop

userData.LongDescription: The magic shop is on the far southwest portion of Quelb. The cliffs wrap around from the north to the south blocking travel to the west. There is a sign left of the door, and a well sits near the southern cliffs.

Smaller than the dining hall in every way, this hallway connects the living quarters of the mansion. The floors are made of stone, however the walls have been constructed of timber. On the north side of the intersection is a closed door, while to the south is an open door into the main hall. The smells coming from the east make promises of a tasty meal.

The eastern section of Quelb is a sunlit grassy little clearing surrounded on three sides by tall cliffs. To the northwest is the inn, and to the west is the town entrance. There is a small pen here for sheep to graze on the plentiful greenery.

The narrow path leading up the mountain from the Bal Plains to the south opens up suddenly to reveal Quelb village. Quelb is a quaint little village high in the mountains. The warm summer weather has brought a delightful cheeriness to the village. Between the bright sun, ample grass, pine trees and wonderful buildings Quelb feels like it sprang from a painting... except the werewolves.

A large ornate bed occupies much of the northern end of the room.  A table set up on the western side of the room provides seating for four. The light in the room is currently being provided by a window on the northeastern corner over a small study, however the fireplace in the northwest corner is likely the source during the darker hours.

A closed wooden door is set into the northern wall, while to the west leads into the rest of the mansion. The walls continue the trend of the living quarters by being made of wood planks rather than the grey stone that was used for the floors.

The local magic shop is a large single room building built into one of the cliffs that surround the village. Though this room is plenty large, the all wood construction and over-sized fireplace leave room with a certain coziness. The center of the room is dominated by a large counter that wraps around and separates the center of the room from the outer edges. An older looking werewolf stands behind this counter ready to sell his wares.

Two vast ancient pine trees break free of the soil and reach above the cliffs, that make up the west and southern walls, to obtain their share of the region's sun. The back end of the equipment shop pokes out of the southern cliff providing one of the only breaks in the stone texture. To the east lays the center of Quelb and the front door of the mansion.

Large columns of flowstone extend from the southern wall of the passage, forcing the path to the north. Drops of water occasionally drip from the ends of the draperies into a small pool below them. The walking path winds through the cave, around various mound-like stalagmites.

The ceiling of the tunnel extends far above into a tight crevice with many limestone formations reaching down. Water drips from the formations onto the shale-covered floor, which has broken off from the northern wall. Most of the shale has been pushed to the sides of the passage, creating a clear path from the east to the limestone stairs that lead up to a smaller tunnel.

Chunks of shale have been piled against the end of the tunnel to the east, which was removed to allow for the massive silver door on the northern wall. Stalagmites reach up to a limestone shelf positioned on the southern wall which drops of water fall from periodically.

The wide passage winds as it follows the edges of the faults between limestone slabs from different ages. The ceiling and floor of the passage are filled with different types of active cave formations that reach towards each other. A warm breeze from the west pushes deeper into the cave.

The ceiling extends far above the limestone floor and can no longer be seen. Only the very tips of stalactites can be seen through the darkness. A large crevice to the northwest leads into a deep passage that bends out of sight into a void. A crude set of steps have been carved into the limestone to the south, towards an expansive space.

The winding tunnel takes a sudden turn at a long set of worn steps which descend into darkness. Claw marks and long scrapes fill the bottom of the tubular tunnel, indicating a significant amount of traffic. Limestone flowstone has begun to form on the eastern wall, which extends down into the stairwell.

An incredibly large flowstone formation occupies the entire southern wall. Thick columns of limestone have melded together to create a feature that looks similar to a church organ. The floor is slightly slanted toward the formation but is otherwise very smooth. To the south, an unnaturally tubular tunnel disappears into the shadows under the formation.

This dark, canyon-like passage is very narrow and runs between a fault of limestone and shale. The southern wall is a pale yellow limestone that pushes into the path with its active formations, while the northern wall is an ever-yielding feature that crumbles to the touch. High above the floor, stalactites reach down and occasionally drip water onto the dusty pieces of shale.

Rills along the limestone walls are filled with condensation and are cool the touch. A faint breeze pushes through the from the depths of the winding tunnel towards the stairs to the west. Heavy, slow-moving scraping noises echo throughout the passage, though the origin is not apparent.

The limestone cavern sprawls in every direction, but each seems to end in a tight, useless crevice except to the south towards an opening in the cave wall. Daylight pours in onto the smooth cavern floor and makes the stalactites on the ceiling glisten.

A long set of stairs leads north, up and out of this tunnel. To the east, the tubular tunnel delves deeper into the earth. The limestone floor and walls are filled with deep scratches, created by the titanic creatures that inhabit this subterranean cave.

The passage quickly dwindles to a tight crevice which cannot be traversed. A steady stream of water trickles down from the ceiling on the northern wall which in turn flows into a crack along the floor. Large claw marks are all along the floor and seem to congregate near this spring.

The twisting passage that leads into the mountains of the Bal Overlands quickly winds away from the light and delves into the darkness. Small droplets of water trickle down the sides of the sandstone tunnel and flow into small crevices between the different layers of strata.

A long, shallow set of stairs leading north have been carved into the sandstone floor, which have become smooth and rounded. The water that flows in from cracks in the walls flows down these steps towards the chasm to the southeast. The area to the north is extremely bright, compared to the dark passage to the southeast.

A crisp, humid breeze pushes through a large crevice on the northern wall. The sounds of an underground river echo off this small chamber. A small passage between two large limestone columns leads to the east, towards the entrance of the cave.

Dark, sinuous passages lead into a deep cavern. A vast opening above the smooth limestone floor transitions into decrepit castle ruins, and many vines have begun to grow into the cave. The breeze from the caverns below pushes the mist from the river into the ruins above.

The path is reduced to nothing more than a small ledge above an expansive, shadowy abyss. A cool breeze carries a mist of groundwater throughout the chamber and ensures the thin ledge is always wet. A few immense pillars in the center of the cave rotunda extend from the domed ceiling down into the river below.

The top of this sandstone slab seems to have been eroded by the heavy mist in the area, which has resulted in a fairly flat platform. A small chest is positioned in the center of it. Far below the edge of the slab, an underground river rages through the cave system. A stalactite hangs directly above this spot.

The path follows the edge of the cave rotunda, winding along the sinuous cave walls. A monolithic limestone pillar to the south drips with sediment-rich groundwater that is supplied by the underground river below the ledge. The northern wall is filled with cracks, which make for excellent handholds.

A broad ledge protrudes from the western wall, which provides ample space for traversing the cave. Despite that, a small portion of the southern path has fallen to the shadows below, leaving only a small sliver. To the southeast, a few limestone pillars connect the dome-like ceiling to the bottom of the chasm. A few rays of sunlight peeking through the ceiling highlight the mist-filled air.

A deep crevice that runs from the ground to the ceiling along the southern wall. The line of skull-shaped buttons continues from the west and goes further east. A constant trickle of ground water is coming from the southern wall.

The cave walkway is quickly reduced to a tight crevice as the walls rejoin. A large stalactite hangs from the ceiling, though it appears to have dried up long ago. A small copper chest is situated in the crevice and looks as if it's been open for a very long time.

The cavern opens into a large rotunda with a massive chasm in the center. A broad ledge follows the edge of the room and runs southwest to east. A small walkway has been created to the northwest by a collapsed slab of sandstone. Gigantic pillars of ancient bedrock reach into the abyss below, on either side of the collapsed slab.

Heavy tooling marks and deep grooves run along the ground in this section of the cave which ends as abruptly as they began. The score marks disappear into the western wall, where a massive, rectangular sandstone slate has been carved from the natural wall. A silver door with elaborate embossing is embedded into an alcove on the eastern wall.

Small mineral deposits have collected on the ground, leftover from mineral-rich water that constantly evaporates. The sinuous passage bends and winds, but eventually ends near a skull-shaped button. A large section of a sandstone slab has fallen apart, revealing a passage into the cave.

The ceiling of the passage slowly connects with the floor as the hallway comes to an end. The long line of skull-shaped buttons on the northern wall continues from the west. A pile of rocks has been stacked against the southern wall.

The path is fractured as a large crack slowly consumes part of the level ground. Against the western wall, a large pile of fallen rocks has been made in an attempt to keep the walking path cleared. A small tubular tunnel extends to the northwest where daylight can be seen pouring in from above.

The northern wall of this excavated tunnel has a line of skull-shaped buttons running along it. The southern wall has become reclaimed by the cave and is slowly encroaching on the passage. A small stream of ground water flows in from the east.

This section has been completely scraped clear of natural cave formations to accommodate for the mechanism that drives the sandstone slab. Dust fills the air, replacing the stale air with a heavy spray of loess powder. Daylight can barely be seen to the northwest through the thick airborne sediment.

The sounds of an underground river echoes off the narrow passage walls. A few slabs of shale have been stacked near the ledge to the southwest. The cave winds around a few limestone columns before opening to the west. The path is fairly constrained by the formations which will likely overtake the passage at some point.

The cave passage splits in three directions. The walls of the cave are covered in thick dust, which has accelerated the formation of flowstone draperies along the ceiling. An old, dust-covered chest sits in a small alcove.

A slab of sandstone has collapsed onto the path from the southeast, blocking the way forward. A small wooden chest has been placed against the wall and is covered in a thick coat of dust-covered mud. A large hole in the ground to the southeast occasionally emits a spray of fine mist. The narrow ledge above the chasm wraps around a pillar and is the only available path.

The thin walkway along the southern ledge leads between two shale slab staircases. Rough sandstone ledges on the northern wall are worn from being used as handrails. The echoes of underground rapids can faintly be heard from the northeast. A small chest is tucked into the side of the wall.

Bright daylight pours through the cave's main entrance to the north as a cool breeze pushes out. Strange sounds echo from deep within the cavernous tunnels leading south. Deep crevices to the southwest have been filled with gobbing. A small skull has been affixed to the wall near the entrance.

The passage becomes constrained as the naturally occurring formations congeal into columns near the walls. A constant flow of trickling water has smoothed the limestone floor, making it fairly slick. The water streams into a deep crevice within the western wall, before disappearing from sight.

The path from the north widens dramatically and overlooks the cave rotunda. Rays of sunlight extend into the abyss, providing a glimpse of the raging waters far below. Massive stalactites and flowstone formations hang from the ceiling, which seem to congregate around the gigantic limestone columns that extend into the dark, water-filled abyss.

Ancient cave formations line the eastern and western walls, while an intricate silver door has been embedded on the southern wall. A few slabs of shale have been stacked near a ledge to the northwest, which appears to be the only way to access the passage beyond the ledge to the north.

The broad walkway extends east to west and leads up to a massive chasm to the north. The cavernous room has a large dome-like ceiling with a substantial column that protrudes into the shadowy depths of the chasm. The unmistakable sounds of running water and a mist-filled breeze gush up from the shadows below. A large crevice in the southern wall leads into a small darkened chamber.

The path wraps around a limestone pillar that extends from the ceiling and into the shadowy abyss below. Near the southern wall, large cracks in the floor have filled with water and are illuminated by some unseen opening on the other side. An unreachable cenote beyond the southern wall can be seen through the water-filled cracks in the ground.

The sinuous passage winds from west to north as it delves deeper into the earth. Formations along the eastern wall leave plenty of space to walk. The floor of the cave is extremely worn and bears long grooves that disappear into the northwestern wall.

This area has been appropriated for military storage, and numerous weapons and suits of armor are propped up and ready for use.  A tall stained glass window, depicting a lone knight defeating an army of dragons, reaches from the stone floor almost all the way up to the ceiling high above.

A small glass window in the stone wall peers out of this storage room and into the main shop.  Crates and chests are filled with excess merchandise such as clothes and battle gear.  A single large wooden barrel appears to not belong to the shop, as it is marked with the Bal royal crest.

This is clearly a royal bedroom, but the amount of dust on the oversized bed indicates that no one has lived in it for some time.  A pair of small bookshelves holds a variety of literature, mostly fiction.  The royal bed is on a beautiful carpet.  Blue drapes hang over a window with tinted glass.

The entrance to the main castle structure is near the eastern side of the outer walls that surround the castle and courtyard.  The national banner hangs over the great doorway.  Engraved on the walkway at the foot of the door are these words: "Light will follow dawn."

Large, irregular stone tiles dot the worn grass of Bal Castle's plaza.  The western castle wall, which stretches alongside this open yard, is covered in small holes for archers to fire out through.  Among the carts and wares of merchants are a pair of out-of-place catapults, aimed south.

The local inn shares its space with a shop where one can buy healing items.  Ceramic tiles cover the floor.  Though this is actually a room inside the castle, the inn and item shop appear to be privately run businesses, with advertisements targetted at soldiers and travellers alike.

From this stone bridge, straddling the murky moat below, the scars in the stone bridge are a telltale sign of battles that have been fought before Bal Castle's front entrance.  The massive wooden gate, heavy and solid, looks like it would do a superb job of withstanding an attack.  Right now, though, the gateway is wide open.

From this height, the roaring wind of the Bal region can be felt at full strength, making it an ideal place for Bal Castle's wind drakes to take off from.  This balcony is quite a bit higher than the walls that surround the castle courtyard.  Harnesses and other riding equipment are scattered around.

A bookshelf on the wall contains old tomes, mostly about the history of the nation of Bal.  From the ceiling, an old globe hangs, with a map of an alien world.  From this corner, the hallway extends north to the stairs leading up and east to the stairs leading down.  A wooden door with a carving of a wind drake on it leads into a side room.

Several merchants have set up shop within this section of the castle, which is disconnected from the main castle building.  Weapons and armor are on display behind the counters.  An aisle treads between the merchant counters to a small utility staircase, leading up to some sort of back room.

The center of this circular tower room is dominated by three walls that surround a set of stone stairs, leaving the stairs only visible from the north.  The stairs lead down.  A large opening leads out from the south side of the tower to a large balcony.

Although the building below is a shopping center, it's also part of the castle.  As such, it's a little bit odd, but not totally unexpected, that the roof is being used by the castle guard as a lookout station.  A barricade and surveillance equipment have been set up to allow the soldiers on duty to discreetly watch the plaza below, and several harpoon guns are mounted on the edge of the roof in case there's trouble.

An archer's post is high above at the top of the great stone wall surrounding the Bal Castle courtyard.  A narrow ladder leads up to the post.  On the ground level, an open door leads into a section of Bal Castle's interior.  The main entrance into the castle proper is further east.

On the inner bank of the moat sleeps a ballista, waiting for a day when it can be used in battle.  The water weaves around the corner of the castle, guided by the brick sides of the trench.  Bal Castle's outer wall rises up majestically, a flag hanging from it.

The Bal Castle moat finishes its path around the castle and washes into a stream.  A metal gate in the water seperates the moat from the stream.  Several crates, having fallen into the moat, are jammed up against the gate.  The stream continues northeast into the distance, weaving through the forest.

This small storage area is connected to the shops below.  Various supplies such as mops, ladders and extra shelving are stacked on the floor, though there is no actual merchandise being stored in this room.  The staircase that comes up from the floor below also continues on up to the roof.

A blue carpet with gold and white patterns leads up to the raised platform atop which the throne of Bal Castle is perched.  The throne itself is brushed steel with royal blue cushions.  A great curtain covers most of the wall behind the throne.  Four massive pillars reach up to the vaulted ceiling, each carved with a different image of a warrior.

The main stone bridge into Bal Castle crosses above the moat, just a few feet overhead.  The crisp, clear water rushes past the bridge, weaving through the man-made trench which is lined with bricks on the sides and bottom.  The moat is at least 20 feet wide, making it a formidable obstacle to those who would dare assault the castle walls.

A thin mist, almost imperceptible, weighs down the air in these ruins.  Ornate stone pillars support the ceiling, carved with images of dragons and warriors, but several of the pillars have collapsed and now lie on the ground.  Holes in the floor and loose stones which have fallen from the ceiling make it necessary to tread carefully.

Intricate patterns have been carved into the stone walls, as well as the floor, but the passage of time has worn them down.  Two smaller pillars, still intact, mark the sides of a massive stone gateway.  In the gateway door, a picture has been carved beneath some writing, but the image has crumbled beyond recognizability and the writing is an unknown language.

Great, sharpened wooden spikes stick out from the muddy banks of the castle moat, deterring approach.  An unmanned ballista, set upon the inner bank of the moat, points out toward the forests.  The moat rushes around the corner of the castle walls, flowing through the path of the trench which is made up of underwater brick walls.

Within the great gates, on the threshold of majestic Bal Castle, towers a larger-than-life statue honoring the late King Galuf.  The mighty bronze monument stretches nearly to the ceiling of this closed entranceway.  To the north is the courtyard.

A pair of ornamental torches, shaped like the heads of drakes, hang over the large royal bed.  A writing desk, covered in a mess of barely legible papers, stands next to an antique wooden clothes dresser filled with expensive dresses.  An alcohol set is laid out on a small table with a white tablecloth.

A nearby stream has been diverted to create a moat which circles around Bal Castle.  The moat's importance to the castle's defenses is obvious, as it prevents the castle walls from being easily scalable.  Wooden spikes positioned strategically around the moat fortify the castle further.  There is also an underwater drain.

This underground room appears to be completely empty.  The walls are shaped oddly, making the small room take on the shape of a capital letter H.  Dust covers the empty shelves.  Whatever the room was intended for, it does not appear to have been used at all in some time.  The crumbling stone stairs lead further down.

Sandbags piled along the east side of this roof suggest that it is used by the castle military, and a pair of mounted harpoon launchers solidify the idea.  A trap door in the floor of the roof leads down into the building via ladder.  A utility ladder is mounted on the north outer wall of the building, but a merchant cart positioned at the bottom makes it unusable.

At the bottom of a ramp is a small stone pool of running water.  An open grate leads to a trench which allows the water to pass under the castle wall.  This appears to be the castle's main source of water.  An intruder might be able to covertly enter Bal Castle through this passage, as it appears to have no lock.

A spiral staircase ascends from this side corridor up to the third floor.  At the foot of the staircase are two bronze statues of dragons, as though standing guard over the chambers above.  The stone walls are decorated with several paintings.  Two glass windows look out upon the northern woodlands.

This raised lookout platform is high enough to be able to see over the castle walls of Bal Castle.  Stockpiles of arrows are sitting in wooden holders which are firmly attached to the castle wall.  There is also an alarm, ready to be sounded in case of an attack.

The grand hall of Bal Castle is enormous, with grand stone pillars supporting a ceiling that must be at least 40 meters high.  Royal banners hang from the ceiling, depicting a dragon above a rising sun.  A large stone stairway in the center of the hall leads up to the throne room.

A circular stone walkway is the centerpiece of Bal Castle's main courtyard.  Narrower stone paths lead north and south out from the circle, the stones adorned with the same tiled pattern that grants some stability to this busy castle's courtyard.  From the grass gaze a pair of stone gargoyle monuments, watching over the castle's gate to the south.  Stairs to the north lead up to a lookout post.

For such a grand castle, this hallway is rather sparsely decorated.  Three stone pillars are in the center of the hallway, dividing it into two sections.  Aside from the pillars, the only form of decoration is a single shield and spear hanging on the wall outside of a doorway.  A long spiral staircase descends to the floor below.

This narrow corridor leads between the royal bedrooms to a set of stairs leading up to the top floor.  There is no room for decorations in this tight hallway; it's barely wide enough for one person to walk through comfortably.  The stairs leading up are constructed of solid stone.

A freshwater pool occupies fully half of the large terrace. The pool is the primary source of water for the entire town of Jachol. To the north, there is another shop next to a small set of steps into the pool. A slender alley between two buildings leads to the south end of the town, while stone stairs leads up to the merchant's terrace.

A boldly ornate carpet, with a gilded border, spans the distance from the shop entrance to the counter. A large number of weapon racks are organized behind the counter. The twin white swords painted on the back wall mark this as a place to buy weapons. A plump man in a bright blue outfit is hanging out behind the counter, waiting to serve the next patron. Jachol's armor vendor resides to the east.

The acrid smell of chemicals permeates throughout the little shop. Multiple vats of marinating chemical compounds are arranged behind the long wooden counter. While called a magic shop, the small store in Jachol hasn't sold magic since the worlds merged. Now they sell various explosives, which explains the acrid smell.

This large lot is the only entrance to the town of Jachol. Enticing odors emanate from the expansive building that sits on the northern edge of the lot. A sign on the second floor marks this building as an inn. To the east a small bridge, spanning the stream that cuts through Jachol, leads to the rest of town.

The large patio is its own stand-alone terrace. The patio wraps around the western side of the inn allowing patrons of the inn the opportunity to get some fresh air without the hustle and bustle of the street below. A collection of barrels and crates occupy a portion of the patio.

The door to the weapons merchant is aligned perfectly with the stairs to the lower terrace. The bold wooden sign makes it improbable that anyone coming up the stairs could fail to notice the shop. A stone banister on the western edge of the merchant's terrace provides an excellent view of the area below.

Two buildings, separated by a slender alley, are built into the brick wall of a higher terrace. A wooden sign posted next to the front door marks the building on the east as the local item shop. Jachol's stream flows along the western side of the terrace.

A border of stone pavers frames the large pool. A stone grate on the southern edge funnels excess water into a stream while preventing larger items from being swept away.  The townsfolk utilize this pool for their day to day needs, while the children tend to use it for more recreational purposes. A short set of stairs in the northwestern corner allows people to get in and out of the pool easily.

The corner of the terrace offers an uninterrupted view of the mountains to the east. The rise Jachol is built on is particularly steep from this vantage which only amplifies the view. To the north a set of stairs leads to the merchant's terrace.

The upstairs of the inn has five beds arranged for comfortable rest on the eastern end of the room. Four chairs surround a dining table, and several dining sets are stored in a large cabinet on the western end of the room. There is a door on the southern wall leading out to a patio.

The grassy hillside rises up nearly level with the merchant's terrace. A tall building made of white bricks has a wooden sign out front marking it as the armorer's establishment. Another door on the same building to the west has a similar sign claiming it as the weapons vendor. The stairs to the south connect to the pub terrace.

The building on the northern edge of the terrace, marked as the magic shop by the sign in front, is no exception to the fine craftsmanship found throughout Jachol. The white, brick building is all straight lines and sharp edges, yet manages to not look out of place next to the pool. A set of stairs built onto the side of the shop lead to the top of the town fountain.
A man of Jachol is idling about.

Jachol cleverly captured a natural spring into a fountain which flows into two pools before getting funneled down the hillside as a small stream. The end result is a pool at the top for potable water, a lower pool for daily chores, and a lovely stream to wash the residue away. This small platform allows access to the upper pool.

The pub is a bustling place where people are gathered for food, drink, and entertainment. There is a rather rotund man behind a counter on the western side taking orders and serving food. A pretty girl with blue hair is dancing on a stage that fills the eastern end of the pub. Between the bar and the stage is a mismatched collection of tables and chairs for patrons.

A boldly ornate carpet, with a gilded border, spans the distance from the shop entrance to the counter. Behind the counter an organized assortment of crates contains various pieces of inventory. The white shield painted onto the back wall indicates this is a place to buy armor. A plump man in a bright blue outfit is hanging out behind the counter, waiting to serve the next patron. Jachol's weapons vendor resides to the west.

The main room of the inn is a simple room. Stone floors and white plaster walls are all well-lit by lamps mounted on the walls. A friendly looking innkeeper is sitting behind the counter waiting for customers. There is a door leading further into the inn.

The smooth stone cobbles that form this terrace are comfortable to walk on. The town's stream flows along the southern border of this terrace. To the north, there appears to be an item shop. To the east, there is a set of stairs that go up to another terrace.

Behind the counter is a distracted shopkeeper is busy sorting through a stack of wooden crates. A large sign with a painted potion bottle is hung on the wall next to the counter. Loud music and laughter are coming from the top of the stairs on the eastern side of the room.

A large piano with odd tubes springing out of the back is placed against the northern wall, leaving the majority of the stage for performers. Currently, there is a very pretty girl with blue hair dancing for the gathered pub crowd. A set of stairs to the south would make for a quick exit.

An artificial waterfall cascades down a stone facade to fill a small pool with cold, fresh water. Jachol is practically built around the, apparently limitless, supply fresh water. The stones that surround this pool have a small gap along the southern edge allowing the overflow to drain into the pool below. Anyone in this pool is advised to stay from gap lest they be dragged over by the current.

The library is fairly small, consisting of but a few bookshelves.  Two tables sit in the south part of the room, and a stool sits below one of the bookshelves for ease of selection.  To the north, a staircase leads up to the main chamber, while to the south a door leads out.

This chamber is filled almost entirely by a large table.  On the table, a candle, a book, and a few flasks sit.  To the west of the table, on a smaller table, an athame sits. A few small piles of wood sit around the table.  To the south, a staircase leads down to the library.  To the north, a door leads to a ritual area.

The wall splits, allowing passage into the courtyard.  The edges of the walls are smooth, indicating that the breach was meant to be there.  A few stones are scattered around the ledge, but not so many that movement is impeded.  Southwards, the ledge follows the outside of the walls.  To the west, the courtyard opens.

The walkway ends, going no further west.  A deep pit opens to the northeast.  To the north, a short staircase leads up to another walkway.  To the east, this walkway continues a short distance, then turns north at another staircase.  A third staircase leads up and to the south from the center of this walkway.

The great gate of Elinee's Castle stands open.  The castle walls are smooth beyond the skill of human hands.  The ramparts of the castle are high above the ground.  To the east and west, a ledge follows the castle walls around the corners, while to the south a small peninsula of land juts away from the castle.  To the north, the gate opens onto a courtyard within the walls.

This room is little more than a closet.  The floor and walls are uncovered, and the only thing of worth in it is a table along the north wall.  A clock sits on the table, and a few chairs sit in front of it.  To the south, a door leads out of this room.

The path runs through the center of the courtyard, east to west. To the south, the main gate of the castle is visible across a chasm in the ground.  Northwards, the door to the castle sits in the center of the main building.  To the east and west, the path continues toward identical breaches in the wall.

The hallway splits into two parts.  The floor is clear, but a sealed window adorns the northern wall.  Further to the west, a section of wall appears to have been drawn back to allow passage.  To the north, the hallway leads around a corner, eventually turning west, while to the west the hallway continues to a turn, from which it goes north.

This part of the landing is home to a switch, long since made useless.  Far to the north, the wall is home to a door.  Around the room, three walkways span a deep pit.  Two windows in the north wall admit some light to the room.  Just to the south, a staircase leads downwards.  To the west, the landing continues to the end of a walkway, while northward lies another walkway, leading to a door.

The path leads to the corner of the courtyard.  Far to the south, the castle gate is just visible.  The courtyard stretches away to the south and east, to the castle walls in the distance.  The path leads away south through the courtyard and east towards the castle door.

The ledge takes a turn, following the castle walls.  The walls reach high above the ledge, their smooth craftsmanship clearly visible.  To the east, the ledge follows the wall past the front gate, while to the north it narrows considerably as it follows the western wall of the castle.

The jail opens eastward, continuing a short distance before ending at a gray stone wall.  The entire jail is quiet and dark, due to a lack of prisoners and the fact that little to no light reaches it.  Two cells stand open along the northern wall of the jail, while to the east a hallway links them.

A narrow walkway lines a deep pit.  To the north, another walkway is visible.  The stonework around the edges of the pit is exquisite.  To the east and west, the walkway continues away, while to the south a staircase leads back out of the castle.

The hall turns a corner.  The wall to the north is home to a sealed window, while the walls to the south and west are quite smooth.  The floor is clear.  Just to the east, a section of wall appears to have been drawn back to allow passage through.  To the east, the hall leads around a corner, while to the north it leads to a door.

The cell is small, only a couple of paces across.  The floor is clear.  The walls are unadorned, except for a set of shackles.  The cell is extremely dark, owing to the depth of this part of the castle.  To the south, the door out of the cell stands open.

rooms.name: East end of the northern walkway

userData.LongDescription: The walkway on this side of the pit is slightly higher than the one to the south.  Far below, the pit disappears into darkness.  The walkway continues no further to the east, but to the north there is a gate, while to the south a short staircase leads across the pit to the opposite walkway.

The cell is small, only a few feet across.  The door out stands open.  The walls are unadorned, and nothing sits on the floor.  Very little light reaches this cell, making it quite dark.  To the south, a door leads to the main hallway of the dungeon.

This room acts as a foyer for the rooms further within the castle.  Three large pillars intersect the room at regular intervals.  The floor and walls are unadorned.  The north wall is punctuated with three doors.  To the south, a short passage leads to another door.

This room is set up like an arena.  The floor is stained with the blood of previous victims.  Two pillars rise, one to either side of the room, about halfway to the ceiling.  A huge metal gate in the north wall stands closed.  To the south, a door heralds the way out.

Just south of the castle of the witch Elinee, the ground is fairly clear.  It is possible to see the smooth, grey stone walls of the castle itself.  The main gate stands directly in the middle of the front wall.  The gate stands open, and appears to have stood thus for many years.  A small outcropping of land is home to a portal back into the forest.

This room serves as a storage room.  A small wooden table sits against the northern wall, surrounded by a few chairs.  A single clock ticks away on the table.  The floor is uncovered, and the walls are plain.  Back to the south, a  doorway leads to another part of the castle.

The walls loom high above the ledge. Their craftsmanship is remarkable.  A solitary stone sits on the ledge, a few feet from the wall.  The ledge is fairly narrow, as it leads away to the north, but widens further along.  To the west, it passes in front of the main gate of the castle.

The landing juts out from the south wall of the room, and is the terminus for two walkways.  Across the pit to the north, two windows and a door are visible.  Directly northward, a walkway leads to the northern landing, while to the west the landing leads to another walkway as well as a staircase.

rooms.name: Western end of the northern walkway

userData.LongDescription: The walkway on the northern edge of the pit is slightly higher than the one to the south.  Far below the walkway, the pit fades away into darkness.  The walkway ends at the wall to the west, while to the north there is a gate.  A short staircase leads southward across the pit. To the east, this walkway continues a short distance.

The jail continues no further.  The stone wall to the east heralds the end of the area.  This end of the hallway is quite dark.  To the north, a cell stands open, void of any inhabitant.  To the west, the hallway leads out of the jail to other parts of the castle.

A small room sits between the entrance hall and the deeper parts of the castle.  A small table sits in the center of the room, surrounded by a few chairs.  To the north, a staircase leads down, deeper into the castle, while to the south a door leads towards the exit.

The wall has an opening large enough to allow travel through to the courtyard inside.  Unfortunately, a few well placed flagstones prevent passage through it.  The walls continue to the north and south, but the ledge tapers off just north of the breach.

The inside of the castle is quite drab.  Plain stone floors, unadorned walls, unimaginative architecture are all that greet the eye here.  The only breaks to the monotony are two pillars set into the wall, and an old switch set into the floor.  To the north, a gateway leads deeper within the castle, while to the south a door leads outside.

The northern landing holds up the two walkways going away to the south.  On the north wall, a window looks out on the forest.  A pair of pillars adorns the wall alongside the window.  To the west, the landing continues to another walkway leading south, while to the south a walkway leads away to an exit from the room.

The hallway takes a turn.  The north wall is broken by a pair of windows, while to the east the wall is smooth.  The floor is covered only by a light layer of dust.  Westward, the hall stops a short distance away, while to the south it leads away and around a corner.

The hall continues no further.  The walls are plain, and the floor is clear.  A single, deep crack runs across the floor.  The only other thing of note is the door, leading to the chamber of Elinee, and the hallway leading away to the south and around a corner.

The walkway ends at a door.  To the south and east, the room stretches away, continuing some distance before ending at the walls of the room.  The north wall is broken by a few pillars and two windows.  Three walkways cross the room, over a deep pit.  Directly south lies a walkway to a staircase, while to the north a door sits in the wall.

The room ends at the western wall.  The walls are plain, uncovered by any decoreation.  The stone floor is covered only by a thin layer of dust.  Just north, a door leads deeper withing the castle.  Eastwards, the room continues away.

A walkway leads north into this room.  The walkway leads across a deep pit.  The room opens to the northwest, and is crossed several times by walkways.  Far to the northwest, a door leads out of the room, while to the north the walkway leads to a landing on the northern wall.  To the south, a gateway leads to another part of the castle.

The room goes no further east.  The walls are uncovered, and the stone floor is covered only by a thin layer of dust.  Directly to the north, a door leads further within the castle, while to the west the room continues a short distance.

The landing along the north wall supports a pair of walkways southward.  The north wall itself is home to a window overlooking the Haunted Forest outside.  A pillar sits to either side of the window.  To the east, this landing continues a short distance, while to the south, a walkway leads across the pit.

The center of the northern wall of the castle is home to the castle entrance.  A short flight of stairs leads up to the door.  Two stones have been placed on the ground, directly north of either side of the main gate, far to the south.  A set of double doors, set into an archway on the wall, leads into the castle.  To the west, a path leads through the courtyard.

This room is quite small and quite empty.  The floor is clear, the walls are bare, not a single object can be seen.  Three paces wide, three paces deep, it is all full of nothing.  A door is the only thing to see, and that leads to another part of the castle, as bleak as this.

The walkway ends, going no further east.  A deep pit opens to the northwest.  To the north, a short staircase leads up to another walkway.  To the west, this walkway continues a short distance, then turns north at another staircase.  A third staircase leads up and to the south from the center of this walkway.

A narrow passage leads from a door in the south wall to a room to the north.  The walls are plain, and the floor is clean.  To the north, the passage continues a short distance to a room, while to the south a door leads to another part of the castle.

The basement of the castle is the entrance to the dungeon.  There is very little light in this area, adding to the inhospitable atmosphere.  To the east, two large cells stand open.  The cells are empty now, but once held many prisoners.  To the north, a staircase leads up and out of the dungeon.

The hall goes no further.  The wall to the north is broken by a window.  The other walls are smooth and without fault.  The floor is clear except for a switch embedded in the stone floor.  To the east, the hallway disappears around a corner.

The path through the courtyard ends at a breach in the wall.  The breach is impassible, as several large stones have been placed across it. To the north and south, the castle walls stretch away, enclosing the area.  Far to the east, another breach is visible in the wall.  To the north, the path follows the inside of the wall.

This room is quite small, acting only as a passage from the entrance to the rest of the castle.  A large crack runs down the east wall, showing the age of the castle.  A pillar stands to either side of a door to the north, while to the south, a gate leads toward the door.

The library is small, but there are still plenty of books to be found. There are four separate bookshelves, each with two sides that are filled with books. The shelves stand upon a large rug that covers the floor. There are a few small tables at which visitors can sit and enjoy one of the books. There is a sign attached to the eastern wall of the library.

This is a very cozy-looking room. A rug exactly like the one in the main lobby is laid on the floor, upon which sit six single beds. A small table sits in the room. A brick fireplace has been placed in the room, providing it with ample heat. There are a couple of pictures and small bookshelves that help add some decoration to the room.

This home is small and cozy. To the west there is a room with a bed, a small desk, a small bookcase and a brick fireplace. The main part of the home has a small table with four chairs around it, a display case, and a piano in the northeast corner. A rug covers the ground, and a couple of barrels stand near the front door.
