The Crescent Inn looks rather busy. Just to the west of the front door is a large ornate rug upon which five circular tables sit. Each table is covered in a fine white cloth and has a small vase with a red flower inside of it. The inn's check-in desk stands to the north end of the room, and a door stands to the west of the counter.

The area here looks to be some kind of community garden. Many different plants are growing, separated into four sections. The paths in the middle provide easy access to all sides of the garden. Pine trees dot the land near the garden and provide a thick wall toward the east.

The center of town is wide open and seems very big. The stone ground spans nearly the entire area. The main focus of this area is a large, square fountain, its walls made of large grey stones. It has two layers: the main base which sits on the ground and a smaller section higher up in the middle which has a stem that spills water over itself.

The area here is mostly laid with stone, but is grassy toward the west. Tall pine trees stand to the west providing a makeshift wall while oak trees dot the area. A large building stands toward to the north end of the area, lined to the west with overgrown shrubs.

The shop is small and cozy, and looks much smaller than the building might indicate from the outside. A large counter stands toward the back of the shop. The floor looks to be made of stone, but a wooden platform has been crafted to cover it almost entirely. It has three steps that lead up to it. There is an open doorway behind the counter, with two large signs depicting crossing swords hanging on either side.

A large building stands toward the northern end of the area. Grass grows all around and the ground is littered with shrubs and pine trees. The building looks new, but the sign outside of it shows its age. Part of the ground, mostly toward the west and southwest of the area, is covered by stone.

The area here is mostly grass, with a little bit of stone ground toward the southeastern section.  Large amounts of shrubs and oak trees can be seen to the very northwest. Pine trees stand thickly to the west and north, providing a natural wall to the town. A large building stands here with a sign on the outside of it.

Grass covers the ground entirely.  Pine trees stand densely towards the south end of town, but also randomly dot the grassy land. Two houses stand to the west and east of this area, but only the one to the east seems to have a visible entrance.

Three large oak trees form a semi-circle on each side of a stone path that leads toward the entrance of town. Grass covers the ground anywhere that stone has not been laid.  Various shrubs and flowers grow amidst the grass. Pine trees surround the town but also randomly spring up inside town as well. A large building stands just a short walk northwest from the entrance of the town.

This shop appears to sell items, judging from the various vials and such found on the shelves behind the counter. The floor is made out of smooth stone that has been painted to look like tiny rocks. There are flower pots standing on the corners of the counter, and a couple of crates are stacked by the back wall.

The shop is small and cozy. The floor is made out of smooth stone that has been painted to look like tiny rocks. There are barrels and crates stacked in the northeast corner, and a counter stands to the northwest. Behind the counter can be seen a few pots and crates, as well as an open doorway.

Eight stone-faced columns, spaced evenly around a larger support pillar at the center of a symmetrical icosioctagonal room, hold up the mighty tower.  There is no obvious path towards ascension, but perhaps an investigation can reveal the tower's secrets.

Four stone-faced columns, linearly spaced in pairs on either side of a central support pillar at the center of a symmetrical icosioctagonal room, hold up the mighty tower.  Staircases within the pillar allow traversal of the tower: down from the northern face, up from the southern.

Four stone-faced columns, linearly spaced in pairs on either side of a larger central support pillar at the center of a symmetrical icosioctagonal room, hold up the mighty tower.  There is no obvious path towards ascension, but perhaps an investigation can reveal the tower's secrets.

Two stone-faced columns standing astride a central support pillar at the center of a symmetrical icosioctagonal room hold up the mighty tower.  There is no obvious path towards ascension, but perhaps an investigation can reveal the tower's secrets.

Four stone-faced columns, linearly spaced in pairs on either side of a central support pillar at the center of a symmetrical icosioctagonal room, hold up the mighty tower.  Staircases within the pillar allow traversal of the tower: down from the northern face, up from the southern.

Two stone-faced columns standing astride a central support pillar at the center of a symmetrical icosioctagonal room hold up the mighty tower.  There is no obvious path towards ascension, but perhaps an investigation can reveal the tower's secrets.

Two stone-faced columns standing astride a larger central support pillar at the center of a symmetrical icosioctagonal room hold up the mighty tower.  There is no obvious path towards ascension, but perhaps an investigation can reveal the tower's secrets.

Four stone-faced columns, linearly spaced in pairs on either side of a larger central support pillar at the center of a symmetrical icosioctagonal room, hold up the mighty tower.  There is no obvious path towards ascension, but perhaps an investigation can reveal the tower's secrets.

Six stone-faced columns, forming center-pointing isoceles triangles on either side of a central support pillar at the center of a symmetrical icosioctagonal room, hold up the mighty tower.  Staircases within the pillar allow traversal of the tower: down from the northern face, up from the southern.

rooms.name: Chamber of the Sealed Weapons - Southwest Corner

userData.LongDescription: This is the southwest corner of the ancient armory of the castle of Kuzar, where monuments of a different time have been abandoned. The pillars around here have been turned into shrines of some sort, with red carpeted steps and a small glass pane embedded into the pillar. Some broken stained-glass windows on the west side of the room let some bright light in. Towards the center of the room, a large pillar rises high, arcing out to the edges of the room.

The floor in the hall here is beginning to crumble, leaving deep holes in the concrete path. In the alcove in the wall to the east, piles of suits of armor and large racks of weapons are stored. A broken torch rests in the sconce on the west wall, which possibly explains why the room is so dark. Far to the north, a staircase can vaguely be made out at the end of the hallway. To the south, the open doorway to the grand hall lets in the very little amount of light there is.

rooms.name: Chamber of the Sealed Weapons - Southeast Corner

userData.LongDescription: This is the southeast corner of the ancient armory of the castle of Kuzar where some ancient shrines have fallen out of use. The shrines have ornate red carpeting over a pair of steps that lead up to a glass pane embedded on a pillar. Some stained-glass windows on the east side of the room let some colored light in. Towards the center of the room, a large pillar rises high, arcing out to the edges of the room.

This hallway is poorly lit and not very wide. Racks of armor and crates of spears are lined up against the east wall, stored inside little arch-shaped crevices. The great hall lies to the south, and most of the light in this hallway is emanating from the entrance in that direction.

The walls inside the Grand Hall come to a sharp corner, thus extending northward and eastward. The ornate rug stretches out almost completely to the wall but leaves a bit of space for some of the stone floor to show through. High along the walls, openings let a few beams of light in, which scarcely illuminate the area.

This end of the Grand Hall of Kuzar shows signs of age, including cobwebs and cracks in the wall. The stone floor is also cracking underneath the ornate, yet dull red rug. Windows high against the wall let scattered beams of light filter through the room. The hallway expands northward, eastward, southward, as well as to the northeast and southeast.

The ground begins to shift upward slightly, leading to a stairwell connected to a large wooden door at the north end of the hallway. Attached to the ceiling is a candelabra filled with unlit candles and burnt, stubby wicks. The way south leads back to the small armory and the great hall of Kuzar, the light from which has long since faded.

rooms.name: Chamber of the Sealed Weapons - Northeast Corner

userData.LongDescription: This is the northeast corner of the ancient armory of the castle of Kuzar, where some empty, ruined shrines lay untouched. There are some rather large cracks in the tiled floor here, as well as in the stone walls. Some stained-glass windows on the east side of the room let some colored light in. Towards the center of the room, a large pillar rises high, arcing out to the edges of the room.

The entryway into the sealed castle is adorned with large stone pillars on either side of a towering, ancient staircase that leads to a dull wooden door with a heavy-set locking mechanism. High along the walls, open windows let sunlight into the hallway as well as a slight breeze that stirs the dust in the air. Another, larger, heavy-set door on the south wall separates the castle from the outside world.

This side of the grand hall is fairly well-kept, minus the excessive dust over the floor, the rug and the walls. Even more dust sifts through the air, occasionally being illuminated by a faint ray of light emanating from a small window high in the wall on the east side.

A flat, faded carpet with baroque ornamentation stretches out over the stone floor of the Grand Hall of Kuzar. This spacious hallway stretches out to various directions due to its size. The ceiling is decrepit and covered with cobwebs, and unlit candles are lined up at the top of towering pillars that stretch to the ceiling from the ground. The door to the south is slightly tattered, yet its large size still conveys its protective design.

The ground here is raised on a platform in a circle around the entrance, which is fixed in a large pillar in the center of a gigantic empty room. Just out in front of the doorway is a small, raised panel that seems to glisten in the darkness. A small staircase leads off of the platform and onto a tan-colored tile floor. All around the room are shrines with glass panels in the back.

rooms.name: Chamber of the Sealed Weapons - Northwest Corner

userData.LongDescription: This is the northwest corner of the ancient armory of the castle of Kuzar, where antiquated shrines continue to age in silence. The shrines themselves are led to with ornate, red carpeted steps and a small glass pane embedded into the pillar. Some broken stained-glass windows on the west side of the room let some bright light in. There are a few shards of broken glass close to the wall. Towards the center of the room, a large pillar rises high, arcing out to the edges of the room.

A hallway entrance remains ajar on the north wall. One of the doors on the entrance appears to be broken off of its hinges. To the south, past a few pillars, large double doors lead to the exit of the castle. The rug on the ground is a faded shade of red, and the edges of it are tattered and shredded.

This is the northwestern corner of the grand hall. The north wall is covered in glass windows that stretch to the ceiling. High along the west wall, a small arched window lets a small shaft of light in. The faded red carpet comes to a tattered end against the corner of the castle.

This section of the large hall is crumbling slightly because of the immense amount of time the castle has been standing. The red rug makes its appearance at this end of the hall as well, covering most of the cracks in the stone floor. To the north, a paneled glass covered wall looms.

The northeastern corner of the great hall is dusty and slightly more dark than the rest of the great hall. On the east wall there is a collapsed passageway filled with rubble. The pillar that holds the ceiling up is deteriorating and cracked, more so than the others in the hall. To the west there is a passageway leading north.

The center of the grand hall exhibits its grandiose structure effectively. The ceiling peaks above the center of the room, and the red rug that covers the floor is most worn along a line going from the north to the south. Tall, spiraling columns hold the weight of the castle up high at well placed points between the center of the hall and the far corners.

The item shop lobby is almost entirely covered by a large, rectangular rug.  The counter seals off the item shop's owner from any physical contact.  Three wooden stools are before the counter to allow customers to wait when they place their orders.  Behind the counter, there are a number of barrels and pots containing the various wares of the item shop.  There is a staircase that leads to the upper floor, where the weapon and armor shops are located.

Lix is a small town hidden within a forest that is at the northern edge of the Tule continent. The trees are divided by a narrow grassy path to mark the way leading north into the town.  Towards the west is the inn, and to the east leads to the magic shop.

In front of the house, there is a display of shrubs and flowers that have been lovingly cared for.  A house plant resides in the window of the western side of the house.  To the west, there is a path that leads into the forest; the southern direction goes towards the inn.

The exterior of the inn is richly decorated with vegetation.  A wide variety of flowers can be seen along the walls of the building, and shrubs that have been meticulously cared for are near the wooden door.  The entrance of Lix is to the east, and there is a house to the north.

A warm fire inside a brick fireplace is crackling away.  Bookcases and display shelves are lined along the northern side of the room.  The books are filled with information about the world outside the isolated village of Lix.  A dining set is readily available for a hungry adventurer at the southeast corner of the room.  There is a room entryway between the bookcases and display shelves that leads to a wooden desk.

The tallest building in Lix is in this corner of town, standing three stories in height.  The building overlooks the magic shop to the south, but a cliff denies passage. The town center can be seen to the west, and the shops can be seen to the northwest.

The grassy ground forms into an incline, forming a hill which a building sits upon.  There is a wooden sign plunged into the ground on the right side of the magic shop.  The sign has the shape of a staff on it.  The inn can be seen to the west, and the town center can be seen to the northwest.

At the entrance of the magic shop, there is a vibrantly colored rug displaying many shades of red and orange.  A pot can be seen at the southwestern side of the room, containing a large quantity of wine.  A dining set sits on the east side of the room.  Along the north wall lie a bookcase, desk, and a fireplace.

A large building sits on a hill overlooking the town center to the south.  On the front of the building, there are three wooden signs.  The first sign is a picture of a sword, the second sign is a picture of a shield and the third sign is a picture of a potion.

In the middle of the forest, there is a tombstone erected from the ground.  The tombstone is surrounded by pink wild flowers and has an inscription on it.  The eastern path leads back into the town of Lix.

In the center of the room, there is a dining table surrounded by four wooden stools; all of these stand upon a colorful rug.  Along the northern wall, there are many objects including a fireplace, a desk, a bookshelf, a wooden table and a stove.  On the east side, there is a bouquet of flowers and a ceramic pot.  To the west, there is a neatly made bed.

In front of the staircase, there is an opened, empty storage box.  Next to the storage box is a barrel of metal that is to be shaped into weapons and armor.  The south part of the room has a large display rack of spears.  A large wooden counter goes through the center of the room, separating two shop keepers from the eastern side.  Behind the counter and along the western wall, there are bookshelves, display cases and crates.

In the middle of the town, a pond can be seen.  Many flowers surround the pond, emitting a peaceful atmosphere that the town of Lix has always known.  Every building in Lix can be seen from this location.  The item and equipment shops are to the north, the inn to the southwest and the magic shop towards the southeast.

There is a well in front of the house which goes deeper than light can reach.  The house strangely has no visible entrance other than the two windows in front.  To the east, the item and armor shops can be seen, and another house can be seen to the south.

The sound of water lapping gently at the walls fills this small room. The floor ends before the base of the walls, and a moat-like waterway takes up the rest of the ground. Carved pillars support the roof, though some of them are covered in vines and look fairly unstable.

This narrow, dank end of the room at first appears to be a dead-end. However, the other side of a small structure built in the middle of the floor turns out to have an opening onto a staircase leading to the shrine's upper floors. Pillars covered in twisted vines stand to either side of the stairwell entry while two more support the stone ceiling further to the south.

Vines twist and stretch their way up the back wall of this small room. The floor is covered in a mix of dust and dead, dried leaves, but the air is too still to rustle the leaves or stir up the dust. Strange sounds occasionally invade the otherwise silent room.

The stairs open into a small entry room to the Wind Crystal itself. Tall double doors guard the Wind Crystal and its altar room. Unlike those on the previous floors, the doors are made of pure white marble. The room is completely silent, casting into doubt whether there is anything alive beyond this point.

At the top of the stairs is a small room. There is no way out but back down the stairs. The floor is still dusty, the air still, and the sense of approaching danger undiminished, but the silence is occasionally broken by strange sounds somewhere to the northwest.

The walls of the fourth floor of the Wind Shrine are barely visible beneath the mass of vines that has grown up the stones. The floors are covered with dust and leaves, making it difficult to tell where the footprints lead from here. The room extends further to the southeast and southwest. The stairs lead back down to the third floor.

The suffocating darkness closes in on all sides, preventing anything from moving too quickly through the passage. The strange sounds begin to take the form of scraping mixed with an occasional leathery flapping. The light seems to increase farther down the southeastern end of the hall.

Light from the large room just to the west makes seeing in this part of the tunnel much easier than to the northwest. A door in the north wall leads into a small room. To the northwest, the passage heads off into a shroud of darkness, but to the west it ends in a well-lit room. The squawking, scraping, and flapping noises seem to be coming from the room just to the west.

The walls of the easternmost quarter of the room are covered in more vines, almost completely covering the grey stones. The decaying, dry leaves mixed with a thick layer of dust make it difficult to discern any footprints on the floor. The stairs down are to the northwest. To the southwest is the far side of the central stairwell.

The sense of peace and safety that pervades the still air of this room is a sharp contrast to the uneasy atmosphere in the rest of the Wind Shrine. A soft glow, purple in color, illuminates the room to a degree that is much easier to see by than the dim, murky light found elsewhere. The doors to the north and south are heavy and secure. This room is the perfect resting place.

Grey stone walls darken as they reach the damp floor of this wide open room. A passage fades into darkness to the east. There is a large, ornate set of doors leading to the northern stairway and another smaller door to the northwest. The air here is deathly still and any chill felt is not from the cool, damp atmosphere alone.

The stairs open into a small room which quickly narrows into a tight passageway along the western side of the Wind Shrine.  The faint noises from the east worsen the almost overwhelming sense of fear and dread that fills this place. The grey stone walls suddenly do not seem like enough protection against whatever terrible thing is making those sounds. The passage continues to the northeast in near-darkness.

A cool breeze carrying the scent of the forest blows in through the small stone entry room to the wind shrine. The walls are composed of large stone blocks, some of which are cracked and chipped, making evident the deterioration of the building's condition. A large set of double doors stands to the north, leading deeper into the wind shrine. The large oak door on the south wall leads out into the wilderness.

The air here is musty and the floor covered in heavy dust. A small structure made of the same grey stone as the walls has a doorway in it that opens onto a stairway going up. Flanked by pillars that are decorated with the same cruel-faced gargoyles as below, the doorway is a forbidding sight. The passage continues to the southwest, back towards the safe room and the trail of footsteps. The heavy silence is punctuated only by a growing feeling of dread.

There is not much in this small room. The only way out is the door to the south. The dusty floor shows no recognizable footprints and the air is quiet and still. The silence is broken once in a while by strange sounds from the west.

The doorway to the north is flanked by heavy stone columns. Their gargoyle-like faces stare maliciously at the blank space just in front of them, daring anyone to walk past. The room extends to the northwest and northeast, but both ends are lost to the deepening shadow. A faint glow escapes the under the door of the room to the north. The dust on the floor is thick and undisturbed but for the faint outline of footsteps heading to the northwest.

Unlike the fear and dread that pervade the rest of the Wind Shrine, the turbulent air in this room seems to move with an overwhelming feeling of power. The vine-enshrouded altar in the center of the room is empty, as the crystal it was meant to guard has shattered, but a strange energy emanates from it nonetheless. Tall marble columns line the walls of the room, silent witnesses to the events that have taken place here. A faint glow is coming from behind the altar.

The corners of this room, including the way out to the southeast, are lost in shadow. The thick dust covering the floor is the only decoration in the otherwise bare room. Oppressive silence lays its heavy hand over the area, making talking in anything above a whisper seem horribly loud and out of place. A door leads to the south, and the passage also extends into the darkness to both the southeast and southwest.

The western part of the room seems to curve around a central structure, perhaps another stairwell. Vines provide welcome relief from the plain grey stone of the walls on which they grow. Dust and dried leaves that have fallen from the vines litter the floor, making it difficult to tell if anyone has come this way. The room continues to the northeast and southeast.

A door to the southwest and a passage to the southeast are visible in the dim light of the murky shrine. Voices echo through the long room; they seem to be coming from the southwestern door. A few pillars line each side of the door to the south, which leads out of the Wind Shrine. The faces carved into the pillars seem to leer threateningly despite the fact that they are merely stone.

The musty air is heavy with dust. The grey stone walls are dark and damp at their bases, lightening in color as they reach towards the ceiling. To the northwest, the passage continues to lead deeper into the shrine. The air is eerily still, seemingly heavy with dread and fear. No sound can be heard from anywhere, as even footsteps are greatly hushed by the stillness of the air and the thick layer of dust.

This heavily shadowed passage is a dead-end. The cold, grey stone walls close in three sides of the room, leaving the passage back to the southeast as the only way out. Even in this enclosed area, silence mixes with a chill sense of dread in the deathly still air. Any sound at all would be better than this eerie lack of noise.

An opening to the north leads into the stairwell in the center of this large, round room. The trail of footprints begins again at the base of the stairs and then ascends them to the next floor. The room circles around the central stairwell to the northeast and northwest.

Another stairwell, much like those on the floors above and below, provides access to the third floor. Ornate stone pillars stand to either side of the doorway like guardians. Their carved faces, ugly and cruel, give pause to those thinking to ascend the stair. The room continues to the southeast, but the trail of footsteps is clear as it heads up the stairs.

Tall, ornately carved stone pillars line the walls of this diamond-shaped room. A door in the north wall leads further into the dimly lit shrine. Light floods in through the door to the south, showing the way out and making the carvings on the pillars shift and move in an eerie play of light and shadow.

The sun shines brightly in the sky, making the dry heat of the desert feel oppressive.  A gentle breeze blows sand across the dunes of the desert, but fails to provide relief from the blistering light of the sun in any way.  The desert spreads in all directions, meeting mountains in the distance on all sides. The faint sound of a waterfall can be heard in the distance.

The sun shines brightly in the sky, making the dry heat of the desert feel oppressive.  A gentle breeze blows sand across the dunes of the desert, but fails to provide relief from the blistering light of the sun in any way.  The desert spreads in all directions, meeting mountains in the distance on all sides. The faint sound of a waterfall can be heard in the distance.

The sight of the Istory waterfalls is truly a sight to behold. The river above expands as it nears the falls, lending to the impressive spectacle. Water sprays into the air, causing the area to feel considerably cooler in comparison to the heat of the desert to the east. Despite the gargantuan size of the falls, a path can be seen among the rocks leading behind the falls.

Other than the entrance of the magic shop, the wooden counter seals off the entire room from any physical access.  Bookcases containing many volumes of magical text are lined up against the back wall.  Above a wooden desk on the north side of the room, a sign with a staff painted onto it can be seen.  The magic shop owner awaits customers to purchase his goods.

At the entrance, a bronze vase contains an arrangement of flowers.  The floor is wooden and covered by a rug with many colors.  Four beds form a square on the east side of the room.  A dining table set for four is placed before a brick fireplace in the northern part of the room.  An old man is greeting customers from behind the counter.

The exterior of the pasture has a wooden fence surrounding it to prevent sheep from wandering off or falling into the river of Istory.  The river is coming in from the east and arcs to a southern direction under the bridge.  There are more pastures to the north and west, and the southern bridge leads back towards the magic shop.

The magic shop sits on a rise of grassland which can be accessed by a small hill that leads all the way to the front door.  A wooden bridge allows passage over the Istory River to the west.  The northern direction leads to another bridge that provides entrance into the pastures of Istory.

rooms.name: Between the Magic Shop and Pastures

userData.LongDescription: A small wooden bridge connects the magic shop and pastures.  The Istory River flows from the east to the west under the wooden structure.  The pastures of Istory lies to the north, and the southern direction leads towards the magic shop.

The intersection is the center of Istory.  Three paths head into different parts of the town.  A wooden bridge extends to the east and leads into the eastern part of Istory.  A hill to the north goes towards the armor shop.  The southern direction leads towards the item shop.

A cliff takes the place of the wooden fence to prevent sheep from becoming strays on the southwestern corner of the pasture.  The armor shop can be seen on top of the cliff, but there is no way to climb the cliff from this location.  There are more pastures to the north and east.

The item shop is small in size and has a stone chimney poking out from the top of the blue rooftop.  A wooden sign is planted next to the door of the item shop.  The Istory River runs to the north right next to the building.  The entrance of Istory is to the west, and the north path goes further into town.

A house sits on the far northeastern end of the pasture.  The house is small and only one story, and there are pink flowers on the west side of the building.  The Istory River is nearby to the east, running a gentle current in a southerly direction.  There are more pastures to the south and west.

The item shop's floor is composed entirely of stone.  In front of the entrance, a small colorful rug sits on the stone floor.  Two wooden stools are placed at the southeast corner of the room.  The shop keeper is standing behind a wooden counter and is ready to serve customers.

The field is the highest, most northwestern point in Istory.  A garden of many flowers are arranged in a square shape, with an empty patch of grass in the center.  The warm season apparently attracts many frogs to this area.  The field overlooks the pastures to the east and the armor shop to the southeast.

The town of Istory is a peaceful, sheep herding village.  The Istory River can be seen to the far east and runs through the entire town.  An inn lies to the west and the item shop to the east.  The forested path leads to the exit of Istory.

A large, wooden counter surrounds the armor shop's vendor.  In the southeastern corner, a dining table is prepared for three people.  Two signs are hung on the northern wall, each bearing a picture of a shield.  The western part of the room is a living area for the owner of the armor shop.

The armor shop sits on a hill overlooking the pastures to the northeast.  A sign is displayed in front of the shop, bearing the symbol of a shield.  Another hill goes further up towards the northwest and the southern direction leads to the center of town.

There is a wooden fence sealing off access from the northwestern forest.  Many shrubs and trees are just behind the fence, but it does seem like it is traversable if someone could get behind the fence.  More pastures are to the south and east.

The inn is a medium-sized, one-story building.  Outside the building, a small garden of flowers attempts to increase aesthetic value of the inn.  A wooden sign is planted next to the front door.  The entrance of town is towards the eastern direction.

The town's inhabitants stroll through the heart of Carwen's commercial district, chatting with each other and looking in the shops. The trees from the well kept gardens that line the street provide a bit of shade in the hot afternoon. The weapons shop is nestled in among the other buildings along the road, which runs to the east and west. A staircase leads back down to the lower level of the town.

This is the town wall of Carwen, a high stone structure made to protect the town. From this vantage point, Carwen appears to be deep in the midst of a great forest. The scent of salt water is still present, though much fainter. The western, inland end of the town wall is a peaceful part of Carwen.

This is the entrance to the small port town of Carwen. A tunnel under the walking bridge continues to the north from this courtyard. Small trees line the borders of the cobblestone courtyard. The road continues east towards the docks, and a staircase leads to the upper level of the town.

This cobblestone walking bridge connects the east and west sides of upper Carwen. A look over the edge reveals the courtyard at the entrance to the town on one side, and the road that passes under the bridge on the other. Small shops can be found at either end of the bridge.

This room is painted in a celestial theme. The vaulted ceiling has small twinkling stars which seem to be a little further away than the size of the room would suggest. The floor is a polished marble that reflects the stars above, creating the illusion that it's not even there. What appears to be a closet door is faintly glowing.

The second floor of the pub looks like it is used as a little entertainment area, though right now it is empty. A wooden stage has been built against the far wall. The rest of the room is filled with little tables for the patrons to sit at.

The eastern end of the docks is empty and quiet except for the sounds of the ocean and the sea birds. Small waves drift in and out with the tide. The strong smell of salt water and dead fish is everywhere. To the south are more docks and a very large ship.

The road through Carwen continues on, heading towards the ship docks. A small flower garden is on the left, and the stairs just ahead lead to the second level of the town. A row of barrels full of some sort of produce line one wall, and the road continues to the east.

Closer to the docks, the smell of fish and the ocean is noticeable. The docks can be seen to the east and south. Another set of stairs going up lies to the north. A small girl is here playing in her garden, watching the people stroll by on the street.

The item shop is situated in a quiet section of the town. A quaint building, it is surrounded by flower gardens, and is settled of the main roadway. To the south is the stone town wall, Carwen's only protection from the neighboring wild lands.

The muffled sound of the ocean is just barely detectable, as is the faint scent of it on the wind. A small house and a shop with a small flower garden occupy this western edge of the town.  The armory is here, and the road continues east.

A warm, welcoming place, the inn is filled with bright light and fresh flowers. It seems well kept, with nice comfortable beds and cheery surroundings. The innkeeper stands behind the counter, ready to show his customers to their rooms.

This is one of the stone docks that projects out into the water. The salty ocean breeze blows through the area, accenting the gentle sound of the waves lapping against the ships and the dock. A ship is docked here, and sailors are busy unloading the goods from inside.

A hardened looking shopkeeper is working on some bronze armor behind his counter. Pieces of armor, both metal and cloth, are strewn about the clerk. The rest of the shop is full of neatly arrayed clothes and armor. A passage to the east connects the armory to the weapon shop.

This is the east end of Carwen. The shops and buildings end here. The last of the buildings on this street is a warm inviting pub; the sounds of laughter and music can be heard from inside. A set of stairs leads down to the docks and the road continues off to the west.

The eastern end of the wall that protects Carwen from the wild areas outside looks out over the countryside. In one direction you see the ocean, and in the other, a large expanse of dark forest. At this height, a strong breeze blows continually.

This is a more heavily travelled section of Carwen. An inviting looking inn is nestled in this corner of the town, and roads to the east and north lead to shops. To the east lies the walking bridge, and a set of stairs leads down to the courtyard.

The first floor of the pub is filled with good cheer and laughter. A beautiful old piano stands against the back wall of the room. Richly patterned carpets cover the floor, helping to keep the large, airy room warm. A set of stairs lead to the pub's second floor.

The light here is dimmer than out in the street. There are no windows, and the shop is musty and quiet. Racks of weapons fill every bit of wall space there is, and a coat of arms hangs above the counter. An old man sits behind the counter, sharpening blades. A sign hangs on the wall.

The entrance to the town passes under this part of the town wall, and the courtyard can be viewed from this height. Only forests can be seen from here, though the smell of the ocean is still carried on the wind. The wall continues east and west.

This is Carwen's item shop. Fairly small and set away from the rest of the shops, it still carries all of the basic supplies an item shop should. There are crates of items stacked all around the store. The shopkeeper smiles from where he stands behind the counter. A sign hangs on the wall.

Surrounding this small island is a deep trench full of water, the bottom of which is not visible.  The ground's surface is covered in a thick layer of moss.  Tiny streams of water pour down from every part of the cavern, flowing quietly into the trench.  In the very back of the cave, three larger waterfalls are pouring in from sizable holes in the wall.  A narrow strip of land leads across the water to the cave exit.

A knee-deep pool of water begins at the entrance to this cave and extends about twenty strides into the cavern before giving way to dry stone.  Dozens of small waterfalls trickle down from the cave walls.  A large, deep body of water is to the north, with a narrow natural stone path leading overtop it to a small island in the water's center.

rooms.name: Karnak - Outside of the Luxury Suite

userData.LongDescription: This is a fairly simple room. The dull beige of the walls is the same as downstairs, interrupted only by the wooden trim, stretching out beneath the windows. These strips of wood even continue along the wall above the stairs. Other things of notable interest are a pair of windows side by side along the northern wall, and a heavy, sound-proofed door that leads into the luxury suite.

A small stream of molten rock travels from north to south, passing under the town walls. This is where the magic shop once stood. The building itself appears fine, but it appears to be boarded up. A pine tree stands behind the former store. Further back rests a private residence. The home has a red-shingled roof and appears to be made of brick. The bricks themselves are painted white.

rooms.name: A small room above the tavern

userData.LongDescription: A private dining area, perhaps? There are a few windows overlooking the town, near which there is a table, set for two, as well as a decent stock of various liquors and wines on a nearby shelf. Beyond that, the room is rather drab. Beige walls give the room a dull appearance, where as a fancy rug simply comes off as loud.

This is the weapon shop. Behind the shopkeep, there are a pair of crossed swords hanging on the wall. A mace resides on the countertop. Between the counters, a large fireplace is set into the the wall. An oriental rug lies on the floor before it. Near the shopkeep there is a row of pikes standing up.

Plush carpet leads into the main tavern, wherein barrels of rum are stacked to the ceiling, centralized around five wooden tables, some occupied more than others. In the back of the saloon are the bartender and a series of stools. An alcove in the wall nearby houses an earthen fireplace, keeping the room deliciously warm. Next to it is an old organ.

A long row of private homes line the city's wall, stretching to the east and west. Just as with the rest of the city, small cinders burn in controlled gardens. There is a stairway leading to the walkway atop the city walls, but it seems to be blocked by rather large pits of molten rock. In an attempt to counter this, there are the scorched remains of a ladder that appear to have been previously leading to the ramparts.

The town gates are here, lit torches lining the stone walls in a long row. A moat of boiling lava follows the city walls, in an attempt to keep the monsters at bay. The moat continues to both the east and west with little space to walk. Through the gates, a large pillar can be seen acting as a landmark.

A moat of molten fire continues along the gates. Up ahead, the moat edges up against the town wall, leaving the path inaccessable further onward. The only visible path is back to the east, unless a bath in molten lava sounds like a good plan. There is only one torch lit on this wall, as the others seem to have burnt out.

A moat of molten rock continues along the gates; however, the walls corner against the moat up ahead, leaving it inaccessable further onward. The only visible path is back to the west, excepting an extended dip in the excessively hot magma. A sign stands next to the pit, scorch marks covering the sign, leaving it partially concealed. More torches line the wall in spectacular glory.

This inn may have once served a dual purpose, from the looks of things. Now, however, it seems to be host for simple lodgings. The room seems to be divided into two styles of flooring, with the entrance to the bedchambers as the faultline. On the left, the floor is paved with cobblestone tiles, where as the right side of the room is hard-wood. Not much else is out of order, beige walls with wood paneling the order of the day. In a western alcove, the innkeep's own bed resides, a store of supplies not far off. On the opposing side, taking up a large portion of the hardwood area would be the reception desk. Between this alcove and the reception desk is a doorway. Beyond the doorway is a large rug that encompases the entirety of the room. There are few decorations, four beds, a table and two chairs. A brick fireplace finishes things off.

This armor shop looks newly refurbished. A picture of a shield hangs behind the shopkeep. A vase of flowers lays upon the counter, giving it some decoration. An oriental rug is upon the floor, between the counters; a large fireplace on the wall just in front of it. A row of pikes stands near the shopkeep, possibly for display or self protection. This shop is identical in almost every form to the one opposite of it.

There lies a large column within this section of Karnak. It extends a far piece into the sky. Being a wide column, one would have to go around it for further travel north. To the west of it is the weapon and armour shops, as well as a home. To the east, the scorched remains of a spell shop are scattered about. The town gates are to the south.

In this corner of town is the newly refurbished armory. Both the weapon and armor shops have a home in this building, each door residing at opposing ends: The weapon dealer to the east, and armor to the west. Signs hang above the doors, each with a symbol of it's respective commodity painted on. More structures can be seen to the north and east.

The pub is a rather large building, lacking in paint. It's a simple wooden building with a sign on it. The tavern stretches from the western wall into the side of a private home. Underneath the windows of the building are rather thick pockets of molten goo, and they seem to run under the building itself.

Private homes stretch from one direction to another, many of them surrounded by bubbling moats of liquid magma, churning out large bubbles that splatter the ground. Needless to say, there are fires here and there. The small stream of molten rock leaks towards the southeast. Further travel west is blocked by a building.

The Inn stands here, covered in a 'fresh' coat of paint, but despite that the sheer heat of the area seems to cause it to crack and peel. A beautiful pine tree that stands off to the side offers shade to the doorway, as well as blocking out the view of a window not too far away. The building stretches to the east, stopping at the outer wall of the city. The weather-worn shingles of the roof loom overhead, casting even more shade around the somewhat large hotel.

rooms.name: In the Hall of the Pillars

userData.LongDescription: Large pillars adorn this giant room, which is one of the biggest rooms in the castle. Each pillar, like all other pillars in the castle, is covered by ornate scrollwork. A torch on each pillar lights the hall in a rather warm light. A long stretch of carpet covers the main walkway all the way to the stairs leading up to the throne room.

Tall stone walls adorned with gargoyles guard the monument that is Karnak Castle. Torches adorn the castle walls above both of the gargoyles, and light the path for any traveller. Stone steps lead up to the only entrance to the castle, which happens to be a rather imposing oak door. This door is guarded by two men at arms, one on either side of the it. The forest surrounding the castle also acts as a passive deterrant, inhibiting passage to both the east and the west.

The low ceilings here are designed to give the impression of security and safety. The stonework, while not on the whole as good as it could have been, is not overly shabby either. This is the entrance to the main hall, which extends to the north, and it is guarded by a rather ornate looking set of double doors. On each side of the door sits a single torch, providing all the light one needs in this area.

The walls of this hallway are lined with long range weapons of all kinds. Large longbows line one wall, while opposite of those are examples of handheld crossbows. Smaller and easier to wield bows are placed up near the top of the walls, close to where the torches reside. Next to the crossbows lie bins of bolts and arrows, with a few empty quivers nearby.

The stairwell here is hidden inside a darkened alcove to the north. There seems to be an utter lack of a decent light source in this part of the castle. What can be made out, however, is that the alcove itself is made out of two things that look like pillars. The stonework here is even worse than normal, and it is rather blatantly obvious that the lack of light in this area is more purposeful than neglectful.

This stairwell curves up clockwise towards the next level. A small rug is placed on the bottom of the stairwell, whether to cover up a crack or for visitors to wipe their feet on is unknown. Given the amount of dust that is present in the room, the rug being just a rug seems highly unlikely. Above the entrance to the stairwell hangs a small blue rose, with its long stem bent in such a way that it forms a stylized 'K'.

The smell of decay, or at least neglect, lies heavy in the air. Or it would, if the air moved. This unlit corridor plays host to only one thing of interest, which lies upon the north wall. It looks like a rather faded portrait of a chocobo. Mortar dust lies upon the floor rather heavily, as this corridor looks to not often be used.

Long spikes extend down from the portcullis, which is only retracted halfway. This poses absolutely no danger to visitors, however menacing it may seem. Around the top of the portcullis are holes that can be used to help defend the castle while under siege, and as an additional measure this entire area is without its own source of light. The stone floor in this area has numerous burn marks, scars, and dents due to use over the years. Towards the north is a courtyard, and towards the south is the exit to the castle.

The main thing that is noticable in this room is the giant staircase leading up to the throne. Benches line the southern walls, which allows the supplicants a place to sit while they wait their turn for their assigned audience. The floor is a random pattern of different shapes, all set in stone, and designed to attract one's attention. Upon the west and east walls are set lines of torches that light up the room evenly.

Not much can be made out about this floor, as dark tarps completely cover all the walls. Two tall poles in the center of the room provide the light for this area by way of torches attached to the top of them. A small flap exists in the far end of the room for construction workers to pass through.

The lower levels of Karnak Castle serve mostly as storage rooms for the inhabitants of the castle. Bright torches line the walls of this area, giving a rather cozy touch to the surroundings, in direct opposition to the rather decrepit stairwell. A small sign on the wall gives directions towards the different places of interest of this subterranean area.

This floor of the castle is completely dedicated to housing the various implements of war that Karnak needs and is broken down into sections. The southern wall contains racks of swords and daggers, above which is a single row of torches that extends the entire length of the wall. The armory continues to the east and west, while the stairs lead up to the path to the infirmary and the castle proper.

The hospital wing is located in this section of the basement, but seems to be vacant. Towards the east is the door leading to the actual hospital itself, however before that sit a few rows of chairs and a desk. The desk, which is next to the door, is completely unstaffed. Behind the desk lies the normal hospital door which is a white with a red cross on it. Torches on either side of the doorway to the hospital proper provide a warm, flickering light.

A couple rows of beds, none of which are occupied, reside next to the far wall of this room. The smell of antiseptic fills the air, which is juxtaposed against the smell of flowers which reside on the south wall. A few bookcases line the eastern wall, filled with different books on topics ranging from 'ABCs of Diagnosis' to 'The Hiryuu and You: A guide to ownership'.

This corner of the armory is dedicated to spears and polearms. The weapon racks normally synonymous with an armory have been modified slightly here to accommodate the increased length of the weapons they must hold. This area is lighted by means of torches placed along the walls, between which are stored the spears. In the very southeast corner of the room is placed a small water fountain, above which is a small plaque.

The southwest corner of Karnak Armory contains all different styles of axes, from small throwing axes to large poleaxes. Small alcoves cut into the wall hold axes that look to be a bit more special than normal, or at least more valuable, as there are metal grates over the openings. Towards the top of the south wall is where a row of torches is installed, whose light sparkles and reflects off of the numerous, murderous blades.

The torches are rather unevenly spaced and look rather haphazardly placed. Unfinished stones stick out from different various areas of the walls, constricting the hallway considerably on both sides. A few workers are busy chipping away at walls in an effort to even them out somewhat. Dust wafting in from the west covers the floor in a fine gray mist, but thankfully stays low to the ground.

The door looks like it has stood here for ages. The stone engravings upon it are a bit worn down in places, and the imprint of a hand can clearly be seen on the exact middle of it. The carpet that adorns the main part of this hall is absent, along with any pride of workmanship in the masonry. On the ground in front of the door is a rather large burn mark, as if a fire once burned.

Rack upon rack of headgear, in all manner of shapes and sizes, resides here upon the wall. Torches inset into the upper portion of the north wall illuminate the small signs above each rack, listing the size of each item. The light barely touches the stairwell in the southern wall, which has numerous planks nailed across it. A hand-painted sign is tacked onto one of these boards which reads, 'Closed while excavation in progress'.

A single red rose sits above the entranceway to the stairwell, its stem looping around the entire alcove. The stairs lead up to the next level of the castle, and look to be well maintained, even the steps themselves. The everpresent dust on this side of the castle is still everpresent, but not in such obscene amounts. Covering the walls, floors, and even the ceiling, it still doesn't look as pervasive as it is in other areas of the castle.

From the patchwork of stonework to the south, this area is a nice change. The stonework is nicely jointed and of a lighter color than the rest of the castle. Set in alcoves against the south wall are flowering rose bushes of all colors. To the north is a door that leads to the main part of the castle, above which lie a few windows that seem more for defense than for anything else. The exit to the castle lies to the south, whereas the entrance to the castle is to the north.

This portion of the armory is noticably empty. A few guns are placed haphazardly in racks that line the walls, but for the most part the racks lie barren. Two giant bins occupy space on the west wall and are labeled 'ammo'; next to each bin is a rather large red cylinder. Placed on the walls is a single row of torches, with a long wide shelf running underneath.

Special precautions have been taken in this area to minimize the chance of a conflagration. Torches line the uppermost region of the wall, below which extends a wide shelf. Under this shelf are stored several types of cloth armor inside separate compartments, segregated by armor type and size.

It is hard to make out any kind of details in this area due to the massive amount of scaffolding blocking the view in all directions. Rising up to the ceiling and encompassing almost the entire room is a giant scaffold patchwork. Two tall posts ending in torches light this area for the workers so that they can work easily.

The complete lack of workmanship is rather obvious in this part of the castle. The stonework, or what supposedly passes for stonework, is actually made up of mostly mortar, in which smaller bits of stone are thrown in for good measure. The door to the north also shows some signs of neglect, as one of its hinges is barely attached to the wall, while another is attached only to the door itself. The light in the room is provided by the pillars in the main hall, so it's not entirely too clear what, exactly, is around.

What once might have been rows of armor now is nothing more than a line of empty pegs. The floor below each peg seems brighter than the rest of the floor, as if whatever was set on the peg shielded the floor from wear. Above the pegs and imbedded slightly into the wall is a row of torches, each sputtering in response to random air currents. A small sign on the wall reads,'Lower levels: West. Upper levels: South'.

Looking to be chiseled right out of the upper stratum, the hallway here presents an image of uniform continuality. Evenly spaced torches dot the walls and provide a warm light that envelops this stretch of hallway from one end to the other. On the south wall is located a staircase which leads to the lower levels of the castle and from which comes a slight draft.

Two columns guard what seems to be a rather normal, empty chest. Like the rest of the castle, the stonework in this hallway seems to be rather hastily done, with patchworks of mortar everywhere along the walls. Above the chest lies a wreath, composed of thorns and roses.

This brightly lit hallway runs from the main level of the castle to the northeast and continues towards the lower levels to the southwest. Torches are placed at set intervals along the walls of this hallway in order to provide this area with an even amount of light. Small plants are hung in shaded alcoves along the wall to supplement the castle's food supply.

Blue drapes adorn the back of this room, accenting the blue carpet which covers the entire floor of this room. Hung off of the numerous pillars, the torches light the entire room from the back. A single throne sits in the center of the room, but is currently unoccupied. Near the throne is a small stool upon which the minister normally sits.

An empty chest stands guarded by two columns in an alcove on this side of the castle. The columns are adorned with scrollwork from top to bottom, along with inscriptions in some incomprehensible language. Above the empty chest sits a wreath attached to the wall, made up of blue roses.

The blue entryway carpet ends at a stairway on the way to the throne room. A large oak door, which spans the width of the hallway, greets supplicants on their way to the throne room. Unlike the other doors in the castle, this one happens to be rather plain looking, with no scrollwork or ornateness about it. On either side of the door are small alcoves, which hold blue and red roses, respectively.

The western side of the inn opens up into a modest item shop.  There is a counter near the back of the shop where business is conducted.  A vibrant red, gold, and green rug is spread out, covering the hardwood floor.  Two crates are lying on the rug against the western wall.  Behind the counter, two signs with an image of an elixir drawn on each hang from the wall.  The only apparent exit is to the east, back to the main part of the inn.

A well used counter sits at the back of the room.  On one side of the room, several crates packed with various types of armor have been stacked.  On the other side of the room, barrels filled with various liquids useds to aid in armorsmithing are resting against the wall.  The soft light of the sun shines through the open windows, hitting the wooden floor and brightening the shop.  The only exit appears to be out through the door.

This grassy, open area of Moore is one of the few unused areas of the village.  An incredibly steep ridge wraps northward from the northern side of the pub, then eastward all the way to the inn, making it impossible to travel to the north or the west.  A few trees dot the space, providing a modicum of shade.  The village pub can be seen to the south, and the village inn can be seen to the east.

The hardwood floors, glowing softly, reflect the light coming in through the windows.  A few racks of weapons are resting at the back of the room, and many unopened crates appear to be stacked nearby.  A large, wooden sign with crossed swords is hanging on the wall behind the shop's counter.  The only exit appears to be outside through the door.

A large building with a blue, slate roof stands atop the middle of a hill in the village of Moore.  Three bushes with pink flowers decorate the front of the building, and a sign emblazoned with a sword hangs above the entrance.  A grassy slope leads down the ridges south to the main part of the village.  Behind the building is a well and another natural ramp that leads up to a path that hugs a cliff face as it leads to the east.

A grassy path near the back of the village hugs a raised and unclimbable cliff face to the north.  A grassy ramp leads down the steep cliff to the south towards the weapon shop and further to the main section of the village.  A bush covered in pink flowers and a large tree block any progress to the west.  Several trees line the path as it continues to the east, where it curves and settles near the lake to the east of Moore.

rooms.name: Near the Entrance to Moore Village

userData.LongDescription: The village of Moore is situated in the middle of a forest with a lake to the east of the village.  Most of the village itself is on hills that have collapsed and formed sheer ridges that, though they aren't large, could certainly cause injury if someone were to fall from one.  A few light colored buildings with blue roofing can be seen to the east, north, and west of the entrance to the village.  To the south, trees line the path out of the village.

The pub in Moore is a vibrant place.  Four long tables with nearly two dozen chairs between them covers most of the space.  There are four seats lining the bar.  Behind the bar there are shelves of liquor and dishes as well as a large stove for cooking.  A small dance floor can be seen on the far side of the pub, with a large upright piano sitting unattended on it.  Many casks of ale line one of the walls south of the dance floor.  There is only one exit that leads back to the village proper.

A tiny building that is more shack than actual building is nestled between bluffs at the far end of the village.  The bluffs appear unclimbable, so the only path away from the building is back to the south.  Two trees line either side of the house.  An old sign, nearly in shambles, rests near the entrance to the building.  On it is a painted emblem of a staff.

The former magic shop in Moore is a very tiny shop; barely large enough to fit more than half a dozen people in it comfortably.  The magic shop has since been repurposed into an item shop for the sale of the local magical liquor.  An ornate gold, red, and green rug has been spread out, giving a sharp contrast with the polished hardwood floor.  A long counter near the back of the building takes up a large portion of the room.  A wooden sign with the emblem of a staff hangs on the back wall.

The inn in Moore has a relaxed atmosphere to it.  Right next to the entrance is a counter with a large, potted flower on it.  A small but moderately stocked bookshelf and a writing desk are behind the counter.  To the west, the room opens up into what appears to be a small shop.  Through a door to the north is the sleeping area for the inn.  It holds several beds with crisp, white sheets, a sitting table, and a few chairs.  A door to the south leads out to the main part of the village.

A much smaller building with similar architecture stands to the southwest of the village's pub.  The doors are locked, making entry impossible, but the smell of various liquors wafts in the air.  This is probably where the pub stores most of their alcohol.  Trees and a ridge block access to the west and south.  The entrance to the pub lies to the northeast.

rooms.name: A Peaceful Lakeside Meadow in Moore

userData.LongDescription: A small, peaceful area is situated at the eastern edge of Moore.  Several bushes with pink flowers are scattered around the area.  The waters of the lake to the east of Moore splash softly against the bluffs.  A grassy path leads southwest to the main part of the village while another heads west along a cliff face to a different part of the village.

A moderately sized building with a blue, slate roof that seems to be common for the village sits near the center of the village.  A few bushes with pink flowers decorate the area in front of the building.  An old, slightly faded sign is stuck in the ground to the left of the door, clearly marking the building as the inn.  A path to the side of the building leads to another building to the north.  The largest building in the village can be seen to the southwest.  To the east, a grassy ramp climbs one of the ridges, leading to the weapon shop.

A large, two-story building overlooks the lake at the southeastern end of Moore.  A steady stream of smoke billows out of a large chimney on the western side of the building.  A wooden sign with an emblem of a shield hangs above the entrance door to the building.  To the north, a grassy ramp climbs the steep cliffs to the weapon shop.  A path can be seen around the building leading to the northeast.  To the west, a couple more buildings can be seen.

The largest building in Moore stands at the western edge of the village.  The stench of wine and ale wafts through the air while raucous sounds can be heard coming from inside the building.  To the right of the door hangs a wooden sign informing any passersby that this is definitely the local pub.  A path between the building and a cliff leads to a smaller building to the southwest.  To the east lie a few more buildings, and an open, grassy area lies to the north.

Moving through the forest becomes more difficult as the vines underfoot thicken. Trees appear through the forest, threatening to block the path that is barely visible. Faint sunlight shows through the top of the trees where branches have collapsed.

The underground cave extends further on. Stalagmites cover the floor, making navigating through the cave difficult. Pools of water form in the center of the cave, seemingly at random. The cave extends to the north and south.

Darkness envelops the path as the sunlight from the entrance fades away. Two trees which once formed a barrier to outsiders appear at the beginning of the path, far enough apart to allow a single person to pass through. The path extends forward beyond the trees.

The forest damage appears to be worse as the forest continues deeper. To the east, what used to be a path appears to be blocked by a wreckage of collapsed trees, allowing no passage through. The sunlight once again shines brighter through the trees than usual.

A narrow, worn-away bridge leads into a dark and gloomy forest. Massive canopy trees envelop the area, blocking out all sunlight. The forest shows clear signs of fire damage, becoming more evident as the forest continues. To either side are rivers far below the bridge, with paths leading out and into the forest.

Shortly within the underground cave, the sounds of the forest fade away. They are replaced with the rhythmic sounds of dripping water, and the occasional sounds of something scurrying out of sight. No visible light enters the cave, leaving the cave in darkness.

The forest path leads into a dead end clearing, surrounded by trees on all sides. A single beam of sunlight shines through the top of the trees, where there appears to be excessive fire damage. Branches have fallen to the forest floor and many of the nearby trees look ready to collapse.

The deep forest path splits into two new routes, to the north and to the east. The eastern path seems to continue deeper into the forest, as the path expands, providing more room to move around. The northern path is a narrow and seems to lead to a dead end.

rooms.name: Moore Forest -- A Tangle of Trees

userData.LongDescription: The trees barely allow access to this region, allowing only a small path through a mess of trees. Past a small clearing, a wall of tangled trees appears beyond, preventing any passage forward. The only way to go is backwards through the path.

The cave emerges into a small path surrounded by trees on all sides, barely allowing a single person to pass through. The wall of trees widens into a forest surrounded by trees on all sides. The only way out appears to be back through the cave, and a grassy path leads deeper into the forest.

The forest seemingly comes to an end. The trees form an imposing barrier to all sides. The only direction ahead is entering a dark, cold cave that opens up from the foot of a massive tree. The passage appears to lead under the forest.

rooms.name: Moore Forest -- By the Guardian Tree

userData.LongDescription: The forest comes to an end here, and a single massive brown tree extends upward so far that it seems to join Heaven and Earth themselves. The Guardian Tree serves as the protector of the forest, sealing it off. A hole at the bottom of the tree provides a way in for those who would like to enter the tree.

The deep forest continues to the north and south, the path getting smaller and smaller as branches and other debris covers the ground. Trees block movement to all sides except the north, leading further into the deep forest, and south, leading back to the cave.

Leaving behind the safety of the flowers, the ground below becomes increasingly scorched. The trees here are burned beyond recognition, forming a wall of darkness. The path continues to the north, with the peak of a cliff appearing in the distance.

The solid cliff wall and the forest create a boundary between the path, only allowing passage through the east and west. A gentle wind blows over the cliff, stirring the leaves on the ground into the cold air. The branches and cliff face extends overhead.

The exit to the cave becomes visible, which looks to lead to an even deeper forest region. Near the exit, leaves and branches lie scattered on the ground after blowing into the underground cave. On the other side of the cave, the wind howls.

A now-deserted underground shelter, originally built by the Moogles and hidden under a blanket of leaves. A small river runs through the shelter. This shelter was used in the past for protection both from the forest creatures and the fire that once raged through the forest.

Along the right-hand side of the forest, the tree line has entirely burned away. Through the charred remains of the trees, you can see a smooth stone cliff extending into the air, allowing beams of sunlight to shine over and into the forest.

A soft grass path extends underfoot, in contrast to the burnt leaves and vines covering the forest floor. The path extends to the east, though there seems to be a fork in the path ahead. The soft sound of insects and distant creatures can be heard.

Near the end of the scarred path, the trees around the forest are in a clear state of collapse. Branches lie across the ground, broken to pieces underfoot. The scarred path continues to the north and south. A huge cliff becomes visible to the north.

The forest opens into a small clearing before a fork in the path. To the west appears to be a semicircle of trees, leading to a dead end. In the northern clearing, the trees appear to open up and allow passage into a dark tunnel.

Under the deepest cover of trees, sunlight coming from above is blocked off. The thick trees to all sides block movement and dull the sounds of the forest. Sunlight bleeds into the grove from the east and west, where the cover of trees is not as great.

rooms.name: Moore Forest -- Heart of the Forest

userData.LongDescription: The forest again becomes thicker at the path nears the center of the forest. A thick blanket of leaves covers up a hole in the ground that was once used as a refuge. Rusted weapons and armor are strewn about the forest, clear evidence of an old conflict. To the north, a massive tree is visible.

Sunlight once again breaks through the cover of trees, providing some illumination. The cover of trees is less apparent here than in the rest of the forest, allowing more movement than usual. The forest to the north and south is still too thick to move through, forcing movement through the east or west.

rooms.name: Moore Forest -- A Circle of Flowers

userData.LongDescription: As a stark contrast to the rest of the burnt forest, this small clearing seems to have avoided any harm. A circle of beautiful flowers grows around the center of the clearing, untouched. This is the only location in the forest where they have survived.

Brown vines cover the interior of the Guardian Tree, forming a floor and great walls that rise and form a ceiling above. On the far end of the room, a series of living pillars rise from the ground, the source of the Guardian Tree.

A long set of stone steps lead down into the depths of this damp cavern. A warm breeze blows in from the entrance to the southeast, which carries down the steps. The blue-tinted walls of the cavern seem to be covered in a thick coat of algae that thrive in these conditions.

Stairs carved into the blue limestone wall lead up to a platform that connects with the entrance of the cave. The path leads to the west, where another set of stairs can be seen leading down into the cavern. Rocky outcroppings protrude into the small space that's available for walking, but there's just enough to squeeze by.

Water trickles down the damp cavern walls, likely a product of the steam rolling in from the north. Limestone cave features fill the small path, which twists and turns as it winds through them. A set of steps has been carved into the subterranean wall to the east, which leads up to another portion of the cave.

Stalactites reach down from the craggy ceiling, some of them connecting to paired stalagmites below. The path levels out between two sets of stairs. One leads down into the cavern and the other, to the east, leads up. The sound of a roaring engine echos off the rocky cavern walls.

Steam rises from the hull of the massive airship that lies in wait at the surface of the still water. The roaring engine echos off the cavern walls, making the thrumming machine dominate the space. A small stone path leads south through a tight crevice.

Warm rays of sun pour in from a wide opening to the south. The cave's entrance allows a gentle breeze in that reflects off the cool, algae-covered stone walls. An unnatural sound echos from deep within the shadows of the cavern's passage to the northwest.

At the bottom of a long set of natural stairs, a pool of water is fed by multiple cracks in the ceiling, the torrent from the steps, and a peculiar column of limestone. Blunted stalactites on the ceiling direct water towards the flooded walkway in steady streams. The current pulls in two different directions, south towards a cacophonous roar and westward around a few natural columns.

Algae covers the walls of the cavern which has been carved out by the subterranean river. Water trickles down the cave walls and flows across the raised portion of bedrock that sticks out of the torrent rushing towards the southern wall. A small wooden chest atop a natural limestone pedestal lies abandoned and empty.

A large limestone column resembling a pagoda sticks out of the water and looks dry compared to the rest of the cavern. Tucked behind it, a long set of stairs leads to the north. Multiple waterfalls flowing to the south crash into lower platforms after a long drop.

The narrow hallway junctions to three paths. The underground river pours in from the northern wall. Knee-deep water rushes down sets of stairs along the outer paths, though the current flows most fiercely towards the center path, into a large, roaring cavern.

Water flows out from a hole high in the northern wall, which in turn flows off the ledge to the south. On a small recessed portion of the ledge, an old wooden chest sits and rots. To the south of it, a waterfall flows onto a limestone platform.

The walls of the cavern are covered in a layer of water as a result of the nearby splashing waterfalls; one of which leads to a small platform to the south. A long set of stairs leads north, which is right next to a deep groove which channels most of the water from that direction.

Multiple waterfalls pour onto an immense limestone slab at the bottom of this cavern. The water is fairly deep and rushes towards the sheet of water that acts as the southern wall of the cave. A long set of stairs to the north is carved from the limestone and has gallons of water pouring down it.

The walls wrap around a small clearing, creating a small stone room. A small chest, covered in a fine white dust sits quietly in the center of the chamber. Near the entrance of the chamber, a small gray button is inconspicuously mounted into the stone walls.

Frigid spray shoots up from the slow-moving section of river below the ledge. It's constantly fed by the many waterfalls along the northern wall. A crude set of steps leads down into the water, forcing the path through the pool before immediately popping back onto dry land again.

The path constricts considerably and the southern wall pushes in towards the opposing side. A few steps have been carved into the ledge along the northern wall, which has a small opening in it. The passage widens into a larger space to the west. Embedded into a crack in the southern wall, a steep set of stairs lead down to a lower level.

Water pours from the limestone slab above and creates a strong current towards the southern ledge. The roaring waterfalls throughout the cavern create a thunderous echo. Anything that isn't covered in running water is subjected to a cool mist instead.

A long ledge of limestone sticks out from the western and northern walls, offering a large amount of dry footing. A few waterfalls to the east disturb this tranquil pool of water. A descending tunnel with a narrow staircase has been carved into the southern wall. A peculiar button on the northern wall seems out of place.

The water near the edges of the cave is not as deep, though a few waterfalls ensure this platform is kept wet. The western wall of the cavern curves up towards the ceiling of the massive cavity and is filled with a variety of limestone formations. A long set of stairs to the north has a deluge of water pouring down it.

A limestone outcropping hangs overhead and water gushes from a hole above it. Similar features fill the northern wall and serve as the source of all the cascading waterfalls within the cave. A massive waterfall to the south pounds a lower level with a constant downfall and frigid spray.

Three monolithic limestone columns connect the submerged floor to the ceiling around this raised platform. One of the columns is attached to the southern ledge of the platform and has a large hole in it. Water rushing down the stairs from the north flows through the opening, creating a small waterfall that pours into the area below.

A massive collection of stalactites have coalesced into a gigantic column that penetrates the mirror-like surface of the cenote. The path wraps around the feature before continuing its seemingly random progression. A tunnel in leading out of the cave can be seen to the east.

Sharp crystals protrude out of the ground around a chest near the northern wall. There's also a strange little button on a nearby wall. Small tube-shaped tunnels litter the eastern wall, though none appear on the northern one. A layer of white dust covers the floor and swathes of it have been pushed into long piles.

The limestone cavern has a few inches of standing water which reflects the light from the cave's opening. Illuminated by the reflected light, the stalactites appear as a dazzling array of colors from bright cerulean to deep indigo. A tarnished silver door with intricate etchings is inset on the northern wall.

The monstrous cavity behind Istory Falls is comprised of a raging river flowing down a multitude of limestone ledges. The miniature waterfalls and rapids roar and echo throughout the cavern, creating a thunderous din. The light that pierces the main waterfall colors the entire cave in a beautiful palette of blue.

A slurry drips onto the path from a large crack in the ceiling far above. The mineral-dense liquid feeds the growth of the path. Similar occurrences repeat throughout the cavern, creating sprawling, yet easily traversed terrain. The calm waters of the massive cenote extend far to the northwest and disappear into the dark.

Water cascades from the ledge to the north, immersing this limestone platform in a constant deluge of frigid water. A slight lip on the platform channels the water to a single point to the south, where it falls onto a small outcropping before crashing into another level below.
