An intricate circle with strange symbols has been painted on the floor of this opening. Dark crystals surround the circle and a sense of tranquility seems to fill the area. A set of stairs on the northern wall leads up, while the set on the southern wall leads further down into the cave.

The path widens dramatically before it abruptly ends. A small destroyed chest sits near the edge of the water. Far below the surface, shadows dart between submerged stalagmites. A static-like rumble comes from the southeast, out of the mouth of a dark tunnel.

A cool wind blows from the southern end of the cavern. White dust covers most of the surfaces within the tunnel and much of it has collected near the walls. A pile of rubble in the center of the passage is covered in the same dust and seems to have formed after a stalactite fell from the ceiling.

A large column of limestone occupies the center of this large fissure. Small creatures scurry to their various hovels as the silence is disturbed. A discarded wooden chest sits against the back wall within a large puddle of water; it was emptied long ago by some other spelunker.

A long thin crevice in the northern wall seems to extend into a long tunnel. Water trickles down the sheer walls and continues flowing towards the many waterfalls to the south. Stalactites hanging from the ceiling reach towards the water-covered walkway.

A ledge of bedrock protrudes from the southern wall and hangs over the underground river. A set of steps has been carved into it, which leads east, into the water. Perhaps, many years ago this platform was submerged like much of the cavern. A few waterfalls to the north seem to have carved out sections of the path. Now they just feed directly into the water below.

This elevated platform offers a grand view of the entire cavity. Waterfalls flow down limestone ledges. Water flows in from large crevices on the northern wall which covers the platforms below them in about a foot of cold water. Stalactites reaching down from the ceiling of the cavern are almost within reach.

The slick and gritty path widens as it comes to an unexpected end. A large portion of it has broken away, creating an impasse to the southwest path. A wooden chest sits in the middle of the broken path, covered in algae and empty. The waters of the cenote ripple as small drops of water disturb the surface.

Two thunderous waterfalls flood this platform with a torrent of chilled groundwater. The water crashes into the limestone, throwing mist into the air. Multiple waterfalls to the south leading down to a platform near the entrance of the cave system.

Connecting the ceiling to the bottom of the expansive pool, a monolithic column of limestone stands firm and is covered in a muddy mix of water. Cracks in the ceiling near the top of the column spout water onto it and natural flutes have begun to form. The path near the column is covered in the mud but clears up quickly as distance builds. A large opening in the southern wall leads to a set of stairs that descend into darkness.

At the top of some extremely worn stairs, waterfalls drench the limestone shelf in a deluge of frigid water. A thin ledge leads to the west where a waterfall pours onto another ledge to the southwest. Despite all the moving water, there isn't much of a breeze thanks to the curtain of water Istory Falls provides.

Thousands of gallons of water pour from a limestone ledge above. The water rushes away from the plunge pool below the ledge and feeds into the many waterfalls below and down the stairs to the south. A large opening in the northern wall leads deeper into the cavern.

A row of stalactites and stalagmites along the southern wall intermingle and create a limestone maw. Water filters through the limestone before plummeting into the abyss beyond. On the western and eastern sides of the cavern, a set of steps leads to a raised portion of dry land. An odd echo from the eastern wall betrays the size of the space.

At the top of a pedestal-like slab of limestone, a massive chest divides the water rushing in from the waterfall behind it. A broad waterfall nearby washes the platform in a flood of water, most of which flows onto a large chunk of limestone to the south.

A thick layer of blue algae covers this limestone platform. The waterfall from the north feeds another to the south. A small wooden chest sits in a crevice along the northern wall. Algae cover the wooden planks of the chest and the metal hinges have long rusted.

The expansive cavern stretches out into a sprawling labyrinth that has small tubes extending deep into the walls of earth. Multiple stalactites have fallen from the ceiling shattering into hundreds of pieces, which cover the cavern floors. A large column of limestone within the center of the room houses a set of stairs, which leads up the cave system.

Ancient stalagmites reach up and out from the bottom of the deep pool. Having been fed by the slurry dripping from the ceiling, they've coalesced and formed a twisting path throughout the cenote. The slippery path curves and falters unpredictably. It branches in multiple directions, though the path to the south seems to connect with a large column of stone.

A large chunk of limestone sticks up out of the platform and has water trickling down its sides. Sets of stairs lead north, south and another is visible to the southwest; each of them concealed by the frigid waters that cascades down them. A meager ledge leads east and wraps around the limestone chunk to the northeast.

The faint rumble of the roaring waterfalls near the entrance of the cave can scarcely be heard through the narrow tunnel within the northern wall. A long path of stone twists and turns through the cavern. Below it, a body of water is only occasionally disturbed by drips of water from the stalactites far above.

The path broadens as the room opens into a large dome-like structure. A long ledge spans across the length of the room and a short set of steps leads down to an insignificant area. The wind coming from the east seems to be going north, though there doesn't appear to be a path in that direction.

Long stalactites hang from the ceiling near the western wall. Small tunnels fill the wall and many of the openings are covered in fine white dust. A small wooden chest is tucked behind a giant crystal, which is sticking out of the ground. A little button on the northern wall barely stands out against the similarly colored wall. Wind pushes out from a darkened chamber in the southern wall.

The ledge passes a natural cave which leads into the crater wall. The airship dock is only a short climb up from here while the bottom of the pit still is quite a long way to go. Somewhere below the angry roar of two monsters fighting it out over the choicest bits of prey can be heard.

This part of the walkway is littered with boulders of varying sizes. The only way past all the rubble would be climbing over it carefully. Nearly the whole of the western wall is thickly coated with hardened lifestream pieces which keep it from collapsing. Down below monsters can be heard fighting each other for the little meat which ventures into the crater.

Rain water and the lifestream have eroded much of the stone walls which once stood firm and strong. In time, the volcanic mountain will collapse, perhaps caused by another lifestream eruption. For now this lower walkway still seems strong enough to withstand the weight of heavy monsters and adventurers. A sickly looking moss is covering the rock where the water is trickling down.

The wind blows through the crater creating small dust clouds creating eerie whistling sounds. It is noticably cooler here in the shadows, especially with all the air currents which blow through cracks and holes in the wall. In time, the whole crater will probably collapse into itself because the already unstable walls are being subjected to the forces of nature constantly.

This platform barely provides enough space for a few people to stand on. Luckily, another one is right below it which can be reached by climbing down. Since the distance isn't huge, it is also possible to climb back up to this ledge. A pebble loosens and drops down into the near darkness.

rooms.name: In Front of the Tunnel Exit

userData.LongDescription: A dark tunnel leads down into the depths of the earth. It spirals downwards so it's not possible to see where it leads to. Angry roars of mythical beasts are echoing from the tunnel walls. To the left there's a tight formation of rocks and platforms which can be climbed. The tunnel has been closed for security reasons.

Along the western side of the crater the ledge doesn't seem to be that stable. Judging by the fissures and missing parts of the walkway the erupting lifestream must have hit hard enough to throw even boulders out of the crater. The force must have been a multiple of an active volcano's. In any case, it is not safe to stay on this uneven ground.

The shadows of the huge airship which has anchored at the crater's edge are falling onto the rubble path which leads further into the depths. The slightest touch sends dozens of little pebbles and rocks tumbling down into the  darkness below. It seems that the lifestream explosion hasn't finished off all of the crater's monsters as roaring noises can be heard from deep down.

This side of the walkway ends at a chasm. The only way down would be jumping over a set of narrow platforms below. On the other hand returning to the airship could be a nice and much safer alternative as well. The gap to the nearest platform isn't that broad so there isn't any danger of falling down, not even for the clumsiest tourists.

The green radiation from the lifestream is very intense. Even though it's not possible to guess exactly how deep it is to the bottom of the pit, the walkways seem to end a good deal before reaching the deepest parts. There's a cavern about ten yards below which can be reached by going down the walkway. The other alternative is climbing back up over the platform onto the upper path and then following it to the exit.

A bit of sunlight shines in from above. It's a welcome change from the greenish aura which seems to permeate the crater from below. The sun is also warming up the air which is already quite humid. Considering that the surrounding region is an arid or even frozen wasteland, it is quite a contrast. The atmosphere certainly is very relaxing.

Here the stone platforms form a ledge which runs around the crater dropping steadily in height. Looking downwards here all that can be seen are the lower platforms and a green shimmer at the bottom, probably caused by remaining lifestream pools. Little stones which are dislodged from the platforms take a very long time to reach the bottom from here however.

One of the many nearly parallel walkways connects the upper with the lower ledge. The lower ledge is only six feet below and can be reached by jumping off the edge. To the left several boulders form steps up to another stone block. The temperature is slightly higher here and the air is a bit stale.

Looking up and down, the ledges almost seem to form a giant irregular natural stairway. It involves some climbing but the rock formations still easily connect the top of the cavern with the lower caves. The walkway ends here, forcing travelers to either return or jump down to the next lower 'step'.

The rocky walkway leads to the left and right here. To the west, it ends after a few steps giving way with another ledge not far below. To the east, it drops off sharply after a few feet too but at least it seems to be possible to climb down there. Since another walkway is only two yards above, climbing back up is not really difficult either. The glowing lifestream residue is especially plentiful here bathing the area in a warm yellow-green light.

Along the western wall the walkway meets a collapsed column which once rose up from a lower walkway. It now conveniently provides a bridge which is steadily leading downwards. Claw marks on the walkway tell grisly tales of a brutal fight between at least two monsters, probably dragons or gargoyles. Relying on outside people or animals to venture in doesn't seem to be enough for those beasts, thus it's another case of 'survival of the fittest'.

A collapsed stone column and a walkway meet at the western wall. Climbing up on the walkway is no big deal while the spiralling path downwards continues to the east. Some flies are buzzing around the cadaver of a semi-eaten parasite which was probably killed off by stronger monsters. The stench from its remains is very annoying and acidic.

Only when standing on the bottom of this cave is it possible to fully grasp its enormous size. The stone formations above form interesting patterns, like a natural staircase to the west or a ladder to the east. Walking around here creates sounds of shattering glass with because little parts of green crystal which covers the whole floor shatter with every step.

This rock platform is only a few feet wide connecting two walkways directly above and below. It's very easy to either jump back up (which takes a little bit of strength) or to jump down to the other ledge. The wind is blowing through the crater and making eerie noises. It is a bit irritating because it also blows dust around which has the annoying tendency to get into everyone's eyes.

Even though the bottom of the shaft is nowhere in sight, the walkway ends a little further down as if nature wanted to prevent adventurers from coming any closer to the center of the world. A little further ahead a little cavern looms, more like a crack in the wall. On the other hand one could always climb back to the surface by following the upward spiralling ledge which leads clockwise around the crater twice before reaching its edge.

rooms.name: At the Foot of a Rock Formation

userData.LongDescription: This is the bottom left corner of this large cave. To the east, a tunnel which leads downward to the deeper caverns looms. Using the rock formations on the western side of the cave, it is also possible to scale back up to the outer volcanic shaft. The dim green light casts weird shadows on the floor as something large moves overhead.

A crack in the crater wall connects the volcanic shaft with the deeper regions. Warm and moist air is wafting up from below. The tunnel seems to lead into a large open cavern, judging by the first impression. Entering this cave will mean leaving the sunlight behind and descending even deeper into the bowels of the earth. As if on cue, the angry roar of a large beast can be heard from below.

The way ends at the western edge of the platform. The shattered remains of an opened treasure chest lie here, scattered all over the walkway. Looking down, a series of platforms of no height difference greater than two to three yards makes reaching the bottom of this cave very easy. It also seems to be a convenient way to climb back up from below.

The slow drip of water leaking through cracks in the wall onto the walkway can be heard. It is probably rain water which has seeped through fissures because it is not deep enough here to be from an underground stream. Slipping here would lead to a messy end hundreds of feet below.

Footsteps echo through the volcanic shaft. The open space carries the sound well and provides interesting acoustics. Bats flutter around, perturbed by the uncommon sounds. Making too much noise is sure to attract roving bands of monsters which is something only the hardiest of adventurers might be able to get away with.

This ledge leads up slightly to the right to reach a rock pile. Above those stones a walkway leads further upwards. The cavern floor is directly below and can be reached by either climbing down or jumping off this ledge. The stone seems to be a bit unstable though, many cracks and holes can be seen. A few pebbles fall to the floor creating echoing sounds throughout the cavern.

This is the only platform in the near vicinity which is large enough for a group of people to stand on. Only experienced wall-climbers with the right equipment would be able to scale the cavern walls to climb back up from here. The only way to leave this stepping stone is jumping down to another platform far below which is just barely within jumping distance.

The uppermost platform is only the first of a long series of stepping stones which form a spiral that leads from the edge of the crater deep down into the earth. Luckily, the distances between the platforms are only minor, so it's not too difficult to jump from one to the next. Going counter-clockwise each platform is a little lower than the previous, they almost form a staircase.

Bats flutter around agitated by the sounds of footsteps. The moist and warm climate of the crater seems to attract those little scavengers who are hunting insects that are in turn feeding on the moss that is growing on the walls. To the northeast the ledge ends forcing travellers to jump down over a few platforms, to the southwest the ledge leads back to the crater's edge.

It is almost pitch black here apart from the faintest hint of greenish light from the crater and a little sunlight from above. The path seems to lead upwards to a wall with several foot- and handholds which can easily be climbed. Looking upwards it seems that the cave leads outside and ends behind a boulder close to the airship dock. Talk about luck!

A collapsed stone column leads over to the western wall where it is possible to step over to another ledge which leads upwards. The stone isn't easy to walk on because there's not much space to step on. The light is very dim here making it even more difficult not to slip and tumble down onto the cavern floor which should result in grave injuries from this height. Getting down one step at a time certainly is preferable.

rooms.name: Entrance of the Labyrinth of Ledges

userData.LongDescription: A small cave entrance connects the outer crater with this huge cavern. A rocky cliff leads even further down. Stone ledges provide the only stepping stones on the way up and down. The area is illuminated by the faintest greenish glow which is a residue of crystallized lifestream that sticks to the stone.

This part of the walkway has been nearly covered by rubble which has fallen down from the adjacent wall. The vibrations have been strong enough to dislodge stones and dirt and erode parts of the ledge. Stepping too close to the edges might shift the weight enough to make them collapse. That's probably the reason why most of the footprints in the dust are closer to the wall.

The distance to the next lower platform is even less than the one between the higher ledge and this one. Looking down, reaching the next platform would require quite a jump into the depths which are obscured by near total darkness. Climbing back up from there seems to be impossible. There would need to be another way to reach the crater exit.

It's quite difficult to remain standing after a jump onto this platform because it's slightly tilted to the right making it difficult to keep one's footing. Straight down, a tunnel looms which leads deeper into the mountain. It would just require two jumps down to explore it. How to get back up is another question though.

The walkways continue with the zig zag course and cross about two thirds of this cave's height. A few bats flutter past searching for small insects to consume. To the right, a deep chasm leads all the way to the floor of the cavern which means the only way to get down from here would be climbing down the walkways.

The stone formations nearly form a slightly irregular but still easy to use stairway in the western part of the cavern. Apart from the roving monsters, travel is safe here without natural hazards like collapsing walls or walkways. To the east it's possible to climb down a 'floor' but it's also quite easy to reach the upper walkway from here.

A breeze of fresh air from above blows a bit of dust and dirt around. To the right, the walkway ends but climbing down to the lower one is an option. To the west a mound of stones and rubble should be good enough to get back up to the cavern exit which is already a good way above.

An especially large vein of lifestream runs through the rock, pulsing in a warm green light. Its outer shell has hardened long ago, but lifestream is still flowing through it. Huge quantities of it must still be present in the lower regions considering the pressure which it needs to get it to this height. The vein is warm to the touch and also illuminates some treacherous parts of the path.

The walkway ends at a deep chasm. The lifestream which blasted out of the crater seems to have torn off the rest of this ledge. At the bottom of this cave there seems to be another tunnel exit, but that is so far below that jumping down would almost certainly not be a good idea.

rooms.name: At the Entrance of the Northern Crater

userData.LongDescription: The airship has anchored at the top of the northern crater. The mountain seems to be completely hollow; it's probably the remnant of a no longer active volcano. Rocks litter the surface, which is nearly devoid of plant life. Parts of the the ground are coated with crystalized lifestream which burst out of the crater with an explosive force long ago. To the south a rocky path leads down into the depths.

The path here is almost too steep to walk on safely. Looking down it's possible to jump over to a rock platform. The shaft drops almost vertically and the only way down seems to be a series of jumps over the platforms starting with the one below. A strong odour of salty air wafts up mixed with the musky smell of....something else. The way back to the airship is just a short climb to the north towards more even terrain.

Deep shadows which are cast by the upper path are falling onto the walkway. Without the sunlight, the temperature is dropping noticeably. A small cave to the northwest leads into the darkness. The wall looks a lot darker, probably consisting of molten volcanic rock. This suggests that the lifestream either developed a lot of heat or that the crater is of truly volcanic origin and the lifestream just burst through the earth here.

This is the final platform above the tunnel exit to the lower caverns. The cavern floor glows slightly and seems to be covered with a crystalline substance, probably lifestream. The air is stale and very hard to breathe due to the rising humidity. Since climbing back up here is impossible, jumping down is the only way.

The reflective floor mirrors the surroundings in a green tint. Against the northern wall, a door leading to a library has a blue light above and a small plaque beside it. A pair of elevator doors line the southern wall and a long hallway goes north, spliting off in a few directions. There's another library door further west and another hallway beyond it.

The elevator to the upper levels lies in pieces across the stairs to the south. Large columns of broken glass remain standing in the corner of the room. A short row of benches line the wall of shattered windows. A small plaque is mounted near the elevator, but the rust has made it impossible to read.

Two long windows provide a view of Midgar's Sector 2, one of them has shattered and the glass covers the carpeted area. Some simple benches line the atrium railing, covered in grime. An overturned garbage can near the elevators to the south has settled against the eastern wall.

A large control panel lists the various floors available, however most of them are not lit. Yellow and black caution tape on the floor mark the demarcation zone and padded mats were provided for the security guards that once stood watch in this cab. Tether points for heavy machinery line the walls of this industrial lift. A large indicator above the door shows which floor the cab is currently on, but it's also unlit.

The plaque for the library has fallen onto the floor and the door frame leading into it has fractured. On the eastern wall, a large crack in the wall has allowed the elements into the area. Covered with pieces of broken ceiling panels, a large amount of debris has collected by the walls near the stairwell access to the southeast.

The light coming through the windows futher west is glaring off the reflective tile floor. The glare from the floor is illuminating the plaque for the library through the door. The elevator door seems to be inoperable, but a second lies to the east across from another library entrance. To the northwest, a small office and more hallways can be seen.

A large circular table is situated next to the windows, overlooking Sector 4 and some of Wall Market in Sector 5. Informational displays line the walls, but are not powered. The door on the eastern wall is labeled 'Training Room'. This room would have been appropriate as a large congregation area with its open and recessed layout.

A blue carpet covers the floor and silences the sound of footsteps. Against the eastern wall, rows of green bookshelves create small rows of walkable space and lights along the western wall give off a faint glow. Standing at the back of the room a small kiosk allows patrons to easily checkout books and the southern wall has a door leading out of the library.

Two large materia storage banks are on either side of the door leading into this room. Along the back wall there are multiple materia fusion chambers with various gauges and dials. The ventilation in this room must have been isolated, as the air is very stagnant. The floors are smooth, metallic, and relatively dust free, unlike the rest of the floor.

A large 'No Entry' sign hangs from the pipes overhead. The rattlings of rusting pipes echo off the side of the Shinra Tower and bare concrete, which has replaced the white marble of the plaza. Garbage has collected between the pipes and a damp smell fills the air. To the south a fire exit lit by a flickering lamp can be seen.

The center of the walkway appears to be made with a different material than the sidewalks surrounding it. Benches line the foundation of the building and the fence, providing plenty of space for people to wait for the next train. There is a small gap in the pipes behind the chain-link fence that grants a view of Sector 6 and 7. The train station security gate can be seen to the south and entrance to the Shinra Tower plaza is north.

In the center of the room a gigantic hole acts as a centerpiece. Access hatches line the northern wall and allow access to the electrical systems for the building. A small and obviously fake plant sits in the corner, near a support pillar. Conduits and pipes run along the pillar into the ceiling and floor.

Benches line the edges of the walkway, giving train passengers a spot to wait when things got busy at the train station. A large piece of debris from the top floor has crushed a few benches and blocks one side of the walkway. To the north, stairs wrapping around the corner of the building can be seen.

A small metal table is positioned between two benches. A little black, transparent dome on the ceiling directly above the table contains a security camera aimed squarely at the tabletop. Attached to the southern wall, thick pipes with directional flow arrows run from the floor below into the one above.

Splintered wood from crates and shattered glass from item displays cover the floor. The center island where the clerk would stand is brightly colored, but covered in dust. The inventory has been completely looted and there isn't anything of value in the store anymore.

The walls glow with a diffused light, generated by an array of projectors controlled by the Virtual Reality System. Headsets ready for use are hung near the door and each has a slight yellow glow about them. Supervisory displays line the western wall and there's a terminal near the door that controls the training programs.

The massive front doors of the Shinra Tower are overshadowed only by the equally large sign overhead: 'Shinra Electric Power Company'. Exposed metal beams from under the cracked granite wall tiles are rusted from years of exposure. The marble columns that once accentuated the haughty design of the vestibule are now reduced to piles of rubble.

A yellow carpet covers the floor and silences the sound of footsteps. Against the western wall, rows of red bookshelves create small rows of walkable space and small light fixtures hang, unpowered, from the eastern wall. Standing at the back of the room a small kiosk allows patrons to easily checkout books and the door on the southern wall leads out to a darkened hallway.

The stairs leading to the other floors of the building have collapsed. An incredible amount of debris from the upper levels has landed on the stairs leading down. Painted on the northern wall, a large number '62' is barely visible through the layer of dust and grime covering the walls. The southern wall is completely destroyed and has fallen into the connecting hallway.

A damaged platform with tire tracks leading towards a shattered Shinra sign is missing its exhibit. On the wall, pictures of an airship showcase the grand scale of the Highwind. Smaller components of the airship are displayed under the pictures and a small kiosk has more information on the nearby exhibits.

Sector 1 is visible through a large window, providing a view of city below. A small, fake plant sits under the window and is covered in dust. The decorative railing surrounding the hole in the middle of the room connects to a short column before continuing around. An inconspicuous security camera has been mounted near the support pillar in this corner of the room.

Rows of unlit recessed lights create a walkway that leads in from Sector 8. The stairs leading down to Loveless Avenue are blocked by an enormous piece of debris from the tower's top floors. Seemingly random floors of the Shinra Tower are lit, while entire portions are veiled in shadow. The entrance to the old headquarters is directly south and there appears to be a space between the pipes to the north.

A large scanning device acts as the entry point to the train station. Massive pipes line the walkway and would restrict movement if not for the 10 foot high chain-link fence. Large lights dot the side of the building which provided light in the shadow of the imposing Shinra Tower. The walkway follows the edge of the building to the north and east.

Large sections of the wall which seperate the hallway from the stairwell have collapsed. Rubble and debris has taken its stead. The tiled floor has deep grooves and scratches from where debris has been cleared. To the northwest, a small library waits at the beginning of a hallway leading west. Further south a pair of elevators are at the end of the hall.

The suspension system of one of Shinra's vehicles is on display in the corner. Large cylinders that contain mannequins wearing lavish clothing are the only displays that haven't been looted. A green carpet covers the floor and silences the sound of footsteps. A short row of uncomfortable looking seats lines the edge of the floor. The shattered Shinra sign can be seen over the edge. In the carpeted half of the room, two long tables are positioned in a V-shaped configuration around a very large display. A glass partition divides the room, keeping the area around the table quiet. Along the wall near the entrance, there are supply pods where mission relevant gear would be stored and a display where assignments could be viewed.

The walls are filled with old maps and outdated information that were likely often referenced after briefings. The hallway narrows as it leads north to the lobby and has a large door on the western wall labeled 'Materia Room'. Metal benches line the atrium window, unused for years.

The western wall is completely comprised of glass which stretches from the floor to the ceiling. However, a damning view of the the collapsed plate of Sector 7 is all that can be seen through the grand windows. An unapparent and trivial plaque is attached near the door to the Mayor's office, making it appear as if the space wasn't dedicated to him.

A large directory, the centerpiece of the lobby, still displays the departments and their location in this building. Beyond it a large shattered glass sign lies in pieces. The stairs leading up to the second floor act as walls in this portion of the lobby and are lined with small maintenance access doors.

The walkway narrows to the north and to the south, expands to include a vehicle path.

Reception benches line the railing, proving a simple function. The large hole behind them appears to go down to an atrium a few floors down. A relatively simple carpet lines the floor next to the benches, but doesn't continue all the way to the opposing wall.

On the western wall a fire exit is clearly marked. The decorative railing surrounding the atrium is unobstructed by benches or plants, providing easy viewing to the dead tree it harbors now. The open layout contributes to the original purpose of the floor being dedicated to the reception of visitors.

This desert is marked as one of the least hospitable places on the planet. The nearly endless assault of the sun is rarely disturbed by clouds, and the island has no geographical features that would provide any shade. Ocean fueled storms occasionally interrupt the grueling heat only to drowned the island in their fury. Unexpectedly a single lifeform thrives in the absurd environment: the cactuar.

Many deserts are impressive due to their massive size, this one is not. Cactus Island is a small, flat rock that happens to have enough sand on it to resemble a classic desert. The harsh sun bakes the sands during the day and cold ocean breezes brings a chill to the bone in the evening. This is not a life-friendly environment, however, the legendary cactuar calls it home.

rooms.name: Blasted Wasteland, Next to the Crevice

userData.LongDescription: Any hope of westward travel has been completely closed off here, blocked by the wide crevice that runs beside this area.  It appears as though the Mako Reactor accident created a forcewave strong enough to split the ground, resulting in this crevice.  Sand and dirt still comprise the land, and slightly larger chunks of wrecked metal lie about in seemingly random places.  There are more pieces of the Reactor across the chasm, jutting out of the earth.  There's enough room to continue north, east, or south.

rooms.name: Around the Mako Reactor, Dead End

userData.LongDescription: Coming around the corner reveals nothing more than a dead end.  The devastation continues here, but passage further into the remains of the Mako facility are blocked off by heaps of rubble and steel that probably weigh tons.  Unfortunately, there is nothing more that can be done here.  The only exit lies to the southwest.

The wasteland ends abruptly here, as the lifeless ground is once again swallowed by the impassable forest and underbrush.  As such, movement to the south or east is impossible from here, but the way north and west are open.  The Reactor can still be seen quite easily, standing as a broken monument to the fate of Mako Energy extraction.

The interior of the inn is in FAR better shape than the exterior might lead one to believe.  Though small, the inn is kept tidy and neat, and there is a doorway separating the main room from the beds.  A heavy curtain can be drawn for privacy, and there appear to be two comfortable looking beds in the back.  The innkeeper is sitting at a small table, playing solitaire and keeping an eye on things.  A small orange chest lies in one corner of the room, its lid open.  A small wall mounted lamp burns cheerfully, providing plenty of light.  On the table is a small sign.

Here lies all that remains of the once functioning Mako Reactor.  Gauges and dials cover its surface, but none of them are even remotely close to being in working order.  The door to the reactor has been pried open, and the interior core appears to be an empty glass tube.  Judging by how there is a slight rise in the floor, it appears that the floor was once a catwalk that collapsed from high above and settled here.  The roof of the Reactor has been blown open, revealing a calm blue sky line.  A few more outlines can be seen here, as well as wrecked monitoring stations and other types of Shinra equipment.  There is enough room on the catwalk-turned-floor to head off to the northwest or northeast, around the perimeter of the Reactor.  The exit of the entire facility lies to the south.

rooms.name: Around the Mako Reactor, Dead End

userData.LongDescription: The make-shift corridor comes to an end here, as the wreckage becomes too cluttered and concentrated to push ahead any further.  The open-air roof gives a good look at the calm sky line, a drastic contrast to the devastation all around.  The side of the reactor is visible here, blackened and burnt from the explosion.  The only way to go is back to the southeast.

This is a small, cozy house.  A small fireplace burns cheerfully over on the right wall, and a small wooden counter has been set up.  A young woman stands behind the counter, humming to herself and keeping things tidy.  There are several shelves here, but they're either empty or hold personal items.  There is a sign on the counter.

rooms.name: Blasted Wasteland, Next to the Crevice

userData.LongDescription: The wasteland continues here, only to be suddenly interrupted by a large crack that runs through the very earth.  It appears that the force of the explosion was so great that it managed to create a forty or so foot wide crevice.  Across the divide, one can see more twisted wreckage and broken metal.  The crevice snakes around enough to cut off any movement to the south, but the way north and east are still open.

A small dirt road runs through the jungle and vegetation here.  All around are high grasses and scrub, with only the dirt path to mark any sign of others having been here before.  A few trees supply gentle shade from the sun's rays, and large boulders occasionally jut out of the ground at odd angles.  The trail comes to a fork and then splits into three directions.  To the northeast the path begins to incline towards a small hill top, while the path northwest continues along deeper into the scrublands.  There is also a glowing blue portal that hangs just off to the southeast.  A small sign has been hammered into the ground where the path forks.

The featureless wasteland continues here, especially this close to the Ground Zero of the Reactor's explosion.  Now, dirty sand covers the once lush territory, and pieces of the Reactor lie about.  The forests rise up against the wasteland here, barring any passage to the north.  However, the way to the east and south are clear, and to the west, the entrance to the Reactor can be seen.

This is roughly the center of the wasteland.  There's very little out here, unless one were to start counting all of the pieces of metal that lay strewn about.  Soft breezes blow dirt and sand about, and the Reactor stands quietly to the north.  There's a large crevice off to the west, but the angle here makes it look smaller than it truly is.  The forest rises up to the east and south, but does not intrude into this devastated land.

The wasteland continues here, and there is still no evidence that the planet has had any success with reclaiming the area.  Dirty sand blows about, creating tiny dustdevils and occasionally revealing a bit of bone.  Fragments of the dead Reactor clutters the area, and the forest begins to loom closer to the east.  A broken sign lies half buried in the dirt here, but still looks legible.

rooms.name: Blasted Wasteland, Approaching the Reactor's Entrance

userData.LongDescription: The wasteland continues right up to the entrance of the Reactor, which is only a few feet away.  The once heavy doors are blasted and gone so that only jagged husks now remain.  There is a higher concentration of wreckage here, and extremely large pieces of metal cover the ground.  A sign that once hung from the top of the entrance is lying on the ground, broken and half covered in dirt.  One could go into the reactor from here, or head back south, west, or east.

The dusty path continues to the northeast, but just before it enters the village proper, it makes a quick jaunt into a small graveyard.  Looking past that, there are 5 huts that are visible, and small plumes of smoke vent out through chimneys.  The village seems almost deserted, but there is an old man pacing back and forth in the graveyard.  The path leads north into Gongaga, or back to the southwest.

From atop this hill, one can see down into the valley where the Shinra Mako Reactor is... or rather, what's left of it.  Even at this distance, it is rather apparent that the reactor exploded, and the surrounding area has been stripped clean of any types of plant life.  The division between where the influence of the reactor's explosion begins and ends is quite obvious, as there is a tree that still lives just off to the right of the path.  Five feet past the tree... there is nothing more than sand and bits of metal.  To the left of the path is an arch of metal that apparently impacted with such force that it has become permanently embedded into a rock.  The path continues into the wasteland to the north, or back down the hill to the southwest.

This is the Center of Gongaga Village.  Five small huts are arranged in a roughly circular pattern, and two of them have small plumes of smoke trailing out of their chimneys.  The hut in the southeastern corner of the village looks dilapidated and abandonded, but the rest look inhabited.  According to the signs over their doors, the westernmost hut is an inn, whereas the centermost hut is an accessory shop.  Next door to that is the item shop.  The mood hanging over this town does not appear to be a cheerful one, and all of the huts are damaged in some fashion.  Off in the distance lies more forest, and also an unobstructed view of the destroyed Mako Reactor.

The interior of this house is not as cramped as some of the other huts appear to be, judging by their dimensions.  It is well furnished, even if the inside appears to be somewhat run down.  A small carpet covers the right side of the room, and a dining table with two chairs stands on the left.  The back wall holds a small, burning lamp that is currently providing all of the light in the room, and just to the right of it is an armoire.  Between the armoire and the lamp is an open, orange chest.  There is a broken set of stairs over in the far right corner, but with the upper floor having crashed down, they no longer lead anywhere.  On the right side of the room is a writing desk, but instead of stationery, there's a model of the Mako Reactor.  A barrel sits next to the desk, and various shelves holding books are scattered throughout the room.

The corridor ends here at the mouth of the main Reactor room.  Along the corridor are pieces of broken equipment, unidentifiable pools of slag, and blasted outlines.  A metal sign that once hung above the remains of the Reactor room's door lies on the ground.  Due to all the wreckage and jagged metal, passage is limited to going north or south.

The division between the lifeless wasteland and the teeming forest comes to a head here, as one gives way to the other.  The thick vegetation makes further travel east impossible, so movement is restricted to going north, west, or south.  The land surrounding the Reactor is covered in sand and dirt, and a few large pieces of metal lay half-buried here.  The Reactor itself lies off to the northwest.

The area surrounding the Mako Reactor is dull and lifeless.  Brief gusts of wind kick up some of the sand and grit, which will occasionally reveal bits of metal or even bone.  No plant life seems to have any chance of surviving out here, almost as if the planet has given up hope on this place.  To the north the Reactor looms silently, while to the east and west the wasteland continues.  There is also the trail that leads south, back to the hill.  Off to the west is a wide crevice which is far too wide to jump across.

rooms.name: Blasted Wasteland, Next to the Crevice

userData.LongDescription: The large crevice originates from here, and is at its widest point just beside the burnt out Reactor.  It tapers slightly as it winds its way off to the southwest, right through the wasteland that the accident created.  While the crevice is quite wide, the reactor itself is large enough so that it is not in any risk of falling into the precipice.  There is a high concetration of twisted steel and other types of metal here, as well as a few pieces of concrete.  Passage is blocked by the side of the burnt out Reactor to the north, and the chasm to the west.  This leaves the east and south as the only unobstructed exits.

A long corridor has been created out of the rubble and twisted steel that litters the ground here.  What appears to have been an office wing has been completely cut off, and there isn't a single piece of working machinery left.  The floor is covered with dust and soot, but upon a second look it appears to be comprised of concrete.  Scraps of something still cling to certain parts of the floor, but it's sparse at best.  The only exits are back out to the wasteland, or further north down the hallway.

This cramped, but cozy little store does not show any of the damage that its exterior has suffered.  There is a counter a few feet away from the door, and behind it stands the shopkeeper.  Behind him are shelves stuffed with various items that are for sale.  There is also a hatrack on the right side of the room.  The shopkeeper flips through a book to pass the time, and a sign rests on the counter.

The wasteland continues here, heading off to the north, east, and west.  Far to the north, the burnt out Reactor looms silently, and there is impassable forest to the south.  Sand and dirt covers the area, denying any hope of plants surviving here.  Small bits of metal glint in the sun, and short gusts of wind occasionally blow them around.

The wasteland comes to something of a naturally imposed 'corner' here.  The forest blocks any further hope at progressing to the east or north, leaving only the west and south open for movement.  The dirty, sand covered land seems almost in pain as the planet slowly, over years and years, attempts to re-take it.  The reactor is off to the west, and pieces of it lie scattered about the area.

The path continues into a more wooded area.  Ferns and miniature palm trees, along with other leafy plants, line the trail which splits once again to the northeast and to the northwest.  A few trees have been uprooted and are lying about just off the path, and overhead a particularly large tree has fallen across the path.  Luckily it hit a large rock outcropping and is suspended high enough so that it does not impede movement.  A few pieces of metallic trash lie abandoned at the fork, most of which has rusted and corroded.  A small village can be seen up the northeastern path, and the path to the northwest continues deeper into the forest until it hits a natural barrier of plant life and rocks.  The only other path lies to the southeast.

Cropped grass lilts in a crisp breeze as it rings the eastern half of the island, framed by a forest and shoals to the west and a sloping beach to the east.  Thin peninsulas extend off the north and south edges of the island, though the southern peninsula is decidedly more mangy in its appearance.
To your west is a small staircase that leads to the top of Fort Condor. To your east is a small rope ladder that leads back to the main area of Fort Condor. Right next to the stairs are a few pipes.

You have entered the cave entrance to Fort Condor. There are three torches on the walls, so the cave is well lit. A few drops of water drip on your head as you look up to see nothing. Up north you see a rope leading up.

You look at your surroundings and find yourself to be standing in front of a large, moss-covered mountain. At the top you can see an old-style Mako Reactor with a huge condor perched at the top of it. To the north, a path leads you to a cave.

You stand in front of another rope ladder that seems to lead down into another room. Looking down the hole in which the ladder goes through, you see a bedpost right next to the ladder. It must be the inn.

Outside the door, this rooftop is at the very top of the building, where the huge condor resides. This is what used to be the old reactor, or at least the main part of it.  Bullet holes and burn marks cover the walls, telling tales of the past battles when Shinra repeatedly attacked to retake their reactor.

You now stand before a rounded threshhold. On top of the threshhold is a blue arrow pointing up. Looking at the wall you see it is made of bolted steel plates. Looks sorta like a building Shinra would have made. A rope-ladder leads up.

You seem to be right in the middle of the area. You can see almost everything from this spot: The well south, the pipes west, and the stairs leading to the second section. Up north there seems to be a rope ladder.

Now having climbed the rope ladder, you stand east of a small set of stairs that leads to the surface of Fort Condor. Hanging above you is an orange colored light that seems to illuminate the whole small room.

You finish climbing yet another rope ladder and find yourself in the merchants area. To the west is the item shop and to the east is the materia shop. Looking behind you you find curtains hanging on walls without windows. You figure it must be an advertisement thing.

After ascending a set of stairs you find yourself in a small wooden shack. There's a wide window, where you can see for a pretty long distance. This appears to be the watchtower where they watch out for Shinra attacks. There's a door here, and stairs that leads back to the main area.

rooms.name: Entrance to Fort Condor - Cave: 2nd Floor

userData.LongDescription: Right in front of you stands a tall rope-ladder leading into Fort Condor. You can still see the pipes from the other end of the cave. The hole in which the ladder goes through seems brighter than the cave you are in. The rope-ladder leading up seems sturdy. To the west is the rope leading back to the exit

This is the Fort Condor Item Shop. One of the rebels of Fort Condor stands behind the desk. Behind him are empty shelves and more curtains. There's three small lights shining down on the counter. There's a small sign here.

rooms.name: Fort Condor - Entrance to Merchant Area.

userData.LongDescription: Directly to your left and right are bright neon signs indicating that up above is an item shop and a materia shop. Directly in front of you is another of Fort Condor's famous rope ladders.

You have ascended the stairs to your southwest. Right in front of you is a blue vending machine. There's a little piece of paper with 'Out of Order' written on it. Doesn't look like it's been re-stocked in a while anyways.
Right to the south of you is a small water well. The ground surrounding the cement bricks that form the well is muddy, and you happen to be standing right in the mud.

To your right is a set of wooden stairs leading up to the rest of Fort Condor. You kick it a little, still unsure of this place's stability, and hear a slight creaking noise. To your south is a table with some chairs.

This is the Fort Condor Equipment Shop. One of the rebels of Fort Condor stands behind the desk. Behind him are empty glass cabinets and empty jars. Hanging above his head is a small ceiling lamp. There's a sign here.

This section of Fort Condor's exterior is the home of the magnificent and enormous condor, which is as large as a small house.  It is sitting on a huge pink egg, which is being held up by a round metal structure. The condor looks to be asleep at the moment.

rooms.name: Entrance to Fort Condor - Path to Cave

userData.LongDescription: The cave entrance is here, yawning like a giant waking from a century long nap.  The mountain obscures the top limiting any chance of seeing the true purpose of this base.  The moss continues to be plentiful here. South is the main entrance.
The cave is still well lit. You now stand right in front of the rope that leads up. Giving the rope a few good tugs, you decide it is safe to continue. The humidity in here is really bad.

At the bottom of the ladder, there are several beds with weird patterns on the bedsheets, and a little nightstand below each bed. South of them is a nice little couch, and looking up one can see a ceiling light. There's a sign here with a bucket right next to it.

To your right is an old table with three three-legged chairs surrounding it. On top of the table is an old oil lamp. You think this is probably where they plan their defense against Shinra. To the west is the well, and north leads to the rest of Fort Condor.

rooms.name: Entrance to Fort Condor - Cave: 2nd Floor

userData.LongDescription: After climbing the rope safely, you find yourself in yet another cave. You wonder if the builders had an ant farm in mind while building making it. In this are two torches and some rusted pipes coming out of the wall. To the east is a rope ladder.

You stand directly south of a small room with a ladder leading up to the Item and the Materia shops. You know this because there's a huge neon green sign that says ITEM in the shape of a box, and a yellow sign that probably says Materia in Japanese.

You emerge from the small enclosed area and now you can see most of the area known as Fort Condor. It looks like a Mako Reactor turned into a rebel hideout. You hope that ugly, huge condor on the top isn't their cause. There are more pipes to your left.

A range of high mountains can be seen far off to the northwest, but with the current conditions, reaching them would be nearly impossible.

While this snowy path is much like the many other numerous paths in Great Glacier, what it connects is very different than usual. West is a path that winds along the base of a long range of mountains, while east is an absolutely massive snow field. The field stretches for as far as the eye can see, which isn't very far considering the blizzard there is blowing harder than anyplace else. Further travel east is not advisable in the least.

rooms.name: Great Glacier - Path to a Cave

userData.LongDescription: A small slope separates the western road from the entrance to a cave. The cave is located on the side of a mountain and looks to be a safe, if cold place to rest. A huge pile of rocks block the southern exit, leaving the western road to be the only open path. Strangely, even though the blizzard has calmed down a great deal from the snow field, there are no animal tracks or signs of wildlife.

The little outcropping of the lake has lead to this dead end. The only way to go now is back southeast, away from the lake. There's a small island with a cave on it in the middle of the lake, but it's impossible to reach it. There may have been a land bridge at one point that connected the outcropping to the island, but if there was one there before, it's long gone now.

The snowboarding slope has now taken a turn into a glistening cave. Numerous stalactites hang from the ceiling, looking dangerously unstable and ready to plunge into the skull of an unsuspecting snowboarder. A few stalagmites also stick out of the ground here and there along the sides of the slope, ready to trip up anyone who can't move out of the way in time. Another fork in the slope is approaching rapidly, and it looks like this one decides where travellers are spit out into the maze that is Great Glacier.

The inside of the cave, besides being small and cramped, is also exceedingly cold. It looks like the cave was used as some sort of shelter sometime in the past, though, for a small tent is set up in the middle of the room. There are also a couple of icicles hanging off the ceiling, just waiting to fall and give someone a nasty cut.

The only ways to go are west, which leads to a lake near the center of Great Glacier, and south, which leads further up the side of a small mountain.

This is quite an odd area. Numerous pillars of ice stick up out of the ground, restricting travel in many directions. A small cave rests in the center of the area, able to provide protection from the weather when needed. The cave doesn't look like it's been used in a while, though. The normally fierce blizzard that blows in most of Great Glacier has died down a bit here, making this an ideal spot to rest.

The interior of this cave is very awe inspiring indeed. The walls of the cave are covered in a shiny layer of ice, providing for a spectacular light show when the sun shines through the hole at the top of the cave. Huge stalactites hang from the ceiling, giving the cave a very ancient and mysterious feeling to it. Further up in the cave is an opening that looks like it might have led out of here at some point, however, the path to the opening is blocked with a huge pile of rocks, so it's no longer possible to exit via that way.

A furious blizzard blows in the snow field, cutting vision down to only a few feet in all directions. Every direction looks the same, snow everywhere. The snow field itself is huge, covering the northern half of Great Glacier. The danger here is so great that more travellers have been lost in the field than have died due to the beasts that roam the land, so extreme caution is advised to those crossing.

This is quite a dangerous room. Looking over the side of the path, a strange green glow can be seen below. This may mean that the cave is infused with mako energy. A few icicles hang overhead, threatening to drop and skewer someone. Going north on the path leads under a low overhanging and to a dead end. Going south leads to the second level of the cave's entrance.

The walls in this room have taken a strange, pale purple glow to them. The source of this glow is unknown, but it may be related to the green glow in another part of the cave. Other than the unusual walls, this is an unremarkable room. A hole in the southern wall leads outside, and the western exit leads to some sort of ice filled room.

It looks like this platform was once much bigger than it is now. The jagged edge on the right side makes it look like part of the platform broke off sometime in the past. The remaining part looks steady enough to rest on, though. It's possible to climb up and down the rock wall with a bit of work.

The fierce wind that blows along the entire rock wall has become even more violent up this far. The wind threatens to blow climbers right off the wall, and the snow blowing around obscures climbing routes and makes it difficult to see anything. In fact, if it weren't for the red flags planted at every platform, it might be impossible to scale the cliff. The usual hand and footholds mark out routes going up and down.

This particular climbing path has led to a dead end. Although it's possible to go back west with some cautious climbing, it's impossible to go up the cliff any more via this route. As it is, this tiny platform is too unstable to even provide a good resting place. The gusty wind and shaky ground make it dangerous to stay here an extended period of time.

This is the base of Gaea's Cliff. The huge rock wall that covers the entire northern area is in fact the main part of the cliff itself. The only way to get on top of the cliff is to climb it, bit by bit. Looking up, it's impossible to tell how tall the rock wall is. Going south leads first to a house, then to a massive snow field.

A rather expansive cave appears to be inside of Gaea's Cliff. Other than a few rocks scattered about, the room looks bare. A second level is in this particular section of the cave, but reaching it from here is impossible. A small opening in the southern part of the room leads outside, while going north and under an archway leads further into the cave.

Another platform sticks out of the rock wall for climbers to rest upon. A red flag is planted in the ground, marking out the platform as safe to rest on. It is impossible to tell how far up the cliff this platform is, and the remaining distance to the peak is also unknown. The wall of the cliff has become more and more unsteady the higher it is, and before long it may become too dangerous to climb.

This particular platform is much bigger than most of the others on the wall. And even stranger, the sun is starting to peek out through the clouds. This may mean that the summit of the cliff is close by. Looking up, no more platforms can be seen. Instead, going up leads into the entrance to a cave. Going down can also be accomplished by using the hand and footholds that appear at regular intervals.

The typical red flag marks the presence of another platform for climbers to rest upon. Looking down, all that can be seen are clouds and snow blowing around, the ground is much too far to see. A few shaky looking hand and footholds going up lead not to another platform, but to a cave entrance in the very rock wall itself. Of course, going down is also possible through another set of holds.

Despite the fact that this is the house's bedroom, there is no bed in here. The only place to sleep at is a small loft just above the room. A crate and a few empty bottles litter the floor, giving the impression that no one has cleaned up in quite some time. A few blankets and pillows are up in the loft, providing at least some comfort for those willing to sleep here. A small can is also up in the loft with a sign sitting beside it.

This rather small platform provides little room to rest for climbers. In fact, if it wasn't for the usual red flag planted in the ground, it would be all but invisible. It is now impossible to see the ground from this height, and it is still impossible to see the top of Gaea's Cliff. Familiar looking hand and footholds mark ways up and down from this platform.

This is the other side of the crystal room, seperated by a row of ice crystals. Many more of the crystals stick out of the ground, and most of these are even larger than the others. They look like they're quite sharp, so caution is advised around them. A path south leads to the other side of the crystal room. Going east, on the other hand, leads to a rather open space.

The inside of the house, although quite small, is the most welcome thing for miles around. The contents of the living room consist of a ragged couch, a shelf full of bottles, a table covered with various nick-nacks, a couple of guns in the corner, and a large bearskin rug on the floor. A short staircase leads to the only bedroom of the house.

A small platform in the rock wall provides a rest spot of sorts for those climbing up Gaea's Cliff. The platform is small, and if it wasn't for the flag planted in the ground, it might be nearly impossible to see. Hand and footholds mark out a way up the rock wall, and it's possible to go down with a bit of strategic climbing.

This is the second level of the cave's entrance. Although the ground floor of the entrance isn't that far down, it's impossible to get down from here because of the slick floor and icy walls. On the western side of the room, there's a small hole that leads down to another area. Going north leads to an archway and another exit.

Another platform is carved into the rock wall, this one a bit larger than normal. A flag is also planted into the ground to mark the platform as safe for climbers. It's becoming harder and harder to see the ground on the higher platforms, and a fall from this height will almost certainly prove fatal. More hand and footholds mark paths up and down the wall.

A red flag marks out the presence of a platform sticking out of the rock wall. Also carved into the rock wall is the entrance to a cave. Peering inside, it looks like the cave goes quite a way inside of the cliff. With some careful climbing, it's possible to go up the wall some distance. A route is also available that goes east instead.

The air is noticeably cooler here. This may be due to the fact that there's very little circulation around. Other than an odd indentation in the ground, there is absolutely nothing in this room. The indentation in the ground looks like something was once sitting in it something heavy. The path south, back through the overhanging, is the only way out of this dead end.

Out of all the rooms in the cave, this is the most spectacular. Numerous ice crystals sprout out of the ground, and while they may be beautiful to look at, they impede travel somewhat. A crystal lined path leads north, while the exit south leads back towards the entrance to the cave. In the southwest corner of the room, a small upwards slope looks like it leads to a different floor.

rooms.name: Great Glacier - Base of Gaea's Cliff

userData.LongDescription: A long, winding path leads from the end of the snow field to the base of Gaea's Cliff. Along the path, on the right side, sits a cozy looking house. It is unknown why anyone would build a house out in the middle of nowhere, but it's a welcome sight for those preparing to scale the cliff. A tall tower also stands beside the house with a flag attached to the top to gauge what direction the wind is blowing in.

A long balcony spans along the north wall of this elaborate foyer, the eastern-most point being where you now stand.  A red door leads through the wall to the northeast.  Immediately beside the door stands a plant in a vase.  Following the wooden ledge to the northwest leads to the Don's office, while a staircase leads down to the main entrance.

rooms.name: At The Door To Corneo's Quarters

userData.LongDescription: To the north, a wide red and yellow door stands guard, beyond which lies the Don's office.  Bright light seems to be heavily concentrated on this area, placing you directly in the spotlight for the moment.  The balcony leads southwest to a dark open doorway, or southeast towards the staircase.

A small cobblestone entrance way leads into an extravagant foyer filled with fancy decorations.  The floor is made from polished mahogany wooden planks which glamorously reflect the beams of light shining upon them.  A reception desk is set up to the west, while a staircase leads up to a balcony which spans the north wall.

A cold cobblestone floor is illuminated by an eerie blue hue of light.  A stone fireplace is in the northwest corner of the room, full of red hot coals.  In the center of the room there is a wide table large enough for the average person to lie down upon.  In the northeast corner a metal chair stands tall.  Along the south wall, various tools and instruments are laid out neatly upon the counter.

The west end of the balcony offers an open doorway leading to a stone staircase.  A vase has been placed just to the left of the doorway.  Directly beneath the balcony, the reception desk sits downstairs on the main floor.  To the northeast, the entrance to the Don's quarters awaits.

A privacy screen erected just inside the open doorway provides some element of secrecy.  On the centre of the floor is a very large bed, beneath which lies a decorative rug.  The room itself is octagonal in shape, full of furniture, and is illuminated with a bright lamp.

This is the den of the mansion, which is where the master's lackeys spend their free time lounging.  The room itself bends around the northeast corner.  Against the eastern wall, a few mats are laid out with pillows.  Meanwhile to the north, a gaming table has been set up beside a tiny television set.  In the center of the room there is a dinner table.  While it is quite elegantly decorated with fancy pots and exquisite rugs, the whole place is littered with trash and is in a disastrous state of disarray.

From wall to wall, planks of wood are tightly aligned to form an exquisite hardwood floor.  A carpet makes its way between several elaborate statues all the way from the southern doorway to a modest looking desk sitting in the center of the room.  A mere curtain stands between this office and another room to the north.

The way up or down the stairs is scantily illuminated by four tiny torches mounted and spaced evenly along the wall.  The walls and steps are formed from dark black cobblestone.  Through the doorway at the top of the staircase, warm light gently aids in lighting the way up.  Meanwhile, a strange blue glow is emitted from the basement floor at the bottom.

Several pipes reach down the northeast wall to connect to a large green tank.  One of them runs horizontally and has a red wheel attached.  Both the wall and the outer layer of the tank itself are made of green bricks.  A fence, with a wide gap in it, runs from the northwestern wall and across the tank, connecting to the edge of a sidewalk which begins immediately to the southeast.

Two pipes emerge from the ground at the end of the walkway, which funnel waste to its inevitable destination.  A lamp hangs on the wall, providing a light source to the nearby area.  A ladder descends down into the sewage channel.

rooms.name: At The Top Of A Staircase

userData.LongDescription: The sidewalk comes to an abrupt ending immediately to the southeast.  Immediately before the wall there is a pile of old tires that have not been disposed of properly.  A staircase nearby offers an invitation to wade through the green stream below.  On the opposite side of the channel, a ladder looks like it leads up and out of the sewer.

This sidewalk overlooks a channel of flowing sewage running towards the southeastern wall, and leads northwest from here.  A long pipe with a red wheel attached to it bends here, running both horizontally to a massive tank to the northwest as well as directly up to the ceiling.  A sign has been posted behind the pipe.  A ladder climbs the wall to the northwest straight up a manhole.

A walkway leads northwest alongside the sewer channel, while a large dumpster sits at the corner of the bend, overflowing with trash.  A set of stairs descends into the flowing waste.  Along the wall up above, a long pipe stretches to the end of the sidewalk.

The walkway leads northwest and northeast from here.  Both directions lead to ladders which allow access to the sewage.  A grate crosses the channel of waste, but is too slippery to walk along.  A paper note has been posted on the wall.

The walkway comes to an end here, concluding with a pile of debris.  A large grate on the northwestern wall has been broken wide open, but it's too high up to gain access.  A pile of rat droppings sits in a pool of yellow fluid.  To the southeast a staircase leads down into the sewage.

The running sewage gradually flows through a rusted metal grate on the northeastern wall.  To the southwest a staircase leads up to a sidewalk on the southeastern side of the channel.  A ladder is here, leading up on the opposing side.

Directly above you is the opening to a air vent that tunnels its way into the ceiling.  A sidewalk overlooks a channel of flowing sewage which slowly drifts to the southeast.  On the other side of the channel, there is a large tank which looks climbable.  To the southeast the walkway leads to a staircase leading down into the waste.

Liquid sewage rises waist deep in this underground moat and runs to the southeast.  On the northeast wall a ladder offers reprieve.  Just to the right of it, a pipe emerges from the brick wall which continues to dump more waste into the channel.

A waterfall of waste continuously falls over balcony to the northwest.  A very large green tank lies to the northeast, with a broken fence line running along the top.  It looks to have a texture with enough friction to climb.  The grotesque river flows to the southeast.

Immediately to the southeast, a large grate filters the large pieces of trash out of the fluids which gently flow through it.  There is a massive collection of garbage that is being accumulated on this side of the rusty bars.  Upstream to the northwest, a  large green tank dumps a small stream of waste into the river.

The sewage flowing from upstream bends to the northeast and begins to flow through an impassable metal grate.  Some steps lead out of the liquid waste and lead up to a sidewalk which oversees the channel from the southwest.  Travelling against the gentle current to the northwest is the only other option.

A concrete walkway leads northeast from here towards an open ventilation system.  A staircase leads down into a river of flowing waste.  To the southwest a grate blocks any travel.  On the other side of it is a large pile of trash beside a dumpster.

The river of green waste bends around a corner here as it flows in gently from the southwest through a rusted metal grate.  The floor of the channel has a gradual slope to the northeast, which is where the sewage continues its journey.  A staircase leads up to a sidewalk overlooking the channel from the southeast.

rooms.name: At The Top Of A Ladder

userData.LongDescription: A concrete walkway leads southeast towards a bend in the underground sewage channel.  A refrigerator occupies the dead end to the northwest.  A ladder leads down into the channel.  A lamp protrudes from the wall nearby, illuminating the area.

At the end of the walkway, immediately before the northeast wall, an open ventilation duct emerges from the concrete.  Just down over the edge of the sidewalk, in the sewage river, a large pile of garbage has accumulated in front of the filtration grate.  To the southwest, a staircase descends into the green filth.

The designs on the walls glow a bright fiery orange. Statues of fierce monstrosities stand on the edges of the platform. A strange pattern is carved into the ground, almost beckoning to be examined. The boiling, glowing lava surrounds the platform. The room seems to be untouched by the ravaging blizzard outside.

The entrance to the Sun Palace seems quite warm. In the distance, towering statues can be seen, but it is difficult to make out what the statues are. A small rock lies next to the door of the palace. The snow keeps falling heavily, making seeing quite difficult. The surrounding, desolate oceans are frozen over.

The slippery ground is covered in snow and ice. An enormous heap of rocks sits on the floor, almost serving as a marker. To the north, a huge, deserted, shining palace can be seen. A treacherous crater lies quietly on the western side of the road. An abandoned robot rusts away on the right side of the road.

A large pedestal stands in the center of the room, as if something of great importance had been left on it. Two statues surround the pedestal. Strange engravings on the walls seem to call out. Swirls of fire dance near the ceiling, upheld by some magical force. The simmering lava seems to be not as hot here.

The murals on the walls seem to depict the sun burning brightly, and then falling to the moon. Steaming lava surrounds the walkway. Statues of monsters line the walkway on its edges. A layer of dust has descended on the floor. The palace seems to be isolated from the outside quite well. The air is shimmering constantly, because of the heat.

A small fence has been built here in place of the larger original fence that was vandalized by escapees. The land visible outside of the fence looks impossible for travel. The many desert winds blow strong and are blinding to any type of directional sense. The hopes of any travelers surviving look impossible.

An old green truck with a rusty trailer and broken headlights rests beside a rusted pipe structure. The pipe structure continues northeast where it is attached to an old cabin. The blistering sun beats down on broken wood and tires on the ground.
The only light that can been seen in here is from the eerie rays of

Though this cabin is not in horrible shape, those who have passed by must have been afraid to go inside out of fear of the roof caving in. A worn bed is set along one side of the room and a couch with many tears in it sits opposite the bed. The floor has small holes in it but is still holding out. The ceiling looks weak but is also managing to hold strong so far. A cracked and rusted wood stove stands across from the door.

A large fence surrounds this area. The heat is nearly unbearable as the sun beats down from the empty, cloudless sky, blinding and silent. Lots of shady characters roam this secluded land, eyeing around for any kind of treasure they can find. Two burly men stand in front of a rusty trailer keeping a sharp eye out for any suspicious activity.

The rotten roof of the cabin is creaking and it appears to be about to cave in. The windows have cracked from the pressure, but they have not yet shattered. The walls still look sturdy and the frame is firm. The door is closed and still in fair condition. A large cactus grows beside the cabin, just inside the small fence that surrounds it. Bricks form a walkway leading to the door.

Broken boxes, barrels, and other junk litter the ground. A rusty pipe structure connects a dusty cabin to an odd blue vehicle. A warm, dry wind blows small dirt clouds through the air, making the land seem very barren. A large dust devil can be seen on the other side of the fence where it clouds any sense of direction for those who would dare venture there.

This abandoned well dried out long ago. Two green barrels are down here along with some other worthless junk. A breeze blows down from above, making the dark well feel much more comfortable than the desert above. The stone walls even have a little bit of moss growing on them. The only way out seems to be back up the ladder.

A eerie glow is being emitted from a well that was once used as the source of the village's water supply. As wasted as the land is, the well is most likely dried out and no longer in use. Two broken pipes run outward from the well to lie neglected and rusted in the desert heat. The road around the well is rather clean, decorated with not a single scrap of garbage.

A well kept road leads to the northeast, where a cabin can be seen in the distance. This road is smooth and clean. The lack of any life gives the land a barren appearance. The dry air and burning sun still make this a very uncomfortable place to wander. The lack of anyone hanging around in this particular section of the prison makes the place feel calm and almost peaceful.

A small wooden fence surrounds two cabins that look like they were once set on fire. A village of some sort may have resided here, long ago when the desert was still lush and green. Pipes are constructed in and out of the ground, polluting the land with mako energy and sucking the life out of it, causing it to become a vast wasteland.

A pile of junky cars is stacked in front of the fence, blocking any view of the outside desert. There appear to be some motorcycles and other parts for vehicles of unknown origin strewn about. If the parts were not packed away here in the desert, one could probably put together a fabulous machine or vehicle. There is an unrecognizable pile of melted metal near the bottom of the pile.

High above, the towering structure of the Gold Saucer casts a shadow on this portion of the Corel desert, providing a cool spot in an otherwise suffocating heat.  Sand stretches as far as the eyes can see in almost any direction save for back through the gate to the Corel Prison.

The floor of this trailer is covered in old torn car mats. Ripped clothes serve as drapery for this establishment and boxes as tables and counters.
