This room is the most decorative place in this prison. This place must harbor someone of some importance. The foundation seems to be very sturdy compared to its outside appearance. The trailer is definately well-maintained.

Piles of ashes cover the floor of this small cabin. The walls and ceiling have been completely burned out. All of the indoor furniture, or what remained of it, was removed after the fire. The sun beats down powerfully through the roofless cabin.

A large metal structure resides to the left with more pipes protruding from it. A yellow car sits on the other side of the pipes, rusted and broken. Two dirtballs the size of large rocks lie in the northwestern and southeastern corners. Cigarette butts are scattered on the ground amongst other garbage.

A ruined sign lies fading and rotting on the ground. A large rock rests near the middle of the area in the moistureless desert sand. Some pipes attached to a cabin descend into ground that looks as if it has not seen water in years, though some softer sand can be seen farther from the pipes near the rock. The blazing sun continues to beat down on the barren land and its miserable inhabitants.

This is the most active area in the prison. The prisoners walk by here everyday, which also makes it one of the more dangerous places. Groups of prisoners seem to be occupying themselves with various activities and conversations. The sun beats down here the most, so the air is hot and dry, making the environment uncomfortable and dessicated. A cautious eye should be kept when passing through here.

Three odd tents made of various torn fabrics reside behind the trailer. The patchwork on them is awful and their only purpose appears to be covering the boxes and appearing to look like tents. The ground is cracked and dry, making it look barren and rock-hard. The trailer's position here shades this area, making it seem cooler. Two small boxes have been set up for chairs and one larger box for a table.

An old, worn down cabin stands here with a rusty pipe protruding from it and continuing south. The windows in the cabin have all been broken and cobwebs have formed where the glass once was. The door is hanging on its hinges and may break off at any moment. Some activity can be heard in the center of the prison. The cabin, however, remains silent.

This is a dark, secluded corner of the prison. A large reactor stretches towards the sky, blocking out some of the hot sun. The building's massive shadow makes this the coolest place in the desert. Several small pipes thrust out from it and sink into the ground. Various colors of steam blow from some of the smaller pipes. Whispering can be heard, as this quiet corner is the perfect area for plotting, planning, and other forms of illegal activity.

A cabin, badly burned, stands here, though only the frame remains. Some old barrels are scattered on the ground along with piles of burnt wood and rubble. A large fence surrounds the area, entrapping it from the outside desert and its possible dangers. A small pillar slants out of the ground. Some debris shows that a railroad may have been here long ago.

The stairwell landing is quite dim, brightened slightly by the sunlight streaming in from an open-air window in the north wall. Steep stairs progress upward to the east and west, leading to other parts of the dungeon tower. The landing continues to the south past a pair of tall stone pillars.

Two nearly identical towers rise up from far below on either side of the slender stone bridge. The wind blows wildly, intensified by the narrow space between the towers. The bridge ends, both to the east and west, in a small balcony connected to the respective side's tower. From each balcony, an archway opens into into the towers.

Two red and yellow shields, each emblazoned with the silhouette of a flying reptile, hang on the north wall, flanking the east and west sides of an ascending stairwell. The gray stone walls and floor are illuminated by three torches mounted on the north wall. An ample wooden desk is tucked away in the eastern portion of the room, situated in front of a sturdy wooden chair. A doorway leads out of the room to the south.

The landing extends to the south, ending in a tall wall. Staircases lead down from the landing to the east and west. A slight breeze and the faint sound of howling wind float up the eastern staircase. A little light shines up from the western staircase, adding to the small amount of illumination from the window on the northern half of the landing.

Towering flames roar above the four brass braziers hanging on the north wall. The fires heat up the room, as well as illuminate it, creating an area of light and warmth nearby. Two wide doors are set in the north wall, opening into prison cells, and a staircase heads up to the east, leading higher into the dungeon tower.

Two heavy, metal prison cell doors are set into the north wall, each flanked by bulky brass braziers hanging on either side. The braziers' flames burn brightly, illuminating the area well, along with a pair of small lanterns on the east wall, next to the doorway.

Visible in the distance, mountains to the north ring the castle. A long stone bridge reaches across the empty expanse to the west, leading into Guardia Castle proper. A powerful wind blows through the gap between the two towers on either side of the bridge, drowning out all other noise. A doorway opens in the tower to the east, leading down into the dungeon of Guardia Castle.

rooms.name: Guardia Castle Dungeon Torture Chamber Entrance

userData.LongDescription: Fire rises out of dual braziers on each side of the large, partially-barred door, the flames crackling and snapping randomly. A lever is set against the north wall and is currently pulled down. Next to the lever, the wide door opens into a chamber to the north, and a hallway leads off to the west.

The howling wind drowns out all other noises at the top of this Guardia Castle tower. A bridge spans the wide gap to the east, leading into the castle dungeon. In the distance, the mountains that gird the castle to the north are visible. To the west, a doorway opens to the downward staircase heading into the castle.

A pair of unoccupied iron maidens sit in opposite corners, to the northeast and southwest. A small guillotine stands ready against the east wall, its blade raised. Several sets of balls and chains are scattered on the floor. A pair of braziers provide light from either side of the door in the north wall.

Wild winds whip across the narrow stone bridge between two towers to the east and west. Like mirror images, the two towers stand facing each other, horizontally flipped but otherwise identical copies. An archway is centered in each tower, opening into its interior and connected to the bridge between the towers.

A long, dark hallway runs east and west, turning south at its east end. The west end of the hallway leads into a stairway that heads upward. The only light in the hallway is provided by a pair of lanterns hanging on either side of this western stairway. Three tiny alcoves are set into the southern wall.

Two tall stone pillars separate this northern half of the platform from the half to the south. Stairs rise up on the east and west walls, leading away from the platform and to other parts of the tower. Little light shines on the platform; only the small amount of light from the exits to the east and west provide any illumination.

The north wall is dominated by the two massive cell doorways. Heavy metal cell doors are pulled up in the doorways, allowing access to the cells on the other side. Each doorway is flanked by a pair of brass braziers, each lit and burning brightly. An archway opens in the east wall with a descending stairway on the far side of the arch.

A duo of towering stone pillars divide this part of the platform from its northern half. This gloomy area is illuminated only slightly by the few slivers of light that shine up the stairways to the east and west. No light filters in from the northern half of the platform.

A decaying corpse lies splayed out on the floor of the cell, reduced to little more than a desiccated husk. One bony arm is outstretched, reaching up on to the the straw mattress the body is sprawled next to. An iron ball and chain is shackled to one of the corpse's legs, the manacle over-sized compared to the withered limb that remains.
An animated skeleton slowly marches in place.

A wooden doorway and a descending stairwell take up much of the north wall, along with three brightly flaming torches. The door opens into the warden's office to the north. Flickering torchlight lights this room well, giving it an orange tint, but the stairwell is heavily shadowed as it leads down into the castle dungeon.

This chamber is quite bright, with two lanterns hanging from the east wall, and four braziers attached to the north wall. Two large, arched doorways are open in the north wall. The doorway to the east hangs open, the door itself pulled high in the doorway. The western doorway is only partially pulled open, making entrance to the cell on the far side difficult but not impossible.

A large portion of the north wall of the cell has completely collapsed, leaving it open to the elements. Some of the stone of the floor has likewise fallen through, allowing access to the chamber below. The partial remains of an old straw mattress are scattered against the west wall. The cell door in the south wall is open.

This cell is dry and has almost no grime on the floor, walls or furniture, though a thin layer of dust covers almost everything in the room. A narrow window in the north wall allows in a little light, along with the occasional light breeze, which creates some small dust swirls. A metal chest lies open and empty in the southwest corner of the cell.

Constant wind flurries buffet the area between the two towers, making travel between them mildly hazardous. The noises produced by the blasts of air forced between the towers cause any other sounds to go completely unheard. A cramped stone bridge connects the towers.

Some of the bricks on the north wall have been pulled partially out, creating a make-shift climbing surface to reach the hole in the ceiling above. The door leading out the southeast chamber is partially closed, making passage difficult but not unreasonablely so.

This short hallway is lit up to the west by a pair of lanterns and to the east by twin braziers. The braziers flank a hefty arched doorway in the north wall, while the lanterns hang on either side of a much smaller archway in the west wall. Stairs lead up out of the hallway through the small archway.

Some small amount of light from the entrances above and below manages to keep this stairwell landing from being completely bathed in darkness. The weak, flickering light obscures most of the features of the landing, though the uneven stone bricks of the walls are visible. The openings at the top and bottom of the stairs do not provide much illumination, but the rooms beyond are plainly much more brightly lit.

Most of this hallway is cloaked in darkness. A small amount of light shines up the stairway to west, and to the east some faint illumination is discernable. The hallway branches off to the north, though that path is as murky as the rest of the corridor. The north wall is inset with three small alcoves.

rooms.name: Guardia Castle Dungeon Torture Chamber Storage Room

userData.LongDescription: Wooden pegs and shelves line the walls, filled with various instruments of torture. Several whips, maces and clubs hang from the pegs, and the shelves are stacked with many smaller tools of misery. A few busted manacles lie discarded on the floor under one set of shelves.

Part of the back wall of the cell has collapsed, exposing the outside through a gaping hole. A soiled straw mattress lies on the floor by the west wall and next to a hefty iron ball and chain. The cell door is pulled up in its frame and opens into a large chamber to the southeast.

A narrow window opens in the north wall. The window is far too thin for egress but it does allow in a smidgen of sunlight and a gentle breeze. A thick mattress lies on the western side of the cell, and a small wood stool sits against the wall to the east. A door opens to the chamber to the southwest.

The northwest corner of this small cell is filled with a dirty, worn mattress laying on the hard stone floor. A short wooden stool leans against the east wall, in such a state of disrepair that it is barely still standing. A thin window on the exterior wall of the cell supplies a little light and fresh air.

Several sets of manacles hang from hooks on the walls, and a few balls and chains are spread out on the floor. Two straight and tidy rows of weapon racks sit in the center of the room, filled with swords and spears. Pieces of wood and two partially put together wooden stools are resting on a shelf on the east wall.

Shadows dance on the walls, as the torches throughout the room provide only the barest light. Some brightness pours in from the west, where the basement landing is better illuminated. A great wooden door is slightly swollen in its frame to the north, standing between the entrance and the remainder of the basement.

Torches line the walls in this large chamber, producing abundant light throughout. The north-most end of the vault is comprised of a raised platform at the top of a pair of steps. A sizable purple rug covers the platform, and a smaller rug lies in the middle of the lower section of the room. Neat piles of crates have been stacked in the northeast and southwest corners of the vault. Around those crates, all manner of chests and other containers have been heaped. A few battleaxes and a spinning wheel have also been stored on the floor. A quartet of decorative shields are hung high on the northern wall. To the south, a large, wooden door leads out of the vault.

A hallway along the eastern side of this room leads out to the north and south. The western side is well-lit with several torches and filled with various containers and a few loose items. A substantial stack of crates has been piled in the middle of the storage area and is surrounded by several locked metal chests. A few long axes lean against the the southern end of the crate pile, seemingly long abandoned.

Railed stairs connect the hallway at the southern end of this area to the small platform before the northern door. Dual torches attached to either side of the door brighten the platform, but the hallway below is covered in shadows cast by the upper area. The hallway continues to the south, past a narrow archway.

This section of the hallway is bathed in darkness, only a small amount of light coming from a few torches shining far to the north. The floor and walls appear to be plain, gray stone, though they are largely obscured by the murkiness. This hallway continues a great distance to the north and opens to a storage room to the south.

Stagnant air chokes this area, and only a piddling amount of torchlight trickles in from the north and south, leaving this segment of hallway in near total blackness. Though difficult to make out in the darkness, the floor and walls appear to be made from the same rough stone that makes up the rest of the basement.

Lit only dimly by torchlight, this dank landing sits at the bottom of the staircase that links the basement to the other parts of Guardia Castle above. A pair of narrow steps connects the stairs in the north wall to the bare stone basement floor. The rest of the basement opens to the east.

Considerable amounts of dust have come to rest on the floor throughout this portion of the hallway, suggesting that it has not been traveled often. Hung on both sides of the archway that connects to the northern end of the passage, a pair of torches sheds a good deal of light, though they only reveal the plain, gray stone of the floor and walls.

A stone archway sets this section of the hallway off from the remainder that extends to the north. Torches have been hung on either side of the archway, supplying generous amounts of light throughout the area. The passageway grows darker to the south before it opens to a storage area.

This is a small fenced-in area behind the house, where the Tiny Bronco is kept.  A small runway leads away from the town, paved with blacktop and marked with reflectors.  A shed stands nearby, holding various tools and small machinery.

Atop the stairs, you are on the boarding sub-platform, located about halfway up the rocket's side. Now standing next to the engine with the faded wording, 'Shinra No. 27', a ladder climbs up to the top, where the entrance is.

This is the engineer's home. Modestly decorated, it has a cozy feel to it. There is a side room to the east, containing what appears to be a half-built car, among many tools and papers. To the northeast, there is a door leading to the back yard, where the Tiny Bronco is kept.

This is a large building, containing both an inn and a bar. The bar section is to the southeast, past some collapsing woodwork. From behind a large oak counter, the innkeeper smiles at you. There is a sign on the counter.

The path continues on past town, and through a small clearing where the rocket lies dormant. It sits upon a huge metal base, the only thing that keeps it from falling over. The oxidation of the metal seems to indicate that it has been here a long while.

This is the central area within town, surrounded by trees and housing. From here, the main path splits into three directions; east and west lead to more houses, and to the north, the path continues onward toward the rocket. You hear the name 'captain' mentioned in some of the scattered conversations of the townfolk, and wonder if he's a leader here. Meanwhile, an old man stands here, next to the item shop, gazing at the rocket.
This is the west side of the main path, where a house is located. Many trees surround this part of road, adding to the lush scenery.

This is the town's item shop. The building is actually a house, with a family, that has converted the main room into a store. There is a stock of useful-looking items for sale, sitting on the shelves. The man behind the counter points at his sign.

Just inside the entrance is a hallway with two doors; one door sealed shut, the other leading to the cockpit. There isn't much to this corridor, though there is a certain feeling of uneasiness inside of the failed rocket that is slowly tilting over. Cid still frequents this place, casually working on the rocket, hoping it may someday fly.

A rack of guns stands on either end of the counter. Six more gun racks are lined up agains the wall behind the counter, and another two on a side wall. Beside the counter, next to some shelves stocked with accessories and other merchandise, is a door into the owner's bedroom. A small sign is on the counter.

On this side of the path, there is another house. However, something more noticeable is just north, as another house there seems to have a plane of sorts in its backyard. There are a few people here, talking casually amongst themselves.

Having reached the top of the rocket, looking around offers quite an impressive view, and the ground seems a distant land. The entrance to the rocket is before you, just a few feet away. You can go back down the rocket by using the ladder behind you.

This house belongs to a young couple. It's small, but cozy, and nicely decorated. A fireplace radiates a placid warmth from a wall near the beds, while a lamp near the couch lights the rest of the room.

The stairway to the rocket's boarding platform is before you, and a glance up shows the entrance high above. Some engineers have gathered here, sharing memories about the old days building the rocket, reliving happier times.

This is the house of the pilot and mechanic, Cid Highwind. Entering space was his ambition, and he was to be the pilot of the rocket. However, an unfortunate circumstance shattered his dream. Since then, he has made this place, the rocket's launch site, his home, as have many of the other engineers.

A building is on either side of the path. One seems to be an inn; the other, an equipment shop.  The road leads north to the center of town, a commons of sorts, where people are seen going about their business. Further north, a towering metal structure can be seen in the distance, tilting slightly, and aged with rust.

Continuing around the rocket, there are a pair of small bridges to take you over the rocket's umbilical. Looking up at the rocket, you see the faded words 'Shinra No. 27' in faded letters upon the side. Up ahead are stairs that take you up to the rocket's metal base.

This house is small and somewhat lacking in style. There are two beds in the corner of the main room, next to the sofa and chairs. A small kitchen shares the room with a circular table with a pair of wooden chairs. Cramped as it may be, it still seems a comfortable place to live.

There are two large circular tables along the south wall of the bar, each with four chairs, and the bartender's counter is in the northeast corner. A neon sign behind the counter flashes the words 'Shanhaj-Tej' in green letters. The barkeeper is behind the counter.

You stand at the entrance to the most bizarre room yet seen in the Black Omen, there is a long catwalk leading north, to the far end of the room, and strange cylinders with what appear to be cloned people in them it is truly odd, there is one cylinder which is however not fully visible to the north a little way.

Another metal platform provides a base for adventurers to continue. This one seems no different than the others, except it has a more ominous feeling, which would appear to get stronger and more obvious the deeper the Black Omen goes.

There are numerous dormant monsters here, and a strange dark red pattern inlayed in the center, which seems odd, as red isn't a color that has shown itself a great deal throughout the Black Omen. To the northeast, and off the platform there is an exit, it is not particularly far and there seems to be a strange feeling of safety eminating from the room it leads to.

All around there are decorations and figurines carved into the wall. It looks like some of these figurines came alive to form guards at one point, but now it appears someone has destroyed them. There is a soft, velvet carpet forming a path to the north, it leads out into another room, and back to the south leads through a large archway and onto a jagged looking platform.  The walls zig zag in and out, emphasising the strange architecture that seems so apparent throughout the black omen, and set into the floor are flashing golden grids, they seem to fade on and off, as do the lights set into the walls.

Amongst the cylinders, one stands out in particular, looking closer might reveal a shocking truth, and a reason to destroy the monstrosity that is the Black Omen. To the far north, Empress Zeal sits on her throne, laughing at you.

In this room there appear to be what look like buttons set into long strips of shining blue metal set into the floor. They don't appear raised out of the floor, or pushable in any way, as if they were meant to be activated by some kind of presence, rather than being pushed. To the south and north there are doors, but this room is so similar all around, it is hard to discern which is the way out, and which is the way forward...
The orb monsters seem to have backed off for now, but in there place there are still more monsters, these one's appear to be fairly alert to what is happening aswell.

The path forward is dark and ill lit, the walls are barely visible, and the air is filled with a strange smell not familiar to you. The path seems to continue northward, with no breaks to the east or west, none that are visible at least anyway, there is also a low hum, akin to the whirring noise of a large machine up ahead, perhaps it is the room where the Black Omen is controlled.

Directly west of the large hole, there are exits to the north and east, and green flames dance around on top of their candles, illuminating the northern door brightly. A small disturbance starts whirling on the floor, and a bright yellow spiral of light shoots upward from it, when it is gone, something sinister remains

The light level seems to have picked up a bit, as if there is something lighting the way, but it is not bright enough to be fully visible, more like an after thought, or a dream of some kind. There is a large crack in the floor here also, it can be easily avoided by walking on the metal girder that has been placed across it to serve as a walkway, but it is hard to see exactly how wide the crossing is, and the hole beneath it seems to travel some way down...

After walking eastward and now to the north, it becomes apparent that, judging from the increasing amount of resistance, and guards, this path is, indeed, nearing the center of the Black Omen. The walls close in tight along this northerly path, which has been spawned from the road now back to the west.

After walking westward and now to the north, it becomes apparent that, judging from the increasing amount of resistance, and guards, this path is nearing the center of the Black Omen. The walls close in tight along this northerly path, which has been spawned from the road now back to the east.

This is the throne room of the Black Omen, and where the once peaceful and sound Empress Zeal now rules the world with an iron fist, feeding off the power of Lavos, and waiting for him to awaken from his sleep so he may plunder the earthly world of its life. To the north, there is a large archway, through it there appears to be the image of Gaspar, and some bright lights.

This is the lower level of the transport beam that leads up through the Black Omen. If one were to head up, then they would be taken to the upper level, and back onto the route out of the Black Omen. A large green guardian stands vigilant over the shaft of orange light leading upwards.

The walls are carved out into huge white statues, resembling guardians of some sort, although from the types of things dwelling in the Black Omen, protection is the last thing it needs. A small round pad is in the center of the room, just big enough for a person to stand on, and from the pad there is a brilliant beam of orange light reaching upward, and through the transparent pad, it seems to be stretching downward as well. An exit is to the south, out of the Black Omen, and down, through the orange beam.
The path west ends here, in a dark dead-end.

The Highest Platform, it branches off to the west.  A long pipe runs directly below the platform, and gives a low humming noise, as if it were charged with electricity, as a kind of power conduit. To the far north, beyond reach, two tubes spiral downward, interweaving to create a stunning method of transport between platforms.

There is a small stairway leading upto the platform that has been raised above level of the floor. A long rectangular carpet resembling spun gold lies right in the miffle of the platform, it aslo seems to have small cogs and mechanisms in it, that although hard to see, are moving and working away for some unknown purpose. Another striking thing about this room is how symetrical it is, two large pillars rise out of the ground, complementing each other just as the square's they are set in lie exactly symetrical to their counterpart on the other side of the room.

A large section is missing from the middle of this platform, forcing one to walk around the edge hugging the wall closely. In the hole there seems to be nothing visible, just an immensely bright white light, almost like a fog. There are, however, a couple of large monuments that have reached above the white fog, although they are still far too low for one to reach from here. On the opposite side of the room, across the hole, there is a door directly north, but it is unreachable.

rooms.name: The Nu's Shop and Save Point

userData.LongDescription: There is a small mat laid on the floor, where the Nu has spread his wares for a passerby to examine. His comical appearence should not be taken lightly, the Nu are very serious traders, and have a temper when it comes to being ripped off. There is a warm light coming from the walls and come into the center of the room, it is very noticable.

You stand directly opposite the room where the Nu are, and can awake you from your dream. However, this is the platform you spotted earlier, the one which was previously inaccessable from where you where, it appears that you have travelled a long way since then, and to find a way out it would probably faster to go northwest, and forward, rather then trail back to the northeast.

There appears to be little way of getting through the Black Omen without encountering some structural oddity. The floor is metal, except this time, it is wet and slippery, as if some creature has salivated on it. There is an escape route straight through the center and to the north, with a little luck, one may be able to leave with their life.

There are disgusting Ruminators everywhere here, it seems that this room is where they breed and raise their kin. The floor is dirty and stained, and there are large holes that seem to have been worn away by teeth of some kind. To the south and back through the pillars there is an exit, and another lies to the northeast.

The trail branches off to the northeast here, and leads to what appears to be a small set of stairs leading up onto another platform with two large adjacent pillars on either side. There is also a doorway on the raised platform to the northeast, nestling in the middle of the pillars.

Finally, this is the largest room in the black Omen, it stretches out in every direction further than you can see, it is littered with bright lights, burning flames, picturesque figurines, and wonders to make the mind boggle, it is an amazing work of beauty. To the center there is a large junction, which seems to have pathways leading of into dead ends, apart from one to the north, which leads to another grand doorway, it seems possible to reach it by heading in a northwesterly direction.

This room looks truly remarkable, there are statue's of Empress Zeal standing tall, erected from somewhere down in the bright light that eminates from the large hole in the center of the room. A carpet sits on the floor leading a path around the room, it is a deep royal blue, and is very plush to stand on. This room is so large, it is hard to see any exits at first, but there must be one to the south, as there is an attractive light coming from that direction.

This is the bottom of a small flight of stairs, leading upwards, in a northerly direction. To the left and right there seem to be semi-platforms attached to the main one, as if they were some kind of counter balance.  There are many lights shining on the ground, casting shadows all along the floor.  To the south is the way out of the Black Omen, while the stairs lead deeper in.

The floor beneath glows incredibly bright, as if it's feeding of some incredibly strong power source nearby. It lights the way forward, but the path only runs to the east and west once again. It is impossible to see what lies in each direction as they both turn off directly north after a few feet. Back to the south, and a very long journey, is the exit to the Black Omen.

A giant creature resides on this platform.  It glares at you, and if you are not prepared to fight, it may destroy you!  In the distance, partially visible behind this montrosity, is a doorway leading north.  The remains of an inn lie not far to the south.

After regrouping it appear the orb's are back, and in greater numbers than ever. To the south is an escape route if you can make it before they get to you, and back to the east leads to the beginning of the orb trail, and out into the Ruminator's lair.
The very depths of the Omen are here; it is an easy sensation to feel as the distorted space around pushes inward, centering the dark energies that dwell within.

The northern path is blocked, by two heavy pillars, it would be pointless to try and move them. More immediately, there is the large platform that could be seen from the entrance, it looks like there are some guards there, but they should pose little problem now, and a route forward will surely reveal itself from there.

This is the top part of the platform that the green shaft of light emerges from, it's deep emarald color is entrancing to behold, and could distract someone's attention just long enough for them to be attacked from behind, never knowing what hit them. Fortunately there seems to be no such creature here that could attack you at the moment. Two large gargoyle statue's stare inward at the light, as if to warn anyone who might consider going further, to turn back.

This is the lower level of the light beam transportation device, there is a doorway to the north, and embedded above it is a blinking green crystal, that seems to flash more rapidly the closer toward it you move.  Again, as in the top level of the transport device, there are two statue's leaning inwards, although these seem to welcoming visitors, rather than warning them, but they are also surrounded in a false presence...

This is the second safe room run by a Nu, they must enjoy it here because of the intense magical energy emitted by Lavos. It still would seem to be a strange place to have an inn though, as there is presumably a lack of visitors most of the time. Fortunately, due to the good nature of Nu, it's possible to sleep and save here.

This room is immediately bisected by a large pillar, adorned with images of guards set into it. To the north is a way to go deeper into the Black Omen, up a flight of steps. There also appears to be a new pattern, one of intersecting diamonds, and looks very magical.

The inside of this flying technological monster is very similar to the outside, it is constructed from the same metal, but inside it is a strange rustic color as opposed to the royal blue decorating the outside. The huge metal platforms that are suspended from wall to wall by girders and pillars of various kinds, form a base for walking on. There are many doors in sight, but only a few seem to be accessible via the route one takes.  Up ahead appears to be a doorway which is open, and there are also doors to the left and right, although they are impossible to get to from here. Back to the south is the outside of the Omen, and a way back to the Epoch.

A huge platform with jagged edges, it stretches for quite some distance to the north. There are some odd features built into the platform that have no apparent purpose. There are what appear to be vents and raised blocks in the floor, but this is a merger of magic and technology, nobody could truly say exactly what the function of all the twisting shapes and lights that appear to have no source or fuel are in the Black Omen...except for Empress Zeal and the Gurus, of course.  The defensive capabilities of the Black Omen appear to be working, as loud shrieks and the whirring of metal can be heard from nearby.

The path has converged with other, smaller paths to meet here, in a large rectangular shaped platform with one of the largest statue's that you've seen so far in the Black Omen, it stands a good 12 feet tall, towering above on it's own pedestal, and it's beady eyes seem to follow you around the room. To the southeast is the way you came, and further northwesterly lies the main platform in the center of the room, which also provides and exit.

This is the entrance to the ever ominous Black Omen. There are no walls or barriers to keep someone from falling to their doom with one misplaced step, and there are large diamond shaped holes in the metal floor.  The view extends as far as the eye can see, for this is miles above the earth, the Black Omen soars with the gods, and has a strong magical presence that is easily felt.  A large blue door engraved with gold patterns lies directly ahead, but beware of what lies inside.  The Epoch hovers below.

There is a series of platforms interlinked by pyramid-like stairs, and on each of them there appears to be a bunch of Orb monsters, although they also appear to be rather dormant. Perhaps with a little luck and cunning, it would be possible to get through this area without aggrevating any of the monsters dormant here.

There is an elevator platform, it appears to go down a couple of levels deeper into the Black Omen. There is a small button here, that looks as if it activates the elevator, and goes yet deeper into the heart of the Black Omen. The path goes north, towards the exit of the Omen.

On this lower level elevator platform, the shaft rises high in the air. The elevator can take one back up the shaft, towards the transport beam and the upper halls of the Black Omen. To the north, off the elevator, is another room, but the Black Omen may have more creatures or lasers guarding the passage.

The walls are littered with huge statues and ominous guardian creatures. They do not seem to move, but they seem to be fixed on nothing in the room. The lights behind them range from orange, green and a dark red. The path has taken on a 'zig-zagging' motion, as it trails off to the northwest, and from the reflection on the far wall, it then heads off to the northeast.

The southern platform comes to an end -- it seems less stable than the lower part, and only seems to be held in place by the two exits that are connected to other platforms. Below the dark expanses of the Black Omen seem to stretch out forever, and it would appear almost bottomless to those who do not know better. Keeping a good strong foothold is a necessity here, as one wrong move could send an adventurer plumeting to their doom.  Up ahead the platform ends, while back to the south it continues and then joins onto another platform through a small doorway.

The Middle Platform, this platform is placed between to sets of stairs, one leading down, to the south, and one leading upwards to the north. Lights in the ceiling provide some illumination on the ground. The path seemingly runs north and south forever, into the darkness, without an exit in sight.

The floor, covered in goop, makes for a sticky and slippery place for feet. The path through the Black Omen goes north and south, into poorly lit darkness. Lights flash in the sides of the walls, casting alien shadows across the wall and floor.

The path splits in two directions here, one route leads east, and of course, the other west. The floor here is different to the upper levels of the Black Omen, it is a smarter, warmer black color. Decorated in a modern sort of way, yet still with the strange markings that have become so typical throughout the upper levels of the Black Omen. A gold strip of engraved metal runs east and west, along the top of the metal floor, it catches the light and reflects it around the room, which is another apparent thing here, the light level seems to be a little dimmer, fortunately it is still strong enough to allow navigation with relative ease
Three pillars form a tri-doorway here, but each side of the pillar appears to be guarded by a monster. To the north and up some stairs there is a nest of Ruminators.

The entrance to this cave opens broadly into a crystalline cave. Two giant pillars stand on either side of the entryway and shape the paths of the main room. A faint humming sound can be heard reverberating throughout the room, though exactly where it is coming from is difficult to tell.

The east wing of the cave curves around here, opening into another room. Two short stone columns stand on either side of a smooth tile, which appears to have been well worn. The crystal walls in this room resonate with a faint humming sound.

The northern end of the cave stretches outward. The walls are roughly hewn, but almost perfectly straight in both directions, as though they were meticulously carved over a very long period of time. At the far end are two short stone columns, each on either side of a smooth stone tile.

The western part of the cavern opens here, curving into another room. The crystal walls, roughly cut but well-defined, vibrate with the humming that is ever-present within the cavern. There is a pair of small columns at the end of the room, each standing on either side of a tile that appears to be designed for long periods of standing.

A cool breeze blows swiftly through the trees causing the leaves to rustle. Several vines dangle from a higher branch with many different colors of flowers growing on them. The birds songs echo through the forest causing a harmonic tune. The clear blue sky remains empty and restful.

Bright green grass covers the forest floor and the songs of birds fill the air. Some blue flowers sway in the gentle breeze causing a sense of tranquility to be felt. Beams of sunlight shine brightly through the trees here giving the plantlife its vibrant flare.

This cliff stands about as high as the bridge that can now be seen in the distance. The green grass covers the cliff to the very edge. Some bushes with red berries on them grow on the right side of the cliff. The leaves continue to block out a majority of the sunlight, but small beams still find their way through the small pockets of leaves. To the north, there seems to be an obscured path to a small stone temple of sorts.

The thick layer of leaves has cleared up some making it easier for the sunlight to shine through. The grass is slowly clearing, revealing a dirt road. The song of the birds can no longer be heard. Several bushes line the road. This part of the forest feels rather uncomfortable and dark compared to the other areas.

The shade of the bridge keeps it cool here. The grass is as green here as in the unshaded areas of the forest. A cool refreshing breeze blows under and through the bridge. The chittering of a chipmunk can be heard in the distance.

The bridge gives a slightly larger view of the forest. Birds can be seen flying to their nests to feed their young. The leaves are dancing to the song of the birds. Sunlight continues to beam through the leaves of the trees. Small flower patches add color to the otherwise bare woods.

The base of the small rock mountain can still be see here. The trees grow tall, hiding the small rock mountain from any outside viewers. The ground is beginning to become green again; the shadow of the rock must have blocked the sun out from those dirt patches that were just passed.

Beams of sunlight shine through the leaves of the trees and onto the flowers that grow in the forest. The warm forest breeze transforms into a cooler, more relaxing breeze. The birds singing carries through the forest into a soft harmonic tune.

An open chest sits on a large stump its treasure has long been lost. A large pink flower feeding off nearby insects rests near a stump. Bright green grass surrounds the stump and flower. Two vines hang down from the trees with flowers blooming off the end.

The dark green grass sways softly in the breeze. A rabbit hole can be seen near the trunk of a thick tree. The hooting of a nearby owl adds some tune to the birds' musical harmony. Several squirrels search the tall grass for acorns and nuts so they may have a meal tonight. Some tall red flowers rise above the grass making themselves known to the world.

A small mountain is here, hidden by the trees of the forest. The ground is absent of any grass or flowers and only the fresh earth remains. A large pink flower rests near the foot of the small rock mountain. In the distance the roar of a large cat or other animal can be heard.

The sun shines brightly upon the tree branches. Yellow flowers are blooming on the trees giving the air a pleasant scent. A butterfly gently flutters from flower to flower. Every now and then a bird flies out of the tree and into the light blue sky.

A soft breeze continues to blow the dark green grass. A raccoon can be seen peeking out of some brush at the base of one of the trees. A bed of red and white flowers is growing at the base of another tree. Cracks of sunlight shine through the thick layer of leaves onto the flower bed. The song of the birds continues to give a sense of harmony to the forest.

The birds' musical tunes are now more distant and quiet. The green blanket of grass spreads to the northwest and west. The sunlight is now struggling to shine through the thick layer of leaves in this part of the forest. A calm cool breeze continues to blow, providing refreshment for a hot tired traveler that may be passing through. Bushes grow between the trees.

This stone temple is nearly symmetric in shape. It rests nearly sunken in the underbrush. It looks fairly ancient, and must have been used as an altar to some kind of god. A thin layer of water covers the ground; a nearby swamp must've nearly flooded the temple. Now unused, it only serves as a reminder of the past for explorers to awe at.

The singing of birds continues to echo through the forest, relaxing weary warriors who happen to pass through. Beams of sunlight shine through the leaves and onto the fragile flowers. The gentle breeze remains soft while rustling the leaves of the trees.

The bright sun shines its warm rays onto the area. The leaves dance slowly to the sound of the birds. The clear blue sky remains peaceful and empty. The sunset up here must be a wonderous sight to see. The branches of the tree spread out in all directions.

The forest floor remains covered in a bright sheet of grass. Bright beams of sunlight shine on the forest environment keeping it green and beautiful. A breeze picks up causing the leaves to blow swiftly in the wind. The birds singing picks up to the sway of the leaves making it feel like the whole forest has a balance it follows. One tree has a small hole in the trunk.

This is the throne room of the castle. Shaped a large square, this room has a large stained-glass window on the northern wall as well as a huge throne standing directly in front of it. Royal red carpet is spread out north-south, from the stained-glass window to the staircase on the southern wall.

The full moon is in plain view from the wooden planks of the outer wall, the only obstacles being a few stray clouds of darkness in the sky. Wooden steps proceeds the path leading up, while a smooth teak plank leads the way to the east. Chunks of stone have been used to create the sturdy castle walls, attached strongly to the wooden frames.

This small anteroom in the eastern wing is especially misty, with only two large candleholders giving light and a sense of direction. To the north and south are large hallways, north leading to an ascending staircase up to the castle keep and south to a descending staircase, to the entrance area of the castle.

This is a small wooden platform high near the peak of the outer wall. A large, grand stone archway close by leads deep into a grand hallway. A set of spiralling steps leads down the castle turret. The full moon glows slightly in the night sky, covered partially by clouds.

The outer wall of the castle is dark and chilly, with strong winds blowing in the night. The moon is barely visible from this point, as wooden frames partially block the view along with the clouds of darkness. A set of planks leads to the west, to the other side of the wall. A staircase nearby provides a path leading down the outer wall.

This section of the outer wall contains a large metal grate blocking the way into an empty hallway. A set of wooden planks continues the ascending road to the west. Nearby is a set of steps leading down to the base of the turret. The moon slightly illuminates the otherwise dull night sky.

A set of steps lie nearby, leading up to a small platform before the entrance to a large hallway. A set of wooden planks leads to the east, to a descending set of steps. Stone bricks have been used to create the entire outer wall. Cold winds howl fiercely in the night. The full moon floats high in the night skies, veiled by dark clouds.

The eastern wing of the castle seems to be filled with thick mist, due to positioning. The corridor is quite spacious and nice, though rather devoid of furniture. The walls and floors are a dark, soot-covered stone. A roll of red carpet leads to the north into the mist, and a set of stairs leads down to the entrance area.

This small room up in the eastern castle keep is above the misty blankets. The personal chambers of Flea, one of Magus' three highest ranking Generals, is long and narrow. The ground is completely covered in royal red carpet, with a large wooden throne at the northern wall. Lanterns are hung about, giving plenty of light to this narrow room.

This small section of the castle has brought many deaths. Shaped in a twisted zig-zag pattern, conveyor belts are placed about it, with large and sharp guillotine blades constantly flying down at a set interval. The moving pathway leads to the northeast. A catwalk is high above, out of reach.

The conveyor belt takes a sharp turn to the southeast, connected by a small stone platform rigged by a guillotine trap high above. Among the guillotine traps above is a long stone catwalk, however it is out of reach. Hurry, or the trap might have to shed more blood on its swinging steel.

This is an extremely dark tunnel, barely able to fit the size of a man. Little torches are placed in increments on the walls, to help illuminate the path. Wooden steps have been placed over the ground, to make travel easier. The path leads further down, but it is too dark to see where it ends.

A wide staircase rests nearby, leading higher up to the east along the turret of the castle. Nearby, the moon shines brightly, only covered by some clouds. East leads along a wooden plank to a spiralling set of steps. The castle walls are a neat, layered stone brick, darkened with soot and blending into the night rather well.

This is the northern hallway of the west wing. Identical in shape and size to the southern hallway, these twin hallways make up most of the lower western portion of the castle. Scattered about are what seems to be skeletal remains of humans. A set of stairs is to the north, leading up to the western keep. South leads to an anteroom connecting the two hallways.

A grand set of stairs leads up to the final few corridors proceeding the highest peak of the castle. South leads to an intricate pentagram made out of holes and large chains. A thin layer of mist wraps the room, signifying thicker blankets of mist high above. It is awfully dark in here...

This U-shaped corridor looks fairly ordinary, with smooth flooring. The walls appear to have alcoves within them, holding large, golden candlesticks that illuminate the room with an eerie glow. On the northern wall is an opening leading out into the outer wall of the castle.

This small corridor connects two larger hallways together. The ground is a cracked stone, arranged in a diamond pattern. A row of golden candleholders are lined against the black, soot-covered walls. North and south leads to identical hallways, north leading to the west wing keep and south down to the main entrance.

This is the peak of the grand staircase. Paths to the left and right are available, leading to the different wings of the castle. Down to the south is a carpeted path leading to the entrance gates of the castle. A large stained-glass window is nearby, filling the room with moonlight.

A large opening is on the wall at the tunnel's western end, though oddly there is nothing visible beyond the hole. Ascending wooden steps are to the east, leading to the castle area. Torches are placed around, illuminating this otherwise pitch black tunnel. The walls of this tunnel are dirt, though some of it have been covered with wooden boards.

This long hallway is slanted, ascending to the north and descending to the south. All around are statues of increasing sizes as the altitude rises. Candles are placed on gourds on the walls, giving a bit of light to the otherwise dark hallway. A metal plaque is attached to the wall nearby.

The Chain Corridor is a particularly strange-looking hallway. It's large and wide with nothing discernible in it, except for large holes on the sides that has a single, large chain hanging from the ceiling in it. To the south is a large hole leading out into the outer wall of the castle.

The castle entrance is dark, silent and intimidating. Gargoyle statues are set up along the sides of the lush red carpet, with large candleholders set up for lighting. A grand stairway is to the north along with a stained-glass window. To the south are the gates of the castle.

This large hallway looks fairly ordinary, with walls made out of crude brick formations and floors of cut stone shaped into tiled squares. The mist is a bit thinner here, due to higher altitude. On the northern wall are stairs leading up to the peak of the eastern wing, and to the south a small anteroom connecting the two large hallways together.

This is the northeastern end of the pitfall corridor. A large iron switch is here, thrown and jammed. On the northern wall is a set of stairs leading up somewhere. South leads into the rigged halls of the pitfall corridor. An eerie, flickering glow surrounds the room, originating from the candleholders placed on the corners.

Near the end of the guillotine corridor is a stone platform and one final conveyor belt leading to the north where a large, open square area lies. There is a ladder leading up to the high catwalk, where a switch for the guillotine traps lies. Blood is present on the platform and walls, permeating the air with a pungent stench.

This peculiar room is shaped a circle, with no visible flooring. Scattered all around are blue fireballs that form a large pattern on the ground, with a small circular pentagram in the center. On the northern wall is a huge demonic statue with three candleholders placed around it, giving it an eerie glow.

The Sky Corridor is a short hall connecting the chain corridor and the castle peak. It has large windows on the walls, providing an excellent view of the skies and scenery about. A set of stairs nearby leads down to the chain corridor. North leads to the center of the corridor.

This long hallway leads a long way up to the north. Statues of beasts are placed on the sides, getting progressively larger as the slope continues upwards. The floor is a surprisingly smooth stone layer, darkish grey in color, and the walls a darkened brick. There's a plaque on the wall.

The center of the chain corridor features a very strange pentagram of chain holes. A large circular pit serves as the border, and a five point star-shaped hole crossing within the middle of the circle, making travel unneccessarily difficult. South leads to an opening connecting into the outer wall, while north holds a trail going up to the central castle keep.

This is a large, empty room, shaped like a large octagon, empty as far as the eye can see. A large set of steps are in the center of the room, leading high up to the pitfall corridor. The walls are a perfectly tiled stone, almost seeming to blend into the similarly crafted floors.

Powerful winds make the outer wall section of the castle particularly dangerous, with no guardrails attached to the platforms for safety. The platforms are made out of a flimsy wood, guaranteeing no safe footing anywhere. A path of wooden planks leads to the east, and a set of wooden steps heads further up the castle turret.

The outer wall of the castle is dark and intimidating. The night sky is wrapped in the glow of the moon, partially covered by dark clouds. A wooden plank leads to the west, where a set of stairs leads higher up around the wall to the upper castle areas. Nearby is a set of spiralling steps descending down to the lower sanctum of the castle.

This large, long room on the peak of the western castle keep is also known as the personal quarters of Slash, one of three Generals of Magus. A long roll of dark red carpet is stretched up to the northern wall, where a crude throne is. Lanterns are hung on the wall, substituting for the regular candleholders.

This is the upper section of the slanted hallway, nearly at the highest point. To the south is a pretty nice view of the row of statues that start small and grow in size as the hallway ascends up. Gourds containing candles are placed on the walls, providing a luminescent glow to the hallway. A metal plaque is attached to the wall.

A large entrance that looks to have been caused by an accident is here on the wall, leading into a long hallway with many chains hanging by the ceiling. A set of stairs rests nearby, leading down the outer wall. Strong winds blow in the night; caution is recommended, especially with no guardrails to prevent accidents from happening.

Another guillotine trap-rigged small stone platform connects two conveyor belts together. The platform and walls around are coated in a permanent layer of dry blood from all the victims this deadly corridor has claimed. A catwalk of stone is barely visible high above the guillotine traps.

This is a wide, open and flat room. To the west is a ladder leading up to the catwalk. North leads up a spiralling set of steps to the outer wall of the castle. A conveyor belt rigged with guillotine traps is to the south, moving to the direction of this room. Large candleholders are placed on the corners of the room, giving it a nice accent.

This is a sharp L-shaped curve in the corridor. The room's floors are seemingly smooth, with no crack or flaw to the stone tiles. Large candleholders have been placed in alcoves along the wall, set in precise increments. East leads to another bend in the hallway, and north to a large opening in the wall.

The west wing of the castle has two central hallways that lead a long way north. There seem to be no doorways leading to stray rooms, however. Candleholders are placed in the corners of the room, providing adequate lighting. The walls are strangely dark, made out of coarse bricks. To the north is a small anteroom between another open hallway, and to the south a set of steps leading into the entrance.

This is a corner in the pitfall corridor, splitting into two paths: west and north. North leads to a long path ending with a set of stairs in the northern wall. To the west is a short path stopping at another cut corner. Candleholders are placed in set increments, partially hidden in alcoves along the wall.

This is the peak of the ascending hallway. Nearby is a set of steps embedded into the wall to the north, leading higher up somewhere. South leads a long way down, eventually reaching the lowest point of the corridor. Statues are placed on the sides of the passageway, growing in size as the hallway continues up. A metal plaque is attached to the wall.

This partially hidden catwalk looms high above the guillotine-ridden conveyor hallway, giving a good view of it. Just to the east is an iron ladder leading down to a wide, open area. West leads to a broken point on the catwalk, the beginning of the guillotine corridor below it.

This area represents another set of wooden planks and steps attached to the castle wall, perhaps the remains of construction frames set up a long time ago. To the west is a straight wooden plank leading to the opposite end of the wall. Nearby is a set of stairs heading down into the castle chambers.

The trapped platform is placed just right beneath an important-looking catwalk. A trap is loaded and set to go right under the blocks of the catwalk. Southeast leads to the next conveyor belt, three guillotines placed high above it. The walls around are made out of darkened, solid stone, giving the place an eerie atmosphere.

The center of the Sky Corridor has strangely no windows, but instead the walls contain huge and beautiful paintings. A grand chandelier hangs from the ceiling, illuminating the hallway brightly. South leads to a descending set of stairs, while the northern path ends at an ascending staircase.

The northern end of the Sky Corridor contains a large staircase leading up to the castle peak, where the throne of the sorcerer is. The windows abruptly end at one point, continued by peculiar designs on stone walls. To the south is the center of the Sky Corridor, marked by a large chandelier and several paintings.
